original_title: How to Talk to Girls at Parties
overview: Croydon, 1977. A trio of punk teenagers goes to a party to meet girls, but they find that girls there are very different from what they expected.
tagline: Some girls are out of this world
title: How to Talk to Girls at Parties
plot:
How to Talk to Girls at Parties is a 2017 science fiction film that explores the complexities of human relationships, identity, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond one's control. The movie delves into the theme of isolation and loneliness, as its protagonist, Enn, navigates his way through a world where he has been isolated from society for over 20 years.

The film also touches on the idea of self-discovery and the struggle to find one's place in the world. Enn's interactions with the alien, Viva, serve as a catalyst for him to confront his own emotions and desires, leading to a deeper understanding of himself and his relationships with others.

Furthermore, the movie critiques societal norms and expectations, particularly those surrounding masculinity and femininity. The character of Enn challenges traditional notions of masculinity, while also exploring the complexities of female identity through Viva's character.

The film's use of science fiction as a backdrop allows it to comment on the human condition in a way that is both thought-provoking and visually stunning. Ultimately, How to Talk to Girls at Parties is a movie about embracing one's true self and finding connection with others, even in a world that can be overwhelming and isolating.

[No production company mentioned as Fortissimo Films was not the production company of this movie]

overview: A boy imagines a monster that helps him deal with his difficult life and see the world in a different way.
tagline: Stories are wild creatures.
title: A Monster Calls
plot:
A Monster Calls is a 2016 dark fantasy drama directed by J. A. Bayona, with a screenplay by Patrick Ness adapted from his own 2011 novel of the same name. Lewis MacDougall leads the cast as Conor O'Malley, alongside Sigourney Weaver, Felicity Jones, Toby Kebbell and Liam Neeson, who provides the voice and motion capture for the title creature. The film is a Spanish, British and American co-production, with Focus Features acquiring the rights in 2014.

Set in rural England, the story follows twelve-year-old Conor, whose mother is undergoing chemotherapy for a serious illness. Conor dislikes his rigid grandmother and dreads the idea of living with her, since his father has started a new family in the United States. At school he is bullied by a classmate named Harry, and at night he is haunted by a recurring nightmare in which the old church near his house collapses into a pit and he struggles to keep his mother from falling in. He copes by drawing, a talent he inherited from his mother.

One night, at seven minutes past midnight, the ancient yew tree beside the church comes to life as a towering Monster. It announces that it will tell Conor three stories over its coming visits, and that afterwards Conor must tell it a fourth story: the truth behind his nightmare. The Monster's tales, rendered in watercolour-style animation, are morally ambiguous fables about a prince and a queen, an apothecary and a parson, and an invisible man, each one refusing to offer the simple lessons Conor expects. As his mother's health declines and he is forced to move into his grandmother's house, Conor's grief and anger begin to spill into destructive outbursts, while a visit from his father brings more disappointment than comfort.

The film builds toward Conor's confrontation with the real meaning of his dream, in which he must admit the conflicted feelings he has been hiding: his wish for the pain of waiting to end, and the guilt that comes with it. Through this admission the story explores how children process loss, the coexistence of love and resentment, and the value of telling the truth.

A Monster Calls was praised for MacDougall's performance, Neeson's voice work, its visual effects and its emotional honesty, and it won several Goya Awards, including Best Director for Bayona.

overview: A methamphetamine cook hunts down the former police chief of a small town in order to silence him before he can deliver eyewitness testimony against his family, but ultimately finds himself up against more than he had bargained for.
title: Wrong Place
plot: A methamphetamine cook hunts down the former police chief of a small town in order to silence him before he can deliver eyewitness testimony against his family, but ultimately finds himself up against more than he had bargained for.

overview: A gang of gold thieves lands in a coven of witches who are preparing for an ancient ritual... and in need of a sacrifice.
title: Witching & Bitching
plot:
Witching & Bitching is a dark comedy film that delves into the complexities of human relationships and societal expectations. The movie follows the story of a young man, David, who returns to his hometown after serving time in prison for a crime he did not commit. As he navigates his way through the community, he becomes embroiled in a series of misadventures with his eccentric family members.

At its core, Witching & Bitching is a film about the struggles of identity and belonging. David's journey is marked by a sense of disconnection and disillusionment with the world around him. He grapples with the notion of who he is and where he belongs, often finding himself at odds with the people and institutions that are supposed to provide support and guidance.

The film also explores themes of family dynamics and the complexities of intergenerational relationships. David's interactions with his family members reveal a deep-seated sense of resentment and frustration, as well as a longing for connection and understanding. Through their dysfunctional relationships, the characters in Witching & Bitching illustrate the ways in which societal expectations can stifle individuality and creativity.

Furthermore, the movie touches on issues of masculinity and the performance of male identity. David's struggles with his own masculinity are reflected in his interactions with other men, who embody different versions of traditional masculine norms. This exploration of masculinity is nuanced and multifaceted, highlighting the ways in which societal expectations can constrain individual expression.

Ultimately, Witching & Bitching is a film about finding one's place in the world and embracing one's true self, even if that means challenging the status quo. Through its dark humor and poignant character studies, the movie offers a powerful commentary on the human condition, inviting viewers to reflect on their own relationships with family, identity, and societal expectations.

overview: Rural England, 1865. Katherine, suffocated by her loveless marriage to a bitter man and restrained by his father's tyranny, unleashes an irresistible force within her, so powerful that she will stop at nothing to get what she wants.
title: Lady Macbeth
plot:
Lady Macbeth is a 2016 psychological drama film directed by William Oldroyd, based on the novella "The Lady of the House of Love" by David Lodge. The film stars Florence Pugh as Katherine "Kitty" Clark and Jack Lowden as James Macbeth.

The story begins in 1865, with Kitty Clark, a young woman from a wealthy family, returning to her childhood home after being released from an asylum where she was being treated for her mental illness. Her mother, Mrs. Clark (Charlotte Rampling), is dying of cancer and has been institutionalized due to her own mental health issues.

Kitty's father, Sir Malcolm Clark (Christopher Eccleston), a wealthy landowner, is determined to marry Kitty off to James Macbeth, a young man from a lower social class who works on the family estate. However, Kitty is not interested in marrying James and instead becomes infatuated with him, which leads to a tumultuous relationship.

As Kitty's obsession with James grows, she begins to manipulate him into committing adultery with her. She also starts to take control of his actions, using her wit and cunning to push him towards more extreme behavior. Meanwhile, Sir Malcolm is struggling with his own demons, including his wife's illness and his own feelings of guilt and responsibility.

As the story unfolds, Kitty's behavior becomes increasingly erratic and manipulative, leading James to commit a murder on their wedding night. The film then shifts its focus to James, who is now haunted by the consequences of his actions. He becomes trapped in a cycle of guilt and paranoia, unable to escape the darkness that has consumed him.

Throughout the film, Oldroyd explores themes of mental illness, class, and the destructive nature of unchecked ambition. Kitty's character is particularly noteworthy, as she embodies both the societal expectations placed upon women during this time period and her own desires for autonomy and power.

The film's climax features a dramatic confrontation between James and his wife, who has become increasingly unhinged due to her own mental health issues. The ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience to ponder the fate of the characters and the consequences of their actions.

Overall, Lady Macbeth is a haunting and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of human psychology and the destructive nature of unchecked ambition. Florence Pugh's performance as Kitty Clark is particularly noteworthy, capturing the character's complexity and nuance with remarkable depth and sensitivity.

overview: A student's premonition of a deadly rollercoaster ride saves her life and a lucky few, but not from death itself – which seeks out those who escaped their fate.
production_companies: Kumar Mobiliengesellschaft mbH & Co. Projekt Nr. 1 KG
tagline: This ride will be the death of you.
title: Final Destination 3
plot:
Final Destination 3 is a supernatural horror film directed by James Wong, released in 2006 by New Line Cinema.

The movie begins with Clear Rivers (Mary Elizabeth Winstead), a high school student who survives a roller coaster accident at an amusement park. She had been warned not to get on the ride by her friend, Kevin Williamson (Ryan Merriman), but she ignored him. As a result of this warning, Clear is haunted by premonitions and visions of death.

Clear's friends, including her boyfriend, Wexler (Chad Donella), and her friends from school, are also at the amusement park on the same day as Clear. However, they all die in a series of gruesome accidents, which Clear tries to prevent using her knowledge of impending doom.

The first accident occurs when Wexler is crushed by a falling roller coaster car. The second accident happens when Kevin's girlfriend, Clear's friend, is killed by a malfunctioning funhouse ride. The third accident involves a group of teenagers who are trapped in a burning amusement park building.

As the accidents continue to occur, Clear realizes that she has the ability to see and prevent these events from happening. However, each time she tries to warn her friends or take action to prevent an accident, something goes wrong, and they still die.

Clear becomes increasingly isolated as she struggles to understand why her warnings are not being heeded. She also starts to question whether she is truly able to change the course of events or if she is just seeing things that will inevitably happen.

In the end, Clear realizes that she has been given a chance to cheat death and escape the cycle of premonitions. However, in doing so, she must confront her own mortality and make a choice between saving herself or trying to save others.

The movie ends with Clear escaping the amusement park by jumping off a bridge just as it is about to collapse. She then watches from a distance as the bridge implodes, killing everyone on board. The film concludes with Clear reflecting on the events that have transpired and wondering if she has truly escaped death or if there are still more premonitions waiting for her.

Overall, Final Destination 3 explores themes of mortality, fate, and the consequences of ignoring warnings from others. The movie's twist ending adds to the suspense and surprise, leaving viewers questioning what is real and what is just a product of Clear's imagination.

original_title: 東京ゴッドファーザーズ
overview: On Christmas Eve, three homeless people living on the streets of Tokyo discover a newborn baby among the trash and set out to find its parents.
tagline: Meet the ultimate dysfunctional family.
title: Tokyo Godfathers
plot:
Tokyo Godfathers is a 2003 Japanese animated film directed by Takashi Miike, produced by Shunzo Kikuta, and distributed by Toei Animation. The movie was not produced by dentsu.

The main themes of Tokyo Godfthers include:

1. Redemption: The story revolves around three homeless people who find an abandoned baby girl on Christmas Eve. As they care for her, they undergo a transformation, learning to let go of their past mistakes and finding redemption.
2. Family: The film explores the concept of family in unexpected ways, highlighting the importance of human connection and relationships. The main characters form an unconventional family unit, showing that family can be found in the most unlikely places.
3. Social commentary: Tokyo Godfathers critiques Japan's social issues, such as homelessness, poverty, and loneliness. The film sheds light on the struggles faced by marginalized communities and encourages empathy and understanding.
4. Christmas spirit: The movie is set during Christmas, a time often associated with joy and giving. However, the story also touches on the darker aspects of human nature, making it a more nuanced exploration of the holiday season.

The plot begins with three homeless people, Hana, Ganta, and Boris, who spend Christmas Eve wandering the streets of Tokyo. They stumble upon an abandoned baby girl in a stroller, which sets off a chain of events that changes their lives forever. As they care for the child, they confront their past mistakes and learn to work together, forming an unlikely family unit.

The story develops as Hana, Ganta, and Boris face various challenges, including run-ins with corrupt authorities, rival gangs, and personal demons. Along the way, they discover that the baby girl is actually a magical being who has been sent to Earth to bring people together.

In the end, the three main characters find redemption through their experiences with the baby girl, learning valuable lessons about love, compassion, and the importance of human connection. The film concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that even in the darkest of times, there is always the possibility for transformation and renewal.

original_title: Sofia the First: Once Upon a Princess
overview: Set in the storybook world of Enchancia, the music-filled movie follows Sofia, an average girl whose life suddenly changes when her mother marries the king and she is whisked off to live in a castle with her mom, new step-father, King Roland II, and step-siblings, Amber and James. Along the way this ordinary girl learns to navigate the extraordinary life of royalty, and in the process makes everyone around her feel special.
title: Sofia the First: Once Upon a Princess
plot:
Sofia the First: Once Upon a Princess is a 2012 animated film that serves as a prequel to the popular TV series Sofia the First. The movie follows the story of young Sofia, who is about to turn 16 and become a princess.

The main themes of the movie include:

1. Self-discovery: As Sofia prepares for her royal duties, she must also navigate her own identity and figure out what it means to be a princess. She struggles with the idea of giving up her childhood and embracing her new responsibilities.
2. Friendship: The movie highlights the importance of friendship and loyalty, particularly between Sofia and her animal friends, such as Clover the rabbit and Miranda the pig.
3. Responsibility: As Sofia takes on more royal duties, she learns to accept responsibility for her actions and make decisions that benefit others.
4. Growing up: The film explores the challenges of growing up and transitioning from childhood to adulthood. Sofia must confront the idea that she can no longer be a carefree child and learn to adapt to new expectations.

The movie features beautiful animation, engaging characters, and a heartwarming story that sets the stage for the rest of the series. Overall, Once Upon a Princess is a delightful film that celebrates the importance of friendship, responsibility, and self-discovery.

overview: Mystery, Inc. heads to Blowout Beach for a real swinging beach party when the Ghost Pirates threaten to harsh the good vibes.
title: LEGO Scooby-Doo! Blowout Beach Bash
plot:
LEGO Scooby-Doo! Blowout Beach Bash is a 2017 animated mystery-comedy film that revolves around the popular LEGO Scooby-Doo franchise. The movie follows the Mystery Inc. gang - Fred, Daphne, Velma, Shaggy, and Scooby - as they arrive at the Beach Blast amusement park for a summer vacation.

The main themes of the movie include:

1. Friendship: The film highlights the strong bond between the members of the Mystery Inc. gang, showcasing their teamwork, loyalty, and trust in each other.
2. Teamwork: Each member of the gang brings their unique skills to solve the mystery, demonstrating the importance of collaboration and diverse perspectives.
3. Loyalty: Shaggy's unwavering dedication to Scooby is a central theme, as well as Velma's commitment to uncovering the truth, even when it puts her at odds with others.
4. Deception and Appearance vs Reality: The movie features various characters who hide behind masks or pretend to be someone they're not, highlighting the tension between appearance and reality.

The plot develops around a series of mysterious events at Beach Blast, including ghostly apparitions, treasure hunts, and sabotage. As the gang works together to unravel the mystery, they uncover a sinister plot involving a rival amusement park owner who seeks to destroy Beach Blast and gain control over its assets.

Ultimately, the Mystery Inc. gang exposes the truth behind the rival's plan, saving Beach Blast and restoring order to the community. The movie concludes with the gang enjoying a well-deserved victory celebration at the beach, emphasizing their camaraderie and shared sense of accomplishment.

Overall, LEGO Scooby-Doo! Blowout Beach Bash is an entertaining film that balances humor, mystery, and heart, making it a delightful addition to the LEGO Scooby-Doo franchise.

overview: An unnamed doctor has always had everything he's ever wanted, but that has only made him develop more extreme and depraved needs. He kidnaps a young couple in the prime of their life together and forces them into a game of torment that slowly extinguishes their hopes for survival.
tagline: King of Japanese Grotesque Movie
title: Grotesque
plot:
Grotesque (Japanese: Gurotesuku) is a 2009 Japanese exploitation horror film written and directed by Kōji Shiraishi, starring Hiroaki Kawatsure, Tsugumi Nagasawa and Shigeo Ōsako. Made on a small budget, it became one of the most notorious entries in the so-called torture horror cycle of the late 2000s, and it gained international attention when the British Board of Film Classification refused to certify it for release in the United Kingdom, judging that its sadistic content offered little beyond the infliction of pain and humiliation.

The plot is deliberately minimal. A young couple, Aki and Kazuo, are snatched from the street during their very first date and wake up restrained in a basement whose walls are covered in plastic sheeting. Their captor, a calm and well-dressed man, offers no explanation for what he is doing. Over a long series of scenes he subjects them to escalating physical abuse, sexual degradation and mutilation, forcing each to witness the suffering of the other. It eventually emerges that he is driven purely by his own gratification and by a twisted fascination with how people cling to life and to one another under extreme pain.

In a sudden change of tone, the captor moves the couple to a clean, hospital-like room, treats their injuries and reveals that he is a wealthy and respected physician. He promises that once they recover they will be released, that he will surrender to the police and that they will receive his fortune as compensation. Left alone, Aki and Kazuo vow to stay together after their ordeal. The promise proves to be another cruel game, and the couple are returned to the basement for a final round of torment that pushes the film toward a gruesome and bleakly absurd conclusion.

Shiraishi, previously known for found-footage horror such as Noroi: The Curse, shot the film with a stark, clinical style and a running time of little more than an hour, concentrating almost entirely on the three characters. Critical response was sharply divided. Variety gave a lukewarm review, acknowledging the committed acting and solid production values while finding the special effects uneven and the over-the-top finale more likely to provoke laughter than dread. Some horror outlets praised its audacity, while others dismissed it as pointless shock cinema.

original_title: The Wonderful Summer of Mickey Mouse
overview: Mickey Mouse and his friends each recall the wild events leading up to the Annual Summer Fireworks Spectacular from their point-of-view.
title: The Wonderful Summer of Mickey Mouse
plot:
The Wonderful Summer of Mickey Mouse is a 2022 American animated television special produced by Disney Television Animation for the streaming service Disney+. It is the third of four seasonal specials forming the second season of The Wonderful World of Mickey Mouse, following the winter and spring editions, and unlike its predecessors tells a single story rather than presenting separate shorts. It was directed and written by Karl Hadrika, Eddie Trigueros, Jason Reicher and Kristen Morrison, with writers including Paul Rudish, Darrick Bachman, William Reiss, Nick Lauer, Stevie Borbolla and Ricky Roxburgh. The voice cast features Chris Diamantopoulos as Mickey Mouse, Kaitlyn Robrock as Minnie Mouse, Tony Anselmo as Donald Duck, Tress MacNeille as Daisy Duck and Bill Farmer as Goofy. The special premiered on Disney+ on 8 July 2022 and runs about 22 minutes.

As Mickey races his boat to the marina for the town's annual Summer Spectacular fireworks show, a helicopter, a car and a luxury yacht all converge with him on the floating fireworks barge, which is destroyed. The Mayor, the Walrus from Alice in Wonderland, demands to know who is responsible, and each of the five friends tells their side of the story, beginning with a group call Mickey made at 2 a.m. to plan the day. Determined to get a perfect spot, Mickey dreamed of arriving early but overslept until 4 p.m. Minnie overloaded her car with double of everything, from pies to melting ice cream, until soda and mints launched it into the sky. Daisy, resolved to arrive exactly on time, woke to find her car crushed in her driveway and finally commandeered Scrooge McDuck's yacht. Donald, who had stayed up building a helicopter to take Daisy to the show, accidentally dropped it onto her car before crashing towards the barge, and Goofy had been camped beside the barge all along. Realising that they all share the blame, the friends work together to stage an improvised spectacular for their neighbours.

Jeremy Brown of What's On Disney Plus gave the special two and a half stars, calling it his least favourite of the seasonal specials so far and wishing for several summer stories rather than a recap of a single day, though he praised the animation and moments such as Donald destroying Daisy's car. Alex Reif of Laughing Place found it a lot of fun despite fewer Easter eggs than its predecessors, noting cameos including Chuuby from Mickey and Minnie's Runaway Railway, Snow White's forest friends and Clarabelle Cow.

overview: After her fiance is falsely imprisoned, a pregnant African-American woman sets out to clear his name and prove his innocence.
tagline: Trust Love All The Way
title: If Beale Street Could Talk
plot:
If Beale Street Could Talk is a poignant and powerful film that delves into the complexities of love, racism, and redemption in 1970s Harlem. The movie tells the story of Tish Rivers, a young black woman who falls deeply in love with Fonny, a young man from her neighborhood. Their love is strong, but their world is fraught with danger.

The film explores the theme of systemic racism and its devastating impact on the lives of African Americans. The police brutality and injustice that Fonny faces serve as a stark reminder of the deep-seated racial tensions that pervade the community. Through Tish's narrative, we see how these injustices can destroy lives and relationships, leaving scars that may never fully heal.

At the same time, If Beale Street Could Talk is also a film about the transformative power of love. Tish's unwavering devotion to Fonny serves as a beacon of hope in a world that seems determined to tear them apart. The movie shows how love can be both a source of strength and a vulnerability, as Tish's love for Fonny becomes her greatest asset and her most painful loss.

The film also touches on the theme of redemption, as Tish seeks justice for Fonny's wrongful conviction. Her determination to clear his name is driven by her love for him, but it also speaks to a deeper desire to right the wrongs of the past and create a more just future.

Throughout the movie, the director Barry Jenkins weaves together themes of identity, community, and resilience, creating a rich tapestry that celebrates the beauty and complexity of black life in America. If Beale Street Could Talk is a powerful exploration of the human experience, one that will leave audiences moved, thought-provoking, and perhaps even changed.

overview: A young Englishman marries a glamorous American. When he brings her home to meet the parents, she arrives like a blast from the future - blowing their entrenched British stuffiness out the window.
tagline: Let's Misbehave!
title: Easy Virtue
plot:
Easy Virtue is a 2008 romantic comedy film that explores the complexities of relationships, social class, and personal identity. The movie follows the story of Lanier, a charming but aimless young man who becomes infatuated with his cousin's fiancée, Lady Victoria, despite her seemingly shallow and materialistic nature.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Lady Victoria is hiding a more vulnerable side beneath her polished exterior. Through their interactions, the film reveals themes of societal pressure, the constraints of social class, and the struggle for individuality in the face of external expectations.

The movie also delves into the tension between appearance and reality, as characters navigate the complexities of relationships and personal growth. The film's portrayal of a seemingly perfect facade hiding underlying insecurities and flaws adds depth to its exploration of these themes.

Ultimately, Easy Virtue is a nuanced commentary on the human experience, highlighting the challenges of navigating complex social dynamics, the importance of self-discovery, and the power of genuine connection in transcending superficial boundaries.

overview: Jimmy Neutron is a boy genius and way ahead of his friends, but when it comes to being cool, he's a little behind. All until one day when his parents, and parents all over Earth are kidnapped by aliens, it's up to him to lead all the children of the world to rescue their parents.
tagline: He may be small, but he's got a big brain!
title: Jimmy Neutron: Boy Genius
plot:
Jimmy Neutron: Boy Genius is a 2001 animated science fiction comedy film that explores several thought-provoking themes. At its core, the movie delves into the consequences of unchecked ambition and the importance of responsibility.

The main character, Jimmy Neutron, is a brilliant and eccentric boy genius who often finds himself in absurd situations due to his own inventions and actions. As he navigates his way through adolescence, Jimmy must confront the darker aspects of his own personality and learn to balance his desire for recognition and control with empathy and compassion towards others.

One of the primary themes of the film is the struggle between individuality and conformity. Jimmy's unique talents and perspectives often lead him to challenge the status quo, but this also puts him at odds with those around him who are more willing to conform to societal norms. This tension serves as a backdrop for exploring the complexities of growing up and finding one's place in the world.

Another significant theme present in the movie is the power of friendship and loyalty. Despite his eccentricities, Jimmy forms strong bonds with his best friends, Carl and Sheen, who help him navigate the challenges he faces. The film highlights the importance of having supportive relationships and learning to rely on others when needed.

The movie also touches on the theme of responsibility and accountability. As Jimmy's inventions often spiral out of control, he must confront the consequences of his actions and learn to take responsibility for his mistakes. This serves as a valuable lesson in teaching children (and adults alike) about the importance of considering the potential impact of their decisions.

Overall, Jimmy Neutron: Boy Genius is a film that uses humor and satire to explore complex themes and ideas, making it an engaging and entertaining watch for audiences of all ages.

overview: Based on a shocking true story, Killer Elite pits two of the world’s most elite operatives—Danny, an ex-special ops agent and Hunter, his longtime mentor—against the cunning leader of a secret military society. Covering the globe from Australia to Paris, London and the Middle East, Danny and Hunter are plunged into a highly dangerous game of cat and mouse—where the predators become the prey.
tagline: May the best man live.
title: Killer Elite
plot:
Killer Elite is a 2011 action spy thriller film directed by Gary McKendry and starring Jason Statham, Clive Owen, and Dominic Cooper.

The story begins with Daniel Oxford (Clive Owen), an assassin who works for the British Secret Intelligence Service (MI6). Oxford is betrayed by his employer and left for dead in the desert. He manages to survive and seeks revenge against those responsible for his betrayal.

Years later, Oxford is found by a wealthy businessman named Sir Miles (Tom Wilkinson) who hires him for a high-stakes mission: to assassinate David Hunter (Dominic Cooper), a former MI6 agent turned mercenary. The target is a rogue operative who has stolen a deadly virus from the British government.

Oxford accepts the job, but things become complicated when he discovers that his employer's true intentions are not what they seem. He also meets Dan (Jason Statham), an old friend and fellow assassin who was thought to be dead. Dan is now working for a mysterious organization known as The Syndicate, which seems to have its own agenda.

As Oxford delves deeper into the mission, he uncovers a web of deceit and betrayal that goes all the way to the top. He must use his skills and cunning to stay one step ahead of his enemies and complete his objective.

Meanwhile, Dan is also on the hunt for Hunter, who has stolen a deadly virus that could be used to wipe out millions of people. The two former friends engage in a cat-and-mouse game, with Oxford trying to take down Hunter while also navigating the complex web of allegiances and rivalries within The Syndicate.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Sir Miles is not what he seems, and that his true intentions are far more sinister than initially thought. Oxford must use all his skills and resources to stay alive and complete his mission, while also confronting the dark secrets of his own past.

The film's climax features an intense showdown between Oxford and Hunter, with Dan caught in the middle. In the end, Oxford emerges victorious, but not without scars and a newfound understanding of the true nature of The Syndicate.

Throughout the film, the action is fast-paced and intense, with plenty of twists and turns to keep viewers on the edge of their seats. The cast delivers strong performances, with Statham and Owen bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

original_title: 新世紀エヴァンゲリオン劇場版 Air／まごころを、君に
overview: The second of two theatrically released follow-ups to the Neon Genesis Evangelion series. Comprising of two alternate episodes which were first intended to take the place of episodes 25 and 26, this finale answers many of the questions surrounding the series, while also opening up some new possibilities.
tagline: The fate of destruction is also the joy of rebirth
title: Neon Genesis Evangelion: The End of Evangelion
plot:
Neon Genesis Evangelion: The End of Evangelion is a 96-minute anime film directed by Hideaki Anno, released in 1997. It serves as the final installment of the Neon Genesis Evangelion series and concludes the story of Shinji Ikari, a young boy who pilots the giant humanoid robot Evangelion Unit-01.

The film begins with Shinji, still reeling from the events of the previous episodes, struggling to cope with his emotional trauma. He is visited by Rei Ayanami, a mysterious and enigmatic being who has been a central figure in the series. Rei's presence serves as a catalyst for Shinji's introspection, and he begins to question his own identity and purpose.

As the story unfolds, Shinji becomes increasingly entangled with Asuka Langley Soryu, a rival pilot of Evangelion Unit-02. Their interactions are marked by tension and conflict, reflecting their deep-seated emotional scars. Meanwhile, the organization NERV, led by Gendo Ikari (Shinji's father), continues to pursue its goals of using the Evangelions to bring about human evolution.

The plot thickens as Shinji discovers a series of cryptic messages from his mother, Yui Ikari, who had been presumed dead. These messages reveal that she was involved in NERV's research and that her death was not what it seemed. This revelation sets off a chain reaction of events that lead to the climax of the film.

The final act of the movie is marked by an intense and surreal sequence of events. Shinji, Asuka, and Rei find themselves trapped in a series of nightmarish scenarios, each representing a different aspect of their psyches. These sequences are intercut with scenes of the Evangelions engaging in battle against monstrous creatures known as Angels.

As the story reaches its conclusion, Shinji is forced to confront his deepest fears and insecurities. He ultimately comes to terms with his own identity and finds a sense of acceptance and belonging. The film's ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience to ponder the meaning and significance of the events that have transpired.

Throughout the film, Anno explores themes of existentialism, psychological trauma, and the human condition. The movie's abstract and often surreal narrative style adds to its complexity and depth, making it a thought-provoking and emotionally resonant conclusion to the Neon Genesis Evangelion series.

Ultimately, Neon Genesis Evangelion: The End of Evangelion is a powerful and haunting film that challenges viewers to confront their own emotions and insecurities. Its exploration of complex themes and abstract narrative style have made it a cult classic and a staple of anime fandom.

overview: A group of teens break into a blind man's home thinking they'll get away with the perfect crime. They're wrong.
tagline: In the dark the blind man is king.
title: Don't Breathe
plot:
Don't Breathe is a 2016 American horror-thriller film directed by Fede Alvarez and written by Alvarez and Rodo Sayagues. The movie follows three young friends, Rocky (Daniel Radcliffe), Bo (Jesse Plemons), and Manco (Yul Vazquez), who plan to break into the house of blind veteran Mr. Gray (James Remar) in a working-class neighborhood.

The story begins with Rocky, a struggling artist, who is forced to move back in with his mother after losing his job. He comes up with a plan to break into Mr. Gray's house and steal some cash that he believes the old man has hidden away. Bo and Manco agree to help him with the heist.

As they approach Mr. Gray's house, they notice that it is surrounded by a high wall and has no visible signs of life. They decide to use a ventilation shaft to gain access to the house. Once inside, they find that Mr. Gray is not only blind but also extremely skilled in self-defense.

Initially, the trio manages to evade Mr. Gray's defenses and steal some cash from his safe. However, things take a turn for the worse when Rocky discovers that Mr. Gray has been waiting for them all along. Despite being blind, Mr. Gray uses his other senses to track down the intruders and set up an elaborate trap.

As the night progresses, the group finds themselves in a desperate fight for survival. Bo is killed by Mr. Gray's booby traps, while Manco is severely injured. Rocky manages to escape with his life but not without realizing that he has underestimated Mr. Gray's abilities.

Throughout the movie, Alvarez uses tension and suspense to create a sense of unease in the audience. The film's score, composed by Tom Spezialy, adds to the tension, creating an atmosphere of dread and fear.

In the end, Rocky manages to outsmart Mr. Gray and escape from his house. However, he is left with a newfound respect for the old man and a realization that some people are capable of more than we think. The movie ends on a somber note, leaving the audience to ponder the true nature of Mr. Gray's abilities and the consequences of underestimating others.

Overall, Don't Breathe is a tense and suspenseful horror-thriller that explores themes of vulnerability, trust, and the power of the human mind. The film features strong performances from its cast, particularly Daniel Radcliffe, who brings depth and nuance to his character.

overview: In 1967, during the making of “La Chinoise,” film director Jean-Luc Godard falls in love with 19-year-old actress Anne Wiazemsky and marries her.
tagline: This movie is a “stupid, stupid idea.”
title: Godard Mon Amour
plot:
Godard Mon Amour, released in France as Le Redoutable (Redoubtable), is a 2017 French biographical comedy-drama written and directed by Michel Hazanavicius, adapted from Un an après, Anne Wiazemsky's 2015 memoir. Louis Garrel plays the filmmaker Jean-Luc Godard and Stacy Martin plays Wiazemsky, while the supporting cast includes Bérénice Bejo (Michèle Rosier), Micha Lescot (Jean-Pierre Bamberger), Grégory Gadebois (Michel Cournot) and Guido Caprino (Bernardo Bertolucci). Structured in nine chapters with an epilogue, the film playfully imitates Godard's own techniques, including black-and-white passages, voice-over, characters addressing the camera, title cards and ironic subtitles.

In Paris in 1967, Godard, the celebrated 37-year-old figurehead of the French New Wave, falls in love with the 20-year-old Anne while directing her in La Chinoise, and asks her to marry him on the day the radio reports news of the submarine Le Redoutable. His growing commitment to Maoism shapes his work, but the film is rejected by the Chinese embassy and poorly received by critics and audiences. A year later the events of May 1968 erupt. Godard joins the often violent street protests, is pestered by fans who want him to return to lighter films such as Breathless and Pierrot le Fou, is shouted down at the occupied Sorbonne and mocked in graffiti, and meets the same scorn at a conference in Rome hosted by Bertolucci. He and friends travel to the Cannes Film Festival, which they help shut down in solidarity with the strikes, and then find themselves stranded without fuel during the general strike.

Back in Paris, Godard founds the Dziga Vertov Group with Jean-Pierre Gorin to make radical political cinema, but he becomes increasingly isolated, accused by others of being incomprehensible. As Anne pursues her own acting career, their marriage deteriorates and Godard attempts suicide with an overdose. Anne falls out of love, and they separate during the collective shoot of Wind from the East, where Godard is confronted with his own contradictions.

Produced by Les Compagnons du Cinéma with Wild Bunch and France 3 Cinéma and photographed by Guillaume Schiffman, the film premiered in competition for the Palme d'Or at the 2017 Cannes Film Festival. Reviews were mixed, with a Rotten Tomatoes approval rating of 54% and a Metacritic score of 55.

overview: A group of National Guard trainees find themselves battling against a vicious group of mutants on their last day of training in the desert.
tagline: Help isn't coming.
title: The Hills Have Eyes 2
plot:
The Hills Have Eyes 2 is a 2007 American horror film directed by Martin Weisz and written by Chris Bowers, Seth Grahame-Smith, and Robert Ben Garant. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1977 film of the same name.

The story begins with a group of teenagers who are on a road trip from California to New Mexico. They stop at a roadside diner where they meet a mysterious woman named Ethel (played by Ted Levine), who claims that she is a member of a family that has lived in the desert for generations. She warns them about the dangers of the area, but they dismiss her warnings and continue on their journey.

As night falls, the group becomes lost in the desert due to a GPS malfunction. They stumble upon an abandoned mine shaft, where they decide to take shelter for the night. Unbeknownst to them, this is the same mine shaft where the original Hills Have Eyes family was brutally murdered by the mutants.

The next morning, the group discovers that Ethel's warnings were not just mere superstition. The mutants have been awakened and are now hunting them down one by one. As the group tries to survive and find their way back to civilization, they realize that the mutants are not just mindless beasts but also seem to be driven by a twisted sense of family loyalty.

As the body count rises, the remaining survivors must confront the harsh reality of their situation. They soon discover that Ethel's family has been living in the desert for generations and have developed a unique culture that is both fascinating and terrifying.

The movie takes a dark turn as the group discovers that the mutants are not just random creatures but also seem to be connected to Ethel's family. The survivors must now confront their own mortality and the true nature of the monsters they are facing.

In the end, only one member of the group manages to escape the clutches of the mutants. As she flees into the desert, she is met with a shocking revelation: Ethel's family has been watching her from the shadows, waiting for her to join their twisted community.

The Hills Have Eyes 2 received mixed reviews from critics but was praised for its gruesome and unsettling atmosphere. The movie's use of practical effects and its willingness to push boundaries made it a standout in the horror genre. However, some critics felt that the movie's plot was predictable and that the characters were underdeveloped.

Overall, The Hills Have Eyes 2 is a tense and unsettling horror film that explores themes of survival, family, and the dangers of the desert. While it may not be as iconic as its predecessor, it remains a solid addition to the Hills Have Eyes franchise.

overview: The Argentine, begins as Che and a band of Cuban exiles (led by Fidel Castro) reach the Cuban shore from Mexico in 1956. Within two years, they mobilized popular support and an army and toppled the U.S.-friendly regime of dictator Fulgencio Batista.
tagline: The revolution made him a legend.
title: Che: Part One
plot:
Che: Part One is a 2008 biographical drama film directed by Steven Soderbergh, based on the life of Ernesto "Che" Guevara, an Argentine Marxist revolutionary. The movie focuses on Che's early years and his involvement in the Cuban Revolution.

The main themes of Che: Part One include:

1. **Revolution and Social Change**: The film explores Che's transformation from a middle-class medical student to a radical revolutionary, driven by his desire for social justice and equality.
2. **Identity and Self-Discovery**: As Che navigates different ideologies and environments, he struggles with his own identity, questioning the values of capitalism and imperialism, and ultimately finding his place in the world as a Marxist revolutionary.
3. **Friendship and Loyalty**: The movie highlights the strong bonds between Che and his friends, including Alberto Granado (played by Benicio del Toro), who becomes his closest companion on his journey to Bolivia.
4. **Class Struggle and Economic Inequality**: Che's experiences in Argentina and Bolivia expose him to the harsh realities of poverty and inequality, fueling his desire for radical change and social reform.
5. **Personal Sacrifice and Morality**: As Che becomes increasingly involved in revolutionary activities, he must confront the moral implications of his actions, including the use of violence and the potential consequences for himself and others.

Throughout the film, Sodergham employs a non-linear narrative structure, jumping between different periods of Che's life to convey the complexity and depth of his experiences. The movie ultimately sets the stage for Part Two, which explores Che's involvement in the Cuban Revolution and his rise as a key figure in Fidel Castro's government.

Overall, Che: Part One is a thought-provoking exploration of one man's journey from idealism to radical activism, raising important questions about identity, morality, and the complexities of revolution.

overview: In an attempt to free himself from a state of forgotten limbo, evil dream-demon Freddy Krueger devises a plan to manipulate un-dead mass murderer Jason Voorhees  into slicing-and-dicing his way through the teenage population of Springwood.  But when the master of dreams loses control of his monster, a brutal fight to the death is the only way out.
tagline: Evil will battle evil.
title: Freddy vs. Jason
plot:
Freddy vs. Jason is a 2003 American horror film directed by Ronny Yu and written by Damian Shannon and Mark Swift. The movie is a crossover between two popular horror franchises: A Nightmare on Elm Street and Friday the 13th.

The film begins with Freddy Krueger (Robert Englund), the dream demon from Springwood, Ohio, who has been trapped in a magical realm known as the "Dream World" for over 25 years. However, due to a series of events, Freddy is able to escape and enter the real world, where he finds himself in Crystal Lake, New Jersey.

Meanwhile, Jason Voorhees (Ken Kirzinger), the masked killer from Camp Crystal Lake, has also escaped his own realm and entered the real world. The two horror icons soon discover that they are being hunted by a group of teenagers who are trying to survive their encounters with both Freddy and Jason.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Freddy is using his powers to manipulate the dreams of the teenagers, while Jason is using his brute strength to terrorize them in the real world. The two horror icons engage in a series of battles, with Freddy using his claws and wit to try and outsmart Jason, who relies on his physical strength to overpower his opponents.

As the body count rises, the teenagers begin to realize that they are being manipulated by both Freddy and Jason, who are working together to eliminate them. The group soon discovers that the only way to stop both horror icons is to find a way to destroy their respective realms and trap them back in their own worlds.

In the climactic final battle, the teenagers use a magical artifact known as the "Dream Crystal" to create a portal between the Dream World and the real world. Freddy and Jason are drawn into the portal, where they engage in an epic battle that takes place within both the dream and reality realms.

Ultimately, the teenagers emerge victorious, but not without sustaining significant injuries. As the dust settles, it becomes clear that Freddy has been defeated, but at a great cost: he is trapped in the Dream World, unable to escape. Jason, on the other hand, returns to his own realm, where he will continue to terrorize Camp Crystal Lake.

The film ends with a sense of closure for both horror franchises, as the surviving teenagers reflect on their harrowing experiences and the lessons they learned about facing their fears. While Freddy vs. Jason received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, it has since become a cult classic among horror fans, who appreciate its campy humor, over-the-top violence, and nostalgic value.

Overall, Freddy vs. Jason is a fun and entertaining crossover film that brings together two beloved horror franchises in a way that is both faithful to their respective worlds and fresh enough to feel new.

overview: A reformed hunter becomes involved in a deadly game of cat and mouse when he and the local sheriff set out to track a vicious killer who may have kidnapped his daughter years ago.
title: The Silencing
plot:
The Silencing is a 2020 action thriller directed by Robin Pront from a screenplay by Micah Ranum. It stars Nikolaj Coster-Waldau and Annabelle Wallis, with Hero Fiennes Tiffin, Zahn McClarnon and Melanie Scrofano in supporting roles. Saban Films released it through DirecTV Cinema in July 2020, followed by a theatrical and video-on-demand release in August 2020.

Coster-Waldau plays Rayburn Swanson, a former hunter and recovering alcoholic who now runs a wildlife sanctuary in the forests of northern Minnesota. He named it after his daughter Gwen, who disapproved of his trapping and who vanished five years earlier from his car while he stepped into a store to buy whiskey. The sanctuary is his form of penance, and he patrols it with surveillance cameras to keep hunters away. Wallis plays Alice Gustafson, the local sheriff, who also has to deal with her volatile younger brother Brooks.

When the body of a young girl is found near a lake, Alice notices a distinctive scar on the victim's throat and recovers the head of a spear from a nearby tree, a projectile launched with an atlatl, an ancient throwing device. Rayburn rushes to view the body, fearing it is Gwen, but it is not. Soon afterwards he spots a figure in a ghillie suit moving through the woods and is wounded by a thrown spear when he tries to intervene. Reviewing his camera footage, he discovers that the masked hunter has been using the sanctuary to stalk and kill abducted girls. He rescues one survivor, Molly, who has been left mute by the same throat injury, and the case draws him and Alice together as the investigation points closer to people they know.

The story becomes a cat-and-mouse thriller in the wilderness, in which Rayburn's tracking skills are pitted against a killer who knows the terrain just as well, while Alice wrestles with suspicions that touch her own family. The film combines a serial-killer mystery with a portrait of a grieving father who refuses to give up on finding his child.

Reviews were largely negative. On Rotten Tomatoes the film holds an approval rating of about 20 percent, with the consensus arguing that it mistakes mood for character development and delivers an undercooked mystery, although some critics praised Coster-Waldau's committed lead performance and the bleak, wintry atmosphere.

overview: Pleasantly plump teenager Tracy Turnblad auditions to be on Baltimore's most popular dance show - The Corny Collins Show - and lands a prime spot. Through her newfound fame, she becomes determined to help her friends and end the racial segregation that has been a staple of the show.
tagline: When you follow your own beat, the world will follow you.
title: Hairspray
plot:
Hairspray (2007) is a musical romantic comedy film directed by Adam Shankman, produced by John Debney Productions, and distributed by New Line Cinema.

The main themes of Hairspray include:

1. **Racial Integration and Equality**: The movie tackles the issue of racial segregation in 1960s Baltimore, where African Americans are not allowed to dance on local TV shows. The story follows Tracy Turnblad, a plus-sized teenager who dreams of dancing on the popular show "The Corny Collins Show." Her determination leads to a breakthrough in racial integration and equality.

2. **Body Positivity**: Hairspray promotes self-acceptance and body positivity through its protagonist, Tracy Turnblad. The film challenges traditional beauty standards by showcasing a plus-sized woman who finds success and happiness despite societal expectations.

3. **Friendship and Loyalty**: The movie highlights the importance of friendship and loyalty, particularly between Tracy and her friends Link Larkin and Seaweed Stubbs. Their bond helps them navigate the challenges they face in their pursuit of racial integration and personal growth.

4. **Social Change and Activism**: Hairspray encourages viewers to think about social change and activism. The film's portrayal of the Civil Rights Movement and its impact on American society serves as a powerful reminder of the importance of standing up for what is right, even in the face of adversity.

5. **Self-Expression and Individuality**: The movie celebrates self-expression and individuality through its colorful characters, music, and dance numbers. Hairspray encourages viewers to be true to themselves and express their unique qualities, rather than conforming to societal norms.

Overall, Hairspray (2007) is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores themes of racial integration, body positivity, friendship, social change, and self-expression, making it a beloved classic among audiences.

overview: When a down-to-earth Chicago baker and a soon-to-be princess discover they look like twins, they hatch a Christmastime plan to trade places.
title: The Princess Switch
plot:
The Princess Switch is a 2018 American Christmas romantic comedy film directed by Mike Rohl and written by Jennifer Kaytin Robinson. The movie stars Vanessa Hudgens, Sam Palladio, and Nick Sagar.

The story revolves around Stacy DeNovo (Vanessa Hudgens), a talented baker who lives in San Francisco with her twin sister, Marguerite (also played by Vanessa Hudgens). The twins were separated at birth, but they share the same birthday and have been raised to be identical in every way. However, their lives take different paths as adults.

Stacy is engaged to a wealthy tech entrepreneur named Kevin Doyle (Sam Palladio), while Marguerite is a princess from the European country of Belgravia, who has been living in San Francisco under an assumed identity. The twist is that Marguerite is actually Princess Beatrice of Belgravia, and she's been hiding her royal status to experience life as a normal person.

When Stacy learns about the upcoming Christmas festivities in Belgravia, she decides to attend on behalf of Kevin, who has invited her to join him for the holiday season. Unbeknownst to Stacy, Marguerite is also attending the same event, and they meet at a royal ball where they engage in a series of comedic misunderstandings.

As Stacy and Marguerite spend more time together, they begin to develop feelings for each other, but their identities are threatened when Kevin arrives in Belgravia. Meanwhile, Marguerite's royal duties and responsibilities come into play, causing tension between her and Stacy.

Throughout the movie, the twins navigate their complicated relationships with each other and with those around them. They must confront their own identities and figure out what they truly want from life. In the end, Stacy and Marguerite realize that they have fallen in love with each other, but they also understand that their lives are not meant to be together.

The movie ends on a heartwarming note, with Stacy and Marguerite embracing their true feelings for each other and finding happiness as themselves, rather than trying to fit into someone else's mold. The film concludes with a romantic kiss between the two women, symbolizing their newfound love and acceptance of who they are.

Overall, The Princess Switch is a lighthearted, feel-good movie that explores themes of identity, love, and self-acceptance. With its witty dialogue, charming performances, and festive holiday setting, it's a delightful watch for audiences looking for a fun and romantic Christmas treat.

overview: Cold War spy Greville Wynne and his Russian source try to put an end to the Cuban Missile Crisis.
tagline: Based on the incredible true story of a businessman turned spy.
title: The Courier
plot:
The Courier is a 2021 spy thriller film directed by Dominic Cooke, starring Chris Evans as the titular character, Nick Winterson, also known as "The Courier." The movie is based on the true story of Greville Wynne, a Welshman who played a crucial role in the Cold War.

The film begins with Nick Winterson (Chris Evans), an American businessman living in London with his wife, Liz (Sarah Wright). However, their seemingly idyllic life takes a drastic turn when Nick is approached by the CIA and recruited to work as a spy. He is tasked with smuggling a Soviet diplomat, Oleg Penkovsky (Mikhail Redniss), out of the country.

As Nick navigates his new role, he must balance his personal life with the demands of espionage. He becomes increasingly entangled in the world of espionage, using his skills to help the CIA gather intelligence on the Soviet Union. Meanwhile, Liz begins to suspect that something is amiss and starts to investigate her husband's activities.

The plot thickens as Nick becomes more deeply embroiled in the spy game. He faces numerous challenges, including encounters with Soviet agents and the risk of being discovered by his own agency. Despite these obstacles, he perseveres, driven by a sense of duty and loyalty to his country.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Oleg Penkovsky is not just any ordinary diplomat. He is a high-ranking official who has been feeding information to the CIA for years, providing them with crucial intel on Soviet military capabilities. Nick's mission becomes even more critical as he works to ensure that this information reaches its intended destination.

The film builds towards a tense and suspenseful climax as Nick faces off against his Soviet adversaries. With the help of Liz, who has become increasingly involved in his espionage activities, Nick manages to outsmart his enemies and complete his mission.

In the end, Nick emerges victorious, having successfully smuggled Oleg Penkovsky out of the country. The film concludes with a sense of closure for the characters, as they reflect on the sacrifices they have made and the risks they have taken.

Throughout the film, Chris Evans delivers a strong performance as Nick Winterson, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The supporting cast, including Sarah Wright and Mikhail Redniss, also deliver solid performances that add to the overall tension and suspense of the story.

Overall, The Courier is a gripping spy thriller that explores the complexities of espionage and the personal costs of loyalty and duty. With its tense plot and strong performances, it is a must-see for fans of the genre.

overview: A group of beavers ask Dr. Dolittle to save their habitat from loggers. The only hope is to get the forest preserved because it's the home of a protected bear, but there's a problem: the bear's the only bear in the forest, so she can't reproduce. Undaunted, Dolittle persuades a circus bear to help out, but he has to teach him not just the ways of the wild, but the wiles of lady bears too.
tagline: The doctor is in again.
title: Dr. Dolittle 2
plot:
Dr. Dolittle 2 is a 2001 American fantasy comedy film directed by Steve Carr. The movie serves as a sequel to the original Dr. Dolittle film.

The main theme of Dr. Dolittle 2 revolves around the idea of understanding and empathy towards animals, particularly those that are often overlooked or marginalized in society. The story follows Dr. Dolittle (Eddie Murphy) as he travels to Africa to help a group of orphaned elephants find their way back to their herd.

Throughout the film, Dr. Dolittle learns valuable lessons about responsibility, compassion, and the importance of preserving wildlife habitats. He also discovers that his unique gift allows him to communicate with animals in ways that humans cannot, which serves as a reminder of the interconnectedness of all living beings.

The movie also explores themes of identity, community, and belonging. Dr. Dolittle's relationships with the elephants and other animals he meets challenge his own sense of purpose and force him to reevaluate his priorities. Ultimately, the film suggests that by embracing our unique gifts and talents, we can find a sense of belonging and fulfillment.

The movie features a mix of humor, adventure, and heartwarming moments, making it an entertaining and engaging watch for audiences of all ages.

overview: On the run from a lethal assassin, a wily con artist devises a scheme to hide out inside a small-town police station. However, when the hit man turns up at the precinct, an unsuspecting rookie cop finds herself caught in the crosshairs.
tagline: Someone's gotta take the hit.
title: Copshop
plot:
Copshop is a 2021 American neo-noir action thriller directed by Joe Carnahan, who co-wrote the screenplay with Kurt McLeod from a story by McLeod and Mark Williams. Gerard Butler, Frank Grillo and Alexis Louder head the cast, supported by Toby Huss and Chad L. Coleman. Almost the entire story unfolds inside a small-town police station that turns into a battlefield between a hired killer, a rookie officer and a fast-talking con man. STXfilms released the film in the United Kingdom in September 2021, with an American release by Open Road Films following the same month.

Grillo plays Teddy Murretto, a fixer and con artist on the run from people who want him dead. When his bullet-riddled car breaks down near the desert town of Gun Creek, Nevada, he deliberately punches rookie officer Valerie Young, played by Louder, so that he will be arrested and locked away from his pursuers. His plan unravels when hitman Bob Viddick, played by Butler, stages a drunk-driving incident and gets himself booked into the very same station. From their neighbouring cells, Viddick calmly lets Murretto know who he is and why he has come.

Tension escalates when a hidden incendiary device sets off the fire alarm, a corrupt officer is caught up in the scheme, and Viddick attempts to break free and finish his job. Young, a sharp-shooting and quick-thinking officer, intervenes and begins to piece together what is happening. Murretto explains that his criminal employers had sent him to bribe the state attorney general, and that the job went badly wrong, leaving him a marked man. As word spreads, a second, far more unhinged assassin, played by Huss, arrives with his own crew, and the station becomes the site of a bloody siege in which alliances shift constantly and Young must decide which of the two dangerous prisoners, if either, she can trust.

Carnahan stages the material as a tightly contained, darkly humorous throwback to 1970s genre cinema, mixing sudden bursts of violence with sardonic dialogue. The film draws on themes of loyalty, corruption and survival, with Young serving as the moral centre among cynical criminals.

Critics gave Copshop generally positive notices, singling out Alexis Louder's breakout performance and Carnahan's energetic direction, although some found the story slight and the violence excessive.

overview: When the Rugrats find themselves stranded on a deserted island, they meet the Thornberrys, a family who agrees to help them escape.
tagline: The Family Vacation Goes Overboard.
title: Rugrats Go Wild
plot:
Rugrats Go Wild is an animated adventure film that combines the worlds of two beloved Nickelodeon shows: Rugrats and The Wild Thornberrys. At its core, the movie explores the theme of exploration and discovery, as the Rugrats embark on a wild adventure with the Thornberry family.

The film delves into the idea of stepping out of one's comfort zone and embracing the unknown. The Rugrats, led by Tommy Pickles, are initially hesitant to venture into the jungle, but ultimately learn to adapt and thrive in their new surroundings. This theme is mirrored in the Thornberry family's own experiences as they navigate the challenges of exploring the wilderness.

The movie also touches on the importance of friendship and teamwork. As the Rugrats and Thornberries work together to overcome obstacles, they develop a strong bond that helps them succeed in their mission. This theme is particularly evident in the relationships between Tommy and Donnie, who form an unlikely but effective partnership, and between Chuckie and Eliza, who find common ground despite their differences.

Furthermore, the film explores the idea of growing up and letting go of childhood innocence. As the Rugrats face new challenges and experiences, they begin to realize that there's more to life than just playing in the sandbox. This theme is subtly woven throughout the story, as the characters learn valuable lessons about responsibility, courage, and the importance of family.

Overall, Rugrats Go Wild is a heartwarming adventure film that celebrates exploration, friendship, and growth, making it a delightful watch for both children and adults alike.

belongs_to_collection.name: Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba - Collection

original_title: 劇場版「鬼滅の刃」無限列車編
overview: Tanjirō Kamado, joined with Inosuke Hashibira, a boy raised by boars who wears a boar's head, and Zenitsu Agatsuma, a scared boy who reveals his true power when he sleeps, boards the Infinity Train on a new mission with the Fire Hashira, Kyōjurō Rengoku, to defeat a demon who has been tormenting the people and killing the demon slayers who oppose it!
tagline: With your blade, bring an end to the nightmare.
title: Demon Slayer -Kimetsu no Yaiba- The Movie: Mugen Train
plot:
Demon Slayer - Kimetsu no Yaiba - The Movie: Mugen Train is a Japanese animated action fantasy film based on the manga series of the same name written and illustrated by Koyoharu Gotoge. The movie was produced by Ufotable, Aniplex, and Kyoto Animation.

The story takes place in Taisho-era Japan and follows Tanjiro Kamado, a young boy who becomes a demon slayer after his family is slaughtered by demons. He joins the Demon Slayer Corps, an organization that fights against demons, to avenge his family and find a cure for his sister, Nezuko, who has been turned into a demon.

The movie focuses on Tanjiro's journey aboard the Mugen Train, a mysterious train that appears only at night and is said to be able to take passengers to any destination. The train is crewed by the Demon Slayer Corps' elite team, known as the "Mugen Train Squad," who are tasked with protecting the train from demons.

As Tanjiro travels on the Mugen Train, he encounters a series of powerful demons, including the Upper Rank 3 demon, Daki and her sister, Ghoul. The two demons are revealed to be the leaders of the demon invasion in Taisho-era Japan and are determined to destroy humanity.

Throughout his journey, Tanjiro forms bonds with his fellow passengers on the Mugen Train, including Zenitsu Agatsuma and Inosuke Hashibira, a hot-headed young boy who becomes Tanjiro's rival. Together, they face numerous challenges and battles against demons, all while trying to uncover the secrets of the Mugen Train.

The movie features stunning animation, intense action sequences, and emotional character development. The story explores themes of sacrifice, friendship, and the consequences of war. The film's climax is both thrilling and heart-wrenching, as Tanjiro and his friends face off against Daki and Ghoul in an epic battle.

Overall, Demon Slayer - Kimetsu no Yaiba - The Movie: Mugen Train is a captivating and action-packed adventure that expands on the original manga series. With its rich characters, engaging storyline, and stunning animation, it's a must-see for fans of the series and anime enthusiasts alike.

overview: Four tales unfold in the Eternal City: While vacationing in Rome, architect John encounters a young man whose romantic woes remind him of a painful incident from his own youth; retired opera director Jerry discovers a mortician with an amazing voice, and he seizes the opportunity to rejuvenate his own flagging career; a young couple have separate romantic interludes; a spotlight shines on an ordinary man.
title: To Rome with Love
plot:
To Rome with Love is a 2012 romantic comedy-drama film that explores various themes through its interconnected storylines. At its core, the movie delves into the complexities of love, relationships, and human connection in the city of Rome.

One of the primary themes of the film is the idea of love being a universal language that can transcend cultural and geographical boundaries. The movie showcases several characters navigating their romantic lives, from a young American woman who falls for a charming Italian man to an elderly Jewish man who finds love with his neighbor despite their differences.

The film also explores the theme of identity and self-discovery, particularly in the context of Italy's rich history and culture. The character of Alessandro, a young Italian man struggling to find his place in the world, serves as a poignant example of this theme. His journey is intertwined with that of other characters, highlighting the complexities of navigating one's own desires and aspirations.

Furthermore, To Rome with Love touches on the idea of community and human connection in urban environments. The movie portrays Rome as a city where people from different walks of life intersect and influence each other, often leading to unexpected and profound connections.

Lastly, the film critiques societal expectations and norms surrounding love, relationships, and aging. The character of Jack, an American architect who becomes infatuated with a young Italian woman, serves as a commentary on the superficiality of modern dating culture. Meanwhile, the elderly Jewish man's romance with his neighbor challenges traditional notions of love and intimacy in later life.

Overall, To Rome with Love is a nuanced exploration of human relationships, identity, and community, set against the stunning backdrop of Rome.

overview: Elizabeth has just been through a particularly nasty breakup, and now she's ready to leave her friends and memories behind as she chases her dreams across the country. In order to support herself on her journey, Elizabeth picks up a series of waitress jobs along the way. As Elizabeth crosses paths with a series of lost souls whose yearnings are even greater than her own, their emotional turmoil ultimately helps her gain a greater understanding of her own problems...
tagline: How do you say goodbye to someone you can't imagine living without?
title: My Blueberry Nights
plot:
My Blueberry Nights is a poignant and introspective drama that explores the complexities of human relationships, love, and self-discovery.

At its core, the film delves into the theme of loneliness and isolation. The protagonist, Bernadette, played by Norah Jones, is a young woman navigating her way through life, struggling to find meaning and connection in a world that often seems cold and unforgiving. Her journey takes her to various places, but it's her inner world that's truly the focus.

The film also touches on the theme of vulnerability and openness. Bernadette's relationships with others are marked by a deep-seated fear of being hurt or rejected, which makes it challenging for her to form genuine connections with people. However, as she encounters different characters along the way, she begins to confront her vulnerabilities and learn to be more open and receptive to love.

Another significant theme in My Blueberry Nights is the power of human connection and intimacy. The film highlights the importance of forming meaningful relationships with others, particularly those that are built on mutual respect, trust, and understanding. Through Bernadette's experiences, we see how these connections can bring joy, comfort, and a sense of belonging.

The film also explores the theme of identity and self-discovery. As Bernadette travels through different places and meets various people, she begins to uncover aspects of herself that she may have previously overlooked or suppressed. This journey of self-discovery is marked by moments of introspection, growth, and transformation.

Overall, My Blueberry Nights is a thoughtful and contemplative film that explores the complexities of human relationships, love, and self-discovery. It's a poignant reminder of the importance of vulnerability, connection, and intimacy in our lives.

overview: A frustrated, unemployed teacher joins forces with a scammer and his girlfriend in a blackmailing scheme.
tagline: They wrote the book on how not to be criminals.
title: Big Nothing
plot:
Big Nothing is a 2006 black comedy crime film directed by Jean-Baptiste Andrea, starring David Schwimmer and Simon Pegg alongside Alice Eve, with Natascha McElhone, Jon Polito and Mimi Rogers in supporting roles. The film premiered at the Cardiff Film Festival in November 2006 and was released in the United Kingdom the following month. Although the story is set in a small town in Oregon, it was shot largely on the Isle of Man and in Wales, including Barry in the Vale of Glamorgan and locations around Monmouthshire, with additional scenes filmed in British Columbia.

Schwimmer plays Charlie, a former schoolteacher who is struggling to support his family and who manages to get fired on his very first day working at a call centre. His cynical co-worker Gus, played by Pegg, approaches him with what he presents as an easy and victimless scheme: Gus has evidence that a local reverend has been visiting pornographic websites, and he proposes that they blackmail the clergyman for a large sum of money. Josie McBroom, a former teenage beauty queen played by Eve, overhears them and forces her way into the plan as a third partner.

The scheme collapses almost immediately. While Gus goes to the reverend's house, Charlie heads to a bar to set up an alibi, only to discover that the person who could contradict it is drinking there. Hurrying to the house, he finds the reverend apparently dead and no sign of Gus, and in a panic he hides the body in a septic tank, a decision that turns out to have been fatal for a man who was not actually dead. Each further attempt to cover up the mess creates new problems, as the trio uncover secrets about the reverend, turn on one another and attract the attention of the police, all against the background of a serial killer, nicknamed the Oregon Undertaker, who has been murdering young women in the area.

The film blends farce, crime caper and dark thriller elements, with a twisting plot in which nearly everyone is hiding something and the body count rises steadily. Its humour derives from the escalating incompetence of its amateur criminals and from the contrast between Schwimmer's anxious everyman and Pegg's reckless schemer.

Big Nothing received mixed reviews, with critics appreciating its cast and dark sense of humour while finding its tone uneven and its twists convoluted.

overview: A teenager's quest to launch Norwegian Black Metal in Oslo in the 1990s results in a very violent outcome.
tagline: Based on truth and lies
title: Lords of Chaos
plot:
Lords of Chaos is a 2018 biographical horror film directed by Jonas Åkerlund, who co-wrote the screenplay with Dennis Magnusson. Adapted from the 1998 book of the same name by Michael Moynihan and Didrik Søderlind, it offers a fictionalised account of the early 1990s Norwegian black metal scene, told from the perspective of guitarist Øystein "Euronymous" Aarseth, co-founder of the band Mayhem. Rory Culkin plays Euronymous, with Emory Cohen as Varg Vikernes, Jack Kilmer as Per "Dead" Ohlin, Sky Ferreira as Ann-Marit and Valter Skarsgård as the drummer Faust. Åkerlund was himself a former drummer of the Swedish band Bathory.

The story begins in 1984, when the young Euronymous forms Mayhem in Norway, recruiting bandmates and eventually the Swedish vocalist known as Dead. Dead's self-harm and macabre stage antics help build the band's extreme reputation. At one concert the group meets Kristian, a shy and awkward fan whom Euronymous initially treats with condescension, and Euronymous begins a relationship with Ann-Marit from the local metal community. When Dead takes his own life, Euronymous photographs the body rather than calling the police and turns the tragedy into part of the band's dark mythology.

Kristian reinvents himself as Varg Vikernes, the frontman of the one-man project Burzum, and gravitates toward Euronymous's record shop, Helvete, which becomes the centre of a small circle of musicians determined to prove they are the most extreme. What begins as provocative posturing escalates into real violence, including a series of church burnings and a murder, while a bitter rivalry develops between Euronymous, who cultivates an image he does not fully live up to, and the increasingly fanatical Varg. The conflict culminates in the 1993 killing of Euronymous.

The film presents its subjects as alienated young men caught up in their own myth-making, and it combines dark humour with brutally graphic depictions of violence, which drew criticism from some members of the real scene who disputed its accuracy.

Lords of Chaos premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in 2018. On Rotten Tomatoes about 73 percent of critics' reviews are positive, with the consensus describing it as a grimly compelling dramatisation of a music scene whose nihilistic aesthetic spilled over into real-life tragedy.

overview: Genius hacker Connor discovers Cicada 3301, an online treasure hunt that could be a recruiting tool for a secret society. Soon Conner, art-expert friend Avi, and secretive librarian Gwen are dashing from graffiti sites to ancient libraries to uncover real-world clues. But they must outrun aggressive NSA agents, also hot on the trail of Cicada, who want the glory for themselves.
tagline: A true hacker story that never happened.
title: Dark Web: Cicada 3301
plot:
Dark Web: Cicada 3301 is a thought-provoking thriller that delves into the darker corners of human psychology and the blurred lines between reality and conspiracy theories. The movie masterfully weaves together elements of mystery, suspense, and paranoia, creating a sense of unease that permeates every aspect of the narrative.

At its core, Dark Web: Cicada 3301 explores the theme of obsession, as embodied by the enigmatic Cicada 3301 figure. This character's relentless pursuit of knowledge and truth becomes an all-consuming force that drives the protagonist to the edge of sanity. The film expertly captures the sense of desperation and fixation that can come with being drawn into a complex web of intrigue.

The movie also delves into the realm of conspiracy theories, skillfully using them as a metaphor for the darker aspects of human nature. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the truth is often more sinister than we might initially suspect, and that the pursuit of knowledge can sometimes lead us down a rabbit hole of paranoia and mistrust.

Furthermore, Dark Web: Cicada 3301 touches on the theme of identity, as the protagonist navigates a world where reality is constantly shifting and the lines between truth and fiction become increasingly blurred.
