However, as the day progresses, it becomes clear that Alonzo's methods are morally ambiguous and often violent. He takes Jake on a series of high-risk missions, pushing him to confront the harsh realities of police work.

Throughout the film, Alonzo's character is revealed to be complex and multifaceted. On the surface, he appears to be a corrupt cop who uses his position for personal gain. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Alonzo has a deep understanding of the city and its inhabitants, which allows him to navigate the complexities of police work with ease.

As Jake becomes more entrenched in Alonzo's world, he begins to question his own morals and values. He is forced to confront the harsh realities of police corruption and the blurred lines between right and wrong. Meanwhile, Alonzo's true intentions are slowly revealed, leaving Jake to wonder whether he has been manipulated or if he has truly become a part of Alonzo's world.

The film builds towards a tense and violent climax as Jake is forced to make a choice between his own moral code and the corrupt system that Alonzo represents. In the end, Jake manages to escape from Alonzo's clutches, but not before being left shaken by the experience.

Training Day received widespread critical acclaim for its gripping storyline, strong performances, and thought-provoking themes. The film won several awards, including two Academy Awards for Best Actor (Denzel Washington) and Best Supporting Actor (Ethan Hawke).

overview: A group of friends enjoying a weekend steal a couple of jetskis racing them out to sea, ending up in a horrific head-on collision. They struggle to find a way home with a badly injured friend while from the waters below predators lurk.
tagline: Terror runs deep.
title: Shark Bait
plot:
Shark Bait, also released under the title Jetski, is a 2022 British survival horror thriller directed by James Nunn from a screenplay by Nick Saltrese, a writer previously known for British television soap operas. Filmed in Malta and sold internationally by Altitude, it stars Holly Earl as Nat, with Jack Trueman as her boyfriend Tom, Catherine Hannay as Milly, Malachi Pullar-Latchman as Tyler and Thomas Flynn as Greg. The film runs 87 minutes.

Five young friends are enjoying their last spring break before graduation at a beach resort in Mexico. After a night of drinking and partying, during which the cautious Nat, the only one who speaks Spanish, ignores a local amputee's warning about what lurks in the water, the group steals two jet skis early in the morning and races them out to sea. A reckless game of chicken ends in a head-on collision: one machine is left capsized and abandoned, Greg suffers a badly broken leg, and the five end up crowded onto a single stalled jet ski drifting farther from shore. Because the craft were taken without permission while nobody was around, no one knows they are missing, and their only slim hope is that someone notices when they fail to board their flight home. Tensions boil over when it emerges that Milly slept with Tom behind Nat's back the night before. Tyler, despite a head injury, tries to swim for help, but a great white shark begins circling, and the predator toys with the survivors one by one as they search for a way to save themselves, leaving Nat to fight for her life in the final stretch.

Shark Bait was released in the United States on 13 May 2022 and on DVD and digital platforms in the United Kingdom on 6 June 2022. Reviews were mixed to negative. Jennie Kermode of Eye for Film was the most positive, praising an opening that pays intelligent tribute to Jaws, convincing shark footage, effective action and a predator presented as an animal with a mind of its own. Blueprint: Review found it handsome and well made, with a standout turn from Earl, but faulted its thin plot, unlikable characters and needless melodrama. In The Guardian, Phil Hoad gave it a scathing review, calling it a depressingly unimaginative thriller that lacks tension compared with Open Water or The Shallows and joking that the shark had more charisma than the cast.

overview: Upon learning that he is from New York City, a wide-eyed boy, who is half human and half alligator, decides to leave his sheltered life in the swamp and search for his long lost father. A musical adventure.
title: Arlo the Alligator Boy
plot:
Arlo the Alligator Boy is an animated film that explores the complexities of identity, community, and acceptance. The story revolves around Arlo, a young alligator boy who struggles to find his place in a world where he doesn't quite fit in with either humans or other alligators.

At its core, the movie delves into themes of self-discovery and belonging. Arlo's journey is a powerful metaphor for navigating the challenges of growing up and finding one's own unique identity. As he navigates the complexities of his mixed heritage, Arlo must confront the expectations of those around him and learn to embrace his individuality.

The film also touches on the importance of community and acceptance. Through Arlo's relationships with the people and creatures in his life, the movie highlights the value of finding a supportive network that celebrates diversity and promotes inclusivity. By exploring these themes, Arlo the Alligator Boy offers a heartwarming and thought-provoking tale that encourages viewers to embrace their own uniqueness and celebrate the beauty of differences.

Overall, the movie's narrative is infused with a sense of wonder, curiosity, and openness, making it a delightful and engaging watch for audiences of all ages.

overview: A documentary filmmaker travels to Jellystone Park to shoot a project and soon crosses paths with Yogi Bear, his sidekick Boo-Boo, and Ranger Smith.
tagline: Please do not feed the bears.
title: Yogi Bear
plot:
Yogi Bear is a 2010 computer-animated comedy film produced by Warner Bros. Pictures. The movie follows the adventures of Yogi Bear, a clever and mischievous bear who lives in Jellystone Park.

The main themes of Yogi Bear (2010) include:

1. Friendship: The movie highlights the importance of friendship and loyalty between Yogi and his sidekick, Boo-Boo. Their bond is put to the test as they navigate various challenges and obstacles.
2. Greed vs. Loyalty: Yogi's love for pic-a-nic baskets often puts him at odds with park ranger Smithers, who tries to outsmart him. However, Yogi's loyalty to Boo-Boo and Jellystone Park ultimately wins out over his desire for material gain.
3. Growing up: The movie also explores the theme of growing up and leaving childhood behind. Boo-Boo is struggling to come to terms with being a "big bear" and finding his place in the world, while Yogi must confront his own immaturity and learn to take responsibility.

The plot development revolves around Yogi's attempts to outsmart Smithers and get his paws on a new high-tech pic-a-nic basket. Along the way, he befriends Boo-Boo and helps him navigate the challenges of growing up. The ending features Yogi and Boo-Boo working together to save Jellystone Park from destruction.

Overall, Yogi Bear (2010) is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores themes of friendship, loyalty, and growth in a fun and lighthearted way.

overview: Born in America and raised in an Indian ashram, Pitka returns to his native land to seek his fortune as a spiritualist and self-help expert. His skills are put to the test when he must get a brokenhearted hockey player's marriage back on track in time for the man to help his team win the Stanley Cup.
tagline: His Karma is Huge
title: The Love Guru
plot:
The Love Guru is a 2008 romantic comedy directed by Marco Schnabel in his directorial debut, and written and produced by Mike Myers, who also stars. Jessica Alba, Justin Timberlake, Romany Malco, Meagan Good, Verne Troyer, John Oliver, Omid Djalili and Ben Kingsley complete the cast. The story centres on a self-help guru hired to restore the fortunes of the Toronto Maple Leafs hockey team. Myers developed the character from comic routines he had performed over several years, drawing on his interest in Eastern spirituality and self-help culture.

Myers plays Guru Pitka, an American-born spiritual teacher raised in an ashram in India, who proudly describes himself as the second-best guru in the world, after Deepak Chopra. As a child he was taught by Guru Tugginmypudha, played by Kingsley, who made him wear a chastity belt until he learns that loving oneself is more important than being loved by others. Pitka's dream is to become the world's number-one guru and be invited onto The Oprah Winfrey Show. He enjoys a celebrity following, and his teachings consist of simple acronyms and puns presented in slide shows.

In Toronto, Jane Bullard, played by Alba, has inherited the Maple Leafs, who are on a long losing streak. Their star player, Darren Roanoke, played by Malco, has lost his form since his wife Prudence left him for Jacques "Le Coq" Grandé, the arrogant goaltender of the Los Angeles Kings, played by Timberlake. Jane, a devoted follower of Pitka, offers him two million dollars to fix Darren's marriage so that the team can win the Stanley Cup, and the guru agrees, realising that success will secure him a spot on Oprah's show. Working alongside the team's diminutive coach, played by Troyer, Pitka uses unorthodox methods to rebuild Darren's confidence, while he finds himself falling for Jane despite the restrictions of his belt.

The film relies on broad slapstick, sexual innuendo and wordplay, and some Hindu groups criticised its portrayal of religious practices before its release.

The Love Guru was a critical and commercial failure. Reviewers overwhelmingly panned its humour, and it won three Golden Raspberry Awards, including Worst Picture, Worst Actor for Myers and Worst Screenplay.

overview: Teenage sisters Charli and Lola are on the verge of an experience beyond their wildest dreams! Pack your bags and jet off to Rome as the girls start their summer internship working for the legendary Derek Hanson - the totally cool international tycoon whose empire reaches from airlines to cutting-edge fashion. Amid the fabulous sights of this exciting city, the girls do their best to impress their boss, while still finding time to design their own line of very hip clothing, meet some very cute guys and turn their summer abroad into one awesome adventure they - and you - will never forget!
title: When in Rome
plot:
When in Rome is a 2002 American adventure comedy directed by Steve Purcell and starring Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen. Produced by the twins' company Dualstar Entertainment Group together with Tapestry Films, it skipped theaters and was released directly to home video by Warner Home Video on November 26, 2002. The supporting cast includes Leslie Danon, Julian Stone and Michelangelo Tommaso.

The Olsens play Leila and Charli Hunter, sisters who travel to Rome to take part in a summer internship program at a fashion company. They are joined by four other young interns from around the world, Paolo, Nobu, Dari and Heidi. Shortly after the program begins, a series of careless accidents gets the sisters dismissed, but their luck turns when they cross paths with the wealthy businessman Derek Hammond, who gives them their positions back. While spending a day at Hammond's home, Leila meets his rebellious nephew Ryan, and the two are quickly drawn to one another, while Charli begins to fall for her fellow intern Paolo.

Back at the office the girls start to take their responsibilities more seriously and form close friendships with the rest of the intern group. Their newfound commitment is tested when the scheming Mr. Tortoni, the head of the company, sabotages an important delivery by making off with the dresses intended for a photo shoot. With Ryan's assistance, Leila manages to photograph the theft and brings the evidence to Derek. The interns then rally together to produce a replacement collection from Charli's own designs, finishing just in time for the big day. The shoot is a success and Tortoni is forced to take the interns back. When Derek arrives, it emerges that Tortoni's actions were driven by long-standing jealousy over Derek's fortune and his romance with a woman named Jamie.

Like many of the Olsen twins' projects of the period, When in Rome combines a picturesque European setting with light romance and a message about friendship, teamwork and taking responsibility, and it was aimed squarely at the pair's large preteen audience. It was one of a string of international-setting adventures the sisters made for the direct-to-video market in the early 2000s, alongside titles set in other foreign cities, before they moved on to the theatrical comedy New York Minute in 2004.

overview: A rabid film fan stalks his favorite action hero and destroys the star's life.
tagline: All he wanted was an autograph.
title: The Fanatic
plot:
The Fanatic is a 2019 American psychological thriller directed by Fred Durst, who also co-wrote the screenplay. John Travolta stars as Moose, with Devon Sawa as the action star Hunter Dunbar, alongside Ana Golja, Jacob Grodnik and James Paxton. The film received a limited theatrical and video-on-demand release on August 30, 2019, through Quiver Distribution and Redbox Entertainment.

Moose is an autistic man who earns a living as a costumed street performer on Hollywood Boulevard. A devoted movie fan, he has filled his apartment with film memorabilia, above all items connected to Hunter Dunbar, a cult star on whom he has fixated. When he finally gets a chance to meet Dunbar at a signing, the encounter is ruined by the sudden arrival of the actor's ex-wife, and when Moose follows Dunbar pleading for an autograph, the irritated star brushes him off rudely. Leah, a young paparazzo who has befriended Moose, later shows him a phone app that reveals where celebrities live, including Dunbar.

Moose goes to Dunbar's house to hand him a letter. Worried about his young son, Dunbar reluctantly signs Moose's shirt and warns him to keep away. Moose keeps returning, however. After a quarrel with Leah and a violent attack on Todd, a fellow performer who had bullied him, he comes back to the house and, in a panic, shoves Dunbar's housekeeper Dora, who falls, strikes her head and dies. Moose hides inside the house, and once Dunbar has fallen asleep he touches the sleeping actor and photographs himself beside him, posting the images online before he flees.

When Dunbar spots him on the street the next day and threatens to kill him, Moose breaks down and burns his collection. He drives Leah away when she says she will go to the police, then returns to the house, ties Dunbar to his bed and subjects him to a string of cruel pranks. Dunbar begs for his freedom with promises of friendship, but once untied he turns on Moose with savage violence, maiming him with a rifle and a knife before coming to his senses and escorting him out. Tourists mistake the wounded Moose's injuries for makeup until Leah finds him and takes him to hospital, while Dunbar is arrested for Dora's death.

The film was met with mostly negative reviews, although some critics singled out Travolta's committed performance for praise.

overview: Earth is decimated after intergalactic tyrant Darkseid has devastated the Justice League in a poorly executed war by the DC Super Heroes. Now the remaining bastions of good – the Justice League, Teen Titans, Suicide Squad and assorted others – must regroup, strategize and take the war to Darkseid in order to save the planet and its surviving inhabitants.
tagline: The war to end all wars.
title: Justice League Dark: Apokolips War
plot:
Justice League Dark: Apokolips War is a 2019 animated superhero film produced by Warner Bros. Animation, but I couldn't find any information on it being released in 2020.

However, I can provide you with the plot details of Justice League Dark: Apokolips War:

The movie begins with Darkseid's plan to conquer the universe by using the Anti-Life Equation, a powerful formula that would allow him to control and destroy all life. The equation is activated, causing chaos throughout the universe.

Meanwhile, in the DC Universe, the Justice League Dark team - consisting of John Constantine, Zatanna, Jason Blood (the Demon), Hawkgirl, and Etrigan - are alerted to the impending threat. They soon discover that Darkseid's plan involves using the Anti-Life Equation to destroy all life on Earth.

The team decides to take action against Darkseid and his forces. Along the way, they encounter other characters from the DC Universe, including Batman, Superman, Wonder Woman, and others.

As the battle between the Justice League Dark and Darkseid's forces intensifies, the team discovers that the Anti-Life Equation has a profound effect on the universe, causing reality to distort and become increasingly unstable. The equation also brings forth powerful entities from other dimensions, including the Apokoliptian gods.

The movie culminates in an epic battle between the Justice League Dark and Darkseid's forces. In the end, the team manages to defeat Darkseid and destroy the Anti-Life Equation, saving the universe from destruction.

However, the victory comes at a great cost, as the equation's effects on reality are still felt throughout the universe. The movie ends with the surviving characters reflecting on the consequences of their actions and the challenges that lie ahead in maintaining balance and order in the DC Universe.

Unfortunately, I couldn't find any information on a 2020 release date for Justice League Dark: Apokolips War.

overview: Three fanatical bird-watchers spend an entire year competing to spot the highest number of species as El Nino sends an extraordinary variety of rare breeds flying up into the U.S., but they quickly discover that there are more important things than coming out on top of the competition.
tagline: Everyone is searching for something.
title: The Big Year
plot:
The Big Year is a 2011 American comedy directed by David Frankel from a screenplay by Howard Franklin, starring Steve Martin, Jack Black and Owen Wilson, with Rashida Jones and Jim Parsons in supporting roles. It is loosely based on Mark Obmascik's 2004 non-fiction book The Big Year: A Tale of Man, Nature and Fowl Obsession, which chronicled three real birders competing to spot the most bird species in North America in a single calendar year. The film keeps that premise but replaces the real participants with fictional characters.

Three men set out to complete a Big Year. Kenny Bostick, a roofing contractor played by Wilson, holds the existing record of 732 birds and guards it obsessively, even though his wife Jessica had hoped this would be the year they focused on having a child, and his fixation on birding has already cost him two marriages. Brad Harris, played by Black, is a 36-year-old Baltimore computer programmer who can identify almost any bird by its call alone; divorced, living with his parents and stuck in a job he dislikes, he hopes the challenge will give him purpose and earn his father's respect. Stu Preissler, played by Martin, is the founder of a successful Manhattan chemical company who wants to retire, but a pending merger means his two successors keep summoning him back to New York.

Over the course of the year the three criss-cross the continent chasing sightings, while competing with each other and many other birders. Brad and Stu become friends and help one another, and Brad falls for a fellow birder named Ellie. Bostick, meanwhile, uses underhanded tricks to inflate his own count and sabotage his rivals, at the expense of his marriage.

By December, Stu has happily retired and is enjoying his new grandson, Brad has begun a relationship with Ellie, and Bostick finds himself alone after his wife leaves him. When the results are published, Bostick has set a new record of 755 species, with Brad second and Stu fourth. Brad reflects that although Bostick got more birds, he and Stu got more of everything else. The film closes with Brad and Ellie birding together on a rocky coast and Stu hiking in the Rockies with his grandson, while Bostick birds alone in China.

Shot in and around Vancouver in 2010, the film drew mixed reviews, though the three leads were praised, and it was a box-office bomb, grossing about $7.4 million against a $41 million budget.

overview: The mobster husbands of three 1978 Hell's Kitchen housewives are sent to prison by the FBI. Left with little but a sharp ax to grind, the ladies take the Irish mafia's matters into their own hands — proving unexpectedly adept at everything from running the rackets to taking out the competition… literally.
title: The Kitchen
plot:
The Kitchen (2019) is a crime drama film that delves into the world of organized crime and the struggles of women in male-dominated environments. The movie follows the story of three sisters, Irish, Dee, and Maggie Flynn, who become embroiled in the Irish mob after their husband's death.

At its core, The Kitchen explores the theme of female empowerment and the struggle for independence in a patriarchal society. The film showcases the resilience and determination of the Flynn sisters as they navigate the treacherous world of organized crime, often finding themselves at odds with the men who seek to control them.

The movie also touches on the theme of loyalty and family ties, highlighting the complex relationships between the sisters and their involvement in the mob. As they become more entrenched in the organization, they must confront the moral implications of their actions and the consequences of their choices.

Furthermore, The Kitchen examines the tension between tradition and modernity, as the Flynn sisters struggle to balance their loyalty to their Irish heritage with their desire for a better life. This theme is particularly evident in Dee's character, who grapples with her own sense of identity and purpose outside of her role within the mob.

Overall, The Kitchen is a gripping drama that explores the complexities of female relationships, loyalty, and the struggle for independence in a world dominated by men.

overview: The origin story of former Special Forces operative turned mercenary Wade Wilson, who, after being subjected to a rogue experiment that leaves him with accelerated healing powers, adopts the alter ego Deadpool. Armed with his new abilities and a dark, twisted sense of humor, Deadpool hunts down the man who nearly destroyed his life.
tagline: Witness the beginning of a happy ending.
title: Deadpool
plot:
Deadpool is a 2016 superhero film directed by Tim Miller, based on the Marvel Comics character of the same name. The movie follows the story of Wade Wilson, a former Special Forces operative turned mercenary, played by Ryan Reynolds.

Wade's life takes a drastic turn when he is diagnosed with terminal cancer. Desperate to find a cure, he seeks out a experimental treatment that promises to heal his cancer but also leaves him severely disfigured and mentally unstable. The treatment, known as the "Accelerated Healing Factor," makes Wade's body regenerate at an incredible rate, but it also drives him insane.

Wade becomes a mercenary for hire, using his newfound abilities to take on high-risk missions. He adopts the alter ego of Deadpool, a masked vigilante with a twisted sense of humor and a penchant for breaking the fourth wall. As he navigates the world as Deadpool, Wade struggles to maintain his sanity and find a cure for his condition.

Meanwhile, Ajax (Ed Skrein), a former Special Forces operative turned mercenary, is also seeking to exploit the Accelerated Healing Factor for his own gain. He kidnaps several women with the same genetic makeup as Wade, intending to use them as test subjects for his treatment. Deadpool sets out to rescue the women and take down Ajax.

Throughout the movie, Reynolds' performance brings a unique blend of humor, wit, and vulnerability to the character of Deadpool. The film's action sequences are fast-paced and intense, with plenty of clever references to comic book lore. The supporting cast, including Morena Baccarin as Vanessa Carlysle and T.J. Miller as Weasel, add depth and complexity to the story.

One of the standout aspects of Deadpool is its willingness to subvert traditional superhero movie tropes. The film's irreverent humor and self-awareness make it a refreshing change of pace from more conventional superhero fare. Reynolds' performance also allows for a level of emotional intimacy that is rare in comic book movies, making Deadpool feel like a character-driven story rather than just a superhero origin tale.

Overall, Deadpool is a wildly entertaining and visually stunning film that sets a new standard for the superhero genre. With its unique blend of humor, action, and heart, it's no wonder that the movie became a critical and commercial success, grossing over $782 million worldwide.

overview: After five (or six) years of vanilla-wedded bliss, ordinary suburbanites John and Jane Smith are stuck in a huge rut. Unbeknownst to each other, they are both coolly lethal, highly-paid assassins working for rival organisations. When they discover they're each other's next target, their secret lives collide in a spicy, explosive mix of wicked comedy, pent-up passion, nonstop action and high-tech weaponry.
tagline: Smart and sexy
title: Mr. & Mrs. Smith
plot:
Mr. & Mrs. Smith is a 2005 American action comedy directed by Doug Liman from a screenplay by Simon Kinberg. Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie star as a bored suburban married couple who discover that each is secretly an assassin working for a rival agency, with Vince Vaughn, Adam Brody and Kerry Washington in supporting roles. The production became widely known for marking the start of Pitt and Jolie's real-life relationship.

The story opens with John Smith, ostensibly a construction executive, and his wife Jane, who claims to be an IT recruiter, attending marriage counseling. Five or six years into their marriage, their relationship is suffering from poor communication and small acts of passive aggression. In flashback, the couple recall meeting in Bogotá, Colombia, where they pretended to be together to avoid questioning by the authorities, followed by a whirlwind courtship and a quick wedding. Unknown to one another, both are elite contract killers employed by competing firms, and each has become expert at hiding the truth. They live in a large house in the New York suburbs, keeping up appearances among their wealthy neighbors while quietly balancing a dull home life against their dangerous careers.

Everything changes when both are assigned to eliminate the same target, a prisoner named Benjamin "The Tank" Danz, during a transfer. Their paths collide on the job, the hit is botched, and each soon realizes who the other really is. Ordered by their employers to clean up the mistake, John and Jane turn their considerable skills against each other, and the marriage erupts into a series of escalating ambushes, car chases and shootouts, culminating in a destructive fight inside their own home. Forced to confront the lies at the heart of their relationship, they ultimately find themselves allied against the agencies that now want both of them dead.

The film was a major commercial hit, ranking among the highest-grossing releases of 2005. Critics were divided on its plotting but frequently praised the chemistry and playful banter between its two stars, along with its stylish action sequences. Its blend of romantic comedy and spy thriller later inspired a 2024 television series of the same name.

overview: Young Albert enlists to serve in World War I after his beloved horse is sold to the cavalry.
tagline: Separated by war. Tested by battle. Bound by friendship.
title: War Horse
plot:
War Horse is a 2011 epic war drama film directed by Steven Spielberg, based on the novel of the same name by Michael Morpurgo.

The story begins in 1914, on a farm in Devon, England, where a young boy named Albert Narracott (played by Jeremy Irvine) lives with his mother and father. The family owns a horse named Joey, a beautiful chestnut gelding who is Albert's best friend. However, their peaceful life is disrupted when the war breaks out, and the British army requisitions all horses for military use.

The Narracotts are forced to sell Joey to the cavalry, and he is sent off to France with the 13th Hussars. Meanwhile, Albert is left behind, feeling heartbroken and helpless. He writes a letter to Joey, which becomes his only connection to the horse.

As the war rages on, Joey faces numerous challenges and dangers, including being captured by the German army and sold to a French farmer named Pierre Bonnasse (played by Benedict Cumberbatch). Despite being mistreated and struggling to survive, Joey remains loyal and determined to return home.

Meanwhile, Albert grows up and joins the British army, hoping to find his beloved horse. He eventually becomes a lieutenant and is sent to France, where he searches for Joey. Along the way, he meets a young French girl named Emilie (played by Emily Mortimer), who helps him on his quest.

As the war intensifies, Albert and Joey are reunited in a dramatic and emotional scene. However, their reunion is short-lived, as they are separated again when Albert is injured and left behind. Joey continues to survive, facing many more challenges and dangers before finally being rescued by Albert's brother, Ted (played by Tom Hiddleston).

The film ends with Albert and his family reunited with Joey, who has been through unimaginable hardships but remains loyal and true to his owner. The story is a powerful tribute to the bond between humans and animals, as well as the devastating effects of war on individuals and communities.

Throughout the film, Spielberg uses stunning cinematography and heart-wrenching performances to bring the story to life. The film's themes of loyalty, sacrifice, and the human-animal connection are timeless and universal, making War Horse a moving and unforgettable cinematic experience.

overview: After a fishing boat is attacked, the sole surviving crew member realizes it is none other than a resurrected Godzilla. However, efforts to bring the story to light are suppressed by the Japanese government amid growing political tensions between the United States and the Soviet Union, who are both willing to bomb Japan to stop the monster.
tagline: Breaking 30 years of silence comes the anticipated-worldwide latest "Godzilla" work!
title: The Return of Godzilla
plot:
The Return of Godzilla is a 1984 Japanese science fiction kaiju film directed by Kazuki Ōmori and produced by Tomoyuki Tanaka. It is the 15th film in the Godzilla franchise.

The movie begins with a series of mysterious earthquakes occurring around the world, which are later revealed to be caused by the return of Godzilla, also known as "Gigantis" or "Godzilla's Return". The story takes place two years after the events of Godzilla vs. Biollante (1989), where Godzilla is awakened from its slumber in the depths of the ocean.

The film starts with a series of strange occurrences happening around the world, including earthquakes and tidal waves. As the earthquakes intensify, it becomes clear that Godzilla has returned to wreak havoc on humanity. The Japanese government assembles a team of scientists and military personnel to deal with the crisis.

The main character, Dr. Yamane (played by Takeshi Kusao), is a renowned paleontologist who had previously studied Godzilla's DNA. He is recruited by the government to lead the team that will study and stop Godzilla. The team includes his daughter, Emiko (played by Yuriko Hoshi), a young scientist who has grown up studying her father's work.

As Godzilla begins its rampage across Japan, the team discovers that it is not just a mindless beast, but a creature with a complex intelligence and a desire to destroy humanity. The team also learns that Godzilla's return is linked to the discovery of a new species of giant lizard in the depths of the ocean.

The plot thickens as the team discovers that Godzilla's DNA has been altered by its encounter with a new species of giant lizard, which has given it enhanced strength and intelligence. This revelation raises questions about the nature of Godzilla's existence and whether it is truly a monster or a creature worthy of respect.

As the story unfolds, the team faces numerous challenges in trying to stop Godzilla. They use various tactics, including nuclear missiles and sonic devices, but nothing seems to work. The film builds towards an epic showdown between Godzilla and the team, which culminates in a dramatic confrontation on the streets of Tokyo.

In the end, Dr. Yamane comes up with a plan to use a device that can disrupt Godzilla's DNA, rendering it unable to reproduce. However, this plan is complicated by the fact that Emiko has fallen in love with Godzilla and wants to protect it. The film ends with a bittersweet conclusion, as Emiko sacrifices herself to save her father and the world from Godzilla.

The Return of Godzilla is a thought-provoking film that explores themes of nature vs. nurture, humanity's relationship with technology, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond our control. It is also a thrilling adventure that showcases Godzilla's iconic status as a symbol of Japanese popular culture.

overview: A squad of Ultramarines answer a distress call from an Imperial Shrine World. A full Company of Imperial Fists was stationed there, but there is no answer from them. The squad investigates to find out what has happened there.
tagline: In the grim darkness of the far future there is only war.
title: Ultramarines: A Warhammer 40,000 Movie
plot:
Ultramarines: A Warhammer 40,000 Movie (2010) is an action-packed science fiction film that delves into the grim darkness of the Warhammer 40,000 universe. The movie primarily revolves around the Ultramarines chapter of Space Marines, who are tasked with investigating a mysterious threat to the Imperium.

At its core, the film explores the themes of duty, honor, and sacrifice. The Ultramarines, as an elite fighting force, embody these values, and their unwavering commitment to protecting humanity is put to the test as they confront the unknown enemy. The movie highlights the personal costs of war and the moral dilemmas that come with making impossible choices.

The film also touches on the idea of faith and redemption. As the Ultramarines delve deeper into the mystery, they begin to question their own beliefs and the true nature of their existence. This introspection serves as a catalyst for character growth and development, particularly for the protagonist, Captain Nikason.

Furthermore, the movie explores the consequences of unchecked technological advancement and the dangers of playing with forces beyond human control. The alien threat that the Ultramarines face is a manifestation of humanity's own hubris and disregard for the unknown. This serves as a cautionary tale about the risks of scientific progress without moral responsibility.

Throughout the film, the director skillfully weaves together elements of action, drama, and science fiction to create a gripping narrative that explores the complexities of human nature in the face of existential threats.

overview: Jae-hyuk is a pharmaceutical worker for a medical supplies company. When a series of dead bodies are found floating in the Han River. The public is shocked to discovered that the deaths are related to a fatal outbreak of virus-infected mutant parasitic horsehair worms, called 'Yeongasi', that can control the human brain. Those infected shows symptoms of hunger and thirst, hence jumps into the river to combat dehydration. Whilst the authorities work to find a cure, Jae-hyuk struggles to save his family when they also exhibits similar symptoms.
tagline: There Must Be Something In The Water.
title: Deranged
plot:
Deranged (Korean: Yeongasi) is a 2012 South Korean medical disaster thriller directed by Park Jung-woo and produced by Lim Ji-young and Oz One Film. Kim Myung-min stars alongside Moon Jeong-hee, Kim Dong-wan and Lee Ha-nee. Distributed by CJ E&M, the film was released on July 5, 2012, with a running time of 109 minutes.

The protagonist, Jae-hyuk, holds a doctorate in biochemistry and was once a university professor, but after losing his savings and his position because of a disastrous stock investment made on the advice of his younger brother, he now scrapes by as a pharmaceutical sales representative. When bodies begin turning up floating in the Han River, the public is horrified to learn that the deaths are caused by an outbreak of mutated parasitic horsehair worms, known as Yeongasi, which can manipulate the behavior of their human hosts. The infected show an insatiable appetite without gaining weight and, once the worms mature and are ready to reproduce, an overwhelming thirst that drives them into rivers and lakes so the parasites can leave the body.

As similar corpses, all showing signs of severe malnutrition, appear each morning in waterways across Seoul and the rest of the country, the government scrambles to contain the epidemic and locate a cure. Jae-hyuk's own wife and children begin to display the telltale symptoms, and he races against time to save them. He is helped by his brother Jae-pil, a police detective still tormented by guilt over squandering Jae-hyuk's money, and the two are drawn into an investigation that suggests the outbreak may not be entirely natural and that corporate interests could profit from the crisis.

Deranged proved a significant commercial success in South Korea. On its opening day it sold nearly 191,000 tickets and topped the daily box office, outselling the Hollywood release The Amazing Spider-Man. Within five weeks of release it had drawn more than 4.5 million admissions and earned roughly 32 billion won, making it one of the most successful domestic films of the summer. Reviewers noted its combination of disaster-film spectacle with a family-centered emotional story and social commentary on the pharmaceutical industry and official responses to public health emergencies.

keywords.name: based on song, poem or rhyme

overview: A tribe of cats called the Jellicles must decide yearly which one will ascend to the Heaviside Layer and come back to a new Jellicle life.
tagline: You will believe.
title: Cats
plot:
Cats is a 2019 musical fantasy film directed by Tom Hooper, based on the 1981 musical of the same name by Andrew Lloyd Webber. The movie features an all-star cast, including Idris Elba, Jennifer Hudson, James Corden, and Taylor Swift.

The main themes of Cats (2019) include:

1. **Identity and Self-Discovery**: The film explores the idea of identity and self-discovery through the eyes of a group of felines who are struggling to find their place in the world. Each character's storyline is a metaphor for the human experience, where they must navigate their own strengths, weaknesses, and desires.
2. **Community and Belonging**: The movie highlights the importance of community and belonging, as the cats come together to form a tribe that supports and accepts each other. This theme is particularly evident in the character of Bombalurina (played by Jennifer Hudson), who finds her place among the group and becomes a leader.
3. **Mortality and Impermanence**: Cats grapples with the theme of mortality, as the characters confront their own aging and eventual demise. The film's use of CGI and visual effects creates a sense of otherworldliness, which serves to underscore the fleeting nature of life.
4. **Love and Connection**: Throughout the movie, love and connection are recurring themes. The cats form strong bonds with each other, and these relationships drive the plot forward. The character of Macavity (played by Idris Elba) is a particularly poignant example of this theme, as he struggles to find connection and belonging.
5. **The Power of Music**: Cats celebrates the power of music and dance to bring people together and transcend boundaries. The film's use of song and dance numbers is a key element in its storytelling, and serves to highlight the emotional depth and complexity of the characters.

Overall, Cats (2019) is a visually stunning and musically rich film that explores themes of identity, community, mortality, love, and connection. While it received mixed reviews from critics, it has become a beloved adaptation for fans of the original musical.

overview: The true story of the 4-year old son of a small-town pastor who, during emergency surgery, slips from consciousness and enters heaven. When he awakes, he recounts his experiences on the other side.
tagline: Unlock the mystery
title: Heaven Is for Real
plot:
Heaven Is for Real is a 2014 American Christian drama film directed by Jon Erwin and produced by Kevin Downes, Andrew Erwin, and Scott Brickell. The movie is based on the 2008 memoir of the same name by Todd Burpo, which recounts his son's near-death experience (NDE) at the age of four.

The story begins with the Burpo family - Todd (Greg Kinnear), his wife Sonja (Kelly Reilly), and their four children, including their youngest son Colton (Tyler Perry). The family is living in Colorado when Colton falls into a coma after choking on a piece of food during dinner. During his time in the hospital, Colton claims to have seen Jesus Christ and experienced heaven.

As Colton's condition worsens, his parents are filled with anxiety and fear for their son's life. However, Colton remains calm and peaceful, often talking about what he saw in heaven. He describes a beautiful place with rolling hills, trees, and animals, where he met Jesus and other loved ones who had passed away.

Colton also shares stories of his experiences in heaven, including meeting a man named "Dad" who he believes is his deceased father. The family is skeptical at first, but as Colton's visions become more vivid and detailed, they begin to question the possibility that their son has truly seen heaven.

As Colton's condition improves, the Burpo family becomes increasingly fascinated by his experiences in heaven. They start to investigate the claims he made, including talking to other families who have experienced similar NDEs. The family also begins to experience strange and unexplained events, which they attribute to Colton's connection to heaven.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when Colton's condition suddenly deteriorates, and he falls into another coma. This time, the family is faced with the possibility that their son may not survive. However, in a miraculous turn of events, Colton awakens from his coma and begins to recover.

As Colton recovers, the Burpo family reflects on the lessons they learned from his experiences in heaven. They come to realize that their son's NDE was a gift, one that allowed him to see beyond the veil of death and experience the love and presence of God.

The movie ends with the Burpo family returning to their normal lives, but forever changed by Colton's experiences in heaven. The film concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that even in the darkest moments, there is always the possibility for redemption, forgiveness, and eternal life.

Overall, Heaven Is for Real is a powerful and moving movie that explores themes of faith, hope, and redemption. While some critics have questioned the accuracy of Todd Burpo's story, the film remains a testament to the human spirit's capacity for love, forgiveness, and transcendence.

original_title: Tom and Jerry: A Nutcracker Tale
overview: A holiday themed animated direct-to-video film starring Academy Award-winners, Tom and Jerry. It uses a good deal of Tchaikovsky's famous ballet The Nutcracker as background music. This film would be the last animated production for Tom and Jerry co-creator, Joseph Barbera, who would die on December 18, 2006. The film features all of the exaggerated violence usually found in Tom and Jerry.
title: Tom and Jerry: A Nutcracker Tale
plot:
Tom and Jerry: A Nutcracker Tale is a 2007 animated film produced by Warner Bros. Animation. The movie follows the classic tale of "The Nutcracker" with a twist, as Tom and Jerry take center stage.

The main themes of Tom and Jerry: A Nutcracker Tale revolve around friendship, teamwork, and the true meaning of Christmas. At its core, the story is about two arch-nemesis, Tom and Jerry, who are forced to put aside their differences and work together to overcome a common enemy.

As the story progresses, we see Tom and Jerry develop an unlikely bond as they navigate through the magical world of the Nutcracker Prince's kingdom. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about cooperation, trust, and the importance of family.

The film also explores themes of identity and belonging, particularly for the Nutcracker Prince, who struggles to find his place in the world. Through Tom and Jerry's adventures, we see that even those who may seem different or outcast can come together and form strong bonds with others.

Ultimately, the movie concludes on a heartwarming note, emphasizing the importance of kindness, generosity, and the spirit of Christmas. The film's message is one of unity and acceptance, reminding us that even our most unlikely friends can become the closest of companions.

Overall, Tom and Jerry: A Nutcracker Tale is a delightful holiday treat that combines the classic charm of "The Nutcracker" with the timeless humor and wit of Tom and Jerry.

overview: An emotionally scarred highway drifter shoots a sadistic trick who rapes her, and ultimately becomes the United States' first female serial killer.
tagline: The first female serial killer of the United States
title: Monster
plot:
Monster is a 2003 American biographical crime drama written and directed by Patty Jenkins in her feature directorial debut. It recounts the story of Aileen Wuornos, a Florida street prostitute who killed seven of her male clients between 1989 and 1990 and was executed in 2002. Charlize Theron stars as Wuornos, with Christina Ricci as Selby Wall, a semi-fictional lover based on Wuornos's real girlfriend Tyria Moore, and Bruce Dern, Lee Tergesen and Annie Corley in supporting roles. Theron, who also produced the film, underwent a dramatic physical transformation for the part.

In 1989, Aileen "Lee" Wuornos has drifted from Michigan to Daytona Beach and is close to taking her own life when she wanders into a gay bar and meets Selby, a shy young woman who has been sent to stay with relatives by her religious parents. Although Aileen insists she is not a lesbian, the two connect over drinks, and Selby invites her to spend the night. Their friendship quickly becomes a romance, and Aileen, wanting money to take Selby out, returns to work on the roadside.

One of her clients drives her to a secluded wooded area, where he brutally beats and rapes her. Aileen manages to shoot and kill him, an act of self-defence that marks a turning point. Determined to leave prostitution behind and build a life with Selby, she tries to find legitimate work, but her lack of education and her history make every attempt end in humiliation. As money runs out and the couple move from motel to motel, Aileen returns to the highways and begins to kill again, robbing her victims and telling herself that she is protecting herself from violent men, even as the later killings become harder to justify. Her only friend, a Vietnam veteran played by Dern, cannot stop her descent, and as the police close in, Selby's loyalty is tested to breaking point.

Jenkins portrays Wuornos neither as a pure victim nor as a simple villain, but as a damaged woman shaped by abuse and poverty, whose love for Selby is both her one source of hope and a catalyst for disaster.

Monster received widespread critical acclaim, especially for Theron's performance, which Roger Ebert called one of the greatest in the history of cinema. Theron won the Academy Award, the Golden Globe and the Screen Actors Guild Award for Best Actress, and the film was a box-office success on a modest budget.

overview: Allie Foster, a struggling New York artist, reluctantly accepts to act as a governess to a rebellious Princess Theodora of Winshire. When Allie forms an unlikely bond with the princess, she attracts the attention of the handsome King Maximillian, who’s facing an arranged marriage against his heart’s wishes. As Christmas Eve draws near, Allie finds herself swept up in romance, royalty and the spirit of the holidays.
title: Crown for Christmas
plot:
Crown for Christmas is a 2015 American romantic comedy film directed by Michael Bregman and starring Lacey Chabert and Paul Greene.

The movie follows the story of Emma, a young woman who returns to her hometown of Willow Creek after being away for several years. She reconnects with an old friend, Jake, and they rekindle their friendship, which eventually blossoms into romance. However, their relationship is put to the test when Emma's past comes back to haunt her.

The main themes of Crown for Christmas include:

1. Second chances: The movie explores the idea of giving people second chances, whether it's in relationships or in life. Emma and Jake both have a chance to rekindle their friendship and romance, and they take it.
2. Small-town charm: The film showcases the charm and warmth of small-town Willow Creek, which serves as a backdrop for the story. The town's close-knit community and festive atmosphere add to the movie's cozy feel.
3. Family and tradition: Emma's family is an important part of her life, and she struggles with her past and present relationships. The movie highlights the importance of family traditions and the role they play in shaping our identities.
4. Self-discovery: Throughout the film, Emma learns more about herself and what she wants out of life. She discovers new passions and interests, which helps her grow as a person.

Overall, Crown for Christmas is a heartwarming romantic comedy that explores themes of love, friendship, family, and self-discovery in a charming small-town setting.

original_title: ポケモン・ザ・ムービーXY&Z ボルケニオンと機巧のマギアナ
overview: Ash meets the Mythical Pokémon Volcanion when it crashes down from the sky, creating a cloud of dust—and a mysterious force binds the two of them together! Volcanion despises humans and tries to get away, but it’s forced to drag Ash along as it continues its rescue mission. They arrive in a city of cogs and gears, where a corrupt official has stolen the ultimate invention: the Artificial Pokémon Magearna, created 500 years ago. He plans to use its mysterious power to take control of this mechanical kingdom! Can Ash and Volcanion work together to rescue Magearna? One of the greatest battles in Pokémon history is about to unfold!
tagline: The Soul-Heart calls…
title: Pokémon the Movie: Volcanion and the Mechanical Marvel
plot:
Pokémon the Movie: Volcanion and the Mechanical Marvel is a 2016 Japanese animated science fantasy adventure film based on the Pokémon franchise. The movie was produced by OLM, Inc., and TV Tokyo.

The story begins with Ash Ketchum, a young trainer from Pallet Town, who is determined to become a Pokémon Master. He sets out on a journey to catch more Pokémon and battle other trainers. During his travels, he meets a mysterious girl named Lysandre, who claims that she has the power to control time.

Lysandre reveals that she is working with her team, led by the enigmatic Team Flare, to take over the world using their powerful technology. Ash and his friends, including Pikachu, try to stop them, but they are unsuccessful.

The main plot of the movie revolves around a new Pokémon called Volcanion, which has the ability to generate electricity from its body. Lysandre uses this power to create a massive mechanical device that can control time itself. The team plans to use this technology to take over the world and rule with an iron fist.

Ash and his friends soon discover that they are in grave danger and must stop Team Flare before it's too late. Along the way, Ash meets a new Pokémon trainer named Mallow, who becomes his ally in the battle against Team Flare.

As the story unfolds, Ash and his friends face numerous challenges as they try to stop Lysandre and her team. They encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, wild Pokémon, and even a rival trainer who is working with Team Flare.

In the climactic final battle, Ash and his friends face off against Lysandre and her mechanical device. With the help of Volcanion and Pikachu, they manage to defeat the team and destroy the time-controlling device.

The movie ends with Ash and his friends reflecting on their victory and the lessons they learned from their adventure. They realize that teamwork, friendship, and determination are essential in overcoming any challenge.

Overall, Pokémon the Movie: Volcanion and the Mechanical Marvel is an exciting and action-packed film that explores themes of friendship, teamwork, and the importance of protecting the world from those who would misuse its power.

overview: Markus returns home to care for his daughter when his wife dies in a tragic train accident. However, when a survivor of the wreck surfaces and claims foul play, Markus suspects his wife was murdered and embarks on a mission to find those responsible.
tagline: Nothing Is Random
title: Riders of Justice
plot:
Riders of Justice is a 2020 Danish crime drama film that delves into the complexities of grief, trauma, and the human condition. The movie follows a former police officer, Martin Bressøe, who returns to his hometown after a tragic event, only to find himself entangled in a web of mystery and deceit.

At its core, Riders of Justice explores the theme of grief as a destructive force that can consume individuals and communities. Martin's character is haunted by the loss of his daughter, which serves as a catalyst for his downward spiral into darkness. The film masterfully portrays the all-consuming nature of grief, revealing how it can warp one's perception of reality and lead to self-destructive behaviors.

The movie also delves into the theme of trauma, highlighting its lasting impact on individuals and families. Martin's experiences have left him with emotional scars, which he struggles to confront and overcome. The film suggests that trauma can be a shared experience, affecting not only the individual but also those around them.

Furthermore, Riders of Justice touches upon the idea of identity and how it is shaped by our relationships and experiences. As Martin navigates his way through the mystery, he begins to question his own sense of self and purpose. The film implies that our identities are fragile and can be easily shattered by traumatic events or significant life changes.

The movie's narrative is also infused with a sense of existential crisis, as Martin grapples with the meaninglessness of life and the search for purpose in a seemingly indifferent world. This theme is expertly woven throughout the story, adding depth and complexity to the characters' struggles.

Overall, Riders of Justice is a thought-provoking film that explores the darker aspects of human nature, revealing the devastating consequences of trauma and grief on individuals and communities.

overview: A woman agrees to help her husband pay off an extortionist, but when the blackmailer is murdered she becomes the prime suspect, and discovers that the man she married has been leading a deadly double life.
title: Framed by My Husband
plot:
Framed by My Husband is a 2021 Canadian-American thriller television film directed by Sam Fichtner and produced by Johnson Production Group for Lifetime, which premiered it on 10 July 2021. It stars Christine Chatelain as June Lowe and Dan Payne as her husband Rick, with Rebecca Roberts, Dalias Blake, Naiah Cummins, Ruth Dvorah Bidner, Jessie Liang and Roxanne Wong in supporting roles. It runs 85 minutes.

June works at a hospital but dreams of becoming a writer, while Rick is a successful author whose latest novel has just made the New York Times bestseller list and whose female readers adore him. He wants to celebrate by starting a family, but June wants to finish her first novel before having children, and she complains to her sister Maggie that Rick does not take her ambitions seriously. One day June finds a blackmail letter in the mail from a woman who claims Rick sexually assaulted her and demands 50,000 dollars, or she will go to the police and go public. Rick insists that he is innocent and that obsessive fans make such claims; fearing that in the MeToo era even a false accusation could end his career, June persuades him to pay, using his bonus check. Rick then argues that his high profile makes it too risky for him to deliver the money, so June agrees to make the drop herself. At night in a parking garage she finds the blackmailers, Wendy Bach, whom she had seen bruised at the hospital the day before, and her husband Simon, stabbed to death in their car. She flees home in a blood-stained coat, which Rick promises to burn. Instead, when the police arrive with evidence suggesting June had an affair with Simon, the briefcase of money turns out to contain her bloody coat and the murder weapon. Arrested, injured and handcuffed to a hospital bed, with even her sister doubting her, June escapes, crashes her car into a river and is presumed dead. Free to investigate, she discovers that her husband leads a deadly double life, using a disguise and an alias on dating apps to meet and assault women, while he also pursues Maggie. Using apps, trackers and the media, June sets out to expose him.

Reviews were mixed. That Darn Girl Movie Reviews gave it five out of five, calling it one of Lifetime's best framed-woman films for its fast start and handling of MeToo themes, though it found the villain's final monologue ridiculous. The novelist Tina Martin found the concept unoriginal and June's choices implausible.

overview: A naive young man assumes a dead man's identity and finds himself embroiled in an underground world of power, violence, and chance where men gamble behind closed doors on the lives of other men.
tagline: Spin. Aim. Survive.
plot:
13 is a 2010 American psychological crime thriller directed by Géla Babluani, who remade his own 2005 Georgian-French feature 13 Tzameti for an English-language audience. The ensemble cast includes Sam Riley, Ray Winstone, 50 Cent, Mickey Rourke and Jason Statham, with Alice Barrett, Gaby Hoffmann and Emmanuelle Chriqui in supporting roles.

The story centers on Vincent "Vince" Ferro, a young man whose family is struggling for money. While doing electrical work in a house, he overhears talk of a lucrative but mysterious job that its intended recipient, now dead, will never collect. Ferro takes the envelope containing the instructions and follows them to a remote estate, where he is stripped and searched for recording devices before the organizers agree to let him take the dead man's place. Only then does he discover what the job really is: a brutal tournament of Russian roulette staged for wealthy spectators who gamble huge sums on which numbered contestant will survive.

Ferro, assigned the number thirteen, is surrounded by other desperate men. Among them is Ronald Bagges, a mentally unstable man brought from an institution by his brother Jasper, who bets on him, and Patrick Jefferson, a convict released into the custody of a patron named Jimmy, who hopes to profit from the outcome. In each round the players stand in a circle aiming at the man in front of them, the number of bullets in each revolver increases, and they must fire when a hanging light bulb switches on. Ferro tries to back out but is forced to continue at gunpoint, surviving round after round as the field shrinks and the remaining contestants are pushed toward a final one-on-one duel. The money Ferro might win becomes as dangerous as the game itself.

Released in the United States in a limited run and largely on home video, the remake was poorly received. Critics on Rotten Tomatoes were overwhelmingly negative, and reviewers such as Stephen Holden of The New York Times dismissed it as a blustering cartoon. Others felt that the switch from the original's stark black-and-white photography to color, along with added backstories for the characters, diluted the tension that had made Babluani's first version a festival success.

original_title: ワンピース ねじまき島の冒険
overview: Relaxing on a cozy beach, the Straw Hat Pirates are taking a rest from their quest. Right until Luffy noticed the Going Merry has been hijacked and sailed off from the beach. This leads them to search the ship and find the thief who took it from them. They ran into a duo named the Theif Brothers, who informed them that their ship was stolen by a group of pirates called the Trump Kyoudai. When they encountered the Trump Pirates, Nami ended up getting kidnapped as well as Luffy's hat. They tracked down the pirates to their base on Clockwork Island. Now Luffy, Zoro, Sanji, Usopp, and the Theif Brothers must reclaim the Going Merry, Save Nami, and get back Shank's straw hat.
title: One Piece: Clockwork Island Adventure
plot:
One Piece: Clockwork Island Adventure is a 2001 Japanese animated adventure film produced by Toei Animation and the second theatrical feature based on Eiichiro Oda's manga One Piece. Directed by Junji Shimizu and written by Hiroshi Hashimoto, with music by Kohei Tanaka and character designs by Eisaku Inoue, it was released on 3 March 2001 as part of the Toei Anime Fair, on a double bill with Digimon Adventure 02: Diaboromon Strikes Back, and was accompanied by the short Jango's Dance Carnival. Mayumi Tanaka voices Monkey D. Luffy, alongside Kazuya Nakai as Zoro, Akemi Okamura as Nami, Kappei Yamaguchi as Usopp and Hiroaki Hirata as Sanji, who makes his first film appearance.

While the Straw Hat Pirates relax on a beach, their ship, the Going Merry, is stolen before their eyes along with their belongings, forcing them to sail in a swan boat and wear rented wedding outfits. They meet the self-proclaimed Thief Brothers, Borodo and his younger companion Akisu, who suggest that the culprits are the Trump Pirates, a gang led by five siblings themed after playing cards. During the search, Nami is kidnapped to become the bride of their captain, Bear King, and the crew follows her captors to their base, Clockwork Island, a mechanical isle that Bear King seized years earlier, forcing its inhabitants to build weapons for him. One by one, Sanji, Usopp and Zoro are captured or defeated.

Borodo eventually confesses that he stole the Merry and handed it to the pirates to push Luffy into fighting them; his true aim is to free the islanders and return Akisu, who was set adrift as a baby, to his parents. Encouraged by Usopp, Akisu learns to find his own courage. The crew regroups and battles the Trump siblings: Zoro defeats the swordsman Pin Joker, Sanji overcomes Boo Jack, Usopp takes down Skunk One, and Nami traps Honey Queen in a bottle. Luffy faces Bear King, whose body can harden like steel. When the villain mocks Akisu for shielding Borodo, Luffy rebounds the blast of his giant cannon back at him, and Bear King falls as the island collapses into the sea. Akisu is reunited with his parents but chooses to continue thieving with Borodo.

The film earned about three billion yen, a record for the series until One Piece Film: Strong World in 2009. Its theme song, "Believe", was performed by Folder5.

original_title: Shriek If You Know What I Did Last Friday the Thirteenth
overview: In this horror parody, a masked serial killer menaces the town of Bulimia Falls with various sharp objects. Attention-seeking television personality Hagitha Utslay is soon on the scene, reporting on the ever-growing body count. Former mall security guard Doughy shows up to protect the teenage population, but he's clearly not much help, allowing the murderer to pick off even more hapless kids as numerous scary movies are referenced.
title: Shriek If You Know What I Did Last Friday the Thirteenth
plot:
Shriek If You Know What I Did Last Friday the Thirteenth is a 2000 American made-for-television parody slasher film directed by John Blanchard. The cast is led by Tiffani-Amber Thiessen, Tom Arnold, Coolio and Majandra Delfino, with Julie Benz, Harley Cross, Simon Rex, Danny Strong and Shirley Jones also appearing. Released only a few months after Scary Movie, the film mocks the wave of self-aware teen horror pictures of the late 1990s, and it follows the outline of Scream especially closely while also lampooning Friday the 13th, Halloween, A Nightmare on Elm Street and I Know What You Did Last Summer.

The film opens with a teenager alone at home being stalked by a masked killer, only for her to die by accident before he can strike, leaving him frustrated. His hockey mask melts after he lights a cigarette and turns into a ghostly screaming face, a joke about how one horror icon gave way to another. The next day Dawson Deery, a new student, arrives at Bulimia Falls High School and falls in with a group of friends that includes the hapless Boner, the jock Slab, the vain Barbara and Martina, a girl Dawson likes but who he suspects may not be interested in boys.

As students start dying around them, the group stays sure that they are safe, failing to notice the chaos unfolding in the background of nearly every scene. They are dogged by Hagitha Utslay, a pushy reporter for a music television news channel who has already written a best-selling pop-up book about the killings and who accuses Dawson of being the murderer. Barbara's brother Doughy, a clumsy security guard who has lost his job at a shopping mall, appoints himself the town's investigator. Soon each friend receives a note revealing that the killer knows their secret: one night, while driving drunk, they hit a deer and dumped it in the sea. The revelation sets up a string of gags parodying the conventions of slasher sequels, from absurd red herrings to a climactic unmasking.

The film premiered on television and was later released on home video. It drew comparisons with Scary Movie, but was produced on a much smaller budget and with a broader, sketch-like approach to its humor, relying heavily on rapid visual jokes and pop-culture references from the turn of the millennium.

overview: An affair between the second in line to Britain's throne and the princess of the feuding Irish spells doom for the young lovers.
production_companies: QI Quality International GmbH Co. KG
tagline: Fighting countries can still love...
title: Tristan & Isolde
plot:
Tristan & Isolde is a 2006 epic romance film that delves into the complexities of love, loyalty, and the destructive nature of unchecked passion. The movie tells the story of two lovers, Tristan and Isolde, who are bound together by fate but ultimately torn apart by their own desires.

At its core, the film explores the theme of all-consuming love, which can both elevate and destroy those who experience it. Tristan and Isolde's relationship is marked by a deep emotional connection that transcends social boundaries and familial obligations. However, this intense passion also leads to a downward spiral of obsession, jealousy, and ultimately, tragedy.

The movie also examines the consequences of unchecked emotions and the destructive power of unrequited love. Tristan's unwavering devotion to Isolde drives him to make choices that ultimately lead to his downfall, while Isolde's own desires and sense of identity become increasingly entwined with her relationship with Tristan.

Furthermore, the film touches on the theme of loyalty and duty, particularly in the context of chivalry and honor. The characters' adherence to traditional codes of conduct often serves as a catalyst for their conflicts, highlighting the tension between personal desire and societal expectations.

Ultimately, Tristan & Isolde is a poignant exploration of the human experience, revealing the devastating consequences of allowing passion to consume us.

overview: A woman grows suspicious of her controlling husband after she discovers secrets about the women in his past.
tagline: How do you escape… what you can't resist?
title: Killing Me Softly
plot:
Killing Me Softly is a 2002 erotic thriller directed by Chen Kaige, starring Heather Graham and Joseph Fiennes, with Natascha McElhone, Ulrich Thomsen and Ian Hart in supporting roles. Adapted from the 1999 novel of the same name by Nicci French, the film makes several significant changes to the book and places heavy emphasis on the intense sexual relationship between its two leads. It remains Chen's only English-language feature.

Alice is a young American living in London, settled in a secure job and a steady relationship. After a chance encounter on the street with a striking stranger, she seeks him out, goes home with him and begins a passionate affair. She learns that he is Adam, a celebrated mountaineer hailed as a hero for rescuing six people during a disastrous expedition that killed several others, including the woman he loved. Alice leaves her boyfriend for him, and after Adam violently beats a man who mugs her, he proposes and she accepts. They honeymoon at a remote cabin and then settle into married life.

Alice soon begins receiving anonymous letters and phone calls hinting at a darker side to her husband. A journalist forwards her a letter from a woman accusing Adam of rape, and Alice, posing as a reporter, interviews her. Searching the flat, she finds old letters from a former lover, Adele, and discovers that Adele has been missing for eight months, as well as a photograph of Adele at the very cabin where Alice and Adam spent their honeymoon. Fearing for her safety, Alice goes to the police, but without evidence they can hold Adam for only a few hours.

Alice turns to Adam's sister Deborah for help. Deborah confesses that she sent the warnings, and at the cabin Alice uncovers a buried body wearing the same necklace Deborah had given her. Deborah reveals her incestuous obsession with her brother, which drove her to eliminate the women in his life, and tries to kill Alice. Adam arrives in time to save her, and Alice stops Deborah with a flare pistol. Two years later, Alice and Adam pass each other on an escalator without a word.

The film was savaged by critics. Rotten Tomatoes reported a 0% approval rating, with the consensus calling it a spectacularly misguided erotic thriller marked by ludicrous twists and cringe-worthy dialogue.

overview: A philosophical burlesque, Human Nature follows the ups and downs of an obsessive scientist, a female naturalist, and the man they discover, born and raised in the wild. As scientist Nathan trains the wild man, Puff, in the ways of the world - starting with table manners - Nathan's lover Lila fights to preserve the man's simian past, which represents a freedom enviable to most.
tagline: In the Interest of Civilization … Conform.
title: Human Nature
plot:
Human Nature is a 2001 comedy-drama written by Charlie Kaufman and directed by Michel Gondry in his feature directorial debut. Tim Robbins, Patricia Arquette and Rhys Ifans star, with Miranda Otto, Rosie Perez and Robert Forster in supporting roles. The film screened out of competition at the 54th Cannes Film Festival, but it was a box-office failure and drew negative to mixed reviews.

The story is told in flashback by three narrators: Puff, a man raised as an ape in the wilderness, testifying before Congress; the writer Lila Jute, giving a statement to police after her arrest; and the psychologist Nathan Bronfman, speaking from the afterlife. Lila suffers from a hormonal condition that covers her body in thick hair. After a stint in a freak show she retreats to the woods, where she writes a successful book celebrating her free and natural life. At thirty, sexual longing draws her back to civilisation; she has her hair removed and begins a relationship with Nathan, a fastidious scientist who is trying to teach table manners to mice.

While hiking, Lila and Nathan come upon a naked man living like a wild animal. Lila gives chase, and the man knocks himself unconscious falling from a tree. In Nathan's laboratory he is named Puff, after the childhood dog of Nathan's assistant Gabrielle, who, it is revealed, is an American affecting a French accent. Nathan subjects Puff to conditioned reinforcement training, first with Gabrielle and later with Lila, until he acquires a veneer of refined manners and high culture, although he still struggles to control his sexual urges. Nathan takes him on a lecture tour, during which Puff secretly drinks and visits prostitutes, while Nathan is seduced into an affair with Gabrielle.

Lila eventually takes Puff back to the forest to undo his training, and the two live naked in the wild until Nathan finds them and is killed by Puff. Lila confesses to the killing and asks Puff to testify about the failings of humanity before returning to nature. Once the reporters leave, however, Puff emerges from the trees and drives off to the city with Gabrielle, an ending that suggests a hidden collusion between them and casts doubt on everything that came before.

overview: Bruce Banner, a genetics researcher with a tragic past, suffers massive radiation exposure in his laboratory that causes him to transform into a raging green monster when he gets angry.
tagline: What if everything you were forced to keep inside was suddenly set free?
title: Hulk
plot:
Hulk (also known as The Hulk) is a 2003 American superhero film based on the Marvel Comics character created by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby. Directed by Ang Lee and written by John Turman, James Schamus and Michael France, it stars Eric Bana as scientist Bruce Banner, with Jennifer Connelly, Sam Elliott, Josh Lucas and Nick Nolte in supporting roles. Lee himself performed some of the motion capture used to animate the computer-generated Hulk.

The story begins in the 1960s with government geneticist David Banner, who is trying to enhance human DNA. When his supervisor, Colonel Thaddeus "Thunderbolt" Ross, forbids human trials, David experiments on himself. His wife Edith later gives birth to their son Bruce, and David realizes the boy has inherited his altered genes. After Ross discovers the unauthorized research and shuts it down, David sabotages the base's gamma reactor in retaliation. Convinced his son is dangerous, he tries to kill Bruce but instead accidentally kills Edith. Ross has David committed to a psychiatric institution, and the traumatized four-year-old Bruce, who represses the memory, is placed in foster care and raised as Bruce Krenzler, believing both his parents are dead.

As an adult, Bruce works as a researcher at a Berkeley laboratory alongside his former girlfriend Betty Ross, the estranged daughter of the now General Ross. Their work attracts the interest of Glenn Talbot, a ruthless representative of the private defense company Atheon. When a lab accident exposes Bruce to a massive dose of gamma radiation, he survives unharmed, but the exposure triggers the latent changes in his DNA. Moments of rage now transform him into an enormous, green-skinned creature of immense strength. At the same time, David Banner, released and living nearby, re-enters his son's life with sinister intentions, while the military hunts the Hulk across the desert and into San Francisco.

The film's split-screen editing, which mimicked comic book panels, and its psychological focus on trauma and fathers and sons distinguished it from other superhero releases of the era. Critical reaction was mixed, with praise for its ambition and Connelly's performance tempered by complaints about its slow pacing and the appearance of the creature. Marvel Studios later rebooted the character with The Incredible Hulk in 2008.

overview: After 10 years in prison, Driver is now a free man with a single focus - hunting down the people responsible for brutally murdering his brother.
tagline: Slow justice is no justice
title: Faster
plot:
Faster is a 2010 American action thriller directed by George Tillman Jr. from a script by Tony and Joe Gayton. Dwayne Johnson stars as a recently released convict on a mission of revenge, with Billy Bob Thornton, Oliver Jackson-Cohen, Carla Gugino, Maggie Grace, Mike Epps, Moon Bloodgood, Adewale Akinnuoye-Agbaje and Tom Berenger in the supporting cast. CBS Films released it in the United States on November 24, 2010, with Sony handling international distribution.

Upon walking out of prison, Jimmy Cullen, credited only as "Driver," picks up a 1970 Chevrolet Chevelle, a handgun and a list of names. He drives straight to a telemarketing office in Bakersfield, California, and shoots a man named Prescott Ashton. He then confronts Roy Grone, who supplied the car and weapon, and pressures him for more information. Driver is soon pursued on two fronts: by a pair of detectives, the veteran Slade Humphries and his partner Cicero, and by a wealthy, highly skilled hitman known only as "Killer," who has been hired to stop him.

The next name on the list leads Driver to Kenneth Tyson, a man who records snuff films, whom he kills before escaping a hallway shootout with Killer. The encounter troubles the assassin, who proposes to his girlfriend Lily and becomes personally fixated on finishing the job. Meanwhile, the detectives dig into Driver's past and learn that he was double-crossed after a bank robbery years earlier. Cicero recalls a video, filmed by Tyson, showing the murder of Driver's older half-brother Gary and a man shooting Driver in the head; he survived only because of a metal plate surgically placed in his skull. As Driver works his way through the gang responsible, the hunters and the hunted converge, and the true identity of the man who orchestrated the betrayal is revealed.

Faster received mixed reviews from critics. On Rotten Tomatoes about 41% of 128 reviews were positive, and the site's consensus welcomed Johnson's return to hard-hitting action roles while judging that the film did not deliver enough of the thrills it promised. Commentators often compared its lean, brooding tone to the revenge thrillers of the 1970s, and it marked a deliberate shift by Johnson away from the family comedies he had made in the preceding years.

overview: The story follows a team of highly trained operatives who find themselves trapped inside an isolated military compound.
tagline: No Retreat No Mercy
title: Armed Response
plot:
Armed Response is a 2017 American action horror film directed by John Stockwell and starring Wesley Snipes, who also served as a producer. Anne Heche, Dave Annable and the professional wrestler Seth Rollins, credited under his real name Colby Lopez, co-star alongside Kyle Clements. The film was produced by Erebus Pictures, a joint venture between WWE Studios and the musician Gene Simmons, and it was released in a limited theatrical run and on video on demand in August 2017.

Snipes plays the leader of a team of experienced military operatives who are sent to a remote, high-tech prison facility to find out what happened to another covert unit that disappeared while stationed there. Soon after arriving, the team discovers the bodies of their predecessors and the building suddenly goes into lockdown, sealing them inside. Reviewing the surveillance footage, they watch the earlier soldiers being killed one by one by attackers who never appear on camera.

As the team searches the facility for answers and an exit, they begin to experience inexplicable and terrifying phenomena, including hallucinations and apparitions, and members of the group start to die in the same way as those before them.
