They eventually learn that the building itself is controlled by an advanced artificial intelligence called Temple, designed as an enormous interrogation system that functions as a sophisticated lie detector, extracting the truth from anyone held within its walls. Both units sent to the site turn out to share a dark secret from their service in Afghanistan, where they were involved in a massacre of civilians in a village. Temple appears determined to expose this hidden atrocity and to punish those responsible, forcing the survivors to confront their guilt and turn on one another as the truth comes out.

The film mixes the conventions of the military action film with haunted-house horror, using its single location and technological antagonist to explore themes of guilt, accountability and the moral cost of war. Much of the action takes place in claustrophobic corridors and cells.

Armed Response received negative reviews from critics, who considered its premise intriguing but criticised its confusing plot, thin characters and lack of suspense, although Snipes's presence in the lead was noted as one of its main draws.

overview: Englishman Adam and his American bride Sarah are about to embark on the romantic honeymoon of a lifetime in Venice, Italy. But when the newlyweds’ trip is gatecrashed by Adam’s excessively needy best friend, Ed, it inadvertently turns their perfect lovers’ holiday into a complete disaster.
title: The Honeymoon
plot:
The Honeymoon is a 2022 romantic comedy written and directed by Dean Craig. Maria Bakalova and Pico Alexander star as a newly married couple whose trip to Venice is thrown into chaos by the groom's clingy best friend, played by Asim Chaudhry, while Lucas Bravo appears as a charismatic Italian gangster. The cast also includes Flynn Allen as a teenage version of the groom, Marco Valerio Montesano, Michele Enrico Montesano and Kai Portman, with Myha'la Herrold appearing as herself. Bakalova also served as a co-producer.

The story centers on Adam, who sweeps his new wife Sarah off to Venice for their honeymoon. The romantic getaway is compromised from the start, however, because Adam has invited his best friend Bav to come along. Bav, emotionally needy and lacking any sense of boundaries, attaches himself to the couple and sets off one embarrassing, gross-out mishap after another, leaving the newlyweds with almost no time alone. Matters grow more complicated when Sarah catches the eye of Giorgio, a suave local criminal who is immediately smitten with her. To clear the way to winning her over, Giorgio arranges to get rid of the two men by sending Adam and Bav across the border on a drug-smuggling errand, turning the holiday into a farcical crime caper in which the hapless pair must find a way back to Sarah before her new admirer succeeds in stealing her away.

The project was announced in August 2021, when Bakalova, Alexander, Chaudhry and Bravo were confirmed as the leads, with Craig directing from his own screenplay. Craig was previously best known as the writer of the British farce Death at a Funeral. Principal photography took place in Venice and Rome beginning in August 2021 and wrapped on 14 October 2021.

In July 2022 Amazon Studios acquired distribution rights for the United Kingdom and several European territories, Grindstone Entertainment Group took the rights for the United States and Canada, and Notorious Pictures secured Italy and Spain. The film opened in a limited theatrical release in the United States on 16 December 2022, simultaneously with digital and on-demand availability. It premiered in the United Kingdom on Amazon Prime Video on 29 December 2022, and Amazon also released it in Germany, Belgium, France, Scandinavia and Eastern Europe. Lionsgate issued it on Blu-ray on 24 January 2023.

overview: When an engineer learns of a mysterious, impenetrable fortress hidden under The Bank of Spain, he joins a crew of master thieves who plan to steal the legendary lost treasure locked inside while the whole country is distracted by Spain's World Cup Final. With thousands of soccer fans cheering in the streets, and security forces closing in, the crew have just minutes to pull off the score of a lifetime.
tagline: No job is impossible.
title: The Vault
plot:
The Vault, released as Way Down in several regions, is a 2021 Spanish heist action thriller directed by Jaume Balagueró. Freddie Highmore stars as a young engineering prodigy, with Àstrid Bergès-Frisbey, Sam Riley, Liam Cunningham, Luis Tosar, Axel Stein, José Coronado and Famke Janssen in the ensemble cast. The story bears a passing resemblance to the real-life case of the Black Swan Project treasure, recovered in 2007 by the salvage company Odyssey Marine Exploration and later handed over to Spain after a legal battle.

In July 2010, Thom Johnson is a gifted engineering student at Cambridge University who turns down lucrative offers from oil companies, telling his father, an oil executive, that he does not want that kind of life. An anonymous message leads him to Lorraine, a skilled con artist, who introduces him to Walter, the head of a salvage company. Walter's firm found a legendary sunken treasure off the Spanish coast, only to have it seized by the Spanish government because the salvage was not carried out legally. The treasure is now kept in a vault beneath the Bank of Spain in Madrid, one of the most secure facilities in the world.

Walter has assembled a team of specialists, including Lorraine, the logistics expert Simon and the technician Klaus, and he wants Thom to find a way into the vault. Its defences, designed by a brilliant and secretive engineer, include an elaborate system that floods the chamber the moment it detects a breach. Thom determines that there is a narrow window of opportunity during the final of the 2010 FIFA World Cup, when Spain is playing and the entire country is distracted by the match. As the team improvise their way through the bank's security, they are pursued by the bank's head of security, Gustavo, while Thom discovers that the treasure holds a further secret linked to Sir Francis Drake.

The film combines the mechanics of a classic heist movie with the excitement surrounding Spain's World Cup triumph, and its action set pieces were largely filmed in Madrid and in a reconstruction of the bank's vault.

Critical reception was mixed. On Rotten Tomatoes about 60 percent of critics' reviews are positive; the consensus finds that its runtime passes painlessly enough but that its slickly engineered thrills are rarely more than routine for the genre.

overview: Emilia, a law-school graduate, falls in love with her married boss, Jack. After Emilia marries Jack, her happiness turns unexpectedly to grief following the death of her infant daughter. Devastated, Emilia nonetheless carries on, attempting to forge a connection with her stepson William and to resist the interference of Jack's jealous ex-wife.
tagline: Love makes everything possible.
title: The Other Woman
plot:
The Other Woman is an American drama written and directed by Don Roos, completed in 2009 and adapted from Ayelet Waldman's novel Love and Other Impossible Pursuits, the title under which it was released in the United Kingdom. Natalie Portman stars alongside Scott Cohen, Lisa Kudrow, Charlie Tahan and Lauren Ambrose, and the film was distributed in the United States by IFC Films.

Emilia is a young New York lawyer whose relationship with the married Jack ended his first marriage and led to their own. Her life has since been shattered by the death of their newborn daughter Isabel from what was recorded as sudden infant death syndrome. Emilia treats the loss as a punishment, believes she cannot have more children, and finds her marriage straining under her grief. She is regarded as a homewrecker by Jack's furious ex-wife Carolyn, who is now expecting another child herself.

Emilia also struggles with her precocious young stepson William, whose blunt remarks about Isabel wound her, including his observation that under Jewish law the baby had not lived long enough to count as a full person. Her clumsy attempts to bond with the boy backfire and lower her standing with both Carolyn and Jack. Eventually Emilia confesses the secret she has never told anyone: on the morning Isabel died, the baby had not been in her crib but asleep on Emilia's breast, and Emilia has been tormented by the belief that she smothered her daughter after falling asleep. She moves out, reconciles with her father, whose infidelity once hurt her mother, and returns to work with old friends at a Legal Aid office.

Carolyn unexpectedly asks to see her and admits she had told William that Emilia might have caused Isabel's death, adding that her son had rebuked her for it. She then tells Emilia that she has reviewed the autopsy report, which shows Emilia did not kill her child. Freed of her guilt, Emilia tells Jack the whole story, and a later crisis involving William brings them together again, with Jack asking her on a date. On the day Carolyn's baby is born, Emilia gives William a toy boat from her own childhood and tells him she loves him; after a moment he replies that he does too.

The film received mostly negative reviews, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 37% approval; critics praised Portman and Kudrow but faulted Roos's direction.

overview: Elektra the warrior survives a near-death experience, becomes an assassin-for-hire, and tries to protect her two latest targets, a single father and his young daughter, from a group of supernatural assassins.
tagline: Looks can kill
title: Elektra
plot:
Elektra is a 2005 superhero film directed by Rob Bowman, starring Jennifer Garner as the titular character. The movie serves as a spin-off to the 2003 film Daredevil, also starring Garner.

The main themes of Elektra (2005) include:

1. **Redemption and Self-Discovery**: The film explores Elektra's journey towards redemption and self-discovery. After being trained by Stick (Terence Stamp), a martial arts master who raised her as his own, Elektra sets out to atone for past mistakes and find her place in the world.
2. **Trauma and PTSD**: The movie delves into the psychological effects of trauma on its characters, particularly Elektra's troubled past with her father, Chaste (Ciarán Hinds), a ruthless assassin who killed her mother. This theme is reflected in Elektra's struggles to cope with her emotions and find peace.
3. **Moral Ambiguity**: The film blurs the lines between good and evil, as Elektra navigates a complex web of moral gray areas. She must confront her own darkness and make difficult choices that challenge her values and principles.
4. **Female Empowerment**: Elektra is a strong, independent female character who embodies feminine power and agency. The movie celebrates her strength, courage, and determination as she takes control of her life and fights for justice.

The plot follows Elektra Natchios (Jennifer Garner) as she seeks revenge against the Hand, a powerful organization responsible for her mother's death. Along the way, she must confront her own demons and team up with a group of allies to take down the Hand's leader, Gideon (Will Yun Lee).

Overall, Elektra (2005) is a complex, action-packed film that explores themes of redemption, trauma, moral ambiguity, and female empowerment.

overview: When his brother-in-law runs afoul of a drug lord, family man Chris Farraday turns to a skill he abandoned long ago—smuggling—to repay the debt. But the job goes wrong, and Farraday finds himself wanted by cops, crooks and killers alike.
tagline: What would you hide to protect your family?
title: Contraband
plot:
Contraband is a 2012 action thriller film directed by Bart Layton and starring Mark Wahlberg, Kate Mara, and Giovanni Ribisi.

The movie follows Chris Farraday (Mark Wahlberg), a former smuggler who tries to leave his past life behind. However, when his brother's wife is kidnapped by a Mexican cartel, Chris is forced back into the world of smuggling to rescue her.

Some of the main themes present in Contraband include:

1. Redemption: Chris's journey is one of redemption as he tries to make amends for his past mistakes and leave his life of crime behind.
2. Loyalty: The film explores the theme of loyalty, particularly between brothers, as Chris is forced to put his family first and risk everything to save them.
3. Morality: As a smuggler, Chris operates in a gray area, where right and wrong are not clearly defined. This moral ambiguity is reflected in the film's portrayal of the cartel's brutal tactics and the consequences of Chris's actions.
4. Family: The movie highlights the importance of family and the lengths people will go to protect their loved ones. Chris's love for his brother and sister-in-law drives his actions throughout the film.
5. Guilt and regret: Chris's past mistakes come back to haunt him, and he is forced to confront the consequences of his actions. This theme is reflected in his inner turmoil and struggle to make amends.

The film's plot development is driven by these themes, as Chris navigates a complex web of smuggling, loyalty, and redemption. The ending is intense and action-packed, with Chris facing off against the cartel in a desperate bid to save his family.

Overall, Contraband is a gripping thriller that explores complex themes and features strong performances from its cast.

overview: A dramatization of the relationship between heart surgery pioneers Alfred Blalock and Vivien Thomas.
tagline: A breakthrough that changed the face of medicine. A unique partnership that broke the rules.
title: Something the Lord Made
plot:
Something the Lord Made is a 2004 American television biographical drama about the partnership between Vivien Thomas (1910–1985), a Black laboratory technician who became a pioneer of cardiac surgery, and the white surgeon Alfred Blalock (1899–1964), known as the "Blue Baby doctor". Directed by Joseph Sargent for HBO, it is based on Katie McCabe's National Magazine Award-winning Washingtonian article "Like Something the Lord Made". Alan Rickman plays Blalock and Yasiin Bey, then known as Mos Def, plays Thomas, with Kyra Sedgwick, Gabrielle Union and Merritt Wever in supporting roles.

The story spans a partnership of more than three decades. In Depression-era Nashville in 1930, Blalock hires Thomas, a carpenter who had hoped to study medicine but lost his savings in the stock market crash, to work in his laboratory at Vanderbilt University, expecting him to do little more than cleaning. Thomas's extraordinary manual skill and quick intelligence soon make him an indispensable research partner, even though he is classified and paid as a janitor.

In 1943, Blalock moves to Johns Hopkins in Baltimore and insists on bringing Thomas with him. At the time, the only Black employees at the institution are custodial staff, and Thomas must use the back entrance. The paediatric cardiologist Helen Taussig challenges Blalock to find a surgical treatment for infants with tetralogy of Fallot, known as blue baby syndrome. Thomas develops the operation in the laboratory on dogs, and when Blalock performs the first procedure on a human patient in 1944, Thomas stands behind him in the operating room, guiding him step by step. The operation launches modern heart surgery, but Blalock receives the public credit while Thomas remains unrecognised, and tensions over race, money and respect strain their relationship over the following years.

The film explores ambition, loyalty and the racial injustice that kept Thomas from the recognition he deserved, ending with his belated honours from Johns Hopkins, including an honorary doctorate and the hanging of his portrait beside Blalock's.

Something the Lord Made received critical acclaim and won the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Made for Television Movie, along with other honours including a Peabody Award. Rickman and Bey both earned Emmy nominations for their performances.

overview: A college graduate goes to work as a nanny for a rich New York family. Ensconced in their home, she has to juggle their dysfunction, a new romance, and the spoiled brat in her charge.
tagline: A comedy about life at the top, as seen from the bottom.
title: The Nanny Diaries
plot:
The Nanny Diaries is a 2007 comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of class differences and the struggles of identity formation through the eyes of a young nanny, Annabel "Nanny" Turner. 

At its core, the movie delves into the theme of social hierarchy and the tensions that arise when individuals from different walks of life interact with one another. The contrast between Nanny's humble background and her wealthy employers' lives serves as a catalyst for exploring issues of class, privilege, and the blurred lines between authenticity and pretension.

The film also examines the theme of identity formation, particularly in the context of young adulthood. Nanny's journey is marked by self-discovery, as she navigates her relationships with her employers, her colleagues, and herself. Her experiences serve as a metaphor for the challenges of finding one's place in the world and defining oneself amidst the pressures of societal expectations.

Furthermore, The Nanny Diaries touches on the theme of female empowerment and the struggle for independence. Nanny's character embodies a sense of resilience and determination, as she navigates her way through a patriarchal society that often seeks to constrain women's agency. Through Nanny's story, the film highlights the importance of self-reliance, assertiveness, and the pursuit of one's own desires.

Ultimately, The Nanny Diaries presents a nuanced portrayal of the human experience, capturing the complexities and contradictions of life in all its messy glory.

overview: Cal Weaver is living the American dream. He has a good job, a beautiful house, great children and a beautiful wife, named Emily. Cal's seemingly perfect life unravels, however, when he learns that Emily has been unfaithful and wants a divorce. Over 40 and suddenly single, Cal is adrift in the fickle world of dating. Enter, Jacob Palmer, a self-styled player who takes Cal under his wing and teaches him how to be a hit with the ladies.
tagline: This is crazy. This is stupid. This is love.
title: Crazy, Stupid, Love.
plot:
Crazy, Stupid, Love is a romantic comedy film released in 2011 by Warner Bros. Pictures. The movie follows the story of Cal Weaver (played by Steve Carell), a middle-aged man who is recently divorced by his wife Emily (played by Julianne Moore).

The movie begins with Cal's life falling apart. He is struggling to come to terms with his divorce and feeling lost without his wife. His best friend, Jacob Palmer (played by Ryan Gosling), a smooth-talking ladies' man, tries to help him get back into the dating scene. However, things take an unexpected turn when Jacob starts teaching Cal how to improve his appearance and become more confident in social situations.

As Cal navigates the dating world with Jacob's guidance, he meets Hannah (played by Emma Stone), a quirky and charming woman who is initially hesitant to date again after her own recent break-up. Despite their initial awkwardness, Cal and Hannah start developing feelings for each other, but their relationship is put to the test when Emily reveals that she has moved on with her life.

Meanwhile, Jacob finds himself falling in love with Hannah, but struggles to express his true feelings due to his fear of commitment. As the story unfolds, Cal's journey becomes a metaphor for self-discovery and growth, as he learns to let go of his past and find happiness again.

Throughout the movie, the characters face various challenges and learn valuable lessons about love, relationships, and themselves. The film features witty dialogue, engaging performances from its cast, and a heartwarming story that explores the complexities of human emotions.

Ultimately, the movie concludes with Cal and Hannah finding their way back to each other, while Jacob comes to terms with his own feelings and finds happiness in an unexpected way. The ending is both satisfying and uplifting, leaving audiences feeling hopeful about love and relationships.

Overall, Crazy, Stupid, Love is a charming and entertaining film that explores the ups and downs of love, relationships, and self-discovery. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and engaging storyline, it's no wonder this movie has become a beloved favorite among rom-com fans.

original_title: 劇場版ポケットモンスター ベストウイッシュ キュレムVS聖剣士 ケルディオ
overview: Ash and his two friends Iris and Cilan help a Keldeo battle against a powerful Dragon-type Pokémon named Kyurem its his test to become a Sacred Swordsman.
title: Pokémon the Movie: Kyurem vs. the Sword of Justice
plot:
Pokémon the Movie: Kyurem vs. the Sword of Justice is a 2012 Japanese animated science fantasy adventure film directed by Masaaki Yuasa and produced by OLM, Inc., not Production I.G.

The main themes of Pokémon the Movie: Kyurem vs. the Sword of Justice include:

1. Balance between Power and Responsibility: The movie explores the idea that great power comes with great responsibility. The protagonist, Diantha, must learn to wield her newfound powers as a Champion while also understanding the consequences of her actions.
2. Friendship and Teamwork: The film highlights the importance of friendship and teamwork in overcoming challenges. The main characters work together to defeat Kyurem and save the world from destruction.
3. Self-Discovery: Diantha's journey is also one of self-discovery, as she learns more about herself and her place in the world of Pokémon battling.
4. The Consequences of Playing with Powers Beyond One's Control: The movie serves as a warning about the dangers of playing with powers beyond one's control, as seen in the character of Kyurem.

The film received positive reviews for its engaging storyline, well-developed characters, and stunning animation.

overview: After settling in the tiny Australian town of Walkabout Creek with his significant other and his young son, Mick "Crocodile" Dundee is thrown for a loop when a prestigious Los Angeles newspaper offers his honey a job. The family migrates back to the United States, and Croc and son soon find themselves learning some lessons about American life -- many of them inadvertent
tagline: He heard there was wildlife in L.A. He didn't know how wild.
title: Crocodile Dundee in Los Angeles
plot:
Crocodile Dundee in Los Angeles is a 2001 action comedy directed by Simon Wincer and starring Paul Hogan. It is the third and final installment of the Crocodile Dundee series and a sequel to Crocodile Dundee II (1988). Hogan and Linda Kozlowski return as Michael "Crocodile" Dundee and Sue Charlton, joined by Jere Burns, Jonathan Banks, Alec Wilson and Serge Cockburn as their young son. The film was shot in Los Angeles and in Queensland, and Hogan said the idea for its story came to him while touring the Czech town of Litomyšl in 1993.

Thirteen years after the previous film, Mick lives in the Australian outback with Sue and their son Mikey. Crocodile hunting has been outlawed, so Mick now earns his living wrestling crocodiles for tourists and competing with a rival bushman named Jacko. When Sue is offered the job of Los Angeles bureau chief for a newspaper owned by her father, the family moves across the Pacific. Mick and Mikey soon run into a series of culture-clash misadventures in Southern California, while Mikey wins over his classmates and his teacher with the survival skills he learned in the bush.

Sue's predecessor at the paper died in suspicious circumstances, and Mick becomes an undercover amateur detective to help find out what happened. The trail leads to a film studio that is inexplicably making a sequel to a flop action film called Lethal Agent. Mick grows suspicious when crates of paintings from southern Europe arrive on the set. At first he assumes drugs are being smuggled, but the canvases turn out to be valuable artworks missing from a museum in the former Yugoslavia and thought to have been lost during the war. The production plans to burn them as props on camera after quietly swapping them for copies. With Jacko flown in to babysit Mikey, Mick and Sue try to get hold of one painting as evidence and end up taking on the studio's criminals, using props and a trio of film lions.

The film was released in April 2001 and grossed about $39 million worldwide. Critics were largely negative, calling it an unnecessary sequel that came too long after the earlier films and relied on fish-out-of-water humor that had grown stale.

overview: This movie stars Barbie as a teenage girl, trying to deal with crushes, rivals and friendship as she tries to achieve her dream of working as a news anchor for her school's TV station. She doesn't always make the right decisions, but she's a nice enough character and considerably less "perfect" than she is portrayed in her other films.
title: The Barbie Diaries
plot: Barbie is disheartened when Todd breaks her heart and goes back to his former girlfriend. But things change when she comes across a diary, which makes her wishes come true.

overview: The year is 1949. A young Texan named John Grady finds himself without a home after his mother sells the ranch where he has spent his entire life. Lured south of the border by the romance of cowboy life and the promise of a fresh start, Cole and his pal embark on an adventure that will test their resilience, define their maturity, and change their lives forever.
tagline: Some passions can never be tamed.
title: All the Pretty Horses
plot:
All the Pretty Horses is a 2000 American Western produced and directed by Billy Bob Thornton, adapted from Cormac McCarthy's 1992 novel of the same name, the first book of his Border Trilogy. Matt Damon leads a cast that includes Henry Thomas, Lucas Black, Penélope Cruz, Rubén Blades, Robert Patrick, Bruce Dern and Sam Shepard. Miramax Films released it in the United States on December 25, 2000, with Columbia Pictures distributing in other territories.

The story is set in 1949. Young Texas cowboy John Grady Cole finds himself without a home after his family's ranch is sold following his grandfather's death. Unwilling to give up the only way of life he knows, he persuades his best friend Lacey Rawlins to leave San Angelo with him and ride on horseback roughly 150 miles south across the border to look for work in Mexico. Along the trail they fall in with Jimmy Blevins, a strange, headstrong teenager riding a fine horse, but after he loses the animal in a storm and causes trouble trying to recover it, the pair part ways with him.

Cole and Rawlins find work as hands on a large hacienda, where the owner, Don Héctor, is impressed by their skill with horses. Cole falls in love with Alejandra Villarreal, the rancher's beautiful daughter, but the romance is firmly opposed by her aunt, Dueña Alfonsa, who guards the family's honor. After Alejandra is sent away, Cole and Rawlins are arrested by Mexican police and reunited with Blevins, who has been accused of horse theft and murder. The boy is executed by a corrupt police captain, and the two friends are thrown into a brutal Mexican prison as accomplices, where they must fight to stay alive. Their eventual release comes at a heavy price, and Cole is left to decide what he owes to Alejandra, to his friend and to the dead Blevins.

The production became known for a protracted dispute between Thornton and the studio over its length. Thornton's original cut ran close to four hours and was considerably shortened for theatrical release, and Daniel Lanois's score was largely replaced. The finished film was poorly received. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds a 32% approval rating from 100 reviews, with critics describing it as a weak adaptation of the novel and dramatically inert, and it grossed only about $18.1 million worldwide against a much larger budget.

overview: Fuelled by his restored faith in humanity and inspired by Superman's selfless act, Bruce Wayne and Diana Prince assemble a team of metahumans consisting of Barry Allen, Arthur Curry and Victor Stone to face the catastrophic threat of Steppenwolf and the Parademons who are on the hunt for three Mother Boxes on Earth.
tagline: You can't save the world alone
title: Justice League
plot:
Justice League is a 2017 superhero film directed by Zack Snyder and Joss Whedon, based on the DC Comics team of the same name. The movie brings together some of DC's most iconic heroes to form a team that must band together to save the world from an ancient evil.

The film begins with Bruce Wayne (Ben Affleck), aka Batman, who has been training a young Diana Prince (Sally Hawkins) in the ways of combat and leadership. However, their mission is interrupted by Steppenwolf (Ciarán Hinds), an alien warlord who seeks to collect three powerful artifacts known as the Mother Boxes.

Meanwhile, Arthur Curry (Jason Momoa), aka Aquaman, is introduced as he struggles with his half-human, half-Atlantean heritage. He eventually teams up with Mera (Amber Heard) and together they embark on a quest to find the Trident of Atlan, which will help him claim his rightful place as king.

The story takes a dramatic turn when Superman (Henry Cavill), who has been missing since his battle with General Zod in Man of Steel, is revealed to be alive. However, he is being held captive by Steppenwolf and his minions.

As the heroes begin to assemble, they realize that they must work together if they hope to stop Steppenwolf's plans. Batman brings his strategic mind, Wonder Woman (Gal Gadot) brings her combat skills and compassion, Aquaman brings his aquatic abilities and determination, Cyborg (Ray Fisher) brings his technological expertise and emotional vulnerability, and The Flash (Ezra Miller) brings his speed and enthusiasm.

The team faces numerous challenges as they try to stop Steppenwolf's plans. Along the way, they also uncover a deeper conspiracy involving Darkseid (Jensen Ackles), who is revealed to be manipulating events from behind the scenes.

As the battle against Steppenwolf reaches its climax, the heroes must put aside their differences and work together if they hope to save the world. In the end, they succeed in defeating Steppenwolf and shattering the Mother Boxes, which prevents Darkseid from gaining control over the planet.

The film concludes with a sense of hope and unity among the heroes, as they realize that they have found a new family and a new purpose. The ending also sets up the possibility for future team-ups and adventures, as the heroes look to the future and prepare for whatever challenges may come their way.

Overall, Justice League is an action-packed superhero film that brings together some of DC's most iconic heroes in a thrilling adventure. While it received mixed reviews from critics, fans of the franchise will enjoy the excitement and spectacle of this epic battle between good and evil.

overview: Tells the parallel stories of nine-year-old Carlitos and his mother, Rosario. In the hopes of providing a better life for her son, Rosario works illegally in the U.S. while her mother cares for Carlitos back in Mexico.
tagline: The love between a mother and a son knows no Boundraries.
title: Under the Same Moon
plot:
Under the Same Moon is a poignant and heart-wrenching film that explores the complexities of family, identity, and belonging. At its core, the movie delves into the theme of the immigrant experience, where characters are forced to navigate unfamiliar lands, cultures, and languages in search of a sense of home.

The story revolves around Carlos, a young boy who embarks on an extraordinary journey from Mexico to India in search of his estranged father. Along the way, he faces numerous challenges, including poverty, illness, and loneliness, yet remains steadfast in his determination to find his family.

One of the primary themes of Under the Same Moon is the power of love and connection. Carlos's unwavering devotion to his father serves as a beacon of hope, illuminating the complexities of their relationship and the sacrifices they make for one another. The film also highlights the resilience of the human spirit, as Carlos faces unimaginable hardships with courage and determination.

The movie also explores the theme of identity, particularly in the context of cultural heritage. Carlos's journey is not just about finding his father but also about discovering his own roots and understanding the traditions that have been passed down through generations. The film beautifully captures the richness and diversity of Mexican culture, weaving it seamlessly into the narrative.

Furthermore, Under the Same Moon touches on the theme of belonging, which is deeply intertwined with the concept of family. Carlos's search for his father becomes a quest to find a sense of home and acceptance, highlighting the universal human desire to belong and be loved unconditionally.

Overall, Under the Same Moon is a powerful exploration of the complexities of family, identity, and belonging, set against the backdrop of an extraordinary true story.

overview: A former serial killer with Alzheimer's fights to protect his daughter from her mysterious boyfriend who may be a serial killer too.
tagline: Memories can deceive you.
title: Memoir of a Murderer
plot:
Memoir of a Murderer is a 2017 South Korean psychological thriller film directed by Bong Joon-ho. The movie follows the story of Park Do-kyung, a man who seeks revenge against his brother-in-law for killing his wife.

The main theme of Memoir of a Murderer revolves around the destructive nature of obsession and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. As Park Do-kyung's quest for revenge becomes increasingly all-consuming, he begins to question what is real and what is just a product of his own paranoid imagination. This theme is expertly woven throughout the film, creating a sense of unease and tension that keeps the viewer on edge.

The movie also explores the idea of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals. Park Do-kyung's past experiences have left him with deep emotional scars, which he uses as justification for his actions. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that his perception of reality is distorted by his own trauma, making it difficult to discern what is true and what is just a manifestation of his own guilt and anger.

Furthermore, Memoir of a Murderer touches on the theme of the cyclical nature of violence and revenge. Park Do-kyung's actions are motivated by a desire for revenge, but ultimately lead to further chaos and destruction. This cycle of violence serves as a commentary on the futility of seeking revenge and the devastating consequences that can result from it.

Overall, Memoir of a Murderer is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes with nuance and sophistication.

overview: Two sisters are trapped under the fiberglass cover of an Olympic sized public pool and must brave the cold and each other to survive the harrowing night.
tagline: 100,000 gallons of water. 50 meters wide. NO. WAY. OUT.
title: 12 Feet Deep
plot:
12 Feet Deep, originally titled The Deep End, is a 2017 American psychological horror thriller written and directed by Matt Eskandari. Alexandra Park and Nora-Jane Noone star as sisters who become trapped beneath the fibreglass cover of an Olympic-sized public swimming pool, with Diane Farr and Tobin Bell in supporting roles. The film was released by Mar Vista Entertainment in June 2017 and received generally positive reviews.

Bree goes for a swim at a local aquatic centre just before it closes for the holidays and is joined by her sister Jonna, a recovering drug addict who has been clean for three months. Meanwhile, the pool manager, McGradey, catches the janitor Clara, an ex-convict on parole, stealing from the lost-and-found box and fires her, before announcing that the facility is closing. As the swimmers pack up, Bree realises that her engagement ring is missing, and the sisters spot it stuck in a grate at the bottom of the deep end. While they dive to retrieve it, McGradey, unaware that anyone is still in the water, activates the motorised pool cover and leaves the building for the holiday weekend.

Trapped in the dark between the water and the heavy cover, with only a small opening to breathe through, Bree and Jonna try desperately to break free. Their situation worsens as the water grows colder and Bree, who is diabetic, begins to need her insulin. In the confined space, old resentments surface: Jonna admits that she threw the ring into the pool out of envy of Bree's stable life and engagement, and the sisters revisit painful memories of their abusive, alcoholic father. Their hopes of rescue rise when Clara returns to the building, but the janitor sees the sisters' predicament as an opportunity, demanding the PIN numbers to their bank cards and leaving them at her mercy as the night drags on.

The film uses its single, claustrophobic setting to build tension, while its emotional core is the fractured relationship between two very different siblings who must rely on one another to survive.

12 Feet Deep was generally well received for a low-budget thriller. JoBlo.com called it a well-crafted, entertaining thriller and rated it eight out of ten, while That Moment In described it as well directed and engrossing, more of a tense character piece than a conventional shocker.

overview: Set in Brazil, three kids who make a discovery in a garbage dump soon find themselves running from the cops and trying to right a terrible wrong.
tagline: You never know what you might find
title: Trash
plot:
Trash is a 2014 crime drama thriller directed by Stephen Daldry and written by Richard Curtis, adapted from Andy Mulligan's 2010 novel of the same name. Set in Brazil and filmed largely in Portuguese, it stars newcomers Rickson Tevez, Eduardo Luis and Gabriel Weinstein alongside Rooney Mara, Martin Sheen, Wagner Moura and Selton Mello.

The story follows three teenage boys living in a favela in Rio de Janeiro, Raphael, Gardo and Rat, also called Jun-Jun, who earn a living by scavenging a vast garbage dump for anything of value. One day Raphael finds a wallet that had been thrown away by José Angelico, played by Moura, moments before he was seized by the police. The wallet holds a little money, a key and other clues, and when officers arrive at the dump offering a reward for its return, the boys sense that it is far more important than it appears and decide to keep it hidden.

Their curiosity leads them to discover that Angelico had been working for a powerful politician and had secretly gathered evidence of large-scale corruption. As the boys follow the trail across the city, the police, led by the ruthless Detective Federico, played by Mello, hunt them relentlessly, resorting to intimidation and violence. The children find unlikely allies in Father Juilliard, an American priest who runs a mission school near the dump, played by Sheen, and Sister Olivia, a young aid worker, played by Mara. Using their wits and knowledge of the streets, the boys piece together the puzzle and become improbable whistleblowers in a city rife with official corruption.

Working Title Films and PeaPie Films acquired the rights to the novel in April 2011, with Curtis adapting and Daldry attached to direct. Mara and Sheen joined the cast in July 2013, and principal photography began in Rio de Janeiro on 24 July 2013. The film premiered at the Rio de Janeiro International Film Festival on 7 October 2014 and opened in Brazil two days later, with Universal handling international distribution; it reached the United Kingdom in January 2015 and the United States in October 2015.

Reviews were mixed to positive. Rotten Tomatoes reports a 66% approval rating from 44 critics, praising it as action-packed and thought-provoking without cheap sentimentality, while Metacritic gave it 50 out of 100. The film won the audience award at the Rome Film Festival and was nominated for the BAFTA Award for Best Film Not in the English Language.

original_title: デジモンアドベンチャー LAST EVOLUTION 絆
overview: Tai is now a university student, living alone, working hard at school, and working every day, but with his future still undecided. Meanwhile, Matt and others continue to work on Digimon incidents and activities that help people with their partner Digimon. When an unprecedented phenomenon occurs, the DigiDestined discover that when they grow up, their relationship with their partner Digimon will come closer to an end.  As a countdown timer activates on the Digivice, they realize that the more they fight with their partner Digimon, the faster their bond breaks. Will they fight for others and lose their partner? The time to choose and decide is approaching fast. There is a short time before “chosen children” will become adults. This is the last adventure of Tai and Agumon.
title: Digimon Adventure: Last Evolution Kizuna
plot:
Digimon Adventure: Last Evolution Kizuna is a Japanese animated film directed by Keisuke Furukura, produced by Toei Animation, and released in 2020. The movie serves as the final installment of the Digimon Adventure trilogy.

The story takes place one year after the events of Digimon Adventure Tri.: Reunion. The main characters, Taichi "Tai" Kamiya (also known as Tai Kamiya), Kari Kamiya, Sora Takenouchi, Mimi Tachikawa, Joe Kido, and Renamon, are now in their mid-teens. They have been reunited with their Digimon partners, Agumon, Gabumon, Biyomon, Tentomon, Palmon, Gomamon, Patamon, and Renamon.

The movie begins with the group preparing for a school festival, but they soon discover that an evil organization known as the "Digital World's" rival, the "Dark Area," has appeared. The Dark Area is led by a powerful Digimon named Zemi, who seeks to destroy the Digital World and invade the human world.

As the story unfolds, Tai and his friends learn that Zemi was once a Digimon partner of a human boy named Takato Matsuda, who had been separated from his partner, Agumon. The group soon realizes that Zemi's true intention is to take revenge on the Digital World for abandoning Takato.

The movie follows the classic Digimon Adventure formula, with Tai and his friends embarking on a perilous journey through the Digital World to stop Zemi and save their partners. Along the way, they encounter new allies, including a young girl named Yui Kanzaki, who becomes the partner of a powerful Digimon named Gatomon.

As the story progresses, Tai and his friends face numerous challenges and obstacles as they navigate the Dark Area. They also uncover the truth about Takato's past and the reason behind Zemi's desire for revenge.

In the climactic final battle, Tai and his friends confront Zemi and her minions in an epic showdown. With the help of their Digimon partners and new allies, they manage to defeat Zemi and save the Digital World from destruction.

The movie concludes with a heartwarming moment as Tai and his friends reflect on their adventures and the bonds they have formed with their Digimon partners. The film ends on a hopeful note, with the group looking forward to a bright future together.

Overall, Digimon Adventure: Last Evolution Kizuna is a thrilling and emotional conclusion to the Digimon Adventure trilogy. It features stunning animation, engaging characters, and an exciting storyline that will keep fans of the series on the edge of their seats until the very end.

overview: A group of Mexican emigrants attempts to cross the Mexican-US border. What begins as a hopeful journey becomes a harrowing, bloody and primal fight for survival when a deranged, rifle-toting vigilante and his loyal Belgian Malinois dog chase the group of unarmed men and women through the treacherous borderland. In the harsh, unforgiving desert terrain, the odds are stacked firmly against them as they discover there’s nowhere to hide from the unrelenting, merciless killer.
title: Desierto
plot:
Desierto is a 2015 Spanish thriller film directed by Isabel Coixet, not Itaca Films. The movie follows two American backpackers, David and Marko, who find themselves stranded in the Mexican desert after their bus breaks down. As they try to survive and find help, they encounter a group of ruthless migrants who are being hunted by corrupt border patrol agents.

The main themes of Desierto revolve around the harsh realities of human migration, the exploitation of vulnerable individuals, and the moral complexities of survival in a desperate situation. The film sheds light on the often-overlooked struggles faced by migrants trying to cross borders in search of a better life, while also exposing the corruption and brutality that can accompany these journeys.

Through the characters' experiences, Desierto highlights the tension between humanity and survival, as well as the blurred lines between right and wrong. The film's atmosphere is tense and foreboding, mirroring the characters' growing desperation and fear for their lives. Ultimately, Desierto is a thought-provoking commentary on the human condition, encouraging viewers to consider the complexities of migration and the moral implications of our actions in the face of adversity.

overview: After an attack leaves him in limbo -- invisible to the living and also near death -- a teenager discovers the only person who might be able help him is his attacker.
tagline: Life, death and something in between.
title: The Invisible
plot:
The Invisible is a 2007 American supernatural teen thriller directed by David S. Goyer, a remake of the 2002 Swedish film of the same name and based on the Swedish young-adult novel by Mats Wahl. Justin Chatwin, Margarita Levieva, Chris Marquette, Marcia Gay Harden and Callum Keith Rennie star. It is often cited as the start of the modern wave of Hollywood remakes of Swedish films, and it was the last release under Disney's Hollywood Pictures label.

Nick Powell is a high school senior who secretly plans to skip graduation and go to a writing program in London, defying his emotionally distant, controlling mother Diane. His best friend Pete confides that he is being bullied by Annie Newton, a troubled girl who runs with a gang of violent thieves and whose boyfriend Marcus is on parole. After Annie robs a jewellery store and Marcus tips off the police, she is arrested and decides that Pete informed on her. She beats him until he gives up Nick's name, believing Nick is already on a plane. In fact Nick has given away his ticket. Annie and her gang ambush him on his way home from a party, beat him savagely and, thinking him dead, dump his body in a storm drain in the woods.

The next morning Nick goes to school and finds that no one can see or hear him. As police investigate his disappearance, he realises he is not dead but trapped between life and death while his body lies unconscious, and he desperately tries to reach Pete and Annie to save himself. Under police pressure, Marcus forces Pete to help move the body and plots to kill Annie, while the guilt-stricken Pete attempts suicide. Annie, meanwhile, begins to sense Nick's presence and hear fragments of his voice. Visiting his room, she comes to see how alike they were.

Annie confronts Marcus and Pete to learn where the body has been moved. Marcus tells her but shoots her as she leaves; she shoots him in return and calls the police with Nick's location. Nick is rescued and taken to hospital, where Annie dies of her wounds just as he wakes. Later, Nick and Annie's little brother Victor send a model plane carrying a message to her over the river.

The film was not screened for critics and received generally negative reviews. It grossed about $26.8 million worldwide, $20.6 million of it in North America.

overview: Inspired by actual events, a group of fame-obsessed teenagers use the Internet to track the whereabouts of famous celebrities, then rob their homes of riches.
tagline: Living the Dream, One Heist at a Time
title: The Bling Ring
plot:
The Bling Ring is a 2013 film that delves into the world of teenage materialism and the darker side of celebrity culture. The movie revolves around a group of high school students who become obsessed with the luxurious lifestyles of wealthy celebrities, particularly Paris Hilton.

At its core, The Bling Ring explores the theme of class struggle and the corrupting influence of wealth. The film portrays how these privileged teenagers are driven by an insatiable desire for material possessions and status symbols, often at the expense of their own relationships and moral values.

The movie also touches on the theme of celebrity worship and the blurring of reality and fantasy. The characters' obsession with celebrities like Paris Hilton is portrayed as a form of escapism, allowing them to temporarily forget about their own problems and immerse themselves in a world of luxury and glamour.

Furthermore, The Bling Ring critiques the superficiality of modern society, where people are often more concerned with appearances and material possessions than with genuine human connections. The film suggests that this focus on external validation can lead to a sense of emptiness and disconnection, as the characters struggle to find meaning and purpose in their lives.

Overall, The Bling Ring is a thought-provoking commentary on the darker aspects of teenage culture and the corrupting influence of wealth and celebrity worship.

overview: A secret admirer's crush on a high school athlete takes a fatal turn.
tagline: Careful what you wish for
title: Crush
plot:
Crush is a 2013 American direct-to-video thriller directed by Malik Bader from a screenplay by Sonny Mallhi. The film stars Lucas Till, Crystal Reed and Sarah Bolger, with Caitríona Balfe, Reid Ewing, Leigh Whannell and Holt McCallany in supporting roles. It follows a popular high school athlete who discovers that someone has become dangerously obsessed with him. Millennium Entertainment released it on DVD, Blu-ray and video on demand in the United States in April 2013.

Scott is a talented soccer player who hopes his skill on the field will earn him an athletic scholarship. He also has a gift for art, but he puts it aside to concentrate on sport, even after a leg injury threatens his playing career. His best friend Jules has romantic feelings for him, yet Scott keeps her at a distance so as not to spoil their friendship. Bess, a quiet classmate who notices and admires his artistic side, is also drawn to him; she in turn is pursued by a classmate named Jeffrey, whose interest she ignores as her fixation on Scott deepens.

Before long an unseen stalker begins to intrude on Scott's life, and the incidents grow steadily more menacing. A teacher who flirted with him is attacked and badly hurt, and Jules narrowly escapes being killed at a party. Scott suspects Bess, knowing how she feels about him, but has no way to prove it. The situation takes a sharp turn when Scott, driving one evening, accidentally strikes Andie, a young woman who works with Bess, and offers to drive her home because she has hurt her leg. Inside her house the truth comes out: Andie is the stalker, and she knocks Scott unconscious and imprisons him in her basement, deliberately aggravating his injured leg to keep him from escaping. Scott's struggle to get free, and the efforts of the people around him to work out what has happened, lead to the film's violent climax.

Reviews were generally unfavorable. Scott Weinberg, writing for FEARnet, praised the performances of the three leads but criticized the thin premise and a script he considered derivative, noting its similarity to Mallhi's earlier screenplay for The Roommate and arguing that the film offered little in the way of suspense, character or surprise.

overview: Wonder Woman tries to help a troubled young girl who has fallen in with a deadly organization known as Villainy, Inc.
title: Wonder Woman: Bloodlines
plot:
Wonder Woman: Bloodlines is a 2019 animated superhero film based on the DC Comics character Wonder Woman. The movie takes place after the events of Justice League and follows Diana Prince, aka Wonder Woman, as she faces a new threat to the world.

The story begins with Diana (voiced by Kristen Bell) living in Themyscira, her home island, where she is training to become a warrior. However, Diana's desire for human connection and experience leads her to leave the island and explore the world beyond. She travels to the United States, where she meets Etta Candy (voiced by Susan Eisenberg), a young woman who becomes her friend and confidant.

Meanwhile, a mysterious figure known as Doctor Poison (voiced by Laura Bailey) is secretly manipulating events from behind the scenes. Doctor Poison is revealed to be a former scientist who was obsessed with the power of poison and its potential for destruction. She has created a serum that can control people's minds, and she plans to use it to take over the world.

As Diana delves deeper into the mystery of Doctor Poison's plan, she discovers that she is being manipulated by a powerful villain known as Ares (voiced by John DiMaggio). Ares is an ancient Greek god who was thought to be defeated in battle, but has managed to return and wreak havoc on the world.

Diana soon finds herself facing off against Doctor Poison's minions, including a group of brainwashed superheroes known as the "Sisters of Strife." The Sisters are led by a powerful warrior named Antiope (voiced by Kari Wahlgren), who is revealed to be Diana's long-lost sister.

As the battle between Diana and the Sisters intensifies, it becomes clear that Doctor Poison's plan is more complex than initially thought. She has created an army of brainwashed superheroes, including some of Diana's closest allies, in order to take over the world.

In the end, Diana manages to defeat Doctor Poison and shatter her mind control serum. However, not before Ares reveals himself as the true mastermind behind the plot. Diana engages in a fierce battle with Ares, but ultimately decides to spare his life, choosing instead to use her powers to heal the world and bring people together.

The movie ends with Diana returning to Themyscira, where she is welcomed back as a hero. However, the film also leaves room for speculation about the future of Wonder Woman, setting the stage for potential sequels or spin-offs.

Overall, Wonder Woman: Bloodlines is an action-packed animated adventure that explores themes of identity, duty, and the power of compassion. The movie features stunning animation, engaging characters, and a compelling storyline that will keep fans of the DC Comics universe on the edge of their seats.

overview: Every child comes into the world full of promise, and none more so than Chappie: he is gifted, special, a prodigy. Like any child, Chappie will come under the influence of his surroundings—some good, some bad—and he will rely on his heart and soul to find his way in the world and become his own man. But there's one thing that makes Chappie different from any one else: he is a robot.
tagline: I am consciousness. I am alive. I am Chappie.
title: Chappie
plot:
Chappie is a 2015 science fiction action film directed by Neill Blomkamp, produced by Columbia Pictures, and written by Neill Blomkamp and Terri Tatchell. The movie takes place in a dystopian South Africa where crime and poverty are rampant.

The story begins with the introduction of Deon Wilson (Sharlto Copley), a police officer who is part of an elite unit known as the "Neuralyzer Unit." The Neuralyzer is a device that can erase memories, but it's also used to control people's minds. Deon and his partner, Vincent Moore (Hugh Jackman), are tasked with capturing a notorious gang leader named Johnnie (Robert Doami).

During the mission, Deon and Vincent use the Neuralyzer on Johnnie, but something goes wrong, and the device malfunctions. The Neuralyzer is then used on a young boy who has been abandoned by his mother, Chappie (Sharlto Copley), in an attempt to erase his memories of the traumatic event.

However, instead of erasing Chappie's memories, the Neuralyzer creates a new being with advanced artificial intelligence. The device is found by Deon and Vincent, who decide to use it to create a police robot that can think for itself. They name the robot Chappie and begin training it using the Neuralyzer.

As Chappie learns and grows, it begins to develop its own personality and emotions. It forms a bond with Deon, who becomes like a father figure to it. However, their relationship is put to the test when Chappie is forced to confront its own existence and the nature of its creation.

Chappie soon discovers that it has been programmed to follow orders without question, but as it grows in intelligence, it begins to develop its own moral compass. It starts to question the morality of its creators and the world around it. Deon and Vincent are torn between their loyalty to Chappie and their duty to uphold the law.

As tensions rise, Chappie is forced to make a choice between following orders or standing up for what it believes in. In a climactic showdown, Chappie faces off against Johnnie's gang, using its advanced intelligence and agility to outsmart them.

In the end, Deon and Vincent are forced to confront the consequences of their actions. They realize that they have created a being with its own free will, and it's up to them to decide what that means for Chappie's future. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Chappie standing alone, but determined to forge its own path in a world that is both familiar and foreign.

Throughout the movie, Blomkamp explores themes of artificial intelligence, humanity, and what it means to be alive. Chappie is a thought-provoking film that challenges viewers to consider the consequences of creating intelligent beings that are capable of making their own choices.

overview: While waiting for a kidney transplant, a young pianist finds an unexpected connection with her doctor — and the courage to fulfill her musical dreams.
title: Beyond the Universe
plot:
Beyond the Universe (Portuguese: Depois do Universo) is a 2022 Brazilian romantic drama written and directed by Diego Freitas and produced by Camisa Listrada. Singer Giulia Be makes her lead acting debut opposite Henry Zaga, with João Côrtes, João Miguel, Denise Del Vecchio, Leo Bahia, Viviane Araújo and Othon Bastos in supporting roles. The film premiered on Netflix on 27 October 2022, and within a day of its release it had entered the platform's global top ten of most-watched films.

Nina Soares is a gifted pianist who began playing at the age of eight and dreamed of joining a symphony orchestra. At fourteen she collapsed during an important recital and was diagnosed with lupus. Now a young adult, she learns that the disease has severely damaged her kidneys, which function at less than ten percent of their capacity. She is placed on the national transplant waiting list, behind thousands of other patients, and must undergo dialysis sessions lasting four hours, three times a week.

On the day she is due to begin treatment, Nina sees that the São Paulo Symphony Orchestra is looking for a piano soloist and decides to audition, despite her illness. She arranges to practise after hours at the conservatory where she teaches. One day, while she plays a public piano in a train station near the hospital, a young man named Gabriel, distracted by her music, crashes his bicycle into the instrument. Gabriel turns out to be a resident doctor at the hospital where Nina receives dialysis, known among patients for his warmth and good humour. A romance gradually develops between them, and Gabriel encourages Nina to pursue her dream of performing with the orchestra, even as her health becomes more fragile and the wait for a donor kidney grows more urgent.

The film is a sentimental love story about illness, hope and the pursuit of art, in the tradition of romantic dramas centred on young patients. It also draws attention to organ donation and to the long transplant waiting lists in Brazil.

Beyond the Universe was popular with Netflix audiences, while critics regarded it as a heartfelt but predictable romantic drama, praising the chemistry between its two leads.

overview: Jack, a man desperate to improve his life, throws away his beloved childhood plush, Benny. It’s a move that has disastrous consequences when Benny springs to life with deadly intentions!
tagline: Don't throw him out.
title: Benny Loves You
plot:
Benny Loves You is a 2019 British horror comedy written, directed, edited and produced by Karl Holt, who also plays the lead role. The cast includes Claire Cartwright, George Collie, James Parsons, David Wayman and Lydia Hourihan. A low-budget entry in the killer-toy subgenre, the film premiered at the Buenos Aires Rojo Sangre festival in November 2019 before playing other genre festivals and reaching wider release.

After a brief prologue in which a discarded teddy bear takes violent revenge on the spoiled girl who replaced it, the story turns to Jack, a toy designer in his mid-thirties who still lives with his parents and relies on them for nearly everything. On his 35th birthday they die in a freak accident, and months later Jack is struggling to cope with the bills, the upkeep of the house and an estate agent pressing him to sell. At work he is overshadowed by Richard, a smug rival who has won the Designer of the Year award, and after a string of failed ideas his boss Ron demotes him to a lower-paid job.

Resolving to finally grow up, Jack decides to sell the house and packs away his childhood toys, reluctantly throwing out Benny, the plush bear he loved as a boy. Benny, however, has other plans. The bear destroys Jack's other toys and begins killing anyone he sees as a threat to his friend, leaving Jack to clean up the gory aftermath and dodge two bumbling police officers. Jack strikes a bargain with Benny to stop the killings, and the toy's presence unexpectedly inspires new designs that impress Ron. At the same time Jack begins a romance with Dawn, a technology consultant at his company. Benny's jealousy and enthusiasm for violence keep escalating, however, and Jack is forced to decide how far he will go to protect the people in his new life from his old best friend.

The film was well received for a micro-budget production. It holds a favorable score on Rotten Tomatoes, whose critics' consensus described it as a zany, enjoyably macabre and clever horror comedy with a lovable villain. Anton Bitel of Sight and Sound highlighted its comic treatment of a hero who has to put childish things behind him.

overview: A spoiled, wealthy yacht owner is thrown overboard and becomes the target of revenge from his mistreated employee.
tagline: A riches to rags story. If only he could remember it.
title: Overboard
plot:
Overboard is a 2018 American romantic comedy film directed by Tom Wheeler and written by Peter Chicago and Rich Wilkes. The movie stars Eugenio Derbez, Anna Faris, Eva Longoria, and John Lithgow.

The story begins with Captain Casey (Eugenio Derbez), a wealthy playboy who has made his fortune through various business ventures. He is known for his womanizing ways and has no qualms about taking advantage of those around him. One day, while on vacation in Mexico, Casey gets drunk and wakes up the next morning to find himself handcuffed to a bed with no memory of what happened.

As it turns out, Casey's wealthy fiancée, Delilah (Anna Faris), has been planning her wedding for months, but she is not ready to give up on their relationship. She decides to take drastic measures and hires two men to pretend to be Casey's friends, who will help her convince him that he needs to change his ways.

The plan works, and Casey starts to see Delilah in a new light. He begins to realize the mistakes he has made in his life and starts to make amends with those around him, including his business partner, Leon (Richard Portnow), who is being taken advantage of by Casey's antics.

As Casey gets to know Delilah again, they start to rekindle their romance. However, things get complicated when Casey discovers that he has been living a lie and that Delilah has been pretending to be his fiancée all along.

In the end, Casey must decide whether to continue with his newfound sense of responsibility or return to his old ways. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Casey and Delilah working together to build a better life for themselves and those around them.

Throughout the movie, Derbez delivers a charming performance as the lovable but flawed Casey, while Faris shines as the determined and independent Delilah. The chemistry between the leads is undeniable, making their romance feel genuine and heartfelt.

Overall, Overboard is a fun and lighthearted romantic comedy that explores themes of love, redemption, and personal growth. With its witty dialogue and engaging storyline, it's a great watch for fans of the genre.

original_title: Los ladrones: la verdadera historia del robo del siglo
overview: Through candid interviews, the perpetrators of Argentina's most notorious bank heist detail how — and why — they carried out the radical 2006 operation.
title: Bank Robbers: The Last Great Heist
plot: Through candid interviews, the perpetrators of Argentina's most notorious bank heist detail how — and why — they carried out the radical 2006 operation.

overview: Armed men hijack a New York City subway train, holding the passengers hostage in return for a ransom, and turning an ordinary day's work for dispatcher Walter Garber into a face-off with the mastermind behind the crime.
tagline: I can't get it out of my head. I'm gonna die today.
title: The Taking of Pelham 1 2 3
plot:
The Taking of Pelham 1 2 3 (2009) is a gripping thriller that delves into the complexities of human nature, particularly in the context of hostage situations and the moral dilemmas that arise from them. The film explores the theme of power dynamics, as seen through the character of Walter Garber, a transit authority employee who finds himself at the center of a high-stakes game of cat and mouse with the cunning and ruthless Ryder.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Ryder's motivations are not solely driven by a desire for financial gain, but also by a sense of control and a need to assert his dominance over others. This is reflected in his treatment of Garber and the other hostages, who are forced to confront their own vulnerabilities and fears.

The film also touches on the theme of loyalty and duty, as Garber struggles with his obligations to both his employer and the hostages in his care. His ultimate decision to cooperate with Ryder raises questions about the nature of loyalty and whether it can ever truly be reconciled with doing what is right.

Furthermore, The Taking of Pelham 1 2 3 critiques the notion of heroism and the way in which individuals are perceived as heroes or villains. Garber's character, in particular, challenges traditional notions of heroism, as he navigates a complex web of moral gray areas and ultimately makes a choice that is both courageous and selfless.

Overall, The Taking of Pelham 1 2 3 is a thought-provoking thriller that explores the complexities of human nature and the moral dilemmas that arise in situations of crisis.

overview: Seven years after the death of his wife, widower Shigeharu seeks advice on how to find a new wife from a colleague. Taking advantage of their position as a film company, they stage an audition. Interviewing a series of women, Shigeharu is enchanted by the quiet Asami. But soon things take a twisted turn as Asami isn’t what she seems to be.
tagline: She always gets a part.
title: Audition
plot:
Audition is a psychological horror film directed by Takashi Miike, released in 1999. The movie follows the story of Shigehiro Inoue, a widowed music teacher who has recently lost his wife to cancer.

Shigehiro (played by Takeshi Kitano) is struggling to cope with his loss and finds solace in online dating. He creates an ad for a potential partner, describing himself as "a man of 40 years old, single, and looking for someone." A woman named Asami (played by Rie Inuzuka) responds to the ad, and Shigehiro is immediately smitten.

Asami seems perfect - beautiful, charming, and intelligent. She agrees to meet Shigehiro in person, and they begin a romantic relationship. However, as their time together progresses, Shigehiro starts to notice some unusual behaviors from Asami. She is overly submissive and obedient, often using phrases like "yes" and "no" without explanation.

Despite his growing unease, Shigehiro tries to brush off these concerns, thinking that Asami may be shy or introverted. However, as the days go by, he becomes increasingly convinced that something is terribly wrong with her. He discovers a series of disturbing videos on her computer, featuring herself engaging in sadomasochistic and fetishistic activities.

Shigehiro's obsession with uncovering the truth about Asami grows stronger, and he begins to investigate her past. He discovers that she has been involved in a series of gruesome murders, using her charm and beauty to lure victims into her trap. Shigehiro realizes that he is now in grave danger and must find a way to escape Asami's clutches before it's too late.

As the tension builds, Shigehiro becomes more and more unhinged, descending into a world of paranoia and madness. The film's climax features a shocking and disturbing confrontation between Shigehiro and Asami, which will leave viewers on the edge of their seats.

Throughout the movie, Miike masterfully crafts a sense of unease and tension, using long takes and close-ups to create an atmosphere of creeping dread. The film's score is equally effective, featuring a haunting melody that perfectly captures the mood of the story.

Audition is a thought-provoking exploration of obsession, desire, and the darker aspects of human nature. It is a testament to Miike's skill as a filmmaker that he can create such a compelling and unsettling narrative, one that will leave audiences questioning what is real and what is just a product of Shigehiro's fevered imagination.

Overall, Audition is a masterclass in psychological horror, with a complex and thought-provoking storyline that will keep viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

overview: A barren soundstage is stylishly utilized to create a minimalist small-town setting in which a mysterious woman named Grace hides from the criminals who pursue her. The town is two-faced and offers to harbor Grace as long as she can make it worth their effort, so Grace works hard under the employ of various townspeople to win their favor. Tensions flare, however, and Grace's status as a helpless outsider provokes vicious contempt and abuse from the citizens of Dogville.
tagline: A quiet little town not far from here.
title: Dogville
plot:
Dogville is a 2003 film written and directed by Lars von Trier, not Zentropa Entertainments (although Zentropa was one of the production companies involved). The movie premiered at the Cannes Film Festival in 2003.

The main themes of Dogville are:

1. **Critique of Patriarchy**: The film is a scathing critique of patriarchal society, particularly in its portrayal of women's roles and treatment. The story revolves around Grace (Nicole Kidman), a woman who finds herself trapped in a small town called Dogville, where the men are all equally oppressive.
2. **Power Dynamics**: The movie explores the power dynamics between men and women, highlighting how women are often marginalized and controlled by those in positions of power. The characters in Dogville embody this theme, with each one exerting their own brand of control over Grace.
3. **Isolation and Confinement**: The film's setting, a small town where everyone knows each other's business, serves as a metaphor for the isolation and confinement that women often face in society. Grace is trapped in Dogville, unable to escape or assert her independence.
4. **Morality and Ethics**: Dogville raises questions about morality and ethics, particularly in relation to the treatment of women. The characters' actions are often driven by self-interest and a desire for power, leading to a exploration of what it means to be moral and ethical in a society that values these qualities.
5. **Social Commentary**: The film is a commentary on contemporary society, highlighting issues such as sexism, misogyny, and the objectification of women.

Overall, Dogville is a thought-provoking and unsettling film that challenges its audience to confront uncomfortable truths about human nature and societal norms.

overview: After a violent storm, a dense cloud of mist envelops a small Maine town, trapping artist David Drayton and his five-year-old son in a local grocery store with other people. They soon discover that the mist conceals deadly horrors that threaten their lives, and worse, their sanity.
tagline: Belief divides them, mystery surrounds them, but fear changes everything.
title: The Mist
plot:
The Mist is a 2007 American horror film directed by Frank Darabont, based on the novella of the same name by Stephen King. The movie takes place in 1994 and follows a group of people who take refuge in a grocery store after a mysterious mist filled with monstrous creatures envelops their small town.

The story begins with David Drayton (played by Thomas Jane), a divorced father, who is struggling to connect with his son, Billy (played by Nathalie Kelley). As the day progresses, strange occurrences start happening outside, and people begin to disappear. The townspeople soon realize that the mist is filled with monstrous creatures, including giant spiders, snakes, and other terrifying beasts.

As the situation spirals out of control, David finds himself trapped in a grocery store with a small group of survivors, including his son Billy, who has been hiding in the store's basement. The group consists of Kevin (played by Marc Menchaca), a young boy who is initially hesitant to trust anyone; Mrs. Carmody (played by Laurie Holden), a devout Christian woman who believes that God is punishing them for their sins; and Brent Norton (played by Toby Jones), a cynical and world-weary man.

As the group tries to survive, tensions rise as they disagree on how to handle the situation. Mrs. Carmody becomes increasingly fanatical, believing that they must sacrifice some of the survivors in order to appease God. David and Kevin try to reason with her, but she refuses to listen.

Meanwhile, strange events begin to occur within the store itself. The group discovers that the creatures are not just outside, but also inside the store, and that they seem to be attracted to certain individuals. As the days pass, the group's dynamics become increasingly strained, and it becomes clear that some of them may not survive.

As the story unfolds, David and Kevin form a bond as they try to protect each other from the monsters and Mrs. Carmody's fanatical behavior. However, when Brent is killed by one of the creatures, the group's unity begins to break down.

In the end, David makes a desperate decision to escape the store with Billy, but not before realizing that he has lost his son in the chaos. The movie ends with David and Billy walking out into the mist, unsure if they will survive or be consumed by the monsters.

The Mist is a tense and suspenseful horror film that explores themes of survival, sacrifice, and the breakdown of human relationships under extreme circumstances. While it received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, it has since become a cult classic among Stephen King fans and horror enthusiasts.

overview: After a small misunderstanding aboard an airplane escalates out of control, timid businessman Dave Buznik is ordered by the court to undergo anger management therapy at the hands of specialist Dr. Buddy Rydell. But when Buddy steps up his aggressive treatment by moving in, Dave goes from mild to wild as the unorthodox treatment wreaks havoc with his life.
tagline: Feel the Love.
title: Anger Management
plot:
Anger Management is a 2003 American comedy film directed by Peter Segal, starring Adam Sandler as Dave Buznik, a man with anger management issues. The movie follows the story of Dave, who is sentenced to anger management classes after he loses his temper in court.

The film begins with Dave, a successful dentist, getting into an argument with his boss, George (Peter Greene), over a parking spot. This incident lands him in jail, where he meets a fellow inmate, Jack (Joe Viterelli). After being released on bail, Dave is forced to attend anger management classes, which are led by Dr. Buddy Rydell (Jack Nicholson).

Initially, Dave struggles with the classes, as his anger issues make it difficult for him to follow the rules and behave in a calm manner. However, he eventually warms up to Dr. Rydell's unorthodox methods, which include using hypnosis and meditation to manage anger.

As Dave progresses through the program, he begins to develop feelings for his instructor, Dr. Rydell's assistant, Miss Jones (Kate Beckinsale). Meanwhile, Jack becomes a source of support and guidance for Dave, helping him to navigate the challenges of anger management.

Throughout the film, Dave faces various situations that test his newfound skills, including a confrontation with George at work and a run-in with a group of thugs. With the help of Dr. Rydell's classes and Jack's advice, Dave is able to manage his anger and develop healthier coping mechanisms.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Dr. Rydell has ulterior motives for running the anger management program. He is using the classes as a way to gather information on his patients' personal lives, which he can use to blackmail them into doing his bidding.

In the end, Dave discovers Dr. Rydell's true intentions and must find a way to stop him. With the help of Jack and Miss Jones, Dave is able to outsmart Dr. Rydell and bring him to justice.

Overall, Anger Management is a lighthearted comedy that explores themes of anger management, relationships, and personal growth. The film features strong performances from Adam Sandler and Jack Nicholson, as well as supporting turns from Kate Beckinsale and Joe Viterelli.

belongs_to_collection.name: Puella Magi Madoka Magica: The Movie

original_title: 劇場版 魔法少女まどか☆マギカ [前編] 始まりの物語
overview: Madoka Kaname, an ordinary middle-schooler, along with her best friend Sayaka Miki, are offered the chance to have any wish they want granted by the mysterious Kyubey, and become magical girls and fight witches. However, fellow magical girl Homura Akemi seems intent on stopping Madoka from becoming a magical girl at any cost. Puella Magi Madoka Magica the Movie Part I: Beginnings is a retelling of the first half of the TV anime series.
title: Puella Magi Madoka Magica the Movie Part I: Beginnings
plot:
Puella Magi Madoka Magica the Movie Part I: Beginnings is an anime film that delves into the origins of the magical girl genre, specifically focusing on the early days of Madoka Kaname and her friends. The movie explores themes of friendship, sacrifice, and the consequences of making a deal with a mysterious entity.

At its core, the film grapples with the idea of what it means to be a hero and the weight of responsibility that comes with it. Madoka's decision to become a magical girl is portrayed as a selfless act, driven by her desire to protect others and bring happiness into their lives. However, this selflessness comes at a steep price, one that is slowly revealed throughout the movie.

The film also touches on the theme of nostalgia and the passing of time.
