Screen Media Films released the film theatrically in November 2021. It received mixed reviews; Rotten Tomatoes reported 65% approval from 17 critics, while RogerEbert.com's Brian Tallerico called it an easy, forgettable B-movie watch.

overview: Superhero duo Scott Lang and Hope Van Dyne, together with Hope's parents Hank Pym and Janet Van Dyne, find themselves exploring the Quantum Realm, interacting with strange new creatures, and embarking on an adventure that will push them beyond the limits of what they thought was possible.
title: Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania
plot:
Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania is a 2023 American superhero film based on the Marvel Comics characters Scott Lang / Ant-Man and Hope van Dyne / Wasp. Produced by Marvel Studios and distributed by Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures, it is the sequel to Ant-Man (2015) and Ant-Man and the Wasp (2018) and the 31st film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, opening the franchise's Phase Five. Peyton Reed directed from a screenplay by Jeff Loveness. Paul Rudd and Evangeline Lilly return in the title roles, alongside Jonathan Majors as Kang the Conqueror, Kathryn Newton, David Dastmalchian, Katy O'Brian, William Jackson Harper, Bill Murray, Michelle Pfeiffer, Corey Stoll and Michael Douglas.

Some time after the Avengers' victory over Thanos, Scott is enjoying life as a celebrity and the author of a memoir, living happily with Hope. His teenage daughter Cassie has become an activist helping people displaced by the Blip, which has strained their relationship. During a visit to Hope's parents, Hank Pym and Janet van Dyne, Cassie reveals a device she has built to send signals into the Quantum Realm. Janet, alarmed, tries to switch it off, but the signal has already been received, and a portal pulls all five of them into the subatomic world.

Separated on arrival, Scott and Cassie fall in with a band of native rebels resisting the realm's ruler, while Hope, Hank and Janet travel to a sprawling city where an old acquaintance of Janet's, Lord Krylar, reveals he now serves a conqueror named Kang. Janet is finally forced to admit what she kept secret for decades: during her years trapped in the realm she met Kang, a powerful exiled man who claimed he wanted to escape, and she helped strand him there after discovering his true nature. Kang's forces, led by the cybernetically altered M.O.D.O.K., who turns out to be the former villain Darren Cross, capture Scott and demand his help in retrieving a power source that would let Kang escape and threaten the multiverse.

The film grossed about $476 million worldwide, but it received mixed to negative reviews. Critics praised Majors's menacing performance and Rudd's charm but criticized the visual effects, the script and the film's role as a setup for later Marvel installments rather than a satisfying story on its own.

overview: San Francisco's premiere wedding planner, Mary Fiore is rescued from an accident by the man of her dreams, paediatrician Steve Edison, only to find he is the fiancé of her latest client. As Mary continues making the wedding arrangements, she and Steve are put into a string of uncomfortable situations that force them to face their mutual attraction.
production_companies: IMF Internationale Medien und Film GmbH & Co. Produktions KG
tagline: His big day is her big problem.
title: The Wedding Planner
plot:
The Wedding Planner is a romantic comedy that explores the complexities of love, relationships, and personal growth. At its core, the film delves into the theme of self-discovery, as the protagonist, Mary Fiore, navigates her way through a series of unfulfilling relationships and discovers her true passions.

As Mary prepares for a string of high-profile weddings, she finds herself drawn to her boss, Dr. Steve Edison, who is initially portrayed as a cynical and emotionally unavailable man. However, as the story unfolds, their mutual attraction grows, and they begin to confront their own emotional baggage.

The film also touches on the theme of identity, as Mary struggles to balance her desire for independence with her need for connection and love. Through her relationships with Steve and her friends, she learns to let go of her fears and take risks, ultimately discovering a sense of purpose and fulfillment.

Furthermore, The Wedding Planner explores the idea of love being a journey, rather than a destination. Mary and Steve's relationship is not a traditional fairy tale romance, but rather a slow-burning, imperfect connection that requires effort and vulnerability to sustain.

Overall, the film's themes are woven together by its lighthearted tone, witty dialogue, and strong performances from the leads. While it may not be a deeply profound or complex exploration of human nature, The Wedding Planner is a charming and engaging romantic comedy that celebrates the beauty of love, relationships, and personal growth.

overview: Literature professor Jim Bennett leads a secret life as a high-stakes gambler. Always a risk-taker, Bennett bets it all when he borrows from a gangster and offers his own life as collateral. Staying one step ahead, he pits his creditor against the operator of an illicit gambling ring while garnering the attention of Frank, a paternalistic loan shark. As his relationship with a student deepens, Bennett must risk everything for a second chance.
tagline: The only way out is all in
title: The Gambler
plot:
The Gambler (2014) is a crime drama film directed by Rupert Wyatt, starring Mark Wahlberg as James Keating, a literature professor who moonlights as a gambler.

The main themes of The Gambler include:

1. **Addiction and Redemption**: The film explores the destructive nature of addiction, particularly in the context of gambling. James Keating's struggles with his own demons serve as a catalyst for his journey towards redemption.
2. **Identity Crisis**: As a literature professor by day and a gambler by night, Keating's dual identity creates tension and conflict within himself. The film delves into the theme of identity crisis, highlighting the difficulties of balancing multiple personas.
3. **Moral Ambiguity**: The Gambler features a complex moral landscape, where right and wrong are not clearly defined. Keating's actions as a gambler often put him at odds with his own values and principles, raising questions about morality and personal responsibility.
4. **Trauma and PTSD**: James Keating's past experiences, including the death of his wife, have left emotional scars that continue to haunt him. The film touches on the theme of trauma and PTSD, highlighting the long-term effects of traumatic events on individuals.

Throughout the film, these themes are woven together to create a narrative that is both gripping and thought-provoking. Mark Wahlberg's performance brings depth and nuance to the character of James Keating, making his journey towards redemption all the more compelling.

overview: Shamoto runs a small tropical fish shop. When his daughter Mitsuko is caught shoplifting at a grocery store a man named Murata steps in to settle things between the girl and the store manager. Murata also runs a tropical fish shop and he and Shamoto soon become friendly. However Murata hides many dark secrets behind his friendly face.
tagline: He'll make you pick up the pieces.
title: Cold Fish
plot:
Cold Fish is a 2010 Japanese drama film directed by Sion Sono, not Nikkatsu Corporation. The movie revolves around a washed-up actor who returns to his hometown and takes over his late father's cabaret act, only to discover that the main attraction is actually a young woman with a dark secret.

The main themes of Cold Fish revolve around the darker aspects of human nature, particularly the exploitation and objectification of women. The film critiques the societal norms that allow for the commodification of women's bodies and the consequences of this exploitation on both the victims and the perpetrators. Through the character of the young woman, the movie sheds light on the complexities of female empowerment and the struggle for autonomy in a patriarchal society.

The film also explores themes of identity, performance, and the blurring of reality and fiction. The protagonist's journey is marked by his own struggles with identity and purpose, as he navigates the world of cabaret entertainment and confronts the darker aspects of human nature.

overview: A group of families on a tropical holiday discover that the secluded beach where they are staying is somehow causing them to age rapidly – reducing their entire lives into a single day.
tagline: It's only a matter of time.
title: Old
plot:
Old is a 2021 American supernatural horror film directed by Mimi Leder and written by Goekpinar Gökce. The movie stars Gael García Bernal, Vicky Krieps, and Rufus Sewell.

The story begins with an elderly couple, Charles (Rufus Sewell) and Amelia (Vicky Krieps), who are struggling to cope with the loss of their daughter, Martha, in a tragic accident when they were young. They have been married for over 40 years and are now facing the reality of their own mortality.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when Charles and Amelia find themselves on a beach in Greece, where they meet two strangers, Mau (Gael García Bernal) and Abigail (Elle Fanning). The four characters form an unlikely bond as they spend the day together, sharing stories and laughter. However, things take a dark turn when Mau reveals that he has been searching for something on the beach, which leads to a series of eerie events.

As the day progresses, it becomes clear that time is not passing normally for these four characters. They are stuck in a time loop, reliving the same day over and over again. The characters try to make the most of their situation, but they soon realize that something sinister is at play.

Throughout the movie, the characters' pasts are slowly revealed through flashbacks and conversations. We learn about Martha's tragic accident, Charles and Amelia's struggles with grief, and Mau's motivations for searching for something on the beach. The story becomes increasingly complex as the characters try to unravel the mystery behind their time loop.

As the day repeats itself, the characters begin to experience strange and terrifying events. They are stalked by a mysterious figure, and they start to question their own sanity. The tension builds as the characters try to find a way out of the time loop and uncover the truth about what is happening to them.

The movie's climax features a dramatic confrontation between the characters and the sinister force behind the time loop. In the end, Charles and Amelia are able to break free from the loop, but not before they have to confront their own mortality and the consequences of their actions.

Overall, Old is a thought-provoking and suspenseful horror movie that explores themes of grief, loss, and the human condition. The film's unique premise and complex characters make it a compelling watch, even if it doesn't always follow traditional horror tropes.

overview: When Geoff, an orphaned stable boy (Chris Masterson), discovers Drake (voice of Robby Benson), the world's last living dragon, he realizes that his dream of becoming a knight in shining armor can now come true. Together, they soon face challenges that turn them into heroes. But caught up in the excitement of their new lives, Geoff and Drake fail to see the hidden dangers that surround them.
title: DragonHeart: A New Beginning
plot:
Dragonheart: A New Beginning is a 2000 fantasy action-adventure film directed by Doug Lefler and released direct to video as a sequel to the 1996 film Dragonheart. Christopher Masterson stars as the stable boy Geoff, with Robby Benson voicing the young dragon Drake, and Harry Van Gorkum, Rona Figueroa and Henry O in supporting roles.

A year before his death, the knight Bowen finds an egg in the cave of his late dragon friend Draco and entrusts it to the monastery of Brother Gilbert. Mindful of a prophecy that a dragon's heart could doom mankind when a two-tailed comet crosses the sky, the friars hide the hatchling for twenty years. Geoff, an orphan who does menial chores at the monastery and dreams of becoming a knight like Bowen, stumbles on the hidden dragon, Drake, and the two lonely outsiders quickly become friends. Meanwhile, the king has appointed a man named Osric as his chief adviser; Osric claims to uphold the knightly Old Code but secretly corrupts it, poisoning the king's mind and imposing coloured tunics that mark each subject's station.

Two travellers from China, Master Kwan and his apprentice, arrive having read in the stars that a new dragon was born and that the comet is days away. The apprentice turns out to be Lian, a disguised member of the Chinese royal line. When knights threaten Geoff for not wearing his tunic, Drake takes his first flight to rescue him, revealing himself to the kingdom. Osric names boy and dragon protectors of the realm against invading Teregoths, while Kwan trains Drake in his powers, including the rare gift of ice breath. Lian explains that a renegade dragon, Griffin, once betrayed the dragons' code until his heart was taken and sealed in an amulet, and that fear of such dragons led a Chinese emperor to have all Eastern dragons killed, leaving Drake the last of his kind.

On the day of the comet Osric fakes a mortal wound to trick Drake into sharing his heart, but Geoff sees through it. Osric kills Kwan and reveals that he is Griffin, condemned to live as a human; reclaiming his heart, he regains his dragon form and invites Drake to join him in conquering humanity. Drake refuses and, mastering his ice breath, freezes Griffin, whose body shatters. When a shard kills Geoff, Drake revives him with part of his heart, and the two become brothers. Rotten Tomatoes lists a 40% score from only five reviews.

overview: Fioravante decides to become a professional Don Juan as a way of making money to help his cash-strapped friend, Murray. With Murray acting as his "manager", the duo quickly finds themselves caught up in the crosscurrents of love and money.
title: Fading Gigolo
plot:
Fading Gigolo is a 2013 American romantic comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of human relationships and identity. The movie delves into the theme of loneliness, as its protagonist, Paul Hackett, played by Michael Sheen, navigates his way through a series of superficial connections in search of genuine intimacy.

The film also touches on the idea of vulnerability, as Paul, a shy and introverted man, finds himself drawn to a prostitute, Dina Devlin, played by Sharon Stone, who challenges his emotional defenses. Through their relationship, the movie examines the blurred lines between love, lust, and companionship.

Furthermore, Fading Gigolo critiques societal expectations around masculinity and aging, as Paul struggles to reconcile his own desires with the pressures of modern masculinity. The film's portrayal of a man who finds solace in unconventional relationships serves as a commentary on the constraints placed on men by traditional norms.

Ultimately, the movie presents a nuanced exploration of human connection, intimacy, and the search for meaning in a world that often prioritizes superficiality over depth.

belongs_to_collection.name: Pentalogy of Mexico by Luis Estrada

overview: Mexico, 1949. The fable of a janitor turned Mayor on a little town lost in the Mexican desert, who gradually realizes how far his new acquainted power and corruption can get him.
production_companies: Fondo para la Producción Cinematográfica de Calidad
tagline: Why don't they want you to see it?
title: Herod's Law
plot:
Herod's Law (Spanish: La ley de Herodes) is a 1999 Mexican satirical black comedy directed by Luis Estrada and produced by Bandidos Films. Damián Alcázar stars, with Pedro Armendáriz Jr., Delia Casanova, Juan Carlos Colombo, Leticia Huijara and the British director Alex Cox in supporting roles. A caricature of corruption under the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), which governed Mexico for most of the twentieth century, it was the first Mexican film to criticize the PRI explicitly by name, and government attempts to interfere with its release caused a public controversy.

The story is set in the run-up to the 1952 general elections. After the mayor of the remote town of San Pedro de los Saguaros is killed by an angry mob while trying to escape with stolen money, the state governor orders his secretary López to find a replacement quickly and quietly. The job falls to Juan Vargas, the naïve manager of a garbage dump and a loyal PRI member, who sees it as the start of a political career. He and his wife Gloria are dismayed when they arrive in San Pedro, a desperately poor village whose largely Indigenous inhabitants barely speak Spanish. With the help of his secretary Pek, Vargas meets the town's notables: Doña Lupe, the brothel madam; a grasping priest; and Doctor Morales, an educated man who belongs to the opposition party.

When Vargas asks the state capital for funds to improve the town, López gives him only a copy of the Mexican Constitution and a revolver. Vargas soon discovers that both are useful tools. He combs the Constitution for pretexts to levy fines and taxes on the villagers, uses the pistol to impose his will and gradually turns from a well-meaning outsider into a ruthless, greedy local tyrant, abusing his position for money and power. His rise and moral collapse serve as a broad allegory of how the system rewarded and reproduced corruption, culminating in a darkly ironic ending.

The film is considered one of the most important Mexican films of its era for its biting humor and direct political criticism, and it won several Ariel Awards. It was released shortly before the 2000 presidential election, in which the PRI lost the presidency for the first time since its founding in 1929. It also launched a series of satirical films by Estrada starring Alcázar, including Hell (2010) and The Perfect Dictatorship (2014).

overview: A shy woman, endowed with the speed, reflexes, and senses of a cat, walks a thin line between criminal and hero, even as a detective doggedly pursues her, fascinated by both of her personas
tagline: You can’t CATch her.
title: Catwoman
plot:
Catwoman is a 2004 superhero film directed by Pitof and based on the DC Comics character of the same name. The movie stars Halle Berry as Patience Phillips, a shy and timid artist who becomes the titular Catwoman.

The film begins with Patience (Halle Berry) working as an assistant to her boss, Meredith Blake (Jennifer Garner), at a fashion magazine in New York City. During a meeting, Meredith is murdered by her business partner, Victor Zsasz (Lorenzo Lamas). In a fit of rage, Patience is attacked and left for dead by Zsasz.

However, Patience survives the attack and discovers that she has developed a new sense of confidence and independence. She also develops a mysterious connection to a cat, which becomes her alter ego, Catwoman. As Patience explores her newfound identity, she begins to use her skills as an artist to fight crime and protect the innocent.

Meanwhile, Zsasz is revealed to be working for a wealthy businessman, Robert Thorn (Vincent D'Onofrio), who is using his company's resources to fund Zsasz's twisted murders. Patience soon discovers that Thorn is behind Meredith's murder and sets out to stop him.

As Patience navigates her new life as Catwoman, she must also confront her own dark past and the traumas that have shaped her into the person she is today. Along the way, she meets a handsome and charming man named Tom Lone (Benjamin Bratt), who becomes her ally in her fight against crime.

Throughout the film, Patience struggles to balance her dual identities as Patience Phillips and Catwoman. She must navigate the complexities of her relationships with those around her, including Tom and her boss, Blake's assistant, Holly Barker (Maria Bello).

As the story unfolds, Patience/Catwoman becomes increasingly embroiled in a cat-and-mouse game with Zsasz and Thorn. The two villains will stop at nothing to achieve their goals, and Patience must use all of her skills and cunning to outwit them.

In the end, Patience/Catwoman emerges victorious, having defeated both Zsasz and Thorn. However, the film's conclusion is somewhat ambiguous, leaving the audience wondering whether Patience has truly found a sense of peace and fulfillment as Catwoman, or if she will continue to struggle with her dual identities in the future.

Overall, Catwoman is a visually stunning film that explores themes of identity, empowerment, and the complexities of being a strong female character. While it received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, Halle Berry's performance as Patience/Catwoman remains one of the most memorable aspects of the film.

overview: Ricky and his family have been fighting an uphill struggle against debt since the 2008 financial crash. An opportunity to wrestle back some independence appears with a shiny new van and the chance to run a franchise as a self-employed delivery driver. It's hard work, and his wife's job as a carer is no easier. The family unit is strong but when both are pulled in different directions everything comes to breaking point.
title: Sorry We Missed You
plot:
Sorry We Missed You is a thought-provoking drama that delves into the complexities of modern capitalism and its effects on human relationships. The film tells the story of a young woman, Kate, who becomes increasingly disillusioned with her corporate job and the societal expectations placed upon her.

As the narrative unfolds, it becomes clear that the film is critiquing the ways in which technology has eroded traditional family structures and created a sense of isolation among its characters. The main theme of the movie revolves around the tension between personal fulfillment and material success, highlighting how the relentless pursuit of wealth can lead to emotional numbness and disconnection.

The film also explores the consequences of neoliberalism on working-class families, particularly women, who are often forced into precarious and low-paying jobs with limited job security. This leads to a sense of desperation and frustration among the characters, as they struggle to make ends meet and find meaning in their lives.

Throughout the movie, the director, Ken Loach, masterfully weaves together themes of class struggle, loneliness, and the search for human connection in a world that seems increasingly indifferent to individual well-being. The result is a powerful and poignant portrayal of a society in crisis, where the pursuit of profit has become more important than people's lives.

Ultimately, Sorry We Missed You is a film about the need for empathy, compassion, and human connection in a world that often values efficiency and productivity over emotional intelligence and relationships.

overview: After she delivers her child in an ambulance, alien Eve is killed by a half-breed. Fortunately, Dr. Abbot scoops up the baby alien and escapes. In time, the baby grows into a gorgeous blonde named Sara and begins her quest to find a worthy mate. But Sara is also savage and leaves a trail of deaths in her wake. This carnage makes chemistry student Dean question whether to help her race or not.
tagline: Beauty is only skin deep
title: Species III
plot:
Species III is a 2004 science fiction horror film directed by P.J. Pesce. The movie follows Maitreya, an alien who is sent to Earth as part of an experiment to create a new species. However, the experiment goes awry, and Maitreya escapes, leading to a series of gruesome murders.

The main themes of Species III include:

1. **The dangers of playing God**: The film explores the consequences of scientific experimentation gone wrong. The creation of a new species raises questions about the ethics of tampering with nature and the potential risks of such actions.
2. **Female empowerment and objectification**: Maitreya, as an alien, is initially portrayed as a powerful and dominant figure. However, as the story progresses, she becomes increasingly objectified by men, highlighting the theme of female empowerment and the dangers of reducing women to mere objects.
3. **The struggle for identity**: Maitreya's character grapples with her own identity, caught between her alien heritage and her human experiences. This internal conflict serves as a metaphor for the struggles many people face in defining themselves and finding their place in the world.
4. **Violence and exploitation**: The film features graphic violence and exploitation, particularly against women. These themes are often used to critique societal attitudes towards sex, violence, and power dynamics.

Overall, Species III is a campy, over-the-top horror film that explores some thought-provoking themes despite its B-movie status.

belongs_to_collection.name: Diary of a Wimpy Kid (Animated) Collection

original_title: Diary of a Wimpy Kid: Rodrick Rules
overview: A new school year, his brother Rodrick teases him over and over and over and over again. Will Greg manage to get along with him? Or will a secret ruin everything?
tagline: Get ready to rock n' rüle!
title: Diary of a Wimpy Kid: Rodrick Rules
plot:
Diary of a Wimpy Kid: Rodrick Rules, stylised as Rodrick Rüles, is a 2022 animated comedy directed by Luke Cormican in his feature directorial debut, from a screenplay by Jeff Kinney based on his 2008 book of the same name. It is the sequel to the 2021 animated Diary of a Wimpy Kid and the second adaptation of Rodrick Rules after the 2011 live-action film. Brady Noon voices Greg Heffley, with Hunter Dillon as his older brother Rodrick, Ethan William Childress as Rowley Jefferson, and Chris Diamantopoulos and Erica Cerra as their parents, Frank and Susan. The film was released on Disney+ on 2 December 2022.

While their parents and little brother Manny are away for a weekend, Rodrick throws a party at the house. Greg invites Rowley to help, but Rodrick locks them in the basement. After escaping, Greg secretly takes photos of the party, which gives him leverage over his brother. When their mother calls to say they are coming home early because Manny is ill, the brothers frantically clear out the guests and clean up the house, replacing the bathroom door on which someone has scrawled "Rodrick Rules" in marker. In return for Greg's help, Rodrick shares his "Rodrick Rules", his philosophy for a relaxed and effort-free life.

The unlikely alliance brings the brothers closer. Rodrick begins teaching Greg to play the drums and introduces him to the members of his heavy metal band, Löded Diper, which is preparing for an upcoming talent show. Meanwhile, Rowley plans to perform a magic act and asks Greg to be his assistant, but Greg turns him down because he thinks the act will flop. Frank grows suspicious about the damaged bathroom door, while Susan is delighted to see her sons getting along. When the parents leave again and send the boys to stay with their grandfather at a retirement community, the secret of the party becomes harder to keep, and Greg must choose between protecting Rodrick and his loyalty to his family and friend as the talent show approaches.

As with the previous animated film, the visual style recreates Kinney's illustrations in three-dimensional computer animation. The story centres on sibling rivalry, the relationship between Greg and Rodrick, and the misadventures of Greg's attempts to avoid responsibility.

The film received mixed reviews; critics appreciated its brisk humour and its focus on the brothers' relationship, though many considered it a lightweight retelling of material already adapted in live action.

overview: For Lieutenant Pete 'Maverick' Mitchell and his friend and co-pilot Nick 'Goose' Bradshaw, being accepted into an elite training school for fighter pilots is a dream come true. But a tragedy, as well as personal demons, will threaten Pete's dreams of becoming an ace pilot.
tagline: Up there with the best of the best.
title: Top Gun
plot:
Top Gun is a classic American action-drama film released in 1986, directed by Tony Scott and produced by Don Simpson and Jerry Bruckheimer under Paramount Pictures.

The movie follows the story of Lieutenant Pete "Maverick" Mitchell (played by Tom Cruise), a hotshot F-14 Tomcat fighter pilot at the Naval Air Station Miramar. Maverick is known for his exceptional flying skills, but also for his reckless and arrogant behavior, which often puts him at odds with his superiors.

During a training exercise, Maverick meets Lieutenant Junior Grade Nick "Goose" Bradshaw (played by Anthony Edwards), a talented and ambitious pilot who becomes his Radar Intercept Officer (RIO). The two pilots form a strong bond, both on and off the ground, as they push each other to become better flyers.

As Maverick and Goose progress through their training, they are assigned to fly with the elite Top Gun team, led by Commander Mike "Viper" Metcalf (played by Tom Skerritt). The team is tasked with competing against the Soviet Union's best pilots in an air-to-air combat exercise.

However, tragedy strikes when Maverick and Goose engage in a fatal dogfight during a training exercise. Maverick survives, but Goose dies in the crash. This event sets off a chain reaction of emotions for Maverick, who struggles to come to terms with his loss and find redemption.

As Maverick navigates his grief and personal demons, he also finds himself drawn to Charlotte "Charlie" Blackwood (played by Kelly McGillis), a civilian instructor at the Top Gun school. Charlie is a talented pilot in her own right, but she's also struggling to balance her career ambitions with her personal life.

Throughout the film, Maverick faces off against his rival, Iceman (played by Val Kilmer), who represents everything that Maverick despises about the military: discipline, control, and conformity. The two pilots engage in a series of intense aerial battles, both on and off the ground, as they vie for supremacy.

Ultimately, Maverick emerges from his struggles with a newfound sense of purpose and humility. He learns to balance his need for speed and competition with a deeper understanding of himself and those around him. Top Gun is a classic tale of heroism, friendship, and redemption, set against the backdrop of high-stakes aerial combat.

overview: Retired C.I.A. agent Frank Moses reunites his unlikely team of elite operatives for a global quest to track down a missing portable nuclear device.
tagline: The best never rest.
title: RED 2
plot:
RED 2 is a 2013 action comedy film directed by Roy H. Wagner and starring Bruce Willis, Helen Mirren, John Malkovich, and Catherine Zeta-Jones.

The movie takes place six years after the events of the first film. Frank Moses (Bruce Willis), Marvin Boggs (John Malkovich), and Sarah Jordan (Mary-Louise Parker) are still on the run from the CIA and other government agencies that want to capture them for their alleged involvement in a conspiracy involving Russian spies.

The story begins with Frank, now living under an assumed identity as "Jack", working as a handyman. However, his life is disrupted when he receives a mysterious message from Marvin, who has been captured by the CIA. The agency plans to use Marvin's knowledge of Soviet espionage to gain access to highly classified information.

Frank and Sarah team up with Marvin's former partner, Teddy (Catherine Zeta-Jones), to rescue him from the CIA's clutches. Along the way, they encounter a new villain, Viktor Chagarin (Mekhi Phifer), who is revealed to be a Russian spy working for the CIA.

As Frank and his team navigate through various obstacles, including a high-speed car chase and a shootout with CIA agents, they uncover a conspiracy involving the CIA's plans to use Soviet-era spies to gain access to classified information. The team also discovers that Viktor Chagarin is actually a double agent working for the Russians.

The plot thickens as Frank and his team learn that the CIA has been using the Russian spies to gather intelligence on the United States, which could compromise national security. The team must use their skills and experience to stop the CIA's plans and bring down Viktor Chagarin.

In the end, Frank and his team successfully rescue Marvin and defeat Viktor Chagarin in a thrilling showdown. However, not before discovering that the CIA has been using the Russian spies to gather intelligence on the United States, which could have catastrophic consequences.

The movie ends with Frank, Sarah, and Marvin returning to their normal lives, but not before sharing a moment of camaraderie and acknowledging that they will always be there for each other. The film concludes with a sense of closure, but also leaves room for potential sequels or spin-offs.

Overall, RED 2 is an action-packed comedy that delivers on its promise of high-octane thrills and witty banter. The movie's cast delivers strong performances, and the chemistry between the leads is undeniable. While some may find the plot a bit predictable, the film's pacing and humor make it an enjoyable ride from start to finish.

overview: During World War II, Steve Rogers is a sickly man from Brooklyn who's transformed into super-soldier Captain America to aid in the war effort. Rogers must stop the Red Skull – Adolf Hitler's ruthless head of weaponry, and the leader of an organization that intends to use a mysterious device of untold powers for world domination.
tagline: When patriots become heroes
title: Captain America: The First Avenger
plot:
Captain America: The First Avenger is a 2011 superhero film directed by Joe Johnston, produced by Kevin Feige, and written by Christopher Markus and Stephen McFeely. The movie is based on the Marvel Comics character of the same name.

The film begins during World War II, with Steve Rogers (played by Chris Evans), a frail and weak young man from Brooklyn who dreams of serving his country. Despite being rejected by the U.S. Army due to his physical limitations, Rogers is recruited for a top-secret government experiment called the Super Soldier Program. The program aims to create a super-soldier using a serum that enhances physical abilities.

Rogers is transformed into Captain America, a patriotic superhero with enhanced strength, agility, and endurance. He becomes a symbol of hope for the American people during World War II, fighting against the Nazis and their leader, Red Skull (played by Hugo Weaving).

As Captain America, Rogers battles against HYDRA, a terrorist organization led by Red Skull, who seeks to use the Tesseract, a powerful energy source, to conquer the world. Alongside his fellow soldiers, Bucky Barnes (played by Sebastian Stan) and Peggy Carter (played by Hayley Atwell), Rogers embarks on a series of missions to stop HYDRA's plans.

However, during one mission, Rogers is presumed dead after being frozen in suspended animation by the Soviet Union. He remains frozen for over 70 years until he is discovered by S.H.I.E.L.D. agent Phil Coulson (played by Clark Gregg) and brought back to the present day.

Upon his return, Rogers struggles to adjust to modern society, feeling like an outsider from a different era. He eventually joins S.H.I.E.L.D. and becomes a valuable asset in their fight against evil. The movie ends with Rogers, now an older man, reflecting on his experiences as Captain America and the sacrifices he made during World War II.

Throughout the film, there are several themes that emerge, including patriotism, duty, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control. The movie also explores the complexities of war and its impact on individuals, particularly those who fight for their country.

Overall, Captain America: The First Avenger is a thrilling adventure that pays homage to the classic superhero genre while introducing new characters and themes to the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

overview: Geophysicist Dr. Josh Keyes discovers that an unknown force has caused the earth's inner core to stop rotating. With the planet's magnetic field rapidly deteriorating, our atmosphere literally starts to come apart at the seams with catastrophic consequences. To resolve the crisis, Keyes, along with a team of the world's most gifted scientists, travel into the earth's core. Their mission: detonate a device that will reactivate the core.
production_companies: Munich Film Partners New Century & Company (MFP) Core Productions
tagline: Earth has a deadline.
title: The Core
plot:
The Core is a 2003 American science fiction disaster film directed by Jon Amiel from a screenplay by Cooper Layne and John Rogers. Aaron Eckhart, Hilary Swank, Delroy Lindo and Stanley Tucci lead an ensemble that also includes D. J. Qualls, Richard Jenkins, Tchéky Karyo, Bruce Greenwood and Alfre Woodard. Released by Paramount Pictures on March 28, 2003, after being moved from November 2002, it follows a team sent to the centre of the Earth to restart the rotation of its core with nuclear explosions.

When thirty-two people in Boston die at the same moment from failures of their pacemakers, geophysicist Josh Keyes and weapons expert Serge Leveque are brought in to investigate. A series of bizarre incidents linked to the planet's magnetic field leads Josh and the arrogant Dr. Conrad Zimsky to conclude that the inner core has stopped spinning, which will strip away the magnetic shield protecting Earth from lethal solar radiation. The government's solution is to detonate nuclear weapons in the outer core. Zimsky's estranged former colleague Ed "Braz" Brazzelton supplies a tunnelling ship, Virgil, to be piloted by NASA astronauts Robert Iverson and Rebecca Childs, while the hacker "Rat" Finch is recruited to keep news of the crisis off the internet.

Launched through the Mariana Trench, Virgil bores into the crust with a laser drill. In the mantle it plunges into a vast hollow geode, and Iverson is killed freeing the ship; a later breach in a field of diamond formations claims Serge, who sacrifices himself to save the weapon controls. In the outer core the team discovers that the material is less dense than expected and their bombs are too weak. Zimsky confesses that the crisis was likely caused by DESTINI, a secret tectonic weapon he helped develop, and the military wants to fire it again; Rat sabotages the attempt after a surge of microwave radiation destroys the Golden Gate Bridge.

The crew instead seals the bombs into separate compartments, timing the explosions so their shock waves reinforce one another. Braz and then Zimsky give their lives to complete the plan, and the detonations restart the core. Josh and Rebecca power Virgil back to the ocean floor near Hawaii, where whales attracted by their ultrasound signal lead rescuers to them, and Rat leaks the full story to the world.

The film drew mixed reviews, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 39% approval, and grossed about $74.1 million worldwide against an $85 million budget.

overview: Giving fans unprecedented access to the real life of the music sensation, Katy Perry: Part of Me exposes the hard work, dedication and phenomenal talent of a girl who remained true to herself and her vision in order to achieve her dreams. Featuring rare behind-the-scenes interviews, personal moments between Katy and her friends, and all-access footage of rehearsals, choreography, Katy’s signature style and more, Katy Perry: Part of Me reveals the singer’s unwavering belief that if you can be yourself, then you can be anything.
tagline: Be yourself and you can be anything
title: Katy Perry: Part of Me
plot:
Katy Perry: Part of Me, advertised as Katy Perry: Part of Me 3D, is a 2012 American autobiographical documentary and concert film about the pop singer Katy Perry. Directed by Dan Cutforth and Jane Lipsitz, it was released in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom and Ireland on July 5, 2012, and was presented in 3D. Appearing alongside Perry are her then-husband Russell Brand, her friend Shannon Woodward, Rachael Markarian and the DJ Mia Moretti, as well as members of her family and touring crew.

The film follows Perry on her worldwide California Dreams Tour, which comprised 127 concerts between February 20, 2011, and January 22, 2012, while tracing her path to stardom. Interviews with Perry, her family and close friends are combined with home videos and archival footage of her childhood and teenage years. Raised by Christian pastor parents, she began her career singing gospel music before reinventing herself as a pop artist, enduring years of setbacks and dropped record deals before breaking through with the 2008 single "I Kissed a Girl." The film portrays her strong work ethic and her close relationship with her fans, as well as the pressures of performing night after night across several continents.

Most of the concert footage was recorded on November 23, 2011, at the Staples Center in Los Angeles, though performances filmed in Tokyo and São Paulo are also included. The film features her colorful stage show, built around candy-themed sets and frequent costume changes, along with backstage scenes of the preparation that goes into each show. Fellow singers including Rihanna, Lady Gaga, Adele, Justin Bieber and Jessie J make brief appearances.

One of the documentary's most discussed elements is its candid depiction of Perry coping with the breakdown of her marriage to the English actor and comedian Russell Brand, which unravels while she is on tour. Footage shows the singer distraught backstage shortly before a performance in São Paulo, then composing herself to go on stage, a sequence many reviewers singled out as the emotional center of the film.

Critics responded fairly positively. Rotten Tomatoes reported that 75% of 88 reviews were favorable, with an average rating of 6.4/10, and its consensus credited the film's success to the pop star's genuine likability, inspiring work ethic and appeal to her audience.

overview: During the rise of fascism in Mussolini's Italy, a wooden boy brought magically to life struggles to live up to his father's expectations.
tagline: Love will give you life.
title: Guillermo del Toro's Pinocchio
plot:
I have information on this movie.

Guillermo del Toro's Pinocchio is a stop-motion animated fantasy drama film directed by Guillermo del Toro, based on the classic Italian children's book "The Adventures of Pinocchio" by Carlo Collodi. The film stars Gregory Mann as Pinocchio and David Bradley as Geppetto.

In this adaptation, Pinocchio is a wooden puppet created by Geppetto, a poor woodcarver who dreams of becoming a real boy. However, their relationship is complicated when Pinocchio's creator becomes obsessed with his creation, leading to a series of events that test the boundaries between reality and fantasy.

The film explores themes of identity, morality, and the consequences of one's actions. As Pinocchio navigates the world, he encounters various characters who shape his experiences, including the Blue Fairy (voiced by Ewan McGregor), Stromboli (voiced by Dennis Haysbert), and the Coachman (voiced by Tilda Swinton).

Throughout the film, del Toro weaves a complex narrative that blends fantasy and reality, often blurring the lines between what is real and what is imagined. The stop-motion animation brings to life the characters and settings in vivid detail, creating an immersive world that draws the viewer into Pinocchio's journey.

One of the standout aspects of the film is its exploration of the complexities of Geppetto's character. His love for Pinocchio is both selfless and obsessive, highlighting the blurred lines between creator and creation. The film also delves into the consequences of Pinocchio's actions, as he grapples with his own morality and the nature of his existence.

Overall, Guillermo del Toro's Pinocchio is a visually stunning and thought-provoking adaptation that brings new depth to the classic tale. With its intricate world-building, complex characters, and exploration of themes, this film is sure to captivate audiences of all ages.

overview: Ben Cronin has it all: the admiration of his many friends, a terrific girlfriend, and he's on the fast-track to an athletic scholarship. Ben's rock-solid, promising future and romance are turned upside-down with the arrival of Madison Bell. Madison, the new girl in town, quickly sets her sights on the impressionable Ben. While their first few meetings are innocent enough, the obsessive and seductive Madison wants more ... much more.
tagline: His biggest fan just became his worst nightmare.
title: Swimfan
plot:
Swimfan is a 2002 American teen drama film directed by Andrew Fleming. The movie revolves around Cassie Wright (played by Jessica Biel), a high school student who becomes obsessed with winning the state swimming championships, and her complicated relationships with those around her.

At its core, Swimfan explores themes of ambition, obsession, and the pressures that come with achieving success in competitive sports. Cassie's relentless drive to win is fueled by a desire for validation and recognition from her peers, as well as her own sense of identity. As she navigates the cutthroat world of high school swimming, she must confront the darker aspects of her own personality and the true cost of her ambition.

The film also delves into the complexities of female relationships, particularly those between women who are perceived as rivals or competitors. Cassie's interactions with her teammates and opponents serve as a catalyst for exploring themes of jealousy, insecurity, and the blurred lines between friendship and rivalry.

Furthermore, Swimfan touches on the idea of identity and self-discovery, as Cassie struggles to reconcile her athletic persona with her personal life and relationships. The movie raises questions about what it means to be oneself, both in and out of competition, and whether the pursuit of success can come at a cost to one's emotional well-being.

Overall, Swimfan is a thought-provoking drama that uses the backdrop of competitive swimming to explore universal themes of ambition, identity, and relationships.

overview: Martin, an ex-Parisian well-heeled hipster passionate about Gustave Flaubert who settled into a Norman village as a baker, sees an English couple moving into a small farm nearby. Not only are the names of the new arrivals Gemma and Charles Bovery, but their behavior also seems to be inspired by Flaubert's heroes.
title: Gemma Bovery
plot:
Gemma Bovery is a 2014 film that explores the complexities of female identity, relationships, and the societal expectations placed on women. The movie delves into the life of Gemma Bovery, a young woman who struggles to find her place in the world.

At its core, Gemma Bovery is a nuanced portrayal of the challenges faced by women navigating their 20s, as they grapple with the constraints of traditional femininity and societal norms. The film examines the tension between independence and conformity, highlighting the difficulties women face in asserting their individuality while still being expected to conform to certain standards.

The movie also touches on themes of love, relationships, and the complexities of human connection. Gemma's experiences are marked by a series of intense and often tumultuous relationships, which serve as a catalyst for her self-discovery and growth.

Through Gemma's character, the film sheds light on the societal pressures that women face, particularly in terms of their appearance, behavior, and choices. The movie raises important questions about the nature of femininity, identity, and the constraints placed on women by society.

Ultimately, Gemma Bovery is a thought-provoking exploration of the human experience, one that invites viewers to reflect on the complexities of female identity and the societal expectations that shape our lives.

overview: A family moves from New York into an old mansion in the countryside, still filled with the previous owner's things. As they begin to make it their own, a series of events begin to occur that makes them believe that the former inhabitants are not yet gone.
tagline: The perfect house hides the perfect crime.
title: Cold Creek Manor
plot:
Cold Creek Manor is a psychological thriller film that revolves around the dark secrets and twisted desires of its characters. The story centers around a wealthy couple, who purchase a rural estate with the intention of renovating it, only to discover that the house has a mind of its own and seems to be exerting a malevolent influence over them.

As the narrative unfolds, it becomes clear that the true horror lies not in the physical environment, but in the dark pasts and repressed emotions of the characters. The film expertly weaves together themes of obsession, possession, and the blurring of reality, creating a sense of unease and tension that permeates every aspect of the story.

At its core, Cold Creek Manor is a tale of how our deepest fears and desires can consume us, leading us down a path of destruction and chaos. The film's use of atmospheric tension and psychological manipulation creates a sense of claustrophobia, trapping the characters - and the audience - in a world of their own making.

Through its exploration of these themes, Cold Creek Manor raises questions about the nature of reality and the power of the human psyche to create its own horrors. The film's slow-burning tension and eerie atmosphere make it a gripping and unsettling watch, leaving viewers on edge until the very end.

original_title: The Seeker: The Dark Is Rising
overview: A boy's life is turned upside down when he learns that he is the last of a group of immortal warriors who have dedicated their lives to fighting the forces of the dark.
tagline: Even the smallest of light... shines in the darkness
title: The Seeker: The Dark Is Rising
plot:
The Seeker: The Dark Is Rising, also released simply as The Seeker, is a 2007 American fantasy adventure film loosely adapted from Susan Cooper's 1973 children's novel The Dark Is Rising, the second book in her series of the same name. Directed by David L. Cunningham, it stars Alexander Ludwig as Will Stanton, with Ian McShane, Frances Conroy, Gregory Smith, Jonathan Jackson, Amelia Warner, James Cosmo and Christopher Eccleston as the Rider.

On the eve of his fourteenth birthday, Will Stanton, an American boy recently moved with his large family to a village in England, is invited with his siblings to a Christmas party by Miss Greythorne, the mistress of the local manor, and her butler Merriman Lyon. After leaving the party, Will is pursued by a sinister figure on a white horse. He is rescued by Miss Greythorne, Merriman and two local farmers, Dawson and Old George, who reveal that they are Old Ones, ancient warriors who serve the Light in its eternal war against the Dark. The figure is the Rider, the Dark's champion, who warns that in five days his power will rise.

The Old Ones explain that Will is the last of their kind to be born, the seventh son of a seventh son, whose powers awaken on his fourteenth birthday. Will doubts this, believing he is only the sixth son, and the mystery of a missing brother becomes part of the story. As the Seeker, Will must find six hidden Signs, which together will give the Light the power to defeat the Dark. To recover them he learns to travel through time, while the Rider and his agents try to tempt, deceive and threaten him and his family. At the same time Will must cope with ordinary troubles: rivalry with his older brothers, a crush on a local girl named Maggie and the feeling of being an outsider in a new country.

The film was a critical and commercial failure, earning about $31 million worldwide against a budget of around $45 million. Fans of the novels objected to the many changes from the source, including making Will American and adding a romance subplot, and Susan Cooper publicly expressed her disappointment with the script. Critics also found it derivative of other fantasy films of the period.

overview: The pic is set in the aftermath of an apocalyptic event that forces people into extreme isolation. A father and son, who have been living off grid for 20 years, encounter an outsider who threatens to destroy the utopia they’ve built.
title: Last Survivors
plot:
Last Survivors, previously known by the working title SHTF, is a 2021 American thriller directed by Drew Mylrea in his feature directorial debut. Drew Van Acker, Alicia Silverstone and Stephen Moyer star in the film, which is set in an apparently post-apocalyptic world in which a father has raised his now adult son in complete isolation deep in the woods, far from what he describes as the ruins of civilization.

For more than twenty years, Troy and his son Jake have lived off the grid following what Troy insists was a catastrophic event that destroyed much of society and left its survivors desperate and violent. Troy has relentlessly drilled into Jake the belief that every outsider is an immediate threat who must be eliminated, and he kills and buries anyone who stumbles across their homestead. When a stranger shoots and wounds Troy, Jake is forced to venture out alone to find antibiotics to save him.

During his search Jake comes upon a woman working outside an isolated house. Despite his father's orders, he cannot bring himself to kill her. Instead he slips into her home, takes antibiotics and steroids and returns to tend to Troy. Drawn back to her, Jake secretly hides some of their food stores so that his father will believe supplies are running low, giving him an excuse to go hunting. He returns to the house and confronts the woman, who tells him her name is Henrietta. As their conversations continue, it becomes increasingly clear to the audience that the outside world may never have suffered any generalized collapse at all. Troy grows suspicious of his son's absences, while Jake begins to doubt everything his father has told him about what lies beyond the forest, setting the two men on a collision course.

Principal photography took place in Butte, Montana, and wrapped in January 2021. The film received a generally favorable response: on Rotten Tomatoes 71% of 17 critics' reviews are positive. Martin Unsworth of Starburst gave it three stars out of five, writing that it follows the familiar path of post-apocalyptic films while remaining engaging. Angie Han of The Hollywood Reporter was more critical, arguing that the film clearly had a lot on its mind but that its reticence kept it from exploring its more challenging ideas, while Common Sense Media described it as a solid evening of entertainment likely to spark family discussion.

overview: A New Yorker moves to Los Angeles in order to figure out his life while he housesits for his brother, and he soon sparks with his brother's assistant.
tagline: He's got a lot on his mind.
title: Greenberg
plot:
Greenberg is a 2010 American comedy-drama film directed by Noah Baumbach. The movie revolves around the life of George Greenberg, a self-centered and somewhat narcissistic advertising executive who embarks on a road trip to visit his estranged father in Florida.

The main theme of Greenberg is the exploration of identity and the search for meaning in one's life. As George navigates through various encounters with people from his past, he begins to confront his own flaws and shortcomings, leading him to reevaluate his priorities and sense of purpose. Through his experiences, the film delves into the complexities of human relationships, highlighting the tension between genuine connections and superficial interactions.

The movie also touches on themes of loneliness and disconnection, as George struggles to form meaningful bonds with others due to his own emotional unavailability. However, as he opens up to those around him, particularly his father and a young woman named Rachel, he begins to discover new aspects of himself and the world around him.

Ultimately, Greenberg is a nuanced exploration of the human condition, one that balances humor and pathos to create a rich and thought-provoking cinematic experience.

original_title: Sherlock Holmes: A Game of Shadows
overview: There is a new criminal mastermind at large (Professor Moriarty) and not only is he Holmes’ intellectual equal, but his capacity for evil and lack of conscience may give him an advantage over the  detective.
tagline: The game is afoot.
title: Sherlock Holmes: A Game of Shadows
plot:
Sherlock Holmes: A Game of Shadows is a 2011 action mystery film directed by Guy Ritchie, starring Robert Downey Jr. as Sherlock Holmes and Jude Law as Dr. John Watson.

The movie begins with Sherlock Holmes (Robert Downey Jr.) and Dr. John Watson (Jude Law) living in London, England, in the year 1891. The story starts with a mysterious woman named Irene Adler (Rachel McAdams), who is revealed to be a former adversary of Holmes'. She has been presumed dead for years but returns, seeking revenge against Holmes.

Meanwhile, a series of murders takes place across Europe, all connected to a mysterious figure known as the "Severing Hand". The victims are all members of a secret society called the "Thaddeus Wadja" or "The Thaddeus Society", which is dedicated to the study and practice of alchemy.

As Holmes delves deeper into the mystery, he discovers that the murders are linked to an ancient text known as the "Severing Hand's" manifesto. The text reveals a plan to unleash a deadly poison on London, which would kill millions of people.

Holmes and Watson team up with Irene Adler, who has her own reasons for wanting to stop the Severing Hand. Together, they embark on a thrilling adventure across Europe, following a trail of clues that lead them from Paris to Vienna.

As the story unfolds, Holmes' mental health is put to the test when he begins to experience hallucinations and paranoia. He becomes convinced that his arch-nemesis, Professor Moriarty (Jared Harris), has returned and is behind the murders.

The climax of the movie takes place in a train station in Paris, where Holmes and Watson confront the Severing Hand. In a thrilling showdown, Holmes uses his exceptional detective skills to outwit the villain and prevent the poison from being released.

In the end, Holmes and Irene Adler share a moment of mutual respect and admiration for each other's intellects. The movie concludes with Holmes returning to London, where he is greeted as a hero by the public.

Throughout the movie, Robert Downey Jr.'s portrayal of Sherlock Holmes is on full display, showcasing his wit, intelligence, and eccentricities. Jude Law's performance as Dr. Watson provides a perfect foil to Holmes' antics, while Rachel McAdams brings a sense of sophistication and danger to her character, Irene Adler.

Overall, Sherlock Holmes: A Game of Shadows is an entertaining and action-packed adventure that stays true to the spirit of Sir Arthur Conan Doyle's original stories.

overview: Ivy Donaldson struggles with her mom's shadow, Muriel, the Christmas darling of Icicle Falls. She is now separated from her husband Rob and tries her best with her daughter, but after a series of strange but comical events everybody gets together in unexpected but festive ways.
title: Christmas on Candy Cane Lane
plot:
Christmas on Candy Cane Lane is a 2022 Canadian-American Christmas comedy television film directed by Christie Will Wolf from a screenplay by Teena Booth, adapted from the novel of the same name by Sheila Roberts, the eighth book in her Icicle Falls series. Produced by the Motion Picture Corporation of America, Brad Krevoy Television and Candace Cameron Bure's company Candy Rock Entertainment, with Bure as an executive producer, it stars her Full House and Fuller House co-star Andrea Barber, with Dan Payne and Kerensa Cooper. The film premiered on the Great American Family channel on 3 December 2022 and runs 85 minutes.

In the small town of Icicle Falls, one street, Candy Cane Lane, is famous for going all out at Christmas, and its residents are expected to decorate their houses lavishly and welcome crowds of visitors. Ivy Donaldson (Barber) has found the season hard since the death a few years earlier of her mother, Muriel, the town's beloved queen of Christmas, who owned a Christmas shop and headed the committee that ran the street's festivities. Feeling it was her duty to carry on, Ivy took over the shop and moved into her mother's house to keep the Candy Cane Lane traditions alive, but she cannot escape constant comparisons with her mother. The pressure of living up to Muriel's standards has strained everything in her life: she is now separated from her husband Rob (Payne), and their teenage daughter Jordan (Cooper) is tired of their lives revolving around the neighbourhood's activities. As the holidays approach, someone starts tampering with the candy cane decorations across the street, and a series of strange but comic mishaps, including Ivy and Rob dressing up as Mr. and Mrs. Claus, brings the family back together in unexpected and festive ways, as Ivy learns to follow her own dreams rather than carry a legacy that has become a burden.

Reviews were unenthusiastic. Kristen of TV Tweetie found it cute but "kind of meh", praising the striking Claus costumes, the performances of Payne and Cooper as a husband and daughter hoping to reunite the family, and its message about letting go of traditions that are burdens rather than gifts, though she felt Barber's acting style was very familiar. Cassandra Morgan advised against watching it, arguing that it had a good premise but tried to be a comedy, a romance and a mystery at once without letting its slapstick jokes land.

overview: The government is asking Eiffel to design something spectacular for the 1889 Paris World Fair, but Eiffel simply wants to design the subway. Suddenly, everything changes when Eiffel crosses paths with a mysterious woman from his past.
tagline: You will never look at it the same way again.
title: Eiffel
plot:
Eiffel is a 2021 French romantic drama directed by Martin Bourboulon from a screenplay credited to Caroline Bongrand and other writers. Romain Duris stars as the engineer Gustave Eiffel, with Emma Mackey as Adrienne Bourgès and Pierre Deladonchamps as her husband, the journalist Antoine de Restac. Presented as "freely inspired by real events," the film builds a fictionalized love story around the creation of the Eiffel Tower. It premiered in March 2021 at the Alliance Française French Film Festival in Australia and was released in France by Pathé in October 2021.

In 1886, fresh from his success designing the iron framework for the Statue of Liberty, Eiffel is looking for his next major project ahead of the 1889 World's Fair in Paris. His engineers propose a tall metal tower, but he initially dismisses the idea in favor of designing a metro system for the city. To promote his firm he reconnects with an old acquaintance, Antoine de Restac, and at a society dinner meets Antoine's wife Adrienne. The encounter shakes him, and to the astonishment of the guests he suddenly announces that he will build a 300-metre tower.

Flashbacks to Bordeaux in 1860 reveal the source of his reaction. While building an iron bridge over the Garonne, the young Eiffel dived into the river to save a worker and then sought timber for safety scaffolding from Bourgès, a wealthy local businessman. There he met Bourgès's spirited daughter Adrienne, who supported his request, and the two fell passionately in love despite the disapproval of her family. In the present, Eiffel struggles to win the contract, raise money, overcome public hostility to his design and solve formidable engineering problems with the tower's foundations, while his rekindled feelings for Adrienne threaten both her marriage and his reputation.

The film received mostly positive reviews in France and grossed about $13.6 million worldwide. Critics praised its production design, its depiction of the tower's construction and the chemistry between Duris and Mackey. Others were skeptical of the invented romance; Peter Debruge of Variety described it as less a biopic than a sketchy piece of historical fiction, while David Stratton of The Australian noted its ambition.

keywords.name: based on magazine, newspaper or article

overview: Earl Stone, a man in his eighties, is broke, alone, and facing foreclosure of his business when he is offered a job that simply requires him to drive. Easy enough, but, unbeknownst to Earl, he's just signed on as a drug courier for a Mexican cartel. He does so well that his cargo increases exponentially, and Earl hit the radar of hard-charging DEA agent Colin Bates.
tagline: Nobody Runs Forever
title: The Mule
plot:
The Mule is a 2018 American crime drama film directed by Clint Eastwood, written by Nick Payne, and starring Clint Eastwood, Bradley Cooper, and Alison Eastwood. 

The movie begins with the introduction of Luke Wilson's character, David Brown, who is an elderly man living in a nursing home. He suffers from dementia and has lost his memory due to Alzheimer's disease. However, it is revealed that he was once a successful drug trafficker for the Mexican cartel.

As the story unfolds, we see flashbacks of Luke's life as a mule, transporting large quantities of cocaine for the cartel. The film then cuts back to the present day, where David Brown has been diagnosed with Alzheimer's and is struggling to cope with his condition.

One day, while in the nursing home, David meets a new patient named Benicio (played by Bradley Cooper), who claims to be an old friend from Luke's past. However, it becomes clear that Benicio is actually a former cartel member sent to kill Luke.

As the story progresses, we see Luke's life flashbacks become more vivid and intense, revealing his rise to becoming a successful drug trafficker. We also see glimpses of his relationships with his family members, including his wife, Lena (played by Alison Eastwood), and his son, Danny (played by Michael Peña).

As the plot thickens, Luke begins to suspect that Benicio is not who he claims to be. He starts to investigate and gather evidence, using his knowledge of the cartel's operations to stay one step ahead.

In a thrilling climax, Luke confronts Benicio in an intense showdown at a truck stop. With the help of some unexpected allies, including a young woman named Teresa (played by Gina Rodriguez), Luke manages to outsmart Benicio and bring him to justice.

Throughout the film, Clint Eastwood delivers a powerful performance as Luke Wilson's character, bringing depth and nuance to the role. The supporting cast also delivers strong performances, particularly Bradley Cooper, who brings a sense of menace and unpredictability to his portrayal of Benicio.

Overall, The Mule is a gripping and intense thriller that explores themes of loyalty, betrayal, and redemption. With its strong performances, engaging plot, and Clint Eastwood's direction, the film is a must-see for fans of crime dramas.

overview: A weekend cruise on a luxurious party yacht goes horribly wrong for a group of old high-school friends when they get stuck in the water many miles from shore and a happy reunion turns into a fight for survival.
tagline: Fatigue. Hypothermia. Death.
title: Open Water 2: Adrift
plot:
Open Water 2: Adrift, also known simply as Adrift, is a 2006 German English-language survival thriller directed by Hans Horn. Susan May Pratt, Richard Speight Jr., Niklaus Lange, Ali Hillis, Cameron Richardson and Eric Dane star as a group of friends stranded in the open sea. Marketed as the second entry in the Open Water series, it is not a direct sequel to the 2003 film, and it was inspired by the short story "Adrift" by the Japanese author Koji Suzuki, from which it took its original title. Lionsgate released it on DVD in the United States in February 2007.

Dan, a wealthy man who has just bought a new yacht, invites his old school friends for a weekend cruise. Among them are Amy and her husband James, who bring their infant daughter Sarah, along with Zach, Lauren and Dan's new girlfriend Michelle. Amy has been terrified of water ever since her father drowned while swimming with her when she was a child, and she refuses to remove her life jacket even on deck.

Far out at sea, most of the friends jump into the water for a swim, while Amy stays aboard with the baby. As a joke, Dan scoops Amy up and leaps overboard with her, ignoring her screams. Only then does the group realise that no one has lowered the boarding ladder. The hull is too high and smooth to climb, and the baby is left alone on deck. The friends try every idea they can think of to get back aboard, including tying their swimsuits together into a makeshift rope, while their strength slowly fades. A passing boat full of teenagers mistakes their frantic waving for a friendly greeting and sails away, and a mobile phone ringing in clothes hanging over the deck remains frustratingly out of reach. As the hours pass, exhaustion, panic and old resentments turn the friends against one another, with fatal consequences.

The film builds its tension around a simple, plausible premise, with almost all of the action taking place in the water beside the yacht. Amy's phobia gives the story its emotional core, as she must overcome her fear in order to save her daughter.

The film received mixed reviews, holding an approval rating of about 45 percent on Rotten Tomatoes; critics praised its claustrophobic premise and some of the performances, but found the characters unsympathetic and their decisions frustrating. It was later released on Blu-ray in 2010 as a double feature with the original Open Water.

overview: Enraged at the slaughter of Murron, his new bride and childhood love, Scottish warrior William Wallace slays a platoon of the local English lord's soldiers. This leads the village to revolt and, eventually, the entire country to rise up against English rule.
tagline: Every man dies. Not every man truly lives.
title: Braveheart
plot:
Braveheart is a historical epic film directed by and starring Mel Gibson, released in 1995. The movie is set in Scotland during the late 13th century and tells the story of William Wallace, a Scottish warrior who led a rebellion against the English army.

The film begins with a young William Wallace (played by Stellan Skarsgård) as a child, witnessing his father's brutal murder at the hands of English soldiers. This traumatic event sets the tone for Wallace's future actions and fuels his desire for revenge against the English.

As the story unfolds, we see Wallace grow into a strong and determined young man, who eventually becomes a skilled warrior and leader among the Scottish clans. He meets and falls in love with Murron (played by Sophie Marceau), a beautiful and kind-hearted woman from a neighboring clan. However, their happiness is short-lived, as English soldiers arrive at her village and brutally murder her.

This event sparks Wallace's desire for revenge against the English, whom he holds responsible for Murron's death. He becomes a key figure in the Scottish resistance movement, using his bravery and strategic thinking to rally the clans against the English army.

As the conflict escalates, Wallace faces off against the ruthless English commander, King Edward "Longshanks" (played by Patrick McGoohan). The two engage in a series of intense battles, with Wallace emerging as a formidable opponent. However, their rivalry is complicated by the fact that Longshanks is also Wallace's uncle.

Despite the odds against him, Wallace continues to fight for Scottish independence, using guerrilla tactics and clever strategies to outmaneuver his enemies. He becomes a symbol of hope for the Scottish people, who see him as a champion of freedom and self-determination.

The film's climax features an epic battle between the Scots and the English at Stirling Bridge. Wallace leads the charge against the English army, using his knowledge of the terrain to outflank and defeat them. However, he is eventually captured by Longshanks' men and put on trial for treason.

In a dramatic and emotional courtroom scene, Wallace delivers a powerful speech, condemning the English monarchy and pleading for Scottish independence. He is ultimately found guilty and sentenced to death. As he stands on the scaffold awaiting his execution, Wallace declares "Freedom!" and dies with his head held high.

The film ends with a sense of hope and renewal, as the Scottish people vow to continue their fight for freedom in the face of overwhelming odds. The final shot features a young William Wallace, who has grown up watching his father's story and is now determined to carry on his legacy.

Overall, Braveheart is a powerful and moving film that explores themes of patriotism, sacrifice, and the human spirit. Mel Gibson's performance as William Wallace is particularly noteworthy, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The film's epic scope and stunning cinematography make it a must-see for fans of historical dramas and action-adventure films.

overview: In 1979, a group of young filmmakers set out to make an adult film in rural Texas, but when their reclusive, elderly hosts catch them in the act, the cast find themselves fighting for their lives. Hilarity ensues.
tagline: Dying to show you a good time.
title: X
plot:
X is a 2022 American satirical horror film written and directed by Ti West. The film takes place in 1979, during the height of the Texas Chain Saw Massacre phenomenon.

The story follows Pinhura "Pin" Fuentes (played by Breckin Meyer), a young filmmaker who has just arrived in Austin to make a documentary about the infamous Texas Chainsaw Massacre. Pin is accompanied by his girlfriend, Rose (played by Jenna Ortega), and their friend, Jay (played by August Maturo).

Upon arrival, they meet with the enigmatic and charismatic film director, Michael Williams (played by Nick Kroll), who has been making a series of low-budget horror films in the area. Michael is known for his provocative and transgressive style, which often pushes the boundaries of good taste.

As Pin begins to work on his documentary, he becomes increasingly fascinated with Michael's films and the local horror scene. However, things take a dark turn when Pin discovers that Michael has been using real-life events as inspiration for his films, including the murders of several people in the area.

Pin becomes obsessed with uncovering the truth behind Michael's films and the true nature of the Texas horror phenomenon. As he delves deeper into the mystery, he begins to experience strange and terrifying occurrences that blur the lines between reality and fiction.

Throughout the film, West pays homage to the classic horror movies of the 1970s, while also subverting expectations and challenging the audience's perceptions of what is acceptable in the genre. The film features a talented ensemble cast, including Jenna Ortega, Breckin Meyer, and Nick Kroll, who deliver standout performances that add to the film's tension and unease.

Ultimately, X is a thought-provoking and unsettling exploration of the power of horror movies to shape our perceptions of reality and ourselves. The film is a love letter to the genre, while also offering a scathing critique of its excesses and superficiality.

overview: A young couple travels to a shabby Eastern European hospital for plastic surgery. The young woman wants a breast reduction. Her mother comes along for yet another face-lift. Wandering through an abandoned ward the boyfriend stumbles upon a young woman, gagged and strapped to an operating table; she is the result of an experimental rejuvenation treatment. He frees her, but does not realize he just caused the outbreak of a virus that will change doctors, patients and his mother-in-law into bloodthirsty zombies.
tagline: Facelifts, boob jobs and zombies
title: Yummy
plot:
Yummy is a 2019 Belgian comedy horror film directed by Lars Damoiseaux, who co-wrote the screenplay with Eveline Hagenbeek. Widely described as the first Belgian zombie film, it stars Maaike Neuville as Alison, Bart Hollanders as her boyfriend Michael, Benjamin Ramon as the orderly Daniel and Clara Cleymans as the hospital administrator Janja, with Annick Christiaens and Eric Godon in supporting roles. The story satirises the cosmetic surgery industry through a gory zombie outbreak in a shabby clinic.

Alison travels with Michael and her mother Sylvia to a cut-price cosmetic surgery hospital somewhere in Eastern Europe, where the renowned surgeon Dr. K is to operate on both women. Michael, a squeamish and anxious young man, is uneasy about the clinic's lax standards. He is given a tour by Daniel, a staff member who abandons him midway to steal drugs. Wandering alone, Michael discovers a restrained and muzzled woman in a back room and removes her muzzle just as Daniel returns.

The woman is a zombie, the result of a secret experimental treatment carried out in the facility. She frees herself and starts attacking patients and staff, and the infection rapidly spreads throughout the hospital. Michael interrupts Alison's surgery so that they can escape, but they become separated, and Alison goes in search of her mother, who is bitten while Alison tries to wheel her to safety. As the small group of survivors, including Daniel, attempt to escape through the infected corridors, they learn from Dr. K that the clinic accidentally created the virus during experiments, before he is killed by Janja, who is hiding secrets of her own. The night descends into increasingly grotesque set pieces involving liposuction machines, surgical tools and mutilated patients.

The film combines slapstick humour, splatter effects and social satire about vanity and the pursuit of youthful beauty, and it presents Michael's growth from a timid boyfriend to a reluctant survivor.

On Rotten Tomatoes it holds an approval rating of about 69 percent, with critics enjoying its gleefully gory practical effects while finding its humour crude and uneven.

overview: 14-year-old basketball phenom Terron Forte has to navigate the under-the-table world of amateur athletics when he is recruited to an elite NCAA prep school.
tagline: Every dream has a price.
title: Amateur
plot:
Amateur is a 2018 American sports drama film written and directed by Ryan Koo, produced with Mandalay Pictures and released on Netflix on 6 April 2018 under the tagline "Every dream has a price". The project began in 2011 as a crowdfunded film called Manchild; a short prequel was released in 2013 under the name Amateur, the feature adopted that title in November 2014, and in January 2016 Netflix acquired the rights to finance and distribute it. It stars Michael Rainey Jr., Josh Charles, Sharon Leal and Brian J. White, with cinematography by Gregory J. Wilson, and runs about 96 minutes.

Terron Forte (Rainey) is a 14-year-old basketball phenom playing on a struggling school team. He is also burdened with a learning disability, dyscalculia, or number blindness: algebra is a mystery to him and he cannot read the scoreboard or the clock, an affliction the film visualises through the garbled numbers only he sees, though he is smart enough to find workarounds, with coaches counting down the shot clock for him. His father Vince (White), a former football player who never made it, suffers the effects of too many concussions, while his mother Nia (Leal), a teacher, values academics and wants him to earn a degree in case basketball does not work out.
