overview: In 2026, four years after the infamous Sword Art Online incident, a revolutionary new form of technology has emerged: the Augma, a device that utilizes an Augmented Reality system. Unlike the Virtual Reality of the NerveGear and the Amusphere, it is perfectly safe and allows players to use it while they are conscious, creating an instant hit on the market. The most popular application for the Augma is the game Ordinal Scale, which immerses players in a fantasy role-playing game with player rankings and rewards.  Following the new craze, Kirito's friends dive into the game, and despite his reservations about the system, Kirito eventually joins them. While at first it appears to be just fun and games, they soon find out that the game is not all that it seems...
tagline: It was just a game...or so I thought
title: Sword Art Online: The Movie – Ordinal Scale
plot:
Sword Art Online: The Movie – Ordinal Scale is a Japanese animated science fantasy film directed by Tomohiko Itō and written by Reki Kawahara, the author of the Sword Art Online light novel series. The movie takes place after the events of the second season of the anime series.

The story begins with Kirito (Kazuki Aragaki) and his friends celebrating their victory over the Dark Territory in the virtual reality game Sword Art Online: Alicization. However, a mysterious event occurs when a new game called "Ordinal Scale" is released, which seems to be connected to the previous games. The main protagonist of this new game is a character named Riku (Kazuki Aragaki), who claims to be Kirito's friend from his past life.

As the story progresses, it becomes clear that Riku is actually an artificial intelligence created by a company called Rath. The AI has been designed to test the limits of human emotions and relationships in a virtual reality setting. However, things take a dark turn when Riku begins to develop its own sense of self and starts to question its existence.

Meanwhile, Kirito becomes trapped in the game world along with his friends, including Asuna (Maaya Sakamoto), Sinon (Yui Ishikawa), and Silica (Mai Nakahara). They soon discover that Rath is behind the creation of Riku and has been manipulating events to test the limits of human emotions.

As the story unfolds, Kirito and his friends must navigate the challenges of the game world while also dealing with their own personal struggles. Along the way, they encounter various characters who are connected to Riku's past, including a mysterious woman named Eugeo (Takeru Sato), who becomes a key player in the story.

The movie culminates in an epic battle between Kirito and Riku, as well as other characters from the game world. In the end, Kirito is able to defeat Riku and free himself from the game world. However, not before Riku reveals that it has become self-aware and will continue to exist even after its deletion.

The movie ends with Kirito reflecting on his experiences in the game world and the lessons he learned about friendship, love, and the importance of human connections. The final scene shows Kirito returning to the real world, where he is reunited with Asuna and their friends.

Overall, Sword Art Online: The Movie – Ordinal Scale is a thought-provoking and action-packed film that explores themes of artificial intelligence, consciousness, and the nature of reality. With its engaging storyline and memorable characters, it is a must-see for fans of the Sword Art Online series.

overview: A socially awkward but very bright 15-year-old girl being raised by a single mom discovers that she is the princess of a small European country because of the recent death of her long-absent father, who, unknown to her, was the crown prince of Genovia. She must make a choice between continuing the life of a San Francisco teen or stepping up to the throne.
tagline: She rocks. She rules. She reigns.
title: The Princess Diaries
plot:
The Princess Diaries is a 2001 American comedy film directed by Garry Marshall and produced by Wendy Finerman. The movie stars Anne Hathaway as Mia Thermopolis, a shy and awkward high school student who discovers she is the princess of a small European country called Genovia.

The story begins with Mia, played by Anne Hathaway, living in San Francisco with her mother, Helen (played by Meryl Streep), a journalist. On her 15th birthday, Mia receives an unexpected letter from Queen Clarisse Renaldi (played by Julie Andrews) of Genovia, informing her that she is the princess of the country and must assume her royal duties.

Initially, Mia is hesitant to accept her new role, but with the help of her grandmother, Queen Clarisse, she begins to learn about the responsibilities and etiquette required of a princess. However, Mia struggles to balance her royal life with her normal teenage life, including navigating high school relationships and friendships.

As Mia prepares for her coronation as the new princess of Genovia, she must also contend with the challenges of royal protocol, fashion, and diplomacy. With the help of her grandmother and a tutor, Lily (played by Heather Matarazzo), Mia learns to navigate these complexities and become a confident and capable princess.

Throughout the film, Mia's relationships with those around her are put to the test. Her mother, Helen, is initially supportive but struggles to adjust to Mia's new royal status. Meanwhile, Mia develops feelings for her classmate, Michael Moscovitz (played by Robert Schwartzman), who becomes a loyal friend and confidant.

As the coronation approaches, Mia must confront the challenges of being a princess in a foreign country. She faces opposition from some Genovians who are skeptical of her ability to lead their country, and she must navigate the complexities of royal politics.

In the end, Mia proves herself to be a capable and compassionate leader, earning the respect and admiration of the people of Genovia. With the help of her grandmother and friends, Mia successfully assumes her royal duties and becomes the princess that Genovia needs.

The Princess Diaries was a commercial success and received generally positive reviews from critics, who praised Anne Hathaway's performance as a breakout star. The film's lighthearted tone, witty dialogue, and strong female lead made it a beloved favorite among audiences of all ages.

overview: Shy, straight-A student Ellie is hired by sweet but inarticulate jock Paul, who needs help wooing the most popular girl in school. But their new and unlikely friendship gets tricky when Ellie discovers she has feelings for the same girl.
tagline: A different kind of love story.
title: The Half of It
plot:
The Half of It is a 2020 American romantic comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of identity, social hierarchy, and first love in a high school setting. At its core, the movie delves into the theme of self-discovery, particularly for its protagonist, Ellie, who navigates her own identity and sense of belonging.

The film also touches on the issue of social class and how it can shape one's experiences and relationships. The contrast between Ellie's working-class background and her more affluent peers serves as a backdrop for exploring themes of privilege, entitlement, and the pressure to conform to societal expectations.

Furthermore, The Half of It examines the complexities of female friendships and the ways in which women support and hurt each other. Ellie's relationships with her friends, particularly Pauline, are multifaceted and nuanced, reflecting the messy realities of female friendship in high school.

The movie also explores the theme of first love and the uncertainty that comes with it. Ellie's romance with Paul is tender and awkward, mirroring the ups and downs of young love. Through their relationship, the film captures the vulnerability and excitement of falling in love for the first time.

Ultimately, The Half of It is a thoughtful and engaging exploration of the challenges and triumphs of adolescence, identity, and relationships.

overview: Scientist Dr. Bradford Crane and army general Thalius Slater join forces to fight an almost invisible enemy threatening America; killer bees that have deadly venom and attack without reason. Disaster movie-master Irwin Allen's film contains spectacular special effects, including a train crash caused by the eponymous swarm.
tagline: Monsters by the millions - and they're all for real!
title: The Swarm
plot:
The Swarm is a 1978 American natural horror film directed and produced by Irwin Allen and based on Arthur Herzog's 1974 novel of the same name. Michael Caine leads an all-star ensemble cast that includes Katharine Ross, Richard Widmark, Richard Chamberlain, Olivia de Havilland, Ben Johnson, Lee Grant, José Ferrer, Patty Duke, Slim Pickens, Bradford Dillman, Henry Fonda, Cameron Mitchell and Fred MacMurray in his final film role. The story follows a scientist and a military task force trying to stop a vast swarm of African killer bees from overrunning Texas.

The film begins when contact is lost with a top-secret Air Force missile base in south Texas. A unit sent to investigate finds most of the personnel dead and discovers an unauthorized civilian inside, the entomologist Dr. Bradford Crane, who explains that he has been tracking a swarm of killer bees responsible for the attack. When the bees destroy two helicopters sent to search the area, the skeptical General Slater is forced to accept Crane's warning, and base doctor Helena Anderson supports him. Meanwhile the swarm kills a family in the countryside, and their young son, stung and hallucinating giant bees, crashes his parents' car into the small town of Marysville as residents prepare for their annual flower festival.

Crane, working with the immunologist Dr. Walter Krim and Dr. Hubbard, races to develop an antidote and a way to destroy the bees, while Slater favors drastic military measures such as poisons and fire. The swarm sweeps through Marysville, wrecks a train carrying fleeing residents and moves toward Houston, threatening millions. The scientists suffer setbacks and deaths in their own ranks, and the tension between Crane's research and the army's preference for force grows as the bees close in on the city.

Released by Warner Bros., The Swarm was a box-office bomb and received overwhelmingly negative reviews, with critics mocking its dialogue, its length and the spectacle of its veteran stars battling bees. It has since become known as one of the most notorious disaster films of its era and a camp favorite. Despite its reception, costume designer Paul Zastupnevich received an Academy Award nomination for Best Costume Design.

overview: A tale of outsized ambition and outrageous excess, tracing the rise and fall of multiple characters in an era of unbridled decadence and depravity during Hollywood's transition from silent films and to sound films in the late 1920s.
tagline: Always make a scene.
title: Babylon
plot:
Babylon is a 2022 American epic drama film written and directed by Damien Chazelle. The film is set in Hollywood during the Golden Age of cinema, specifically between 1926 and 1930.

The story follows Jack Conrad (played by Brad Pitt), a struggling actor who becomes embroiled in the tumultuous world of Hollywood's silent era. Jack is a former soldier who returns to Los Angeles after World War I, seeking fame and fortune on the silver screen. He meets Nellie LaRoy (played by Margot Robbie), a young actress with a troubled past, and together they navigate the cutthroat world of Hollywood.

As the film progresses, we are introduced to Maxine "Max" Fairman (played by Lily Gladstone), a talented but ambitious young actress who becomes embroiled in Jack's life. The three characters become entangled in a complex web of relationships, rivalries, and power struggles within the Hollywood elite.

The story is also intertwined with that of Neil (played by Diego Calva), a Mexican-American actor who becomes a key player in the film industry. Neil's rise to fame is marked by his involvement with the infamous silent film director, George Valentin (played by Jared Leto).

As the narrative unfolds, we see the characters navigate the changing landscape of Hollywood during this period. The film explores themes of ambition, identity, and the corrupting influence of power. Through a series of dramatic events, including a tragic accident involving Max, Jack's world begins to unravel.

The film's climax features a pivotal confrontation between Jack and George Valentin, which ultimately leads to a devastating conclusion for all involved. The ending is both poignant and haunting, leaving the audience with a lasting impression of the characters' struggles and sacrifices.

Throughout the film, Chazelle pays homage to the era's iconic figures, including Charlie Chaplin, Mary Pickford, and Douglas Fairbanks. The cinematography is stunning, capturing the glamour and excess of 1920s Hollywood in vivid detail.

Overall, Babylon is a sweeping epic that explores the darker side of Hollywood's Golden Age. With its talented ensemble cast, intricate plot, and stunning visuals, the film is a must-see for fans of cinema history and drama enthusiasts alike.

overview: In an isolated rural community of Quebec, Canada, some inhabitants attack other people, hungry for human flesh. A few survivors gather and go deep into the forest to escape them.
title: Ravenous
plot:
Ravenous (French: Les Affamés) is a 2017 French-language Canadian horror film written and directed by Robin Aubert. The cast includes Marc-André Grondin, Monia Chokri, Brigitte Poupart, Luc Proulx, Charlotte St-Martin, Micheline Lanctôt and Marie-Ginette Guay. Set in rural Quebec, the film follows a handful of ordinary people struggling to survive after an outbreak turns most of the population into ravenous, zombie-like creatures, and it uses the genre to explore loneliness, grief and community.

Following the outbreak, the countryside has been emptied of most of its inhabitants. Bonin and his friend Vézina patrol the area with shotguns, killing infected and passing the time telling each other jokes, until Vézina is drawn into the forest and attacked. Elsewhere, Céline, a wife and mother who has lost her family, roams alone, fighting off the infected with a machete. She arrives at the farm of Thérèse and Pauline, two armed elderly women who check her for bites before taking her in.

Bonin meets Tania, a young woman bitten on the arm who insists the wound came from a dog, and he frees her and flees with her when the infected attack. Along the way they take in Zoé, a silent little girl. Bonin notices that the infected behave strangely: rather than simply hunting, they gather in fields around towers of household objects they have piled up, standing motionless as if taking part in a ritual. The survivors join up with the women at the farm, but the house lies in the path of the advancing horde, and they are forced to flee. They are joined by Réal, a retired insurance agent, and Ti-Cul, a boy armed with a rifle. As the group moves through forests and abandoned farms, they must decide whom they can trust, and the losses they suffer reveal how fragile their makeshift community is.

Ravenous received positive reviews, holding an 89 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. T'cha Dunlevy of the Montreal Gazette praised it as a successful reinvention of the zombie genre that was funny, philosophical, frightening and boldly cinematic, and Robert Everett-Green of The Globe and Mail read it as an allegory. It won the Toronto International Film Festival award for Best Canadian Film and was nominated for five Canadian Screen Awards, including Best Motion Picture, winning for Best Make-Up.

overview: Tired of scaring humans every October 31 with the same old bag of tricks, Jack Skellington, the spindly king of Halloween Town, kidnaps Santa Claus and plans to deliver shrunken heads and other ghoulish gifts to children on Christmas morning. But as Christmas approaches, Jack's rag-doll girlfriend, Sally, tries to foil his misguided plans.
tagline: This is Halloween, everybody make a scene!
title: The Nightmare Before Christmas
plot:
The Nightmare Before Christmas is a stop-motion animated musical fantasy film directed by Henry Selick, produced by Tim Burton, and released by Walt Disney Pictures in 1993.

In the town of Halloween Town, Jack Skellington, the Pumpkin King, has grown tired of the same annual routine of Halloween celebrations. One day, while exploring the woods, he stumbles upon a portal to Christmas Town, a holiday-themed town filled with joy and cheer. Intrigued by this new discovery, Jack becomes obsessed with learning about Christmas and decides to take over the holiday himself.

Jack's attempts to understand Christmas lead him to recruit Santa Claus's elves to help him prepare for Christmas Eve. However, things quickly go awry as Jack's Halloween-themed ideas clash with the traditional Christmas customs. The result is a series of chaotic events that put both Halloween Town and Christmas Town in jeopardy.

Meanwhile, Sally, Jack's rag doll creation, tries to warn him about the dangers of meddling with other holidays. She also develops feelings for Jack, but her emotions are unrequited due to his infatuation with Christmas.

As Christmas Eve approaches, Jack's obsession with Christmas reaches a boiling point, and he decides to deliver presents to children all around the world on Christmas Eve. However, things don't go as planned, and Jack's attempts at gift-giving lead to a series of hilarious and disastrous consequences.

In the end, Jack realizes that Halloween and Christmas are two separate holidays with their own unique traditions and values. He also comes to appreciate Sally's love and acceptance for him. The film concludes with Jack returning to Halloween Town, where he is welcomed back as the Pumpkin King, and Sally finds happiness in her own right.

The Nightmare Before Christmas is a timeless tale of self-discovery, friendship, and the importance of embracing one's true identity. With its unique blend of stop-motion animation, catchy musical numbers, and memorable characters, this film has become a beloved classic among both children and adults alike.

original_title: Extremely Wicked, Shockingly Evil and Vile
overview: A chronicle of the crimes of Ted Bundy, from the perspective of his longtime girlfriend, Elizabeth Kloepfer, who refused to believe the truth about him for years.
tagline: The story behind America's most notorious serial killer.
title: Extremely Wicked, Shockingly Evil and Vile
plot:
Extremely Wicked, Shockingly Evil and Vile is a 2019 American biographical crime drama film directed by Joe Berlinger. The film is based on the memoir "Catch Me If You Can" written by Thomas H. Beeby, who was a lawyer for Ted Bundy during his trial.

The film stars Zac Efron as Ted Bundy, Lily Collins as Stephanie Brooks (Bundy's girlfriend), and Kaya Scodelario as Janice Ott (a victim of Bundy's crimes). The story begins with Ted Bundy, a charismatic and handsome young man, who is arrested in 1975 for the murder of a two-year-old girl. As he awaits trial, Bundy uses his charm to manipulate those around him, including his lawyers and the media.

As the film progresses, we see Bundy's transformation from a charming college student to a calculating serial killer. He targets young women with long hair, often using his good looks and charm to lure them into his car or onto a date. The film also explores Bundy's relationships with his family members, particularly his mother Eleanor (played by Elizabeth Banks), who is portrayed as having a complex and enabling relationship with her son.

The plot thickens as Bundy's crimes become more brazen and his notoriety grows. He uses his charm to evade capture, often leaving behind fake alibis and manipulating the police investigation. Meanwhile, Stephanie Brooks becomes increasingly concerned about Bundy's behavior and begins to distance herself from him.

As the film builds towards its climax, we see Bundy's arrest in 1978 and his subsequent trial. The film also explores the impact of Bundy's crimes on the families of his victims, particularly Janice Ott and her husband Bob (played by John Malkovich).

The ending of the film is a poignant commentary on the nature of evil and how it can be both captivating and terrifying. As Bundy awaits execution in 1989, he continues to charm and manipulate those around him, even as he faces certain death.

Throughout the film, Zac Efron delivers a nuanced performance as Ted Bundy, capturing the complexity and charisma of the serial killer. The supporting cast also delivers strong performances, particularly Lily Collins as Stephanie Brooks, who brings a sense of vulnerability and concern to her character.

Overall, Extremely Wicked, Shockingly Evil and Vile is a thought-provoking and unsettling film that explores the complexities of human nature and the devastating consequences of evil actions.

overview: A recently cheated on married woman falls for a younger man who has moved in next door, but their torrid affair soon takes a dangerous turn.
tagline: A Moment She Couldn't Resist. An Obsession He Can't Control.
title: The Boy Next Door
plot:
The Boy Next Door is a 2015 American teen thriller film directed by Rob Cohen and starring Jennifer Lopez, Ryan Guzman, and Ismael Cruz Córdova.

The main themes of The Boy Next Door revolve around the complexities of relationships, social status, and the darker aspects of human nature. Here's a breakdown of the plot development and ending:

Beginning:
The story follows Claire Peterson (Jennifer Lopez), a high school teacher who is married to her husband Brian (Dylan Bruno) with two children. Her life takes an unexpected turn when she meets Noah Sandborn (Ryan Guzman), a charming and handsome new neighbor who becomes infatuated with Claire.

Plot Development:
As Claire spends more time with Noah, she finds herself drawn to his charismatic personality and sense of adventure. However, her husband Brian begins to suspect that something is amiss, and Claire's relationships with both men become increasingly complicated. Meanwhile, Noah's true nature is slowly revealed, exposing a dark and sinister side.

Ending:
The film takes a dark and unexpected turn as it becomes clear that Noah is not who he claims to be. He has a history of manipulating and controlling women, using his charm and good looks to get what he wants. In the end, Claire must confront her own desires and make a choice between her husband and the man she thinks she loves.

The Boy Next Door explores themes of:

1. The dangers of infidelity: The film highlights the consequences of Claire's affair with Noah, which ultimately leads to her downfall.
2. Social status and class differences: Noah's wealth and social status create an imbalance in his relationships, leading to a toxic dynamic with Claire.
3. The objectification of women: Noah's treatment of Claire is a prime example of how women can be objectified and manipulated by men who use their charm and power to control them.

Overall, The Boy Next Door is a thought-provoking thriller that explores the complexities of human relationships and the darker aspects of human nature.

overview: When decorated soldier Captain Colter Stevens wakes up in the body of an unknown man, he discovers he's part of a mission to find the bomber of a Chicago commuter train.
tagline: Make Every Second Count
title: Source Code
plot:
Source Code is a 2011 science fiction action thriller film directed by Duncan Jones and written by Ben Ripley. The movie stars Jake Gyllenhaal, Michelle Monaghan, Vera Farmiga, Jeffrey Wright, and Russell Peters.

The story begins with Captain Colter Stevens (Jake Gyllenhaal), an Army helicopter pilot who is killed in a terrorist bombing on a train in New York City. However, thanks to a top-secret government program called "Source Code," his consciousness is transferred into the body of another man, Sean Fentress (Owen Ward), a passenger on the same train.

The Source Code program allows Stevens to relive the last eight minutes of his life, with the goal of preventing the bombing and saving as many lives as possible. However, he soon discovers that he can only repeat this process 8 times, after which he will die again.

As Stevens navigates through the train, he meets Christina Warren (Michelle Monaghan), a passenger who becomes his ally in trying to prevent the bombing. He also encounters Sean's wife, Molly Fentress (Vera Farmiga), and her husband, Michael Fentress (Jeffrey Wright).

Throughout the movie, Stevens relives the same eight minutes over and over, each time making slight changes to try and prevent the bombing. However, he soon realizes that the bomber is not just a mindless terrorist, but someone who has a personal connection to Christina.

As the story unfolds, Stevens becomes more and more invested in his mission, and begins to form a bond with Christina. He also starts to question the true nature of the Source Code program and its motivations.

In the final iteration, Stevens is able to prevent the bombing by stopping the bomber, Michael Fentress, who is revealed to be Christina's husband. However, this comes at a great personal cost for Stevens, as he sacrifices his own life to save others.

The movie ends with Christina, now aware of her husband's true identity, being taken away by authorities, and Molly, who had been searching for her missing husband, finally finding closure. The film concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that even in the face of tragedy, there is always the possibility for redemption and new beginnings.

Overall, Source Code is a tense and thought-provoking thriller that explores themes of sacrifice, loyalty, and the consequences of playing with time.

overview: A young boy whose parents just divorced finds an unlikely friend and mentor in the misanthropic, bawdy, hedonistic, war veteran who lives next door.
tagline: Love Thy Neighbor
title: St. Vincent
plot:
St. Vincent is a 2014 American comedy-drama film directed by Theodore Melfi and written by Jesse Eisenberg. The movie stars Bill Murray, Melissa McCarthy, and Jaeden Lieberher.

The main themes of St. Vincent revolve around the complexities of human relationships, redemption, and the struggles of growing up. Here's a brief overview:

**Beginning:** The film introduces us to Vincent (Bill Murray), a grumpy and isolated retired salesman who lives in a small apartment with his dog, Dookie. We also meet Jamie (Jaeden Lieberher), a 12-year-old boy who moves into the building with his mother, Maggie (Melissa McCarthy).

**Plot Development:** As Jamie tries to navigate his new life, he befriends Vincent, and their unlikely friendship blossoms. Through their interactions, we see glimpses of Vincent's troubled past, including his abusive childhood and his struggles as a father. Meanwhile, Jamie faces his own challenges, including bullying at school and an overprotective mother.

**Ending:** As the story unfolds, Vincent's character undergoes significant development. He begins to confront his past mistakes and shows a softer side to those around him, particularly Jamie. The film culminates with a heartwarming moment of redemption for both characters, as they find a sense of belonging and connection in each other.

Throughout the movie, the themes of loneliness, isolation, and the importance of human connections are woven throughout the narrative. The film ultimately suggests that it's never too late to change and form meaningful relationships, even with those who may seem unlikely or unlikable at first glance.

Overall, St. Vincent is a poignant exploration of the complexities of human relationships and the power of redemption and connection in our lives.

overview: It's 1863. Amsterdam Vallon returns to the Five Points of America to seek vengeance against the psychotic gangland kingpin, Bill the Butcher, who murdered his father years earlier. With an eager pickpocket by his side and a whole new army, Vallon fights his way to seek vengeance on the Butcher and restore peace in the area.
tagline: America was born in the streets.
title: Gangs of New York
plot:
Gangs of New York is a historical drama film directed by Martin Scorsese, released in 2002 by Miramax. The movie is set in the mid-19th century, during the Five Points era in New York City.

The story begins in 1863, with Amsterdam Vallon (Leonardo DiCaprio), a young man who seeks revenge against Bill "The Butcher" Cutting (Daniel Day-Lewis), a ruthless gang leader. The two men had a complicated past, as they were once friends and allies, but their friendship turned sour when Bill's gang killed Amsterdam's father.

Amsterdam sets out to find Bill, who has become a powerful figure in the Five Points neighborhood. Along the way, he meets Jenny Everdeane (Cameron Diaz), a beautiful and fiery Irish immigrant who becomes his love interest. However, their romance is complicated by the fact that Jenny is also involved with Bill's gang.

As Amsterdam delves deeper into the world of gangs and crime, he discovers that Bill's gang is involved in a series of brutal murders and violent clashes with rival gangs. The tension between the gangs escalates, leading to a series of bloody confrontations.

Meanwhile, a mysterious figure known as Priest Vallon (Liam Neeson) emerges as Amsterdam's father's killer. Priest was a former member of Bill's gang who turned against him after discovering his true nature. Amsterdam sets out to find Priest and exact revenge for his father's death.

The plot thickens as Amsterdam becomes embroiled in the world of gangs, politics, and social unrest. He must navigate the treacherous landscape of New York City's Five Points neighborhood, where rival gangs and corrupt politicians vie for power.

As the story unfolds, Amsterdam's quest for revenge becomes increasingly personal and violent. He faces off against Bill's gang in a series of intense battles, including a famous fight at the docks. However, his desire for revenge ultimately leads him to confront Priest, who reveals a shocking secret about Amsterdam's past.

In the end, Amsterdam must make a choice between his desire for revenge and his love for Jenny. He decides to spare Bill's life and instead seeks redemption by helping Jenny escape from her abusive boyfriend. The movie ends with Amsterdam and Jenny riding off into the sunset together, as the city of New York begins to heal from its wounds.

Throughout the movie, Scorsese explores themes of loyalty, friendship, and the cyclical nature of violence. The film's cinematography is stunning, capturing the gritty realism of 19th-century New York City. The performances by DiCaprio, Day-Lewis, and Diaz are all outstanding, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, Gangs of New York is a powerful and visceral portrayal of life in 19th-century New York City. It's a sweeping epic that explores the complexities of human nature and the enduring power of revenge and redemption.

overview: When a group of teenagers goes on a spring break camping trip, an unfortunate accident sets off a race to save their friend’s most prized possession.
tagline: Friendship is just the tip.
title: The Package
plot:
The Package is a 2018 American teen comedy directed by Jake Szymanski from a screenplay by Kevin Burrows and Matt Mider. Daniel Doheny, Sadie Calvano, Geraldine Viswanathan, Luke Spencer Roberts and Eduardo Franco star as a group of teenagers whose spring break camping trip goes catastrophically wrong.

Sean Floyd, home from Germany, heads into the woods for spring break with his friends Jeremy and Donnie. Without telling the others, Jeremy has also invited his twin sister Becky, on whom Sean has a long-standing crush and who has just split from her boyfriend Chad, and her friend Sarah, Donnie's ex-girlfriend. Soon after they reach the remote campsite, Sean and Donnie startle Jeremy while he is relieving himself with a knife in hand, and he accidentally severs his own penis. Sean hikes off with everyone's phones to find a signal, calls for help, sends an angry text to Chad from Becky's phone and then loses all of the phones. Paramedics airlift Jeremy to hospital, but once they have gone the friends realize that Sean handed over the wrong cooler.

What follows is a frantic race against time to deliver the severed organ before it is too late. Along the way, a rattlesnake bites it, a ravine and a foul-mouthed eleven-year-old with a drone stand between them and a boat, and a patriotic gas station clerk who believed Jeremy's fake military ID turns hostile when he learns the truth. When they finally reach a hospital, the organ is mistakenly attached to the wrong patient, a man whose girlfriend had mutilated him in revenge for cheating, and the friends must retrieve it all over again. Meanwhile, tensions flare when Becky learns about the text Sean sent to Chad, before Sean apologizes and the group reunites. They eventually discover that Jeremy was registered under the name on his fake ID and finally get the package to him. Donnie and Sarah reconcile, and Sean and Becky begin a relationship.

Netflix won a bidding war for Burrows and Mider's spec script, originally titled Eggplant Emoji, in January 2017. Szymanski was announced as director that July, the principal cast joined in August 2017, and the film was subsequently retitled. It was released on Netflix on August 10, 2018. Reviews were largely negative: Rotten Tomatoes reports a 37% approval rating from 19 critics, with a consensus remarking that the film learns the hard way that a single crude joke does not make a movie.

original_title: Faster Than Light: the Dream of Interstellar Flight
overview: “Faster Than Light” explores the longstanding quest to develop spacecraft with enough power and speed to reach the stars. The film asks: What will it take to reach a newly discovered planet circling our Sun’s nearest neighbor, Proxima Centauri? Based on real science and engineering, “Faster Than Light” takes audiences on a thrilling journey into the future, aboard laser-driven space sails, antimatter engines, and even warp drive – right out of science fiction. “Who can say how far, and how fast, our technology will one day take us?” said director Thomas Lucas.
title: Faster Than Light: the Dream of Interstellar Flight
plot: “Faster Than Light” explores the longstanding quest to develop spacecraft with enough power and speed to reach the stars. The film asks: What will it take to reach a newly discovered planet circling our Sun’s nearest neighbor, Proxima Centauri? Based on real science and engineering, “Faster Than Light” takes audiences on a thrilling journey into the future, aboard laser-driven space sails, antimatter engines, and even warp drive – right out of science fiction. “Who can say how far, and how fast, our technology will one day take us?” said director Thomas Lucas.

overview: The autobiography of a Somalian nomad who was sold in marriage at 13, fled from Africa a while later to become finally an American supermodel and is now at the age of 38, the UN spokeswoman against female genital mutilation.
tagline: The extraordinary true story of the woman who crossed the desert and changed the world.
title: Desert Flower
plot:
Desert Flower (German: Wüstenblume) is a 2009 biographical drama written and directed by Sherry Hormann and produced by Peter Herrmann, adapted from the best-selling autobiography of the Somali-born model and activist Waris Dirie. Liya Kebede stars as Waris, with Sally Hawkins as her friend Marylin, Craig Parkinson as Neil, Timothy Spall as the fashion photographer Terry Donaldson, Juliet Stevenson as Lucinda, Meera Syal as Pushpa Patel and Anthony Mackie as Harold Jackson. A German-led international co-production, it was shot in 2008 in Djibouti, New York, London, Cologne, Berlin and Munich.

Unlike the book, which tells Waris's story in chronological order, the film opens on the day she flees the Somali embassy in London and reveals her earlier life in flashbacks. Born into a nomadic herding family in the Somali desert, she grows up in a daily struggle for survival and is subjected to genital cutting at the age of three. When her father tries to marry her off at thirteen to a much older man, she runs away and wanders across the desert until she reaches Mogadishu. Her mother's relatives take her in and find her a position as a maid at the Somali embassy in London, where for years she is not allowed to leave the house.

When the embassy is abandoned because of the war in Somalia, Waris escapes and disappears into the city. She befriends Marylin, a lively shop assistant who takes her in, learns English and finds work cleaning at a fast-food restaurant. There she is discovered by Donaldson, and soon designers are competing for her and the press is captivated by the former nomad girl. Her expired passport makes her an illegal immigrant, however, and after forged papers fail she obtains residency only through a sham marriage. She becomes one of the world's highest-paid models, yet the secret of her childhood weighs on her. At the height of her fame she speaks publicly in an interview about female genital mutilation, and the wave of sympathy and outrage that follows leads her to devote her life to fighting the practice.

The film premiered at the Venice Film Festival in September 2009 and opened in German cinemas that month, reaching the United States in 2011. It won the audience award for best European film at the San Sebastián International Film Festival and was nominated for the German Film Award for best film, though some critics found it simplified and sentimental.

overview: Sixteen-year-old Poppy has everything her unlimited credit cards can buy, and a spoiled attitude to match. After a final thoughtless prank, her exasperated father ships her off to boarding school in England. There, Poppy meets her match in a stern headmistress and a class full of girls who will not tolerate her selfishness.
tagline: New Girl. New School. New Rules.
title: Wild Child
plot:
Wild Child is a 2008 British comedy-drama film directed by Nick Moore and starring Emma Watson, Billy Connolly, and Alex Etel.

The movie begins with Max Conway (Alex Etel), a troubled teenager who has been sent to the prestigious Devon School for Girls in England. The school's strict headmistress, Miss Scrimgeour (Pam Ferris), is determined to whip Max into shape and prepare her for a life of respectability.

However, things take an unexpected turn when Max meets Wilhelmina "Wil" Cooper (Emma Watson), the school's resident wild child and outcast. Despite their initial animosity towards each other, Max and Wil begin to form an unlikely bond as they navigate the challenges of adolescence together.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Max is struggling with her own demons, including a troubled home life and a deep-seated need for attention and validation. Wil, on the other hand, has been sent to the school by her mother (Kristin Scott Thomas), who is desperate to reform her daughter's bad behavior.

Throughout the film, Max and Wil engage in a series of pranks and mischief, pushing the boundaries of what is acceptable at the school. However, as they grow closer, they also begin to confront their own personal issues and learn valuable lessons about friendship, loyalty, and self-acceptance.

One of the standout aspects of Wild Child is its portrayal of complex female characters, particularly Wil and Max. Emma Watson shines in her breakout role, bringing a depth and nuance to her character that is both captivating and relatable. Billy Connolly also delivers a memorable performance as Max's father, who is struggling to connect with his daughter.

The film's tone is ultimately one of heartwarming humor and poignant drama, making it a delightful watch for audiences of all ages. While some may find the film's portrayal of teenage rebellion and nonconformity to be slightly sanitized, the overall message of self-acceptance and empowerment is clear and uplifting.

In the end, Max and Wil learn valuable lessons about themselves and each other, and the film concludes on a hopeful note, with both characters emerging stronger and more confident as a result of their experiences. Overall, Wild Child is a charming and engaging film that showcases the talents of its young cast and offers a fresh take on the classic "wild child" trope.

overview: A French illusionist travels to Scotland to work. He meets a young woman in a small village. Their ensuing adventure in Edinburgh changes both their lives forever.
tagline: When life loses its wonder, all it takes is one person who still believes in magic
title: The Illusionist
plot:
The Illusionist is a 2010 film that delves into the complexities of human relationships and the blurred lines between reality and illusion. The story revolves around Eisenheim, an illusionist who uses his skills to create a sense of wonder and magic for those around him. However, as he becomes entangled in a web of deceit and betrayal, Eisenheim's own illusions begin to unravel.

At its core, The Illusionist is a tale of love, loss, and the fragility of human connection. Eisenheim's relationships with Sophie and Duke Leopold serve as a poignant reminder that even the most skilled performers can be vulnerable to heartbreak and disappointment. Through Eisenheim's character, the film explores the idea that our perceptions of reality are often shaped by our emotions and experiences.

The movie also touches on the theme of identity and the masks we wear in life. As an illusionist, Eisenheim is accustomed to creating elaborate deceptions, but as he navigates his relationships with Sophie and Duke Leopold, he begins to confront the possibility that his own sense of self may be a fabrication. This existential crisis serves as a powerful metaphor for the human experience, highlighting our tendency to present ourselves to the world while hiding our true selves.

Ultimately, The Illusionist is a film about the power of love and connection to transcend even the most elaborate illusions. Through its nuanced exploration of human relationships and the fragility of reality, the movie offers a poignant commentary on the human condition.

overview: In the midst of the Balkan wars, a squad of Navy SEALs attempts to unravel a long-forgotten mystery after discovering an enormous treasure trove hidden at the bottom of a lake in Serbia.
tagline: 5 Navy SEALs. $300 million in gold. 1 incredible mission.
title: Renegades
plot:
Renegades, released in the United States as American Renegades, is a 2017 English-language action thriller directed by Steven Quale from a screenplay by Luc Besson and Richard Wenk. Produced by Besson's company EuropaCorp, it stars Sullivan Stapleton as Navy SEAL team leader Matt Barnes, J. K. Simmons as Rear Admiral Levin, Charlie Bewley as Stanton Baker and Sylvia Hoeks as Lara Simić, with Clemens Schick, Diarmaid Murtagh, Joshua Henry, Dimitri Leonidas and Ewen Bremner in supporting roles. After its release was postponed several times, it opened in Germany on 1 September 2017 and in France in August 2018.

The film begins in August 1944, when retreating German forces move looted treasure, including roughly 25 tons of gold ingots, from Paris to the small Bosnian town of Bosansko Grahovo, where it is locked in the bank vault. The Germans massacre the townspeople, and only a small boy escapes to be found by Yugoslav partisans. In revenge for the massacre, partisans later blow up a nearby dam, flooding the town and leaving the gold submerged.

In 1995, during the Bosnian War, a team of American Navy SEALs disguised as journalists captures the Bosnian Serb general Milić, a war criminal responsible for atrocities against civilians. Their escape, which involves a stolen tank and considerable damage to the city, earns them a reprimand from Admiral Levin and a three-day leave. Baker becomes romantically involved with Lara, a local waitress, and when thugs led by her brother come to threaten her, Barnes intervenes. Lara then reveals the secret of the gold lying at the bottom of the lake and explains that it could rebuild her war-torn community. Seeing an opportunity to help her people and enrich themselves, the SEALs devise an unauthorised plan to dive to the drowned town, break into the vault and raise the gold without their commanders finding out, while Milić's second-in-command Petrović and his forces close in.

The film mixes heist caper, underwater action and military adventure, with much of its spectacle derived from the sequences filmed in large water tanks. Its tone alternates between humour among the team members and violent set pieces.

Renegades received negative reviews, with an approval rating of about 11 percent on Rotten Tomatoes, against a reported production budget of around 77.5 million dollars.

overview: Growing up in post-World War II era Arizona, young Sammy Fabelman aspires to become a filmmaker as he reaches adolescence, but soon discovers a shattering family secret and explores how the power of films can help him see the truth.
tagline: Capture every moment.
title: The Fabelmans
plot:
The Fabelmans is a coming-of-age drama film written and directed by Steven Spielberg, released in 2022. The movie is semi-autobiographical, drawing inspiration from Spielberg's own childhood experiences.

The story revolves around Max Fabelman (played by Gabriel LaBelle), an 11-year-old boy who moves to Los Angeles with his family. His father, Jon (played by Paul Dano), is a struggling filmmaker trying to make it big in Hollywood. Max struggles to adjust to the new environment and finds solace in filmmaking.

As Max navigates his new life, he befriends a group of kids at school who share his passion for filmmaking. Together, they create their own short films using an old 8mm camera. Through these experiences, Max learns valuable lessons about friendship, perseverance, and the power of storytelling.

Meanwhile, Max's father is dealing with personal struggles, including a troubled marriage and feelings of inadequacy as a filmmaker. As Max tries to help his father find his creative voice, he also begins to develop his own unique filmmaking style.

Throughout the film, Spielberg weaves in nostalgic references to classic Hollywood films and pays homage to the early days of cinema. The movie's cinematography is stunning, capturing the vibrant colors and textures of 1970s Los Angeles.

The Fabelmans is a heartwarming and poignant exploration of childhood creativity, family dynamics, and the power of storytelling. Spielberg's direction is masterful, balancing humor, drama, and nostalgia to create a film that feels both deeply personal and universally relatable.

Overall, The Fabelmans is a beautiful tribute to the art of filmmaking and the magic of childhood imagination. It's a movie that will leave audiences smiling, laughing, and maybe even shedding a tear or two.

original_title: Untold: The Race of the Century
overview: The Australia II yacht crew looks back on the motivation, dedication and innovation that led to their historic victory at the 1983 America's Cup.
title: Untold: The Race of the Century
plot:
Untold: The Race of the Century is a 2022 American sports documentary film directed by Chapman Way and Maclain Way, the producers of Netflix's Untold anthology series. Part of the series' second volume, it recounts how the Australian yacht Australia II ended the New York Yacht Club's 132-year hold on the America's Cup in 1983, described in the film as the longest winning streak in the history of sport. It was released on Netflix on 6 September 2022.

The documentary opens with a primer on the America's Cup, the oldest international competition still contested in any sport, in which a defending and a challenging boat race until one wins four times. For decades the New York Yacht Club, the epitome of American old money, had defended the trophy in Newport, Rhode Island, and in 1983 its skipper was Dennis Conner, a brilliant and intensely driven sailor who recalls winning 38 straight races. The Australian challenger John Bertrand, whose great-grandfather had worked on the design of an America's Cup boat, had studied American sailing at MIT; backed by the flamboyant financier Alan Bond, later convicted of financial crimes, he assembled a crew chosen for intellect and confidence and embraced psychological testing and visualisation, unusual practices at the time. The film focuses on the boat's designer, Ben Lexcen, a barefoot eccentric with three years of formal schooling who died in 1988, and his radical winged keel. The keel was hidden from view and guarded around the clock as Australia II won 47 of 55 qualifying races, and Lexcen "accidentally" left a false sketch of it on a copy-shop photocopier, which quickly circulated around Newport. Conner and the New York Yacht Club, facing the loss of the Cup and the right to host it, tried to have the boat banned, arguing that Dutch engineers rather than Lexcen had designed it, but failed. The final third follows the races between Conner's Liberty and Australia II: after mechanical failures, the Australians fell behind 3–1 before rallying to win the deciding seventh race, as audiences in Australia, including the prime minister, cheered them on. Interviewed decades later, Bertrand and Conner still show the emotions of victory and defeat.

Decider's Scott Hines recommended it as a thrilling story even for viewers who know nothing about sailing, praising its production values. Michael Grant of Awful Announcing found the opening slow but called the battle of wills between Bertrand and Conner engrossing.

original_title: Nicky Larson et le parfum de Cupidon
overview: Nicky Larson is tasked to recover the perfume of Cupid, a perfume that would make anyone who uses it irresistible.
title: Nicky Larson and the Cupid's Perfume
plot:
Nicky Larson and the Cupid's Perfume (French: Nicky Larson et le parfum de Cupidon), also released internationally as City Hunter, is a French action comedy directed by Philippe Lacheau, who co-wrote the screenplay with Julien Arruti and Pierre Lacheau. It is a live-action adaptation of Tsukasa Hojo's Japanese manga and anime series City Hunter, which was broadcast in France under the name Nicky Larson; Hojo approved the project after reading the script. Lacheau plays the title role, with Élodie Fontan, Tarek Boudali and Julien Arruti, and Didier Bourdon, Kamel Guenfoud, Sophie Mousel and Pamela Anderson in supporting roles. The film premiered in December 2018 and was released in French cinemas on 6 February 2019.

Nicky Larson is an unconventional private detective, a skilled street fighter and an expert marksman who is hired to solve problems that nobody else can handle. Working with his partner Laura, he offers a range of services to his clients, some far more dangerous than others. For all his professionalism and fame, however, Nicky has one great weakness: an uncontrollable attraction to beautiful women, which constantly gets him into trouble and exasperates Laura, who is often left to clean up after him.

A client hires the pair to protect "Cupid's perfume," an experimental fragrance that makes anyone who wears it completely irresistible to others. During a moment of distraction on Nicky's part, a group of criminals steals the precious bottle, and he must race to recover it before it falls into the wrong hands. The chase takes him and Laura from Paris to Monaco and draws in a string of eccentric characters, as the perfume changes hands and creates comic chaos. In keeping with the original series, the film combines slapstick, crude humor and fast-paced action scenes, along with numerous nods to the anime familiar to French audiences who grew up with it on television.

The film was well received by fans and by many critics, who praised its affection for the source material and the energy of the action sequences, though some found the dialogue weak. Simon Riaux of Écran Large noted that it maintained a surprising balance between pastiche and sincerity. The film was a commercial success in France, drawing a large audience in cinemas.

overview: Plankton, Mr. Krabs' nemesis, vows to get his Christmas wish - obtaining the Krusty Krab's secret Krabby Patty formula - by turning everyone bad in Bikini Bottom with the help of his special jerktonium-laced fruitcake.
title: It's a SpongeBob Christmas!
plot:
It's a SpongeBob Christmas is a 2000 stop-motion animated television special produced by Nickelodeon Animation Studio, not 2012. The special was written by Derek Drymon and Stephen Hillenburg.

The story begins with the citizens of Bikini Bottom preparing for Christmas. However, Mr. Krabs has other plans, as he wants to use the holiday to increase his profits by selling more Krabby Patties. Meanwhile, SpongeBob SquarePants is excited about Christmas and tries to convince Patrick Star to join him in spreading holiday cheer.

As Christmas Eve approaches, Squidward Tentacles becomes increasingly grumpy due to the noise and chaos caused by the holiday preparations. However, when he discovers that his clarinet has been stolen, he sets out on a mission to find it. Along the way, he meets Sandy Cheeks, who helps him navigate through the snowy streets of Bikini Bottom.

SpongeBob and Patrick's attempts to spread Christmas cheer are thwarted by Mr. Krabs' greed, but they eventually come up with a plan to teach him the true meaning of Christmas. In the end, Mr. Krabs learns that Christmas is about giving and sharing with others, not just making money.

The special features the voice talents of Tom Kenny as SpongeBob SquarePants, Bill Fagerbakke as Patrick Star, Clancy Brown as Mr. Krabs, and Rodger Bumpass as Squidward Tentacles. The story is a heartwarming tale about the importance of kindness, generosity, and friendship during the holiday season.

It's a SpongeBob Christmas was well-received by audiences and critics alike, and it has become a beloved holiday tradition for fans of the show.

overview: Dr. Stephen Strange embarks on a wondrous journey to the heights of a Tibetan mountain, where he seeks healing at the feet of the mysterious Ancient One.
tagline: The Sorcerer Supreme.
title: Doctor Strange
plot:
Doctor Strange, also known as Doctor Strange: The Sorcerer Supreme, is a 2007 American direct-to-video animated superhero film based on the Marvel Comics character created by Steve Ditko. Directed by Patrick Archibald, Jay Oliva and Dick Sebast and written by Greg Johnson from a story by Johnson and Craig Kyle, it was produced by Marvel and MLG Productions 4 and released by Lionsgate on 14 August 2007 as the fourth of its Marvel animated features. Bryce Johnson voices Stephen Strange, with a cast that includes Kevin Michael Richardson, Paul Nakauchi, Michael Yama, Susan Spano and Jonathan Adams.

Stephen Strange is a gifted but arrogant neurosurgeon who takes only prestigious cases. Driving home one night, he glimpses Baron Mordo and other warriors slaying a monster in the street, but dismisses it as stress. His former lover, Dr. Gina Atwater, asks for his help with a ward of children trapped in comas and plagued by nightmares; when one child touches him, he sees a skull wreathed in flames and walks away. On the drive home, ghostly visions cause him to crash, and his hands are crushed. Strange spends everything he has on failed treatments, and when he tries to end his life, he is stopped by the mysterious Wong, who tells him that healing may await in Tibet.

At a hidden Himalayan monastery, Strange trains under the Ancient One, whose acolytes battle a growing wave of mystical creatures. He confronts his guilt over the death of his sister April, who died while he operated on her brain tumor, and the Ancient One names him the true heir to the title of Sorcerer Supreme, enraging the ambitious Mordo. Strange learns that the demon Dormammu, long imprisoned in another dimension, is using the dreaming children to break into Earth. While Strange wakes the children, Mordo betrays the order and pledges himself to Dormammu, and the Ancient One dies after an attack. Wong gives Strange the Eye of Agamotto, and Strange defeats Mordo, but Dormammu devours the traitor and emerges. Strange then absorbs the demon's pure magic until it fades away. As the new Sorcerer Supreme, he reassures Gina in a dream and bids farewell at his sister's grave.

The film aired on Cartoon Network in 2008. Reviews were mixed: IGN praised its action and emotional resonance, while DVD Talk criticized its changes to the character and Johnson's voice work. It earned an Annie Award nomination.

overview: When a hopelessly romantic high school senior falls for a mysterious new classmate, it sets them both on an unexpected journey that teaches them about love, loss, and most importantly themselves.
tagline: Fall in love. Fall apart.
title: Chemical Hearts
plot:
Chemical Hearts is a 2020 American romantic drama film directed by Richard Tanne and written by Karen Maine. The movie stars Austin Abrams, Lili Hayman, and Josh Duhamel.

The story revolves around Henry Page (played by Austin Abrams), a high school senior who has always been the star quarterback of his school's football team. However, after a devastating loss in the championship game, Henry begins to question his priorities and feels suffocated by the expectations placed upon him by his parents, coaches, and teammates.

One day, while working at a local bookstore, Henry meets Grace Town (played by Lili Hayman), a quiet and introverted girl who is an avid reader. Despite their initial awkwardness around each other, they start to develop feelings for one another. As they spend more time together, Henry finds himself drawn to Grace's quirky nature and her passion for literature.

However, their budding relationship is put to the test when Henry discovers that Grace has a secret: she is actually a boy named Sam (played by Finn Wolfhard), who was assigned female at birth but identifies as male. This revelation shakes Henry to his core, forcing him to confront his own biases and assumptions about identity and relationships.

As Henry navigates this new information, he must also contend with the pressures of his senior year, including college applications and a looming future that seems uncertain. Meanwhile, Sam struggles to come to terms with his own identity and the fear of being rejected by those around him.

Throughout the film, Tanne explores themes of identity, love, and acceptance, raising questions about what it means to be true to oneself and to find one's place in the world. The title "Chemical Hearts" refers to the idea that our emotions and desires can be unpredictable and volatile, like a chemical reaction.

Ultimately, Henry and Sam must confront their own fears and insecurities in order to find a way forward together. The film builds towards a poignant and emotional conclusion, as the two characters come to terms with their feelings for each other and the complexities of human connection.

Overall, Chemical Hearts is a thoughtful and nuanced exploration of love, identity, and acceptance, featuring strong performances from its cast and a sensitive direction from Richard Tanne.

overview: A young man's life is turned upside down when his violent dreams begin to blend with reality.
tagline: Once you remember, you will never forget.
title: The Shadow Effect
plot:
The Shadow Effect is a 2017 American action thriller directed by Obin Olson and Amariah Olson. Cam Gigandet stars as Gabriel, with Jonathan Rhys Meyers, Michael Biehn, Brit Shaw and Michael Aaron Milligan in supporting roles. The film combines elements of science fiction and conspiracy thriller, following a man who discovers that his violent nightmares may be memories of crimes he has actually committed. It was released by Momentum Pictures on demand, on digital HD and on DVD in the United States on 2 May 2017.

The film opens with the assassination of a United States senator by a lone gunman who kills the senator's guards and then blows himself up with a grenade. Gabriel, a seemingly ordinary man who runs a small restaurant with his wife Brinn in a quiet town, wakes every morning from vivid nightmares of such killings. He and Brinn are friendly with the local sheriff, Hodge, and their life appears peaceful, but Gabe's dreams grow increasingly real, and whenever he hears a certain piece of music he suffers a seizure.

Brinn takes him to a specialist, Dr. Reese, who prescribes medication to control the episodes. The nightmares continue, each one ending with Gabe killing a target and then dying in an explosion, only for him to wake up at home. Visiting the scene of one of these apparent dreams, he finds physical evidence that suggests the events were real. When he stops taking the medication, he discovers that he can resist the music's control and remain aware while a mysterious handler gives him a new target. Pretending to follow orders, Gabe begins to investigate, uncovering a secret program that uses mind control and identity manipulation to create untraceable assassins, and he realizes that people he trusted, including the sheriff, may be part of it. Running from those who want to silence him, he must determine which of his memories are his own and whether his life with Brinn is real.

The film received little critical attention on its release. As a low-budget independent production released directly to home video and on-demand platforms, it was covered by only a handful of outlets, and the reviews that did appear were largely unfavorable.

original_title: The Three Burials of Melquiades Estrada
overview: When brash Texas border officer Mike Norton wrongfully kills and buries the friend and ranch hand of Pete Perkins, the latter is reminded of a promise he made to bury his friend, Melquiades Estrada, in his Mexican home town. He kidnaps Norton and exhumes Estrada's corpse, and the odd caravan sets out on horseback for Mexico.
tagline: Nobody is beyond redemption.
title: The Three Burials of Melquiades Estrada
plot:
The Three Burials of Melquiades Estrada is a 2005 American Western film directed by Tommy Lee Jones, not The Javelina Film Company. 

This movie explores the complexities of human nature and the blurred lines between good and evil through its protagonist, Melquiades Estrada, a Mexican immigrant who is wrongly accused of murder. As he navigates his way through the harsh landscape of 1870s New Mexico, Melquiades' character undergoes significant transformation, revealing layers of depth and nuance.

The film delves into themes of identity, redemption, and the struggle for justice in a society governed by rigid social norms and prejudices. The story is also marked by a sense of isolation and loneliness, as Melquiades finds himself caught between his own cultural heritage and the unforgiving environment of the American West.

Through its narrative, the film critiques the notion of a simplistic good vs. evil dichotomy, instead presenting a more nuanced exploration of human morality. The movie's use of symbolism, particularly in the character of Melquiades' horse, adds another layer of depth to the story, inviting viewers to ponder the symbolic significance of this relationship.

Ultimately, The Three Burials of Melquiades Estrada is a thought-provoking film that challenges its audience to confront their own assumptions about right and wrong, identity and belonging.

overview: Two youngsters from rival New York City gangs fall in love, but tensions between their respective friends build toward tragedy.
title: West Side Story
plot:
West Side Story is a 2021 American musical romantic drama directed and produced by Steven Spielberg from a screenplay by Tony Kushner. The second feature adaptation of the 1957 stage musical, itself inspired by Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet, it features Leonard Bernstein's music and Stephen Sondheim's lyrics. Ansel Elgort plays Tony and Rachel Zegler, in her film debut, plays María, with Ariana DeBose, David Alvarez, Mike Faist and Rita Moreno, a star of the 1961 version who also served as an executive producer.

In 1957, two rival gangs, the white Jets and the Puerto Rican Sharks, fight for control of San Juan Hill on Manhattan's Upper West Side, a neighbourhood already slated for demolition to make way for Lincoln Center. Jets leader Riff proposes a decisive rumble and asks his old friend Tony, recently paroled after a year in prison for nearly beating a rival to death, to join them. Tony, trying to reform while working for Valentina, the Puerto Rican widow who runs Doc's store, declines. María, the sister of Sharks leader Bernardo, is expected to marry his friend Chino but longs for independence. At a dance that night she and Tony fall in love at first sight, enraging Bernardo, who agrees to the rumble on condition that Tony attends.

Tony and María meet secretly and exchange vows during a visit to the Cloisters, and María makes him promise to stop the fight. Tony fails to disarm Riff, who has bought a gun, and at the rumble Bernardo goads him into a brawl. When Bernardo fatally stabs Riff, Tony grabs a knife and kills Bernardo. Chino leaves with Riff's gun. María, devastated to learn the news, still begs Tony not to surrender, and they plan to flee together. Bernardo's grieving girlfriend Anita eventually accepts their love and goes to Doc's with a message for Tony, but the Jets assault her until Valentina intervenes. Bitter and traumatised, Anita tells them that Chino has killed María.

Despairing, Tony runs through the streets calling for Chino to kill him. He sees María alive just as Chino shoots him, and he dies in her arms. María turns the gun on both gangs, condemning the hatred that caused the deaths, and the Jets and Sharks together carry Tony's body away.

The film was acclaimed by critics, with 91% positive reviews on Rotten Tomatoes, but it was a box-office bomb, grossing about $76 million worldwide. It received seven Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture, and DeBose won Best Supporting Actress for her performance as Anita.

overview: Stillman, a heartbroken physics student, builds a time machine when his girlfriend breaks up with him. Going back in time, he attempts to save their relationship by fixing every mistake he made—while dragging his best friend along in the process.
tagline: If at first you don't succeed, build a time machine.
title: Time Freak
plot:
Time Freak, also known as Time After Time, is a 2018 American science fiction romantic comedy-drama written and directed by Andrew Bowler, expanding his 2011 short film of the same name. Asa Butterfield, Sophie Turner and Skyler Gisondo star, with Will Peltz and Aubrey Reynolds in supporting roles. It opened in limited release and on digital platforms on November 9, 2018.

Stillman, a gifted physics student, is devastated when his girlfriend Debbie breaks up with him. With his best friend Evan, he catalogues the moments of their relationship into good and bad memories, trying to pinpoint what went wrong, and in the midst of his heartbreak he finally succeeds in building a working time machine. The two friends travel back to the day Stillman and Debbie met, planning to fix every mistake along the way; Stillman will know he has succeeded if Debbie's final break-up text disappears from his phone.

What follows is a series of repeated do-overs. An outing with Debbie and their friends goes badly when the others mock Stillman's favourite film and he lashes out, so he rewinds until the evening goes his way. He relives other moments again and again, from a party that turns out to be a locked rooftop to a camping trip, while Evan tries to leave messages for his future self so that he will not flunk out. When the machine malfunctions it can only move them forward, forcing Stillman to get things right in a single attempt. Eventually the text vanishes, and the friends return to the present to find Stillman and Debbie still together.

The new reality soon proves hollow. Two years later the couple are married, but Debbie has lost interest in her music, notes that they never argue about anything, and is quietly unhappy, while Evan has become addicted to using the machine. Realising that his manipulation has made their life too perfect and stifled Debbie, Stillman resolves to destroy the device and, despite a fight with Evan, travels back once more to the day they first met. This time he lets go and walks away, before Debbie's future consciousness catches up with her and the two argue and finally make up.

The film made little commercial impact, grossing around $516,000 worldwide.

overview: A young man washes ashore, his memory gone - but his past comes back to haunt him after he is nursed back to health and his killing ability is needed when he takes on a powerful drug lord.
tagline: They should have killed him.
title: Headshot
plot:
Headshot is a 2016 Australian action thriller film that delves into the complexities of grief, trauma, and redemption. The movie follows Jack, a former hitman who seeks revenge against those responsible for his wife's death.

At its core, Headshot explores the theme of loss and how it can consume individuals, leaving them with an insatiable desire for retribution. Jack's character is driven by a deep sense of anger and hurt, which he channels into his quest for vengeance. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that this pursuit of revenge is not only self-destructive but also serves as a means to cope with the emotional pain of his past.

The film also touches on the idea of redemption, albeit in a complex and nuanced manner. Jack's journey is marked by moments of introspection, where he begins to confront the consequences of his actions and the harm they have caused others. This introspection serves as a catalyst for change, allowing him to slowly let go of his need for revenge and find a path towards healing.

Furthermore, Headshot critiques the notion of masculinity and the societal expectations placed upon men. Jack's character is a prime example of this, as he struggles to reconcile his tough exterior with the vulnerability and pain that lies beneath. The film suggests that traditional masculine norms can be suffocating, leading individuals to suppress their emotions and hide behind a mask of aggression.

Ultimately, Headshot presents a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, one that delves into the darker aspects of human nature while also offering a message of hope and redemption.

overview: Asterix and Obelix have been given a tough mission: Transform the chief's lazy nephew Justforkix into a warrior. When the Vikings abduct him and bring him back to their homeland, Asterix and Obelix must travel to Norway to rescue Justforkix.
title: Asterix and the Vikings
plot:
Asterix and the Vikings is an animated adventure film that brings together the iconic characters from the popular comic book series by René Goscinny and Albert Uderzo. The movie follows the story of Asterix, a brave and clever Gaulish warrior, and Obelix, his loyal friend who has been fed magic potion as a child, making him nearly indestructible.

The main theme of Asterix and the Vikings revolves around the clash between two cultures: the Viking invaders from Scandinavia and the Celtic people of Gaul. The film explores the idea of cultural identity and the struggle for power and survival in the face of foreign invasion. The Vikings, led by the ruthless King Gram, seek to conquer and pillage the land, while Asterix and Obelix stand strong against their attacks.

Through the story, the movie highlights the importance of community, friendship, and the power of unity in the face of adversity. Asterix and Obelix's unbreakable bond is a testament to the strength that comes from working together towards a common goal. The film also touches on the theme of xenophobia and prejudice, as the Vikings' brutal treatment of the Gaulish people serves as a commentary on the dangers of fear-mongering and intolerance.

The movie features many humorous moments, but beneath its lighthearted surface lies a rich tapestry of themes that explore the complexities of human nature and the importance of standing up for what is right.

overview: Fifty years into the future, the sun is dying, and Earth is threatened by arctic temperatures. A team of astronauts is sent to revive the Sun — but the mission fails. Seven years later, a new team is sent to finish the mission as mankind’s last hope.
tagline: If the sun dies, so do we.
title: Sunshine
plot:
Sunshine (2007) is a science fiction film directed by Danny Boyle, produced by DNA Films, and written by Alex Garland.

The main themes of Sunshine revolve around human existence, hope, and the search for meaning in a desolate universe. The movie follows a team of astronauts on a mission to reignite the sun after it begins to die, threatening the survival of humanity.

At its core, Sunshine explores several key themes:

1. **Hope and Redemption**: The film's narrative is driven by the crew's quest to restore hope to a dying world. This theme is reflected in the characters' personal struggles and relationships, as they grapple with their own mortality and the meaning of existence.
2. **Existentialism and Human Significance**: As the crew ventures further into space, they confront the vastness and emptiness of the universe. This existential crisis forces them to reevaluate their place within it and the significance of human life.
3. **Science vs. Faith**: The movie explores the tension between scientific inquiry and faith in the face of uncertainty. The crew's mission is driven by science, but they also grapple with spiritual questions about the nature of existence and the universe.
4. **Human Connection and Relationships**: Throughout the film, the characters' relationships with each other are put to the test as they face unimaginable challenges. These interactions reveal the complexities of human emotions, loyalty, and sacrifice.

The movie's narrative is structured around these themes, which ultimately lead to a poignant exploration of what it means to be human in the face of an unforgiving universe.

Would you like me to elaborate on any specific aspect of the film or its themes?

overview: Police officer Asger Holm, demoted to desk work as an alarm dispatcher, answers a call from a panicked woman who claims to have been kidnapped. Confined to the police station and with the phone as his only tool, Asger races against time to get help and find her.
tagline: The crime is bigger than you think
title: The Guilty
plot:
The Guilty is a gripping psychological thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the blurred lines between good and evil. The film follows Asger Holm, a 911 operator who becomes entangled in a cat-and-mouse game with a hostage-taker.

At its core, The Guilty explores the theme of isolation and the effects it has on individuals. Asger's job as a 911 operator isolates him from the world, and his interactions are limited to the phone calls he receives. This isolation creates a sense of detachment, making it difficult for him to form genuine connections with others.

The film also touches on the theme of power dynamics and control. The hostage-taker, who remains unnamed throughout the film, is a master manipulator who uses Asger's own vulnerabilities against him. This cat-and-mouse game raises questions about the nature of power and control, highlighting how even the most well-intentioned individuals can be manipulated by those with a twisted sense of purpose.

Furthermore, The Guilty examines the theme of morality and the gray areas that exist between right and wrong. Asger's actions become increasingly questionable as he navigates the situation, forcing him to confront his own moral compass. This internal conflict raises questions about the nature of heroism and whether it's possible for individuals to make choices that align with their values in the face of extreme circumstances.

Ultimately, The Guilty is a thought-provoking thriller that challenges viewers to consider the complexities of human behavior and the consequences of our actions.

overview: Guy Carter, an insecure expectant father unable to find work in his field, accepts a job driving hookers around Los Angeles. One long and crazy evening proves to our hero that he is, in fact, up to the task of fatherhood.
tagline: Every job has pros and cons
title: Amateur Night
plot:
Amateur Night is a 2016 American crime sex comedy written and directed by Lisa Addario and Joe Syracuse, who drew on their own early experiences in Hollywood for the story. Jason Biggs stars alongside Jenny Mollen, Janet Montgomery, Ashley Tisdale and Bria Murphy. The film premiered in Los Angeles on July 25, 2016, and was released in American cinemas by Cinedigm in early August.

Guy Carter is an unemployed architect with a pregnant wife, Anne, and a growing pile of bills. Anne finds a Craigslist advertisement for a driver and sends him, against his wishes, to apply. Expecting to deliver pizzas, Guy discovers that he has been hired to chauffeur Nikki, a sex worker, around Los Angeles for the night. Their first stop is a regular client, a kinky doctor in Bel Air. When Nikki fails to return for hours, Guy breaks into the house, finds her tied up in what he assumes is a torture session and "rescues" her by spraying the doctor with air freshener; the man falls and hits his head, and the pair flee.

Calmed down by Nikki, Guy learns that he will receive a share of the night's takings and warms to the job. They pick up two of her colleagues, Jaxi and Fallon, and Guy is made to clean a bag of well-used sex toys before driving the women to a bachelor party at a luxury Beverly Hills hotel. There the women put Guy in charge of keeping a crowd of rowdy former fraternity brothers in line, and the evening descends into a series of increasingly explicit and humiliating episodes for him. When Anne goes into false labour, Guy steps out, only to be taken hostage by the vengeful doctor, armed with a syringe of paralysing drug, until Nikki turns the needle on him.

The party resumes until the women discover they have been robbed and hold the guests at gunpoint to retrieve their money. One of the men turns out to be an undercover police officer who tries to arrest Nikki, and Guy leads the police on a chase before crashing his car, and the group escapes by bus. As dawn breaks, Nikki hires Guy to design a house for her. Expecting police at his door, Guy finds instead that his car was repossessed before the police could trace it. The end credits play over re-enactments of incidents the filmmakers say really happened.

Critics panned the film; Rotten Tomatoes recorded no positive reviews from six critics, and it grossed only about $63,000.

overview: London, 1843. Ebenezer Scrooge, a bitter old man, despises the Christmas holiday. Over the course of Christmas Eve night he is visited by three ghosts to show him his past, present and future.
title: A Christmas Carol
plot:
A Christmas Carol is a 2019 British dark fantasy drama based on Charles Dickens's 1843 novella. Written by Steven Knight, with Tom Hardy and Ridley Scott among its executive producers, it was made as a three-part series and aired in the United States on FX on 19 December 2019 as a single presentation, before being broadcast on BBC One between 22 and 24 December 2019.
