In "The Birthday Party", directed by Clark from a script she wrote with Benjamin, a mother named Mary finds her husband dead in his study on the morning of her daughter Lucy's birthday party and, rather than call for help, spends the day frantically hiding the body, eventually stuffing it into a rented panda costume, with predictably disastrous results in front of the young guests.

In Benjamin's "Don't Fall", four friends camping in the desert come across an ancient rock painting of an evil spirit; that night a creature possesses one of them, Gretchen, and hunts down the others. In Kusama's "Her Only Living Son", conceived as an unofficial sequel to Rosemary's Baby, a woman calling herself Cora has raised her son Andy in hiding, and as he nears his eighteenth birthday she watches him reveal his true nature as the child of Satan.

The project was announced in 2014 with a different line-up of directors, two of whom left before production. XX premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2017 and was released in select theaters and on demand by Magnet Releasing. Reviews were generally favorable: critics praised the range of female voices and the strongest segments, while some noted that the short running times left little room for character development and that the overall quality was uneven, a common problem in anthologies.

overview: Teenagers Zach and Josh have been best friends their whole lives, but when a gruesome accident leads to a cover-up, the secret drives a wedge between them and propels them down a rabbit hole of escalating paranoia and violence.
title: Super Dark Times
plot:
Super Dark Times is a poignant and introspective coming-of-age drama that delves into the complexities of adolescent angst, social isolation, and the struggles of growing up. The film masterfully captures the turmoil and uncertainty of its characters as they navigate the challenges of high school, friendships, and first loves.

At its core, Super Dark Times explores the theme of disconnection and loneliness in a world where technology seems to be increasingly isolating individuals from one another. The protagonist, Evan, is a sensitive and introverted teenager who struggles to form meaningful connections with his peers, while his best friend, Matt, appears to have it all together on the surface but is hiding his own vulnerabilities.

The film also touches on the theme of toxic masculinity, as both Evan and Matt grapple with traditional masculine expectations and the pressure to conform. Their relationships with women, particularly their respective crushes, serve as a catalyst for self-discovery and growth, forcing them to confront their own emotions and desires.

Furthermore, Super Dark Times examines the fragility of male friendships and the ways in which they can both support and suffocate one another. The film's portrayal of Evan and Matt's relationship is particularly noteworthy, as it captures the intensity and complexity of male bonding in a way that feels both authentic and relatable.

Ultimately, Super Dark Times is a powerful exploration of the human experience, tackling themes that are both universally relatable and deeply personal. Through its thoughtful and nuanced storytelling, the film offers a poignant portrayal of adolescence's struggles and triumphs, inviting viewers to reflect on their own experiences and emotions.

overview: Under the oppressive Japanese colonial rule, Deok-hye, the last Princess of the declining Joseon Dynasty, is forced to move to Japan. She spends her days missing home, while struggling to maintain dignity as a princess. After a series of failed tries, Deok-hye makes her final attempt to return home with help of her childhood sweetheart, Jang-han.
tagline: Based on the true story of the last princess of the last empire.
title: The Last Princess
plot:
The Last Princess (Korean: Deokhye Ongju, literally "Princess Deokhye") is a 2016 South Korean period drama directed by Hur Jin-ho and based on the best-selling 2009 novel by Kwon Bi-young. Son Ye-jin stars as Princess Deokhye, the last princess of the Joseon dynasty, with Park Hae-il as Kim Jang-han, her childhood friend. The film depicts Deokhye's life in Japan after she was forced to move there as a teenager under Japanese colonial rule, and her long struggle to return home. Son had previously worked with Hur on the 2005 film April Snow.

In 1925, Korea is under Japanese rule, and thirteen-year-old Deokhye, the daughter of Emperor Gojong, is sent to Japan, officially to study but in reality as part of the colonial authorities' efforts to assimilate the Korean royal family. Homesick and isolated, she tries repeatedly to return to Korea after finishing school, but her attempts are blocked by Han Taek-soo, a pro-Japanese Korean official who serves the colonial government.

Deokhye is reunited with Kim Jang-han, her childhood friend, who is now an officer in the Japanese army but secretly working with the Korean independence movement. He plans a covert operation to smuggle Deokhye and her brother, Crown Prince Yi Un, to Shanghai, where the Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea is based. The plan fails when Han discovers it, and Deokhye and Kim lose contact. In 1931, Deokhye is forced to marry the Japanese aristocrat Count Sō Takeyuki, and after the birth of their daughter she suffers a severe mental illness. Decades later, Kim, now a newspaper journalist, discovers her confined in a Japanese psychiatric hospital and campaigns to persuade the South Korean government to allow her to come back. In 1962, Deokhye finally returns to her homeland.

The film portrays Deokhye as a symbol of the suffering of the Korean people under colonial rule. Its story mixes historical events with fiction: Kim Jang-han is an invented character, and the film takes dramatic liberties with the historical record.

The Last Princess was a commercial success, drawing about 5.6 million admissions in South Korea, and Son Ye-jin won Best Actress at both the Grand Bell Awards and the Baeksang Arts Awards.

overview: Weekend trips, office parties, late night conversations, drinking on the job, marriage pressure, biological clocks, holding eye contact a second too long… you know what makes the line between “friends” and “more than friends” really blurry? Beer.
tagline: A comedy about knowing when to say when.
title: Drinking Buddies
plot:
Drinking Buddies is a 2013 American comedy-drama written, directed and edited by Joe Swanberg, starring Olivia Wilde, Jake Johnson, Anna Kendrick and Ron Livingston, with filmmaker Ti West in a supporting role. Set at a real Chicago brewery and built largely on improvised dialogue, it premiered at the South by Southwest film festival in 2013 and also screened at the Maryland Film Festival.

Kate and Luke are co-workers at Chicago's Revolution Brewing, where she handles marketing and public relations and he works in production. They share the same goofy sense of humour and spend their evenings drinking with the rest of the brewery crew, and they seem made for each other, except that both are already in relationships. Kate is dating Chris, a reserved introvert, while Luke lives with Jill, a kind and practical woman who is gently pressing him to talk about marriage.

Chris invites Luke and Jill to join him and Kate for a weekend at his lakeside cottage. During a hike, Chris and Jill share a kiss, while back at the house Luke and Kate stay up drinking, build a bonfire and go skinny-dipping. Soon after the trip Chris, recognising how different he and Kate are, breaks up with her. Kate celebrates her new freedom on a night out with the brewery crew and ends up sleeping with a colleague, Dave, which leaves Luke irrationally angry with them both.

When Jill goes away for a week with old college friends, Luke and Kate grow closer. They share dinner, fall asleep together on the couch, and he spends the weekend helping her move apartments. The move goes badly: Luke badly cuts his hand, Kate proves squeamish and unhelpful, a confrontation with an impatient driver leaves him bruised, and when Kate drops their dinner plans to go drinking with Dave, the two argue bitterly. Luke returns home to find Jill back early and in tears. Tending his wounds, she confesses to kissing Chris, insists that she loves him and still wants to marry him, and Luke forgives her and says he feels the same.

At work the next day, Kate and Luke are awkward with each other until they sit down together at lunch, trading bits of food in a silent gesture that their friendship will survive. The film received positive reviews, holding an 84% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: A car magnate watches his personal and professional life hit the skids because of his business and romantic indiscretions.
tagline: Ben loves his family almost as much as he loves himself
title: Solitary Man
plot:
Solitary Man is a 2009 American drama film directed by Allen Coulter and starring Michael Douglas. The movie follows the story of Ben Kalmen, a used car salesman who has spent his life chasing after women and making poor decisions.

At its core, Solitary Man explores themes of loneliness and isolation. Despite being surrounded by people, Ben's life is marked by emptiness and disconnection. He struggles to form meaningful relationships, often using his charm and good looks to manipulate those around him. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Ben's shallow existence has left him feeling unfulfilled and alone.

The film also delves into the consequences of a life of selfishness and poor decision-making. Ben's actions have hurt those he cares about, including his daughter, and he is forced to confront the damage he has caused. This serves as a catalyst for Ben's journey towards self-discovery and redemption.

Furthermore, Solitary Man touches on the theme of regret and the importance of taking responsibility for one's actions. As Ben navigates his way through life, he is confronted with the choices he has made and the opportunities he has missed. The film suggests that it's never too late to make amends and start anew, but this requires a willingness to confront one's past mistakes and take ownership of them.

Overall, Solitary Man is a poignant exploration of the human condition, highlighting the complexities and challenges of living a life of purpose and connection.

overview: Two movie producers who owe money to the mob set up their aging movie star for an insurance scam to try and save themselves. But they wind up getting more than they ever imagined.
tagline: Hollywood has never pulled a stunt like this!
title: The Comeback Trail
plot:
The Comeback Trail is a 2020 American crime comedy film directed by Jay Roach. The movie follows two washed-up screenwriters, Howard Ratner and Jeremy Klein, who team up with a shady Hollywood producer, Seth Kaplan, to write a script for a biopic about a fictional boxer.

At its core, The Comeback Trail explores the themes of desperation, opportunism, and the commodification of art. The film delves into the darker side of Hollywood's power dynamics, where struggling artists are often forced to compromise their creative vision in pursuit of fame and fortune.

The movie also touches on the theme of toxic masculinity, as embodied by Seth Kaplan, a character who embodies the worst excesses of 1990s Hollywood. His character's ego, entitlement, and lack of empathy serve as a foil to the more vulnerable and insecure characters, highlighting the destructive nature of unchecked male privilege.

Furthermore, The Comeback Trail critiques the way in which art is often reduced to a commodity, with creators being exploited for their talent and creativity. The film's portrayal of the writers' struggles to maintain control over their work serves as a commentary on the broader cultural phenomenon of creative labor exploitation.

Overall, The Comeback Trail offers a scathing satire of Hollywood's excesses and the ways in which the industry can both enable and destroy artistic expression.

overview: Queen Victoria strikes up an unlikely friendship with a young Indian clerk named Abdul Karim.
tagline: History's most unlikely friendship.
title: Victoria & Abdul
plot:
Victoria & Abdul is a 2017 historical drama film that tells the story of an unlikely friendship between Queen Victoria and an Indian clerk named Abdul Karim. The movie explores several themes, including cultural exchange, prejudice, and the power of human connection.

At its core, the film is a heartwarming tale of how two individuals from different walks of life came together, bridging the gap between their cultures and backgrounds. The story highlights the challenges faced by Abdul Karim as he navigates the complexities of British society, where he is met with suspicion and prejudice due to his Indian heritage.

The movie also delves into the theme of loneliness and isolation, particularly in Queen Victoria's character. Her life has been marked by duty and responsibility, leaving her feeling disconnected from the world around her. Abdul Karim's presence in her life serves as a catalyst for change, introducing her to new experiences and perspectives that help her find joy and companionship.

Furthermore, the film touches on the theme of colonialism and its impact on indigenous cultures. The story is set against the backdrop of the British Empire's expansion into India during the late 19th century, highlighting the complexities and contradictions of this period in history.

Ultimately, Victoria & Abdul is a film about the transformative power of human connection and the importance of embracing diversity and understanding. Through its portrayal of an unlikely friendship between Queen Victoria and Abdul Karim, the movie shows that even in the face of adversity, people from different backgrounds can come together and find common ground.

overview: The fate of the galaxy rests in the hands of bitter rivals. One, James Kirk, is a delinquent, thrill-seeking Iowa farm boy. The other, Spock, a Vulcan, was raised in a logic-based society that rejects all emotion. As fiery instinct clashes with calm reason, their unlikely but powerful partnership is the only thing capable of leading their crew through unimaginable danger, boldly going where no one has gone before. The human adventure has begun again.
tagline: The future begins.
title: Star Trek
plot:
Star Trek (2009) is a science fiction film directed by J.J. Abrams and written by Roberto Orci and Alex Kurtzman. The movie takes place in an alternate timeline, often referred to as the "Kelvin Timeline," which diverges from the original Star Trek timeline established by Gene Roddenberry.

The film begins with a prologue that shows the events leading up to the destruction of the USS Kelvin, a Federation starship, by the Romulan ship Narada. The crew of the Kelvin is led by Captain James T. Kirk (Chris Pine), who attempts to stop the Narada but ultimately fails. As the Kelvin is destroyed, the Narada escapes with the ship's captain, Jonathan Archer (Bruce Greenwood), and his daughter, Carol (Winona Ryder).

The movie then jumps forward in time to 23rd century Earth, where a young James T. Kirk is a cadet on the USS Enterprise NCC-1701 under the command of Captain Christopher Pike (Anson Mount). However, during a mission to rescue a group of stranded scientists from a Romulan ship, the Enterprise is attacked by the Narada, which has been modified with advanced technology.

The Enterprise is severely damaged, and Captain Pike is killed in action. The crew manages to escape, but not before the Narada escapes with the Enterprise's captain, who is revealed to be Jonathan Archer, the father of Carol. This event sets off a chain reaction that leads to the creation of the alternate timeline.

The movie then follows James T. Kirk as he becomes the new captain of the USS Enterprise NCC-1701, which has been rebuilt and upgraded with advanced technology. Alongside his crew, including Mr. Spock (Zachary Quinto), Dr. Leonard McCoy (Karl Urban), Montgomery Scott (Simon Pegg), Hikaru Sulu (John Cho), and Nyota Uhura (Zoe Saldana), Kirk embarks on a mission to stop the Romulan ship Narada, which has been reactivated by the villainous Nero (Eric Bana).

As the Enterprise crew delves deeper into the mystery of the Narada's return, they discover that it is being controlled by Nero, who seeks revenge against the Federation for not allowing him to join their ranks. The crew also learns that Nero was once a human who was stranded on Romulus and forced to undergo genetic engineering to survive.

The movie culminates in an epic battle between the Enterprise and the Narada, with Kirk and his crew fighting to stop Nero's plan to destroy the Earth. In the end, Kirk manages to defeat Nero, but not before he is mortally wounded by a blast of energy from the Narada's tractor beam.

As the movie concludes, James T. Kirk dies in his quarters, surrounded by his crew. However, it is revealed that he has been revived and is now living on a remote planet with Carol, who has become a key figure in his life. The film ends with a shot of the Enterprise flying off into space, ready for its next adventure.

Overall, Star Trek (2009) is a thrilling and action-packed film that explores the early days of James T. Kirk and the crew of the USS Enterprise. With its stunning visual effects, engaging characters, and epic battles, it sets the stage for the rest of the rebooted Star Trek franchise.

overview: After a remote diamond mine collapses in far northern Canada, an ice road driver must lead an impossible rescue mission over a frozen ocean to save the trapped miners.
tagline: This mission is on thin ice.
title: The Ice Road
plot:
The Ice Road is a 2021 American action thriller written and directed by Jonathan Hensleigh. Liam Neeson stars alongside Laurence Fishburne, Benjamin Walker, Amber Midthunder, Marcus Thomas, Holt McCallany, Martin Sensmeier, Matt McCoy and Matt Salinger. Influenced by Henri-Georges Clouzot's 1953 film The Wages of Fear, it follows a team of truck drivers hauling vital equipment across frozen lakes to save workers trapped in a collapsed mine.

When an explosion at a diamond mine in northern Manitoba traps 26 miners, the clock starts ticking on any rescue. In North Dakota, trucker Mike McCann and his younger brother Gurty, an Iraq War veteran living with PTSD and aphasia, lose their jobs after Mike punches a co-worker for mocking Gurty. They travel to Winnipeg and join a rescue convoy led by veteran driver Jim Goldenrod, who has been hired to deliver heavy wellheads needed to reach the miners. The team also includes Tantoo, a young Indigenous driver whose brother is among the trapped men, and Varnay, an insurance actuary representing the mining company, Katka.

The journey across the thawing ice road proves deadly. Goldenrod's truck breaks down and he is lost when the ice gives way, and the survivors soon discover that the accident was no misfortune: Varnay has been sabotaging the convoy on behalf of Katka's general manager, who wants to avoid the company being held responsible for the disaster. After Varnay leaves Mike and Gurty for dead and abducts Tantoo, the brothers fight their way back through avalanches, cracking ice and armed contractors. Mike eventually kills Varnay, but Gurty dies saving the last truck on a collapsing bridge. Mike and Tantoo reach the mine in time to free the miners, and the corrupt manager is fired and arrested.

The film was shot in and around Winnipeg, including Gimli and Île-des-Chênes, in February 2020. Netflix acquired the US rights for $18 million and released it on June 25, 2021, when it became the most-streamed film on the service in its debut weekend; Amazon Prime Video released it in the United Kingdom. Reviews were mixed, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting a 44% approval rating from 89 critics and a consensus describing it as a predictable downhill trundle despite Neeson's continued appeal as an action hero. A sequel, Ice Road: Vengeance, was released in June 2025.

overview: Still reeling from a heartbreaking family event and his parents' subsequent divorce, Tyler Hawkins discovers a fresh lease on life when he meets Ally Craig, a gregarious beauty who witnessed her mother's death. But as the couple draws closer, the fallout from their separate tragedies jeopardizes their love.
tagline: Live in the moments.
title: Remember Me
plot:
"Remember Me" is a 2010 American romantic drama film directed by Scott Hicks and written by Jason Keller. The movie stars Robert Pattinson, Emilie de Ravin, and Julianne Moore.

The main themes of "Remember Me" include:

1. **Love and Sacrifice**: The film explores the idea that true love requires sacrifice and putting the needs of others before one's own desires. The protagonist, Tyler Hawkins (Robert Pattinson), falls in love with his sister's fiancée, Ally (Emilie de Ravin), but ultimately decides to give up on their relationship for her happiness.
2. **Grief and Loss**: The movie delves into the theme of coping with loss and grief, particularly in the context of a tragic event that occurs early in the film. Tyler's experiences with loss shape his perspective on life and love.
3. **Identity and Self-Discovery**: As Tyler navigates his relationships and personal growth, he begins to question his own identity and sense of purpose. The film encourages viewers to explore their own values and aspirations.
4. **Family Dynamics**: The movie highlights the complexities of family relationships, particularly in the context of sibling love and loyalty. Tyler's bond with his sister, Ally, is a central aspect of the story.

The film's narrative is character-driven, focusing on the emotional journeys of its protagonists as they navigate love, loss, and self-discovery. Through its exploration of these themes, "Remember Me" offers a poignant and thought-provoking portrayal of human relationships and the complexities of the heart.

overview: Being kidnapped shatters a brother and sister's harmony, forcing them to confront their desires.
title: Daniel & Ana
plot:
Daniel & Ana is a 2009 Mexican thriller drama directed by Michel Franco in his feature debut, starring Darío Yazbek Bernal and Marimar Vega as a brother and sister whose lives are torn apart by a violent crime. It premiered on May 18, 2009, at the Cannes Film Festival. The story was inspired by a real case, and the film deals with the abduction of two siblings who are forced to perform sexual acts together on camera, and with the trauma that follows.

Daniel and Ana are siblings from a wealthy family in Mexico City. Daniel, the younger of the two, is dating a girl named Mariana, while Ana is engaged to Rafa, who is considering a job offer in Spain. One day while they are out running errands, the pair are kidnapped at gunpoint. Under threat of death they are filmed being forced into intercourse, and their captors confirm to an unseen client that they have the footage before releasing them. Although they are physically unharmed when they return home, the experience shatters both of their lives. Unable to speak about what happened to each other or anyone else, they search in vain for the video online.

Over time Ana proves more resilient. She sees a psychiatrist and repairs her relationship with Rafa, and she urges Daniel to join her in therapy, but he refuses. Daniel's emotional state deteriorates as he struggles with confused feelings about his sister and with guilt and anger he cannot express. His behavior grows increasingly disturbing and violent, culminating in an assault on Ana and an attempt to force himself on Mariana. Ana decides to leave and move to Spain with Rafa, and Daniel's attempts to make her stay come to nothing. On Ana's wedding day, he arrives with a dagger intending to harm Rafa but cannot bring himself to do it. The newlyweds say goodbye, and the siblings part after an awkward embrace.

The film closes with title cards warning of a rise in pornography made with coerced amateurs and stating that the real siblings never learned what became of the video. Vega later said she was initially nervous about the film's nudity but was reassured after the director explained how he would approach the scenes.

Critical reception was mixed. The film has a 50% rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 43. The New York Times suggested that its stylistic restraint deflected accusations of exploitation but that its muted emotions impeded the audience's connection with the victims, while The Village Voice felt it was effective until its final act.

overview: Eugenie has a unique gift: she hears and sees the dead. When her family discovers her secret, at the end of the 19th century, she is taken by her father and brother to the neurological clinic at La Pitié Salpêtrière with no possibility of escaping her fate. Her destiny becomes entwined with that of Geneviève, a nurse at the hospital.
title: The Mad Women's Ball
plot:
The Mad Women's Ball is a 2021 French drama film directed by Olivia Guillaumaud. The movie is set in the late 19th century and revolves around the lives of three women who are sent to an asylum for being deemed "mad" by society.

At its core, The Mad Women's Ball explores themes of female empowerment, rebellion, and the struggle for independence in a patriarchal society. The film delves into the lives of these women, showcasing their unique personalities, skills, and experiences, as they navigate the confines of the asylum and find ways to resist the oppressive forces that seek to control them.

Through the characters' stories, the movie highlights the societal norms and expectations placed on women during this time period, emphasizing the limitations and constraints imposed upon them. The film also touches on the theme of mental illness, blurring the lines between reality and madness, and challenging the notion of what it means to be "sane" or "insane".

The Mad Women's Ball is a powerful exploration of female solidarity, resilience, and the human spirit, as these women find ways to support each other and resist the oppressive forces that seek to silence them. The film ultimately becomes a celebration of their strength, courage, and determination to live life on their own terms.

overview: In the midst of World War II, the battle under the sea rages and the Nazis have the upper hand as the Allies are unable to crack their war codes. However, after a wrecked U-boat sends out an SOS signal, the Allies realise this is their chance to seize the 'enigma coding machine'.
tagline: Heroes are ordinary men who do extraordinary things in extraordinary times.
title: U-571
plot:
U-571 is a 2000 American war film directed by Jonathan Mostow and starring Matthew McConaughey, Bill Paxton, Harvey Keitel, and Jon Voight. The movie is set during World War II and follows the story of Captain Chuck Yeager (played by Matthew McConaughey), a U.S. Navy test pilot who is recruited to lead a team of sailors on a mission to capture a German U-boat.

The main themes of U-571 include:

1. **Bravery and Sacrifice**: The movie highlights the bravery and sacrifice of Captain Yeager and his crew as they risk their lives to complete their mission. The film shows how Yeager's determination and leadership skills are put to the test in the face of danger.
2. **War and Its Consequences**: U-571 depicts the harsh realities of war, including the destruction caused by enemy submarines and the moral dilemmas faced by soldiers on both sides. The movie also explores the consequences of war on individuals and communities.
3. **Leadership and Teamwork**: The film emphasizes the importance of leadership and teamwork in achieving a common goal. Captain Yeager's ability to inspire and motivate his crew is crucial to their success, and the movie shows how they work together to overcome obstacles and achieve victory.
4. **Personal Growth and Redemption**: Throughout the movie, Captain Yeager undergoes significant personal growth and redemption. He begins as a somewhat arrogant and self-centered individual but learns valuable lessons about humility, sacrifice, and loyalty.

The plot of U-571 unfolds as follows:

The movie opens with Captain Chuck Yeager (Matthew McConaughey) being court-martialed for disobeying orders during a previous mission. However, he is soon recruited by the Navy to lead a team on a secret mission to capture a German U-boat.

Yeager and his crew embark on a perilous journey across the Atlantic, facing numerous challenges and dangers along the way. As they close in on their target, they must use all their skills and resources to outwit the enemy and complete their mission.

In the end, Captain Yeager and his crew successfully capture the U-boat, but not without sacrifices. The movie concludes with a sense of pride and accomplishment, as well as a deeper understanding of the importance of leadership, teamwork, and bravery in the face of adversity.

overview: Deck the halls with Donkey’s laughter in this all-new holiday collection. Donkey presents his very own carolling stage show featuring his Far Far Away pals in this merry, musical treat with all the trimmings! Join in the fun as they bring their own Shrektacular spirit to festive holiday songs, a fun Donkey Decoration scramble, and a hilarious virtual Yule Log that’s so funny… it’s on fire.
title: Donkey's Christmas Shrektacular
plot:
Donkey's Christmas Shrektacular, whose short is also titled Donkey's Caroling Christmas-tacular, is a 2010 American computer-animated musical holiday short from DreamWorks Animation, set in the world of the Shrek films. Directed by Walt Dohrn, with Raman Hui also credited as co-director in some sources, and written by Dohrn and Ryan Crego, it was produced by Gina Shay, Teresa Cheng and Chad Hammes with music by Matt Mahaffey. It was released on 7 December 2010 as a bonus holiday DVD packaged with the home release of Shrek Forever After, and as a special feature on that film's Blu-ray.

The short takes place in the Candy Apple, the friendly new incarnation of the Poison Apple tavern, where Donkey hosts a Christmas party and persuades everyone to join him in a caroling stage show. He opens with "It's the Most Wonderful Time of the Year" alongside his fairy-tale friends. Shrek, who surprises everyone by agreeing to sing, joins Fiona, their three ogre children and the ogre army in a gleefully gross ogre version of "Jingle Bells", with lyrics about bug cocoons and cricket slurps. Puss in Boots follows with "Fleas Navidad", a take on "Feliz Navidad" that he claims is a classic from his village, and the whole company closes with "Fairy Tale Rock", a rendition of "Jingle Bell Rock". Running gags in the background include Gingy trying to rescue lifeless gingerbread cookies, the Three Little Pigs preparing for swimsuit weather and Rumpelstiltskin trapped in a cage.

Eddie Murphy returns as Donkey, after being replaced by Dean Edwards in Scared Shrekless, alongside Mike Myers as Shrek, Cameron Diaz as Fiona and Antonio Banderas as Puss. Walt Dohrn voices Rumpelstiltskin, Jon Hamm the ogre Brogan, Cody Cameron Pinocchio and the pigs, Conrad Vernon Gingy and Aron Warner the Big Bad Wolf, with Craig Robinson and Jane Lynch also among the ogres. It was the last Shrek production to reunite the core original cast until Shrek 5.

The holiday disc rounds out the main short with a Donkey decoration game and Shrek's Yule Log, a half-hour virtual fireplace in Shrek's house in which characters such as Rumpelstiltskin, Puss, Fiona and Gingy wander through with festive gags.

overview: Fed up with being single on holidays, two strangers agree to be each other's platonic plus-ones all year long, only to catch real feelings along the way.
tagline: Who's your perfect plus-one?
title: Holidate
plot:
Holidate is a romantic comedy film released on Netflix in 2020, directed by John Whitesell and written by Mark L. Smith.

The movie follows the story of two people who are tired of being single during the holidays. Jessica (played by Emma Roberts) and Simon (played by Luke Bracey) meet at a mutual friend's wedding and agree to be each other's platonic dates for every holiday, starting with Christmas. They make a pact that they will not cheat on their significant others or fall in love.

As the story progresses, we see Jessica and Simon going through the motions of being each other's holiday dates, but things start to get complicated when they begin to develop real feelings for each other. Despite their initial agreement, they find themselves growing closer with each passing year.

Throughout the film, we also see glimpses of Jessica's troubled past and her struggles with commitment. Her boyfriend, Jake (played by Craig Roberts), is a bit controlling and possessive, which makes it difficult for Jessica to open up to Simon.

As Christmas approaches, Jessica and Simon are forced to confront their feelings for each other. They embark on a series of misadventures, including a disastrous trip to the mountains and a chaotic New Year's Eve party. Along the way, they must navigate their complicated relationships with their significant others and figure out what they truly want from life.

In the end, Jessica and Simon realize that their feelings for each other are genuine, but they also understand that they can't be together without hurting those around them. The movie ends on a bittersweet note, leaving the audience wondering if Jessica and Simon will find happiness with someone else or if they'll take a chance on love.

Overall, Holidate is a charming and witty romantic comedy that explores the complexities of relationships and the challenges of finding love during the holiday season. With its talented cast and engaging storyline, it's no wonder this movie became a fan favorite among Netflix viewers.

overview: A group of misfits encounter a young Yeti named Everest, and they set off to reunite the magical creature with his family on the mountain of his namesake.
tagline: Find your way home.
title: Abominable
plot:
Abominable is a 2019 American computer-animated adventure comedy film produced by DreamWorks Animation and distributed by Universal Pictures.

The movie begins with a young girl named Yi, who lives in the Himalayas with her grandmother. Yi's mother had passed away when she was a baby, and her father has been absent since then. Yi is fascinated by the Yeti, also known as the Abominable Snowman, which is said to inhabit the mountains.

One day, while exploring the forest, Yi discovers a young Yeti boy who has been separated from his family. She decides to take care of him and names him Everest. As they spend more time together, Yi learns that Everest's family was killed by poachers, and he is now on the run.

Yi and Everest embark on an adventure to return him to his home in the Himalayas. Along the way, they meet a group of orphaned pandas who are also being pursued by the same poachers. The group decides to work together to reach their destinations safely.

As they journey through the mountains, Yi and Everest face various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, harsh weather conditions, and the poachers. They also learn valuable lessons about friendship, loyalty, and the importance of family.

Meanwhile, a wealthy businessman named Luan is determined to capture the Yeti for his own gain. He believes that the Yeti's DNA can be used to create a new species of super-soldier. Yi and Everest must outsmart Luan and his team to protect themselves and their friends.

As they near their destination, Yi and Everest face one final challenge: reaching the Yeti's home before it falls into the wrong hands. In a thrilling finale, they successfully return Everest to his family, and in the process, Yi finds a new sense of belonging and purpose.

Throughout the movie, the animation is stunning, with beautifully rendered landscapes and lovable characters. The voice cast, including Chloe Moretz as Yi, Zhang Ziyi as Luan, and Albert Tsai as Everest's father, deliver memorable performances that bring the story to life.

Overall, Abominable is a heartwarming and action-packed adventure that celebrates the power of friendship and family. With its stunning animation and engaging storyline, it's a must-see for families and fans of animated movies alike.

overview: An acclaimed writer, his ex-wife, and their teenaged children come to terms with the complexities of love in all its forms over the course of one tumultuous year.
tagline: A story about first loves and second chances.
title: Stuck in Love
plot:
Stuck in Love is a 2013 American romantic comedy-drama film written and directed by Mark Webber. The movie follows the story of Sam (played by Josh Duhamel), a successful author who has just published his second novel, but struggles with commitment and intimacy in his personal life.

The story begins with Sam's marriage to Faye (played by Rachel McAdams) on the eve of her 30th birthday. However, their relationship is put to the test when Faye announces that she is pregnant. The couple decides to get married, but their happiness is short-lived as they soon realize that they are not compatible.

The film then shifts its focus to Sam's teenage daughter, Ruth (played by Felicity Price), who is struggling to find her place in the world. Ruth is a creative and sensitive young girl who feels like an outsider among her peers. She begins to develop feelings for her English teacher, Will (played by Matt Lanter).

As the story unfolds, we see flashbacks of Sam's own relationship with his mother, Mary (played by Patricia Clarkson), which had a profound impact on his life. We also see glimpses of Sam's complicated relationship with Faye, who is struggling to balance her desire for independence with her need for love and connection.

Throughout the film, the narrative jumps back and forth in time, weaving together multiple storylines and character arcs. As Ruth navigates her own relationships and identity, she begins to understand the complexities of her family's dynamics and the ways in which they have shaped her into the person she is today.

One of the standout aspects of Stuck in Love is its nuanced portrayal of complex emotions and relationships. The film tackles themes of love, loss, and identity with sensitivity and humor, never shying away from the difficulties and imperfections that make life so rich and messy.

Ultimately, the movie builds towards a heartwarming and satisfying conclusion, as Ruth finds her own path in life and Sam comes to terms with his past and present. The film's title, Stuck in Love, is a clever play on words, referencing both the romantic entanglements of its characters and the ways in which love can become stuck in our lives.

Overall, Stuck in Love is a thoughtful and engaging film that explores the complexities of human relationships with humor, sensitivity, and heart.

overview: A big-game hunter for zoos books passage on a Greek shipping freighter with a fresh haul of exotic and deadly animals from the Amazon, including a rare white Jaguar – along with a political assassin being extradited to the U.S in secret. Two days into the journey, the assassin escapes and releases the captive animals, throwing the ship into chaos.
tagline: The ultimate hunter vs the ultimate predator
title: Primal
plot:
Primal is a 2019 American action thriller directed by Nick Powell from a screenplay by Richard Leder. Nicolas Cage stars as Frank Walsh, a big-game hunter, with Famke Janssen as Navy doctor Ellen Taylor, Kevin Durand as the assassin Richard Loffler, and LaMonica Garrett, Michael Imperioli and Jeremy Nazario in supporting roles. Shot in Puerto Rico, it reunited Cage with Powell after their earlier collaboration on Outcast, and it was released in the United States in cinemas and on premium video on demand on 8 November 2019.

Frank Walsh makes his living capturing rare and dangerous animals for zoos and collectors. Deep in the Brazilian rainforest, he has just trapped an extraordinarily rare white jaguar by tranquilising it from a platform high in the trees, even though his local assistant refuses to help move the creature out of superstition. Expecting to sell it for a fortune, Walsh books passage on a cargo ship bound for the United States, loading the jaguar alongside a collection of other animals, among them venomous snakes.

The ship has another unusual passenger. United States marshals are using it to transport Richard Loffler, a notorious political assassin and former special forces operative who is being extradited to stand trial. Because he suffers from seizures triggered by changes in air pressure, Loffler cannot be flown, and he is kept chained to a chair inside a cage, under the medical supervision of Dr. Ellen Taylor. Walsh and Taylor clash immediately, as she considers him arrogant and dishonest. During the voyage, Loffler escapes and deliberately frees the dangerous animals, including the jaguar, to sow chaos among his captors. Some of the crew flee in a lifeboat, leaving Walsh, Taylor and a handful of others aboard with a killer and a ship full of predators. Loffler takes Taylor and a young crewman named Rafael hostage, and Walsh must use his tracking and trapping skills to hunt both the man and the animals, culminating in a confrontation in which the jaguar plays a decisive role.

The film is a deliberately old-fashioned B-movie that combines a confined-setting action thriller with creature-feature elements, and Cage plays the gruff hunter with a knowing, larger-than-life energy.

Primal received mostly negative reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds an approval rating of about 37 percent; the consensus describes it as chiefly of interest to Nicolas Cage completists and hardcore B-movie fans, suffering from a lack of primal energy.

overview: A mysterious force knocks the moon from its orbit around Earth and sends it hurtling on a collision course with life as we know it.
tagline: Humanity will face the dark side of the Moon.
title: Moonfall
plot:
"Moonfall" is a 2022 science fiction disaster film directed by Roland Emmerich, produced by Centropolis Entertainment, and written by Drew Pearce.

The movie follows two main storylines that eventually intersect. The first storyline revolves around Sam Bell (played by Patrick Wilson), an astronaut who wakes up on the Moon with no memory of how he got there or what happened to his crew. As he tries to piece together his past, he discovers a mysterious message from an unknown sender that sets him on a mission to prevent a catastrophic event.

The second storyline takes place in 2055, where we meet J.T. O'Grady (played by Halle Berry), the daughter of Sam Bell, who is now a renowned astrophysicist. She's recruited by a team of scientists and engineers, including her colleague Brian Harper (played by John Bradley), to prevent a massive asteroid from colliding with Earth.

As the story unfolds, we learn that the asteroid is not just any ordinary rock - it's actually a piece of the Moon that has broken off due to an unknown cataclysmic event. The team discovers that the Moon was once part of a larger celestial body called Kaltain, which was destroyed in a catastrophic collision with Earth millions of years ago.

The movie takes a thrilling turn as Sam Bell and J.T. O'Grady embark on a perilous journey to prevent the asteroid from colliding with Earth. Along the way, they encounter numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, malfunctioning equipment, and personal demons.

Throughout the film, Emmerich's signature style of explosive action sequences and heart-pumping suspense is on full display. The movie's climax features an intense showdown between Sam and J.T., as they work together to prevent the asteroid from destroying Earth.

While "Moonfall" received mixed reviews from critics, it has its fans who appreciate the film's over-the-top action sequences and thrilling plot twists. However, some viewers may find the pacing a bit uneven and the scientific explanations lacking in depth.

Overall, "Moonfall" is an entertaining sci-fi disaster film that will keep you on the edge of your seat. With its breakneck pace and mind-bending plot twists, it's sure to appeal to fans of Roland Emmerich's signature style.

overview: Geeky 14-year old Ethan is left to babysit his younger sister, Jane, with his best friend Benny but after Ethan inadvertently puts Jane in harm's way, his parents hire a professional babysitter, the beautiful yet mysterious 17-year-old Sarah who, unbeknownst to them, is actually a fledgling vampire.
tagline: No parents. No rules. No pulse.
title: My Babysitter's a Vampire
plot:
My Babysitter's a Vampire is a 2010 Canadian television film that explores the complexities of adolescence and the struggles of growing up. The movie delves into the theme of identity, as the protagonist, Jen, navigates her relationships with her family, friends, and romantic interests.

At its core, My Babysitter's a Vampire is a story about self-discovery and acceptance. Jen must confront her own desires and insecurities as she tries to balance her normal life with her secret vampire existence. The film expertly captures the angst and uncertainty of being a teenager, making it relatable to audiences of all ages.

The movie also touches on the theme of loyalty and friendship, highlighting the importance of having supportive relationships in one's life. Jen's friendships with her friends, particularly her best friend, Ryan, serve as a source of comfort and strength during difficult times.

Furthermore, My Babysitter's a Vampire explores the idea of secrecy and deception, as Jen struggles to keep her vampire nature hidden from those around her. This theme is woven throughout the story, adding an element of tension and suspense to the narrative.

Overall, My Babysitter's a Vampire is a heartwarming and humorous coming-of-age tale that celebrates the ups and downs of adolescence and the power of friendship and self-acceptance.

overview: Set in the 22nd century, when a battered salvage ship sends out a distress signal, the seasoned crew of the rescue hospital ship Nova-17 responds. What they find is a black hole--that threatens to destroy both ships--and a mysterious survivor whose body quickly mutates into a monstrous and deadly form.
tagline: In the farthest reaches of space, something has gone terribly wrong.
title: Supernova
plot:
Supernova is a 2000 American science fiction thriller directed by Walter Hill, who was credited under the pseudonym "Thomas Lee", from a screenplay by David C. Wilson based on a story by William Malone and Daniel Chuba. James Spader, Angela Bassett, Robert Forster, Lou Diamond Phillips, Peter Facinelli, Robin Tunney and Wilson Cruz star. Malone had first developed the project in the late 1980s as Dead Star, pitched as a cross between Hellraiser and Dead Calm in space, before Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer acquired and retitled it. The production was notoriously troubled: after Hill left, other directors were brought in for uncredited reshoots and Francis Ford Coppola was involved in re-editing the film.

In the early twenty-second century, the medical rescue ship Nightingale 229 patrols deep space with a six-member crew: captain and pilot A. J. Marley, co-pilot Nick Vanzant, medical officer Kaela Evers, medical technician Yerzy Penalosa, paramedic Danika Lund and computer technician Benjamin Sotomejor. They receive a distress call from an ice-mining operation on a distant moon, Titan 37, more than 3,000 light-years away. The crew makes a dimension jump to respond, but a malfunction during the jump fatally injures Captain Marley, and the ship arrives in the path of a debris cloud that destroys most of its manoeuvring fuel.

Worse still, the moon orbits a blue giant star whose gravity is dragging the damaged ship toward destruction within seventeen hours, almost exactly the time needed to recharge the jump drive, leaving only a narrow window to escape. Under Vanzant's command, the survivors take aboard Karl Larson, a disturbing young man who claims to be the only survivor of the mining operation, and who has brought with him a mysterious alien artefact. The object has strange effects on whoever touches it, and as Larson's true intentions emerge, the crew find themselves fighting for their lives against a threat that could destroy not only them but Earth itself.

The film combines elements of space survival drama and horror with sexual tension among the crew, set aboard a sleek, technology-filled vessel.

Supernova was a critical and commercial failure. It opened with about 6.7 million dollars over the Martin Luther King Jr. holiday weekend in January 2000, and on Rotten Tomatoes only about 12 percent of critics' reviews are positive.

overview: Justin Quayle is a low-level British diplomat who has always gone about his work very quietly, not causing any problems. But after his radical wife Tessa is killed he becomes determined to find out why, thrusting himself into the middle of a very dangerous conspiracy.
tagline: Love. At any cost.
title: The Constant Gardener
plot:
The Constant Gardener is a thought-provoking film that delves into the complexities of human nature, morality, and the consequences of one's actions. Set against the backdrop of global politics and corporate greed, the movie explores the themes of identity, loyalty, and the blurred lines between right and wrong.

At its core, The Constant Gardener is a story about a man who embarks on a journey to uncover the truth about his wife's mysterious death, only to find himself entangled in a web of corruption and deceit. As he navigates this treacherous landscape, he must confront his own sense of identity and purpose, all while grappling with the moral implications of his actions.

The film is also a scathing critique of the pharmaceutical industry and its role in perpetuating violence and exploitation around the world. The Constant Gardener shines a light on the darker aspects of human nature, revealing the ways in which individuals can be complicit in their own oppression and the oppression of others.

Through its complex characters and intricate plot, The Constant Gardener raises important questions about the nature of truth, power, and responsibility. It is a movie that challenges viewers to think critically about the world around them and to consider the consequences of their own actions. Ultimately, it is a powerful exploration of the human condition, one that lingers long after the credits roll.

overview: Secluded in a desolate forest, a broken family is observed by Sator, a supernatural entity who is attempting to claim them.
tagline: After you have suffered, he will find you.
title: Sator
plot:
Sator is a 2019 American found-footage horror film directed by Justin Baldoni and written by Michael Leeson. The movie follows two brothers, Brian and Mike, who are on a road trip to visit their father in the hospital when they stumble upon an ancient ritual that unleashes a malevolent force.

The main themes of Sator include:

1. **The Power of Language**: The film explores the idea that words have power and can be used to manipulate and control others. The title "Sator" is derived from the Latin phrase "Carpe Diem," which means "Seize the Day." However, in this context, it's revealed that the phrase has a dark and sinister meaning.
2. **The Dangers of Obsession**: Brian becomes increasingly obsessed with uncovering the truth behind the ancient ritual, which leads him down a rabbit hole of conspiracy theories and paranoia. This obsession ultimately consumes him, highlighting the dangers of becoming too fixated on a single idea or goal.
3. **Family Dynamics**: The film also explores the complex relationships within families, particularly between brothers. Brian's fixation on uncovering the truth puts a strain on his relationship with Mike, who is more skeptical and cautious. This tension highlights the difficulties of navigating family dynamics, especially when it comes to matters of trust and loyalty.
4. **The Blurred Lines between Reality and Paranoia**: As the story unfolds, it becomes increasingly difficult for the viewer to distinguish between what's real and what's just Brian's paranoia. This blurring of reality creates a sense of unease and uncertainty, mirroring the characters' own experiences.

Overall, Sator is a thought-provoking horror film that explores themes of language, obsession, family dynamics, and the blurred lines between reality and paranoia.

overview: To land a major client, an LA wine exec travels to an Australian sheep station, where she signs on as a ranch hand and hits it off with a rugged local.
title: A Perfect Pairing
plot:
A Perfect Pairing is a 2022 American romantic comedy directed by Stuart McDonald and released by Netflix on May 19, 2022. Victoria Justice stars as Lola, a driven Los Angeles wine executive, and Adam Demos plays Max, a rugged Australian station hand, with Luca Sardelis, Craig Horner and Lucy Durack in supporting roles. The film combines a workplace comeback story with a fish-out-of-water romance set on a sheep station in rural Australia.

Lola feels undervalued at the wine distributor Mythos, where her boss Calder routinely dismisses her ideas. A chef friend introduces her to an excellent but little-known Australian wine from the Vaughn winery, which has never been exported. When her colleague Audra pitches the idea to Calder behind her back, Lola quits, founds her own company and flies to Australia to sign the winery before her old firm can. She books a stay at a farm that turns out to be connected to the business, but her pitch to its owner, Hazel, is quickly rejected.

Learning that the station is short of a hired hand, Lola volunteers to work under the station boss, Max, hoping to prove her determination. The manual labour is a shock: the other hands tease her, she uses up the hot water with long showers and blows the circuit breaker on her first day, and she struggles to mend fences, sort tagged sheep and load a manure spreader. After five days she gives up, but when Max's truck breaks down on the way to her flight, he urges her to stay. Inspired by a book about the farm's founding matriarch, Lola fixes the water heater, wins over her co-workers, shows off her singing voice at their evening gathering and learns to help with the shearing.

As Lola and Max grow close, she discovers that he is Hazel's brother. On a trip to the vineyard they camp overnight and finally act on their feelings, but the next morning Max admits that he is a Vaughn and his sister's silent partner, and Lola feels betrayed. Returning to the station, she finds Calder and Audra negotiating with Hazel and refuses Calder's offer to rehire her. Months later, Lola is running her small company in California with Audra at her side when Max appears at her wine expo stand, announcing that the winery has chosen her firm over Calder's and that he wants to be with her. They reconcile and fly back to Australia for a friend's wedding.

Critics were split, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 50% positive reviews; one reviewer likened it to a polished Hallmark romance.

original_title: The Ice Age Adventures of Buck Wild
overview: The fearless one-eyed weasel Buck teams up with mischievous possum brothers Crash & Eddie as they head off on a new adventure into Buck's home: The Dinosaur World.
tagline: Disney+ gets wild.
title: The Ice Age Adventures of Buck Wild
plot:
The Ice Age Adventures of Buck Wild is a 2022 animated adventure comedy directed by John C. Donkin in his feature directorial debut, from a screenplay by Jim Hecht, Ray DeLaurentis and William Schifrin based on a story by Hecht. A spin-off and the sixth instalment of the Ice Age franchise, it features the voices of Simon Pegg, the only returning member of the earlier cast, as the one-eyed weasel Buck, alongside Vincent Tong, Aaron Harris, Utkarsh Ambudkar and Justina Machado. Originally developed as a television series, it was released as a streaming film on Disney+.

While practising one of their extreme stunts, the opossum brothers Crash and Eddie trigger an avalanche that wrecks the herd's summer home. When Manny, Sid, Diego and their sister Ellie declare that the brothers could never survive on their own, the pair slip away during the night to prove them wrong. They stumble into the Lost World, a hidden realm of dinosaurs, where their old friend Buck rescues them from raptors. Buck tells them that Orson, a bipedal Protoceratops with a huge brain who was mocked in his youth, has escaped from exile and is bent on conquering the Lost World.

Buck explains that he once belonged to a team that founded a watering hole where all creatures could live in peace, and that Orson, who believed the strong should rule the weak, was defeated and banished to an island, where he learned to control raptors with fire. When raptors find Buck's hideout, they are knocked out by Zee, a zorilla and former member of Buck's team. Orson's raptor army then attacks the watering hole. Buck and Zee, still at odds over the team's break-up, set aside their differences and summon Momma, a friendly Tyrannosaurus, but Buck is captured while acting as a decoy.

Meanwhile, the herd follow the brothers into the Lost World and are carried by Momma to the watering hole, where Orson plans to feed Buck to his raptors as an example. Zee and the possums free Buck, and in the ensuing battle Crash and Eddie realise the secret of Orson's power. Using fire-breathing lizards to make flames of their own, they turn the raptors against their master, who is chased away. Proud of how much the brothers have grown, Ellie lets them stay in the Lost World with Buck and Zee, and they promise to visit often.

The film was poorly reviewed, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 19% approval and criticising its animation and dull story.

overview: The haunted Lambert family seeks to uncover the mysterious childhood secret that has left them dangerously connected to the spirit world.
tagline: It will take what you love most.
title: Insidious: Chapter 2
plot:
Insidious: Chapter 2 is a 2013 American supernatural horror film directed by James Wan and written by Leigh Whannell. The movie serves as a prequel to the first film, exploring the backstory of Josh Lambert's (Patrick Wilson) possession and his wife Renai's (Rose Byrne) subsequent journey.

The story begins with Josh, a paranormal investigator, who is struggling to cope with the aftermath of his previous encounter with the spirit world. He is haunted by nightmares and visions of his son Dalton (Ty Simpkins), who was possessed by an evil entity in the first film. Josh's wife Renai tries to be supportive, but their relationship is strained due to Josh's inability to shake off the traumatic events.

As Josh delves deeper into his past, he discovers that his father, John (Lew Temple), a fellow paranormal investigator, had been investigating a series of mysterious child abductions. The investigation leads them to a house in New York City, where they encounter a malevolent entity known as "The Red-Faced Demon." This demon is responsible for the abductions and is connected to an ancient ritual that has been passed down through generations.

Josh's father becomes increasingly obsessed with uncovering the truth behind the ritual, which ultimately leads to his downfall. The story takes a dark turn when Josh discovers that his father had made a pact with the entity, trading his own soul for the chance to save his son from the spirit world.

As Josh tries to make sense of his family's past and the events that led to his possession, he begins to experience more terrifying visions and nightmares. He becomes convinced that the only way to save himself and his family is to confront the entity head-on.

The climax of the film features a heart-pumping sequence where Josh faces off against the Red-Faced Demon in an abandoned asylum. With the help of his father's research, Josh manages to uncover the secrets behind the ritual and ultimately defeats the demon, saving his own soul.

However, the victory comes at a great cost, as Josh is left with severe emotional trauma and a newfound understanding of the horrors that lie beyond the veil of reality. The film concludes with Josh returning home to Renai and Dalton, but the audience is left wondering if he has truly overcome his demons or if they will continue to haunt him.

Overall, Insidious: Chapter 2 is a gripping horror film that explores themes of trauma, possession, and the supernatural. With its tense atmosphere and well-crafted plot twists, it sets the stage for the events of the first film and provides a chilling glimpse into the world of the Insidious franchise.

original_title: 名探偵コナン 瞳の中の暗殺者
overview: Police officers around Tokyo are being murdered by an unknown assailant. When Ran witnesses an attempt on the life of one of her friends in the police, she loses her memory. Now, Conan and Inspector Megure must find the murderer while Ran attempts to regain her lost memories.
title: Detective Conan: Captured in Her Eyes
plot:
Detective Conan: Captured in Her Eyes is a psychological thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. The movie follows Ran's quest to uncover the truth behind her sister's death, which leads her down a rabbit hole of deceit and manipulation.

At its core, the film explores the theme of obsession, as Ran becomes increasingly entangled in a web of lies and half-truths that threaten to consume her. Her fixation on the truth drives her to confront the darker aspects of human psychology, including the capacity for cruelty, deception, and even madness.

The movie also touches on the idea of identity and how it can be manipulated and distorted. The main antagonist's ability to create multiple personas and alter their appearance raises questions about the nature of self and how easily it can be changed or fabricated.

Furthermore, the film critiques the societal pressures that can lead individuals to conform to certain expectations or norms, even if it means sacrificing their own desires and autonomy. Ran's journey is a powerful commentary on the constraints placed on women in particular, as she navigates a patriarchal society that seeks to control her every move.

Ultimately, Detective Conan: Captured in Her Eyes is a gripping thriller that probes the depths of human psychology, revealing the complexities and nuances of the human condition.

belongs_to_collection.name: Diary of a Wimpy Kid Collection

original_title: Diary of a Wimpy Kid: Dog Days
overview: It's summertime, and Greg Heffley is looking forward to playing video games and spending time with his friends. However, Greg's dad has other plans: He's decided that some father-son bonding time is in order. Desperate to prevent his dad from ruining summer vacation, Greg pretends he has a job at a ritzy country club. But Greg's plan backfires, leaving him in the middle of embarrassing mishaps and a camping trip gone wrong.
tagline: School's out for summer.
title: Diary of a Wimpy Kid: Dog Days
plot:
Diary of a Wimpy Kid: Dog Days is a 2012 American comedy film directed by David Bowers and written by Jeff Kinney, based on the novel of the same name. The movie stars Zachary Gordon as Greg Heffley, Devon Bostick as Rodrick Heffley, and Rachael Harris as Susan Heffley.

The story begins with Greg Heffley (Zachary Gordon) trying to navigate his summer vacation. His parents have given him a lot of freedom, but he's not sure how to handle it. Greg is worried that he'll get into trouble or lose his friends. Meanwhile, Rodrick (Devon Bostick), his older brother, is trying to make the most of his own summer by getting a job and impressing girls.

As the story progresses, Greg tries to fit in with his friends Rowley (Robert Capron) and Fregley (Grayson Russell). However, things don't go as planned. Greg gets into various misadventures, including trying to start a pet-sitting business and getting into a rivalry with a new kid at school.

One of the main plot points is Greg's attempt to impress a girl named Angie (Laine MacNeil) by pretending to be more mature than he actually is. However, things quickly spiral out of control as Greg tries to keep up the act and avoid getting caught.

Throughout the movie, there are also several flashbacks that show Greg's summer vacation from the previous year, which provides some comedic relief and insight into his character development.

As the story reaches its climax, Greg learns a valuable lesson about being true to himself and not trying to be someone he's not. He also comes to terms with his relationships with his family members, particularly his brother Rodrick.

The movie ends on a positive note, with Greg reflecting on what he's learned from his summer vacation. Despite the ups and downs, Greg is grateful for the experiences he had and the friends who stood by him throughout it all.

Overall, Diary of a Wimpy Kid: Dog Days is a lighthearted and entertaining movie that explores themes of identity, friendship, and growing up. With its relatable protagonist and humorous plot twists, it's sure to appeal to fans of the book series and anyone looking for a fun summer watch.

original_title: Tinker Bell and the Lost Treasure
overview: A blue harvest moon will rise, allowing the fairies to use a precious moonstone to restore the Pixie Dust Tree, the source of all their magic. But when Tinker Bell accidentally puts all of Pixie Hollow in jeopardy, she must venture out across the sea on a secret quest to set things right.
tagline: Adventure beyond Pixie Hollow
title: Tinker Bell and the Lost Treasure
plot:
Tinker Bell and the Lost Treasure is a 2009 animated adventure film produced by DisneyToon Studios, directed by Kevan Brighting, and written by Ron Clements. The movie follows Tinker Bell's journey as she searches for her lost treasure.

The story begins with Tinker Bell (voiced by Mae Whitman) living in Pixie Hollow, a magical community of fairies who live among the flowers and trees of Neverland. Tinker Bell is known for her exceptional tinkering skills and creates innovative gadgets to help her friends. However, she has lost her most prized possession - a small, golden treasure that holds sentimental value.

The movie begins with Tinker Bell's best friend, Fawn (voiced by Lucy Hale), who has recently discovered the location of the Lost Treasure of Pixie Hollow. The treasure is hidden in a cave deep within Neverland, guarded by the infamous pirate, Captain Hook (voiced by Brian Blessed). Tinker Bell sets out on a journey to find the treasure and prove herself as a valuable member of the fairy community.

Along the way, Tinker Bell meets a new friend, Vidia (voiced by Raven-Symoné), a sassy and confident fairy who is initially skeptical of Tinker Bell's abilities. However, as they work together, Vidia becomes Tinker Bell's ally and helps her navigate the challenges of Neverland.

As Tinker Bell and Vidia journey deeper into Neverland, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, ferocious creatures, and even Captain Hook himself. The two fairies must use their wit, courage, and teamwork to overcome these challenges and reach the treasure before it falls into the wrong hands.

Throughout her adventure, Tinker Bell learns valuable lessons about friendship, perseverance, and believing in herself. She also discovers that the true value of the treasure lies not in its monetary worth but in the memories and experiences it represents.

In the end, Tinker Bell and Vidia successfully retrieve the Lost Treasure of Pixie Hollow, but not before facing a final confrontation with Captain Hook. With the help of her friends and newfound confidence, Tinker Bell outsmarts the pirate and returns to Pixie Hollow as a hero.

The movie concludes with Tinker Bell reflecting on her journey and realizing that the true treasure was the friendships she made along the way. The film ends on a heartwarming note, showcasing the beauty of Neverland and the magic of friendship among its inhabitants.

overview: Alice hires a professional negotiator to obtain the release of her engineer husband, who has been kidnapped by anti-government guerrillas in South America.
title: Proof of Life
plot:
Proof of Life is a 2000 American thriller film directed by Antoine Fuqua and starring Meg Ryan, Russell Crowe, and David Morrissey.

The main themes of Proof of Life revolve around:

1. **Kidnapping and Hostage Situation**: The movie revolves around the kidnapping of a group of American aid workers in Kenya by a ruthless terrorist organization. The story explores the complexities of hostage situations, negotiations, and the moral dilemmas faced by the characters.
2. **Humanitarianism and Compassion**: The film highlights the importance of humanitarian work and the sacrifices made by individuals who dedicate their lives to helping others. The protagonist, Teri (Meg Ryan), is a doctor who has dedicated her life to providing aid in Africa, and her experiences serve as a catalyst for the story.
3. **Power Dynamics and Manipulation**: The movie explores the power dynamics between the kidnappers and the hostages, as well as the manipulations used by both sides to achieve their goals. This theme is particularly evident in the character of Amira (Kim Basinger), who uses her intelligence and cunning to manipulate the situation to her advantage.
4. **Personal Sacrifices and Redemption**: Throughout the film, characters are forced to confront their personal demons and make difficult choices that test their moral compass. The story ultimately becomes a journey of redemption for Teri, as she finds a way to escape and reclaim control over her life.

The movie's themes are expertly woven throughout the narrative, creating a tense and thought-provoking thriller that keeps audiences on the edge of their seats.

overview: A raw and emotionally revealing look at one of the most iconic artists of our time during a transformational period in her life as she learns to embrace her role not only as a songwriter and performer, but as a woman harnessing the full power of her voice.
title: Miss Americana
plot:
Miss Americana is a 2020 documentary film that delves into the life of Taylor Swift, an American singer-songwriter. The movie explores themes of identity, feminism, and the complexities of fame.

At its core, Miss Americana is a deeply personal and introspective film that examines the tensions between Swift's public persona and her private self. As she navigates the pressures of being a global superstar, Swift grapples with the expectations placed upon her as a woman in the entertainment industry. The film sheds light on the ways in which societal norms and media scrutiny can shape our perceptions of ourselves and our place in the world.

Throughout the documentary, Swift's character is portrayed as a multifaceted individual struggling to maintain her artistic integrity amidst the demands of fame. Her relationships with others, including her family and romantic partners, are also subject to scrutiny, highlighting the challenges of balancing personal and professional life.

One of the primary concerns of Miss Americana is the performative nature of identity in contemporary culture. Swift's character embodies this theme as she navigates the blurred lines between her public persona and private self. The film raises questions about the ways in which we present ourselves to the world, and whether these performances can ever truly be authentic.

Ultimately, Miss Americana presents a nuanced exploration of the human experience, one that is both deeply personal and universally relatable. Through Swift's story, the documentary sheds light on the complexities of fame, identity, and the search for meaning in a hyper-mediated world.

overview: Mario is a young fisherman who dreams of becoming a poet. He gets a job as the postman to Pablo Neruda when the legendary writer moves there after being exiled from Chile.
title: Burning Patience
plot:
Burning Patience (Spanish: Ardiente paciencia) is a 2022 Chilean romantic drama directed by Rodrigo Sepúlveda from a screenplay by Guillermo Calderón, based on Antonio Skármeta's novel, which had already inspired Skármeta's own 1983 film and Michael Radford's Il Postino (1994). Produced by Fábula, it was the first Chilean film produced by Netflix. Andrew Bargsted stars as Mario and Vivianne Dietz as Beatriz, with Claudio Arredondo as the poet Pablo Neruda, Paola Giannini as Beatriz's mother Elba, Amalia Kassai as Clarita, Rodolfo Pulgar as Cosme, Pablo Macaya as Jorge, Trinidad González as Elvira and Giordano Rossi as Julio.

The story is set in 1969 on the coast of Chile at Isla Negra, where Neruda lives, hoping to devote his later years to writing while being pressed by supporters to run for president. Mario, a young man barely out of his teens who tells his father he has no interest in continuing the family's fishing tradition, takes a job at the post office because he owns a bicycle, and becomes the postman for a single client, the famous poet, whose thoughts he constantly interrupts. Mario falls for Beatriz, a newcomer who works at the inn and cantina run by her mother, but Elba fiercely opposes the romance, warning her daughter against men who seduce with words. To win Beatriz over, Mario writes her love letters, but he plagiarizes Neruda's poems, and since everyone in Chile knows the poet's verses by heart, she catches him. The two begin exchanging notes through a young nun, with Beatriz challenging Mario to express himself as a real poet, and later send messages through the dedications of the local radio station, while Neruda mentors the young man in metaphor and love.

Netflix announced the project with Fábula in November 2021; Boris Quercia was initially reported as director before Sepúlveda took over. Filming began on 4 April 2022 in Isla Negra, the village of Neruda's favorite house. The film premiered in the Galas section of the Mar del Plata International Film Festival in Argentina in November 2022 and was released on Netflix on 7 December 2022. Reviews were mildly positive. Roger Moore of Movie Nation called it a lightly charming romance that works on its own terms and finishes wonderfully, singling out Giannini's disapproving mother, but felt it never surpasses Il Postino and missed a more larger-than-life Neruda. Other critics similarly found it sweet and pleasant but unremarkable.

overview: A soldier and member of the Dutch resistance investigates stolen art in the wake of the Second World War, including a Vermeer sold to the Nazis by a flamboyant forger.
tagline: Deception is a fine art.
title: The Last Vermeer
plot:
The Last Vermeer is an American historical drama directed by Dan Friedkin from a screenplay by John Orloff (credited as James McGee), Mark Fergus and Hawk Ostby, based on Jonathan Lopez's 2008 book The Man Who Made Vermeers. Guy Pearce plays the Dutch painter and dealer Han van Meegeren, accused of selling national treasures to the Nazis, and Claes Bang plays Joseph Piller, the former resistance fighter assigned to investigate him, with Vicky Krieps and Roland Møller. It premiered at the Telluride Film Festival in August 2019 and was released in American cinemas by Sony's TriStar Pictures label on November 20, 2020.

At the end of the Second World War, Captain Joseph Piller, a Dutch Jew who fought in the resistance, works for the Allied military administration of the Netherlands. When a Vermeer is found in Hermann Göring's looted collection, Piller and his assistant Dekker arrest van Meegeren, the flamboyant artist who sold it to him, on charges of collaboration. Fearing that Dutch authorities led by the zealous De Klerks will either let him slip away or sacrifice him in a postwar purge, Piller hides him in a safe house under Allied protection.

Under interrogation, van Meegeren demands painting materials and explains himself: dismissed by critics before the war, he became the source of several "lost" Vermeers that surfaced in the 1930s and funded a lavish life, later enriched by dealings with the Nazis, whom he claims to despise. Finally he insists that the Göring Vermeer is a fake. When the Allies withdraw, De Klerks takes custody of him, and he faces the death penalty. Piller, now working as a labourer, finds the unfinished canvas van Meegeren painted in the safe house and realises it matches the recovered painting. Convinced, he agrees to defend him and learns how he faked the works, using Bakelite to harden his paint and heating and rolling the canvases to simulate age.

At the trial, the art experts who once authenticated the paintings persuade the judges to convict. Piller has Dekker create a diversion, splashes acid on one canvas and reveals van Meegeren's own signature underneath, and the verdict is overturned to public acclaim. Later, however, De Klerks shows Piller a book from the safe house bearing van Meegeren's dedication to Adolf Hitler. Realising he was deceived, Piller confronts the painter, is coldly dismissed, and burns the book.

Rotten Tomatoes reported 70% approval, with critics praising Pearce's performance.

overview: Ip Man's peaceful life in Foshan changes after Gong Yutian seeks an heir for his family in Southern China. Ip Man then meets Gong Er who challenges him for the sake of regaining her family's honor. After the Second Sino-Japanese War, Ip Man moves to Hong Kong and struggles to provide for his family. In the mean time, Gong Er chooses the path of vengeance after her father was killed by Ma San.
tagline: In Martial Arts there is no right or wrong, only the last man standing.
title: The Grandmaster
plot:
The Grandmaster (2013) is a biographical martial arts drama film directed by Wong Kar-wai, produced by Toivyan Productions and Sil-Metropole Organisation.

The main themes of The Grandmaster revolve around the life of Ip Man, a grandmaster of the Wing Chun style of Kung Fu. Some of the key themes include:

1. **Legacy and Heritage**: The film explores the complexities of legacy and heritage through Ip Man's journey as he navigates his role as a master of Wing Chun while also dealing with the challenges of adapting to changing times.

2. **Identity and Belonging**: Ip Man struggles with his identity, caught between his loyalty to his family, his students, and his own sense of self. This theme is reflected in his relationships with his son, Raymond, and his rival, Chan Wah-shun.

3. **Martial Arts as a Way of Life**: The film showcases the spiritual and philosophical aspects of Wing Chun, highlighting its emphasis on discipline, respect, and self-control. Ip Man's approach to martial arts is deeply rooted in his Buddhist faith and his desire to cultivate inner peace.

4. **War and Trauma**: The film depicts the impact of war on individuals and communities, particularly during the Second Sino-Japanese War. Ip Man's experiences as a soldier and his subsequent struggles with PTSD serve as a backdrop for the story.

5. **Family and Loyalty**: The relationships between Ip Man and his family members are central to the narrative. His love for his son Raymond is tested by his own sense of duty and responsibility, while his loyalty to his students and fellow martial artists is unwavering.

6. **Adaptation and Change**: As the film progresses, Ip Man must confront the changing world around him, including the rise of modernity and the decline of traditional values. His ability to adapt and evolve as a master is a key aspect of his character development.
