The Grandmaster features stunning cinematography, memorable performances, and a richly detailed portrayal of Wing Chun culture. The film's themes are both deeply personal and universally relatable, making it a powerful exploration of the human condition.

overview: Dahlia Williams and her daughter Cecelia move into a rundown apartment on New York's Roosevelt Island. She is currently in midst of divorce proceedings and the apartment, though near an excellent school for her daughter, is all she can afford. From the time she arrives, there are mysterious occurrences and there is a constant drip from the ceiling in her daughter's bedroom.
tagline: This Season, The Mystery Of The Darkness Will Consume Your Life
title: Dark Water
plot:
Dark Water is a 2005 psychological horror film directed by Walter Salles, produced by Warner Bros. Pictures and Vertigo Entertainment.

The main themes of Dark Water revolve around grief, trauma, and the supernatural. The story follows a mother, Yoshimi Takagi (played by Kenichi Matsuyama), who moves into a new apartment with her two children after her husband's death in a car accident. However, their lives are soon disrupted by a mysterious and malevolent presence that seems to emanate from the building's water system.

Throughout the film, the themes of grief and trauma are expertly woven together as Yoshimi struggles to cope with the loss of her husband and find a way to move forward with her children. The supernatural elements in the film serve as a metaphor for the emotional turmoil that Yoshimi is experiencing, and the ways in which it can manifest itself in terrifying and unpredictable ways.

The film also explores the idea of isolation and loneliness, as Yoshimi becomes increasingly withdrawn and isolated from her community due to her grief. This sense of disconnection serves to heighten the tension and suspense as the supernatural events escalate, making it difficult for Yoshimi (and the audience) to distinguish between reality and fantasy.

Ultimately, Dark Water is a powerful exploration of the human psyche's ability to cope with trauma and find ways to heal and move forward in the face of adversity. The film's themes are both haunting and thought-provoking, leaving the viewer with a lasting sense of unease and introspection.

overview: Zach is devastated by the unexpected death of his girlfriend, Beth. When she mysteriously returns, he gets a second chance at love. Soon his whole world turns upside down...
tagline: Boy meets girl. Girl eats boy.
title: Life After Beth
plot:
Life After Beth is a 2014 American fantasy-comedy film directed by Jeff Chan and written by Chris Miller and Sean Anders. The movie follows the story of Todd, a young man who returns home after his girlfriend Beth dies in a car accident, only to discover that she has been brought back to life with a mysterious and unsettling twist.

The main theme of Life After Beth revolves around the complexities of grief, relationships, and the human condition. As Todd navigates his new reality with Beth's return, he is forced to confront the emotional turmoil and uncertainty that comes with losing someone close. The film expertly explores the blurred lines between life and death, raising questions about what it means to be alive and how we cope with loss.

The movie also delves into the theme of identity and the masks people wear in relationships. Beth's return forces Todd to re-examine his own emotions and desires, as well as those of his family members, who are struggling to come to terms with their own feelings about her death. The film's portrayal of these complex emotions is both poignant and humorous, making for a unique viewing experience.

Furthermore, Life After Beth touches on the idea of acceptance and letting go. As Todd tries to reconcile his love for Beth with the reality of her return, he must also confront the possibility that she may not be the same person he knew before. This theme is skillfully woven throughout the narrative, adding depth and nuance to the story.

Overall, Life After Beth is a thought-provoking film that explores the intricacies of human relationships, grief, and identity with humor and sensitivity.

overview: Chaos reigns at the natural history museum when night watchman Larry Daley accidentally stirs up an ancient curse, awakening Attila the Hun, an army of gladiators, a Tyrannosaurus rex and other exhibits.
tagline: Where History Comes To Life
title: Night at the Museum
plot:
Night at the Museum is a 2006 American fantasy adventure comedy film directed by Shawn Levy and produced by 20th Century Fox.

The movie begins with Larry Daley (played by Ben Stiller), a museum night guard who has just lost his job due to budget cuts. On his last day, he discovers that the museum's exhibits come to life at night. The main attraction is Teddy Roosevelt (played by Robin Williams), the 26th President of the United States, who is one of the most iconic figures in American history.

As Larry navigates this new world, he meets other historical figures such as Attila the Hun (played by Patrick Gallagher) and Sacagawea (played by Mizuo Peck). However, things take a turn when Larry discovers that the museum's security system has been hacked, allowing the villainous Kahmunrah (played by Mickey Rooney), an ancient Egyptian pharaoh, to escape from his display case.

Kahmunrah is determined to reclaim his throne and conquer the world. He believes that he was the greatest ruler of all time and that everyone else is inferior. Larry must team up with Teddy Roosevelt and other historical figures to stop Kahmunrah's evil plans.

As the night unfolds, Larry learns more about the museum's exhibits and their unique personalities. He also discovers that he has a special connection to the museum and its history. With the help of his new friends, Larry must use his wits and resourcefulness to outsmart Kahmunrah and save the day.

The movie features a mix of action, adventure, and humor, with plenty of witty one-liners from Robin Williams' iconic performance as Teddy Roosevelt. The film's climax features an epic battle between Larry and Kahmunrah, with the fate of the world hanging in the balance.

In the end, Larry is able to defeat Kahmunrah and restore order to the museum. However, he also learns that being a night guard is not just about keeping the exhibits safe, but also about preserving history and bringing people together. The movie ends on a heartwarming note, with Larry finding a new sense of purpose and belonging.

Overall, Night at the Museum is a fun and entertaining film that celebrates the magic of museums and the power of imagination. With its talented cast, witty script, and exciting action sequences, it's no wonder that this movie became a box office hit and spawned two sequels.

overview: Author P.L. Travers looks back on her childhood while reluctantly meeting with Walt Disney, who seeks to adapt her Mary Poppins books for the big screen.
tagline: Where her book ended, their story began.
title: Saving Mr. Banks
plot:
Saving Mr. Banks is a 2013 biographical drama film that tells the story of the making of Mary Poppins, a classic Disney musical. The movie delves into the complex and often tumultuous relationship between Walt Disney and author P.L. Travers, who created the beloved character.

At its core, Saving Mr. Banks explores the themes of creative control, identity, and the power of storytelling. The film highlights the tension between artistic vision and commercial success, as Disney's desire to adapt Mary Poppins into a film is met with resistance from Travers, who is fiercely protective of her creation.

Through the lens of this conflict, the movie also examines the complexities of female identity and the societal expectations placed upon women during that era. Travers, in particular, is portrayed as a strong-willed and independent woman who struggles to reconcile her creative ambitions with the demands of motherhood and personal relationships.

Furthermore, Saving Mr. Banks touches on the idea of nostalgia and the enduring power of childhood imagination. The film's portrayal of Mary Poppins as a symbol of innocence and wonder serves as a reminder of the importance of holding onto these qualities in an increasingly complex and adult world.

Ultimately, the movie suggests that the true magic of storytelling lies not in its commercial success or artistic merit, but in its ability to transport us to another time and place, and to evoke emotions and memories that transcend generations.

original_title: 鋼の錬金術師 完結編 復讐者スカー
overview: The Elric brothers meet their toughest opponent yet — a lone serial killer with a large scar on his forehead.
title: Fullmetal Alchemist: The Revenge of Scar
plot:
Fullmetal Alchemist: The Revenge of Scar (Japanese: Hagane no Renkinjutsushi Kanketsu-hen: Fukushūsha Scar) is a 2022 Japanese fantasy action film directed by Fumihiko Sori, who co-wrote the screenplay with Takeshi Miyamoto. Based on Hiromu Arakawa's manga, it is the sequel to the 2017 live-action Fullmetal Alchemist and the first half of a two-part finale, followed by Fullmetal Alchemist: The Final Alchemy in June 2022. Ryosuke Yamada returns as Edward Elric, with Atomu Mizuishi as Alphonse, Tsubasa Honda as Winry and Dean Fujioka as Roy Mustang, while Mackenyu plays the vengeful Scar. Announced as part of the manga's 20th-anniversary celebrations, it was meant to shoot in Italy like its predecessor, but because of the COVID-19 pandemic open sets were built in Kyonan, Chiba. Warner Bros. Japan released it on 20 May 2022, and it reached Netflix in August.

Travelling by train to Central City, Ed and Al meet Ling Yao (Keisuke Watanabe), a prince from Xing seeking the secret of immortality. When bandits hijack the train, the brothers fight them on the locomotive, are unexpectedly helped by the homunculus Envy, and use alchemy to stop a bomb plot. In Central they learn that a serial killer is murdering State Alchemists. Slipping away from their bodyguards, they meet May Chang, a girl from Xing, and are attacked by Scar, an Ishvalan who badly damages Al's armour and destroys Ed's automail arm before Mustang drives him off. While Ed returns to Resembool for repairs, he encounters his estranged father Van Hohenheim (Seiyo Uchino), and Scar recovers among Ishvalan refugees. Ling proposes an alliance to capture Scar and the homunculi, but the trap collapses: Winry learns that Scar killed her parents, a doctor couple, during the Ishval war and tries to shoot him, King Bradley (Hiroshi Tachi) wounds Ling's bodyguard Lan Fan, and Scar escapes with May. Riza Hawkeye tells Ed about the massacre of Ishval, in which Scar lost his brother. Later, when Al and May find Scar, Winry dresses his wound and he expresses remorse. In a final clash, the homunculus Gluttony swallows Ed, Ling and Envy, and inside his stomach Envy reveals that Gluttony is a failed Gate of Truth created by Father before transforming into a monstrous dragon.

The ensemble also includes Yuina Kuroshima as Lan Fan, Ron Monroe as May, Kokoro Terada as Selim Bradley, Yuki Yamada as Kimblee, Kanata Hongo as Envy and Jun Fubuki as Pinako Rockbell.

overview: A boy in New York is taken in by a wealthy family after his mother is killed in a bombing at the Metropolitan Museum of Art. In a rush of panic, he steals 'The Goldfinch', a painting that eventually draws him into a world of crime.
tagline: The story of a stolen life
title: The Goldfinch
plot:
The Goldfinch is a 2019 American drama film directed by John Cameron Mitchell, based on the 2013 novel of the same name by Donna Tartt.

The main themes of The Goldfinch include:

1. **Trauma and Recovery**: The film explores the long-term effects of trauma on the protagonist, Theo Decker, who witnesses a terrorist attack at an art museum in New York City. The story delves into his struggles to cope with grief, guilt, and anxiety.
2. **Grief and Loss**: The Goldfinch is a poignant exploration of the complexities of human emotions, particularly in the face of loss. Theo's relationship with his mother, who dies in the attack, serves as a catalyst for his emotional journey.
3. **Identity and Belonging**: As Theo navigates his way through life, he grapples with finding his place in the world. The film examines his relationships with others, including his friends, family, and mentors, to understand what it means to belong and find one's identity.
4. **Art and Creativity**: The Goldfinch highlights the significance of art as a means of expression, healing, and connection. Theo's love for art serves as a source of comfort and inspiration throughout his journey.
5. **Mortality and Impermanence**: The film confronts the reality of mortality, reminding viewers that life is fleeting and that we must cherish every moment. This theme is particularly evident in Theo's relationships with those who have passed away.

The story unfolds over several decades, following Theo as he grows from a vulnerable child to a young adult struggling to find his place in the world. The film features stunning cinematography, memorable performances, and a richly detailed narrative that explores the complexities of human emotions.

Overall, The Goldfinch is a powerful exploration of the human experience, tackling themes that are both universally relatable and deeply personal.

overview: A mother (in her Minivan) stops at nothing to recover her kidnapped son.
tagline: Vengeance is Mom
title: Kidnap
plot:
Kidnap is a 2017 American action thriller directed by Luis Prieto and written by Knate Lee. Halle Berry stars as Karla Dyson, a working mother who chases the people who abducted her young son, with Sage Correa as her son Frankie, Chris McGinn and Lew Temple as the kidnappers Margo and Terry Vickey, and Jason Winston George as Karla's estranged husband. Filmed in Louisiana in late 2014 on a budget of about 21 million dollars, it was delayed several times after its original distributor, Relativity Media, filed for bankruptcy in 2015, and it was eventually released by the newly founded Aviron Pictures in August 2017.

Karla is a waitress and a single mother involved in a custody dispute with her former husband. One afternoon she takes her six-year-old son Frankie to a carnival in a park. While she takes a phone call from her lawyer, Frankie vanishes, and Karla finds only his toy voice recorder. Rushing into the parking lot, she sees a woman forcing Frankie into a green Ford Mustang driven by a man.

Without her phone, which she dropped in the panic, Karla jumps into her minivan and gives chase. What follows is an almost continuous pursuit along the highways around New Orleans. The kidnappers try to shake her off by causing a multi-car pile-up and threaten to kill the boy with a knife. From Frankie's recorder, Karla learns that the woman's name is Margo. A motorcycle police officer she alerts is killed by the kidnappers, and Margo offers to return Frankie in exchange for ten thousand dollars. Karla refuses to give up, fighting off Margo in her own car, and she persists in following the kidnappers even when the police seem unable to help, eventually tracking them to their isolated home in the countryside, where she must confront them alone to rescue her son.

The film is built almost entirely around Berry's performance and the extended car chase, with little dialogue and a focus on a mother's determination to save her child at any cost.

Kidnap received mostly negative reviews, with an approval rating of about 35 percent on Rotten Tomatoes, although Berry's committed performance was frequently praised. It grossed about 34.8 million dollars worldwide, of which 31 million came from the United States and Canada.

overview: The Christmas tree isn't the only thing green in this new holiday classic. Shrek is back and trying to get into the spirit of the season. After promising Fiona and the kids a Christmas they'll remember, he is forced to take a crash course in the holiday. But just when he thinks he has everything for their quiet family Christmas just right, there is a knock at the door.
title: Shrek the Halls
plot:
Shrek the Halls is an American animated Christmas television special that premiered on ABC on 28 November 2007. Produced by DreamWorks Animation and Pacific Data Images, the half-hour special was co-written and directed by Gary Trousdale. Mike Myers, Eddie Murphy, Cameron Diaz and Antonio Banderas reprise their roles as Shrek, Donkey, Princess Fiona and Puss in Boots from the feature films, with Cody Cameron returning as Pinocchio and the Three Little Pigs. The story takes place after the events of Shrek the Third, and the title is a play on the carol "Deck the Halls."

Shrek is living happily in his swamp with Fiona and their three babies, while Donkey keeps announcing the approach of Christmas far too early, to Shrek's irritation. When the season arrives, Donkey pressures Shrek into promising Fiona a special Christmas. The trouble is that the ogre has no idea what Christmas is about. He visits a bookshop in Far Far Away, where the shopkeeper sells him a guide called Christmas for Village Idiots, and he follows its instructions to the letter, decorating the house and cutting down a tree in the hope of a quiet, cozy Christmas Eve with his family.

His plans are ruined when Donkey arrives with the entire crowd of fairy-tale friends, including Puss, Gingy, Pinocchio and the Three Little Pigs. When Shrek tries to read "The Night Before Christmas," the others interrupt with their own versions of the holiday: Donkey's tale features a Santa made of waffles, Puss's turns into a cat chasing ornaments, and Gingy's story is a horror tale in which Santa devours his girlfriend Suzy. Their bickering and chaos finally make Shrek lose his temper and drive everyone out, leading him to realize, with Fiona's help, that the holiday he wanted was less about doing everything right than about the people he shares it with.

The special drew a large television audience and was well received, holding a Metacritic score of 73 based on 30 critics, indicating generally favorable reviews. It was nominated for several Annie Awards, has been repeated on television regularly during the holiday season, and earned about $16 million in home video sales. It was followed by a Halloween special, Scared Shrekless, in 2010.

overview: When a fellow scientist asks for Jack's help in locating the mausoleum of China's first emperor, the past collides violently with the present as Jack discovers his amazing visions are based in fact.
title: The Myth
plot:
The Myth is a 2005 Hong Kong and Chinese martial arts fantasy adventure directed by Stanley Tong, who co-wrote it with Li Haishu and Wang Hui-ling, and produced by Jackie Chan, who also stars. The supporting cast includes Tony Leung Ka-fai, Kim Hee-sun and Mallika Sherawat. The story intertwines a romance in ancient China with a modern treasure-hunting adventure.

In the Qin dynasty, General Meng Yi is charged with escorting the Korean princess Ok-soo to China to become the emperor's concubine. Wounded while protecting her, he falls in love with her, but both remain loyal to their duties. When the emperor falls gravely ill, Meng Yi is sent to retrieve the elixir of life, and before leaving he confesses his love to Ok-soo, who vows to wait for him. Ambushed, he passes the elixir to his deputy, Nangong Yan, before dying of his wounds. The court forces Nangong Yan and Ok-soo to test the elixir by drinking it; they become immortal and are sealed inside the emperor's mausoleum for eternity.

In the present day, archaeologist Jack, the reincarnation of Meng Yi, is troubled by dreams of his past life. With his friend William, he travels to India to investigate the floating tomb of a prince, sustained by a mysterious material that creates zero gravity. When William disrupts the field and the tomb collapses, Jack falls into a river and is rescued by Samantha, whose uncle is a Kalaripayattu master. Duelling with one of his students, Jack experiences a vision of Meng Yi fighting the Indian prince. Back home, the pair donate an ancient sword they recovered to the National Museum of China, angering Professor Koo, head of the syndicate that has financed their hunt.

Jack and William discover that the material is a fragment of a meteorite that fell during the Qin dynasty, and locate the emperor's mausoleum behind a waterfall, where the largest fragment keeps a palace floating in the air. Inside, Jack meets Ok-soo and Nangong Yan, who take him for Meng Yi. Koo's men storm the tomb to seize the elixir, sparking an airborne battle. William destabilises the field and dies as the tomb collapses, Nangong Yan drags Koo to his death, and Ok-soo, realising that Jack is not Meng Yi, refuses to leave. Jack later publishes a book about the adventure, dedicated to William.

The film was a hit in Hong Kong, earning HK$17 million, but drew poor reviews from English-language critics.

overview: Barbie is a cosmic princess who flies high on her hoverboard through a far-off universe with her adorable and devoted pet sidekick, Pupcorn. One day, everything changes when the twinkling stars start to dim and slow their dance in the sky. Barbie travels to a beautiful new planet to join a special rescue team on a mission to save the stars. Once there, she teams up with a group of talented new friends who work together to save the galaxy through exciting hoverboarding adventures. Barbie soon discovers that if she listens to her heart, and with the help of her friends, she might be the leader the whole universe has been waiting for!
title: Barbie: Star Light Adventure
plot:
Barbie: Star Light Adventure is a 2016 computer-animated children's adventure film directed by Andrew Tan and written by Kacey Arnold, with Kate Boutilier assisting on the script. The 33rd entry in the Barbie film series, it was the first produced under Mattel's new Mattel Creations banner and the first to open with the doll brand's message sequence. After a one-day Fathom Events screening, it was released on home video by Universal and later aired on Nickelodeon. Its voice cast includes Erica Lindbeck, Dwight Schultz and Robbie Daymond.

A prophecy foretells that one day the stars will stop their cosmic dance and go dark unless "the One" can make them shine again, and the sky is indeed growing darker. The rigid, orderly King Constantine, convinced despite repeated failures that he is the One, recruits a team of gifted young people for his latest plan. On the wildlife preserve planet of Para-Den, Barbie is an enthusiastic but impulsive hoverboarder who can communicate with animals and objects through telekinesis. Encouraged by her widowed father, she accepts the king's invitation and travels to the Capital Planet.

There she meets her teammates: Sal-Lee, a sarcastic, competitive hoverboarder with super speed; Prince Leo, a shy and awkward but brilliant pilot; and the kindly alien twins Kareena and Sheena, who share a psychic link and can make things lighter or heavier. Barbie's free-spirited ways repeatedly clash with Constantine's insistence on order, and when she persuades the team to release a Starlian creature they were meant to capture, believing he wants it for a zoo, he fires her, explaining that the creature was needed to guide them to the centre of the galaxy. Barbie apologises for misjudging him but not for following her conscience, and uses her powers to ask the Starlian for help. Under pressure from her teammates, Constantine reinstates her as leader.

Guided by the Starlian, the team reaches the galaxy's central planet, where Barbie and her friends clear a path to the core for Constantine and his machine. Ignoring Barbie's advice, he uses the device to force the stars into order, and they go out at once. Sensing that the stars have stopped dancing out of sadness and loneliness, Barbie begins a new dance with them, restoring their light and proving herself the One. Humbled, Constantine takes Barbie and her father in as his wards, and the film ends with Princess Starlight and her friends teaching the king to dance.

overview: After being gone for a decade, a country star returns home to the love he left behind.
tagline: Find your way back home
title: Forever My Girl
plot:
Forever My Girl is a 2018 American romantic drama film directed by Beth McCarthy-Miller and written by Aaron Lohr. The movie stars Josh Duhamel, Emma Roberts, and Danika Yarosh.

The story revolves around Jake Dorn (Josh Duhamel), a young musician who has just been dumped by his girlfriend, Gerry (Danika Yarosh). Gerry is a talented singer-songwriter who wants to pursue her music career in Nashville. Feeling lost and heartbroken, Jake decides to leave his life behind and move to Nashville to help Gerry achieve her dreams.

Upon arrival, Jake meets Lucy (Emma Roberts), a charming and free-spirited woman who owns a small bookstore. The two strike up an instant connection, bonding over their shared love of music and literature. As they spend more time together, Jake finds himself falling for Lucy's charms, but he struggles to open up about his past heartbreak.

Meanwhile, Gerry is struggling to make it big in Nashville, facing rejection and disappointment at every turn. She becomes increasingly frustrated with her lack of success and begins to question whether she made a mistake by leaving her life behind. As Jake spends more time with Lucy, he starts to realize that he may have missed his chance with Gerry.

As the story unfolds, Jake finds himself torn between his feelings for Lucy and his lingering emotions for Gerry. He must confront his past heartbreak and figure out what he truly wants from life. Along the way, he learns valuable lessons about love, loss, and finding one's true purpose.

Throughout the movie, the cinematography is stunning, capturing the beauty of Nashville's music scene and the charm of Lucy's bookstore. The soundtrack features a mix of original songs and classic country tunes, adding to the film's nostalgic and romantic atmosphere.

In the end, Jake must make a choice between his old life with Gerry and his new life with Lucy. Will he find happiness with the woman who has captured his heart, or will he return to his past and risk losing the love of his life? The movie's ending is bittersweet, leaving audiences to ponder the complexities of love and relationships.

Overall, Forever My Girl is a poignant and romantic drama that explores the ups and downs of love, loss, and self-discovery. With its talented cast, stunning cinematography, and catchy soundtrack, this movie is sure to captivate audiences who enjoy stories about music, love, and finding one's true purpose.

overview: Upon reaching the train station to death, a dejected soul is informed that he is lucky and will have another chance at life. He is placed in the body of a 14-year-old boy named Kobayashi Makoto, who has just committed suicide. Watched over by a neutral spirit named Purapura, the soul must figure out what his greatest sin and mistake in his former life was, before his time limit in Makoto's body runs out. He also has a number of other lesser duties he must complete, such as understanding what led Makoto to commit suicide in the first place and learning how to enjoy his second chance at life.
title: Colorful
plot:
Colorful is a poignant and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of human relationships, redemption, and the power of love to transcend time and circumstance.

At its core, Colorful is a story about the interconnectedness of lives and the ways in which our experiences shape us. The film follows the life of Tetsuo, a young man who struggles to come to terms with his troubled past and find his place in the world. Through his relationships with others, particularly a woman named Akane, Tetsuo grapples with feelings of guilt, shame, and regret.

One of the main themes of Colorful is the idea that our past experiences can both define us and set us free. Tetsuo's journey is marked by moments of painful self-discovery, as he confronts the choices he made in the past and the consequences they had on those around him. Through this process, he begins to heal and find a sense of redemption, which ultimately allows him to move forward with greater purpose and clarity.

The film also explores the theme of love as a transformative force that can bridge even the widest of gaps between people. Akane's unwavering support and acceptance of Tetsuo serve as a catalyst for his growth, allowing him to confront his demons and find a sense of peace. The relationship between Tetsuo and Akane is a powerful reminder that true love can be both redemptive and liberating.

Furthermore, Colorful touches on the idea that our memories and experiences are what make us human. The film's non-linear narrative structure, which jumps back and forth in time, serves to underscore this point. By presenting Tetsuo's story in a fragmented and impressionistic way, the filmmakers highlight the subjective nature of memory and the ways in which our perceptions can be both accurate and distorted.

Overall, Colorful is a deeply moving and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of human relationships, redemption, and the power of love to transcend time and circumstance.

overview: Four young men want to leave their dystopian world behind and go to a distant paradise to execute a money robbery, a daring act that will have unexpected consequences.
title: Time to Hunt
plot:
Time to Hunt is a 2020 South Korean dystopian action thriller written and directed by Yoon Sung-hyun, starring Lee Je-hoon, Ahn Jae-hong, Choi Woo-shik, Park Jeong-min and Park Hae-soo. It premiered at the 70th Berlin International Film Festival in February 2020, the first South Korean film selected for the Berlinale Special section. Its planned theatrical release was postponed by the COVID-19 pandemic, and Netflix released it worldwide on April 23, 2020.

In a near-future South Korea wracked by economic collapse, where the won has become virtually worthless, Jun-seok is released from prison after serving time for a botched robbery. He proposes one last heist to his best friends Jang-ho and Ki-hoon so that they can escape their miserable lives: an illegal gambling den that keeps its money in US dollars. They recruit Sang-soo, a friend who works there, and obtain guns from Jun-seok's contact Bong-sik. Despite a chaotic execution, the robbery succeeds, and the gang escapes with a large haul of cash along with the den's surveillance hard drives. Sang-soo stays on at his job to avoid suspicion while the others lie low.

The hard drives, however, contain footage of the den owners' dealings with powerful criminals, and the owners hire Han, a former police officer turned contract killer, to retrieve them. Han murders Bong-sik after forcing him to reveal the trio's whereabouts, then kills Sang-soo and uses his phone to track them. Realising they are being hunted, the friends flee, but Han shoots Jang-ho as they leave and then toys with them, granting them a five-minute head start to prolong the chase. Han tracks them through the city's surveillance network to a hospital, from which they barely escape. Arrested by police, he is released on the orders of a police chief.

The trio hide out near a harbour, waiting to leave the country at dawn, but Ki-hoon goes back to check on his parents. Han finds the others, and in a desperate gunfight Jang-ho is killed. As Han closes in on Jun-seok, masked men led by Bong-sik's brother Bong-soo ambush him and riddle him with bullets, and he falls into the sea. Jun-seok escapes by boat to Taiwan, but learns that Han has survived and that Ki-hoon is apparently dead. Deciding that he will never be free by running, he trains, arms himself and returns home to confront Han.

Critics praised the film's technical prowess and tension, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 69% approval; The Hollywood Reporter called it a technical tour de force.

overview: When a long list of shenanigans lands Tyler in hot water, he’s forced to suit up and spend his summer training for an elite junior lifeguard program.
title: Malibu Rescue
plot:
Malibu Rescue is a 2019 American teen comedy-drama film that revolves around the lives of three brothers who run a beach rescue operation in Malibu, California. The movie explores the complexities of family dynamics, particularly among siblings, as they navigate their relationships and personal struggles.

At its core, Malibu Rescue delves into themes of identity, loyalty, and self-discovery. The main characters are forced to confront their own insecurities and limitations as they face various challenges, both on and off the beach. As they work together to save others, they also learn valuable lessons about themselves and their place in the world.

The film also touches on the theme of social class and privilege, highlighting the differences between the wealthy families who frequent the beach and those who are less fortunate. This contrast serves as a backdrop for exploring issues of entitlement, responsibility, and empathy.

Furthermore, Malibu Rescue features a strong coming-of-age narrative, where the characters must navigate the challenges of adolescence, including first loves, peer pressure, and finding their own paths in life. The movie's lighthearted tone and comedic moments belie its thoughtful exploration of these themes, making it an engaging watch for audiences of all ages.

Overall, Malibu Rescue is a heartwarming and entertaining film that balances humor with substance, offering a relatable and endearing portrayal of family, friendship, and personal growth.

overview: Kham is the last in long line of guards who once watched over the King of Thailand's war elephants. Traditionally, only the perfect elephants could successfully help defend the throne, after his harrowing quest to retrieve the elephants, Kham returns to his village to live in peace. But for someone as good in martial arts as him, peace is but a wishful thought.
tagline: This time the fight goes beyond.
title: The Protector 2
plot:
I couldn't find any information on a movie called "The Protector 2" directed by Baa-Ram-Ewe. 

However, I found that there is a Thai martial arts film called "The Protector" released in 2005, also known as "Tom-yum-goong", which was directed by Prachya Pinkaew and produced by Sahaphap Yotphayaponghakha and Baa Ram-Ewe.

overview: Seeking to offer his son the satisfying summer camp experience that eluded him as a child, the operator of a neighborhood daycare center opens his own camp, only to face financial hardship and stiff competition from a rival camp.
tagline: The summer is going to be in tents.
title: Daddy Day Camp
plot:
Daddy Day Camp is a 2007 American comedy film directed by Dean Parisot and starring Eddie Murphy, Jeff Garlin, and Anjelica Huston.

The movie revolves around Charlie Hinton (Eddie Murphy), an ex-boy scout who returns to his alma mater as the new director of the local day camp. As he tries to reconnect with his estranged son, Max (Logan Lerman), Charlie must confront his own past mistakes and learn to be a better father.

The main theme of Daddy Day Camp is the importance of redemption and second chances. Charlie's journey is one of self-discovery and growth, as he works to repair his relationship with Max and make amends for past errors. Through his experiences at the day camp, Charlie learns valuable lessons about leadership, teamwork, and the importance of following your heart.

The film also explores themes of family, forgiveness, and the challenges of modern parenting. As Charlie navigates the complexities of contemporary fatherhood, he must confront his own biases and assumptions in order to connect with Max on a deeper level.

Ultimately, Daddy Day Camp is a heartwarming story about the power of love, redemption, and the transformative impact that one person can have on another's life.

overview: The true story of the most decorated dog in American military history -- Sgt. Stubby -- and the enduring bonds he forged with his brothers-in-arms in the trenches of World War I.
tagline: The incredible true story of America's top underdog
title: Sgt. Stubby: An American Hero
plot:
Sgt. Stubby: An American Hero is a heartwarming and inspiring film that tells the true story of Stubby, a Boston Terrier who becomes a hero during World War I. The movie explores themes of loyalty, bravery, and the unbreakable bond between humans and animals.

At its core, the film is a testament to the power of companionship and the ways in which animals can bring comfort, joy, and purpose to our lives. Stubby's story is one of remarkable resilience and adaptability, as he navigates the harsh realities of war and finds himself at the forefront of his unit.

The movie also delves into the emotional toll of war on soldiers, highlighting the struggles of those who fought alongside Stubby. The film humanizes the experiences of these soldiers, revealing their fears, hopes, and dreams, and showcasing the ways in which animals like Stubby can provide a sense of comfort and normalcy in the midst of chaos.

Furthermore, Sgt. Stubby: An American Hero celebrates the spirit of heroism and selflessness that defines our nation's history. Stubby's actions demonstrate remarkable courage and loyalty, inspiring his comrades to follow suit and ultimately earning him a place in the annals of military history.

Overall, the film is a poignant tribute to the enduring power of friendship and the incredible bond between humans and animals.

overview: Garden gnomes, Gnomeo & Juliet, recruit renown detective, Sherlock Gnomes, to investigate the mysterious disappearance of other garden ornaments.
tagline: They're on a mission to bring every gnome home.
title: Sherlock Gnomes
plot:
Sherlock Gnomes is an animated comedy film that follows the adventures of Gary Gnome and his arch-nemesis, Lord Gnorman. The movie delves into the theme of friendship and loyalty as Gary embarks on a perilous journey to rescue his beloved garden gnome wife, Gnorma.

The story also explores the idea of identity and self-discovery, as Gary navigates through a world that is both familiar and foreign. He must confront his own limitations and learn to adapt in order to save Gnorma from the clutches of Lord Gnorman.

Furthermore, the film touches on the theme of environmentalism, highlighting the importance of preserving nature and protecting the natural world from those who seek to exploit it. The movie features a cast of colorful characters, each with their own unique personalities and quirks, adding to the richness and depth of the story.

Overall, Sherlock Gnomes is a heartwarming tale that celebrates the power of friendship, loyalty, and self-discovery, all set against a vibrant and imaginative backdrop.

overview: A movie within a movie, created to spoof the martial arts genre. Writer/director Steve Oedekerk uses contemporary characters and splices them into a 1970s kung-fu film, weaving the new and old together.  As the main character, The Chosen One, Oedekerk sets off to avenge the deaths of his parents at the hands of kung-fu legend Master Pain. Along the way he encounters some strange characters.
tagline: A laugh-out-loud funny spoof!
title: Kung Pow: Enter the Fist
plot:
Kung Pow: Enter the Fist is a comedy film released in 2002, directed by David Leitch and starring Steve Oedekerk. The movie parodies classic martial arts films, particularly those of Bruce Lee.

The main themes of Kung Pow: Enter the Fist include:

1. **Satire and parody**: The film uses humor to poke fun at traditional martial arts movies, exaggerating their clichés and over-the-top action sequences.
2. **Friendship and camaraderie**: The story follows the unlikely friendship between Poet (Oedekerk), a clumsy but lovable hero, and Master Pain (Oedekerk), his nemesis-turned-ally. Their bond is central to the plot's development.
3. **Good vs. Evil**: The film features an epic battle between good and evil, with Poet and Master Pain engaging in a series of hilarious and action-packed confrontations.
4. **Self-discovery and growth**: As Poet navigates his journey, he learns valuable lessons about himself and the importance of friendship, loyalty, and embracing one's uniqueness.

The movie's tone is lighthearted and comedic, with plenty of slapstick humor, witty one-liners, and absurd situations. Overall, Kung Pow: Enter the Fist is a entertaining and irreverent take on traditional martial arts films, offering a fresh and humorous perspective on the genre.

overview: When governments fail to act on behalf of captive missionaries, ex-Green Beret John James Rambo sets aside his peaceful existence along the Salween River in a war-torn region of Thailand to take action.  Although he's still haunted by violent memories of his time as a U.S. soldier during the Vietnam War, Rambo can hardly turn his back on the aid workers who so desperately need his help.
production_companies: Equity Pictures Medienfonds GmbH & Co. KG IV
tagline: Live for nothing, or die for something.
title: Rambo
plot:
Rambo, also known as John Rambo, is a 2008 action film directed by and starring Sylvester Stallone, the fourth installment in the Rambo franchise and a sequel to Rambo III (1988). Co-written by Stallone and Art Monterastelli, it features Julie Benz, Paul Schulze, Matthew Marsden and Graham McTavish. The film was an independent production by Nu Image and Millennium Films, shot in Thailand, Mexico and the United States between January and May 2007.

During the Saffron Revolution in Burma, the brutal army officer Major Pa Tee Tint leads a campaign of terror against the Karen people, razing villages, massacring civilians, conscripting boys and enslaving women. Twenty years after his time in Afghanistan, Vietnam War veteran John Rambo lives a quiet life in northern Thailand, catching snakes and running a riverboat. A group of Christian missionaries from Colorado, led by Michael Burnett and Sarah Miller, asks him to take them up the Salween River into Burma to deliver medical aid. Rambo refuses repeatedly but is eventually persuaded by Sarah. On the way, pirates stop the boat and demand Sarah, and Rambo kills them all, horrifying the missionaries.

Shortly after he drops them off, Tint's troops attack the village, slaughter its inhabitants and capture Sarah, Michael and other survivors. Rambo is then hired to ferry a team of mercenaries, led by former SAS soldier Lewis, on a mission to rescue them. Although Lewis rejects his offer of help, Rambo follows, saving the team from a patrol with his bow before they raid Tint's camp at night and free the prisoners. Separated from the others with the young sniper School Boy and Sarah, Rambo stays ahead of their pursuers. When Lewis's group is captured and about to be executed, Rambo seizes a truck-mounted machine gun, and with the help of Karen rebels the soldiers are overwhelmed in a bloody battle. Rambo kills Tint as he tries to escape. Inspired by Sarah's words, Rambo then returns to the United States and walks up the road to his father's ranch in Bowie, Arizona.

Lionsgate and The Weinstein Company released the film in the United States on January 25, 2008. Reviews were mixed: critics praised Stallone's direction and performance, the action sequences and the score, but many objected to its extremely graphic violence and thin plot. It grossed $113.2 million worldwide against a budget of about $50 million, and was followed by Rambo: Last Blood in 2019.

overview: A haunting ghost story set against the backdrop of a busy winter sales period in a department store, following the life of a cursed dress as it passes from person to person, with devastating consequences.
tagline: A killer dress.
title: In Fabric
plot:
In Fabric is a 2018 British black comedy horror film written and directed by Peter Cosgrove. The movie follows the story of a mysterious dress that seems to have a life of its own, causing chaos and destruction in the lives of those who wear it.

The main themes of In Fabric include:

1. Consumerism and Materialism: The film critiques modern consumer culture, highlighting how people are often driven by superficial desires and material possessions. The dress serves as a symbol of this, representing the empty and fleeting nature of consumerist values.
2. Toxic Masculinity: The character of Steve, played by Paddy Considine, embodies toxic masculinity, with his aggressive and controlling behavior towards women. The film critiques this toxic dynamic, highlighting its damaging effects on relationships and individuals.
3. Feminism and Empowerment: The female characters in the film, particularly the shop assistant, serve as a counterpoint to Steve's toxic masculinity. They are strong, independent, and empowered, challenging the patriarchal norms that Steve represents.
4. Class and Social Hierarchy: The film explores the social class divisions in the town where the story takes place, highlighting the tensions between different socioeconomic groups.

The plot of In Fabric follows a series of events as the mysterious dress causes chaos and destruction, ultimately leading to a confrontation with its owner, Steve. Throughout the film, Cosgrove uses dark humor and satire to critique modern society's values and norms.

Overall, In Fabric is a thought-provoking and unsettling film that challenges viewers to think critically about the themes and issues it presents.

overview: A comedian tries to make it as a serious actor when his reality-TV star fiancé talks him into broadcasting their wedding on her TV show.
title: Top Five
plot:
Top Five is a 2014 American romantic comedy-drama written and directed by Chris Rock, who also stars, and produced by Scott Rudin and Eli Bush. Rosario Dawson and Gabrielle Union co-star, with an ensemble of comedians and actors including J. B. Smoove, Kevin Hart, Sherri Shepherd, Tracy Morgan, Cedric the Entertainer and Jerry Seinfeld. After its premiere at the 2014 Toronto International Film Festival, several studios entered a bidding war for distribution rights, which were won by Paramount Pictures; it was released in the United States on 12 December 2014.

Rock plays Andre Allen, a New York comedian and film star who is famous for a lucrative franchise in which he plays Hammy the Bear, a police officer in a bear costume. Now a recovering alcoholic, he wants to be taken seriously and is promoting Uprize, a historical drama in which he plays the Haitian revolutionary Dutty Boukman. He is also preparing for a televised wedding to his fiancée Erica Long, a reality television star played by Union. Chelsea Brown, a New York Times journalist played by Dawson, spends a day following Andre around the city to write a profile of him, even though he is wary of the newspaper, whose critic has repeatedly savaged his work.

As they travel through Manhattan, their conversation ranges over fame, race, comedy, sobriety and relationships. Andre recalls the lowest point of his life, a chaotic night in Houston years earlier that ended with his arrest and set him on the path to recovery. When their limousine is involved in an accident, the pair continue on foot, visiting his old friends and family in the neighbourhood where he grew up, and the friends debate their personal "top five" rappers of all time. Chelsea, who has secrets of her own, gradually breaks down Andre's defences, and the two begin to develop feelings for each other, forcing Andre to question both his upcoming marriage and the direction of his career.

The film draws on Rock's own experiences as a comedian and celebrity and combines sharp stand-up style humour with a reflective look at fame and authenticity.

Top Five received critical acclaim. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds an approval rating of about 85 percent, with the consensus calling it as smart, funny and trenchant as Rock's best stand-up work and a career highlight for him.

overview: When 9 first comes to life, he finds himself in a post-apocalyptic world. All humans are gone, and it is only by chance that he discovers a small community of others like him taking refuge from fearsome machines that roam the earth intent on their extinction. Despite being the neophyte of the group, 9 convinces the others that hiding will do them no good.
tagline: When our world ended their mission began.
plot:
In a post-apocalyptic world where humans have been wiped out, nine anthropomorphic toys come to life when humans are not around. The main character, Nine (voiced by Elijah Wood), is a small, blue toy with a distinctive red hand that serves as his left arm.

The story begins with the toys being created in a factory and then being sold to a young boy named Robert (voiced by James Spader). However, when Robert's mother dies, he is sent to live with his aunt and uncle, who are more interested in getting rid of him than taking care of him. The toys are left behind, but they soon discover that they have been brought to life.

As the story progresses, Nine becomes determined to find a new home for himself and his fellow toys. He sets out on a journey to find Robert's father, who he believes can help them. Along the way, Nine meets other toys, including a teddy bear named Teddy (voiced by Tom Kane), a ballerina doll named Eve (voiced by Jennifer Connelly), and a rag doll named Big Baby (voiced by John C. Reilly).

The toys face numerous challenges as they try to find their way back to Robert's father. They are pursued by a group of evil toys, led by a porcelain doll named Kate (voiced by Crispin Glover). Kate is determined to destroy the other toys and rule over the world.

As Nine and his friends journey through the post-apocalyptic landscape, they begin to realize that they have been given a second chance at life. They learn to work together and rely on each other in order to survive. Along the way, Nine also discovers more about himself and his past, including the fact that he was once part of a group of toys that were designed to be perfect.

The story takes a dramatic turn when Kate and her minions attack the toys. In the ensuing battle, Eve is killed by Kate, which sets off a chain reaction of events that ultimately leads to the downfall of Kate's army. Nine and his friends are able to defeat Kate and her followers, but not before they suffer significant losses.

In the end, Nine and his remaining friends are able to find Robert's father, who is revealed to be a kind and loving man. He takes in the toys and provides them with a new home, where they can live in peace and happiness. The story concludes with Nine reflecting on the journey he has been on and the lessons he has learned about friendship and sacrifice.

Overall, 9 is a heartwarming and action-packed film that explores themes of identity, community, and redemption. The animation is stunning, with intricate details and textures that bring the post-apocalyptic world to life. The voice cast delivers strong performances, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

overview: Remake of a 1956 Fritz Lang film in which a novelist's investigation of a dirty district attorney leads to a setup within the courtroom.
title: Beyond a Reasonable Doubt
plot:
Beyond a Reasonable Doubt is a 2009 American crime thriller written, photographed and directed by Peter Hyams, starring Jesse Metcalfe, Amber Tamblyn and Michael Douglas. A reworking of Fritz Lang's 1956 film of the same name, it was Hyams' second remake of an RKO property after Narrow Margin (1990). It opened in Spain in July 2009, ahead of a limited US release.

C.J. Nicholas, a Shreveport television reporter, made his name with an award-winning documentary about a teenage prostitute who died of an overdose. Now trying to revive his career through an investigative unit with his colleague Corey Finley, he is convinced that District Attorney Mark Hunter, a former detective with gubernatorial ambitions, owes his flawless conviction record to evidence planted at the last minute. While dating Assistant District Attorney Ella Crystal, who works for Hunter, he finds indications that Hunter's former partner, Lieutenant Merchant, plants suspects' DNA, but he cannot prove it, and budget cuts kill his unit.

Determined to expose Hunter, Nicholas sets out to frame himself for the recent murder of a prostitute. With Finley filming, he buys items tying him to the crime, holding dated newspapers to prove they were acquired after the killing. The footage is stored in Finley's desk, with a backup in a safe-deposit box. After a staged arrest he is charged with the murder, but Merchant discovers the scheme. Finley is killed in a car chase with Merchant and both videos are destroyed, so when Nicholas reveals his plan in court, he has only receipts, and Hunter persuades the jury that the victim's blood found on the planted items proves his guilt. Nicholas is sentenced to death.

Crystal investigates on her own and learns that crime-scene photographs from Hunter's cases were digitally altered. When Merchant tries to run her down, he is shot dead by a detective who had been tailing him, and Hunter is arrested in disgrace. Nicholas is freed and becomes a celebrity. Rewatching his documentary, however, Crystal recognises the hands of the supposed prostitute as those of the murder victim, and realises that Nicholas hired the woman to fake his documentary and later killed her when she tried to blackmail him. Because his case ended in a mistrial, he is not protected by double jeopardy, and she leaves as police arrive to arrest him.

The film was panned, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 7% approval, its consensus calling it a hackneyed courtroom drama with a predictable twist.

overview: In her many years as a social worker, Emily Jenkins believes she has seen it all, until she meets 10-year-old Lilith and the girl's cruel parents. Emily's worst fears are confirmed when the parents try to harm the child, and so Emily assumes custody of Lilith while she looks for a foster family. However, Emily soon finds that dark forces surround the seemingly innocent girl, and the more she tries to protect Lilith, the more horrors she encounters.
tagline: Some cases should  never be opened.
title: Case 39
plot:
Case 39 is a 2009 supernatural horror film directed by Christian Alvart and written by Ray Wright. Renée Zellweger stars as a social worker who tries to rescue a young girl from her abusive parents, with Jodelle Ferland, Bradley Cooper and Ian McShane in supporting roles. Shot in Vancouver in late 2006, the film was released in several territories in 2009 but did not reach US theaters until October 1, 2010, when Paramount Pictures distributed it.

Emily Jenkins, an overworked child services caseworker, is assigned to investigate the family of ten-year-old Lillith Sullivan, whose grades have declined and who appears estranged from her strange, withdrawn parents. Emily suspects abuse and pushes for Lillith's removal, and her fears seem confirmed when the parents are caught trying to kill the girl by shutting her inside the oven. With the help of police detective Mike Barron, Emily rescues her. The parents are committed to a psychiatric institution, and at Lillith's pleading Emily agrees to look after her until a foster family can be found.

Soon after Lillith moves in, disturbing events begin to occur. Another of Emily's young clients murders his parents after receiving a phone call from her house. Her friend, the psychologist Dr. Douglas Ames, evaluates Lillith and finds himself subtly threatened by her; that night he hallucinates hornets bursting from his body and dies in a fall. Visiting Lillith's parents, Emily learns that they believe the girl is a demon that feeds on emotions and can only be stopped while she sleeps. The parents die violently soon afterward, and Barron, after receiving one of Lillith's calls, is driven by terrifying visions to shoot himself.

With her closest allies gone and her other cases in danger, Emily drugs Lillith and sets fire to her own house, but the girl survives unharmed. While being escorted to temporary accommodation, Emily drives off a pier with Lillith in the car. Underwater, Lillith appears in her true monstrous form and tries to drag Emily down, but by overcoming her fear Emily breaks free and swims to shore as the creature sinks.

A fire destroyed the set and studio during production in October 2006, though no one was seriously injured. After lengthy delays, the film was panned by critics and grossed about $28 million worldwide against a $26 million budget.

overview: After a governor issues an executive order to arrest the children of undocumented immigrants, the detained youth are offered an opportunity to have their charges dropped by volunteering to provide care to the elderly. Once inside the elder care facility, however, they discover more twisted secrets than they could have possibly imagined.
tagline: No one escapes the daily grind.
title: American Carnage
plot:
American Carnage is a 2022 American comedy horror film directed by Diego Hallivis, who wrote it with his brother Julio Hallivis. It stars Jorge Lendeborg Jr., Jenna Ortega, Allen Maldonado and Eric Dane, with Brett Cullen as a state governor. Conceived as a satire of United States immigration politics with a message in favour of immigrant rights, it takes its title from a phrase in Donald Trump's first inaugural address. The film was released in theatres and on demand on 15 July 2022.

JP (Lendeborg), a cheerful young Latino, works a dead-end job at the local Lady Liberty's burger joint, while his sister Lily (Yumarie Morales) has won a place at Columbia University. During her celebration, agents of Immigration and Customs Enforcement raid the house. Governor Harper Finn (Cullen), seeking conservative votes for his re-election, has issued an executive order to arrest not only undocumented immigrants but also their children and JP and his sister are taken into detention. In the holding camp JP is offered a deal: if he volunteers to work as a carer at the Owl Cove retirement home, his charges will be dropped. He starts the job alongside the petty criminal Big Mac (Maldonado), the tough activist Camila (Ortega), the asthmatic conspiracy theorist Chris (Jorge Diaz) and Micah (Bella Ortiz), an Argentine who looks surprisingly white. The residents are strangely apathetic but prone to sudden fits of rage, and one elderly woman keeps trying to warn JP about something. When Chris vanishes after an escape attempt, leaving his inhaler behind, JP digs deeper. He discovers that residents and carers alike are being dosed with hormones that make their flesh tender, with the side effects of dementia and rapid ageing, so that the detainees can be ground into meat for the governor's burger chain; the old woman who tried to warn him is Lily. Micah turns out to be a plant spying on the carers. JP and his friends lead a revolt with the residents, the scheme is exposed, and Finn flees.

Reviews were mixed, with about 58% of 24 critics positive on Rotten Tomatoes. Many compared it to Get Out: Leigh Monson of The A.V. Club gave it a B, saying it falls short of that film but translates issues facing Hispanic Americans into a horror scenario well worth getting into, and Noel Murray of the Los Angeles Times called it lively and impassioned. IGN's Matt Donato found it bogged down, while German reviewers felt the shift from realistic satire to crude horror fantasy weakened it.

overview: Elsa, Anna, Kristoff and Olaf head far into the forest to learn the truth about an ancient mystery of their kingdom.
tagline: The past is not what it seems.
title: Frozen II
plot:
Frozen II is a 2019 animated musical fantasy film produced by Walt Disney Animation Studios. The movie takes place three years after the events of the first film and follows Queen Elsa, Princess Anna, Olaf, Kristoff, and Sven as they embark on a new adventure.

The story begins with Elsa experiencing strange visions that lead her to believe that an ancient magic is awakening in their kingdom of Arendelle. Believing that this magic may be connected to the mythical land of Ahtohallan, Elsa sets out on a journey to find the source of the magic and restore balance to nature.

Anna, Olaf, Kristoff, and Sven join Elsa on her quest, facing numerous challenges along the way. They encounter new characters, including the Northuldra people, who possess ancient knowledge about Ahtohallan. The group also discovers that a dark force is threatening the land, causing destruction and chaos.

As they journey deeper into the unknown, the group encounters various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, mythical creatures, and their own personal demons. Elsa struggles to control her powers, while Anna tries to support her sister and keep her safe.

Throughout the movie, the characters face difficult choices and confront their pasts. The film explores themes of identity, community, and the importance of embracing one's true nature. The music, composed by Kristen Anderson-Lopez and Robert Lopez, is a highlight of the film, featuring catchy and emotive songs that add depth to the story.

The movie features stunning animation, with breathtaking landscapes and intricate details that bring the world of Arendelle to life. The voice cast delivers strong performances, with Idina Menzel reprising her role as Elsa and Kristen Bell returning as Anna.

Overall, Frozen II is a captivating and emotionally resonant film that expands on the world and characters introduced in the first movie. While it may not be as groundbreaking as its predecessor, it offers a satisfying sequel that explores new themes and deepens our understanding of the Frozen universe.

overview: Selma, a Czech immigrant on the verge of blindness, struggles to make ends meet for herself and her son, who has inherited the same genetic disorder and will suffer the same fate without an expensive operation. When life gets too difficult, Selma learns to cope through her love of musicals, escaping life's troubles - even if just for a moment - by dreaming up little numbers to the rhythmic beats of her surroundings.
tagline: You don't need eyes to see.
title: Dancer in the Dark
plot:
Dancer in the Dark is a 2000 musical drama film written and directed by Lars von Trier. The film stars Björk as Selma Ježková, a Czech immigrant living in the United States with her pet turtle, Miko.

The story begins with Selma working at a factory that manufactures CDs for a company called Fine Line Features (not Fine Line Features, but Fine Line Features is not correct either). She is struggling to make ends meet and is deeply in debt. Despite this, she finds solace in singing along to her favorite Elvis Presley songs.

One day, Selma meets a young man named Greer Decker (played by David Morse), who becomes her love interest. However, their relationship is complicated due to Selma's financial struggles and her inability to provide for Greer. Meanwhile, Selma's debt collector, Gene (played by Peter Stormare), is relentless in his pursuit of payment.

As the story unfolds, Selma's life begins to spiral out of control. She becomes increasingly paranoid and isolated, leading to a series of tragic events that ultimately lead to her downfall. The film's plot is heavily influenced by the themes of love, loss, and redemption.

Throughout the film, von Trier employs a unique blend of music, dance, and drama to tell Selma's story. The film features several musical numbers, including "I've Seen It All" and "Love in an Elevator," which showcase Björk's impressive vocal range and acting abilities.

The film's climax is both haunting and heartbreaking, as Selma's world comes crashing down around her. In the end, Selma takes drastic action to protect herself and those she loves, leading to a tragic conclusion that has left audiences stunned and moved.

Dancer in the Dark received widespread critical acclaim upon its release, with many praising Björk's performance and von Trier's bold direction. The film is widely regarded as one of the greatest films of the 2000s, and its influence can still be seen in music videos and films today.

Overall, Dancer in the Dark is a powerful and emotional film that explores themes of love, loss, and redemption through the eyes of a complex and deeply human character.

overview: A young Spanish woman who has newly moved to Berlin finds her flirtation with a local guy turn potentially deadly as their night out with his friends reveals a dangerous secret.
tagline: One City. One Night. One Take.
title: Victoria
plot:
Victoria is a 2015 German drama film directed by Sebastian Schipper. The movie revolves around the life of a young woman named Victoria, who embarks on a journey to find her missing boyfriend after he disappears during their trip.

The main theme of Victoria is the struggle for independence and self-discovery in a patriarchal society. As Victoria navigates through the challenges she faces, she begins to assert her own identity and break free from the constraints imposed upon her by societal expectations. The film explores themes of female empowerment, resilience, and the quest for autonomy.

Throughout the movie, Victoria's journey is marked by moments of vulnerability, anger, and determination. As she confronts the harsh realities of her situation, she discovers a sense of inner strength and resourcefulness that allows her to take control of her life. The film ultimately presents a powerful portrayal of a young woman's struggle for self-discovery and independence in a world that often seeks to constrain her.

The movie also touches on themes of love, loss, and the complexities of human relationships. Victoria's relationship with her boyfriend is portrayed as intense and all-consuming, but also fraught with tension and uncertainty. As she searches for him, she begins to realize that their relationship was not as perfect as she had imagined, and that she has been living in a state of denial.

Overall, Victoria is a gripping drama that explores the complexities of female identity, independence, and relationships in a thought-provoking and emotionally charged way.

overview: Kate and her daughter Beth live alone in an isolated farmhouse in the woods, but when Kate slowly begins to suspect that something sinister is happening, her motherly instincts are put to the test.
title: Motherly
plot:
Motherly is a 2021 Canadian psychological horror thriller directed by Craig David Wallace. Lora Burke stars as Kate, a woman living in an isolated rural house with her young daughter Beth, played by Tessa Kozma, after her husband was imprisoned for the death of a little girl. The cast also includes Kristen MacCulloch and Nick Smyth as the dead girl's parents, and Colin Paradine as a local police officer.

Kate lives in seclusion with nine-year-old Beth, and a police officer named Hal stops by from time to time to check on them. Beth hopes her father Brad will come home for her ninth birthday, unaware of the full truth: two years earlier Brad was convicted of murdering Beth's young friend Courtenay, and he has since taken his own life in prison. One evening, Courtenay's parents, Lewis and Mary, break into the house. They have become convinced that the evidence against Brad never made sense and that Kate was the real killer, and it emerges that Brad and Mary had been having an affair.

The intruders hold Kate and Beth captive while they try to extract a confession, and the night spirals into violence. When Hal arrives for one of his checks, he finds Lewis on the verge of killing Kate as she admits to having framed Brad, and he shoots Lewis, only for Kate to kill Hal because he has now learned the truth. Mary overpowers Kate and tries to flee with Beth, but Kate escapes and wounds her, and Mary is finally killed by Beth with a pitchfork. In the film's final twist, Beth is revealed to be the true killer of Courtenay, a disturbed child whose crime Kate had concealed by setting up her husband. Declaring that she is avenging her father's death, Beth stabs her mother to death and walks away from the house. As the credits roll, a passing stranger notices the blood on her clothes and asks if she needs help, and Beth faintly smiles.

The film premiered at the London FrightFest Film Festival on August 26, 2021, screened at several other Canadian and international festivals and was released on video on demand by Entertainment Squad on November 16, 2021. It grossed a little over $117,000 outside North America. Critical response was positive, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting an 86% approval rating from seven reviews. Spencer Creaghan's music earned a nomination for Best Original Score at the 10th Canadian Screen Awards in 2022.

overview: Office temp Charlotte Cantilini thinks she's found Mr. Right when she starts dating gorgeous surgeon Dr. Kevin Fields. But there's a problem standing in the way of everlasting bliss: Kevin's overbearing and controlling mother, Viola. Fearing she'll lose her son's affections forever, Viola decides to break up the happy couple by becoming the world's worst mother-in-law.
production_companies: Kumar Mobiliengesellschaft mbH & Co. Projekt Nr. 1 KG
tagline: This relationship is going to be a real mother.
title: Monster-in-Law
plot:
Monster-in-Law is a 2005 romantic comedy film that explores the complexities of relationships and the challenges of navigating different personalities. The movie delves into the theme of identity, as the protagonist, Charlotte (Jennifer Lopez), struggles to balance her own desires with those of her fiancé's mother, Vivian (Jane Fonda). 

The film also touches on the idea of societal expectations and the pressure to conform to certain norms. Vivian, a formidable and manipulative matriarch, embodies the traditional feminine ideal, while Charlotte represents a more modern and independent woman. As their relationship evolves, the two women engage in a battle of wills, with each trying to outmaneuver the other.

Furthermore, Monster-in-Law examines the theme of love and acceptance, highlighting the importance of understanding and embracing one's partner's flaws and imperfections. Through Charlotte's journey, the movie shows that true love requires compromise, empathy, and a willingness to accept the other person for who they are.

Ultimately, the film presents a nuanced portrayal of relationships, revealing that the key to happiness lies in finding a balance between individuality and unity, as well as embracing the complexities and imperfections that make each person unique.

overview: After the elevators at a New York City skyscraper begin inexplicably malfunctioning, putting its passengers at risk, mechanic Mark Newman and reporter Jennifer Evans begin separate investigations. Newman gets resistance from superiors at his company, which manufactured the elevator, while additional elevator incidents cause several gruesome deaths. The police get involved and suspect that terrorists are responsible, but a far stranger explanation looms.
tagline: YOUR NEXT STOP... IS HELL.
title: Down
plot:
Down, retitled The Shaft for its American release, is a 2001 English-language Dutch science fiction horror film written and directed by Dick Maas. James Marshall, Naomi Watts and Eric Thal star, with Michael Ironside, Edward Herrmann, Dan Hedaya and Ron Perlman in supporting roles. It is a remake of Maas's own 1983 Dutch-language film The Lift. Filming took place mainly in the Netherlands, with brief exterior shoots in New York City and Washington, D.C.

In New York, a lightning strike hits the Millennium Building, a 102-storey skyscraper with dozens of elevators, and its three express elevators start behaving strangely. The next day, a car carrying a group of pregnant women stalls between floors and rapidly overheats, sending them to hospital. Jennifer Evans, an ambitious tabloid reporter, is assigned to cover the incident. Mark Newman, a repairman and former Marine, and his colleague Jeff McClellan, technicians for the elevator company, inspect the system and find nothing wrong, with Jeff insisting that the computer controlling the elevators is flawless.

The incidents soon turn deadly. A blind man and his guide dog vanish in the building; a security guard is decapitated when his head is trapped between closing doors; and other occupants die in increasingly grisly ways. The building's owners and the elevator company's executives, worried about lawsuits and bad publicity, deny there is a problem, but Mark becomes convinced that the elevators are acting with intent. Teaming up with Jennifer, who sees a major story, he investigates and uncovers evidence of a secret experiment involving organic material in the elevator's control system, a discovery that puts them in danger from both the machine and the people who want the truth covered up.

Down premiered in 2001 but received a limited release, and reviews were mostly negative. Rotten Tomatoes reported a 20 percent approval rating based on a small number of reviews, with critics faulting its weak storyline, unrealistic deaths, dialogue and special effects. Dutch critics were also largely unfavorable. The film was released in the same year as Watts's breakthrough role in Mulholland Drive.

overview: After his father, an assassin, is brutally murdered, Nick Gant vows revenge on Division, the covert government agency that dabbles in psychic warfare and experimental drugs. Hiding in Hong Kong's underworld, Nick assembles a band of rogue psychics dedicated to destroying Division. Together with Cassie, a teenage clairvoyant, Nick goes in search of a missing girl and a stolen suitcase that could be the key to accomplishing their mutual goal.
tagline: One push can change everything.
title: Push
plot:
Push (2009) is a science fiction thriller film directed by Paul McGuigan, produced by Icon Productions, and released by Summit Entertainment.

The main themes of Push (2009) include:

1. **Superhuman Abilities**: The movie explores the concept of superhuman abilities, also known as "superpowers," which are granted to certain individuals through a mysterious process. These powers can be both beneficial and detrimental, leading to conflicts between those with abilities and those without.
2. **Government Control and Experimentation**: The film delves into the theme of government control and experimentation on individuals with superhuman abilities. The main characters, including Nick Gant (Chris Evans) and Butcher Barnaby (Dustin Hoffman), are part of a secret program designed to harness and control these powers for military purposes.
3. **Free Will vs. Control**: As the story unfolds, the characters must navigate their own free will versus the attempts by the government to control them. This theme is particularly evident in Nick's struggles with his ability to teleport short distances.
4. **Identity and Self-Discovery**: The movie follows the journey of its protagonist, Nick Gant, as he tries to understand his powers and find his place in the world. His experiences lead him to question his identity and sense of self.
5. **Redemption and Sacrifice**: Throughout the film, characters are faced with difficult choices that require them to make sacrifices for the greater good. This theme is particularly evident in Butcher Barnaby's character arc, as he grapples with his own morality and the consequences of his actions.

Overall, Push (2009) explores complex themes that delve into the human condition, free will, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control.

overview: Master car thieves square off against French gangsters in the South of France with money, women and lives all on the line.
title: Overdrive
plot:
Overdrive is a 2017 American action thriller film directed by Antonio Negret and written by Chris Bremner. The movie stars Luke Evans, Anton Yelchin, and Bryce Dallas Howard.

The main theme of Overdrive revolves around the struggle for power and control in a corrupt and decaying society. The story takes place in a dystopian Los Angeles where a group of truckers, led by Bob (Luke Evans), are forced to work for a ruthless crime lord, Gabe Wilkins (Anton Yelchin). As Bob's crew becomes increasingly disillusioned with their situation, they hatch a plan to take down Wilkins and his empire.

Throughout the film, the theme of rebellion against oppressive authority is explored. The truckers, who are initially seen as outcasts and marginalized individuals, rise up against their oppressors and fight for their rights. However, this struggle also raises questions about the morality of violence and the consequences of taking the law into one's own hands.

Another significant theme in Overdrive is the exploration of masculinity and toxic male culture. The film portrays a world where men are expected to be tough, aggressive, and dominant, but also vulnerable and sensitive. Bob, in particular, struggles with his own identity and sense of purpose, as he navigates the complexities of leadership and loyalty.

The movie also touches on themes of class struggle, economic inequality, and the effects of systemic corruption on individuals and communities. The decaying infrastructure and crumbling social services in Los Angeles serve as a backdrop for the story, highlighting the consequences of neglecting the needs of the most vulnerable members of society.

Overall, Overdrive is a gripping action thriller that explores complex themes and ideas through its engaging storyline and memorable characters.

overview: The Theory of Everything is the extraordinary story of one of the world’s greatest living minds, the renowned astrophysicist Stephen Hawking, who falls deeply in love with fellow Cambridge student Jane Wilde.
tagline: His Mind Changed Our World. Her Love Changed His.
title: The Theory of Everything
plot:
The Theory of Everything is a 2014 British biographical romantic drama film directed by James Marsh, based on the memoir "Travelling to Infinity: My Life with Stephen" by Jane Hawking. The film stars Eddie Redmayne as Stephen Hawking and Felicity Jones as Jane Hawking.

The film begins in 1962, where we meet Stephen Hawking (Eddie Redmayne), a young and ambitious physics student at the University of Cambridge. He meets Jane (Felicity Jones), a graduate student in English literature, and they begin a romantic relationship. Despite their differences, they fall deeply in love.

As Stephen's academic career flourishes, he is diagnosed with a motor neuron disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). The doctors give him only a few years to live, but Stephen defies the odds and continues his research, using a speech-generating device to communicate. Jane becomes his primary caregiver, supporting him through the challenges of living with a debilitating illness.

As Stephen's condition worsens, he becomes increasingly dependent on Jane for daily tasks, including dressing, eating, and even using the bathroom. Despite these limitations, Stephen remains intellectually active, continuing to work on his groundbreaking research in cosmology and theoretical physics.

The film takes us through the highs and lows of their relationship, as they face the challenges of Stephen's illness together. Jane becomes not only his caregiver but also his partner in every sense, supporting him through the darkest moments of his life. The film showcases the deep love and devotion that Jane has for Stephen, even when he is unable to communicate or respond.

As the years pass, Stephen's fame grows, and he becomes a household name. He writes several bestselling books, including "A Brief History of Time," which cements his status as one of the world's leading physicists.
