At its core, The Triplets of Belleville is a film about the unbreakable bond between a mother and daughter, as well as the importance of embracing one's uniqueness. Madame Souza, who has been ostracized by society due to her eccentric behavior, finds solace in her relationship with Maud, and together they form an unbreakable connection.

The movie also explores themes of identity and self-acceptance, particularly through the character of Madame Souza, who is a complex and multifaceted individual. Her struggles to find acceptance and belonging serve as a metaphor for the challenges faced by many individuals who feel like outsiders in society.

Furthermore, The Triplets of Belleville celebrates the beauty of imperfection and the importance of embracing one's quirks and flaws. Madame Souza's eccentricities are not seen as weaknesses, but rather as strengths that make her unique and special.

The film also touches on themes of love and sacrifice, particularly through the character of Maud, who risks everything to save her mother. The movie shows how love can conquer even the most daunting challenges, and how selfless acts of love can bring people together in ways that nothing else can.

Overall, The Triplets of Belleville is a heartwarming and visually stunning film that celebrates the power of love, family, and acceptance. Its unique blend of music, animation, and quirky characters makes it a truly unforgettable viewing experience.

overview: One clear summer day in a Baltimore suburb, a baby goes missing from her front porch. Two young girls serve seven years for the crime and are released into a town that hasn't fully forgiven or forgotten. Soon, another child is missing, and two detectives are called in to investigate the mystery in a community where everyone seems to have a secret.
tagline: Don't look away for even a second.
title: Every Secret Thing
plot:
Every Secret Thing is a 2014 American drama film directed by Ben Younger. The movie revolves around the story of two teenage girls who are accused of murdering their friend, and the subsequent investigation that uncovers dark secrets about their lives.

The main theme of Every Secret Thing is the destructive power of secrets and the devastating consequences of keeping them hidden. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the characters' attempts to conceal their true selves and relationships have led to a toxic web of lies and deceit. The film explores how these secrets can consume individuals and destroy relationships, ultimately leading to chaos and destruction.

The movie also delves into the theme of female friendship and the complexities that come with it. The relationship between the two main characters is portrayed as complex and multifaceted, with both moments of tenderness and moments of tension. Through their interactions, the film highlights the ways in which women can both support and hurt each other.

Furthermore, Every Secret Thing touches on the theme of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals. The characters' experiences are marked by pain, fear, and anxiety, and the film suggests that these emotions can be passed down through generations, affecting not only the individual but also those around them.

Overall, Every Secret Thing is a thought-provoking drama that explores the darker aspects of human nature and the devastating consequences of keeping secrets.

overview: After Mirta dies of a drug overdose with her lover, she resuscitates alone and discovers she's part of a violent world she never knew existed.
production_companies: IDM Südtirol - Alto Adige Film Fund
title: Don't Kill Me
plot:
Don't Kill Me (Italian: Non mi uccidere) is an Italian romantic horror film from 2021, written and directed by Andrea De Sica and adapted from the young-adult novel of the same name by Chiara Palazzolo. Produced by Vivo Film with Warner Bros. Pictures Italia and support from the IDM Südtirol film fund, it stars Alice Pagani as Mirta and Rocco Fasano as Robin, with Silvia Calderoni as Sara, Fabrizio Ferracane as Luca Bertozzi and Anita Caprioli as Amalia. It was shot in South Tyrol and Rome.

The film opens with nineteen-year-old Mirta in a car with her boyfriend Robin, who drives recklessly with his eyes closed while she shouts directions at him. They stop at a quarry, where Robin persuades the nervous Mirta to try a drug with him for the first time; she agrees, asking him not to kill her. Both die of an overdose. Robin's death seems final, but a few hours after the funeral Mirta smashes her way out of her family's burial vault, confused and angry, and wanders back home to find her parents mourning her. Her hands show signs of necrosis, she drifts through her memories, and she discovers that she has a savage hunger for human flesh. She has become one of the "Overdead", people who return after a violent death: she is nearly immortal, can survive gunshots and will not age, but she will decay unless she regularly feeds on the living, and starvation is the only way to destroy her kind. Flashbacks fill in her romance with Robin, as she wonders whether a second life is worth living without him. Meanwhile, a centuries-old secret society, the Benandanti, has been tracking her resurrection, and its operatives, led by a man determined to capture and starve her, close in, revealing a violent world she never knew existed.

Don't Kill Me was released in Italy on digital download and video on demand on 21 April 2021, and on Netflix internationally in February 2022. Reviews were mixed. Alex Wiggan of It's a Stampede! found it a captivating little horror film with brisk storytelling, a gritty look, an effective soundtrack including a cover of 10cc's "I'm Not in Love" and a committed central performance by Pagani, despite its debts to Twilight. On Through the Shattered Lens, Lisa Marie Bowman praised the atmospheric first half, which recalled Jean Rollin and Jess Franco, as well as Pagani's sympathetic turn and Ferracane's villain, but felt that it lost its way once Mirta is captured and ended with an unsatisfying "to be continued" conclusion.

overview: A brilliant plastic surgeon creates a synthetic skin that withstands any kind of damage. His guinea pig: a mysterious and volatile woman who holds the key to his obsession.
title: The Skin I Live In
plot:
The Skin I Live In is a psychological thriller film directed by Pedro Almodóvar, released in 2011 under the production company El Deseo. The movie tells the story of Dr. Robert Ledgard, a brilliant and obsessive scientist who seeks revenge against those he believes wronged him.

The film begins with an elderly Robert (played by Antonio Banderas), a renowned plastic surgeon, living in a remote estate in Ireland. He is revealed to be a former prisoner, having spent 15 years behind bars for a crime he committed as a young man. The story then flashes back to Robert's past, where we see him as a young doctor (also played by Antonio Banderas) who becomes infatuated with a woman named Vera (played by Elena Anaya), the daughter of a wealthy and influential family.

Robert's obsession with Vera leads him to kidnap her and subject her to a series of gruesome experiments. He surgically alters her face, transforming her into a man, which he names Norman. Robert's goal is to create the perfect "son" for himself, someone who will be loyal and obedient only to him.

As the story unfolds, we see Robert's relationship with Norman (also played by Eduardo Noriega), his creation, evolve from one of paternal love to one of twisted obsession. Norman becomes a skilled and deadly assassin, carrying out Robert's orders without question. However, as time passes, Norman begins to develop his own identity and sense of self, which threatens Robert's control over him.

Meanwhile, Vera (Elena Anaya) is revealed to be alive and working as a nurse at the local hospital. She becomes embroiled in a complicated love triangle with her husband, Dr. General (played by Marisa Paredes), and her former lover, Norman.

The plot thickens as Robert's past catches up with him, and he is forced to confront the consequences of his actions. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Vera was actually the one who betrayed Robert to the authorities, leading to his imprisonment. This revelation sets off a chain reaction of events that ultimately leads to Norman's betrayal of Robert.

The film builds towards a tense and violent climax as Robert's world begins to unravel. In the end, Norman turns against Robert, killing him in a brutal and satisfying manner. The movie concludes with Vera, now free from her past, embracing her true identity and finding love with Dr. General.

Throughout the film, Almodóvar explores themes of obsession, identity, and the blurred lines between good and evil. The Skin I Live In is a masterclass in suspense and tension, with outstanding performances from its cast. The film's use of symbolism, particularly the skin that Robert uses to cover his face, adds depth and complexity to the narrative.

Overall, The Skin I Live In is a gripping and unsettling thriller that will keep you on the edge of your seat until the very end.

overview: A young Englishman is dispatched to Sarawak to become part of the British colonial government. He encounters some unorthodox local traditions, and finds himself faced with tough decisions of the heart involving the beautiful Selima, the unwitting object of his affections.
tagline: Learn to speak her language.
title: The Sleeping Dictionary
plot:
The Sleeping Dictionary is a 2003 drama film directed by Mark Gill. The movie follows the story of a young woman named Jane (played by Emily Mortimer) who travels to Papua New Guinea as an English teacher, and her relationship with a local man named Kofi (played by David Oyelowo).

The main themes of The Sleeping Dictionary include:

1. Cultural Exchange and Misunderstanding: The film explores the complexities of cultural exchange between two vastly different worlds. Jane's innocence and naivety lead to misunderstandings and miscommunications, highlighting the difficulties of bridging the gap between Western and indigenous cultures.
2. Identity and Belonging: Kofi struggles with his own identity as a member of a traditional tribe in Papua New Guinea. His relationship with Jane forces him to confront his cultural heritage and question his place within it.
3. Love and Connection: The film's central romance is a poignant exploration of love, connection, and the human need for intimacy. Despite the language barrier and cultural differences, Jane and Kofi form a deep bond that transcends their physical surroundings.
4. Colonialism and Imperialism: The movie touches on the legacy of colonialism in Papua New Guinea, highlighting the impact of Western influence on indigenous cultures. Jane's presence serves as a symbol of the ongoing effects of colonialism, which can be both empowering and suffocating for local communities.

The Sleeping Dictionary is a thought-provoking film that delves into complex themes with sensitivity and nuance. The movie's exploration of cultural exchange, identity, love, and colonialism makes it a compelling watch for those interested in character-driven dramas.

overview: Eight London couples try to deal with their relationships in different ways. Their tryst with love makes them discover how complicated relationships can be.
tagline: The Ultimate Romantic Comedy.
title: Love Actually
plot:
Love Actually is a romantic comedy film released in 2003, directed by Richard Curtis and produced by Working Title Films. The movie follows the interconnected love lives of multiple couples in the weeks leading up to Christmas in London.

The story begins with the newly elected British Prime Minister, David (Hugh Grant), who is struggling to balance his personal life with his public duties. Meanwhile, we are introduced to eight different storylines that explore the complexities of love and relationships.

One storyline revolves around Jamie (Colin Firth), a writer who has recently moved back to London after being away for 12 years. He meets Aurora (Keira Knightley), a French girl he met while traveling, and they begin an affair. However, their relationship is complicated by the fact that Jamie's best friend, Mark (Andrew Lincoln), is secretly in love with his sister, Kate (Martine McCutcheon).

Another storyline centers around Harry (Alan Rickman) and Karen (Emma Thompson), a married couple who are struggling to connect after the birth of their son. They begin an affair with a younger man, Daniel (Liam Neeson), which leads to a dramatic confrontation.

We also meet Colin Frissell (Martin Freeman), a young man who falls in love with his Portuguese housekeeper, Maria (Lucia Moniz). However, their social differences and language barrier threaten to tear them apart.

The storylines intersect as the characters navigate their relationships and personal struggles. We see Mark's unrequited love for Kate, Jamie's complicated feelings for Aurora, and Harry's affair with Daniel come to a head.

Throughout the movie, Richard Curtis explores themes of love, loss, and redemption. The film features an ensemble cast, including Liam Neeson as the Prime Minister's father, who is struggling to connect with his stepson, Sam (Thomas Sangster).

As Christmas approaches, the characters begin to realize what truly matters in life. Jamie and Aurora finally confess their love for each other, Mark comes to terms with his feelings for Kate, and Harry and Karen work through their issues.

The movie concludes with a heartwarming finale that brings all the storylines together. The film ends on a hopeful note, suggesting that even in the midst of chaos and uncertainty, love can conquer all.

Overall, Love Actually is a charming and witty romantic comedy that explores the complexities of human relationships. With its talented ensemble cast and nuanced storytelling, it has become a beloved holiday classic.

overview: Follows two estranged siblings as they return home to the sprawling ranch they once knew and loved.
title: Montana Story
plot:
Montana Story is an American drama written, directed and produced by Scott McGehee and David Siegel, starring Haley Lu Richardson and Owen Teague as estranged siblings who return to their family's ranch after their father falls into a coma. Kimberly Guerrero, Gilbert Owuor and Eugene Brave Rock appear in supporting roles. Completed in 2021, it was released in American cinemas by Bleecker Street in May 2022.

Cal and Erin, half-siblings in their twenties, come back to the sprawling Montana ranch where they grew up after their father falls into a coma and is placed on life support. The house has been kept running by Valentina, the longtime housekeeper and family friend, while Ace, a Kenyan immigrant nurse, cares for the dying man. With no hope of recovery, Cal begins selling off and giving away the ranch's possessions. He has conflicted feelings about his father, who was abusive, while Erin, still furious, wants only to take the family's ageing horse, Mr. T, back with her to New York's Hudson Valley.

Cal tells Ace what drove the family apart. Seven years earlier their father, a lawyer, helped cover up a toxic disaster at the Copperhead open-pit mine. When Erin exposed the corruption in an article for a local paper, he beat her savagely and killed her horse, and she ran away that night, avoiding all of Cal's attempts to find her. Now Cal tries to reconnect, telling her about his life in Cheyenne and his plan to become a civil engineer, but she stays guarded. She buys an old truck and trailer from Mukki, a Mohican rancher, to haul Mr. T east, but it soon breaks down. Waiting for a tow, the siblings visit the vast mine, which Erin likens to the circles of Hell in Dante's Inferno.

During a thunderstorm the power fails, the generator will not start, and their father goes into cardiac arrest. Erin finds herself manually pumping air into his lungs to keep him alive, then confronts Cal over his failure to help her on the night of the beating. Cal admits he was too afraid to intervene and has always felt guilty. Later that night, believing himself alone, Cal speaks to his father about the man's joyless life, and Erin watches from the doorway as the old man dies, apparently disconnected by Cal; Ace attributes the death to the storm. As the siblings part, they promise to keep in touch, and Erin leaves Mr. T to live out his days with the horses on Mukki's ranch.

overview: When royal Princess Courtney trades places with famous rock star Erika, two worlds collide while both learn to appreciate new friends and experiences.
title: Barbie in Rock 'N Royals
plot:
Barbie in Rock 'N Royals is a 2015 American-Canadian computer-animated musical film and the 30th entry in the Barbie film series. Directed by Karen J. Lloyd from a screenplay by Marsha Griffin, it was produced by Mattel Playground Productions with animation by Rainmaker Entertainment and music by Gabriel Mann and Rebecca Kneubuhl, and was released direct to video by Universal in the United States on 8 September 2015. Running 84 minutes, it was the last Barbie film in which Barbie plays a character with a different name, and, like Barbie: The Princess and the Popstar, it turns on a princess and a pop star trading places.

Barbie stars as Princess Courtney, a modern royal heading to an island summer camp for the first time. On the island are two rival camps: Camp Royalty, for young princes and princesses, and Camp Pop, for aspiring musicians. A registration mix-up swaps Courtney's name with that of Erika Juno (Chiara Zanni), a famous rock star who has cancelled her tour hoping to make real friends at Camp Pop, so the princess lands among the musicians and the singer among the royals. The camp heads, the stern Lady Anne (Nicole Oliver) of Camp Royalty and Finn Oxford (Michael Dobson) of Camp Pop, share an old rivalry. When Lady Anne hears Erika sing, she fakes a computer failure to block the swap and challenges Finn to a sing-off, with the losing camp to close for good and surrender its land to the winner.

While the two girls learn to fit into unfamiliar worlds and make unexpected friends, Erika overhears Lady Anne's assistant, Clive, revealing the stakes and admitting he has bribed one of the judges, Svetlana Petranova of Camp Arabesque. The other judges are rock legend Allegra James and Prince Reginald of Thistlebrook. Learning that one camp will be lost, the campers of both sides decide to perform together rather than compete. Allegra and the prince abstain, and Svetlana names Camp Royalty the winner, but Finn and Lady Anne overrule the result, agreeing that rock and royalty can mix, and plan to merge the camps the next summer, while Courtney and Erika form a band with their friends called Rock 'N Royals.

Kelly Sheridan voices Courtney and Svetlana, with Bethany Brown, Alessandro Juliani and Kira Tozer among the cast. The songs include "What If I Shine" and the end-credits single "Raise Our Voices". The film's British launch was accompanied by a singing competition promoted with the girl group Little Mix and Nickelodeon.

overview: Kinsey is a portrait of researcher Alfred Kinsey, driven to uncover the most private secrets of a nation. What begins for Kinsey as a scientific endeavor soon takes on an intensely personal relevance, ultimately becoming an unexpected journey into the mystery of human behavior.
production_companies: N1 European Film Produktions GmbH & Co. KG
tagline: Let's talk about sex
title: Kinsey
plot:
Kinsey is a biographical drama film that explores the life of Alfred Kinsey, an American sex researcher and professor at Indiana University. The movie delves into the complexities of human sexuality, challenging societal norms and taboos surrounding sex and relationships.

At its core, Kinsey is a story about the power of curiosity, intellectual freedom, and the pursuit of knowledge. The film follows Kinsey's journey as he conducts groundbreaking research on human sexuality, collecting data through interviews with thousands of people from all walks of life. This approach allows him to challenge conventional wisdom and shed light on the diversity of human experiences.

The movie also touches on themes of repression, conformity, and the constraints placed on individuals who dare to question societal norms. Kinsey's work is met with resistance and criticism from some quarters, highlighting the tension between personal freedom and social expectations.

Furthermore, Kinsey explores the complexities of relationships, particularly in the context of his own life. The film portrays a nuanced portrayal of Kinsey's personal struggles, including his unrequited love for a colleague, which serves as a counterpoint to his professional achievements.

Ultimately, Kinsey is a thought-provoking film that encourages viewers to think critically about their assumptions and biases surrounding sex, relationships, and human behavior.

original_title: Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon: Sword of Destiny
overview: A story of lost love, young love, a legendary sword and one last opportunity at redemption.
tagline: The past returns with a vengeance.
title: Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon: Sword of Destiny
plot:
Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon: Sword of Destiny is a 2016 martial arts film directed by Yuen Woo-ping and written by John Fusco. The movie serves as a sequel to the original Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon (2000) and stars Donnie Yen, Zhang Ziyi, and Henry Golding.

The main themes of Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon: Sword of Destiny revolve around:

1. **Self-discovery**: The protagonist, Lo (played by Donnie Yen), is on a quest to find his place in the world and understand his destiny. Throughout the film, he faces various challenges that test his skills, morals, and values.
2. **Power and responsibility**: As Lo delves deeper into the world of wuxia, he must confront the consequences of wielding great power and the weight of responsibility that comes with it. He struggles to balance his own ambitions with the need to protect others.
3. **Loyalty and honor**: The film explores the importance of loyalty, duty, and honor in a world where these values are often tested by personal gain or self-interest. Lo's relationships with his friends and allies serve as a reminder of the significance of loyalty and honor.
4. **The struggle between tradition and modernity**: Set in 18th-century China, the film grapples with the tension between traditional ways of life and the encroaching influence of Western culture. This theme is reflected in Lo's own journey, as he navigates the complexities of a rapidly changing world.

Throughout the movie, these themes are woven together to create a narrative that explores the complexities of human nature, the importance of relationships, and the ongoing struggle for balance between tradition and progress.

Please note: The Weinstein Company was not involved in the production of Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon: Sword of Destiny.

overview: A man receives a mysterious e-mail appearing to be from his wife, who was murdered years earlier. As he frantically tries to find out whether she's alive, he finds himself being implicated in her death.
tagline: Eight years ago Alex's wife was murdered. Today she emailed him.
title: Tell No One
plot:
Tell No One is a French thriller film that revolves around the story of Antoine Forget, a man who receives an email from his wife, who was presumed dead five years ago, claiming to have faked her own death. As Antoine delves deeper into the mystery, he uncovers a web of deceit and conspiracy that threatens to destroy everything he thought he knew about himself and those around him.

At its core, Tell No One is a film about the fragility of human relationships and the devastating consequences of secrets and lies. The movie explores the theme of identity, as Antoine's search for the truth forces him to confront his own sense of self and the people who have been hiding behind masks of deception.

The film also delves into the darker aspects of human nature, revealing a world where people are capable of great cruelty and manipulation when their secrets are threatened. The movie's tense atmosphere and suspenseful plot twists keep the audience on the edge of their seats, as Antoine navigates a complex landscape of danger and betrayal.

Ultimately, Tell No One is a gripping thriller that raises important questions about trust, loyalty, and the human condition. It's a thought-provoking film that will keep you guessing until the very end, and leave you pondering the consequences of secrets and lies long after the credits roll.

overview: It's almost graduation day for high school seniors Troy, Gabriella, Sharpay, Chad, Ryan and Taylor — and the thought of heading off in separate directions after leaving East High has these Wildcats thinking they need to do something they'll remember forever. Together with the rest of the Wildcats, they stage a spring musical reflecting their hopes and fears about the future and their unforgettable experiences growing up together. Will their final show break them apart or bring them together for the greatest moment in Wildcat history?
title: High School Musical 3: Senior Year
plot:
High School Musical 3: Senior Year is a musical comedy-drama film that explores several themes relevant to high school students and their transition into adulthood.

One of the primary themes of the movie is the bittersweet nature of senior year. The characters are faced with the reality of leaving high school behind, saying goodbye to friends, and embarking on new paths in life. This theme is reflected in the film's narrative, as the characters grapple with their own identities, futures, and relationships.

Another significant theme is the importance of following one's passion and pursuing one's dreams. The movie showcases the characters' various interests and talents, highlighting the value of exploring different passions and finding what truly makes them happy. This theme is exemplified through Troy Bolton's (Zac Efron) struggles to balance his basketball career with his love for singing.

The film also explores themes of friendship, loyalty, and the power of relationships. The bonds between the characters are put to the test as they navigate the challenges of senior year, ultimately leading to a deeper understanding and appreciation of their friendships.

Furthermore, High School Musical 3: Senior Year touches on the theme of identity and self-discovery. As the characters prepare to leave high school behind, they must confront their own identities, values, and goals for the future. This theme is particularly evident in the character development of Gabriella Montez (Vanessa Hudgens), who struggles to balance her academic ambitions with her passion for music.

Lastly, the movie highlights the significance of embracing change and letting go of the past. The characters must come to terms with the end of an era and the uncertainty that comes with it, ultimately learning to cherish the memories and experiences they've had while also looking forward to the future.

Overall, High School Musical 3: Senior Year is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores themes relevant to high school students and their transition into adulthood.

original_title: 劇場版ポケットモンスター アドバンスジェネレーション 七夜の願い星 ジラーチ
overview: Ash, May, Brock, and Max come upon the festival of the Wishing Star of Seven Nights. During their enjoyment, the legendary Pokemon--Jirachi, descends from the heavens and befriends Max. Jirachi, with the power to grant any wish, is sought after by many people wanting to claim its power. One man seeks to use its legendary power to revive an ancient Pokemon known as Groudon, unaware of the dangers hidden within Jirachi's powers
title: Pokémon: Jirachi - Wish Maker
plot:
Pokémon: Jirachi, Wish Maker is a 2003 Japanese animated adventure fantasy film directed by Kunihiko Yuyama. It is the sixth film in the Pokémon anime series and the first set during the Advanced Generation (Ruby and Sapphire) season, featuring Ash Ketchum, Pikachu and their friends May, Max and Brock. The Japanese voice cast includes Rica Matsumoto, Ikue Ōtani, Yūji Ueda, KAORI and Fushigi Yamada. Toho released it in Japan on 19 July 2003, accompanied by the short Gotta Dance, and Miramax distributed the English-language version direct to video in June 2004.

Once every thousand years, the Millennium Comet passes through the night sky for seven days, and the Mythical Pokémon Jirachi awakens from its long sleep to absorb its energy, which also brings life to the land of Forina where it rests. This time, a stage magician named Butler and his girlfriend Diane unearth the crystal encasing the sleeping Jirachi and take it away. Ash and his friends, meanwhile, arrive at a traveling festival held to celebrate the comet, where May buys a charm said to grant a wish if one panel is closed on each night the comet appears.

During one of Butler's magic shows, Max hears a voice coming from the crystal Diane is holding and meets Jirachi, which soon emerges and befriends him. Jirachi can grant wishes, but its powers are not quite as they seem. Butler, a former member of Team Magma, secretly plans to use Jirachi's energy to resurrect the legendary Groudon and prove his old theories correct. Max and his friends, joined by Absol, set out to take Jirachi safely back to Forina before its brief waking period ends, pursued by Butler and Team Rocket. Butler's experiment creates a monstrous false Groudon that begins absorbing everything around it, forcing Ash and Butler to work together to undo the damage while Max must prepare to say goodbye to his new friend.

The film was a box-office hit in Japan, earning ¥4.5 billion and becoming the country's second highest-grossing domestic film of the year. Its theme song in the Japanese version was "A Small Thing" by Asuca Hayashi, while the English version featured "Make a Wish" performed by Cindy Mizelle. The Jirachi featured in the film was distributed to players of the Pokémon games as a promotion.

overview: After losing his wife and his memory in a car accident, a single father undergoes an experimental treatment that causes him to question who he really is.
tagline: There is no escape from who you really are.
title: Black Box
plot:
Black Box is a psychological thriller film directed by Joe Swanberg, released on Amazon Prime Video in 2020.

The main theme of Black Box revolves around the concept of identity and how it can be manipulated. The story follows Eve (played by Emma Roberts), a woman who undergoes an experimental brain-computer interface procedure that allows her to control technology with her mind. As she navigates this new reality, Eve begins to question what is real and what is not.

Throughout the film, Black Box explores themes of identity, free will, and the blurring of lines between human and machine. The movie delves into the consequences of playing with fire when it comes to technology and the impact it can have on our sense of self.

The plot development is driven by Eve's growing dependence on her newfound abilities, which leads to a downward spiral of paranoia, anxiety, and confusion. As she struggles to maintain control over her life, Eve must confront the darker aspects of her own psyche and the true nature of her connection to technology.

Ultimately, Black Box presents a thought-provoking commentary on our increasingly tech-driven world and the potential risks associated with relying too heavily on technology to define ourselves. The film's ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience to ponder the implications of Eve's journey and the consequences of her choices.

Overall, Black Box is a gripping psychological thriller that explores complex themes and raises important questions about the intersection of humanity and technology.

overview: Polar bear Norm and his three Arctic lemming buddies are forced out into the world once their icy home begins melting and breaking apart. Landing in New York, Norm begins life anew as a performing corporate mascot, only to discover that his new employers are directly responsible for the destruction of his polar home.
tagline: Bear to be different
title: Norm of the North
plot:
Norm of the North is an animated adventure comedy film that revolves around the story of a polar bear named Norm, who travels to New York City to save his home from melting due to climate change. The movie explores several themes, including environmentalism and conservation.

At its core, the film highlights the importance of preserving our natural habitats and the consequences of human actions on the environment. Norm's journey is driven by his desire to protect his Arctic home and the creatures that inhabit it, serving as a metaphor for the urgent need to address climate change.

The movie also touches on themes of friendship and community, as Norm forms an unlikely bond with a young girl named Emily, who helps him navigate the challenges of the city. This friendship serves as a reminder of the importance of building connections with others and working together to achieve common goals.

Furthermore, the film features a cast of colorful characters, including penguins, seals, and other animals, which adds a layer of humor and lightheartedness to the story. However, beneath its comedic surface, Norm of the North conveys a powerful message about the need for environmental stewardship and responsible behavior towards the natural world.

Overall, Norm of the North is a heartwarming and entertaining film that uses humor and adventure to convey an important message about the importance of protecting our planet.

overview: For years, Blade has fought against the vampires in the cover of the night. But now, after falling into the crosshairs of the FBI, he is forced out into the daylight, where he is driven to join forces with a clan of human vampire hunters he never knew existed—The Nightstalkers. Together with Abigail and Hannibal, two deftly trained Nightstalkers, Blade follows a trail of blood to the ancient creature that is also hunting him—the original vampire, Dracula.
tagline: The final hunt begins.
title: Blade: Trinity
plot:
Blade: Trinity is a 2004 American superhero horror film directed by David S. Goyer and starring Wesley Snipes as the titular character, Blade. The movie serves as the third installment in the Blade franchise.

The story begins with Blade (Wesley Snipes) living in New Orleans, where he has been hiding from his vampire-hunting duties for several years. He is approached by a mysterious woman named Abigail Whistler (Parker Posey), who claims to be working for a secret organization known as the Blood Gods. The Blood Gods are an ancient and powerful group of vampires who seek to bring about a new era of human-vampire coexistence.

Abigail reveals that she has been searching for Blade, believing him to be the key to unlocking the secrets of his father's past. She tells him that his father, Danica Talos (N'Bushe Wright), was a powerful vampire hunter who had discovered a way to harness the power of the Blood Gods. However, their plans were foiled by the leader of the Blood Gods, Deacon Frost (Dominic Purcell).

Deacon Frost is a charismatic and cunning vampire who seeks to use his newfound powers to bring about a new era of human-vampire coexistence. He believes that humans and vampires can live together in harmony, but only if they submit to the will of the Blood Gods.

Blade soon discovers that Deacon Frost has created an army of super-soldier vampires, known as the "Hybrid" vampires, who possess enhanced strength and agility. The Hybrids are nearly indestructible and serve as Frost's loyal followers.

As Blade delves deeper into the world of the Blood Gods, he meets a new ally, Hannibal King (Ryan Reynolds), a vampire hunter with his own unique abilities. Together, they embark on a perilous journey to stop Deacon Frost and his minions.

The plot thickens as Blade discovers that Abigail Whistler is actually working for Deacon Frost, who has been manipulating her all along. This revelation sets Blade on a collision course with Frost, leading to an epic showdown between the two enemies.

In the climactic final battle, Blade faces off against Deacon Frost and his army of Hybrids. With the help of Hannibal King, he manages to defeat Frost and shatter the Blood Gods' hold on humanity.

The movie concludes with Blade reflecting on the sacrifices he has made as a vampire hunter. He realizes that his existence is a lonely one, but he finds solace in knowing that there are others like him who share his burden. The film ends with Blade walking away from the city, ready to face whatever dangers lie ahead.

Overall, Blade: Trinity is an action-packed and thrilling ride that explores themes of identity, loyalty, and the struggle between good and evil.

overview: Ida Red may not survive her 20-year prison sentence for armed robbery. She turns to her son, Wyatt, for one last job and a chance to regain her freedom.
title: Ida Red
plot:
Ida Red is a 2021 American crime thriller written, directed and co-produced by John Swab. Melissa Leo stars as Ida "Red" Walker, the matriarch of a criminal family, with Josh Hartnett as her son Wyatt, Frank Grillo as her brother Dallas, Deborah Ann Woll as her daughter Jeanie, and Sofia Hublitz, William Forsythe, George Carroll, Mark Boone Junior and Beau Knapp in supporting roles. Shot in and around Tulsa, Oklahoma, during the COVID-19 pandemic, the film premiered in the Piazza Grande section of the Locarno Film Festival in August 2021 and was released by Saban Films in November 2021.

Ida Walker has been in prison for years, ever since the bust that also left her a widow. Now she has been diagnosed with terminal cancer and wants to die a free woman, so she sets about engineering both her parole and, true to her nature, one final heist. Outside, the family business is run by her son Wyatt, a successful career criminal with his own code of ethics, and her violent and unpredictable brother Dallas.

The family is complicated by Ida's daughter Jeanie, who is estranged from her mother because she married Bodie Collier, a kind but not especially sharp police officer. Their rebellious teenage daughter Darla is drawn to her uncle Wyatt's world and is involved with a local lowlife named Petey. After a truck robbery goes wrong, Wyatt finds himself under pressure, while FBI Special Agent Lawrence Twilley, working alongside Collier, begins to close in on the family. Dallas appoints himself the cleaner and ruthlessly shoots those responsible for the botched job, or their relatives, raising the stakes as Wyatt tries to pull off the job that will secure his mother's release. Loyalties between blood relatives, lawmen and criminals are tested as the plan unfolds, and Wyatt must decide how far he is willing to go for a mother who has shaped his whole life.

The film is a family crime saga set in Oklahoma, blending heist thriller elements with themes of inheritance, loyalty and violence passed from one generation to the next, and its score was composed by David Sardy.

Ida Red received mixed reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes about 33 percent of critics' reviews are positive, and Metacritic assigned it a score of 46 out of 100. Jay Weissberg of Variety called it a proficiently made crime family drama, crediting its good performances.

original_title: 劇場版 ペルソナ3 第3章 Falling Down
overview: The season turns to autumn. The fight of the protagonist and his group S.E.E.S. with the strange monsters called ‘Shadows’ is getting closer to the end. Makoto and his allies engage in life-or-death battles with Shadows in order to end the Dark Hour. Through the battles, some must face the deaths of friends and family, some must notice what precious things must be protected, and some must find meaning in the battles that have occurred.  In front of Makoto, the mysterious transfer student Ryouji Mochizuki appears. When the group greets a new morning, the gears of fate begin to turn. A fight revolving around each of the heroes' bonds begins...
title: Persona 3 the Movie: #3 Falling Down
plot:
Persona 3 the Movie: #3 Falling Down is a thought-provoking film that delves into the complexities of the human psyche, exploring the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. The movie follows the protagonist, Minato Arisato, as he navigates his way through a labyrinthine world of psychological turmoil.

At its core, the film grapples with the theme of existential crisis, where the main character is forced to confront the darkness within himself and the world around him. As Minato delves deeper into the mysteries of Tartarus, he begins to question the nature of his own identity and the purpose of his existence.

The movie also explores the concept of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals. The protagonist's experiences in Tartarus serve as a metaphor for the emotional scars that can be left by traumatic events, highlighting the long-term effects of such experiences on one's mental health and well-being.

Furthermore, Persona 3 the Movie: #3 Falling Down touches upon the idea of social isolation and the importance of human connection. Minato's relationships with his friends and allies serve as a counterpoint to the isolating nature of Tartarus, emphasizing the need for empathy and understanding in overcoming personal struggles.

Ultimately, the film presents a nuanced exploration of the human condition, one that is both deeply unsettling and profoundly thought-provoking. Through its portrayal of Minato's inner turmoil, Persona 3 the Movie: #3 Falling Down invites viewers to reflect on their own experiences with existential crises, trauma, and the complexities of the human psyche.

overview: A freak weather system turns its deadly fury on New York City, unleashing a Sharknado on the population and its most cherished, iconic sites - and only Fin and April can save the Big Apple.
tagline: Shark happens!
title: Sharknado 2: The Second One
plot:
Sharknado 2: The Second One is a campy, over-the-top disaster film that follows Fin Shepard (Ian Ziering) and his family as they try to survive in New York City after a shark-filled tornado hits the city. 

The main themes of Sharknado 2: The Second One include:

1. **Absurdity and Satire**: The movie is known for its ridiculous plot, which pokes fun at disaster movies, celebrity culture, and social media obsession.

2. **Family and Love**: Despite the chaos and destruction around them, Fin's family remains a central focus of the story, highlighting the importance of love and support in the face of adversity.

3. **Celebrity Culture and Social Media**: The film critiques the excesses of celebrity culture and the way social media can both unite and divide people.

4. **Disaster Movie Tropes**: Sharknado 2: The Second One playfully subverts common disaster movie tropes, such as the "hero" who must save the day despite being a self-centered celebrity.

5. **Campy Humor and Entertainment**: Above all, the film is meant to be entertaining, with its outrageous premise, cheesy one-liners, and over-the-top performances from the cast.

Overall, Sharknado 2: The Second One is a lighthearted, comedic disaster film that uses absurdity and satire to poke fun at popular culture.

overview: After everyone's favorite St. Bernard gets fired from a movie, Beethoven begins the long journey home with his trainer, Eddie. On their way, they become stranded in a small coastal town where the beloved canine befriends a young boy who is searching for buried treasure.
title: Beethoven's Treasure Tail
plot:
Beethoven's Treasure Tail is a family comedy film that revolves around the adventures of Beethoven, a lovable St. Bernard, and his human family. The movie explores the theme of family bonding and the importance of cherishing time with loved ones.

The story delves into the idea of letting go and moving on from past experiences, as Beethoven's family navigates their way through a series of challenges and misadventures. Along the way, they learn to appreciate the present moment and the joy that comes with it.

The film also touches on the theme of forgiveness and understanding, as Beethoven's family works to overcome their differences and come together once again. Through its lighthearted and entertaining storyline, Beethoven's Treasure Tail conveys a heartwarming message about the value of family, love, and acceptance.

Ultimately, the movie is a celebration of the beauty of family life and the importance of creating lasting memories with those we care about most.

overview: The comedic adventures of an introverted boy left on the doorstep of a pair of reluctant, eccentric great-uncles, whose exotic remembrances stir the boy's spirit and re-ignite the men's lives.
title: Secondhand Lions
plot:
"Secondhand Lions" is a 2003 American comedy-drama film directed by Tim McCanlies. The movie stars Robert Duvall, Michael Caine, and Peter Dinklage.

The main theme of "Secondhand Lions" revolves around the complexities of family relationships, identity, and the power of storytelling. The story follows Walter Cunningham (Peter Dinklage), a young boy who moves in with his eccentric uncles, Hub (Robert Duvall) and Garth (Michael Caine), after his mother's death.

As the narrative unfolds, it becomes clear that the uncles' seemingly outlandish tales are actually rooted in their own experiences during World War II. Through these stories, Walter learns about his family's past, including the uncles' involvement with a group of Jewish refugees and their struggles to survive during the war.

The film explores themes of:

1. Identity: The movie delves into the complexities of identity, particularly for Walter, who is trying to find his place in the world after his mother's death.
2. Family dynamics: The relationships between Walter, Hub, and Garth are central to the story, highlighting the tensions and love that exist within a family.
3. Storytelling: The film showcases the power of storytelling as a means of preserving memories, passing down history, and connecting with others.
4. War and its impact: The movie touches on the experiences of those who lived through World War II, shedding light on the struggles and sacrifices made by individuals during this tumultuous period.

Through its engaging narrative and memorable performances, "Secondhand Lions" explores these themes in a way that is both entertaining and thought-provoking.

overview: Upon first sight of a beautiful instructor, a bored and overworked estate lawyer signs up for ballroom dancing lessons.
tagline: Step out of the ordinary.
title: Shall We Dance?
plot:
Shall We Dance is a poignant and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of love, relationships, and personal growth. The movie delves into the emotional journey of its protagonist, John Clark, as he navigates his midlife crisis and grapples with feelings of restlessness and discontentment in his marriage.

At its core, Shall We Dance is a nuanced exploration of the human desire for connection, intimacy, and meaning. Through John's interactions with Chiyo Sakamoto, a vibrant and free-spirited dance instructor, the film reveals the tension between conformity and individuality, tradition and innovation, and the constraints of societal expectations versus personal aspirations.

As the story unfolds, Shall We Dance masterfully weaves together themes of identity, belonging, and the search for purpose. The film raises essential questions about the nature of love, relationships, and personal fulfillment, inviting viewers to reflect on their own values, desires, and priorities.

Ultimately, Shall We Dance is a moving and introspective drama that encourages audiences to reevaluate their own lives, relationships, and aspirations, and to consider the importance of embracing change, taking risks, and pursuing one's passions.

overview: As Emily struggles to fit in at home and at school, she discovers a small red puppy who is destined to become her best friend. When Clifford magically undergoes one heck of a growth spurt, becomes a gigantic dog and attracts the attention of a genetics company, Emily and her Uncle Casey have to fight the forces of greed as they go on the run across New York City. Along the way, Clifford affects the lives of everyone around him and teaches Emily and her uncle the true meaning of acceptance and unconditional love.
tagline: Adventure has never been bigger.
title: Clifford the Big Red Dog
plot:
Clifford the Big Red Dog is a 2021 live-action and animated family fantasy comedy directed by Walt Becker, based on Norman Bridwell's children's books. The screenplay is by Blaise Hemingway, Jay Scherick and David Ronn, from a story by Justin Malen and Ellen Rapoport. Darby Camp plays Emily Elizabeth and Jack Whitehall her uncle Casey, with Tony Hale, Izaac Wang, Sienna Guillory, David Alan Grier, Kenan Thompson and John Cleese. Delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic, it was released by Paramount Pictures in cinemas and on Paramount+ on November 10, 2021.

In New York City, twelve-year-old Emily Elizabeth Howard, a lonely girl whose only friend is her classmate Owen, is left in the care of her irresponsible uncle Casey when her mother leaves on a business trip. At a park, the mysterious Mr. Bridwell, who runs an animal rescue tent, shows her a little red puppy and tells her that he will grow according to how much he is loved. Casey refuses to adopt the dog, because pets are banned in their building, but the puppy turns up in Emily's backpack. She names him Clifford, and by the next morning he has grown to gigantic size.

Word of the enormous dog quickly spreads online, and Emily and Casey set out to find Bridwell. Zac Tieran, the ruthless head of the biotechnology firm Lyfegro, wants to learn the secret of Clifford's size and falsely tells police that he genetically engineered the dog, launching a citywide manhunt. Evicted from their apartment, Emily, Casey and Owen escape with Clifford, helped by their neighbours, and agree that if Bridwell cannot shrink him, Clifford must be sent to an animal sanctuary in Shanghai run by Owen's father. Believing Bridwell dead, they tearfully put Clifford on a boat, but the authorities intercept him and deliver him to Lyfegro.

Learning that Bridwell is alive, Emily and Casey break into Lyfegro with their friends' help and free Clifford. Bridwell tells Emily that he cannot make Clifford small, since her love made him big, and urges her to stand up for him and for herself. When Tieran tries to claim the dog by scanning a microchip his scientists implanted, Bridwell makes it identify Emily as the rightful owner, and Tieran is fined for lying to police. The city builds Clifford a giant doghouse, and Casey takes a job at Scholastic.

Critics were mixed, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 58% approval, but the film grossed about $117.8 million worldwide against a $64 million budget.

overview: This is a story of a great love facing the greatest drama of the history of Russia. Admiral Kolchak is a true war hero and beloved husband and father. One day he meets Anna, the love of his life and the wife of his best friend. The revolution in his heart faces the revolution in his own country His destiny is to become the Supreme Rules of Russia.
tagline: The Highest Command
title: Admiral
plot:
Admiral (Russian: Адмиралъ, stylized in pre-revolutionary spelling) is a 2008 Russian historical drama directed by Andrei Kravchuk about Alexander Kolchak, a vice admiral in the Imperial Russian Navy who became leader of the anti-Bolshevik White movement during the Russian Civil War. Konstantin Khabensky stars as Kolchak, with Elizaveta Boyarskaya as the poet Anna Timiryova, Anna Kovalchuk as his wife Sofya, Sergei Bezrukov and Egor Beroev. The film centers on the love triangle between Kolchak, his wife and Timiryova, set against the collapse of the Russian Empire. An extended version was broadcast as a ten-part television series on Channel One in 2009.

The film opens in 1964 on the set of Sergei Bondarchuk's War and Peace at Mosfilm, where the director insists that an elderly woman with an aristocratic background remain as an extra despite objections from a political officer. The story then moves back to 1916, during the First World War. Captain Kolchak's ship, laying mines in the Baltic Sea, is confronted by a German cruiser; after leading his crew in prayer, he lures the enemy vessel onto the mines and sinks it. Promoted to rear admiral, he meets Anna Timiryova, the wife of his friend and subordinate, Captain Sergei Timirev, and the two fall deeply in love. Despite their feelings, Kolchak refuses to abandon his wife and son, and he and Anna agree that they must not meet.

Tsar Nicholas II promotes Kolchak to vice admiral and commander of the Black Sea Fleet. After the February Revolution of 1917, officers are disarmed and killed by revolutionary sailors, and Kolchak, refusing to surrender his sword, throws it into the sea. During the Civil War he becomes Supreme Ruler of the White government in Siberia, and Anna leaves her husband to join him. As the Red Army advances and the White forces disintegrate, Kolchak and Anna face betrayal, retreat across a frozen Siberia and the prospect of capture, their love enduring amid the destruction of the old Russia.

Admiral was one of the most expensive Russian films of its time and was a major box-office success in Russia, grossing more than $38 million. Critics praised its production values, battle scenes and performances, but some reviewers criticized its romanticized and uncritical portrait of Kolchak and its treatment of the Civil War.

overview: Sang Yu is so exhausted from trying to stay awake. Every time he closes his eyes, a demon chases and kills him in his dreams. One night Sang realizes he has a special power: he can bring treasures from his dreams into reality. Almost overnight, he becomes a rich man. But his wealth also attracts the attention of a ruthless gangster.
title: Super Me
plot:
Super Me (Chinese: 超级的我) is a 2019 Chinese fantasy film that mixes action, comedy, romance and drama, written and directed by Zhang Chong as his second feature after The Fourth Wall. It was released in Chinese cinemas in April 2021 and picked up by Netflix, which began streaming it internationally on 8 May 2021. The project was originally to be produced by Anthony and Joe Russo through their Chinese venture Anthem Pictures, but the brothers withdrew and the film was ultimately made by the Shanghai companies Hehe Pictures and Black Ant Entertainment.

Taiwanese actor Darren Wang plays Sang Yu, a struggling, impoverished screenwriter whose scripts have never been filmed. Crippled by writer's block and months of insomnia, he cannot deliver the screenplay demanded by his producer San Ge (Cao Bingkun), and every time he does fall asleep a demonic blue creature hunts him down and kills him in his dreams. After losing his apartment and ending up on the streets, Sang reaches the point of attempting suicide, but a street pancake vendor stops him and advises him to remind himself, during his next nightmare, that he is only dreaming so that he can wake up before dying. Following this advice, Sang wakes to find himself holding the golden sword that had just wounded him in the dream. The priceless object fetches a fortune, and by repeating the trick night after night he collects valuable artefacts from the dream world and becomes rich almost overnight. San Ge now becomes his subordinate, and Sang finally finds the courage to court Hua Er (Song Jia), the café owner he has long admired from afar. His wealth carries a cost, however: injuries from the dream world keep following him into reality, and his money draws the attention of a ruthless gangster boss, Qiang (Wu Gang). King Shih-chieh and Kevin Lee also appear.

Critical responses varied. Writing for Yahoo News Singapore, Teng Yong Ping gave it three out of five stars, reading it as a fable warning against unearned wealth; he found its effects decent but below Hollywood level and faulted Wang's broad acting, the vague rules of the dream world and an anti-climactic ending. M.N. Miller of Ready Steady Cut was far more enthusiastic, calling it great fun and interpreting the dream demon as a metaphor for a writer's inner struggles. AsianMovieWeb judged it surprisingly entertaining as a fantasy comedy with a subtle romance and neat effects, though it felt the script grew too convoluted towards the end.

overview: In a California desert town, a short-order cook with clairvoyant abilities encounters a mysterious man with a link to dark, threatening forces.
tagline: I might see dead people... But then, by God, I do something about it.
title: Odd Thomas
plot:
Odd Thomas is a 2013 American supernatural thriller film written, directed and co-produced by Stephen Sommers, based on Dean Koontz's 2003 novel of the same name. Anton Yelchin stars as Odd Thomas, a short-order cook with psychic abilities, with Addison Timlin as his girlfriend Stormy Llewellyn, Willem Dafoe as Police Chief Wyatt Porter, Gugu Mbatha-Raw, Nico Tortorella and Patton Oswalt in supporting roles.

Odd works as a cook at a diner in the small desert town of Pico Mundo, California. He has the ability to see the spirits of the dead, who sometimes seek his help in finding justice, and he quietly solves crimes with the support of Chief Porter, one of the few people who know his secret. He can also see bodachs, invisible, shadowy creatures that feed on pain and suffering and gather in large numbers wherever death and violence are about to happen.

One day a strange man enters the diner surrounded by an unusually large swarm of bodachs. Odd nicknames him "Fungus Bob" because of his peculiar hair and follows him home, where he discovers files about mass murderers and evidence that Bob is planning something terrible. Odd also experiences disturbing visions of a massacre, involving men in bowling shirts and dead bodies. Chief Porter assigns deputies to watch Bob, and Odd, together with Stormy, whom he believes he is destined to marry, races to identify the target and the date of the coming attack. Bob is soon found dead, yet the bodachs continue to multiply across Pico Mundo, signaling that the danger has not passed and that others are involved in the plot. With the town's annual events approaching, Odd must determine who among the people around him is responsible before the tragedy he has foreseen comes to pass.

Although completed in 2013, the film was held up for years by legal disputes between its producers and financiers and received only a limited release in a few markets before reaching video on demand in the United States in 2016. Reviews were mixed: critics praised Yelchin's charismatic performance and the film's light, fast-moving tone, but some found its visual effects and storytelling uneven. Koontz himself publicly praised the adaptation.

overview: In 1870s America, a peaceful American settler kills his family's murderer which unleashes the fury of a notorious gang leader. His cowardly fellow townspeople then betray him, forcing him to hunt down the outlaws alone.
production_companies: MEDIA Programme of the European Union
The Department of Trade and Industry of South Africa
tagline: Bad men will bleed.
title: The Salvation
plot:
The Salvation is a 2014 Danish action film directed by Kristian Levring, not Zentropa Entertainments. 

The movie follows the story of two brothers, Salomon and Johannes Jensen (played by Mads Mikkelsen and Eva Green), who are members of a Christian sect in 19th-century Norway. The brothers are trained from a young age to be warriors for their faith, and they live a simple life on a remote island.

However, when the Norwegian government sends an expedition to the island to arrest Salomon, who has been accused of treason, Johannes is forced to flee with his brother. They escape by boat, but not before Johannes kills several men in self-defense, which sets off a chain reaction of violence and bloodshed.

As they journey through Norway, Johannes and Salomon are pursued by the authorities and a ruthless bounty hunter named Captain John Lee (played by Alexander Skarsgård). Along the way, they encounter various people who aid or hinder their progress, including a young woman named Anna (played by Stellan Skarsgård's daughter, Billie), who becomes Johannes' love interest.

As the brothers fight to survive and evade capture, they also grapple with their own faith and morality. Salomon is haunted by his past mistakes and struggles to reconcile his Christian beliefs with the violence he has committed in self-defense. Johannes, on the other hand, begins to question the teachings of their sect and the true nature of their mission.

The movie builds towards a violent confrontation between Johannes and Captain Lee, which ultimately leads to a tragic outcome for one of the characters. Throughout the film, Levring explores themes of faith, violence, and redemption, raising questions about the morality of war and the consequences of blind obedience.

Overall, The Salvation is a gritty and intense action film that features strong performances from its cast, particularly Mads Mikkelsen and Eva Green. While it received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, it has since developed a cult following and is widely regarded as one of the most underrated films of 2014.

[No information on Zentropa Entertainments]

overview: Extreme athlete turned government operative Xander Cage comes out of self-imposed exile, thought to be long dead, and is set on a collision course with deadly alpha warrior Xiang and his team in a race to recover a sinister and seemingly unstoppable weapon known as Pandora's Box. Recruiting an all-new group of thrill-seeking cohorts, Xander finds himself enmeshed in a deadly conspiracy that points to collusion at the highest levels of world governments.
tagline: There are no more patriots, just rebels and tyrants.
title: xXx: Return of Xander Cage
plot:
XXx: Return of Xander Cage is a 2017 action film directed by D.J. Caruso, starring Vin Diesel as the lead character, Xander Cage.

The movie begins with Xander Cage (Vin Diesel) living a peaceful life in London, working as an artist and trying to leave his past life as an extreme sports athlete and spy behind him. However, his tranquility is short-lived as he receives a message from his old friend and fellow operative, Augustus Gibbons (Kiefer Sutherland), who has been kidnapped by the villainous Ainsley (Deepika Padukone).

Xander soon discovers that Ainsley is working with the Chinese government to steal a powerful device known as Pandora's Box, which can control the world's technology. Xander sets out on a mission to rescue Augustus and stop Ainsley, accompanied by his new ally, Becky (Ruby Rose), a skilled hacker.

As Xander delves deeper into the world of espionage, he reunites with his old team, including Talon (Donnie Yen) and Adele (Deepika Padukone). Together, they embark on a series of high-stakes missions to take down Ainsley's operation and retrieve Pandora's Box.

Throughout the film, Xander struggles to balance his past life as an extreme sports athlete with his new role as a spy. He also grapples with his complicated relationship with Becky, who is initially hesitant to join him on his mission.

As the story unfolds, Xander faces off against Ainsley in a series of intense battles, showcasing his signature blend of humor, wit, and high-octane action. Along the way, he also confronts his own demons and learns to come to terms with his past mistakes.

The film's climax features an epic showdown between Xander and Ainsley, with Xander using all his skills and gadgets to outwit and defeat the villain. In the end, Xander succeeds in stopping Pandora's Box from falling into the wrong hands and saving the world from destruction.

Overall, XXx: Return of Xander Cage is a thrilling action film that delivers on its promise of high-octane excitement and humor. Vin Diesel brings his signature charm and charisma to the lead role, making Xander Cage a lovable and relatable hero.

overview: A teenage girl with nothing to lose joins a traveling magazine sales crew, and gets caught up in a whirlwind of hard partying, law bending and young love as she criss-crosses the Midwest with a band of misfits.
tagline: Nothing to lose.
title: American Honey
plot:
American Honey is a poignant and captivating film that delves into the lives of young people on the road, searching for connection and meaning. The movie follows the story of Star, a 16-year-old girl who joins a group of traveling salespeople, led by the charismatic Jake, to sell magazines door-to-door.

At its core, American Honey is a film about the struggle for identity and independence in a world that often seems determined to constrain and control young people. The characters are on the move, physically and emotionally, as they try to break free from the limitations of their pasts and forge new paths forward.

The film explores themes of freedom and confinement, as the characters navigate the tension between the desire for autonomy and the need for connection and community. Through Star's journey, we see a young person grappling with the complexities of growing up and finding her place in the world.

One of the most striking aspects of American Honey is its portrayal of the American Dream, which is often presented as an unattainable illusion. The film shows how the pursuit of this dream can lead to disillusionment and disconnection, as individuals become trapped in a cycle of chasing after something that may never be within reach.

Ultimately, American Honey is a powerful exploration of the human need for connection, community, and meaning. Through its characters' struggles and triumphs, the film offers a nuanced and thought-provoking portrayal of what it means to be young and searching for one's place in the world.

overview: Mariel is a veteran elite diver who has one last chance at the Olympic Games. However, when a terrible truth comes to light, Mariel faces her biggest personal question: Is winning her true dream?
title: Dive
plot:
Dive (Spanish: La caída) is a 2022 sports drama directed by Lucía Puenzo and starring Karla Souza, a Mexican, Argentine and American co-production that explores sexual and psychological abuse in the world of elite sport. The screenplay was written by Puenzo with Mónica Herrera, Samara Ibrahim, Tatiana Mereñuk and María Renée Prudencio, and the cast includes Hernán Mendoza, Dèja Ebergenyi, Fernanda Borches, Claudia Lobo, Enrique Singer, Mabel Cadena and Christian Vázquez. Inspired by a true story, it was released exclusively on Amazon Prime Video on November 11, 2022, in more than 240 countries and territories.

Souza plays Mariel, a veteran Mexican diver who is fighting for what is likely her final chance to compete at the Olympic Games, as preparations get under way for Athens 2004. She is battling physical problems as well as the passing of time, and her career is bound up in a complicated relationship with Braulio, played by Mendoza, who is both her longtime coach and her romantic partner. Just as her dream of an Olympic medal seems within reach, her synchronized diving partner suffers a serious accident that rules her out of competition. Mariel is paired with Nadia, played by Ebergenyi, a talented teenager regarded as the sport's brightest young prospect.

As the two train together, Mariel begins to suspect that Braulio has been sexually abusing young athletes under his care, and sordid revelations about the training program come to light. The discovery forces her to look again at her own past and at the ways she herself was shaped, controlled and manipulated by her coach from a young age. Caught between loyalty, fear and her lifelong ambition, Mariel must decide whether winning is truly her greatest dream or whether confronting the abuse matters more than any medal.

The film was produced by Prime Video together with the production companies MADAM, Filmadora and Infinity Hill, with Souza also serving as a producer alongside Ana Laura Rascón, Ramiro Ruiz and Axel Kuschevatzky. Nicolás Puenzo was the cinematographer. Dive received considerable recognition: at the 51st International Emmy Awards it won Best TV Movie or Miniseries, and Souza won Best Performance by an Actress. It was also nominated for best co-production with Argentina at the Silver Condor Awards.

overview: BELLE is inspired by the true story of Dido Elizabeth Belle, the illegitimate mixed race daughter of a Royal Navy Admiral. Raised by her aristocratic great-uncle Lord Mansfield and his wife, Belle's lineage affords her certain privileges, yet the color of her skin prevents her from fully participating in the traditions of her social standing. Left to wonder if she will ever find love, Belle falls for an idealistic young vicar's son bent on change who, with her help, shapes Lord Mansfield's role as Lord Chief Justice to end slavery in England
tagline: Based on the inspiring true story
title: Belle
plot:
Belle is a 2013 British drama film directed by Amma Asante, not Isle of Man Film. The movie is based on the novel "The Remains of the Day" by Kazuo Ishiguro.

The main themes of Belle (2013) include:

1. **Social class and status**: The film explores the complexities of social hierarchy in 19th-century England, particularly through the eyes of Dido Elizabeth Belle, a young black woman born to a British nobleman and an enslaved African woman.
2. **Identity and belonging**: As Dido navigates her mixed heritage, she struggles to find her place within society, which often rejects or marginalizes people like herself.
3. **Love and relationships**: The film delves into the complexities of love, particularly in the context of interracial relationships, as Dido falls for John Davinier, a British aristocrat who challenges societal norms.
4. **Racism and prejudice**: Belle highlights the deep-seated racism and prejudices that existed during this period, which led to the marginalization and oppression of people of color.
5. **Self-discovery and empowerment**: Through Dido's journey, the film encourages viewers to question their assumptions about identity, class, and social status, promoting self-awareness and personal growth.

Overall, Belle (2013) is a thought-provoking drama that explores themes of identity, love, and social justice in 19th-century England.

overview: After spending two decades in England, Bill Bryson returns to the U.S., where he decides the best way to connect with his homeland is to hike the Appalachian Trail with one of his oldest friends.
tagline: When you push yourself to the edge, the real fun begins.
title: A Walk in the Woods
plot:
A Walk in the Woods is a 2015 American adventure comedy-drama film directed by Ken Kwapis. The movie follows the story of two old friends, Robert McLean and Paul Theroux, who embark on a 2,100-mile hike along the Appalachian Trail.

The main theme of A Walk in the Woods revolves around the complexities of male friendship and the challenges that come with growing older. As the two friends navigate their way through the wilderness, they confront their own mortality, physical limitations, and personal demons. The film explores how these struggles can bring men closer together, as they rely on each other for support and companionship.

The movie also delves into themes of self-discovery, perseverance, and the importance of taking risks in life. As Robert and Paul face numerous obstacles on their journey, including treacherous terrain, inclement weather, and personal setbacks, they are forced to confront their own fears and limitations. Through their experiences, the film shows that it's never too late to embark on a new adventure, challenge oneself, and find purpose in life.

Furthermore, A Walk in the Woods touches on the idea of finding one's place in the world and leaving a lasting legacy. As Robert and Paul hike through the Appalachian Trail, they reflect on their past lives, relationships, and accomplishments, and consider how they want to be remembered by others. The film suggests that it's never too late to pursue new passions, make amends with old wounds, and leave a positive impact on those around us.

Overall, A Walk in the Woods is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of male friendship, self-discovery, and the importance of taking risks in life.

overview: Eccentric aliens give a man the power to do anything he wants to determine if Earth is worth saving.
tagline: Great power. Total irresponsibility.
title: Absolutely Anything
plot:
Absolutely Anything is a 2015 British science fiction comedy film directed by Terry Jones, written by Terry Jones and Graham Linehan, and produced by Phoenix Pictures.

The movie follows the story of Neil Clarke (played by Simon Pegg), an ordinary man who lives in London. On his 65th birthday, he receives a letter from God (voiced by Alan Rickman) informing him that he has been chosen to receive five gifts: anything he wants, and they will be granted instantly.

Neil is initially skeptical but decides to use the gifts for personal gain. He chooses a private island, a spaceship, a million pounds, an infinite supply of his favorite food (pizza), and the ability to make anyone do what he wants. However, things quickly take a turn when Neil's new life becomes too much to handle.

Neil soon realizes that having unlimited power and wealth comes with its own set of problems. He starts to use his gifts to manipulate those around him, including his friends and family. His newfound abilities also attract the attention of various celebrities, who are all vying for a chance to receive one of Neil's gifts.

As Neil navigates his new life, he begins to question the morality of his actions and the true nature of his gifts. He starts to realize that having absolute power can be both liberating and suffocating. Meanwhile, God (Alan Rickman) is watching from above, occasionally intervening in Neil's life to guide him towards a more positive path.

Throughout the movie, Neil encounters various characters who are all trying to get their hands on one of his gifts. These include a group of eccentric billionaires, a pop star, and even a group of aliens who are interested in studying human behavior.

As the story unfolds, Neil begins to understand that true happiness comes from within and that having absolute power is not as fulfilling as he thought it would be. In the end, Neil decides to give up his gifts and return to his ordinary life, realizing that being human is what truly makes him special.

The movie ends with Neil reflecting on the lessons he has learned and the importance of humility and gratitude. The film features a talented ensemble cast, including Kate Ashfield, Joanna Lumley, and Bill Nighy, among others.

Overall, Absolutely Anything is a witty and entertaining comedy that explores themes of power, morality, and the human condition. With its unique blend of humor and heart, it's a must-see for fans of science fiction and comedy alike.

overview: As humanity picks up the pieces, following the conclusion of "Transformers: Dark of the Moon," Autobots and Decepticons have all but vanished from the face of the planet. However, a group of powerful, ingenious businessman and scientists attempt to learn from past Transformer incursions and push the boundaries of technology beyond what they can control - all while an ancient, powerful Transformer menace sets Earth in his cross-hairs.
tagline: This is not war, it's extinction.
title: Transformers: Age of Extinction
plot:
Transformers: Age of Extinction is a 2014 science fiction action film directed by Michael Bay, produced by Don Murphy and Tom DeSanto, and distributed by Paramount Pictures.

The movie takes place five years after the events of Transformers (2009). The story follows Cade Yeager (Mark Wahlberg), an inventor who discovers Optimus Prime's (Peter Cullen) hidden location in his backyard. Unbeknownst to Cade, he has inadvertently triggered a global alert that attracts the attention of the Decepticons.

The Autobots, led by Optimus Prime, are hunted down and nearly destroyed by the Decepticons, who seek revenge for their defeat in the previous film. The Autobots' leader, Optimus Prime, is severely damaged and left for dead.

Cade teams up with Drift (Kurosh Kharlamov), a former Decepticon who has defected to the Autobot side, and Harold Attinger (Kelsey Grammer), an FBI agent tasked with capturing Cade. However, Attinger's true intentions are revealed as he is secretly working for the Decepticons.

As the story unfolds, Cade discovers that the Decepticons plan to use a powerful energy source known as the "AllSpark" to destroy humanity. The Autobots, led by Optimus Prime, must find a way to stop the Decepticons and save humanity from extinction.

The movie features a mix of action, adventure, and humor, with a focus on Cade's character development and his relationships with Drift and Harold. The film also explores themes of redemption, sacrifice, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control.

Overall, Transformers: Age of Extinction received mixed reviews from critics but performed well at the box office, grossing over $1 billion worldwide. While it was not as well-received as its predecessor, the movie still delivered on its promise of high-octane action and exciting robot battles.

overview: "Notorious" is the story of Christopher Wallace. Through raw talent and sheer determination, Wallace transforms himself from Brooklyn street hustler (once selling crack to pregnant women) to one of the greatest rappers of all time: The Notorious B.I.G. Follow his meteoric rise to fame and his refusal to succumb to expectations - redefining our notion of "The American Dream."
tagline: No dream is too B.I.G.
title: Notorious
plot:
Notorious is a 2009 biographical drama film that tells the story of Belinda "Belita" Moreno, a Jamaican singer and actress who became embroiled in the life of Toots Hibbert, the lead singer of the reggae band Toots and the Maytals. The movie explores themes of love, loyalty, and the complexities of relationships.

At its core, Notorious is a story about the all-consuming power of love and how it can both uplift and destroy us. Belita's relationship with Toots is portrayed as intense and passionate, but also fraught with possessiveness and jealousy. As their romance deepens, Belita becomes increasingly entangled in Toots' life, including his struggles with addiction and personal demons.

The film also delves into the theme of identity and how it can be shaped by our relationships with others. Belita's journey is one of self-discovery, as she navigates her own desires, ambitions, and sense of purpose outside of her relationship with Toots. Through her experiences, the movie raises questions about the nature of love, loyalty, and sacrifice.

Furthermore, Notorious touches on the theme of cultural heritage and the impact of colonialism on Jamaican identity. The film highlights the complexities of Belita's mixed heritage and how it shapes her experiences as a black woman in Jamaica.

Overall, Notorious is a nuanced and thought-provoking exploration of love, relationships, identity, and culture, set against the vibrant backdrop of 1960s Jamaica.

overview: A stuffy businessman finds himself trapped inside the body of his family's cat.
tagline: His life just got put on paws.
title: Nine Lives
plot:
