overview: Two New York City girls make a pact to lose their virginity during their first summer out of high school. When they both fall for the same street artist, the friends find their connection tested for the first time.
tagline: When we lose our innocence, we have to find ourselves.
title: Very Good Girls
plot:
Very Good Girls is a 2013 American coming-of-age drama film that explores the complexities of female friendship and the struggles of growing up. The movie delves into the theme of female empowerment, as two high school friends, Lydia and Daisy, navigate their way through adolescence and grapple with the societal expectations placed upon them.

The film also touches on the idea of identity and self-discovery, as the characters confront their own desires, aspirations, and values. Through their relationships and experiences, the movie sheds light on the challenges faced by young women in finding their place in the world and asserting their independence.

Furthermore, Very Good Girls examines the tension between innocence and experience, as Lydia and Daisy transition from adolescence to adulthood. The film raises questions about the nature of female friendship and the ways in which it can both support and complicate personal growth.

Ultimately, the movie presents a nuanced portrayal of young women's lives, highlighting the complexities and contradictions that often accompany this stage of life.

overview: Teenagers at a juvenile detention center, under the leadership of their counselor, gain self-esteem by playing football together.
tagline: One goal. A second chance.
title: Gridiron Gang
plot:
Gridiron Gang is a sports drama film released in 2006, directed by Rick Family and starring Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson, Xander Berkeley, and Kyra Sedgwick. The movie tells the story of Sean Porter (Johnson), a former NFL player who becomes a coach at a juvenile correctional facility in California.

At the beginning of the film, we see Sean Porter, a former NFL linebacker, struggling to find his place after retiring from football. He is arrested for driving under the influence and sentenced to community service at a juvenile correctional facility called Red Rock Juvenile Correctional Facility. While serving his sentence, Sean meets a group of troubled teenagers who are being held at the facility.

Sean sees an opportunity to make a positive impact on these young lives and decides to start a football team within the facility. Despite initial resistance from the facility's administrators, Sean is able to convince them to let him coach the team. He uses his experience as a former NFL player to teach the boys about teamwork, discipline, and responsibility.

As the season progresses, Sean forms strong bonds with his players, many of whom are struggling with personal issues such as poverty, abuse, and neglect. Through football, Sean is able to reach these young men and help them find their sense of purpose and belonging. The team begins to show improvement on the field, but more importantly, they start to develop a sense of unity and camaraderie.

However, not everyone is supportive of Sean's efforts. The facility's administrators are skeptical of his ability to manage the team, and some of the players' parents are opposed to their children participating in football due to concerns about safety and discipline.

Despite these challenges, Sean perseveres and continues to work with his team. He uses his experience as a former NFL player to teach them valuable life skills such as communication, teamwork, and leadership. As the season comes to an end, the Red Rock Juvenile Football Team makes it to the championship game, where they face off against their arch-rivals.

In the final game, Sean's team faces off against their toughest opponents yet, but with Sean's guidance and support, they are able to overcome their challenges and emerge victorious. The win is a testament to the power of football as a tool for redemption and personal growth.

The film ends on a hopeful note, with Sean's players having found a sense of purpose and belonging through football. Many of them have also begun to turn their lives around, with some going on to attend college and pursue careers in sports management or coaching. The movie concludes with Sean reflecting on the impact he has had on his players' lives and the lessons they have learned from him.

Overall, Gridiron Gang is a heartwarming and inspiring film that explores the transformative power of football and the human spirit. With outstanding performances from its cast, particularly Dwayne Johnson, the movie is a must-see for sports fans and anyone looking for a story about redemption and personal growth.

overview: A British spy ship has sunk and on board was a hi-tech encryption device. James Bond is sent to find the device that holds British launching instructions before the enemy Soviets get to it first.
tagline: No one comes close to James Bond, 007.
title: For Your Eyes Only
plot:
For Your Eyes Only is a 1981 spy film directed by John Glen, starring Roger Moore as James Bond. The movie is the twelfth installment in the James Bond series and marks the first time that Bond has appeared on screen since The Man with the Golden Gun (1974).

The story begins with Bond, now working for MI6, being tasked with investigating a mysterious device known as "Jewel" that has been stolen from the British government. The thief is revealed to be Aris Kristatos (Julian Glover), a former Greek intelligence officer who had previously worked with Bond in The Spy Who Loved Me.

Bond's investigation leads him to the island of Kauai, where he encounters Kristatos and his accomplice, General Orlov (Louis Jourdan). As Bond delves deeper into the mystery, he discovers that Kristatos has stolen the Jewel device, which is capable of destroying entire cities with a single blast. The device is hidden in a safe deposit box at a bank on the island.

Bond's mission becomes more complicated when he meets Melina Havelock (Carole Bouquet), a beautiful and resourceful Greek woman who is also being pursued by Kristatos. As Bond and Melina work together to uncover the truth behind the Jewel device, they find themselves in a series of high-stakes battles against Kristatos' henchmen.

Throughout the movie, Bond's character is showcased as suave, sophisticated, and deadly efficient. His interactions with Melina are particularly notable, as he struggles to balance his professional obligations with his growing feelings for her.

As the story unfolds, Bond discovers that Orlov has been using the Jewel device to hold the world hostage, threatening to destroy major cities unless his demands are met. In a thrilling climax, Bond and Melina infiltrate Orlov's lair and engage in a fierce battle against Kristatos and his men.

In the end, Bond is able to disable the Jewel device and prevent it from falling into the wrong hands. As he and Melina escape the island together, Bond reflects on the personal costs of his work as a spy, including the loss of relationships and the constant danger that comes with the job.

For Your Eyes Only was well-received by critics and audiences alike, praised for its action-packed sequences, witty dialogue, and Roger Moore's charismatic performance as Bond. The movie's success helped to revitalize the James Bond franchise in the early 1980s, paving the way for future installments in the series.

overview: With Ran, legendary director Akira Kurosawa reimagines Shakespeare's King Lear as a singular historical epic set in sixteenth-century Japan. Majestic in scope, the film is Kurosawa's late-life masterpiece, a profound examination of the folly of war and the crumbling of one family under the weight of betrayal, greed, and the insatiable thirst for power.
tagline: In a mad world, only the mad are sane.
title: Ran
plot:
Ran is a 1985 Japanese epic historical drama film directed by Akira Kurosawa, produced by Toho.

The main themes of Ran include:

1. **The Decline of the Samurai Class**: The film explores the decline of the samurai class in Japan during the late Edo period. The story revolves around the downfall of the Taira clan and their struggle for power against the Minamoto clan.
2. **Fate vs. Free Will**: The movie delves into the idea that fate is an inevitable force that cannot be escaped, while also exploring the concept of free will. The characters' choices and actions are influenced by their circumstances, highlighting the tension between destiny and personal agency.
3. **Loyalty and Betrayal**: Loyalty to one's lord, family, or community is a recurring theme in Ran. However, the film also shows how loyalty can be tested and ultimately lead to betrayal, as characters are forced to make difficult choices that challenge their sense of duty and honor.
4. **The Cycle of Violence**: The movie depicts a cycle of violence and revenge, where past wrongs are avenged by future generations. This theme is reflected in the character of Lord Tairō, who seeks revenge against his enemies while also struggling with his own demons.
5. **Nature vs. Humanity**: Kurosawa often explores the relationship between nature and humanity in his films. In Ran, this theme is represented through the contrast between the natural world (the forest) and human society (the castle). The film suggests that both are interconnected and interdependent.

The story begins with Lord Tairō's return to his ancestral home after a long absence, where he finds himself embroiled in a struggle for power against his half-brother, Lord Hidetora. As the conflict escalates, the characters' motivations and loyalties are tested, leading to a tragic confrontation that ultimately seals their fate.

The film's plot development is marked by a series of intense battles, dramatic betrayals, and poignant moments of introspection. The ending is both devastating and thought-provoking, leaving the audience to ponder the consequences of the characters' actions and the cyclical nature of violence and revenge.

Overall, Ran is a complex and nuanced film that explores themes that are both timeless and timely. Its exploration of human nature, loyalty, and the cycle of violence continues to resonate with audiences today.

overview: Nicholas Nickleby, a young boy in search of a better life, struggles to save his family and friends from the abusive exploitation of his coldheartedly grasping uncle.
title: Nicholas Nickleby
plot:
Nicholas Nickleby is a 2002 film adaptation of Charles Dickens' novel of the same name, directed by Douglas McGrath and produced by United Artists.

The movie explores several poignant themes that were characteristic of Dickens' work. At its core, Nicholas Nickleby is a powerful tale of love, loss, and redemption. The story revolves around Nicholas, a young man who must navigate the complexities of his family's struggles with poverty, abuse, and exploitation.

One of the primary themes of the film is the struggle for survival and the resilience of the human spirit in the face of adversity. Nicholas' journey is marked by hardship, but also by moments of hope, kindness, and generosity from those around him. The movie highlights the importance of empathy, compassion, and understanding in breaking down social barriers.

The film also delves into the darker aspects of Victorian society, exposing the cruel treatment of the poor, the vulnerable, and the marginalized. Dickens' novel was a scathing critique of the social ills of his time, and the movie adaptation stays true to this spirit, shedding light on the injustices faced by those living in poverty.

Furthermore, Nicholas Nickleby is a story about the power of love and relationships to transcend even the most difficult circumstances. The character of Kate Nickleby, Nicholas' sister, is a poignant example of this theme, as her unwavering devotion to her family serves as a beacon of hope in the midst of despair.

Overall, Nicholas Nickleby (2002) is a powerful exploration of the human condition, tackling themes that are both timeless and timely. The movie's thoughtful pacing and nuanced performances bring Dickens' classic novel to life, offering a thought-provoking and emotionally resonant viewing experience.

overview: A drama based on the true story of a college professor's bond with the abandoned dog he takes into his home.
tagline: A true story of faith, devotion and undying love.
title: Hachi: A Dog's Tale
plot:
Hachi: A Dog's Tale is a 2009 American drama film directed by Lasse Hallström and written by Stephen P. Lindsey, based on the 1987 Japanese film Hachikō Monogatari, written by Kaneto Shindo and directed by Seijirō Kōyama. Both films are inspired by the true story of Hachikō, an Akita dog in Japan who continued to wait at a Tokyo train station for his owner for nearly ten years after the man's death. The American version transfers the story to a modern New England setting. Richard Gere, who also produced the film, stars with Joan Allen, Sarah Roemer, Jason Alexander and Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa.

The film is framed by a schoolboy named Ronnie, who tells his class that his hero is Hachi, the dog that belonged to his grandfather. Parker Wilson, a college music professor who commutes to Providence, finds a lost Akita puppy at the train station in the small town of Bedridge and takes him home for the night. When no one claims the dog, Parker grows attached to him despite the reluctance of his wife Cate. His Japanese friend Ken identifies the breed and translates the symbol on the dog's collar as "Hachi," meaning eight, a lucky number, and the name sticks.

Hachi becomes devoted to Parker. Ken explains that Akitas are independent dogs that will not do tricks on command, and that if Hachi ever fetches a ball for Parker, it will be for a special reason. One day Hachi slips out of the yard and follows Parker to the station, and that evening Parker finds him waiting at the station when the train arrives. A daily ritual begins: every morning Hachi walks with Parker to the station, and every afternoon at five o'clock he returns to meet his train. Their routine, and the friendships it creates with the station master, a hot dog vendor and other townspeople, continue for years until a tragedy changes everything, and Hachi's loyalty becomes a source of wonder for the town.

The film premiered at the Seattle International Film Festival in June 2009 and was released theatrically in many countries, although Sony released it directly to DVD in the United States. It received mixed-to-positive reviews, with a 64 percent Rotten Tomatoes rating. Critics described it as an unashamed tear-jerker; Christopher Lloyd of the Sarasota Herald-Tribune admitted that viewers may resent the manipulation but still gave it four out of five stars. It grossed about $47 million worldwide.

overview: Carmen and Juni think their parents are boring. Little do they know that in their day, Gregorio and Ingrid Cortez were the top secret agents from their respective countries. They gave up that life to raise their children. Now, the disappearances of several of their old colleagues forces the Cortez' return from retirement. What they didn't count on was Carmen and Juni joining the "family business."
tagline: Real spies...only smaller
title: Spy Kids
plot:
Spy Kids is a 2001 American family comedy film directed by Robert Rodriguez and written by Carlos Gallardo, Robert Rodriguez, and John Hodgman. The movie follows the adventures of two siblings, Carmen and Juni Cortez, who become spies to save their parents from the evil Fegan Floop.

The story begins with Carmen (Alexa Vega) and Juni (Daryl Sabara), two 10-year-old siblings who live with their parents, Gregorio (Antonio Banderas) and Jane (Carla Gugino), in San Francisco. The family is struggling to make ends meet after Gregorio's spy days are over. However, their lives take a dramatic turn when they receive a message from Fegan Floop (Alan Cumming), the former head of the Spy Kids program, who has stolen the magical Medallion of Spies.

The Medallion allows its wearer to control all the world's spies and is hidden in a museum. Floop plans to use it to take over the world. Carmen and Juni soon discover that their parents were once part of the Spy Kids program and decide to follow in their footsteps to save them. They are recruited by the agency, led by the Chief (Alfred Molina), who trains them in spy skills.

As they embark on their mission, Carmen and Juni face various obstacles and challenges, including Floop's henchmen, the Boto Bandits, and other villains. Along the way, they meet a new ally, Ingrid (Ana Maria Barraza), a former Spy Kid who helps them on their quest.

The siblings use their wits, bravery, and teamwork to outsmart Floop's minions and reach the museum where the Medallion is hidden. In a thrilling finale, Carmen and Juni face off against Floop in an action-packed battle, using all they've learned from their training.

In the end, the siblings successfully retrieve the Medallion and save their parents from Floop's clutches. The movie concludes with the Cortez family reunited and celebrating their victory as heroes. The film ends on a high note, setting the stage for two sequels, Spy Kids 2 (2002) and Spy Kids 3-D: Game Over (2003).

Spy Kids is a fun, action-packed adventure that pays homage to classic spy movies and cartoons. The movie's success can be attributed to its engaging storyline, memorable characters, and Rodriguez's signature style, which blends humor, excitement, and heart.

overview: Zed and Addison are beginning their final year at Seabrook High in the town that’s become a safe haven for monsters and humans alike. Zed is anticipating an athletic scholarship that will make him the first Zombie to attend college, while Addison is gearing up for Seabrook’s first international cheer-off competition. Then suddenly, extraterrestrial beings appear around Seabrook, provoking something other than friendly competition.
tagline: They beam down. We rise up.
title: Z-O-M-B-I-E-S 3
plot:
Z-O-M-B-I-E-S 3, also known as Zombies 3, is a 2022 American science fiction musical comedy-drama and the third installment in the Disney Channel franchise that began with Zombies (2018) and Zombies 2 (2020). Meg Donnelly and Milo Manheim reprise their roles as Addison and Zed, with Trevor Tordjman, Chandler Kinney and Ariel Martin among the returning supporting cast. It premiered on Disney+ on July 15, 2022, and aired on Disney Channel on August 12, 2022.

Zombies, humans and werewolves now live in harmony in the town of Seabrook. It is their senior year at Seabrook High, and Addison has been accepted into Mountain College, where Zed hopes to join her on an athletic scholarship that would make him the first monster to be recruited and open the door for others. On the eve of a crucial football game, however, a UFO lands and three aliens, A-Lan, A-Li and A-Spen, beam down. They are secretly searching for an interstellar map to Utopia, a new home for their people, which is hidden in "the most precious thing in Seabrook." As a cover story, they claim to have come to compete in a national cheerleading competition that Addison has organized.

The werewolves Willa, Wyatt and Wynter distrust the newcomers from the start, while the aliens outshine Zed both academically and athletically, threatening his college hopes. Zed reluctantly helps them in exchange for an improvement to his grades, and A-Spen forms a friendship with Addison. When Addison is accidentally beamed aboard the mothership, the aliens reveal their true purpose and discover that their long-lost scout was none other than Addison's grandmother Angie, meaning Addison herself is part alien. The map turns out to be the Seabrook Cup, the cheer trophy Angie created from materials from the aliens' home world, setting Addison against her new friends in the competition. As the werewolves move against the aliens, the residents of Seabrook must decide whether there is room in their town for yet another group of outsiders.

Critical reaction was mixed, with reviewers often noting its energy and message of acceptance while being less enthusiastic about its alien storyline and songs. The New York Times praised its tone while criticizing its handling of a queer character, and CNN found it progressive but clichéd, singling out "I'm Finally Me" among its songs. A fourth film, Zombies 4: Dawn of the Vampires, premiered on Disney Channel in July 2025.

overview: When Blitzen announces his retirement on December 21st, a miniature horse has 3 days to fulfill his lifelong dream of earning a spot on Santa's team at the North Pole try-outs.
tagline: Big Dreamers Dream Big
title: Elliot: The Littlest Reindeer
plot:
Elliot: The Littlest Reindeer is a 2018 Canadian animated Christmas comedy written and directed by Jennifer Wescott. The voice cast features Josh Hutcherson as Elliot, Samantha Bee as Hazel, and Martin Short, Morena Baccarin, Jeff Dunham and John Cleese. The film follows a miniature horse who dreams of joining Santa Claus's sleigh team and gets an unexpected chance when one of the famous reindeer retires.

Elliot lives on the struggling Witty Bitty Farm in North Dakota, which operates both as a petting zoo and as a training camp for aspiring sleigh reindeer, most of whom are arrogant and self-absorbed. Elliot trains alongside them, but the farm's owner, the former baseball player Walter Whittick, barely notices him, and his only real supporter is his best friend Hazel, a sharp-witted goat. When Blitzen announces his retirement, tryouts are held at the North Pole to find a replacement, and Walter hopes that his most athletic reindeer, DJ, will win the place and save the farm from financial ruin.

At the same time, a businesswoman named Ludzinka arrives and offers to buy the petting zoo animals. Walter agrees, unaware of her real intentions, but Elliot and Hazel discover that she plans to turn the animals into dehydrated food. Hoping to win the tryouts and rescue their friends, the pair stow away in Walter's flying vehicle as he travels north with DJ. At the North Pole, Hazel uses disguises to get Elliot registered for the competition, helped by an elf named Jolene, since Santa and his elves can talk with animals. Elliot faces a series of demanding trials against much bigger and stronger competitors, while Hazel uncovers signs that Christmas itself may be headed for disaster. Back at the farm, Ludzinka threatens the lives of the animals, and Elliot must choose between pursuing his lifelong dream and saving the friends he left behind.

The film was released in Canada in November 2018 and received negative reviews, with a 29 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes. The site's consensus called it a farcical Christmas romp only slightly more entertaining than a heap of coal, and Nell Minow of RogerEbert.com gave it one and a half stars out of four. Tara McNamara of Common Sense Media was also among the critics who reviewed the film for family audiences.

overview: In early 1950s Vietnam, a young American becomes entangled in a dangerous love triangle when he falls for the beautiful mistress of a British journalist. As war is waged around them, the trio sinks deeper into a world of drugs, passion, and betrayal where nothing is as it seems.
production_companies: IMF Internationale Medien und Film GmbH & Co. 2. Produktions KG
tagline: In war, the most powerful weapon is seduction.
title: The Quiet American
plot:
The Quiet American is a 2002 political drama directed by Phillip Noyce, starring Michael Caine, Brendan Fraser and Đỗ Thị Hải Yến, with Rade Šerbedžija and Tzi Ma in supporting roles. The screenplay by Christopher Hampton and Robert Schenkkan adapts Graham Greene's 1955 novel of the same name. Unlike the 1958 film version, which reversed Greene's warning about foreign intervention into an anticommunist message, the 2002 adaptation is faithful to the novel's portrait of the moral responsibility of American agents involved in violence in Vietnam.

The story is set in Saigon in 1952, during the First Indochina War between French colonial forces and the Communist-led Viet Minh. Thomas Fowler, a world-weary British journalist in his fifties who narrates the film, prides himself on remaining an uninvolved observer of the conflict. He lives with Phuong, a young Vietnamese woman, but cannot marry her because his Catholic wife in England refuses him a divorce. His comfortable life is disrupted when he befriends Alden Pyle, a young, earnest American who claims to be working for an economic aid mission.

Pyle falls in love with Phuong and openly courts her, offering her the marriage and security that Fowler cannot, and a rivalry develops between the two men that remains strangely polite. At the same time Fowler grows suspicious of Pyle's activities. He discovers that the idealistic American is deeply devoted to the theories of a writer who believed Vietnam needed a "Third Force," neither colonial nor communist, and that Pyle is in fact a CIA operative working to create such a force by supporting a renegade militia leader, General Thé. When a bombing in a crowded Saigon square kills and maims many civilians, Fowler realizes the extent of Pyle's involvement and must decide whether he can remain neutral any longer, a choice complicated by his personal stake in Phuong.

The film was completed in 2001, but its release was delayed after the September 11 attacks because of concerns about its critical depiction of American foreign policy; Caine campaigned for it to be shown. It received positive reviews, with an 87 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 84, and critics praised its fidelity to Greene. Caine received an Academy Award nomination for Best Actor for his performance as Fowler.

overview: The Coast Guard makes a daring rescue attempt off the coast of Cape Cod after a pair of oil tankers are destroyed during a blizzard in 1952.
tagline: 32 survivors, room for 12.
title: The Finest Hours
plot:
The Finest Hours is a 2016 American biographical drama film directed by Greg Mottola and produced by Walt Disney Pictures.

The movie is based on the true story of the USS Cabot, a U.S. Coast Guard cutter that rescued 33 sailors from the SS Pendleton in 1952. The film follows the story of Bernie Webber (played by Chris Pine), an experienced Coast Guardsman who leads the rescue effort.

Some of the main themes of The Finest Hours include:

1. **Bravery and Selflessness**: The movie highlights the bravery and selflessness of the Coast Guard crew, particularly Bernie Webber, who puts himself in harm's way to save the lives of others.
2. **Teamwork and Camaraderie**: The film showcases the strong bond between the Coast Guardsmen, who work together seamlessly to overcome the challenges they face during the rescue operation.
3. **Perseverance and Determination**: Despite the odds against them, the crew perseveres and stays determined to complete their mission, even in the face of treacherous weather conditions.
4. **Heroism and Sacrifice**: The movie also explores the theme of heroism and sacrifice, as Bernie Webber and his team risk their lives to save others, while also facing personal sacrifices and challenges.

Overall, The Finest Hours is a thrilling and inspiring film that celebrates the bravery, teamwork, and determination of the Coast Guardsmen who risked everything to save the lives of others.

overview: Skylar finds out that her parents are monster hunters after she accidentally releases some monsters from a secret containment chamber; so she and her techno friends must recapture all the monsters and also save her mom and dad from these monsters who are out for revenge.
tagline: Face Your Fears
title: Girl vs. Monster
plot:
Girl vs. Monster is a 2012 American comedy horror Disney Channel Original Movie directed by Stuart Gillard and produced by Tracey Jeffrey. It premiered on Disney Channel on 12 October 2012, as part of the network's Halloween programming. Olivia Holt stars as Skylar Lewis, with Brendan Meyer, Kerris Dorsey, Luke Benward, Katherine McNamara, Jennifer Aspen and Tracy Dawson in supporting roles.

Skylar is a fearless fifteen-year-old with a strong singing voice who is excited about performing at a big Halloween party with her best friends Henry and Sadie and with Ryan, a member of a rock band she admires. On the day of the party, however, her parents unexpectedly forbid her to go out and even activate an alarm system to keep her inside. Determined to attend, Skylar cuts the house's power to disable the alarm, not knowing that her parents use the electricity to run a containment system holding captured monsters.

The power cut releases Deimata, a powerful fear monster that feeds on people's terror and is determined to take revenge on Skylar's family. Skylar learns that her parents have kept a major secret from her: they are monster hunters, and she is the fifth generation of a family of hunters. She also discovers that her fearlessness is not natural; her ability to feel fear was blocked when she was a baby, and now that Deimata is free she is suddenly overwhelmed by fears she has never experienced. The film explains that every person has a personal monster that grows stronger with their fear, and Henry, Sadie and Skylar's rival Myra soon face their own. When Deimata captures Skylar's parents, she and her friends must learn to use the family's monster-hunting tools and confront their fears in order to rescue them and trap the monsters again before Halloween night is over.

The film drew a large audience on its premiere and became a recurring part of Disney Channel's Halloween schedule. Holt, then starring in the Disney XD series Kickin' It, performed songs for the soundtrack, including "Had Me @ Hello" and "Fearless," which were released as singles.

overview: King T'Challa returns home to the reclusive, technologically advanced African nation of Wakanda to serve as his country's new leader. However, T'Challa soon finds that he is challenged for the throne by factions within his own country as well as without. Using powers reserved to Wakandan kings, T'Challa assumes the Black Panther mantle to join with ex-girlfriend Nakia, the queen-mother, his princess-kid sister, members of the Dora Milaje (the Wakandan 'special forces') and an American secret agent, to prevent Wakanda from being dragged into a world war.
tagline: Long live the king.
title: Black Panther
plot:
Black Panther is a 2018 superhero film directed by Ryan Coogler, produced by Marvel Studios, and based on the Marvel Comics character of the same name.

The story takes place in the fictional African nation of Wakanda, where King T'Challa (played by Chadwick Boseman) has assumed the throne after his father's death. T'Challa is a skilled warrior and strategist who must balance his royal duties with his desire to protect his people from threats both within and outside their borders.

Upon his return to Wakanda, T'Challa is challenged by Erik Killmonger (played by Michael B. Jordan), a Wakandan exile who seeks to overthrow him and claim the throne for himself. Killmonger believes that Wakanda's isolationist policies have led to the suffering of African people around the world, and he wants to use Wakanda's advanced technology to spark a global revolution.

As T'Challa navigates this internal conflict, he must also confront external threats from the United States and other nations that seek to exploit Wakanda's resources. He is aided by his sister Shuri (played by Letitia Wright), a brilliant inventor and engineer who helps him develop new technologies to defend his country.

Throughout the film, T'Challa grapples with the weight of his responsibilities as king and the legacy of his father, who was killed in battle against Killmonger. He must also confront his own identity and the expectations placed upon him by his people.

One of the standout aspects of Black Panther is its exploration of themes such as colonialism, imperialism, and cultural identity. The film offers a nuanced portrayal of Wakandan society and culture, highlighting both its strengths and weaknesses. It also features a diverse cast of characters, including Nakia (played by Lupita Nyong'o), a Wakandan spy who becomes T'Challa's love interest.

Overall, Black Panther is a visually stunning and thought-provoking film that offers a fresh take on the superhero genre. Its blend of action, drama, and social commentary makes it a compelling watch for audiences of all ages.

overview: A legendary secret service agent comes out of hiding and returns to France to help the son he's never met get out of trouble.
tagline: The daddy of all secret agents.
title: The Last Mercenary
plot:
The Last Mercenary (French: Le Dernier Mercenaire) is a 2021 French action comedy directed by David Charhon from a screenplay he co-wrote with Ismael Sy Savane. Jean-Claude Van Damme stars as Richard Brumère, a legendary former secret agent, with Alban Ivanov, Assa Sylla and Samir Decazza in the supporting cast. The film was released worldwide on Netflix on 30 July 2021, and it plays as an affectionate parody of the action films that made Van Damme famous, while giving him a role that mocks his own screen persona.

Years earlier, during a covert operation, Richard fathered a son, Archibald, with the former wife of his colleague Jouard. Because Richard could not raise the boy himself, the boy's mother arranged that he would receive two things from the state: a regular financial allowance and a guardian to look after him, together with legal immunity linked to Richard's service. An agent named Fernand was assigned to the task and has cared for Archibald ever since, so the young man has always believed that Fernand is his father.

The arrangement collapses when a zealous government minister discovers that a phantom employee has been paying Archibald money for years. Cutting off the payments also cancels his immunity, and because of a bureaucratic mix-up, Archibald is suddenly identified as a wanted terrorist accused of arms and drug trafficking. Government agents raid his home using a secret electronic device nicknamed the Big Mac, which disables Fernand's pacemaker and causes a fatal heart attack, and Archibald is arrested. Learning that his son is in danger, Richard returns to France and stages a rescue, at first hiding his identity under an alias. Father and son go on the run, pursued by the government and caught up in a conspiracy involving the minister and the Big Mac device, while Archibald slowly learns the truth about the father he never knew.

The film relies on slapstick, absurd disguises and self-referential jokes, including nods to Van Damme's trademark martial arts, alongside a story about an absent father attempting to make amends.

The Last Mercenary received mixed reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes about 58 percent of critics' reviews are positive, and Metacritic assigned it a score of 48 out of 100, with critics enjoying Van Damme's self-parody while finding the comedy uneven.

overview: A story set in Indochina in 1959, a lawless land controlled by the criminal class: Vietnamese warlords and European war-criminals. Den-Dhin-Chan Labor Camp is run by four such dangerous men. The worst prison in the land, it is here that an Irish, former-champion boxer Martin Tillman has made a name for himself fighting tournaments, on which wealthy criminals gamble in high stakes events. When Tillman is due for release, he just wants to return home, but the corrupt forces running the jail will do everything in their power to keep him locked down. When all that Tillman holds dear is taken away in a vicious act of violence, he is forced to confront the men responsible and take his revenge.  The birth of a legend.
tagline: Indochina, 1959. The French left. The Americans have yet to arrive. But one man has declered war.
title: Savage Dog
plot:
Savage Dog is an action-adventure film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the blurred lines between good and evil. The movie follows a U.S. Marine who becomes embroiled in a conflict in Vietnam, where he must confront his own morality and the harsh realities of war.

At its core, Savage Dog explores the theme of moral ambiguity, highlighting how even the most well-intentioned individuals can become consumed by their own darkness when faced with the brutalities of war. The film's protagonist is a complex character, driven by a mix of motivations that make him both relatable and flawed.

The movie also touches on the theme of cultural clashes, as the U.S. Marine navigates the unfamiliar terrain of Vietnam, where he encounters a local woman who becomes embroiled in his conflict. This subplot serves to underscore the senseless violence and destruction that often accompanies war, highlighting the human cost of conflict.

Furthermore, Savage Dog critiques the notion of heroism, suggesting that even those who claim to be fighting for a just cause can become complicit in their own brutality when faced with the harsh realities of war. The film's portrayal of the Vietnam War is unflinching and unsentimental, refusing to shy away from the brutalities and atrocities that occurred during this conflict.

Overall, Savage Dog is a thought-provoking and visceral film that challenges its viewers to confront the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of war.

overview: When a young boy accidentally triggers the universe's most lethal hunters' return to Earth, only a ragtag crew of ex-soldiers and a disgruntled scientist can prevent the end of the human race.
tagline: The hunt has evolved.
title: The Predator
plot:
The Predator (2018) is a science fiction action film directed by Shane Black and written by Black and Fred Dekker. The movie serves as a reboot of the Predator franchise, ignoring all previous films except for the first two installments.

The story begins with Quinn McKenna (Boyd Holbrook), a former Army Ranger who has been struggling to cope with the loss of his son in combat. Quinn is haunted by nightmares and feels guilty for not being able to protect his child. He is approached by a mysterious woman named Casey Bracket (Olivia Munn), a scientist who claims to have discovered evidence of an alien species known as the Yautja, also referred to as the Predator.

Casey believes that the Yautja are a technologically advanced species that hunt and kill each other for sport. She has been tracking a Yautja, which she calls "The Hunter," and is determined to study it. Quinn agrees to help Casey track down The Hunter, and they embark on a perilous journey into the Mexican jungle.

As they delve deeper into the jungle, they are joined by a group of mercenaries, including Baxley ( Trevante Rhodes), a former Army Ranger who has lost his brother in combat; Nettie (Keegan-Michael Key), a skilled sniper; and Riddick (Javier Bardem), a notorious smuggler. The team soon discovers that The Hunter is not just a mindless killer, but a highly intelligent and cunning predator with advanced technology.

As the team navigates the jungle, they are stalked by The Hunter, who begins to hunt them down one by one. Quinn and Casey form an uneasy alliance, with Quinn struggling to come to terms with his past and Casey trying to understand the Yautja's motivations. Along the way, they uncover clues that suggest The Hunter is not just a hunter, but also a warrior who is driven by honor and tradition.

As the body count rises, Quinn and Casey realize that The Hunter is not just a mindless killer, but a complex and nuanced creature with its own code of conduct. In a thrilling climax, Quinn faces off against The Hunter in an intense battle of wits and strength. Despite being outgunned and outmatched, Quinn manages to defeat The Hunter using his knowledge of the jungle and his own resourcefulness.

In the end, Quinn emerges victorious but scarred by his experience. He returns home to his family, where he is finally able to find some measure of peace and closure. Casey, meanwhile, is left to ponder the implications of her discovery and the true nature of The Hunter's motivations.

Overall, The Predator (2018) is a tense and thrilling action film that explores themes of honor, tradition, and the human condition. While it may not be as groundbreaking as some of its predecessors, it offers a fresh take on the franchise and provides plenty of excitement and suspense for fans of science fiction and action movies.

overview: A new breed of aggressive, ravenous sharks cracks the frozen ocean floor of an Arctic research station, devouring all who fall through. As the station sinks into frigid waters, those alive must fashion makeshift weapons or suffer the same fate.
tagline: Just When You Thought it was Safe in the Arctic.
title: Ice Sharks
plot:
Ice Sharks is a 2016 campy horror-comedy film that delves into the darker side of human nature and the dangers of playing with forces beyond one's control.

At its core, the movie explores the theme of revenge and the consequences of seeking retribution. The main character, Jack Morris, played by Michael Eklund, is a former special forces operative who seeks to avenge his brother's death at the hands of a group of ruthless poachers. As he navigates the treacherous world of ice fishing and shark hunting, Jack's quest for revenge becomes an all-consuming force that threatens to destroy him from within.

The film also touches on the theme of obsession, as Jack's fixation on avenging his brother's death leads him down a path of madness and destruction. This obsession serves as a metaphor for the dangers of allowing personal vendettas to consume us, leading us to lose sight of what is truly important in life.

Furthermore, Ice Sharks critiques the notion of masculinity and the societal expectations placed upon men. Jack's character embodies a toxic form of masculinity, driven by aggression and a desire for control. As the story unfolds, however, it becomes clear that this type of masculinity comes at a great cost, both to himself and those around him.

Ultimately, Ice Sharks is a film about the dangers of unchecked ambition and the devastating consequences of allowing personal demons to consume us. Through its over-the-top action sequences and campy humor, the movie delivers a thrilling ride that also serves as a cautionary tale about the importance of self-awareness and emotional intelligence.

overview: It’s the Adventure Bay 500! The pups have built an awesome race track and are ready to be the pit crew for their race hero, The Whoosh! But when the legendary racer is unable to drive in the championship race, he calls on his biggest fan-pup Marshall to take the wheel and race in his place! Marshall has to overcome his lack of confidence and his dastardly competition, The Cheetah, to fulfill his dream of becoming the fastest race-pup ever!
tagline: Get ready to race and rescue!
title: Paw Patrol: Ready, Race, Rescue!
plot:
Paw Patrol: Ready, Race, Rescue! is a 2019 animated adventure film based on the popular children's television series Paw Patrol. The movie follows the PAW Patrol team as they compete in the Great Race, a high-stakes racing competition that requires teamwork and quick thinking to win.

The main themes of the movie include:

1. Teamwork: The film highlights the importance of working together towards a common goal. The PAW Patrol team uses their unique skills and abilities to overcome obstacles and challenges.
2. Friendship: The movie showcases the strong bonds between the PAW Patrol pups, who put aside their differences to work together and support each other.
3. Problem-solving: The film encourages children to think creatively and develop problem-solving skills as the pups face various challenges and puzzles during the Great Race.
4. Perseverance: The movie teaches kids about the value of perseverance and determination, as the PAW Patrol team faces setbacks and obstacles but never gives up.

The story begins with Ryder announcing the Great Race, a competition that will determine which team is the best. The PAW Patrol pups are excited to participate, but things take a turn when they realize that the competition is not just about winning, but also about learning valuable lessons about teamwork and friendship.

As the race progresses, the pups face various challenges, including navigating through obstacles, solving puzzles, and working together to overcome their differences. Along the way, they learn important values such as empathy, selflessness, and cooperation.

In the end, the PAW Patrol team emerges victorious, but more importantly, they have learned a valuable lesson about the importance of teamwork, friendship, and perseverance. The movie concludes with a heartwarming moment of celebration and camaraderie among the pups, emphasizing the power of unity and collaboration.

Overall, Paw Patrol: Ready, Race, Rescue! is an entertaining and educational film that promotes positive values and encourages children to develop essential skills such as problem-solving, teamwork, and perseverance.

overview: Following the death of his wife, Ip Man travels to San Francisco to ease tensions between the local kung fu masters and his star student, Bruce Lee, while searching for a better future for his son.
title: Ip Man 4: The Finale
plot:
Ip Man 4: The Finale is a 2019 martial arts film directed by Wilson Yip and starring Donnie Yen as the titular character. The movie concludes the Ip Man saga, which explores the life of Ip Man, a grandmaster of Wing Chun.

The main themes of Ip Man 4: The Finale revolve around:

1. **Legacy and Passing on Knowledge**: The film delves into Ip Man's struggles to find a worthy successor, as he faces declining health and an increasing number of threats from rival martial artists. This theme is reflected in his relationships with his students, particularly Max (played by Lewis Chan), who becomes the new master of Wing Chun.

2. **Mentorship and Fatherhood**: Ip Man's role as a mentor and father figure to his students is a recurring theme throughout the film. He must balance his desire to pass on his knowledge with the need to protect his students from harm, particularly in the face of external threats.

3. **Identity and Cultural Heritage**: The movie explores Ip Man's struggles to maintain his cultural heritage and identity as he navigates the complexities of modern life. This theme is reflected in his relationships with his family and his efforts to preserve Wing Chun traditions.

4. **Redemption and Self-Sacrifice**: As Ip Man faces increasing danger, he must confront his own mortality and consider the possibility of sacrificing himself for the greater good. This theme is reflected in his final confrontation with the main antagonist, Cheng (played by Louis Koo).

5. **The Passing of Time and Mortality**: The film grapples with the inevitability of aging and death, as Ip Man confronts his own declining health and the passing of time. This theme is reflected in his relationships with his loved ones and his efforts to leave a lasting legacy.

Overall, Ip Man 4: The Finale is a poignant exploration of themes that are both universally relatable and uniquely tied to the world of martial arts.

overview: A series of murders has shaken the community to the point where people believe that only a legendary creature from dark times – the mythical Golem – must be responsible.
tagline: Before the ripper, fear had another name.
title: The Limehouse Golem
plot:
The Limehouse Golem is a 2016 British horror film directed by Juan Martinez Solares and written by Steven Knight. The movie is set in Victorian London, specifically in the Whitechapel district, during the late 19th century.

At its core, The Limehouse Golem explores themes of identity, trauma, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. The story revolves around a serial killer known as the "Limehouse Golem," who is terrorizing the residents of Whitechapel, leaving behind a trail of gruesome murders and mysterious disappearances.

Through the eyes of Mary Kelly (played by Olivia Cooke), a young woman who becomes entangled in the mystery, the film delves into the psychological effects of trauma on its characters. The Limehouse Golem masterfully weaves together elements of horror, suspense, and mystery to create a sense of unease and tension that permeates every aspect of the narrative.

One of the primary themes of the movie is the struggle for identity, particularly in the context of women's lives during the Victorian era. Mary Kelly, as a protagonist, embodies this theme, as she navigates her own desires, ambitions, and sense of self amidst the societal constraints of her time.

The film also touches on the idea of the "other," highlighting the marginalization and stigmatization of certain groups within society, such as prostitutes, immigrants, and those with mental health issues. The Limehouse Golem serves as a metaphor for the darker aspects of human nature, revealing the monster that lurks beneath the surface of seemingly ordinary people.

Ultimately, The Limehouse Golem is a complex, atmospheric tale that explores the darker corners of the human psyche, delving into themes of trauma, identity, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy.

overview: A deep cover operative awakens to find himself imprisoned on a submarine. With the help of a fellow prisoner and an amateur agent, he must race against the clock to escape the vessel and expose who set him up.
tagline: Some secrets never surface
title: Black Water
plot:
Black Water is a 2018 American action thriller directed by Pasha Patriki, starring Jean-Claude Van Damme and Dolph Lundgren in their fifth collaboration and only their second as on-screen allies. Patrick Kilpatrick, Al Sapienza, Jasmine Waltz, Aaron O'Connell, Courtney B. Turk and John Posey round out the cast. The film was released direct to video in the United States on May 25, 2018.

Scott Wheeler, a deep-cover CIA operative, wakes up as a prisoner in a secret CIA black site housed aboard a retrofitted nuclear submarine, alongside another captive named Marco. Through a series of memories he pieces together how he got there. Wheeler and his partner Melissa Ballard had been hunting for a leak within the agency using a USB drive that requires two components to operate: she carried the drive, while he kept the activation key. When armed men attacked their safe house, Ballard was apparently killed. Wheeler escaped, only to find his handler murdered, and was then captured by Agent Ferris, who believes Wheeler is responsible for the deaths of fellow agents.

Aboard the submarine, Wheeler realizes that Agent Rhodes, who claims to believe in his innocence, is in fact the traitor. Rhodes and his henchman kill the other CIA personnel and take control of the vessel's security team. Wheeler escapes and teams up with the rookie agent Cassie Taylor, while her partner Ellis Ryan is killed in an ambush. Together they force the submarine toward the surface and free Marco, a German special forces operative who knows too much to be released or killed. Rhodes plans to sell the drive, which holds information that would endanger agents around the world, and arranges an extraction in Cuba. As Wheeler and his allies fight through the narrow corridors, it is revealed that Ballard faked her death and has been working with Rhodes all along.

Writer Chad Law developed the project after producer Richard Switzer proposed an action film set on a submarine; Law and Switzer had previously worked with Lundgren on Altitude. Filming took place in early 2017, partly in Mobile, Alabama, and wrapped by the end of March. The film was poorly received, holding a 0% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on nine reviews, with an average score of 3.3 out of 10.

overview: Television made him famous, but his biggest hits happened off screen. Television producer by day, CIA assassin by night, Chuck Barris was recruited by the CIA at the height of his TV career and trained to become a covert operative. Or so Barris said.
tagline: Some things are better left top secret.
title: Confessions of a Dangerous Mind
plot:
"Confessions of a Dangerous Mind" is a 2002 biographical comedy-drama film directed by George Clooney, based on the memoir of the same name by Chuck Barris. The movie follows the life of Chuck Barris, a game show host and writer who becomes embroiled in espionage during the Cold War.

The main themes of "Confessions of a Dangerous Mind" include:

1. **Identity Crisis**: The film explores Chuck's struggle to reconcile his dual identities as a game show host and an assassin. This dichotomy serves as a metaphor for the societal expectations placed on individuals, particularly men, to conform to certain roles.
2. **Trauma and PTSD**: Barris's experiences in espionage take a toll on his mental health, leading to symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). The film portrays the long-term effects of trauma on an individual's life and relationships.
3. **The American Dream**: Chuck's journey is often seen as a commentary on the American Dream, which promises success and happiness in exchange for hard work and dedication. However, the film suggests that this dream can be illusory and ultimately unfulfilling.
4. **Loyalty and Betrayal**: The movie highlights the complexities of loyalty and betrayal, particularly in relationships. Chuck's relationships with his wife, his friends, and his employers are all tested by his involvement in espionage.
5. **The Blurred Lines between Reality and Fantasy**: As Barris's experiences become more surreal, it becomes difficult to distinguish reality from fantasy. This theme is reflected in the film's use of humor and satire to explore the darker aspects of human nature.

Overall, "Confessions of a Dangerous Mind" is a thought-provoking film that explores themes of identity, trauma, loyalty, and the American Dream through Chuck Barris's unconventional life story.

original_title: ドラゴンボール 超サイヤ人絶滅計画
overview: Dr. Raichi is one of the only survivors of the Tuffles, a race that once lived on Planet Plant before the coming of the Saiyans. The Saiyans not only massacred the entire Tuffle race, but also stole their technology and conquered the planet, renaming it Planet Vegeta in honor of their king. Raichi managed to escape with a capsule and found refuge on the Dark Planet, a world at the end of the universe. His only wish is to eradicate the last remaining Saiyans.
title: Dragon Ball Z: Plan to Eradicate the Super Saiyans
plot:
Dragon Ball Z: Plan to Eradicate the Super Saiyans (Japanese: Doragon Bōru: Sūpā Saiya-jin Zetsumetsu Keikaku) is a 2010 Japanese original video animation, a complete remake of a two-part 1993 OVA that had been produced as a companion to the Famicom card-battle role-playing game Dragon Ball Z Side Story: Plan to Eradicate the Saiyans, developed by Tose and published by Bandai. The voice cast is led by Masako Nozawa as Goku, Gohan and Turles, with Ryō Horikawa as Vegeta, Toshio Furukawa as Piccolo, Takeshi Kusao as Trunks, Ryūsei Nakao as Frieza and Cooler, Yusaku Yara as Lord Slug and Shinji Ogawa as the villain Dr. Raichi.

The story centres on Dr. Raichi, the last survivor of the Tuffles, a technologically advanced race that once lived on Planet Plant before it was invaded by the Saiyans. The Saiyans massacred the Tuffles, seized their technology and renamed the planet Planet Vegeta in honour of their king. Raichi escaped and took refuge on a distant dark world, where he has spent years preparing his revenge on the last remaining Saiyans.

On Earth, Raichi's devices begin releasing a substance called Destron Gas, which threatens to wipe out all life on the planet. When Mr. Popo discovers that only a few hours remain before the planet is destroyed, Goku, Gohan, Vegeta, Trunks and Piccolo race around the world to destroy the gas machines. They succeed in destroying all but one, which is protected by an impenetrable energy barrier. At that moment, some of their most dangerous past enemies, Frieza, Cooler, Turles and Lord Slug, reappear and attack them. King Kai explains that these villains are ghost warriors who will keep returning to life unless they are defeated in the same way they originally died. Tracking the source to Raichi's hideout, the heroes discover that the ghosts are generated by Hatchiyack, a machine powered by the hatred of the Tuffles, and they must face both Raichi and the monstrous power of the machine itself to save the Earth.

The story functions as a crossover that reunites the heroes with villains from several Dragon Ball Z films and story arcs, offering fans a series of rematches in a compact format.

The 1993 game on which the story is based sold around 300,000 copies in Japan and received a score of 22 out of 40 from Famitsu. Its original OVA had been released in two parts as video strategy guides, and its footage was later reused in a 1994 Playdia video game before the story was fully reanimated in 2010.

overview: The lifelong friendship between Rafe McCawley and Danny Walker is put to the ultimate test when the two ace fighter pilots become entangled in a love triangle with beautiful Naval nurse Evelyn Johnson. But the rivalry between the friends-turned-foes is immediately put on hold when they find themselves at the center of Japan's devastating attack on Pearl Harbor on Dec. 7, 1941.
tagline: It takes a moment to change history. It takes love to change lives.
title: Pearl Harbor
plot:
Pearl Harbor is a 2001 epic romantic drama film directed by Michael Bay, produced by Jerry Bruckheimer Films, and written by James V. Hart and Randall Wallace. The film stars Ben Affleck, Josh Hartnett, Kate Beckinsale, Cuba Gooding Jr., Tom Sizemore, Jon Voight, and Alec Baldwin.

The movie is set in 1941, during the early years of World War II. The story follows two childhood friends, Rafe McCawley (Ben Affleck) and Danny Walker (Josh Hartnett), who grow up together on Oahu, Hawaii. They share a love for flying and adventure, but their lives take different paths after high school.

Rafe enlists in the U.S. Army Air Corps, while Danny joins the Royal Canadian Air Force. The two friends remain close, despite being separated by distance and duty. Rafe meets Evelyn Johnson (Kate Beckinsale), a nurse who becomes his love interest, but he is forced to leave Hawaii to fight in North Africa.

Meanwhile, Danny falls in love with Nurse Evelyn, but she chooses Rafe over him. Unbeknownst to Evelyn, Rafe has been injured and presumed dead by the Japanese during a bombing raid on North Africa. The two friends are reunited when Rafe returns from his injuries, and they rekindle their romance.

The film's plot takes a dramatic turn when Japan launches a surprise attack on Pearl Harbor, drawing the United States into World War II. Rafe and Danny both return to Hawaii, where they join the fight against the Japanese invasion. The movie depicts the events leading up to the attack, including the failed attempt by the U.S. military to warn President Franklin D. Roosevelt of the impending attack.

The film's climax features a dramatic and intense depiction of the Pearl Harbor attack, which includes aerial battles, explosions, and chaos. Rafe and Danny both play key roles in the defense of Pearl Harbor, with Rafe flying his plane into the heart of the Japanese fleet to help turn the tide of the battle.

In the aftermath of the attack, Evelyn is killed by a Japanese bullet meant for Rafe. The film's final scenes show Rafe and Danny returning home, forever changed by their experiences in World War II. The movie ends with Rafe flying off into the sunset, symbolizing his newfound sense of purpose and freedom.

Throughout the film, Michael Bay's signature style is evident, with fast-paced action sequences, dramatic music, and a focus on visual effects. While some critics have panned the film for its over-the-top action scenes and historical inaccuracies, Pearl Harbor remains a beloved and iconic film that pays tribute to the bravery and sacrifice of those who fought in World War II.

Overall, Pearl Harbor is a sweeping epic romance that explores themes of love, loss, and loyalty. The film's performances, particularly from Ben Affleck and Josh Hartnett, are memorable, and the movie's historical significance makes it a must-see for fans of war dramas and romantic epics.

overview: A 9-year-old boy in a remote village in India begins a lifelong love affair with cinema when he bribes his way into a rundown movie palace and spends a summer watching movies from the projection booth.
tagline: The future belongs to storytellers.
title: Last Film Show
plot:
Last Film Show is a 2022 Indian coming-of-age drama film that explores the complexities of growing up and finding one's place in the world. The movie delves into the life of a young boy, who is struggling to cope with his family's past and his own sense of identity.

The film is set against the backdrop of India's rapid modernization and technological advancements, which serves as a metaphor for the protagonist's journey towards self-discovery. As he navigates through adolescence, he grapples with feelings of nostalgia, longing, and disconnection from his family's traditional values.

Through the protagonist's story, the film sheds light on the tensions between tradition and modernity, highlighting the difficulties faced by young people in India who are caught between preserving their cultural heritage and embracing the changing world around them. The movie also touches upon themes of loneliness, friendship, and the search for belonging, as the protagonist forms an unlikely bond with a fellow outsider.

Ultimately, Last Film Show is a poignant exploration of the human experience, capturing the fragility and beauty of adolescence in a rapidly evolving society.

overview: A look at the lives of the strong-willed women of the Weston family, whose paths have diverged until a family crisis brings them back to the Midwest house they grew up in, and to the dysfunctional woman who raised them.
tagline: Misery loves family
title: August: Osage County
plot:
August: Osage County is a 2013 drama film that delves into the dark and complex world of the Weston family, who are struggling to cope with their own personal demons. The movie masterfully weaves together themes of toxic relationships, family dynamics, and the destructive nature of secrets and lies.

At its core, August: Osage County is a powerful exploration of the devastating consequences of unchecked emotions and the corrosive effects of unresolved trauma. The film's portrayal of the Weston family's intricate web of relationships reveals a complex tapestry of love, anger, resentment, and betrayal, which ultimately leads to a downward spiral of self-destruction.

The movie also delves into the theme of female empowerment, as the strong-willed and fiercely independent Violet Weston (played by Meryl Streep) takes center stage, using her sharp wit and sarcasm to navigate the treacherous waters of family dynamics. However, beneath Violet's tough exterior lies a deep well of pain and vulnerability, which threatens to consume her at every turn.

Furthermore, August: Osage County sheds light on the destructive nature of secrets and lies, as the characters' inability to confront their past traumas and painful memories leads to a toxic cycle of recrimination and blame. The film's portrayal of this toxic dynamic is both haunting and thought-provoking, leaving the audience to ponder the long-term consequences of such behavior.

Ultimately, August: Osage County is a gripping drama that masterfully explores the complexities of human relationships, revealing the devastating consequences of unchecked emotions and unresolved trauma.

overview: When Rudy, an artifacts smuggler, goes to Jerusalem to rescue his kidnapped archeologist father, he faces deportation by a scheming police chief. Now, to find his dad and recover a sacred scroll, he'll have to outwit officials and a ruthless sect. With the help of a beautiful Israeli cop, Rudy battles a faction of religious zealots determined to see a holy war at all costs.
tagline: Unleash The Power.
title: The Order
plot:
The Order is a 2001 American action adventure film directed by Sheldon Lettich and written by Jean-Claude Van Damme, who also stars in a dual role. Charlton Heston appears as Professor Walter Finley, with Sofia Milos as police lieutenant Dalia Barr, Brian Thompson as the cult leader Cyrus Jacob, Ben Cross as police chief Ben Ner, and Vernon Dobtcheff as the hero's father. Set largely in Israel, the film was released direct to DVD in the United States on 12 March 2002.

The film opens in 1099 at the end of the First Crusade, as Crusaders sack Jerusalem and slaughter its inhabitants. Horrified by the violence, a Flemish knight named Charles Le Vaillant, played by Van Damme, founds a new religious order intended to unite Christians, Jews and Muslims. Proclaiming himself its leader and messiah, he writes the order's sacred texts, but during a journey to Syria his camp is attacked by Christian knights and he is killed. The final chapter of the order's scripture, which Le Vaillant had buried in a secret location, is lost in the desert.

In the present day, Rudy Cafmeyer, also played by Van Damme, is a thief and smuggler of valuable antiquities. After a botched robbery of a Fabergé egg that ends with the treasure being destroyed, he learns that his father Oscar, an archaeologist and museum curator, has travelled to Israel in pursuit of a secret he has discovered and has been kidnapped. Rudy flies to Israel to find him. His father's associate, Professor Walt Finley, gives him the key to a safe-deposit box in East Jerusalem before being shot dead by unknown attackers. Rudy's search brings him into contact with the Order, which has survived for centuries as a peaceful community, until the fanatical disciple Cyrus seizes control by having its leader killed and begins preaching an imminent holy war. Hounded by the hostile police chief Ben Ner and secretly helped by Lieutenant Dalia Barr, a former member of the Order, Rudy follows a map toward hidden tunnels beneath Jerusalem to rescue his father and stop Cyrus.

The film combines martial arts action with an Indiana Jones-style treasure hunt and touches on themes of religious fanaticism and coexistence in the Holy Land, featuring chases through the streets and markets of Jerusalem.

Released without a theatrical run in the United States, The Order belongs to the series of international action films Van Damme made in the early 2000s, reuniting him with Lettich, who had directed him in Lionheart and Double Impact.

overview: After learning that his terminally ill wife has six months to live, a man welcomes the support of his best friend who moves into their home to help out.
title: Our Friend
plot:
Our Friend is a 2019 American biographical drama directed by Gabriela Cowperthwaite and written by Brad Ingelsby, based on Matthew Teague's 2015 Esquire article "The Friend: Love Is Not a Big Enough Word." Jason Segel, Dakota Johnson and Casey Affleck star, with Gwendoline Christie and Cherry Jones in supporting roles. The film premiered as The Friend at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 6, 2019, and was released in the United States by Gravitas Ventures on January 22, 2021.

The film moves back and forth across thirteen years. In 2013, journalist Matt Teague and his wife Nicole prepare to tell their two young daughters that Nicole's ovarian cancer is terminal, while their best friend Dane Faucheux keeps the girls company outside. Flashbacks trace the friendship from its beginnings in New Orleans in 2000, when Nicole, a theater performer, introduces Matt to her college friend Dane, a camera operator with dreams of stand-up comedy. Over the years Matt's work as a war correspondent keeps him abroad for months, straining the marriage after the family settles in Fairhope, Alabama, while Dane drifts through dead-end jobs and, at one low point, contemplates ending his life while hiking at the Grand Canyon. The Teagues also weather Nicole's affair, with Dane helping them reconcile.

When Nicole is diagnosed in 2012 and begins chemotherapy, Dane offers to stay for a few weeks. As her condition worsens, he remains for months, taking on household duties and caring for the children, at the cost of his relationship with his girlfriend. Nicole draws up a bucket list that Matt and Dane help her complete, including serving as a grand marshal at Mardi Gras and writing letters for her daughters' future milestones. By 2014 her pain and confusion grow, and a hospice nurse is called in. After a final sunrise on the beach, Nicole dies with Matt and Dane at her side. Matt later writes the article that inspired the film as a tribute to his friend.

Released in early 2021, more than a year after its festival premiere, the film grossed under $800,000 against a $10 million budget. Critics praised the performances, particularly those of Affleck and Segel; Vanity Fair called it an effective, small-scale tearjerker, while Variety argued that it had sanitized the unpleasant realities of dying that Teague's essay had confronted.

overview: Gary Hart, former Senator of Colorado, becomes the front-runner for the Democratic presidential nomination in 1987. Hart's intelligence, charisma and idealism makes him popular with young voters, leaving him with a seemingly clear path to the White House. All that comes crashing down when allegations of an extramarital affair surface in the media, forcing the candidate to address a scandal that threatens to derail his campaign and personal life.
tagline: The week America went tabloid.
title: The Front Runner
plot:
The Front Runner is a biographical drama film that explores the life of Gary Hart, an American politician who was a prominent figure in the Democratic Party during the 1980s. The movie delves into the personal and professional struggles of Hart, as he navigates his rise to prominence and ultimately faces a scandal that threatens to destroy his career.

At its core, The Front Runner is a film about the corrupting influence of power and the consequences of one's actions. It examines how Hart's desire for success and recognition led him to engage in questionable behavior, including an extramarital affair with a young woman named Marianne Baker. As Hart's personal life becomes increasingly complicated, he finds himself at odds with his wife, Lee, who struggles to cope with the infidelity.

The film also touches on themes of identity and authenticity. Hart is portrayed as a charismatic figure who presents a polished public image, but behind closed doors, he grapples with feelings of inadequacy and insecurity. This tension between his public persona and private self serves as a catalyst for his downfall.

Furthermore, The Front Runner critiques the media's role in shaping public perception and the consequences of sensationalism. The film depicts how Hart's personal life is exploited by the press, leading to a vicious cycle of scandal and scrutiny that ultimately destroys his reputation.

Ultimately, The Front Runner is a nuanced exploration of the human condition, revealing the complexities and flaws of its protagonist as he navigates the treacherous waters of politics and personal relationships.

original_title: アイアンマン：ライズ・オブ・テクノヴォア
overview: Iron Man enlists the help of ruthless vigilante the Punisher to track down War Machine's murderer. All the while, he's being pursued by S.H.I.E.L.D. agents Black Widow and Hawkeye, who suspect his involvement in a recent terrorist plot.
tagline: Can Iron Man save the world when the world is against him?
title: Iron Man: Rise of Technovore
plot:
Iron Man: Rise of Technovore (Japanese: アイアンマン：ライズ・オブ・テクノヴォア) is a 2013 Japanese animated superhero film produced by Madhouse as a follow-up to the Marvel Anime television series. It was directed by Hiroshi Hamasaki, known for Texhnolyze and Shigurui, from a story by Brandon Auman. In the Japanese version Keiji Fujiwara voices Tony Stark, while the English dub features Matthew Mercer as Stark and Norman Reedus as the Punisher. It was released on home video in Japan and North America in April 2013.

While test-flying alongside War Machine, James "Rhodey" Rhodes, over the Utah desert, Iron Man is ambushed by a mysterious attacker who tries to destroy Tony Stark's new satellite, "The Howard," a global security system. Rhodey is apparently killed in the battle, and Tony sets out to find those responsible. S.H.I.E.L.D. and Nick Fury try to bring him in for questioning, believing his recklessness may be connected to the attack, but he evades them and goes to Pepper Potts for help.

Tony and Pepper discover that the terrorist organization A.I.M. has been researching techno-organic weaponry and trace one of its facilities to Karachi. There Iron Man crosses paths with the Punisher, who is hunting A.I.M. arms dealers, and the two reluctantly join forces. They learn that the attacker is Ezekiel Stane, the son of Tony's late enemy Obadiah Stane, who has fused himself with an experimental techno-organic substance and become a nearly unstoppable foe. As S.H.I.E.L.D. sends Hawkeye and Black Widow to capture Tony, now considered a fugitive, he must clear his name and stop Ezekiel, whose plans threaten both Stark's technology and S.H.I.E.L.D. itself. Along the way Tony relies on Pepper and makes use of his portable suitcase armor.

The film received mixed reviews. John Gholson of Movies.com criticized its dialogue as either vague or awkwardly on the nose and found the animation lacking excitement during action scenes. Tony Guerrero of Comic Vine gave it three out of five, praising its animation and colors and noting the appeal of including several Marvel characters in the story.

overview: When a man's only son goes missing, he travels to the town where his ex-wife lives in search of answers. To play a man whose life is clouded by mystery, McAvoy will not be given a script of dialogue.
tagline: A groundbreaking achievement in filmmaking where both actor and audience uncover a mystery at the same time.
title: My Son
plot:
My Son is a 2021 mystery thriller written and directed by Christian Carion, an English-language remake of his 2017 French film Mon garçon. James McAvoy stars as Edmond Murray, with Claire Foy as his former wife Joan, alongside Tom Cullen and Gary Lewis. As in the original, the lead actor was given no script or dialogue, only his character's backstory, and improvised his way through the shoot. Filmed in Scotland in late 2020, it was released by Peacock in September 2021 and later on The Roku Channel.

Edmond, a largely absent father, is summoned to the remote campsite where his young son Ethan has vanished. He briefly comforts Joan, joins a search party and is questioned by Inspector Roy. Visiting Joan's new partner Frank, he grows enraged on discovering that Frank's plans for a new home include no room for Ethan, and that Frank has given Joan a sedative to help her sleep. Suspecting Frank of involvement, Edmond knocks him unconscious. He is arrested but released without charge. Inspector Roy then quietly tells him that he has been removed from the case without explanation.

Searching Frank's phone, which he took during the fight, Edmond notices the same car lurking in the background of two videos of Ethan filmed two weeks apart. With help from Joan's brother, who works in insurance, he traces the owner to an isolated farm. There he ambushes the man, William O'Connor, ties him up and tortures him with a blowtorch until he confesses to photographing children outside schools for a paedophile kidnapping ring whose members select the children to be taken. O'Connor reveals that Ethan is being held at a hilltop lodge. Meanwhile, Joan arrives at the farm and finds another kidnapped girl unconscious in O'Connor's vehicle, and after taking her to hospital, follows Edmond's directions to the lodge and alerts Roy.

At the lodge, Edmond disables the kidnappers' vehicle as they prepare to move the drugged Ethan, then evades the men in a deadly game of cat and mouse, during which one of them accidentally shoots another. He finds his son and escapes with Joan, but is shot as they flee. Some time later, Edmond is allowed a brief outing with Ethan and Joan before Roy takes him back into custody, assuring him that the network is being dismantled and that the judge will likely be lenient.

Reviews were mixed to negative, with critics faulting the thin plot that resulted from the improvised approach; Rotten Tomatoes gave it 38%.

overview: After his mother’s death, Zucchini is befriended by a kind police officer, Raymond, who accompanies him to his new foster home filled with other orphans his age. There, with the help of his newfound friends, Zucchini eventually learns to trust and love as he searches for a new family of his own.
tagline: SOMETIMES WE CRY BECAUSE WE'RE HAPPY.
title: My Life as a Zucchini
plot:
My Life as a Zucchini is a heartwarming and poignant animated film that explores the complexities of childhood, family dynamics, and the struggles of growing up. The movie follows the story of Zeta, a young boy who is sent to live with his mother in a small apartment after his parents' divorce.

At its core, My Life as a Zucchini is a film about the fragility and beauty of childhood. It delves into the emotional turmoil that children often experience when their lives are turned upside down by adult decisions. The movie portrays Zeta's struggles to adjust to his new environment, navigate his relationships with his mother and her eccentric neighbors, and find his place in the world.

One of the main themes of the film is the importance of family and community. Despite the challenges they face, Zeta's mother and her neighbors form a tight-knit support system that helps him cope with his emotions and find solace in their company. The movie highlights the value of human connection and the ways in which relationships can provide comfort, love, and a sense of belonging.

The film also explores the theme of identity and self-discovery. As Zeta navigates his new surroundings, he begins to explore his own interests and passions, and discovers that he has a unique perspective on the world. The movie encourages viewers to think about what makes them who they are, and how their experiences shape their sense of self.

Furthermore, My Life as a Zucchini touches on the theme of grief and loss. Zeta's parents' divorce is a painful and difficult experience for him, and the movie portrays his emotional struggles in a way that is both authentic and relatable. The film suggests that it's okay to feel sad and angry, and that these emotions can be a catalyst for growth and healing.

Overall, My Life as a Zucchini is a beautifully crafted film that explores the complexities of childhood with sensitivity and nuance. It offers a powerful message about the importance of family, community, identity, and self-discovery, and encourages viewers to think about what makes them who they are.

overview: 12 year old Tinja is desperate to please her mother, a woman obsessed with presenting the image of a perfect family. One night, Tinja finds a strange egg. What hatches is beyond belief.
tagline: She's coming out of her shell
title: Hatching
plot:
Hatching (Finnish: Pahanhautoja, literally "Hatcher of Evil," a play on a Finnish idiom for nursing a grudge) is a 2022 Finnish psychological body horror film directed by Hanna Bergholm in her feature debut and written by Ilja Rautsi. Siiri Solalinna stars as Tinja, with Sophia Heikkilä as her mother, Jani Volanen and Reino Nordin.
