On the night of a local festival, Jimmy paints his face and sets out to take revenge on the four horsemen one by one, while Luc and Lola seek out El Niño, the leader of their satanic order, played by Hopper, to perform the marriage ceremony that will complete Luc's transformation. Jimmy must find a way to show Tanner the truth and stop the ritual before Luc's power becomes unstoppable, even after the crow that grants his invulnerability is wounded.

The film follows the established pattern of the franchise, in which a murdered man returns from the dead to avenge himself and his lover, set against a stylised desert landscape and a story steeped in religious imagery.

The Crow: Wicked Prayer was poorly received. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds an approval rating of 0 percent based on nine reviews. It was later reissued on home video in a double feature with The Crow: City of Angels.

overview: Being one of 101 takes its toll on Patch, who doesn't feel unique. When he's accidentally left behind on moving day, he meets his idol, Thunderbolt, who enlists him on a publicity campaign.
tagline: A new hero unleashed.
title: 101 Dalmatians II: Patch's London Adventure
plot:
101 Dalmatians II: Patch's London Adventure is a 2003 American animated direct-to-video adventure comedy produced by Walt Disney Television Animation. A sequel to Disney's 1961 animated feature One Hundred and One Dalmatians, it was directed by Jim Kammerud and Brian Smith, who also wrote the screenplay. The voice cast includes Bobby Lockwood as Patch, Barry Bostwick as the television star Thunderbolt, Jason Alexander as his sidekick Lil' Lightning, Martin Short as the beatnik artist Lars, and Susanne Blakeslee as Cruella de Vil. It was released on VHS and DVD by Buena Vista Home Entertainment in January 2003.

Some time after the events of the first film, Roger and Anita and their 101 Dalmatians prepare to move to the "Dalmatian Plantation," a country estate with room for the whole family. Patch, one of Pongo and Perdita's puppies, feels lost among his many siblings and longs to be special like his hero, Thunderbolt, the canine star of a television adventure series. When he learns of an open audition to appear on the show, he is accidentally left behind during the move and seizes the chance to go, but he fails to impress the producers.

Unknown to Thunderbolt, his jealous sidekick Lil' Lightning, tired of being overlooked, tricks the star into believing he is about to be written off the show and persuades him to perform real heroic deeds to keep his job, secretly hoping to become the star himself. Thunderbolt, impressed by how much Patch knows about his adventures, asks the puppy to help him. Meanwhile, Cruella de Vil, on probation and forbidden from buying furs, is obsessed with spots and finds a new outlet in Lars, a struggling artist who paints only spots. When Lars's art fails to satisfy her, she schemes to kidnap the Dalmatian puppies again to use them as his living canvas, and Patch must find the courage to be a hero himself while Pongo searches London for his missing son.

The film received moderately positive reviews, with a 67 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on a small number of reviews. Almar Haflidason of the BBC gave it three out of five stars and called it the best Disney direct-to-video sequel so far, and the voice work of Alexander and Short was among the elements highlighted in reviews.

overview: Two teenage girls discover that mermaids really do exist after a violent storm washes one ashore. The mermaid, a sassy creature named Aquamarine, is determined to prove to her father that real love exists, and enlists the girls' help in winning the heart of a handsome lifeguard.
tagline: A Fish-Out-Of-Water Comedy.
title: Aquamarine
plot:
Aquamarine is a 2006 American fantasy romantic comedy film directed by Elizabeth Allen Rosenbaum and written by Karen McCullah Lutz and Kirsten Smith. The movie stars Sara Paxton, Emma Roberts, and JoJo.

The story revolves around two teenage girls, Hailey (Sara Paxton) and Claire (Emma Roberts), who are best friends since childhood. They live in a small town in Florida, where they spend their days lounging on the beach and dreaming of adventure. However, their lives take an unexpected turn when they discover that a mermaid named Aquamarine (JoJo) has washed up on the shore.

Aquamarine is a beautiful but troubled young woman who was once a princess from a magical kingdom under the sea. She was banished by her evil stepmother and forced to live in the human world, where she struggles to adapt to modern life. Hailey and Claire are initially hesitant to help Aquamarine, but they soon become her unlikely friends.

As Aquamarine navigates her new surroundings, she begins to fall for a high school student named Han (Jake McDorman), who is immediately smitten with her. However, their budding romance is threatened when Aquamarine's evil stepmother, Ursula (Kirsten Dunst), returns from the sea and seeks revenge against Hailey and Claire.

Ursula has been searching for Aquamarine, intending to use her magical powers to take over the world. She manipulates Han into helping her capture Aquamarine, but Hailey and Claire intervene, using their own unique skills to outsmart Ursula and save their friend.

Throughout the movie, Hailey and Claire learn valuable lessons about friendship, loyalty, and believing in themselves. They also discover that they have more in common with Aquamarine than they initially thought, as they all share a deep sense of longing for adventure and connection.

In the end, Aquamarine is able to defeat Ursula and reclaim her rightful place on the throne of her underwater kingdom. Hailey and Claire are hailed as heroes, and they finally get their chance to experience the magic and wonder of the ocean world that Aquamarine introduced them to.

The movie features a mix of humor, adventure, and heartwarming moments, making it a delightful watch for audiences of all ages.

overview: When Juli meets Bryce in the second grade, she knows it's true love. After spending six years trying to convince Bryce the same, she's ready to give up - until he starts to reconsider.
tagline: You never forget your first love.
title: Flipped
plot:
Flipped is a 2010 American romantic comedy-drama co-written and directed by Rob Reiner, based on Wendelin Van Draanen's 2001 novel. Callan McAuliffe and Madeline Carroll star as Bryce and Juli, with Rebecca De Mornay, Anthony Edwards, John Mahoney, Penelope Ann Miller and Aidan Quinn. Set from the late 1950s, it alternates between its two leads' perspectives. Warner Bros. released it in American cinemas on August 6, 2010.

In 1957, seven-year-old Bryce Loski moves in across the street from Julianna "Juli" Baker. Juli falls for him at first sight, but Bryce is unnerved and spends the next years trying to avoid her; at one point he pretends to date a popular girl to discourage her, a ruse that backfires. When Bryce's grandfather Chet moves in with the family, he takes an interest in Juli, who climbs an old sycamore tree she loves in an attempt to stop it being cut down. Her father Richard eventually talks her down, then consoles her with a painting of the tree, and Chet shows Bryce a newspaper article about her stand, hoping to open his eyes.

Juli raises hens from a school science project and gives the Loskis free eggs, but she is hurt to discover that Bryce has been throwing them away, supposedly because the Bakers' unkempt yard makes his father doubt their safety. Embarrassed, Juli sets about fixing the yard, and Chet helps her, becoming her friend. When Bryce's father sneers at the Bakers, Chet points out that they rent the house and spend much of their money caring for Juli's mentally disabled uncle Daniel. Encouraged by Chet to look beyond appearances, Juli begins to question her feelings, and after overhearing Bryce appear to go along with his friend Garrett's mockery of her and Daniel, she loses interest in him. A strained family dinner leaves Bryce stung by her new indifference and seeing her as a person for the first time.

At the school's charity auction of "basket boys", Juli spends her egg money on another boy, Eddie, while Bryce is won by the popular Sherry. Realising that he is in love with Juli, Bryce tries to kiss her in front of everyone, and she flees in humiliation. He ends his friendship with Garrett and tries in vain to talk to her. Finally, with her father's permission, he plants a sycamore sapling in her front yard. Juli joins him, and as they plant it together they realise they have never truly talked.

The film drew lukewarm reviews and grossed about $4.3 million, but has since found a wider following.

overview: When Hellboy, Liz Sherman, and Abe Sapien are assigned to investigate the ghost-infested mansion of a publicity-hound billionaire, they uncover a plot to resurrect a beautiful yet monstrous vampire from Professor Bruttenholm’s past. But before they can stop her bloodbath, Hellboy will have to battle harpies, hellhounds, a giant werewolf, and even the ferocious goddess Hecate herself.
title: Hellboy Animated: Blood and Iron
plot:
Hellboy Animated: Blood and Iron is an action-packed animated film that delves into the darker aspects of Hellboy's world. The movie explores the theme of identity, as Hellboy struggles to reconcile his demonic heritage with his human upbringing. This internal conflict is reflected in his relationships with his adoptive father, Professor Trevor "Broom" Bruttenholm, and his love interest, Liz Sherman.

The film also touches on the idea of prejudice and acceptance, as Hellboy faces persecution from humans who fear and misunderstand him due to his demonic nature. This theme is particularly evident in the character of Sir Miles Archer, a human agent who is tasked with capturing Hellboy but ultimately becomes disillusioned with the government's motives.

Furthermore, Blood and Iron examines the consequences of playing with forces beyond one's control. The villainous Grigori, a powerful demon, serves as a catalyst for this theme, highlighting the dangers of meddling with ancient powers and the devastating repercussions that can follow.

Throughout the movie, these themes are woven together to create a narrative that is both action-packed and emotionally resonant. The film's dark tone and complex characters add depth to the Hellboy universe, making it a compelling watch for fans of the character.

overview: In New York City for their annual tradition of Christmas Eve debauchery, three lifelong best friends set out to find the Holy Grail of Christmas parties since their yearly reunion might be coming to an end.
tagline: Their past, present and future. All in one night.
title: The Night Before
plot:
The Night Before is a 2015 American Christmas comedy film directed by Jonathan Levine and written by Jonah Hill and Andrew Cohen. The movie stars Seth Rogen, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Anthony Mackie, Danny McBride, and Jillian Bell.

The story follows three lifelong friends, Evan (Seth Rogen), Chris (Joseph Gordon-Levitt), and Billy (Anthony Mackie), who are struggling to find their place in the world. The trio grew up together in New York City, but as they've grown older, they've drifted apart. They're all facing different challenges in their lives, from Evan's failed business venture to Chris's unfulfilling job.

The friends decide to embark on a Christmas Eve adventure to relive their childhood memories and recapture the magic of their youth. Their plan is to visit three iconic locations: the Empire State Building, the New York Public Library, and the Rockefeller Center Christmas tree. Along the way, they encounter various misadventures, including run-ins with eccentric characters, wild parties, and unexpected romantic entanglements.

As the night progresses, Evan becomes increasingly obsessed with finding a rare and expensive bottle of scotch, which he believes will be the perfect gift for his estranged father. Chris, on the other hand, is trying to reconnect with his high school sweetheart, who has recently moved back to New York. Billy, meanwhile, is struggling to come to terms with his own identity and sense of purpose.

Throughout their journey, the friends face numerous challenges, including a wild goose chase through Manhattan, a run-in with a group of rough-looking men, and a heart-to-heart conversation about growing up and moving on. Along the way, they also encounter a series of hilarious and memorable characters, including a eccentric old man (Morgan Freeman) who becomes their guide for the night.

As the night wears on, the friends begin to confront their own personal demons and insecurities. Evan must face his complicated relationship with his father, Chris must come to terms with his past mistakes, and Billy must learn to let go of his need for control. Through a series of comedic misadventures and heartfelt moments, the trio ultimately learns to reconnect with each other and find their way back to their childhood roots.

The movie ends on a hopeful note, with the friends reunited and ready to face the challenges of adulthood together. As they stand at the top of the Empire State Building, looking out over the city, they share a moment of quiet reflection and newfound appreciation for each other's company. The Night Before is a heartwarming and hilarious holiday film that explores the complexities of male friendship and the power of nostalgia to bring people back together.

overview: Ahead of a promotion, a police chief becomes entangled in a deadly incident and uncovers an intrigue fueled by grudge that threatens his colleagues.
title: Grudge
plot:
Grudge (Turkish: Kin) is a 2021 Turkish crime thriller film directed by Türkan Derya and written by Yılmaz Erdoğan, who also stars as a decorated Istanbul police chief inspector. Produced by BKM Film, it is a Turkish adaptation of the 2015 South Korean film Chronicles of Evil, directed by Baek Woon-hak. The cast also includes Ahmet Mümtaz Taylan, Cem Yiğit Üzümoğlu, Rüzgar Aksoy, Duygu Sarışın, Yosi Mizrahi, Elif Gizem Aykul and Metehan Parıltı. Its trailer was released on 13 September 2021, and the film premiered on Netflix on 8 October 2021.

The film opens with a poor man being arrested in a slum as his children watch in tears. Years later, Chief Inspector Harun (Erdoğan) is named police officer of the year for his work against Istanbul's murders, with a further promotion apparently imminent. After celebrating with his team, he takes a taxi home and dozes off, only to wake in a remote wooded area where the driver tries to kill him. Harun kills his attacker in the struggle but, instead of reporting it, wipes the scene and tells no one. The next morning the cabbie's body is found hanging from a construction crane in full view of police headquarters, and Harun's young protégé Tuncay (Üzümoğlu) quietly finds and hides the tie clip that colleagues had given Harun the night before. As his team, including his lieutenant Yadigar (Aksoy), investigates, Harun runs his own frantic inquiry, threatening old informants and accidentally killing a key witness in a shootout, and he uncovers links between the cabbie and the deaths of three fellow officers. A mysterious woman, Gülendam (Sarışın), then confesses to the killings and reveals to Harun that she is the daughter of a man wrongly arrested years earlier for a mass murder who later died; to avenge him she is killing the officers involved, and she asks Harun to kill his boss Cevat (Taylan). Released as a fantasist, she kills Cevat herself and, before taking her own life, reveals that her brother is Tuncay. After killing Yadigar, Tuncay confesses that he himself committed the poisonings for which their father was blamed, and kills himself. Exposed for the cabbie's death, Harun is led away in handcuffs before his son Aslan, completing Tuncay's revenge.

Reviews were mixed. Jade Budowski of Decider praised Erdoğan, a standout Sarışın and the tight script, while Roger Moore of Movie Nation found it decently plotted but hampered by obvious foreshadowing and a cautious ending.

overview: Dr. Jean Markham returns to the town she left as a teenager to take over her late father's medical practice. When a school-yard scuffle lands Charlie in her surgery, she invites him to visit the hives in her garden and tell his secrets to the bees, as she once did. The new friendship between the boy and the bee keeper brings his mother Lydia into Jean's world.
production_companies: Taking a Line for a Walk Productions
tagline: Some secrets are too powerful to keep
title: Tell It to the Bees
plot:
Tell It to the Bees is a 2018 British romantic period drama directed by Annabel Jankel and starring Anna Paquin and Holliday Grainger. Henrietta and Jessica Ashworth adapted the screenplay from Fiona Shaw's 2009 novel, moving its setting from Yorkshire to a small town in 1950s Scotland. The cast also includes Emun Elliott, Gregor Selkirk, Kate Dickie, Lauren Lyle and Steven Robertson, with Billy Boyd heard as the voice of the adult Charlie, who narrates the story.

Dr. Jean Markham (Paquin) returns to the town she left as a teenager, after a scandal over her love for another girl, to take over her late father's medical practice and his house, where she keeps beehives. Lydia Weekes (Grainger) is a mill worker struggling to pay the rent after her war-scarred husband Robert (Elliott) has walked out on her and their son Charlie (Selkirk). When the lonely, bullied Charlie is brought to Jean's surgery after a playground fight, she shows him the hives and teaches him the old custom of telling one's secrets to the bees. Lydia, wary at first, warms to the reserved doctor. After Lydia loses her job and she and Charlie are evicted, Jean takes them in and hires her as a housekeeper, and the two women slowly fall in love, a relationship that must stay hidden in a gossiping, judgmental community. Meanwhile Lydia's niece Annie (Lyle), the daughter of Robert's sister Pam (Dickie), becomes pregnant. In the final act, Jean must use her medical skills to save Annie after a botched backstreet abortion, while Robert, hostile and homophobic, confronts Lydia, and even the bees are drawn into the violent climax.

Developed with funding from the BFI Film Fund and Creative Scotland, the film was shot near Stirling from August 2017 and scored by Claire M. Singer. It premiered as a Special Presentation at the Toronto International Film Festival on 9 September 2018, opened in limited release in the United States on 3 May 2019 and reached British cinemas that July. Reviews were mixed, with a Metacritic score of 50: critics praised the performances and chemistry of Paquin and Grainger but faulted a didactic script and a melodramatic third act that departs sharply from the novel.

overview: Locked up for a minor crime, 19 year old JR quickly learns the harsh realities of prison life. Protection, if you can get it, is paramount. JR soon finds himself under the watchful eye of Australia's most notorious criminal, Brendan Lynch, but protection comes at a price.
tagline: Everyone gets what they deserve
title: Son of a Gun
plot:
Son of a Gun is an Australian crime drama film released in 2014, directed by Julian Ross and written by Brian King. The movie stars Brendan Gleeson, Fergus Reilly, and Ethan Hawke.

The main theme of the movie Son of a Gun revolves around the complexities of human relationships, particularly the bond between two brothers, Brendan (Fergus Reilly) and Charlie (Ethan Hawke). The story delves into their troubled past, which is marked by violence, abuse, and neglect. As the narrative unfolds, it becomes clear that the brothers' relationship is deeply rooted in a cycle of trauma and loyalty.

The film also explores themes of redemption, forgiveness, and the struggle for identity. Brendan, who has been institutionalized for most of his life due to violent outbursts, begins to question his past actions and seeks to make amends with those he has wronged. Through his journey, he grapples with the consequences of his actions and the impact they have had on his relationships.

Furthermore, Son of a Gun touches upon the theme of masculinity and the societal expectations placed upon men. Brendan's character is often seen as a symbol of toxic masculinity, having been conditioned to be violent and aggressive from a young age. As he navigates his way through life, he must confront these expectations and find a new path that allows him to break free from the cycle of violence.

The movie also features a subplot involving Charlie, who becomes embroiled in a crime scheme with a charismatic con artist (Brendan Gleeson). This storyline serves as a catalyst for Brendan's journey, forcing him to confront his past and re-evaluate his relationships.

Throughout the film, the director Julian Ross employs a non-linear narrative structure, jumping back and forth between different time periods. This technique adds to the complexity of the story, allowing the audience to piece together the characters' backstories and understand the motivations behind their actions.

Overall, Son of a Gun is a thought-provoking drama that explores themes of trauma, redemption, and identity through the complex relationship between two brothers.

overview: According to legend, an ominous entity known as the Queen of Spades can be summoned by performing an ancient ritual. Four teenagers summon the Queen of Spades, but they could never imagine the horrors that await them.
tagline: She will reign.
title: Queen of Spades
plot:
Queen of Spades is a 2021 Canadian supernatural horror film directed by Patrick White, a remake of the 2015 Russian film Queen of Spades: The Dark Rite. Produced with Epic Pictures and its genre label Dread, it stars Ava Preston as Anna, Kaelen Ohm as Mary, Daniel Kash as Smirnov, and Jamie Bloch, Eric Osborne and Nabil Rajo. The Queen of Spades figure traces back to Alexander Pushkin's 1833 short story and Tchaikovsky's opera, and has since become a Russian urban legend similar to Bloody Mary.

According to the legend, the Queen of Spades can be summoned by drawing a door and a staircase on a mirror in lipstick and ordering her three times to show herself. If the rite is performed correctly, the specter appears and grants a wish, but she is often more inclined to harm those who call her. In Ottawa, four teenage friends watch a young man jump to his death from a rooftop, muttering "Queen of Spades" as he dies. Curious rather than shaken, they research the legend online and find instructions for the ritual, which says the youngest member of the group must perform it, so thirteen-year-old Anna is chosen. At first nothing seems to happen and they carry on with their lives, but soon they experience disturbing visions and strange events, and one of the boys discovers a mysterious bloody gash on his arm before dying of a heart attack. When Mary, a single mother whose child is among the group, learns about the rite, she seeks out Smirnov, a Russian expert in the supernatural who has written a book about the legend, hoping he can stop the Queen from claiming more victims. Smirnov's attempts include trying to transfer the demon's spirit into a cat.

Queen of Spades was released on video on demand in the United States and Canada in June 2021. Reviews were mixed to negative. Matt Patti of Film Festival Today gave it two and a half stars out of four, finding it unoriginal and burdened by weak early dialogue and rushed exposition, but an effective paranormal horror film with genuinely frightening jump scares and a creepy demon design. Eric Hillis of The Movie Waffler was far harsher, calling it lacklustre low-budget horror that reduces the legend to a third-rate Candyman knockoff with unremarkable deaths and a lazily designed demon, though he felt Ohm gave a performance worthy of a far better movie.

overview: Su Qi-Er, a wealthy man living during the Qing Dynasty who loses his fortune and reputation as a result of a conspiracy against him. After being forced out onto the streets, Su dedicates his life to martial arts and reemerges as a patriotic hero known as the "King of Beggars."
tagline: "King Of Beggars"
title: True Legend
plot:
True Legend (Chinese: 苏乞儿) is a 2010 Chinese-Hong Kong martial arts film directed by Yuen Woo-ping, his first film as director since Tai Chi Boxer in 1996. Vincent Zhao stars as the Chinese folk hero Su Can, also known as Beggar So, the legendary master of drunken boxing, with Zhou Xun, Andy On and Jay Chou. Gordon Liu, Leung Kar-yan, Michelle Yeoh and David Carradine, in one of his final roles, make cameo appearances. Set in late Qing dynasty China, the film was released in both 2D and 3D.

Su Can is a celebrated general who resigns from military service to devote himself to martial arts and family life. His adoptive brother Yuan Lie has long been jealous of him. Years earlier, Su's father killed Yuan's father, who had turned to evil, and then raised Yuan as his own son. Five years after Su's retirement, he has married Yuan's sister Ying and they have a young son, Feng. Yuan returns as a powerful governor, having mastered a deadly technique known as the Five Venom Fists and fused armor into his body, and he kills Su's father in revenge.

When Su confronts him, Yuan defeats him easily and throws him into a river, and Ying leaps in after him. Rescued by a healer, the couple survive, but Su is badly crippled and turns to drink. With Ying's support he slowly rebuilds his strength in seclusion, training against imagined opponents, the God of Wushu and an old sage, and develops a new fighting style. He returns to rescue his son, but the cost is devastating, and grief drives him into a period of madness during which he wanders the streets with Feng as a beggar. During this time he perfects the drunken fist style that will make him a legend, and in the final act he is drawn into a brutal series of fights against foreign wrestlers.

The film received moderately positive reviews, with a 63 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 62. It won the Lotus Action Asia award at the 13th Deauville Asian Film Festival and was praised for Yuen's choreography; Charlie Jane Anders of Gizmodo's io9 called it pure old-school awesomeness, comparing it to Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon, although some critics found its two halves uneven.

overview: A familiar-looking group of teenagers find themselves being stalked by a more-than-vaguely recognizable masked killer! As the victims begin to pile up and the laughs pile on, none of your favorite scary movies escape the razor-sharp satire of this outrageously funny parody!
tagline: No mercy. No shame. No sequel.
title: Scary Movie
plot:
Scary Movie is a horror comedy film released in 2000, directed by Keenen Ivory Wayans and written by Shawn Wayans and Marlon Wayans. The movie is a parody of popular horror films, particularly Scream (1996) and I Know What You Did Last Summer (1997).

The story begins with Cindy Campbell (Anna Faris), a high school student who is dating Bobby (Timothy Stack). On the night of their prom, they are involved in a car accident that kills a man. The next day, Cindy receives a mysterious phone call from an unknown number, warning her to "get out while you still can." Unbeknownst to Cindy, this is a reference to the infamous "Ghostface" killer from Scream.

As Cindy tries to move on with her life, she becomes the target of a series of murders and stalkings. She soon discovers that she has become the focus of a serial killer known as Ghostface (Brendan Sexton III), who is using a similar M.O. to the one in Scream.

Meanwhile, Bobby's friend Ray (Reginald VelJohnson) becomes suspicious of Cindy's involvement with the murders and starts investigating her past. He discovers that she was involved in the car accident and believes that she may be connected to the killings.

As the body count rises, Cindy teams up with Ray to uncover the identity of Ghostface. Along the way, they encounter a series of wacky characters, including a bumbling police officer (James Woods) and a creepy hotel clerk (Matthew Lillard).

Throughout the movie, the Wayans brothers cleverly parody various horror tropes, from the "final girl" trope to the use of jump scares. The film's humor is often irreverent and self-aware, with the characters frequently breaking the fourth wall to address the audience.

In the end, Cindy discovers that Ghostface is actually her boyfriend Bobby, who has been using a mask and a fake identity to cover his tracks. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Bobby was the one responsible for the murders all along, and Cindy must use her wits to outsmart him and escape alive.

Overall, Scary Movie is a hilarious and clever parody of horror movies, with plenty of laughs and surprises along the way. The film's success spawned a series of sequels and spin-offs, cementing its place as a cult classic in the world of horror comedy.

overview: Momoko is an ordinary girl, living an ordinary life. Ordinary, that is, if you define ordinary as wearing elaborate lolita dresses from the Rococo period in 18th Century France. However, when punk girl and self-styled 'Yanki' Ichiko comes calling, her days as 'ordinary' are most certainly numbered...
tagline: The extraordinary adventures of a Lolita-look aficionado and a tough biker gang chick.
title: Kamikaze Girls
plot:
Kamikaze Girls is a 2004 Japanese romantic comedy film that explores the complexities of female friendship and identity. The story revolves around two unlikely friends, Haruko Morita and Natsuki Shimizu, who couldn't be more different in terms of their personalities, interests, and backgrounds.

At its core, Kamikaze Girls delves into the theme of self-discovery and empowerment, particularly for women. Haruko, a tomboyish and free-spirited young woman, is struggling to find her place in the world after being rejected by her family due to her unconventional lifestyle. Natsuki, on the other hand, is a more traditional and conservative girl who is trying to navigate her own identity amidst societal expectations.

Through their friendship, Haruko and Natsuki learn to appreciate each other's differences and support each other in their individual journeys of self-discovery. The film showcases how their bond helps them to break free from the constraints of societal norms and forge their own paths in life.

The movie also touches on themes of identity, cultural heritage, and the complexities of female relationships. Haruko's struggles with her Japanese heritage and Natsuki's desire to fit into traditional Japanese society serve as a backdrop for exploring these themes. The film ultimately presents a message of acceptance, inclusivity, and the power of female friendship in overcoming adversity.

Overall, Kamikaze Girls is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of the complexities of female identity, friendship, and self-discovery, set against the vibrant backdrop of Tokyo's fashion and pop culture scene.

overview: Set in the small town of Devil's Gate, North Dakota, the film examines the disappearance of a local woman and her young son. Schull plays an FBI agent who helps the local sheriff search for answers. Partnering with a deputy , they track down the missing woman's husband and find that nothing is as it seems.
tagline: Every family has its secrets.
title: Devil's Gate
plot:
Devil's Gate is a 2017 American supernatural horror and science fiction film directed by Clay Staub in his feature debut, from a screenplay he wrote with Peter Aperlo. Amanda Schull stars as FBI Special Agent Daria Francis, with Shawn Ashmore as Deputy Colt Salter, Milo Ventimiglia as the farmer Jackson Pritchard, Bridget Regan as his wife Maria, Jonathan Frakes as Sheriff Gruenwell, and Javier Botet. In some territories it was released as Abduction.

In the small farming town of Devil's Gate, North Dakota, Daria arrives to investigate the disappearance of Maria Pritchard and her young son Jonah. The sheriff wants her to leave Jackson, the boy's ill-tempered and devout father, alone, but she enlists the friendly Colt, and after Maria's sister and mother describe Jackson's worsening temper and Jonah's sketchbook turns up full of disturbing drawings, the pair drive out to the remote Pritchard farm. They find it newly booby-trapped, with a stranded motorist's car outside and Maria's car hidden in the barn. After a standoff, Daria handcuffs Jackson, then discovers what he is keeping in his cellar: a strange humanoid creature locked in a cage. Jackson insists it is a demon like those that took his family, and that he means to trade it for them.

Their phones and car die, and an unnatural lightning storm forces them back into the house. Maria reappears and accuses Jackson of giving Jonah to the beings, whom he had prayed to as angels when the boy fell ill. Daria comes to realize that the visitors are aliens who are colonizing Earth because their own world is dying, replacing people with copies, and that Jackson himself has been replaced. Jonah is the first naturally born human-alien hybrid. One of the beings kills Colt, and when Jonah is returned in a flash of light, Jackson prepares to shoot him, only for Maria to kill Jackson first. The authorities insist on a story that leaves out the aliens, and some time later Jonah shows his mother a hidden collection of the discs used to summon the beings, telling her that it is time for the harvest.

The film premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival on 24 April 2017 and was released by IFC Midnight in January 2018. Reviews were mostly negative, with a 38% rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Critics noted competent effects and photography, and The Village Voice called Staub a formidable director of action, but most found the dialogue weak and the story derivative.

original_title: The Beatles: Eight Days a Week - The Touring Years
overview: The Beatles stormed through Europe's music scene in 1963, and, in 1964, they conquered America. Their groundbreaking world tours changed global youth culture forever and, arguably, invented mass entertainment as we know it today. All the while, the group were composing and recording a series of extraordinarily successful singles and albums. However the relentless pressure of such unprecedented fame, that in 1966 became uncontrollable turmoil, led to the decision to stop touring. In the ensuing years The Beatles were then free to focus on a series of albums that changed the face of recorded music.
tagline: The band you know. The story you don't.
title: The Beatles: Eight Days a Week - The Touring Years
plot:
The Beatles: Eight Days a Week - The Touring Years is a documentary film that explores the early years of The Beatles' career, focusing on their time as a touring band. At its core, the movie delves into the themes of creative freedom, artistic expression, and the pressures of fame.

As the film chronicles the band's rise to international stardom, it highlights the tension between their desire for independence and the commercial demands of their record label, Brian Epstein's NEMS Enterprises. The documentary showcases how The Beatles navigated this delicate balance, often finding innovative ways to express themselves through music and performance.

The movie also touches on the theme of youthful rebellion, as The Beatles' music and style reflected the changing social and cultural landscape of the 1960s. Their music was a reflection of their own experiences, values, and aspirations, which resonated with young people around the world.

Furthermore, the film explores the theme of camaraderie and friendship within the band, showcasing the strong bonds between John, Paul, George, and Ringo as they navigated the challenges of fame together. The documentary provides a unique insight into the inner workings of the band's relationships, revealing moments of humor, affection, and mutual support.

Ultimately, The Beatles: Eight Days a Week - The Touring Years is a film about the power of music to bring people together and transcend boundaries. It celebrates the creativity, energy, and enthusiasm of The Beatles during their formative years as a touring band, offering a captivating glimpse into one of the most pivotal moments in rock history.

overview: The Undertaker has set a trap for the decorated tag team The New Day at his mansion. What they don't know: The Undertaker's mansion is an extreme Haunted House, packed to the brim with supernatural challenges. It's up to viewers to decide the fate of these poor souls trying to survive the wrath of The Undertaker.
title: Escape the Undertaker
plot:
Escape the Undertaker is a 2021 American interactive horror comedy special produced by WWE Studios for Netflix, in which viewers make choices that shape the story, in the tradition of the streaming service's earlier interactive titles such as Black Mirror: Bandersnatch and You vs. Wild. It stars Mark Calaway as his wrestling persona the Undertaker, alongside the tag team The New Day, made up of Kofi Kingston (Kofi Sarkodie-Mensah), Xavier Woods (Austin Watson) and Big E (Ettore Ewen). Aimed at families and released with a TV-G rating, it was launched in October 2021 as a Halloween-season offering, and each viewing runs roughly half an hour.

In the story, the Undertaker has set a trap for The New Day at his mansion. The three decorated champions travel to the Dead Man's house hoping to steal his urn, a relic said to hold supernatural powers, because they want to feel its power for themselves. What they do not know is that the mansion is an extreme haunted house filled with supernatural challenges. When Big E touches the urn, his soul begins to be drained away, turning their quest into a race against time. The trio must investigate the rooms of the eerie house while the Undertaker watches their every move from a basement control room full of old computers and monitors. Viewers choose among two or three options at various points, which usually switch the story to follow a different member of the group, so that Xavier faces his fears or Kofi wanders off alone, and one key decision about halfway through determines whether the heroes escape. At the very first choice, viewers can also tell the Undertaker they are too scared to take part, which ends the special at once with a joke.

The special received lukewarm reviews. Mat Elfring of GameSpot rated it mediocre, describing it as a fun but not fully realized idea that is rushed, with limited replay value and interactivity that disappoints because most choices only show events from a different character's perspective while the outcome hinges on a single decision. He nevertheless praised it as lighthearted entertainment that parents could enjoy with their children, highlighting the natural, zany chemistry and jokes of The New Day, such as Big E repeatedly calling the wrestler "Uncle Taker", and its WWE Easter eggs, while finding the Undertaker's role the weak link. Other reviewers similarly considered it light, low-stakes fun let down by its thin branching.

overview: Five young New Yorkers throw their friend a going-away party the night that a monster the size of a skyscraper descends upon the city. Told from the point of view of their video camera, the film is a document of their attempt to survive the most surreal, horrifying event of their lives.
tagline: Some thing has found us.
title: Cloverfield
plot:
Cloverfield is a 2008 monster horror film directed by Matt Reeves and produced by J.J. Abrams' production company Bad Robot Productions, in association with Universal Pictures.

The film begins on March 12, 2008, in New York City, where we meet our protagonist, Rob Hawkins (played by Michael Stuhlbarg), a young man who is preparing to leave for his job at a financial firm in Tokyo. However, before he can depart, he receives an unexpected phone call from his brother, Jason (played by T.J. Miller), who informs him that their father has died.

As Rob tries to make sense of the situation, we are introduced to other main characters: Marlena Heisencutter (played by Lizzy Caplan), a friend of Rob's who is also preparing for her own trip abroad; Matty Reynolds (played by Mike Vogel), a friend of Jason's who is trying to get in touch with his brother; and Hud (played by Adam Brody), a friend of the group who is initially hesitant to join them on their adventure.

The group decides to embark on a road trip from New York City to New Jersey, where they plan to meet up with Jason. However, as they drive through the city, they notice that something is amiss - buildings are damaged, cars are overturned, and there is a sense of chaos in the air.

As they continue their journey, they come across a massive monster, known as "Cloverfield," which is wreaking havoc on the city. The creature is enormous, with glowing red eyes and a powerful roar that can be heard for miles. The group soon realizes that Cloverfield is not just a mindless beast - it's a highly intelligent and destructive force that seems to be targeting specific locations.

As the group tries to escape the monster's path, they begin to uncover clues about its origins and motivations. They discover that Cloverfield is an extraterrestrial creature that has been awakened by human activity in the city. The creature is drawn to the sounds of human communication, which it uses to navigate and hunt its prey.

Throughout the film, the group faces numerous challenges as they try to survive the monster's attacks. Along the way, they also experience personal struggles and conflicts, including romantic tensions and family drama.

As the night wears on, the group finds themselves trapped in a deserted warehouse, where they are forced to confront Cloverfield head-on. In a tense and suspenseful climax, they manage to fend off the creature long enough for Rob's brother Jason to escape with his life.

The film ends with Rob, Marlena, Matty, and Hud watching as Jason drives away from the city, leaving behind the devastation and destruction caused by Cloverfield. As they reflect on their experience, we see a series of news reports and footage of the monster's rampage, which serves as a reminder that the world is not always a safe or predictable place.

Overall, Cloverfounder is a tense and thrilling horror film that explores themes of friendship, survival, and the human condition in the face of catastrophic events.

original_title: LEGO: The Adventures of Clutch Powers
overview: Clutch Powers ventures on a mission assigned to him by his boss to solve the chaos that occurred on the Space Police prison planet.
tagline: First Full-Length LEGO Movie!
title: LEGO: The Adventures of Clutch Powers
plot:
Lego: The Adventures of Clutch Powers is a 2010 computer-animated action comedy, the first feature-length film based on the Lego toy line. It was directed by Howard E. Baker and released direct to home video. The voice cast includes Ryan McPartlin as the title character, along with Yvonne Strahovski, Roger Rose, Jeff Bennett, Paul Michael Glaser, Gregg Berger, Christopher Emerson and Alex Désert.

Clutch Powers is a daring explorer based in Lego City. The film opens as he tunnels underground to find a Power Crystal and wakes the Crystal King, a rock monster. After a chase, Clutch realizes that the crystal he is carrying is actually the king's baby and returns it, earning a real Power Crystal as a reward. Back in Lego City, his boss Kjeld Playwell assigns him to lead a team on his next mission: firefighter Brick Masterson, biologist Peg Mooring and engineer Bernie von Beam. Their first task is to investigate a breakout on the Space Police prison planet.

Clutch prefers to work alone, and the mismatched team struggles to cooperate. On the prison planet they are attacked by the unseen wizard Mallock the Malign, who escapes along with two other criminals, stealing the team's ship and sabotaging the rest. Clutch builds a new ship by himself and later admits that he was distracted during the mission by a symbol connected to one of the criminals, Omega. Playwell explains that Mallock once terrorized the medieval planet Ashlar, whose king, Revet, sacrificed himself to protect the realm, leaving his inexperienced son, Prince Varen, as heir.

On Ashlar, the team finds that Mallock has seized control with an army of skeletons and goblins. While Peg, Brick and Bernie build a battle chariot, Clutch sets off to persuade Varen to fight. Along the way he outwits a riddle-loving troll named Hogar, who becomes an ally and tells him of the late king's golden sword, the key to defeating Mallock. Varen at first feels unworthy, but with encouragement he and his knights join the battle. Clutch and Varen are captured in Mallock's castle, until Peg calls on a dragon she has befriended to free them, and Varen finds the courage to wield his father's sword.

The film was praised for its action and humor, though its animation and product placement drew criticism. It inspired a 4D attraction, A Clutch Powers 4D Adventure, which ran at several Legoland parks from 2010 until it was replaced in 2016, and Clutch Powers later appeared as a recurring character in the animated series Ninjago.

overview: A former Marine turned doorman at a luxury New York City high-rise must outsmart and battle a group of art thieves and their ruthless leader — while struggling to protect her sister's family. As the thieves become increasingly desperate and violent, the doorman calls upon her deadly fighting skills to end the showdown.
tagline: Be careful who you trust.
title: The Doorman
plot:
The Doorman is a 2020 American action thriller directed by Ryuhei Kitamura. Ruby Rose stars as Ali Gorski, a former Marine who takes a job as a doorman at a luxury building, with Jean Reno as the criminal mastermind Victor Dubois, Aksel Hennie as Borz, and Rupert Evans as her brother-in-law Jon Stanton. The film follows Ali as she defends her family from a gang of thieves searching for valuable artworks hidden inside the building. It was first released theatrically in Russia on 1 October 2020, followed by a direct-to-digital release in the United States on 9 October 2020.

In Bucharest, Marine Gunnery Sergeant Ali Gorski is protecting a convoy carrying an ambassador's family when it is ambushed by mercenaries. Despite fighting fiercely, she cannot prevent the deaths of the ambassador, his wife and their daughter. Traumatised, Ali leaves the Marines and returns to New York City, where her uncle Pat helps her get a job as a doorman at the Carrington, an elegant old apartment building.

Ali discovers that the building is also home to Jon Stanton, the widower of her late sister, and his children, Max and Lily. She and Jon had an affair while her sister was alive, which was partly why Ali enlisted, and she reluctantly accepts an invitation to their Easter dinner. Over the holiday weekend, her fellow doorman Borz kills Pat, revealing himself to be part of a crew led by Victor Dubois. The thieves lock down the building in search of a collection of stolen paintings hidden somewhere in its walls, and they torture an elderly resident, living under an assumed name, who once concealed them. Learning that the paintings are in the apartment now occupied by the Stantons, the gang takes Jon and Lily hostage while Max escapes. Ali must use her combat training to fight her way through the building, outwitting the mercenaries floor by floor, with Max helping her through clever tricks such as sending a message in Morse code over the building's intercom.

The film borrows the single-building siege structure of Die Hard, with a female protagonist at its centre, and it is built around a series of close-quarters fight scenes staged by Kitamura.

The Doorman received negative reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds an approval rating of about 24 percent; the consensus says that it only leads to an assortment of tired clichés that serve as reminders of better action films.

overview: Afghanistan. War correspondent Elsa Casanova is taken hostage by the Taliban. Faced with her imminent execution, a Special Forces unit is dispatched to free her. In some of the world’s most breathtaking yet hostile landscapes, a relentless pursuit begins between her kidnappers who have no intention of letting their prey escape them and a group of soldiers who risk their lives in pursuit of their single aim – to bring her home alive. This strong, independent woman and these men of duty are thrown together and forced to confront situations of great danger that inextricably bind them – emotionally, violently and intimately.
tagline: Survival. Honor. Sacrifice.
title: Special Forces
plot:
Special Forces (French: Forces spéciales) is a 2011 French war action film directed by Stéphane Rybojad, starring Diane Kruger, Djimon Hounsou, Benoît Magimel, Denis Ménochet, Mehdi Nebbou, Raphaël Personnaz and Tchéky Karyo. Shot on location in France, Djibouti and Tajikistan, it follows a team of elite French commandos on a desperate hostage-rescue mission on the border between Afghanistan and Pakistan.

Elsa Casanova, a French journalist based in Kabul, publishes an article branding the warlord Zaief "the butcher of Kabul". Her informant Maina warns her that Zaief will seek revenge, and returns to him expecting to be killed in an honour killing. Elsa, refusing to abandon her, tries to save her with the help of her friend and colleague Amen, who has urged her to leave the country. Zaief's men ambush and capture them both. Amen tells Elsa to show no fear, but she breaks down when their friend Salemani is brutally murdered in front of her, and Zaief releases a video of the killing that reaches the French government.

A small team of French special forces operators, drawn mainly from the naval commandos, is sent in to rescue the hostages. They locate Zaief's hideout in Pakistan and witness Maina's execution before freeing Elsa and Amen. But a bullet destroys their radio during the escape, leaving them unable to contact their base or call for extraction. With no other choice, the commandos set out on foot across the mountains toward the Khyber Pass and the Afghan border, pursued relentlessly by Zaief and his gunmen.

The journey becomes a brutal ordeal. In a village where Elsa asks for shelter, one commando is killed by a sniper, and when Zaief's fighters arrive the warlord himself kills Amen. One by one the soldiers fall: the team's marksman dies drawing the enemy away, another succumbs to his wounds in a snowstorm, and a fourth is killed in a further attack, in which the commando Kovax finally kills Zaief after the warlord seizes Elsa as a hostage. An avalanche then strikes the survivors; Kovax saves Elsa and his wounded comrade Tic-Tac but breaks his leg, and the two men persuade Elsa to go on alone. Exhausted, she reaches a road and is rescued, then refuses to be sent home, and Admiral Guezennec carries her to a helicopter to lead the search that finds both men alive.

The film was poorly received by English-language critics, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 15% approval; the Los Angeles Times called it a leaden, video-game-style war film.

overview: Ray and Ken, two hit men, are in Bruges, Belgium, waiting for their next mission. While they are there they have time to think and discuss their previous assignment. When the mission is revealed to Ken, it is not what he expected.
tagline: Shoot first. Sightsee later.
title: In Bruges
plot:
In Bruges is a 2008 dark comedy film directed by Martin McDonagh, written by McDonagh, and produced by Blueprint Pictures.

The movie begins with Ray (Colin Farrell) and Ken (Brendan Gleeson), two Irish hitmen, who are sent to Bruges, Belgium by their boss, Harry Waters (Ralph Ineson), to lay low for a while after a botched job in London. The story takes place over the course of three days.

Ray is struggling with his own guilt and emotional turmoil following the death of an innocent bystander during the botched hit. Ken, on the other hand, seems more at peace with himself, having recently lost his wife to cancer. As they explore the medieval city of Bruges, Ray becomes increasingly agitated and withdrawn, while Ken tries to help him see things from a different perspective.

The two men's interactions are filled with witty banter, sarcasm, and dark humor, as they navigate their complicated relationship and try to find ways to cope with their emotions. Along the way, they encounter a local priest, Father Peter (Paddy Considine), who tries to help Ray come to terms with his past mistakes.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Ken is hiding secrets of his own, including a mysterious phone call from an unknown number that suggests he may be in danger. Meanwhile, Ray's emotional state continues to deteriorate, leading him to lash out at those around him, including Ken and Father Peter.

In the climax of the film, Ray's past mistakes come back to haunt him, and he is forced to confront the consequences of his actions. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Ken has been playing a long game all along, using their time in Bruges to manipulate Ray into taking care of a problem for him.

The ending of the film is both poignant and darkly comedic, as Ray finally finds some measure of peace and closure, but not before Ken's true intentions are revealed. The movie ends with Ray walking away from the city, symbolically leaving his past behind, while Ken remains in Bruges, waiting for his next move.

Throughout the film, McDonagh explores themes of guilt, redemption, and the complexities of human relationships. The film features outstanding performances from its cast, particularly Gleeson and Farrell, who bring depth and nuance to their characters. The cinematography is also noteworthy, capturing the beauty and charm of Bruges while also conveying the dark undertones of the story.

Overall, In Bruges is a thought-provoking and entertaining film that explores the complexities of human nature through the lens of two troubled hitmen.

overview: Skeeter Bronson is a down-on-his-luck guy who's always telling bedtime stories to his niece and nephew. But his life is turned upside down when the fantastical stories he makes up for entertainment inexplicably turn into reality. Can a bewildered Skeeter manage his own unruly fantasies now that the outrageous characters and situations from his mind have morphed into actual people and events?
tagline: Whatever they dream up... he has to survive.
title: Bedtime Stories
plot:
Bedtime Stories is a 2008 American fantasy comedy film directed by Adam Shankman and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie stars Adam Sandler, Keri Russell, and Guy Pearce.

The story begins with Skeeter Bronson (Adam Sandler), a struggling hotel handyman who dreams of becoming an author. He lives in a small apartment with his wife, Maggie (Keri Russell), and their two children, Max (Taylor Lautner) and Sugar (Bailee Madison). Despite his creative ambitions, Skeeter's life is mundane and unfulfilling.

One night, while working at the hotel, Skeeter stumbles upon an old book of bedtime stories that belonged to a former guest. As he reads through the book, he discovers that the stories come to life when no one is looking. The characters from the stories begin to invade his reality, causing chaos and confusion in his daily life.

Skeeter's world becomes increasingly surreal as the characters from the stories start to interact with him and his family. He must navigate this new reality while trying to keep his sanity intact. Meanwhile, Maggie starts to notice strange occurrences around the house, which puts a strain on their relationship.

As Skeeter tries to find a way to stop the characters from invading his life, he also begins to write his own bedtime stories. However, his writing skills are not as magical as those of the book's author, and his stories start to take on a life of their own.

The plot thickens when Skeeter discovers that the book is actually a magical portal created by a former guest who was a writer himself. The guest had used the book to bring his characters to life, but he had also left behind a curse that would destroy the world if the stories were not completed.

Skeeter realizes that he must finish writing the stories and complete the curse in order to save the world. With the help of his family and some unexpected allies, Skeeter embarks on a journey to write the final story and restore balance to his reality.

In the end, Skeeter completes the story, and the characters from the book return to their own world. The movie ends with Skeeter's family returning to normal life, but not before Skeeter realizes that he has found his true calling as an author.

Throughout the movie, Adam Sandler delivers a comedic performance as Skeeter Bronson, bringing humor and heart to the story. The film's blend of fantasy and comedy makes it an entertaining ride for audiences of all ages.

overview: Kyung-Chul is a dangerous psychopath who kills for pleasure. Soo-Hyun, a top-secret agent, decides to track down the murderer himself. He promises himself that he will do everything in his power to take vengeance against the killer, even if it means that he must become a monster himself.
tagline: Abandon all compassion.
title: I Saw the Devil
plot:
I Saw the Devil is a 2010 South Korean psychological thriller film directed by Lee Dae-hwan and written by Lee Dae-hwan and Park Chan-wook. The movie stars Lee Byung-hun, Choi Min-sik, and Kim So-eun.

The story begins with the introduction of Kim Soo-hyun (Lee Byung-hun), a secret agent working for the National Intelligence Service (NIS). He is tasked with tracking down and killing his brother's killer, who brutally murdered his family. The killer is revealed to be Lee Woo-jin (Choi Min-sik), a wealthy and influential businessman.

As Soo-hyun delves deeper into Woo-jin's life, he discovers that the latter has a seemingly perfect life, with a beautiful wife and children. However, as Soo-hyun gets closer to Woo-jin, he realizes that his brother's killer is not what he seems. Woo-jin's facade begins to crumble, revealing a complex web of deceit and corruption.

Meanwhile, Woo-jin becomes aware of Soo-hyun's pursuit and starts to toy with him, pushing the agent to his limits. The cat-and-mouse game between the two intensifies as they engage in a series of gruesome and violent confrontations.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Woo-jin is not just a mindless killer but a calculating and intelligent individual who has planned every move meticulously. Soo-hyun, on the other hand, is driven by his desire for revenge and justice.

The plot takes a dark and unexpected turn as Soo-hyun's obsession with Woo-jin consumes him. He becomes increasingly unhinged, leading to a series of tragic events that ultimately lead to the downfall of both characters.

In the end, Soo-hyun's quest for revenge is met with devastating consequences, leaving the audience questioning the morality of his actions and the true nature of justice. The film's climax is both shocking and thought-provoking, leaving viewers to ponder the complexities of human nature and the blurred lines between good and evil.

Throughout the movie, Park Chan-wook's direction masterfully weaves together themes of revenge, obsession, and the consequences of playing with fire. The film's tense atmosphere and stunning visuals make for a gripping and unsettling viewing experience that lingers long after the credits roll.

Overall, I Saw the Devil is a gripping and thought-provoking thriller that explores the darker aspects of human nature. With its intricate plot, complex characters, and stunning performances, it is a must-see for fans of psychological thrillers.

overview: After spending eight months in a mental institution, a former teacher moves back in with his parents and tries to reconcile with his ex-wife.
tagline: Watch For The Signs
title: Silver Linings Playbook
plot:
Silver Linings Playbook is a 2012 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by David O. Russell, written by David O. Russell and Chris Terrio, and starring Jennifer Lawrence, Bradley Cooper, and Robert De Niro.

The story revolves around Pat Solitano (played by Bradley Cooper), a former teacher who has just been released from a mental institution after being diagnosed with bipolar disorder. Pat's life is turned upside down when his wife, Nikki (played by Brea Bee), leaves him due to his erratic behavior and inability to cope with the pressures of everyday life.

Pat moves back in with his parents, Pat Sr. (played by Robert De Niro) and Dolores (played by Jacki Weaver), who are struggling to care for their son. Pat's father is a retired mechanic who has become increasingly reclusive since Pat's mother passed away, while his mother is trying to keep the family together.

Pat meets Tiffany Maxwell (played by Jennifer Lawrence), a young widow with her own emotional baggage. Tiffany is still grieving the loss of her husband, who died in a car accident, and is struggling to cope with her new reality. The two meet at a support group for people with mental health issues, where Pat is trying to work through his own demons.

As Pat and Tiffany spend more time together, they develop an unlikely friendship that gradually blossoms into romance. However, their relationship is complicated by Pat's ongoing struggles with bipolar disorder, as well as Tiffany's emotional unavailability due to her recent loss.

Meanwhile, Pat becomes obsessed with winning back his estranged wife, Nikki, who has moved on and started a new life with another man. Pat's fixation on Nikki drives him to participate in a dance competition at the local community center, where he meets Tiffany again.

As the story unfolds, Pat and Tiffany face numerous challenges, including their own personal demons, family conflicts, and societal expectations. Through a series of comedic misadventures and poignant moments, they learn to confront their emotions and find solace in each other's company.

The film takes a dramatic turn when Pat's father is diagnosed with dementia, forcing Pat to re-evaluate his priorities and take responsibility for his own life. In the end, Pat and Tiffany come together to support each other through a series of emotional breakthroughs, ultimately finding love and acceptance in each other's arms.

Throughout the film, David O. Russell masterfully balances humor and pathos, creating a narrative that is both heartwarming and heartbreaking. The performances by Bradley Cooper and Jennifer Lawrence are particularly noteworthy, as they bring depth and nuance to their characters' emotional journeys.

Overall, Silver Linings Playbook is a beautifully crafted film that explores the complexities of mental health, relationships, and personal growth. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and poignant storytelling, it has become a modern classic in the world of romantic comedies.

overview: A mother helps her daughter work through four crucial days of recovery from substance abuse.
title: Four Good Days
plot:
Four Good Days is a 2021 American drama film directed by Abby Kohn and Mary Marc. The movie stars Mila Kunis as Hannah, a mother struggling to cope with her daughter's opioid addiction.

The main themes of the movie Four Good Days revolve around:

1. **Motherly love and sacrifice**: The film showcases the unconditional love and devotion of a mother for her child, even in the face of adversity. Hannah's journey is driven by her desire to save her daughter from the clutches of addiction.
2. **Addiction and recovery**: The movie sheds light on the complexities of opioid addiction, highlighting the struggles of withdrawal, cravings, and the long road to recovery. It also explores the emotional toll of addiction on families and loved ones.
3. **Guilt, shame, and redemption**: Hannah's guilt and shame over her daughter's addiction serve as a catalyst for her journey. As she navigates the challenges of sobriety, she begins to find redemption and a sense of purpose.
4. **The complexities of mother-daughter relationships**: The film delves into the intricate dynamics between mothers and daughters, particularly in situations where addiction is involved. It raises questions about the responsibilities that come with parenthood and the blurred lines between love and enabling.

Throughout the movie, these themes are woven together to create a narrative that is both heart-wrenching and hopeful. Ultimately, Four Good Days is a powerful exploration of the human spirit's capacity for resilience, forgiveness, and transformation.

overview: Boog, a domesticated 900lb. Grizzly bear finds himself stranded in the woods 3 days before Open Season. Forced to rely on Elliot, a fast-talking mule deer, the two form an unlikely friendship and must quickly rally other forest animals if they are to form a rag-tag army against the hunters.
tagline: All Fur One. One Fur All.
title: Open Season
plot:
Open Season is a 2006 American computer-animated comedy film produced by Columbia Pictures Animation and released by Sony Pictures Releasing. The movie follows the story of Otis, a bear who lives in a forest filled with various animals.

The beginning of the movie starts with Otis (voiced by Matthew Fox) being an outcast among his fellow bears due to his unusual appearance and behavior. He is often bullied and ridiculed by the other bears, which makes him feel isolated and alone. However, Otis has a unique gift - he can talk.

One day, Otis meets a group of animals who are planning to take over the forest, led by a sly and cunning raccoon named Cody (voiced by Joe Pesci). The animals plan to overthrow their human oppressors and establish a new order in the forest. However, things don't go as planned, and the animals soon find themselves facing a common enemy - a group of hunters who are determined to wipe out all the animals in the forest.

As Otis tries to navigate his way through this chaos, he meets a young rabbit named Judy (voiced by Brittany Murphy) who becomes his love interest. Together, they try to stop Cody and his gang from taking over the forest. Along the way, Otis discovers that he has a special connection with Judy and that she is not just any ordinary rabbit.

The plot development of the movie takes a turn when Otis and Judy team up with a group of animals who are determined to protect their home from the hunters. They come across a wise old owl named Sam (voiced by Steve Buscemi) who helps them on their mission. As they journey through the forest, they encounter various obstacles and challenges that test their courage and determination.

In the end, Otis and his friends successfully defeat Cody and his gang, saving the forest from destruction. However, not before realizing that there is more to life than just fighting for survival. The movie ends with Otis and Judy sharing a romantic moment, and the other animals celebrating their victory.

Throughout the movie, the animation is vibrant and colorful, bringing the characters to life in a way that is both entertaining and engaging. The voice acting is also top-notch, with each character having its own unique personality and quirks. Overall, Open Season is a fun and action-packed animated film that explores themes of friendship, love, and acceptance.

It's worth noting that while the movie received mixed reviews from critics, it has become a cult classic among fans of animation and comedy. The success of the movie led to two sequels, Open Season 2 (2008) and Open Season 3 (2010), as well as various merchandise and spin-offs.

overview: A man is out for justice after a group of corrupt police officers are unable to catch his wife's killer.
tagline: I lay my vengeance upon them.
title: I Am Wrath
plot:
I Am Wrath is a 2016 American action thriller film directed by Charles Robert Carner. The movie follows a former Special Forces operative, Jack Conner, who seeks revenge against those responsible for his wife's death.

The main theme of I Am Wrath revolves around the destructive nature of unchecked anger and the devastating consequences it can have on individuals and their loved ones. As Jack's quest for vengeance intensifies, he becomes increasingly consumed by his emotions, leading him down a path of self-destruction and moral ambiguity.

Throughout the film, the audience is presented with a complex exploration of the human psyche, delving into the blurred lines between justice and revenge. The movie raises questions about the nature of morality and whether it's possible to reconcile personal vendettas with a sense of right and wrong.

The film also touches on the theme of grief and loss, as Jack's wife's death serves as a catalyst for his actions. His journey is marked by a deep-seated emotional pain, which he struggles to cope with, leading him to lash out at those around him.

Ultimately, I Am Wrath presents a thought-provoking commentary on the dangers of allowing anger to consume us, and the importance of finding healthy ways to process our emotions in order to maintain our humanity.

overview: Cody and Zack are approached to join the Gemini Project, a high-tech research center studying the dynamics between twins. Shockingly, they find themselves interconnected in a whole new way! When one twin experiences something, the other twin feels it too. This newfound revelation helps them see eye to eye for the first time, and it puts them in more danger than they could have imagined.
title: The Suite Life Movie
plot:
The Suite Life Movie is a 2011 American science fiction comedy-drama television film directed by Sean McNamara and written by Michael Saltzman. A Disney Channel Original Movie based on the sitcom The Suite Life on Deck, itself a spin-off of The Suite Life of Zack & Cody, it stars Dylan and Cole Sprouse, who also served as executive producers, alongside Brenda Song, Debby Ryan, Matthew Timmons, John Ducey, Matthew Glave and Phill Lewis. It premiered on Disney Channel on March 25, 2011.

Cody Martin cancels his spring break plans with his girlfriend Bailey Pickett and leaves the cruise ship SS Tipton, where he attends school, to take an internship with Dr. Donald Spaulding at a prestigious research institute, hoping to win a scholarship to Yale. Bailey is so upset that she stops speaking to him. Meanwhile, his twin brother Zack wants the car their parents promised Cody for college, and Cody refuses to give it up. When Zack crashes a billion-dollar research submarine into a seawall while showing off, and Cody wrecks another trying to stop him, Cody is fired and angrily declares that, though they are twins, they are not brothers. Elsewhere, heiress London Tipton eats a fruit meant for the institute's dolphins and gains the ability to understand them.

The estranged brothers are then recruited for the Gemini Project, run by Dr. Ronald Olsen, who studies the physical and emotional connections between twins. On a remote island filled with hundreds of other twin pairs, Olsen claims his goal is to create bonds of empathy that could end evil in the world. Using the same fruit, the experiment allows Zack and Cody to feel each other's sensations and then emotions, and each comes to understand the other: Cody wants the scholarship so he can be with Bailey, while Zack needs the car to find his own purpose. Soon after reconciling, they discover that Olsen has sinister plans. As the island's twins fall under mind control and hunt them down, Bailey, who has finally read Cody's letter explaining his choices, sets out with London, Woody and the ship's manager Mr. Moseby to rescue them, helped by information London receives from a dolphin. Working together, the brothers must use their new connection to defeat Olsen.

The film drew 5.2 million viewers on its premiere. It later aired around the world, and it has streamed on Disney+ since November 2019. BSC Kids rated it seven out of ten, calling it typical but surprisingly funny and a good choice for younger viewers.

original_title: Ultimate Avengers 2: Rise of the Panther
overview: Mysterious Wakanda lies in the darkest heart of Africa, unknown to most of the world. An isolated land hidden behind closed borders, fiercely protected by its young king: Black Panther. But when brutal alien invaders attack, the threat leaves Black Panther with no option but to go against the sacred decrees of his people and ask for help from outsiders.
tagline: To save humanity, the Earth's mightiest heroes must reunite for a rematch of heroic proportions.
title: Ultimate Avengers 2: Rise of the Panther
plot:
Ultimate Avengers 2: Rise of the Panther is a 2006 American animated superhero film released direct to video by Lionsgate on 8 August 2006. The second entry in the Marvel Animated Features line produced by MLG Productions 2 with Marvel Enterprises, it is the sequel to Ultimate Avengers released earlier that year and is loosely based on Mark Millar and Bryan Hitch's comic series The Ultimates. Credited directors include Will Meugniot, Dick Sebast and Bob Richardson, with a screenplay credited to Greg Johnson and Craig Kyle, music by Guy Michelmore and animation by the South Korean studio Dong Woo Animation.

Some time after the defeat of the Chitauri, Captain America continues to fly missions for S.H.I.E.L.D. but is haunted by memories of Kleiser, the shape-shifting alien commander he fought in the Second World War, and takes increasingly reckless risks. In the isolated African kingdom of Wakanda, Kleiser resurfaces and the Chitauri attack, killing the king, T'Chaka. The invaders are after vibranium, a metal found only in Wakanda that they use to build their ships and weapons. Prince T'Challa assumes his father's mantle as the Black Panther and, defying his nation's sacred tradition of isolation from outsiders, seeks out Captain America for help.

Nick Fury reassembles the team, though Thor is initially unavailable and Bruce Banner remains under guard. A misunderstanding with Wakandan soldiers leaves the Wasp injured and Captain America's shield stolen, but the heroes, now joined by Thor, unite with the Black Panther against the Chitauri. From his confinement, Banner works out that gamma radiation weakens vibranium and sends Betty Ross to Wakanda with a gamma-ray projector. The weapon cripples the invaders, and Iron Man and Giant-Man destroy the power core of the Chitauri mothership, though Giant-Man is fatally wounded. After the Black Panther thanks his allies, the team returns home to learn that Banner has transformed into the Hulk and escaped.

The voice cast includes Justin Gross as Captain America, Marc Worden as Iron Man, Olivia d'Abo as Black Widow, Michael Massee as Bruce Banner with Fred Tatasciore as the Hulk, David Boat as Thor, Andre Ware as Nick Fury and Jeffrey D. Sams as the Black Panther, alongside Grey DeLisle and Nolan North. The film was later broadcast on Cartoon Network's Toonami block and received a mixed critical response.

overview: Tony, a promising young motorcycle racer, is forced to do perilous drug runs to save the mother of his child from a dangerous mobster.
title: Burn Out
plot:
Burn Out is a 2017 French and Belgian action thriller written and directed by Yann Gozlan, based on Jérémie Guez's 2012 novel Balancé dans les cordes. François Civil stars as a young motorcycle racer drawn into the drug trade, with Olivier Rabourdin, Manon Azem, Samuel Jouy and Narcisse Mame in supporting roles. It competed at the Noir in Festival in Italy in December 2017 and was released theatrically in France by Gaumont on 3 January 2018.

Tony Rodrigues dreams of breaking into professional superbike racing. When he is not training, he works days as a forklift operator and looks after his young son Sofiane while his former partner Leyla searches for work. One day Tony passes a group of gang members, led by a man named Jordan, leaving Leyla's apartment, and finds her beaten and her home ransacked. She confesses that she had been storing drugs for Jordan and that the stash was stolen by an ex-boyfriend, leaving her with a debt she cannot pay. Determined to protect her, Tony turns to his childhood friend Moussa, now a local gang leader, who helps arrange a meeting with Jordan.

Jordan dismisses him, but Jordan's boss Miguel sees an opportunity in Tony's riding skills. To clear Leyla's debt, Tony must work as a courier for two months, delivering drugs across the city on his motorcycle within strict two-hour windows. The nighttime runs push him to exhaustion, and the strain costs him both his day job and his tryout with a racing team. When the agreed period ends, Jordan changes the terms and insists Tony keep working indefinitely, and in a burst of rage Tony beats him to death with his helmet. With Moussa's help, Tony disposes of the body and devises a dangerous plan to get rid of Miguel, offering his friend Miguel's business in exchange. The scheme goes wrong when Miguel learns the truth about Jordan, but Moussa's gang rescues Tony and kills Miguel. Back in a quiet life as a warehouse worker, Tony finds he cannot let go of the thrill, and the film ends with him provoking a police chase on his bike.

The film earned about $1.1 million at the French box office and premiered in North America at the COLCOA French Film Festival in April 2018. Netflix acquired worldwide rights outside France and released it in March 2019. Critics praised its propulsive motorcycle sequences and tension while noting its familiar premise. A Spanish remake, Centauro, was released on Netflix in 2022.

overview: Desperate to avoid his family’s judgment about his perpetual single status, Peter convinces his best friend Nick to join him for the holidays and pretend that they’re now in a relationship. But when Peter’s mother sets him up on a blind date with her handsome trainer James, the plan goes awry.
tagline: Peter and Nick are just friends. Peter's family knows better.
title: Single All the Way
plot:
Single All the Way is a 2021 American romantic comedy film directed by Chris Sivertson and written by Sean Pearce and Rob McKittrick. The movie stars Michael B. Jordan, Phoebe Bridgers, and Quvenzhané Wallis.

The story revolves around Noah (played by Michael B. Jordan), a successful tech entrepreneur who is struggling to find love in the dating world. On Christmas Eve, his best friend, Matt (played by Peter Gallagher), sets him up with his 17-year-old niece, Amber (played by Quvenzhané Wallis). Despite initial reservations, Noah agrees to spend the holiday season with Amber and her family.

As they embark on this unconventional adventure together, Noah finds himself developing feelings for Amber, who is navigating her own identity crisis as she prepares to leave for college. The two form an unlikely bond, and their relationship blossoms into a romance.

However, their budding connection is put to the test when Amber's mother, Sarah (played by Phoebe Bridgers), becomes increasingly disapproving of Noah's intentions. As Christmas Day approaches, Noah must confront his own feelings and figure out if he's ready for a serious relationship with someone half his age.

Throughout the film, the director explores themes of love, identity, and growing up. The movie also delves into the complexities of adult relationships and the challenges of navigating different stages of life.

As Christmas Day arrives, Noah must make a choice between pursuing his feelings for Amber or respecting her boundaries. In the end, he decides to prioritize their friendship and support Amber's decision to attend college, rather than risking their relationship.
