overview: A group of survivors take refuge in a shopping mall after the world is taken over by aggressive, flesh-eating zombies.
tagline: When the undead rise, civilization will fall.
title: Dawn of the Dead
plot:
Dawn of the Dead is a 2004 American zombie horror film directed by Zack Snyder, starring Ving Rhames, Mena Suvari, and Jake Weber. The movie is a remake of George A. Romero's 1978 film of the same name.

The story begins with a montage of news clips showing the rapid spread of a mysterious virus that turns people into zombies. We then see a group of survivors, including Jim (Jake Weber), Steve (Michael Kelly), and Peter (Ty Burrell), who are trying to escape the chaos in Philadelphia. They eventually find themselves at a shopping mall, where they barricade themselves inside.

As the days pass, the group tries to maintain some semblance of normalcy, with Jim attempting to hold down a job as a security guard while Steve and Peter try to scavenge for food and supplies. However, their attempts are constantly thwarted by hordes of zombies that seem to be attracted to the mall.

The group soon realizes that they are not alone in the mall. They discover a mysterious woman named Ana (Mena Suvari), who is initially hostile towards them but eventually becomes an ally. As the days turn into weeks, the group begins to experience strange and terrifying occurrences, including visions of a zombie-like creature that seems to be watching them.

As tensions rise within the group, Jim's leadership is challenged by Steve, who wants to take more drastic measures to survive. Meanwhile, Ana's past is slowly revealed, showing her to be a former model who was infected with the virus and has since become a zombie herself.

The movie takes a dark turn when the group discovers that the mall is being overrun by an even larger horde of zombies. In a desperate bid to escape, they set fire to the mall, hoping to create a diversion that will allow them to make their way out.

However, as they attempt to flee, Jim becomes increasingly unhinged, and his actions become more erratic. The group eventually splits up, with some members making it out of the mall while others are left behind.

The movie ends with Ana, who has been bitten by a zombie, being taken away by a group of survivors who have managed to escape the mall. As she is carried off into the distance, we see Jim standing alone in the ruins of the mall, his eyes fixed on the camera with a mixture of horror and despair.

Throughout the movie, Snyder's direction adds a layer of social commentary, using the zombie apocalypse as a metaphor for consumerism and the breakdown of society. The film's use of satire and irony is evident in its portrayal of the zombies as mindless consumers who are drawn to the mall like moths to a flame.

Overall, Dawn of the Dead is a tense and unsettling horror movie that explores themes of survival, leadership, and the human condition. While it received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, it has since become a cult classic and is widely regarded as one of the best zombie movies of all time.

overview: While on a last-minute European holiday, a young woman finds herself in the middle of a real-life fairy tale when a chance meeting with a handsome local leads to something more. However, things get complicated when she learns that the "local" is actually a prince who is about to be crowned King, and whose mother is dead-set against her royal son's romance with the tourist.
title: A Royal Winter
plot:
A Royal Winter is a 2017 American romantic comedy television film directed by Ernie Barbarash, who wrote the screenplay from a story he developed with Mark Amato. Produced by the Motion Picture Corporation of America and Brad Krevoy Television as a Hallmark Channel original, it was shot in Romania, in the historic centre and citadel of Sighișoara and in Bucharest, and premiered in the United States on 14 January 2017. It stars Merritt Patterson, Jack Donnelly and Samantha Bond.

Patterson plays Maggie Marks, a young American lawyer who, at her father's urging, is about to begin her first job at a large New York law firm. Before starting, she takes a last-minute winter holiday with her best friend, Sarah Price (Rhea Bailey), to the small European kingdom of Calpurnia. There she meets a charming and daring young man and agrees to a date, unaware that he is Prince Adrian (Donnelly), the heir to the throne, who is about to be crowned king. His mother, Queen Beatrice (Bond), disapproves of his carefree lifestyle and his habit of slipping out of the palace to enjoy himself rather than preparing for his future duties. Maggie and Adrian quickly feel a kinship, since each is facing a "job" neither really wants.

When Maggie discovers Adrian's true identity and reads press reports portraying him as a playboy, she confronts him, and he invites her to keep spending time with him so that she can judge him for herself. At a palace dinner she feels out of place and understands why he so often escapes. Photographs of the couple soon appear in the press, displeasing both Maggie's father, who fears the publicity will harm a future lawyer, and the queen, who uses her influence with Maggie's future employer to lure her back to New York. Torn between a secure career and her young romance with a future monarch, Maggie resolves to cut short her holiday, regretting that she will miss his coronation, which, contrary to tradition, is to be held in public. In the end the queen apologises, having changed her mind about Maggie, and gives the couple her blessing; Maggie attends the coronation and extends her stay in King Adrian's realm indefinitely.

German critics found the film conventional but pleasant. TV Spielfilm called it the usual holiday love story but quite charming, while the Lexikon des internationalen Films noted its attractive settings and familiar, easily resolved complications, judging it comparatively acceptable thanks to solid performances and a light tone.

overview: Does infinity exist? Can we experience the Infinite? In an animated film (created by artists from 10 countries) the world's most cutting-edge scientists and mathematicians go in search of the infinite and its mind-bending implications for the universe.  Eminent mathematicians, particle physicists and cosmologists dive into infinity and its mind-bending implications for the universe.
title: A Trip to Infinity
plot:
A Trip to Infinity is a 2022 American animated documentary film directed by Jonathan Halperin and Drew Takahashi, in their feature directorial debut, and written by Halperin and Alex Ricciardi. Produced by Room 608 and Make Make Entertainment, with animation by Studio AKA, Compost Creative and artists from ten countries, it explores the concept of infinity through interviews with mathematicians, physicists, cosmologists and philosophers. It was released on Netflix on 26 September 2022.

The film's participants include the physicists Brian Greene, Janna Levin, Stephon Alexander, Carlo Rovelli and Anthony Aguirre, the astrophysicist Delilah Gates, the mathematicians Steven Strogatz, Eugenia Cheng and Moon Duchin, the philosophers Rebecca Goldstein and Kenny Easwaran, and the physicist and novelist Alan Lightman. Organised into numbered chapters and illustrated by animation in a wide range of styles, from the literal to the metaphorical, it asks whether infinity exists, whether it can be found in the physical world, and whether a mortal person could ever experience the endless. Strogatz narrates "The Infinite Hotel", a cartoon based on the German mathematician David Hilbert's thought experiment about a fully occupied hotel that can always find room for more guests, even infinitely many. Other segments consider how infinity can make one equal zero, the very large and the very small, black holes and wormholes, and an apple left in a box for so long that it decays into particles and eventually becomes an apple again. Gates reflects on whether the universe might be finite yet appear endless to its inhabitants, like a dot travelling round a circle or across the surface of a ball, and the film notes that there are infinitely many ways for the universe to be finite but only a few for it to be infinite. The film closes by asking whether human creativity itself is infinite, leaving the impression that infinity reveals the limits of human understanding.

A Trip to Infinity won the award for Outstanding Graphic Design and Art Direction at the 44th News and Documentary Emmy Awards. John Serba of Decider found it slickly made and terrifically entertaining without dumbing down its ideas, singling out Strogatz's infectious enthusiasm. In The New Yorker, the mathematician Dan Rockmore praised its experts and the Infinite Hotel sequence but felt that its psychedelic animations and philosophical detours sometimes distracted from the mathematics.

overview: Percy Schmeiser, a third-generation farmer, gets sued by a corporate giant for allegedly using their patented seeds. With little resources to fight a legal battle, Percy joins forces with up-and-coming attorney Jackson Weaver and environmental activist Rebecca Salcau for a monumental case that leads all the way to the Supreme Court.
title: Percy
plot:
Percy, also known as Percy vs Goliath, is a 2020 Canadian, American and Indian biographical drama directed by Clark Johnson from a screenplay by Garfield Lindsay Miller and Hilary Pryor. Christopher Walken stars as Percy Schmeiser, a 70-year-old Saskatchewan farmer who takes on a multinational corporation, with Christina Ricci, Zach Braff, Luke Kirby, Adam Beach, Martin Donovan, Roberta Maxwell and Peter Stebbings in supporting roles. It premiered at the 2020 Quebec City Film Festival and was released in Canada by Mongrel Media on October 9, 2020.

Based on the legal case Monsanto Canada Inc v Schmeiser, the film follows Percy, a canola farmer who receives legal action from the agribusiness giant Monsanto, which claims that his fields contain its patented Roundup-resistant crops and accuses him of intellectual property theft. Monsanto demands his seed and the profits from his harvest. Percy, a lifelong seed saver, insists that he never bought or planted the company's product and that his fields were contaminated by seed from neighboring farms. He hires local lawyer Jackson Weaver, played by Braff, but it soon becomes clear that the law favors the corporation.

The case takes a heavy toll. Percy and his family are shunned by parts of their community and their debts mount. Rebecca Salcau, played by Ricci, an activist with an environmental organization, offers support on the condition that Percy speak out publicly to draw attention and raise funds. Reluctant at first, he changes his mind after discovering that Monsanto has had him followed and branded a thief. His speeches gain international attention and bring donations and letters from around the world. On a trip to India he witnesses the devastating impact of industrial agriculture on indebted farmers, many of whom have taken their own lives. Back home, his wife is injured, his appeals fail and his backers withdraw, but encouraged by her, Percy takes his fight all the way to the Supreme Court of Canada, which ultimately upholds Monsanto's patent but rules that he owes the company nothing because he did not profit from the gene.

Principal photography took place in Winnipeg beginning in September 2018. Rotten Tomatoes reports a 76% approval rating from 49 reviews, with a consensus noting the film's heavy-handed messaging but crediting Walken's performance with keeping it upright. Schmeiser, gravely ill with Parkinson's disease, died on October 13, 2020, days after the film's release.

overview: When a Midwest town learns that a corrupt railroad baron has captured the deeds to their homesteads without their knowledge, a group of young ranchers join forces to take back what is rightfully theirs. They will become the object of the biggest manhunt in the history of the Old West and, as their fame grows, so will the legend of their leader, a young outlaw by the name of Jessie James.
tagline: Sometimes the wrong side of the law is the right place to be.
title: American Outlaws
plot:
American Outlaws is a 2001 American Western film directed by Les Mayfield. The movie tells the story of Jesse James and his gang, who embark on a series of bank robberies across the United States during the late 1800s.

The main theme of American Outlaws revolves around the struggle for freedom and individuality in a society governed by strict rules and regulations. The film portrays Jesse James as a symbol of rebellion against the oppressive government and societal norms, who seeks to challenge the status quo and live life on his own terms.

Through the character of Jesse James, the movie explores the tension between personal desire and social responsibility. As Jesse navigates the complexities of his outlaw lifestyle, he must confront the consequences of his actions and weigh the importance of loyalty, friendship, and family against the allure of freedom and adventure.

The film also touches on the theme of class struggle, highlighting the economic disparities between the wealthy elite and the working-class outlaws who are forced to live outside the law. The movie portrays a world where the haves and have-nots are starkly divided, and the outlaws must navigate this divide in order to survive.

Ultimately, American Outlaws is a story about the human desire for freedom and autonomy, and the consequences that come with choosing a life of rebellion over one of conformity.

overview: A family's suburban home is invaded by angry spirits. When the terrifying apparitions escalate their attacks and take the youngest daughter, the family must come together to rescue her.
tagline: They're here. And they know what scares you.
title: Poltergeist
plot:
Poltergeist is a 2015 American supernatural horror film directed by Gil Kenan, written by David Lindsay-Abaire and produced by Sam Raimi, Rob Tapert and Roy Lee. A remake of the 1982 film of the same name, it is the fourth instalment overall in the Poltergeist franchise. Sam Rockwell and Rosemarie DeWitt star as Eric and Amy Bowen, with Saxon Sharbino, Kyle Catlett and Kennedi Clements as their children, Jared Harris as the television ghost hunter Carrigan Burke and Jane Adams as paranormal researcher Dr. Brooke Powell. Released in 3D after several date changes, the film opened in May 2015.

Facing financial difficulties after Eric loses his job, the Bowen family buys a suburban house that fits their reduced budget. Unknown to them, it was built on the site of an old cemetery whose remains were supposed to have been relocated by the developer. On their first night, they hear strange noises in the walls, and nine-year-old Griffin finds a box of creepy clown dolls left behind in the house. Lights and electronic devices begin switching on and off, and Griffin discovers his six-year-old sister Madison talking to the static on the television, warning that someone is coming.

The next evening, while Eric and Amy are at a dinner party, the paranormal activity intensifies dramatically. Teenage daughter Kendra is grabbed by a corpse's hand emerging from the floor, Griffin is attacked by a clown doll and dragged out of the house by a tree, and Madison vanishes after being drawn through her bedroom closet into another dimension. The desperate parents turn to a team of paranormal researchers led by Dr. Powell, who discover that the house has become a portal for restless spirits. Powell calls in her former partner Carrigan Burke, a reality television host with genuine experience of the supernatural, who explains that the spirits are using Madison to find their way into the light. The family must venture into the spectral realm to bring her back before she is lost forever.

The remake updates the original's story with contemporary technology such as smartphones, tablets and a camera-equipped drone used to explore the spirit world, while preserving key moments from the 1982 film.

Poltergeist received largely negative reviews, with about 29 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and critics considering it inferior to the original, though it was a moderate commercial success, grossing about 95 million dollars worldwide against a budget of 35 million.

overview: Two Swedish/Norwegian half sisters go on a winter diving trip in Northern Norway, when they get trapped after a rockslide.
tagline: There is only you
title: Breaking Surface
plot:
Breaking Surface is a 2020 survival thriller drama written and directed by Joachim Hedén, produced as a co-production between Sweden, Norway and Belgium. Moa Gammel and Madeleine Martin star as two half-sisters whose diving trip turns into a desperate fight for survival, with Lena Hope, Trine Wiggen and Maja Söderström in supporting roles.

Ida and her half-sister Tuva are experienced scuba divers whose relationship carries old tensions. For a winter diving trip they travel to the remote, snow-covered coastline of northern Norway, where they head out to dive in an isolated fjord. Not long after they descend into the icy water, a rockslide crashes down from the cliffs above, pinning Tuva beneath a heavy boulder on the seabed at a depth from which she cannot free herself.

With no other people nearby, no phone signal and the winter daylight quickly fading, Ida must keep her trapped sister alive as Tuva's air supply steadily runs out. Ida repeatedly races back and forth between the seabed, the shore and their car in search of fresh tanks, tools and help, battling exhaustion, the freezing temperatures and the physical dangers of repeated ascents and descents. Every decision carries a risk to both women, and old resentments surface as the sisters confront their shared history under extreme pressure. The film builds suspense through the claustrophobic underwater sequences and the stark beauty and isolation of the Arctic landscape, while exploring themes of sisterhood, endurance and survival against the indifferent power of nature.

The film was shot in Belgium, in Strömstad and Gothenburg in Sweden, and in the Lofoten islands of Norway. It premiered internationally at the virtual Nightstream Film Festival in October 2020 after its Swedish release earlier that year. Critical response was very positive, with a 100% rating on Rotten Tomatoes from seven reviews. Peter Martin of ScreenAnarchy wrote that it consistently surprises as it develops into a gripping story of survival, Bloody Disgusting awarded it four skulls out of five, and Film Threat rated it seven out of ten. The film was remade in English in 2023 as The Dive, starring Sophie Lowe and Louisa Krause.

overview: Paul is a U.S. truck driver working in Iraq. After an attack by a group of Iraqis he wakes to find he is buried alive inside a coffin. With only a lighter and a cell phone it's a race against time to escape this claustrophobic death trap.
tagline: 170,000 sq miles of desert. 90 minutes of oxygen. No way out.
title: Buried
plot:
Buried is a psychological thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the effects of isolation on the mind. The film tells the story of Paul Conroy, a construction worker who finds himself buried alive in a coffin during a kidnapping. As he struggles to survive and find a way out, his mental state begins to deteriorate, revealing a complex web of emotions, fears, and desires.

One of the main themes of Buried is the exploration of claustrophobia and the psychological effects of being trapped in a confined space. The film masterfully builds tension as Paul's physical confinement translates into an emotional prison, where he is forced to confront his inner demons. As the hours tick by, Paul's grip on reality begins to slip, and he becomes increasingly paranoid, hallucinating and experiencing vivid nightmares.

Another significant theme of Buried is the exploration of identity and self-discovery. As Paul navigates his desperate situation, he is forced to re-examine his life choices and relationships. He reflects on his marriage, his job, and his sense of purpose, leading to a deeper understanding of himself and his place in the world.

The film also touches on the theme of redemption and forgiveness. Through Paul's experiences, the movie highlights the importance of letting go of past grievances and finding peace with oneself. As Paul struggles to survive, he begins to see that his life is not defined by his mistakes or regrets but by his ability to forgive himself and others.

Lastly, Buried explores the theme of human resilience in the face of adversity. Despite being trapped and facing seemingly insurmountable odds, Paul refuses to give up, drawing on a deep well of determination and resourcefulness to survive. His story serves as a testament to the human spirit's capacity for hope, perseverance, and transformation.

Overall, Buried is a gripping thriller that delves into the complexities of the human psyche, exploring themes of isolation, identity, redemption, and resilience in a way that is both thought-provoking and deeply unsettling.

overview: A young American couple travel to the arctic mountains of Norway. After pulling over during a snowstorm, they wake up trapped in their SUV, buried underneath layers of snow and ice.
tagline: Based on chilling true events
title: Centigrade
plot:
Centigrade is a 2020 survival thriller directed by Brendan Walsh from a screenplay he wrote with Daley Nixon. Genesis Rodriguez and Vincent Piazza star as Naomi and Matt Ibbotson, an American couple trapped inside their car after it is buried beneath snow and ice in Norway. Nixon's original script was inspired by the real case of Peter Skyllberg, a Swedish man found barely alive in his snowbound car after surviving for two months in sub-zero temperatures. The film was shot in sequence, and both actors lost weight during production. It premiered at the Sidewalk Film Festival on 27 August 2020.

In 2002, Naomi, who is eight months pregnant, and her husband Matt are travelling through the Arctic mountains of Norway. During a heavy snowstorm they pull over to rest, and when they wake they discover that their SUV has been completely encased in snow and ice. The doors will not open, the windows are covered by a thick wall of frozen snow, and they have no way of signalling for help.

As days pass, the couple struggle to survive with only a few snacks, a small supply of water and whatever warmth they can generate. The temperature inside the car falls to dangerous levels, and they face hypothermia, frostbite, dehydration and disturbing hallucinations. In the confined space, tension, mutual blame and long-held secrets about their marriage rise to the surface, but they realise that they will only survive if they work together. After a panic attack, Naomi goes into labour, and Matt helps her deliver a baby girl, whom they name Olivia. Matt, weakened by the cold and his attempts to dig through the window, gives his coat to keep the baby warm. One morning Naomi wakes to find that he has died. Days later, as the snow begins to soften, she must find the strength to break free and carry her newborn daughter through the wilderness in search of help.

Almost the entire film takes place inside the car, making it a two-hander that relies on the performances of its leads and on the claustrophobic atmosphere. The closing captions explain that the snow may have acted like an igloo, trapping heat and protecting the family from the elements.

Centigrade received mixed to negative reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds an approval rating of about 40 percent, with the consensus describing it as a survival thriller largely bereft of thrills that may leave audiences feeling as trapped as its characters, although the performances of Rodriguez and Piazza were praised.

overview: A group of people gather in the California desert to watch a "film" set in the late 1990s featuring a sentient, homicidal car tire named Robert. The assembled crowd of onlookers watch as Robert becomes obsessed with a beautiful and mysterious woman and goes on a rampage through a desert town.
tagline: Are you TIRED of the expected?
title: Rubber
plot:
Rubber is a 2010 American horror-comedy film directed by Quentin Dupieux. The movie follows the story of a mysterious tire named Robert, who comes to life and wreaks havoc on a small Arizona town.

The main theme of Rubber is the exploration of chaos and anarchy in a seemingly ordinary world. The film presents a satirical take on suburban America, where the mundane and the banal are turned upside down by the arrival of this supernatural tire. As Robert's actions become more and more destructive, the film critiques the societal norms and expectations that govern human behavior.

At its core, Rubber is also a commentary on the absurdity of violence and aggression in our society. The film's portrayal of Robert's violent outbursts serves as a metaphor for the ways in which we often express ourselves through aggressive behavior, rather than addressing our emotions in a more constructive manner.

Furthermore, the movie can be seen as an exploration of the relationship between humans and objects. Robert, as a tire, is an inanimate object that has come to life, yet he exhibits human-like qualities and behaviors. This blurs the lines between what is considered "human" and what is not, raising questions about our perceptions of identity and agency.

Overall, Rubber is a darkly comedic film that uses satire and absurdity to explore themes of chaos, anarchy, and the human condition.

original_title: Crystal Lake Memories: The Complete History of Friday the 13th
overview: Taking inspiration from Peter M. Bracke's definitive book of the same name, this seven-hour documentary dives into the making of all twelve Friday the 13th films, with all-new interviews from the cast and the crew.
title: Crystal Lake Memories: The Complete History of Friday the 13th
plot:
Crystal Lake Memories: The Complete History of Friday the 13th is a documentary film that delves into the making and impact of the iconic horror franchise, Friday the 13th. At its core, the movie explores the darker side of human nature, particularly the themes of violence, trauma, and the consequences of unchecked aggression.

The film also examines how the creation of Jason Voorhees, a character who has become synonymous with terror, serves as a metaphor for the destructive power of childhood trauma and the cyclical nature of violence. The documentary sheds light on how the franchise's portrayal of a seemingly idyllic summer camp setting, which is actually a facade hiding dark secrets, taps into our deep-seated fears about the unknown and the uncontrollable.

Furthermore, Crystal Lake Memories: The Complete History of Friday the 13th touches upon the theme of nostalgia and its relationship with horror. The film's nostalgic value lies not only in its portrayal of the original films but also in its exploration of how the franchise has become an integral part of popular culture, influencing countless other horror movies and TV shows.

Ultimately, the documentary presents a cautionary tale about the dangers of unchecked violence and the importance of confronting our dark past. By examining the history of Friday the 13th through a critical lens, Crystal Lake Memories: The Complete History of Friday the 13th encourages viewers to reflect on their own relationship with horror and the impact it can have on society.

overview: A woman turns to prescription medication as a way of handling her anxiety concerning her husband's upcoming release from prison.
tagline: One pill can change your life.
title: Side Effects
plot:
"Side Effects" is a psychological thriller film directed by Steven Soderbergh, released in 2013 under the production company of Summit Entertainment, not Di Bonaventura Pictures. 

The movie follows the story of Jude Sturgess (played by Rooney Mara), a young woman who becomes increasingly unhinged after her husband's release from prison and her subsequent struggles with depression and anxiety.

The main themes of "Side Effects" include:

1. The blurred lines between reality and fantasy: As Jude navigates her mental health, the audience is left questioning what is real and what is just a product of her imagination.
2. The consequences of trauma: The film explores the long-term effects of traumatic events on individuals, particularly women, and how these experiences can shape their lives in profound ways.
3. The complexities of female identity: Jude's struggles with depression, anxiety, and her husband's return serve as a metaphor for the societal expectations placed upon women to be perfect and nurturing.
4. The dangers of prescription medication: The film critiques the over-reliance on pharmaceuticals to treat mental health issues, highlighting the potential risks and unintended consequences of these medications.

Overall, "Side Effects" is a thought-provoking exploration of the human psyche, delving into themes that are both timely and timeless.

overview: In contemporary Los Angeles, two millennials navigating a social media–driven hookup culture begin a relationship that pushes both emotional and physical boundaries.
tagline: Maybe love is not enough.
title: Newness
plot:
Newness is a 2017 American romantic drama directed by Drake Doremus from a screenplay by Ben York Jones. Nicholas Hoult and Laia Costa star as a young couple experimenting with the boundaries of modern love, with Courtney Eaton, Danny Huston, Matthew Gray Gubler and the psychotherapist Esther Perel in supporting roles. It premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 25, 2017.

In Los Angeles, Martin, a divorced pharmacist, and Gabriella, a physical therapy assistant from Spain, each go out on disappointing dates arranged through a dating app. Returning to the app afterward, they match with each other, meet at a bar and spend the whole night talking before going back to Martin's apartment. A relationship quickly blossoms, and Gabriella moves in with him. Cracks appear when a visit to Martin's parents reveals things he never told her, including that his mother has dementia and that he once had a sister who died at sixteen. After a bitter argument, both cheat on each other the same night, confess the next morning and, rather than separate, agree to try an open relationship.

At first the arrangement seems liberating. At a party hosted by Larry, the much older boss of Gabriella's friend Blake, Martin flirts with Blake while Gabriella is drawn to Larry, and the couple embark on a series of encounters with other people. Jealousy and insecurity gradually creep in. Martin learns that his ex-wife Bethany has had a baby, stirring grief over a miscarriage they suffered during their marriage and feelings he never resolved, while Gabriella grows closer to Larry, who gives her a necklace she hides from Martin. Each discovers the other's secrets, and after another fight they break up. Gabriella moves in with Larry, who invites her to join him on a two-year trip through Europe, and Martin meets Bethany, who tells him she has found contentment and wishes him well. Apart, both must decide what they really want from love.

After its Sundance premiere, Netflix acquired worldwide streaming rights, and Lost City released the film in the United States on November 3, 2017. Reviews were mixed to positive. Rotten Tomatoes reports a 71% approval rating from 17 critics, and Metacritic gave it 50 out of 100. John DeFore of The Hollywood Reporter found it a sympathetic portrait of two likable lovers who do not know what is good for them, while Owen Gleiberman of Variety described it as an ambitious but overly calculated thesis movie.

overview: Wallace's whirlwind romance with the proprietor of the local wool shop puts his head in a spin, and Gromit is framed for sheep-rustling in a fiendish criminal plot.
title: A Close Shave
plot:
A Close Shave is a stop-motion animated black comedy film directed by Nick Park and produced by Aardman Animations. The movie follows the story of Wallace, a lovable but dim-witted sheep farmer, and his trusty sidekick Gromit, a clever and resourceful dog.

The main themes of A Close Shave include:

1. **Friendship**: The film celebrates the strong bond between Wallace and Gromit, showcasing their unique partnership and loyalty to each other.
2. **Deception and Appearance vs. Reality**: The movie features a villainous character, Lord Edgar Bottomley, who appears to be a harmless old man but is actually a cunning and ruthless individual. This theme highlights the idea that appearances can be deceiving, and not everything is as it seems.
3. **Social Commentary**: A Close Shave pokes fun at various aspects of rural English life, including the eccentricities of local characters and the absurdity of small-town politics.
4. **Innovation and Creativity**: The film showcases Gromit's inventive genius, which often helps Wallace get out of trouble. This theme celebrates the power of creativity and resourcefulness in overcoming challenges.

The movie's plot is driven by a series of events that unfold as Wallace and Gromit try to uncover the truth behind Lord Bottomley's sinister plans. Along the way, they encounter a range of colorful characters, including a seductive femme fatale, a bumbling police officer, and a group of eccentric villagers.

Ultimately, A Close Shave is a heartwarming and hilarious film that balances humor with clever plot twists and memorable characters. Its themes of friendship, deception, social commentary, and innovation continue to delight audiences to this day.

overview: Navy SEAL Lieutenant A.K. Waters and his elite squadron of tactical specialists are forced to choose between their duty and their humanity, between following orders by ignoring the conflict that surrounds them, or finding the courage to follow their conscience and protect a group of innocent refugees. When the democratic government of Nigeria collapses and the country is taken over by a ruthless military dictator, Waters, a fiercely loyal and hardened veteran is dispatched on a routine mission to retrieve a Doctors Without Borders physician.
tagline: He was trained to follow orders. He became a hero by defying them.
title: Tears of the Sun
plot:
Tears of the Sun is a 2003 American war drama film directed by Antoine Fuqua and starring Bruce Willis, Monica Bellucci, and Dennis Quaid. The movie follows a team of Navy SEALs on a mission to rescue a group of women who are being held captive in Nigeria.

The story begins with Lieutenant A.K. Waters (Bruce Willis), the leader of an elite Navy SEAL team, who is tasked by the President of the United States to lead a team of operatives into Nigeria to rescue a group of American aid workers who have been kidnapped by a ruthless warlord named General Medu (Oscar Isaac). The aid workers, including Dr. Lena Kendricks (Monica Bellucci), are being held captive in a remote village and are subjected to brutal treatment.

As the SEAL team, which includes Lieutenant Waters' second-in-command, Chief Mike Banning (Dennis Quaid), and other operatives, infiltrate Nigeria, they face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, enemy soldiers, and local villagers who are hostile towards them. The team also encounters a group of Nigerian rebels who are fighting against the corrupt government.

Upon arrival at the village, the SEALs discover that the aid workers have been subjected to brutal treatment by General Medu's men, including being forced to undergo female genital mutilation. The SEALs launch a daring rescue mission, using their skills and training to take down the enemy soldiers and free the aid workers.

As the team fights to complete their mission, they also begin to form bonds with the aid workers, who are struggling to cope with their ordeal. Dr. Kendricks, in particular, forms a close relationship with Lieutenant Waters, which adds an emotional depth to the story.

The movie's climax features an intense and action-packed battle between the SEALs and General Medu's men, as well as a dramatic confrontation between Lieutenant Waters and the warlord himself. In the end, the SEALs successfully complete their mission, rescuing the aid workers and killing General Medu in the process.

Throughout the movie, Fuqua uses stunning cinematography to capture the beauty of Nigeria's landscapes and the brutality of its conflicts. The film also features a powerful score by James Horner, which adds to the emotional impact of the story.

Overall, Tears of the Sun is a gripping and intense war drama that explores themes of courage, sacrifice, and redemption. While it received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, the movie has since become a cult classic and is widely regarded as one of Bruce Willis' best performances.

overview: After being brutally murdered, 14-year-old Susie Salmon watches from heaven over her grief-stricken family -- and her killer. As she observes their daily lives, she must balance her thirst for revenge with her desire for her family to heal.
production_companies: New Zealand Large Budget Screen Production Grant
tagline: The story of a life and everything that came after...
title: The Lovely Bones
plot:
The Lovely Bones is a supernatural drama film directed by Peter Jackson, based on the novel of the same name by Alice Sebold. The movie was released in 2009 and stars Saoirse Ronan, Stanley Tucci, Mark Wahlberg, and Rachel Weisz.

The story revolves around Susie Salmon (Saoirse Ronan), a 14-year-old girl who is murdered by her neighbor, George Harvey (Stanley Tucci), in the small town of Lovelace, New York. The film begins with Susie's death, but it doesn't follow the traditional linear narrative. Instead, it jumps back and forth between Susie's life before her murder, her death, and her journey to the afterlife.

In the present day, Susie finds herself in a kind of limbo, watching over her family and killer from above. She observes how her mother, Abigail (Rachel Weisz), struggles to cope with her daughter's disappearance, while her father, Jack (Mark Wahlberg), tries to move on with his life.

As the story unfolds, Susie begins to communicate with her family through various means, including notes and objects left behind by her. She also starts to gather evidence against George Harvey, who is revealed to be a serial killer targeting young girls in the neighborhood.

Meanwhile, Jack becomes increasingly obsessed with finding out what happened to his daughter, and he starts to investigate George's past. Susie, from her afterlife perspective, guides Jack towards the truth about her murder and George's identity as a serial killer.

Throughout the film, Peter Jackson employs a non-linear narrative structure, using Susie's observations of her family and killer to weave together the story. The Lovely Bones is a poignant exploration of grief, trauma, and the complexities of human relationships.

The film features strong performances from its cast, particularly Saoirse Ronan, who brings depth and nuance to Susie's character. Stanley Tucci's portrayal of George Harvey is chilling and unsettling, capturing the complexity of a serial killer's psyche.

Ultimately, The Lovely Bones is a powerful and emotional drama that explores themes of love, loss, and redemption. While it received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, it has since become a cult classic and is widely regarded as one of the most underrated films of the 2000s.

overview: When a strange signal pulsates through all cell phone networks worldwide, it starts a murderous epidemic of epic proportions when users become bloodthirsty creatures, and a group of people in New England are among the survivors to deal with the ensuing chaos after.
tagline: When everyone is connected no one is safe.
title: Cell
plot:
Cell is a 2016 American post-apocalyptic horror film directed by Tod Williams and written by Stephen King, based on his 2006 novel of the same name.

The main themes of Cell include:

1. **The Dangers of Technology**: The movie explores the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control. The cell phone signal that spreads the virus is a metaphor for the dangers of unchecked technological advancement and our reliance on it.
2. **Human Nature in Crisis**: As society collapses, people's darker aspects are revealed, showcasing how quickly humans can descend into chaos when faced with survival instincts and primal fears.
3. **The Power of Love and Human Connection**: Amidst the chaos, a few characters form strong bonds with each other, highlighting the importance of human relationships and love in times of crisis.
4. **The Unpredictability of Nature**: The movie touches on the idea that nature can be unpredictable and unforgiving, as seen in the rapid spread of the virus and its devastating effects on humanity.

These themes are woven throughout the story, which follows a small group of survivors as they try to find a cure for the deadly virus that is turning people into violent, zombie-like creatures.

overview: A mentally unhinged factory worker must decide whether to listen to his talking cat and become a killer, or follow his dog's advice to keep striving for normalcy.
tagline: Hearing voices can be murder.
title: The Voices
plot:
The Voices is a dark comedy-thriller film that delves into the complexities of human nature and the blurred lines between sanity and madness.

At its core, the movie explores the theme of toxic masculinity, as embodied by the main character Jerry Palmer (played by Ryan Reynolds), who struggles with his own demons and finds solace in his inner voice. This voice, a wisecracking and manipulative alter ego named Gerald, serves as both a confidant and a catalyst for Jerry's destructive behavior.

The film also touches on the theme of loneliness and isolation, highlighting Jerry's disconnection from society and his inability to form meaningful relationships. Through Jerry's character, the movie critiques societal expectations of masculinity and the pressure to conform to traditional norms.

Furthermore, The Voices examines the concept of mental illness and the stigmatization that often accompanies it. Jerry's struggles with depression and anxiety are portrayed as a result of his own making, rather than a genuine medical condition. This portrayal raises questions about the nature of mental health and whether individuals can be held responsible for their own suffering.

Ultimately, The Voices is a thought-provoking exploration of the human psyche, delving into the darker aspects of human nature and the complexities that make us who we are.

overview: In a gritty and alternate 1985 the glory days of costumed vigilantes have been brought to a close by a government crackdown, but after one of the masked veterans is brutally murdered, an investigation into the killer is initiated. The reunited heroes set out to prevent their own destruction, but in doing so uncover a sinister plot that puts all of humanity in grave danger.
tagline: Justice is coming to all of us.  No matter what we do.
title: Watchmen
plot:
Watchmen is a 2009 American superhero film directed by Zack Snyder and written by David Hayter and Alex Tse, based on the DC Comics series by Alan Moore and Dave Gibbons. Malin Åkerman, Billy Crudup, Matthew Goode, Carla Gugino, Jackie Earle Haley, Jeffrey Dean Morgan and Patrick Wilson star in a dark, dystopian deconstruction of the superhero genre set in an alternate 1985 at the height of the Cold War.

In this version of history, costumed vigilantes helped the United States win the Vietnam War, Richard Nixon is serving a fifth term as president, and masked heroes have been outlawed. The world edges toward nuclear war with the Soviet Union, held in check only by the existence of Doctor Manhattan, a godlike being created in a laboratory accident. When the government-sanctioned hero known as the Comedian is thrown to his death from his New York apartment, the masked vigilante Rorschach, who still operates in defiance of the law, begins to investigate and comes to believe that someone is targeting former heroes.

Rorschach warns his old colleagues: the retired, insecure Nite Owl; the increasingly detached Doctor Manhattan and his partner Silk Spectre; and Ozymandias, now one of the richest men in the world. As Doctor Manhattan is driven into exile on Mars by accusations that he caused cancer in former associates, and Rorschach is framed for murder, Nite Owl and Silk Spectre are drawn back into crime-fighting. The trail finally leads to Ozymandias's Antarctic retreat, where the heroes discover that he has orchestrated an elaborate conspiracy to avert nuclear war by staging a devastating attack on the world's cities and pinning it on Doctor Manhattan, forcing the superpowers to unite. Faced with peace bought at such a terrible price, the heroes must decide whether to expose the truth, while Rorschach refuses to compromise.

The adaptation spent nearly two decades in development hell, passing through several studios and directors, including Terry Gilliam, who called the comic unfilmable, before Warner Bros. hired Snyder in 2005. A legal dispute with 20th Century Fox over the rights was settled before release. Filming began in Vancouver in September 2007, with Snyder closely following the comic's panels. The film received polarized reviews, with praise for its visuals, faithfulness and performances, especially Haley's, and criticism of its length and violence. It later gained a reappraisal.

overview: As a CIA officer, Evelyn Salt swore an oath to duty, honor and country. Her loyalty will be tested when a defector accuses her of being a Russian spy. Salt goes on the run, using all her skills and years of experience as a covert operative to elude capture. Salt's efforts to prove her innocence only serve to cast doubt on her motives, as the hunt to uncover the truth behind her identity continues and the question remains: "Who is Salt?"
tagline: Who is Salt?
title: Salt
plot:
Salt is a 2010 American action spy thriller film directed by Phillip Noyce and starring Angelina Jolie as Evelyn Salt, a CIA operative accused of being a Russian sleeper agent.

The movie begins with Evelyn Salt (Angelina Jolie) living a seemingly ordinary life in Boston with her husband, Col. Hanin "Hank" Salt (Chiwetel Ejiofor), and their young daughter, Sophia. However, it is revealed that Evelyn's life is actually a carefully constructed cover for her true identity as a Russian sleeper agent.

The CIA discovers that Evelyn has been compromised by the Russians, who have been manipulating her since she was a teenager in Kazakhstan. The agency believes that Evelyn is about to be activated and will carry out a mission to assassinate several high-ranking government officials in Washington D.C.

As Evelyn tries to clear her name and prove her loyalty to the CIA, she must also evade the Russian agents sent to kill her. She teams up with a former CIA operative, Ted Beck (Liev Schreiber), who helps her uncover the truth about her past and the conspiracy against her.

Throughout the movie, Evelyn's character is revealed through flashbacks, showing her training as a sleeper agent in Russia and her subsequent recruitment by the CIA. The film also explores Evelyn's complicated relationship with her husband, Hank, who is unaware of her true identity.

As the plot thickens, Evelyn discovers that she has been framed for the assassination attempts, and that the real traitor is a high-ranking government official named Peter Krilov (Michael York). With the help of Ted and other allies, Evelyn must use her skills as a spy to take down Krilov and his accomplices before it's too late.

The movie culminates in an intense showdown between Evelyn and Krilov at the White House. In the end, Evelyn is able to clear her name and bring the real traitor to justice, but not before she suffers a serious injury that leaves her with a permanent scar on her neck.

Overall, Salt is a fast-paced and action-packed thriller that explores themes of loyalty, identity, and redemption. Angelina Jolie delivers a strong performance as Evelyn Salt, bringing depth and nuance to the character despite the film's somewhat predictable plot.

overview: Detective Hoffman is seemingly the last person alive to carry on the Jigsaw legacy. But when his secret is threatened, he must go on the hunt to eliminate all the loose ends.
production_companies: Canadian Film or Video Production Tax Credit (CPTC)
tagline: You won't believe how it ends.
title: Saw V
plot:
Saw V is a 2008 American horror film directed by David Hackl and written by Leigh Whannell. The film is the fifth installment in the Saw franchise.

The movie begins with Jigsaw (Tobin Bell) being taken away from his lair, where he has been held captive for years. He is rescued by Amanda Young (Shawnee Smith), who had previously worked under him but turned against him. However, it becomes clear that Amanda's intentions are not entirely pure.

The story then shifts to a new protagonist, Daniel Matthews (Angus Macfadyen), a successful businessman who has lost his way in life after the death of his wife and daughter. He is kidnapped by Jigsaw, along with two other men, Peter Strickland (Bahar Soomekh) and Eric Matthews (Donnie Wahlberg), Daniel's son.

The three men are taken to an abandoned warehouse, where they find themselves chained in a room filled with deadly traps and puzzles. They soon realize that they must work together to survive and uncover the reason behind their confinement.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Jigsaw has designed this game for them to play, and that he intends to test their will to live. The men are forced to navigate through a series of gruesome and deadly challenges, including a room filled with venomous spiders and a trap that requires them to use a blowtorch to escape.

Throughout the film, Amanda's character is revealed to be a complex and conflicted one. She is driven by a desire for revenge against Jigsaw, who she believes wronged her in the past. However, as the story progresses, it becomes clear that her motivations are not entirely altruistic.

The climax of the film features an intense and suspenseful showdown between Daniel and Amanda, as they engage in a battle of wits and wills. In the end, Daniel emerges victorious, but not without scars both physical and emotional.

Overall, Saw V is a tense and thrilling horror film that explores themes of survival, redemption, and the consequences of playing with fire. The film's twisty plot and gruesome traps make it a must-see for fans of the franchise, while its complex characters and moral ambiguity add depth and nuance to the story.

original_title: ヴァイオレット・エヴァーガーデン 外伝 - 永遠と自動手記人形 -
overview: Isabella, the daughter of the noble York family, is enrolled in an all-girls academy to be groomed into a dame worthy of nobility. However, she has given up on her future, seeing the prestigious school as nothing more than a prison from the outside world. Her family notices her struggling in her lessons and decides to hire Violet Evergarden to personally tutor her under the guise of a handmaiden.  At first, Isabella treats Violet coldly. Violet seems to be able to do everything perfectly, leading Isabella to assume that she was born with a silver spoon. After some time, Isabella begins to realize that Violet has had her own struggles and starts to open up to her. Isabella soon reveals that she has lost contact with her beloved younger sister, whom she yearns to see again.  Having experienced the power of words through her past clientele, Violet asks if Isabella wishes to write a letter to Taylor. Will Violet be able to help Isabella convey her feelings to her long-lost sister?
title: Violet Evergarden: Eternity and the Auto Memory Doll
plot:
Violet Evergarden: Eternity and the Auto Memory Doll is a 2019 Japanese animated film based on Kana Akatsuki's light novel series Violet Evergarden. Produced by Kyoto Animation and distributed by Shochiku, it was directed by Haruka Fujita from a script by Takaaki Suzuki and Tatsuhiko Urahata. Yui Ishikawa voices Violet, with Minako Kotobuki, Aoi Yūki, Takehito Koyasu, Kouki Uchiyama and Aya Endo in the cast. The film was completed only a day before the arson attack on Kyoto Animation's studio in July 2019, and it was released in Japanese cinemas that September. Netflix began streaming it internationally in April 2020.

Set after the events of the anime series, the film follows Violet, a former child soldier who now works as an Auto Memory Doll, a professional writer of letters for those who cannot express their feelings. She is sent to a prestigious boarding school for girls at the request of a noble family to tutor Isabella York, who is being trained as a debutante before her presentation to society. Isabella is unhappy at the school, struggles to fit in and has no interest in the refined skills she is expected to master, and she suffers from periodic coughing fits.

Initially suspicious of Violet, Isabella warms to her when she realises that Violet has no interest in her aristocratic status. She eventually confides that she was born Amy Bartlett, the illegitimate child of the York family, and grew up in poverty, caring for an orphan named Taylor whom she raised as a younger sister. When the York family tracked her down and demanded that she join them, she accepted in exchange for a promise that Taylor would be given a better life. Before leaving the school, Violet helps Isabella write a letter to Taylor. Three years later, Taylor runs away from her orphanage and arrives at the CH Postal Company in Leiden, determined to become a postman like Benedict Blue, who once delivered her sister's letter. Violet teaches the girl to read, and together with Benedict they set out to find Isabella and deliver a letter of their own.

The film is structured in two parts, centred on the sisters Isabella and Taylor, and explores the bonds between family members separated by circumstance, as well as Violet's own growth in understanding human emotions. It was noted for the detailed, painterly animation characteristic of Kyoto Animation.

It was followed in 2020 by Violet Evergarden: The Movie, which concluded the story.

overview: After exorcising the demons of his ex-, Malcolm starts afresh with his new girlfriend and her two children. After moving into their dream home, Malcolm is once again plagued by bizarre paranormal events.
tagline: It'll scare the #2 out of you.
title: A Haunted House 2
plot:
A Haunted House 2 is a 2014 American comedy horror film directed by Darin Scott and written by Scott, Sean Cunningham, and Matt Peterman. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2013 film A Haunted House.

The story begins with Charlie Hinton (Ethan Suplee), a former paranormal investigator who has retired from his ghost-hunting business after a traumatic experience. Charlie is now living a quiet life in suburban New Jersey, where he's married to a woman named Sarah (Amanda Fuller) and trying to start a family.

However, their peaceful life is disrupted when they receive an invitation from their old friend, Ray (Will Sasso), who has become the new head of Ghostbusters International. Ray informs them that his company has been hired by a wealthy client to investigate a haunted mansion in New Orleans.

Charlie and Sarah reluctantly agree to join Ray on the investigation, along with their friends, Dean (Marlon Wayans) and Wendy (Jenny Mollen). As they arrive at the mansion, they soon realize that it's not just a simple haunting but a complex web of supernatural entities, including ghosts, demons, and other paranormal creatures.

As the team delves deeper into the mystery, they discover that the mansion has a dark history and is home to a malevolent spirit known as "The Devil's Son." The group soon finds themselves in a desperate fight for survival, using their wits, humor, and ghost-hunting skills to outsmart the supernatural entities.

Throughout the movie, Charlie struggles with his past traumas and his desire to leave the paranormal world behind. However, as he faces the challenges of the haunted mansion, he's forced to confront his fears and re-engage in his old profession.

The climax of the movie features an epic battle between the team and The Devil's Son, which culminates in a hilarious and action-packed showdown. In the end, Charlie and his friends manage to defeat the malevolent spirit and escape the mansion, but not before they're left with some unexpected surprises.

Overall, A Haunted House 2 is a lighthearted, comedic take on the horror genre, with plenty of laughs and gags throughout. While it may not be as scary or intense as some other horror movies, it's a fun and entertaining ride that's perfect for fans of comedy horror.

overview: In a small town on Christmas Eve, a snowstorm brings together a group of young people. They soon find their friendships and love lives colliding, and come Christmas morning, nothing will be the same.
tagline: Let love take you by storm.
title: Let It Snow
plot:
Let It Snow is a 2019 American romantic comedy film based on the novel of the same name by John Green, Maureen Johnson, and Lauren Myracle. The movie follows the interconnected love stories of three teenagers: Tess (Shane Harper), Matt (Josh Duhamel), and Sam (Leah Lewis) on Christmas Eve in a small town.

The main themes of Let It Snow include:

1. **Love and Connection**: The film explores the complexities of human relationships, highlighting how people from different walks of life can come together and find love in unexpected ways.
2. **Self-Discovery**: As the characters navigate their personal struggles, they learn to confront their fears, insecurities, and past experiences, ultimately discovering more about themselves and who they want to be.
3. **Small-Town Charm**: The movie celebrates the warmth and intimacy of small-town life, showcasing the close-knit community and the ways in which it brings people together during the holiday season.
4. **Mental Health**: Tess's struggles with anxiety and depression serve as a poignant reminder of the importance of mental health awareness and seeking help when needed.
5. **Christmas Spirit**: The film's title, "Let It Snow," is inspired by the classic song, and it captures the essence of the holiday season: embracing the imperfections, finding joy in the present moment, and letting go of worries.

Overall, Let It Snow is a heartwarming and relatable story that explores the complexities of human relationships, self-discovery, and the importance of mental health, all set against the backdrop of a charming small-town Christmas.

overview: In the West End of 1950s London, plans for a movie version of a smash-hit play come to an abrupt halt after a pivotal member of the crew is murdered. When world-weary Inspector Stoppard and eager rookie Constable Stalker take on the case, the two find themselves thrown into a puzzling whodunit within the glamorously sordid theater underground, investigating the mysterious homicide at their own peril.
tagline: The greatest murder ever staged.
title: See How They Run
plot:
See How They Run is a 2022 British comedy film directed by Sam Bain and Chris Morris, written by Sam Bain and Chris Morris, and produced by DJ Films. The movie stars Sam Rockwell, Saoirse Ronan, Adrien Brody, and David Tennant.

The story revolves around the murder of a wealthy businessman, Richard Harrow (played by Adrien Brody), who is found dead in his mansion with no signs of forced entry or struggle. Detective Toby Wilson (played by Sam Rockwell) is tasked with solving the case, but he's not exactly the most competent detective.

As the investigation unfolds, it becomes clear that everyone at the party where Harrow was killed had a motive for the murder. The suspects include Harrow's wife, Catherine (played by Saoirse Ronan), who stands to gain a large inheritance; Harrow's business partner, James (played by David Tennant); and Harrow's personal assistant, Thomas (played by Jack Lowden).

As Detective Wilson interviews the suspects, he discovers that each of them had a secret relationship with Harrow at some point. The web of deceit becomes increasingly complex as Wilson tries to untangle the truth from the lies.

Throughout the investigation, Wilson's own life is revealed through flashbacks, showing his troubled past and his struggles with addiction. His partner, Detective Sophie Hopkins (played by Phoebe Waller-Bridge), provides a voice of reason and support, but even she seems to be hiding secrets.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Harrow was not as innocent as he seemed. He had many secrets and was involved in some shady dealings. The suspects' motives for the murder become increasingly complex, and Wilson must use all his wits to uncover the truth.

In the end, Detective Wilson discovers that the killer is none other than Catherine, who had been planning her revenge against Harrow for years. However, just as she's about to be arrested, it's revealed that she was actually working with James, who had been manipulating her all along.

The movie ends with Detective Wilson and Sophie Hopkins finally solving the case, but not before they've both been shaken by the revelations about Harrow's life and the secrets he kept. The film is a witty and clever comedy of errors, full of twists and turns that keep the viewer guessing until the very end.

Overall, See How They Run is a hilarious and engaging mystery that keeps you on the edge of your seat from start to finish. With its talented cast, witty script, and clever plot twists, it's a must-see for fans of comedy and mystery alike.

belongs_to_collection.name: Diary of a Wimpy Kid Collection

original_title: Diary of a Wimpy Kid: The Long Haul
overview: A Heffley family road trip to attend Meemaw's 90th birthday party goes hilariously off course thanks to Greg's newest scheme to get to a video gaming convention.
title: Diary of a Wimpy Kid: The Long Haul
plot:
Diary of a Wimpy Kid: The Long Haul is a 2017 American road comedy film directed by David Bowers, who co-wrote it with the series' author Jeff Kinney. It is the fourth installment in the Diary of a Wimpy Kid film series and is based on the ninth book of the same name, with elements of the seventh, eighth and tenth books. The film recast the Heffley family, with Jason Ian Drucker as Greg, Alicia Silverstone as his mother Susan, Tom Everett Scott as his father Frank, Charlie Wright as his older brother Rodrick and Owen Asztalos as his best friend Rowley.

At a family restaurant, Susan announces that the Heffleys will take a road trip to attend Meemaw's 90th birthday party, to the dismay of Greg and Rodrick. Before they leave, Greg suffers a public humiliation when he gets stuck in the restaurant's ball pit with a dirty diaper stuck to his hand. Someone films his panic, and the clip goes viral online as the "Diaper Hands" meme, making him infamous. When Greg discovers that a video game convention, the Player Expo, is taking place near Meemaw's home in Indianapolis, and that his favorite online gamer, Mac Digby, will appear there, he decides to secretly sneak off during the trip, hoping that a video with Digby will make people forget about Diaper Hands.

Susan has declared the trip "technology-free" and confiscates everyone's phones, but Greg retrieves his and enlists Rodrick's help with his plan. Along the way the family endures a long series of disasters. At a county fair, Greg wins a piglet that the family is forced to take along, and they repeatedly cross paths with a menacing family who become convinced the Heffleys have wronged them. Their trip includes a seedy motel, a flock of seagulls, car trouble and other mishaps, as Greg's schemes to reach the Expo keep backfiring and threaten to ruin the family vacation entirely.

Released by 20th Century Fox in May 2017, the film was a critical and commercial failure, grossing about $40 million worldwide. Fans objected strongly to the recasting of the familiar characters, and critics found the humor crude and the story thin. It was the last live-action film in the franchise, which later continued with animated adaptations on Disney+.

overview: Forced into a deadly cat-and-mouse game, a disgraced mixed martial arts fighter is hunted through the jungles of Southeast Asia.
tagline: It's hunting season again...
title: Hard Target 2
plot:
Hard Target 2 is a 2016 American action film directed by Roel Reiné, starring Scott Adkins with Robert Knepper, Temuera Morrison, Rhona Mitra and Ann Truong. Billed as a follow-up to the 1993 film Hard Target, in which Jean-Claude Van Damme played a drifter battling a human hunting operation in New Orleans, it has no narrative connection to the original and reworks its premise of people hunted for sport in a new setting.

Professional mixed martial arts fighter Wes Baylor faces Jonny Sutherland for a welterweight championship in Las Vegas. Angry at the judges' scoring, Baylor tries for a knockout and accidentally kills Sutherland in the ring. Consumed by guilt, he goes into self-imposed exile in Thailand. Six months later, he is still haunted by the tragedy and scraping by in underground fights when he attracts the attention of Jonah Aldrich, a wealthy man who offers him $1 million for a private bout in Myanmar.

On arrival, Baylor learns that there is no fight: he is to be the prey in a lethal hunt organized by Aldrich for a group of rich clients. He is given a water bottle and a money belt that secretly contains a GPS tracker. The hunters include Sofia, a bullfighter named Esparto, a video game designer, a sharpshooter, a Texan and his son Tobias, and Aldrich's right-hand man Madden, supported by a unit of corrupt soldiers. Baylor kills his first pursuer at a waterfall and then meets Tha, a local woman who agrees to guide him to the border. As Aldrich escalates the hunt with armed motorcycles and rocket launchers, Baylor and Tha fight back, picking off hunters one by one. They make their way through a minefield, where an explosion buys them time to hide in a cave in which Tha finds her missing brother, an earlier target of Aldrich's game who had managed to survive in hiding. Baylor then turns the tables on the remaining hunters for a final confrontation with Aldrich, finding a measure of redemption along the way.

The film was released direct to video in 2016. Reviewers frequently noted that it could not match the original, which had been made with a much larger budget by the acclaimed director John Woo, but many judged it a respectable addition to Adkins's catalogue. Critics at HighDef Digest and MMA Torch were particularly enthusiastic, praising the fight scenes, Reiné's slick visuals and the cast of villains surrounding Adkins's sympathetic hero.

overview: One day, in the family manor, four cousins discover a passage to a mysterious world. Trapped in this unearthed land, the Kingdom of Keoherus, they must confront the Guardian of Time and face dark forces and beast to hopefully get home.
tagline: The war of time will begin.
title: Guardians of Time
plot:
Guardians of Time is a 2022 American family fantasy adventure film directed by Stephen Shimek from a screenplay by Sebastien Semon, Katy Baldwin and Jerome Reygner-Kalfon. Produced by Ace Entertainment Films, it stars Samantha Ryan, Ava Torres, Carley Coleman and Nia Salaam as four girls transported to a magical realm, with David Fletcher-Hall, Skip Schwink, Katie Burgess, Natalie Daniels, Harper Heath and Drew Pollock in supporting roles. Rated PG for some peril and fantasy violence, it was released on DVD by Lionsgate in October 2022.

Sisters Sybil (Ryan) and Alex (Torres) and their cousins Zoey (Coleman) and Theo (Salaam) are left at the sprawling family manor of the sisters' grandfather, Papa Nickolaou (Fletcher-Hall), while their parents go away on a trip. On the first afternoon Sybil begins to see strange visions. Exploring her grandfather's library, Alex finds an old book titled The Beginning is the End is the Beginning, filled with mysterious drawings and symbols. The youngest sister, feeling alienated and left out by the others, sets in motion the events that lead them through a hidden passage into the Kingdom of Keoherus, a mysterious land resembling a prehistoric wilderness. Trapped there, the four must confront the Guardian of Time, battle dark forces and face ancient beasts including rock and tree monsters, dinosaurs and a dragon, gaining special powers along the way. Working together to rescue Alex and find their way back to the manor, they learn to trust one another, to accept themselves and not to grow up too fast, while the others come to appreciate the girl who had felt excluded. The story also weaves in references to Amelia Earhart and to Greek and Roman mythology.

Reviews were mixed to negative. John Delia Sr. of ACED Magazine found it a fun adventure aimed at girls from ten into their teens, praising the storyline, the acting and its moral lessons about friendship and standing up for one another, though he called the special effects somewhat elementary. Common Sense Media rated it suitable for ages eight and up, commending its diverse cast of smart, strong and adventurous girls and its coming-of-age themes, while warning that its monsters might scare younger viewers. Jeremy Butler of Upcoming Discs was scathing, judging the obvious green-screen work and sub-par computer graphics below B-movie quality, the characters forgettable and the theme of the excluded younger sibling a cliché.

original_title: Monster High: Scaris City of Frights
overview: The Monstruitas of Monster High are obsessed with going to Scaris, The City of Frights for Fashion international competition where the winner will become the apprentice of the world famous Madame Ghostier designer.
title: Monster High: Scaris City of Frights
plot:
Monster High: Scaris City of Frights is a 2013 animated film produced by Mattel Playground Productions.

The movie follows Frankie Stein, the daughter of Frankenstein's monster and his bride, as she travels to the city of Scaris with her friends Draculaura, Clawdeen Wolf, Cleo de Nile, and Deuce Gorgon. Upon arrival, they discover that Scaris is in danger from an evil spirit known as Malicia, who seeks to destroy the city.

The main themes of Monster High: Scaris City of Frights include:

1. Friendship and teamwork: The movie highlights the strong bond between Frankie and her friends as they work together to defeat Malicia and save Scaris.
2. Embracing one's uniqueness: The characters in the film celebrate their individuality and differences, promoting a message of self-acceptance and empowerment.
3. Overcoming fears and anxieties: Frankie, in particular, struggles with her own fears and insecurities, but ultimately learns to face them head-on and find confidence in herself.
4. Protecting one's community: The characters demonstrate a strong sense of responsibility towards their friends and the city of Scaris, showing that taking care of others is an important part of being a good friend.

The movie features a mix of humor, action, and heart, making it a fun and engaging watch for both kids and adults.

overview: A young husband and wife must fight to return home in a post-apocalyptic mid-western landscape ravaged by gangs.
tagline: In the end, defend.
title: The Domestics
plot:
The Domestics is a 2018 American horror film that explores the darker aspects of suburban life and the complexities of relationships within a family. At its core, the movie delves into the theme of toxic masculinity, where traditional masculine norms are challenged by the patriarch's descent into madness.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the family's seemingly idyllic facade hides a web of secrets, lies, and emotional manipulation. The film masterfully weaves together elements of psychological horror, domestic drama, and social commentary to create a thought-provoking narrative that critiques the societal expectations placed on men and their roles within families.

The Domestics also touches upon themes of isolation, loneliness, and the blurring of reality, as the family's dynamics become increasingly distorted. The film's use of tension and suspense expertly builds towards a shocking climax, leaving the audience questioning what is real and what is just a product of the characters' fragile mental states.

Ultimately, The Domestics presents a searing critique of toxic masculinity, revealing the devastating consequences of unchecked emotions and the erosion of empathy within relationships. Through its unflinching portrayal of domestic violence, emotional abuse, and the breakdown of social norms, the film sparks uncomfortable conversations about the darker aspects of human nature and our collective responsibility to confront them.

overview: A man glimpses the future Fate has planned for him – and chooses to fight for his own destiny. Battling the powerful Adjustment Bureau across, under and through the streets of New York, he risks his destined greatness to be with the only woman he's ever loved.
tagline: Fight for your fate.
title: The Adjustment Bureau
plot:
The Adjustment Bureau is a 2011 American science fiction thriller film directed by George Nolfi and written by Gill Steiner. The movie stars Matt Damon, Emily Blunt, Anthony Mackie, and John Slattery.

The main themes of The Adjustment Bureau revolve around free will vs. determinism, fate, and the consequences of one's choices. The story follows David Norris (Matt Damon), a young politician who discovers that his life is being controlled by a mysterious organization known as the Adjustment Bureau.

As the plot unfolds, it becomes clear that the Adjustment Bureau has been manipulating events to ensure that certain individuals follow predetermined paths in life. However, when David meets Elise Sellas (Emily Blunt), he begins to question the nature of his reality and the choices he's made.

The film explores the tension between free will and determinism, suggesting that our lives are shaped by a complex interplay of factors beyond our control. The Adjustment Bureau serves as a metaphor for the unseen forces that influence our decisions and the consequences that follow.

Throughout the movie, the characters grapple with the idea that their choices may be predetermined, leading to a sense of existential crisis and moral ambiguity. Ultimately, the film raises questions about the nature of reality, the power of individual agency, and the consequences of resisting or accepting one's fate.

The Adjustment Bureau also touches on themes of love, sacrifice, and redemption, as David and Elise navigate their complicated relationship and confront the forces that seek to control them.

Overall, The Adjustment Bureau is a thought-provoking film that challenges viewers to consider the complexities of human decision-making and the consequences of our choices.

overview: Dug is sent on foolish missions by Alpha, Beta, and Gamma so they can hunt for the Bird of Paradise Falls by themselves. Dug may find that where he belongs is not where he's been looking.
title: Dug's Special Mission
plot:
Dug's Special Mission is a 2009 American computer-animated short film from Pixar, directed by Ronnie del Carmen and released as a companion to the feature Up on its Blu-ray and DVD editions, and later on Pixar Short Films Collection: Volume 2. Bob Peterson voices the talking golden retriever Dug as well as the pack leader Alpha, with Delroy Lindo as Beta, Jerome Ranft as Gamma, and Ed Asner and Jordan Nagai reprising their roles as Carl Fredricksen and Russell. Up's producer Jonas Rivera described the short as a glimpse of what Dug was doing on his mysterious mission when audiences first meet him in the feature.

The story takes place during the events of Up. It is Dug's birthday, and the cheerful, simple-minded dog, whose special collar allows him to speak, hopes it will be the happiest day of his life. Instead, he gets in the way of the pack of dogs serving the explorer Charles F. Muntz, who are hunting the giant exotic bird Kevin. The pack's leaders, Alpha, a Doberman with a malfunctioning collar that makes his voice comically high-pitched, Beta, a Rottweiler, and Gamma, a bulldog, are irritated by his blundering and invent a series of "special missions" for him that are really meant to keep him out of their way.

Each assignment backfires spectacularly. Told to guard the bird's "favourite rock" and make sure it does not move, Dug dislodges a pebble that sends a boulder rolling toward the pack. Ordered to sit in the bird's "favourite hole", he sinks through quicksand and lands on the others just as they are about to spring their trap. Told to sit on a rock, he sends Alpha, Beta and Gamma tumbling down a cliff. A string of further mishaps follows, as Dug's obedient attempts to follow orders trigger the very traps laid for Kevin, entangling the pack in nets, firing tranquilliser darts and toppling rock columns with Alpha on top.

Furious, Alpha reports to Muntz that Dug has ruined their hunt. Seeing Muntz's airship, the Spirit of Adventure, in the sky and fearing punishment, Dug flees into a misty, rocky landscape, while Beta sarcastically wishes him a happy birthday. There he notices rocks shaped like a turtle and a man, and when he hears a voice saying "I see you back there", he realises he has found what he wished for: a new master, Carl. The short then joins the moment in Up when Russell first mistakes Dug for a rock, and ends with Dug's greeting, "Hi there!"

Reviewers noted its mild slapstick violence, more humorous than upsetting.

overview: Looking to mine for gold, greedy industrialist Bartholomew Bogue seizes control of the Old West town of Rose Creek. With their lives in jeopardy, Emma Cullen and other desperate residents turn to bounty hunter Sam Chisolm for help. Chisolm recruits an eclectic group of gunslingers to take on Bogue and his ruthless henchmen. With a deadly showdown on the horizon, the seven mercenaries soon find themselves fighting for more than just money once the bullets start to fly.
tagline: Justice has a number.
title: The Magnificent Seven
plot:
The Magnificent Seven is a 2016 American Western action film directed by Antoine Fuqua and written by Nic Pizzolatto and Richard Wenk. A remake of the 1960 film, which was itself a remake of Akira Kurosawa's Seven Samurai, it stars Denzel Washington, Chris Pratt, Ethan Hawke, Vincent D'Onofrio, Lee Byung-hun, Manuel Garcia-Rulfo and Martin Sensmeier as the seven gunmen, with Peter Sarsgaard as the villain Bartholomew Bogue and Haley Bennett as Emma Cullen. It was the final film scored by James Horner, who died in 2015 after composing part of the music, which was completed by Simon Franglen. The film opened the 2016 Toronto International Film Festival and closed the Venice Film Festival.

In 1879, the ruthless industrialist Bartholomew Bogue and his army of private agents take control of the frontier town of Rose Creek, forcing its residents to work in his gold mine for a pittance. When the townspeople protest, Bogue has their church burned and several citizens shot dead in public, including the farmer Matthew Cullen. He gives the survivors three weeks to sell him their land at a fraction of its value.

Matthew's widow Emma and her friend Teddy set out to hire men who can defend the town. Their first recruit is the bounty hunter Sam Chisholm, played by Washington, who shows particular interest when he hears Bogue's name.
