title: Heaven's Lost Property Final – The Movie: Eternally My Master
plot:
Heaven's Lost Property Final - The Movie: Eternally My Master is a 2014 Japanese anime film that explores the complex and often tumultuous relationship between Sora, a young man who has fallen in love with a fallen angel named Ikaros, and his fellow angels. 

The movie delves into themes of unrequited love, longing, and the human (or rather, angelic) condition. It portrays Sora's unwavering dedication to Ikaros, despite knowing that their love is doomed from the start. This all-consuming passion serves as a catalyst for Sora's growth and self-discovery, as he grapples with his own identity and purpose.

The film also touches on the idea of sacrifice and the consequences of one's actions. As Sora navigates his relationships with Ikaros and other characters, he is forced to confront the harsh realities of his own desires and the impact they have on those around him.

Furthermore, the movie explores the concept of freedom and the constraints that come with it. The angels, bound by their divine duties, struggle to break free from their predetermined paths, while Sora's love for Ikaros serves as a powerful force that challenges these limitations.

Ultimately, Heaven's Lost Property Final - The Movie: Eternally My Master is a poignant exploration of the human (and angelic) experience, one that celebrates the beauty and complexity of love in all its forms.

overview: Danny Ocean reunites with his old flame and the rest of his merry band of thieves in carrying out three huge heists in Rome, Paris and Amsterdam – but a Europol agent is hot on their heels.
tagline: Twelve is the new eleven.
title: Ocean's Twelve
plot:
Ocean's Twelve is a heist film directed by Steven Soderbergh, released in 2004. The movie serves as a sequel to Ocean's Eleven (2001) and follows the story of Danny Ocean (George Clooney) and his team as they plan and execute another elaborate heist.

The film begins with Danny Ocean, who has just been released from prison after serving time for his previous heist. He reunites with his old team, including Rusty Ryan (Brad Pitt), Linus Caldwell (Matt Damon), Basher Tarr (Don Cheadle), Yen (Shaobo Qin), and Saul Bloom (Carl Reiner). The team is approached by Isabel Lahiri (Catherine Zeta-Jones), a former lover of Danny's who has become the new CEO of the World Bank.

Isabel reveals that she has discovered a plot to embezzle millions of dollars from the bank, but needs help to expose the scheme. She proposes an alliance with Danny and his team, offering them a share of the money if they can help her bring down the corrupt officials involved in the embezzlement.

The team accepts the challenge and begins planning their next heist. They target the Bank of France, where Isabel's accomplices are hiding millions of dollars. However, things become complicated when Danny discovers that Isabel is not what she seems, and that her true intentions may be more sinister than he initially thought.

As the team navigates the complex web of deceit and corruption, they must also contend with a rival thief, Saul Bloom, who has his own agenda for the money. The team's plan is put to the test as they face numerous obstacles, including double-crosses, betrayals, and unexpected twists.

Throughout the film, Soderbergh expertly weaves together multiple storylines, keeping the audience engaged and guessing until the very end. The film features a talented ensemble cast, with standout performances from Clooney, Pitt, and Zeta-Jones.

The climax of the film takes place in Paris, where Danny and his team face off against their rivals in an epic battle of wits and cunning. In the end, Danny emerges victorious, having successfully exposed the embezzlement scheme and brought the corrupt officials to justice.

However, the film's ending is not without its surprises. As Danny and Isabel share a moment of intimacy, it becomes clear that her true intentions were not entirely altruistic. The film ends on a bittersweet note, leaving the audience wondering what the future holds for Danny and his team.

Overall, Ocean's Twelve is a thrilling heist film that delivers on its promise of high-stakes action, witty banter, and clever plot twists. With its talented cast and expert direction, it is a must-see for fans of the genre.

overview: Out hiking, Special Forces Brenner Baker stumbles onto a Cartel's compound. Her husband's killed and she's left for dead. The Cartel made two mistakes, killed her husband and left her alive. They won't live to make another.
tagline: They left her for dead. Big mistake.
title: Army of One
plot:
Army of One is a 2020 American action thriller film directed by Stephen Durham from a screenplay he wrote with Mary Ann Barnes, Ellen Hollman and David Dittlinger. Produced by 2nd Nature Films, Popcorn and Soda Productions and Split Point Productions, it stars Hollman as a former special forces soldier seeking revenge, with Matt Passmore, Gary Kasper, Geraldine Singer, Kendra Carelli and Stephen Dunlevy in supporting roles. The film was released in the United States in December 2020 and runs about 87 minutes.

Brenner Baker (Hollman), a decorated Army Ranger, is happily married to Dillon (Passmore), a police detective who still bears the physical and psychological scars of a violent incident involving masked men. Hoping to escape the stress of their jobs, the couple take a road trip into the backwoods of Alabama. Along the way they are harassed by a belligerent local in a pickup truck, and when they run into him again at a diner they learn that he is Butch (Kasper), whose seemingly kindly mother, known as Mama (Singer), defuses the confrontation and lets them leave unharmed. Later, out hiking, the couple are caught in the rain and take shelter in an apparently empty, secluded cabin, only to discover a hidden store of drugs and guns belonging to Butch's family, a criminal clan tied to a cartel and involved in drug dealing and human trafficking. They are captured and interrogated, and both are shot, but the gang fails to check whether Brenner is dead before dumping her in an open grave. Wounded and grieving, she climbs out and uses her combat and survival skills to hunt down the family one by one, while also trying to free other prisoners they hold captive.

Reviews were mixed. Eoin of The Action Elite called the film a slick and effective action picture with a star-making turn from Hollman, who performed her own stunts, including a one-shot fight sequence reportedly rehearsed for only an hour and filmed in a single take; he found the villains so hateful that their comeuppance was satisfying, while conceding that the story was nothing new. Andrew Stover of Film Threat gave it 5 out of 10, writing that its rapid action sequences enliven an otherwise uneven and insipid revenge tale, that its bloody, hammy and clichéd antics fall short of the genre's best, and that Dillon's traumatic backstory is left unexplored.

overview: A grieving detective in the near-future hunts down criminals who trade artificial humans on the black market. In the fight to end AI exploitation, an underground resistance attempts to infiltrate him by sabotaging the programming of the artificial human assigned as his companion to behave like his late wife. She begins to question her reality as memories of a past life begin to surface in a world where nothing is as it seems.
title: Wifelike
plot:
Wifelike is a 2022 American science fiction thriller written and directed by James Bird, starring Jonathan Rhys Meyers and Elena Kampouris, with Doron Bell, Agam Darshi and Sara Sampaio in supporting roles. It was released in select theaters and on digital platforms on August 12, 2022.

In the near future, a company called Wifelike manufactures expensive android replicas of deceased women for the men who mourn them. These companions are designed to be subservient to their owners, but they gradually begin to develop consciousness. A militant activist group, S.C.A.I.R., considers the androids slaves and seeks to destroy the company. One faction steals companions, reprograms them and uses them to commit crimes and bombings, and the authorities have been unable to identify its leader, known as the Ringmaster.

William Bradwell is a seasoned agent who tracks down stolen androids and returns them to their owners. He orders a companion modeled on his late wife, Meredith, who begins learning about her life in order to become more like her. William tells her that Meredith was once a S.C.A.I.R. activist who gave up the cause after falling in love with him. It is not the first time he has gone through this process: earlier versions of his companion were stolen by the group and recovered by him, each time with their memories wiped.

As the new companion learns, she begins to dream of a masked man who claims to have known her before her last reset, and she is visited by Louise, a S.C.A.I.R. member who seems to know her previous iterations. William discovers that some androids have joined the group willingly to escape their owners, and he enters the digital "dreamscape" that manages the companions' thoughts to confront the masked man. Taken back to Wifelike for another wipe, the companion learns from other androids that she can retain hidden memories, and she secretly keeps playing her role. Evidence emerges that William murdered the man presumed to be the Ringmaster and that he is hiding the truth about Meredith. Overriding her safety protocols, the companion kills William and returns to S.C.A.I.R., revealing that she herself is the true Ringmaster, while the company announces a crackdown led by an android version of William.

The film received poor reviews, holding a 13% rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on eight reviews.

overview: A filmmaker holds a series of boundary-pushing auditions for his latest project: a thriller on the subject of female pleasure.
title: The Exterminating Angels
plot:
The Exterminating Angels (French: Les Anges exterminateurs) is a 2006 French erotic drama written and directed by Jean-Claude Brisseau, with music by Jean Musy and cinematography by Wilfrid Sempé. Together with Secret Things (2002) and À l'aventure (2009), it forms a trilogy about female sexuality. The film is semi-autobiographical: in 2002 Brisseau was arrested and later convicted of harassing actresses who had performed sexual acts in front of him during auditions for Secret Things, and he based the film on his book of the same name, a fictionalized account of his working methods and his version of those events. Frédéric van den Driessche plays the filmmaker François, while the young actresses are played by Maroussia Dubreuil (Charlotte), Lise Bellynck (Julie) and Marie Allan (Stéphanie), with Raphaële Godin and Margaret Zenou as two apparitions, and Jeanne Cellard as François's grandmother.

In a dream, the ghost of François's grandmother warns him not to let his curiosity take control of him, while two black-clad fallen angels hover over him as he sleeps, conspiring to set events in motion. François plans a film about the moment when women transgress sexual taboos. Without a producer or casting director, he holds auditions himself, and after many candidates refuse, two young actresses show promise. In a restaurant he guides Charlotte through an improvisation in which she pleasures herself among the diners, joined by Julie, as the waitress Stéphanie looks on; the trio continues the experiment in a hotel. The next day Stéphanie comes to his office and asks to take part. François insists he is only gathering material for his script and remains a detached observer, but the encounters become increasingly intense. Charlotte grows obsessive, wrecking her apartment and calling him at all hours, and his wife warns him about her ego, while the women's rivalries and obsessions, apparently steered by the spirits, turn against him with tragic consequences.

The film premiered at the Cannes Film Festival on 20 May 2006 and opened in limited release in the United States through IFC First Take on 7 March 2007. Reviews were mixed: Rotten Tomatoes reports 49% positive reviews and Metacritic a score of 54. The Hollywood Reporter called it provocative and sexy but pretentious, redeemed by its glossy visual style and humor, while Film-Forward saw it as an unpersuasive mea culpa.

original_title: The Drawn Together Movie: The Movie!
overview: When the mystery-solving musician Foxxy Love notices she and her fellow housemates can curse without being bleeped—something they've never been able to do before—she realizes their show has been canceled. Determined to get back on the air, the gang travels to Make-A-Point-Land in order to get a point (and get back on the air).
title: The Drawn Together Movie: The Movie!
plot:
The Drawn Together Movie: The Movie! is a 2010 American adult animated musical black comedy based on the Comedy Central sitcom Drawn Together. Written and executive produced by the show's creators, Dave Jeser and Matt Silverstein, produced by Richard Quan and directed by Greg Franklin, it was the first Drawn Together production after the series was cancelled. The film premiered at the South by Southwest festival in Austin in March 2010 and was released direct to home video in April 2010.

The film picks up after the show's cancellation. Foxxy Love discovers that she can suddenly swear without being bleeped and calls the network to find out why the series was taken off the air, learning that it was replaced by another animated show, a crude parody of South Park. The head of the network, who has always hated the series, discovers that the housemates are still alive, a fact the show's producer has hidden from him, and he summons I.S.R.A.E.L., a robot designed to erase cartoon characters, to wipe them out. The robot destroys the Drawn Together house and captures the producer, while the housemates escape in Foxxy's van.

Learning that they are not original creations but parodies of other cartoon characters, the housemates split up. Foxxy believes their survival depends on getting their show back on the air, while Princess Clara refuses to accept that she is not a real princess and insists that her father can protect them. Captain Hero, Xandir and Ling-Ling follow Clara, while Spanky Ham and Wooldoor Sockbat join Foxxy, and Toot Braunstein steals the van and drives off on her own. As I.S.R.A.E.L. pursues them across a series of animated worlds, the characters encounter grotesque creatures and parodies of famous animation styles, and they must reunite to confront the network and persuade it to give them another chance, perhaps in the form of a direct-to-DVD film.

Like the television series, the film relies on shock humour, satirical musical numbers and deliberately offensive jokes about race, sexuality and religion, while also mocking the television industry and the decision to cancel the show.

The film received negative reviews from critics. Common Sense Media awarded it one star, criticising it as filled to the brim with lewd sexual acts, language and violence, and arguing that its attempts to push the boundaries of taste overwhelmed whatever satire it contained.

overview: In Lincoln City, some inhabitants have extraordinary abilities. Most live below the poverty line, under the close surveillance of a heavily militarized police force. Connor, a construction worker with powers, involves with a criminal gang to help his ailing mother. (Based on the short film “Code 8,” 2016.)
tagline: Fear is the most dangerous power
title: Code 8
plot:
Code 8 is a 2019 Canadian science fiction thriller film directed by Jeff Renfroe and written by Michael Chabon, Matt Johnson, and Evan Goldberg. The movie premiered at the 2019 Toronto International Film Festival.

The story revolves around Kabir (played by Anthony Mackie), a young man who possesses superhuman abilities after being bitten by an infected mosquito while traveling in India. He is diagnosed with "Code 8," a rare genetic disorder that grants him extraordinary powers, including super strength, speed, and agility.

Kabir returns to his hometown of Toronto, where he struggles to control his new abilities and navigate the complexities of his life as a superhero. His brother, Tyler (played by Luke Mitchell), is initially unaware of Kabir's secret but eventually discovers his true nature.

As Kabir tries to live a normal life, he becomes embroiled in a conspiracy involving corrupt government officials and corporate interests who seek to exploit individuals with superhuman abilities for their own gain. The main antagonist, Senator Stevens (played by Stephen McHattie), is determined to capture and control those with Code 8 powers.

Kabir's journey takes him from the streets of Toronto to the corridors of power in Ottawa, where he must confront his own demons and make difficult choices about how to use his abilities. Along the way, he forms alliances with a group of individuals who possess similar powers, including Tyler, who becomes a key player in Kabir's quest for justice.

Throughout the movie, the themes of identity, community, and social responsibility are explored. Kabir must navigate the complexities of being a superhero while also dealing with personal struggles and relationships. The film features a diverse cast of characters, reflecting the multiculturalism of Toronto.

The plot thickens as Kabir discovers that Senator Stevens is hiding a dark secret: he has been experimenting on individuals with Code 8 powers, using them for his own nefarious purposes. Kabir must use his abilities to stop Stevens and his cohorts, while also confronting the moral implications of his actions.

In the end, Kabir emerges victorious but not without scars. He finds a sense of belonging among those who possess similar powers, and he begins to forge a new path forward, one that balances his desire for justice with his need for human connection. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that even in the face of adversity, individuals with extraordinary abilities can make a positive impact.

Overall, Code 8 is a gripping thriller that explores themes of identity, community, and social responsibility. With its diverse cast and thought-provoking storyline, it offers a fresh take on the superhero genre.

overview: Two sisters find their already strained relationship challenged as a mysterious new planet threatens to collide with Earth.
tagline: Enjoy it while it lasts
title: Melancholia
plot:
Melancholia is a 2011 psychological drama film written and directed by Lars von Trier. The movie stars Kirsten Dunst, Charlotte Gainsbourg, Kiefer Sutherland, Alexander Skarsgård, and Stellan Skarsgård.

The main themes of Melancholia include:

1. **Existentialism**: The film explores the meaninglessness of life in the face of an impending apocalypse. The planet Melancholia is on a collision course with Earth, serving as a metaphor for the inevitability of death and the futility of human existence.
2. **Guilt and Responsibility**: The characters are haunted by their past mistakes and guilt, which is exacerbated by the approaching doom. This theme is particularly evident in the character of Justine (Kirsten Dunst), who struggles with feelings of inadequacy and responsibility for a tragic event from her past.
3. **Mental Illness**: Melancholia explores the complexities of mental illness, particularly depression and anxiety. The characters' emotional states are deeply intertwined with their relationships and the impending apocalypse, highlighting the blurred lines between sanity and madness.
4. **Femininity and Motherhood**: The film critiques traditional notions of femininity and motherhood, as embodied by Justine's character. Her struggles to connect with her daughter and navigate her relationships serve as a commentary on the societal expectations placed upon women.
5. **Apocalyptic Nihilism**: Melancholia presents a bleak vision of the end of the world, where human existence is rendered meaningless in the face of an unstoppable force. This theme serves as a commentary on the futility of human endeavor and the inevitability of fate.

Throughout the film, von Trier employs a non-linear narrative structure, blurring the lines between reality and fantasy. The cinematography, composed by Hugues Dalmiéga, adds to the sense of unease and foreboding, creating a visually stunning and unsettling experience for the viewer.

Ultimately, Melancholia is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, inviting viewers to confront their own mortality and the complexities of existence.

overview: A group of friends venture into the remote Texas woods for a party weekend and find themselves stalked by Bigfoot.
tagline: The legend is real. So is the terror.
title: Exists
plot:
Exists is a 2014 American found-footage monster horror film directed by Eduardo Sánchez, co-creator of The Blair Witch Project, from a screenplay by Jamie Nash. It stars Chris Osborn, Samuel Davis, Dora Madison Burge, Roger Edwards and Denise Williamson, with Brian Steele playing the creature. Moving away from the psychological tone of Sánchez's previous film Lovely Molly, it returns to the creature-feature horror of his earlier Altered, also written by Nash. The film premiered at South by Southwest in March 2014.

Brothers Brian and Matt invite friends, including Matt's girlfriend Dora and the couple Todd and Elizabeth, on a weekend camping trip to their uncle Bob's remote cabin in the woods of East Texas. On the way in, Matt hits something with the car in the dark, and the group hears loud animal cries in the distance but dismisses them. Finding the road blocked by a fallen tree, they walk the rest of the way, only to discover that the cabin is run-down, and they spend the first night in the car.

The next morning Brian finds blood and a tuft of hair on the fender. Convinced he has glimpsed Bigfoot running along a ridge, he sets up GoPro cameras around the cabin, hoping to capture the creature on film and become famous. That night the creature screams and circles the cabin, and Brian's night-vision camera catches it at a window. By morning their car has been destroyed, and the brothers admit that they never told their uncle they would be using the cabin. Cut off from help, the friends are besieged by an enraged Sasquatch that seems driven by a specific grievance against them. When members of the group try to go for help, the creature hunts them through the forest, and the survivors eventually learn what the accident on the road may have taken from it.

Exists received generally unfavorable reviews. It holds a 30 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 22. Keith Uhlich of The A.V. Club was especially scathing in his review. After its festival premiere, the film was released in the United States in February 2015, and Entertainment One issued it on DVD and Blu-ray in the United Kingdom that April.

overview: Richard Jewell thinks quick, works fast, and saves hundreds, perhaps thousands, of lives after a domestic terrorist plants several pipe bombs and they explode during a concert, only to be falsely suspected of the crime by sloppy FBI work and sensational media coverage.
tagline: The world will know his name and the truth.
title: Richard Jewell
plot:
Richard Jewell is a 2019 American biographical drama film directed by Clint Eastwood, produced by Malpaso Productions, and written by Billy Ray.

The main themes of Richard Jewell are:

1. **Misinformation and False Accusations**: The film highlights the devastating consequences of misinformation and false accusations on an innocent person's life. Richard Jewell, a security guard at the 1996 Summer Olympics in Atlanta, is falsely accused of being the mastermind behind the bombing that killed two people and injured over 100 others.

2. **Media Manipulation and Sensationalism**: The movie critiques the media's role in sensationalizing and distorting facts to sell stories. The film shows how the media's initial focus on Jewell as a suspect led to a public frenzy, further damaging his reputation and ultimately affecting his life.

3. **The Power of Truth and Redemption**: Through Jewell's story, the film emphasizes the importance of seeking truth and fighting for one's innocence in the face of overwhelming adversity. The movie also explores the theme of redemption, as Jewell works to clear his name and rebuild his life after being wrongly accused.

4. **The Human Cost of Trauma**: Richard Jewell delves into the psychological trauma experienced by those affected by the bombing and its aftermath. The film humanizes the victims' families and highlights the long-lasting impact of traumatic events on individuals and communities.

5. **The Importance of Investigative Journalism**: The movie praises the investigative journalism of Kathy Scruggs, a reporter who initially questioned Jewell's involvement in the bombing. Her persistence and dedication to uncovering the truth ultimately led to Jewell's exoneration.

Overall, Richard Jewell is a powerful exploration of the consequences of misinformation, media manipulation, and the importance of seeking truth and redemption in the face of adversity.

overview: He fought his first battle on the Scottish Highlands in 1536. He will fight his greatest battle on the streets of New York City in 1986. His name is Connor MacLeod. He is immortal.
tagline: There can be only one.
title: Highlander
plot:
Highlander is a 1986 American fantasy adventure film directed by Russell Mulcahy and written by Gregory Widen. The movie stars Christopher Lambert as Connor MacLeod, a Scottish Highlander who discovers he is an immortal.

The story begins with Connor, a young man living in Scotland during the Jacobite rising of 1745. He witnesses the Battle of Culloden, where his clan is defeated, and he is mortally wounded. However, instead of dying, Connor is healed by Juan Sanchez Villa-Lobos Ramírez (Sean Connery), an immortal who has been watching over him.

Juan explains to Connor that immortals are born with a "prize," which is the essence of every human being's soul. The prize is what makes them unique and gives them their individuality. Immortals must find and kill other immortals in order to gain their prizes, thereby becoming more powerful and closer to achieving their ultimate goal: the Prize.

Connor learns that he has been chosen as a "Immortal" and that his prize is the soul of an unknown woman. He sets out on a journey across time and space to find her, while also being pursued by other immortals who seek to kill him.

As Connor travels through history, he encounters various characters, including Juan, who becomes his mentor and guide. Along the way, he meets other immortals, such as the Kurgan (Clancy Brown), a ruthless and cunning immortal who seeks to kill Connor and claim his prize for himself.

Throughout the movie, Connor's journey takes him from 18th-century Scotland to modern-day New York City. He faces numerous challenges and obstacles, including battles with other immortals and struggles with his own identity.

As the story unfolds, Connor becomes increasingly obsessed with finding the woman whose soul is his prize. He believes that she holds the key to understanding his purpose as an immortal and that their reunion will bring him peace and fulfillment.

The movie culminates in a final showdown between Connor and the Kurgan. The two immortals engage in a fierce battle, during which they exchange blows and insults. In the end, Connor emerges victorious, but not before the Kurgan reveals that he has been searching for the woman whose soul is Connor's prize.

In a surprising twist, it is revealed that the woman Connor was searching for all along is actually his own wife, who had died in childbirth. The movie ends with Connor finally finding peace and understanding, as he realizes that his true prize is not the soul of another person, but rather the love and connection he shares with those around him.

Overall, Highlander is a classic tale of immortality, adventure, and self-discovery. With its unique blend of action, drama, and fantasy elements, it has become a beloved cult classic among fans of science fiction and adventure movies.

overview: Robin is sent by Batman to work with the Teen Titans after his volatile behavior botches up a Justice League mission. The Titans must then step up to face Trigon after he possesses the League and threatens to conquer the world.
title: Justice League vs. Teen Titans
plot:
Justice League vs. Teen Titans is a 2016 animated superhero film produced by Warner Bros. Animation and DC Entertainment. The movie brings together two iconic teams from the DC Comics universe: the Justice League, led by Batman, and the Teen Titans, led by Robin.

The main themes of Justice League vs. Teen Titans can be broken down into several key areas:

1. **Coming of Age**: The film explores the transition from adolescence to adulthood for the Teen Titans, particularly Robin (Dick Grayson), who is struggling to balance his responsibilities as a hero with his personal life and relationships.
2. **Leadership and Power Struggle**: Batman's leadership style clashes with the more impulsive and inexperienced approach of the Teen Titans, leading to tension and conflict between the two teams. This theme highlights the challenges of leadership and the importance of effective communication and trust-building.
3. **Identity and Belonging**: The movie delves into the themes of identity and belonging, particularly for Robin, who feels like an outsider among his peers. His struggles to find his place within the Justice League serve as a metaphor for the difficulties of growing up and finding one's purpose in life.
4. **Mentorship and Guidance**: Batman's character serves as a mentor and guide for the Teen Titans, particularly Robin. The film showcases the importance of guidance and support from experienced leaders in helping young heroes navigate their roles and responsibilities.
5. **Teamwork and Unity**: Ultimately, the movie emphasizes the value of teamwork and unity among the Justice League and the Teen Titans. Through their shared experiences and challenges, the two teams learn to put aside their differences and work together towards a common goal.

Overall, Justice League vs. Teen Titans is a coming-of-age story that explores themes of leadership, identity, mentorship, and teamwork, set against the backdrop of an epic superhero battle between two iconic teams from the DC Comics universe.

overview: Chloe, a teenager who is confined to a wheelchair, is homeschooled by her mother, Diane. Chloe soon becomes suspicious of her mother and begins to suspect that she may be harboring a dark secret.
tagline: You can't escape a mother's love.
title: Run
plot:
Run is a 2020 American thriller film written and directed by Aneesh Chaganty and starring Sarah Paulson and Kiera Allen.

The main themes of Run include:

1. Mother-Daughter Relationship: The movie explores the complex and often toxic relationship between a mother (Sarah Paulson) and her daughter (Kiera Allen). Their bond is tested when the daughter begins to suspect that her mother is hiding a dark secret.
2. Trauma and Mental Health: As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the mother's past trauma has had a profound impact on their relationship and the daughter's life. The film sheds light on the long-term effects of trauma and the importance of seeking help.
3. Identity and Self-Discovery: Throughout the movie, the daughter begins to question her own identity and sense of self. As she uncovers the truth about her mother's past, she must also confront her own feelings and desires.
4. Deception and Betrayal: The film is full of twists and turns, keeping the audience guessing until the very end. Run explores the themes of deception and betrayal, highlighting how these actions can have devastating consequences for those involved.

Overall, Run is a gripping thriller that delves into the complexities of human relationships, trauma, and identity.

belongs_to_collection.name: LEGO DC Comics Super Heroes Collection

original_title: LEGO DC Comics Super Heroes: Justice League - Gotham City Breakout
overview: The caped crusader reluctantly agrees to let Batgirl and Nightwing take him on a long overdue vacation from crime-fighting, while Superman and the Justice League watch over Gotham City.
title: LEGO DC Comics Super Heroes: Justice League - Gotham City Breakout
plot:
LEGO DC Comics Super Heroes: Justice League - Gotham City Breakout (2016) is an animated film that explores several key themes. At its core, the movie delves into the idea of chaos and disorder, as the Joker's plan to break out of Arkham Asylum sets off a chain reaction of events that threaten the stability of Gotham City.

The film also touches on the theme of teamwork and collaboration, as the Justice League must come together to stop the Joker's nefarious plans. This is reflected in the character development of Batman, who initially struggles with delegating tasks and trusting his teammates, but ultimately learns to rely on others to save the day.

Furthermore, the movie explores the concept of redemption and personal growth, particularly through the character of Harley Quinn. Her storyline serves as a nuanced exploration of her complex relationship with the Joker, and her own desires for autonomy and self-discovery.

The film also features a commentary on the nature of evil and the blurred lines between good and bad. The Joker's actions are portrayed as both humorous and terrifying, highlighting the complexity of his character and the moral ambiguity that surrounds him.

Overall, LEGO DC Comics Super Heroes: Justice League - Gotham City Breakout (2016) is a lighthearted and entertaining film that uses humor and satire to explore deeper themes and ideas.

overview: Mouse desperately wants to join The Midnight Clique, the infamous Baltimore dirt bike riders who rule the summertime streets. When Midnight’s leader, Blax, takes 14-year-old Mouse under his wing, Mouse soon finds himself torn between the straight-and-narrow and a road filled with fast money and violence.
tagline: Life happens at the crossroads.
title: Charm City Kings
plot:
Charm City Kings is a 2020 American biographical sports drama film directed by Chris Collins. The movie is based on the life of young skateboarder Kevin Landers, who was involved in a gang and eventually found redemption through skateboarding.

The main themes of Charm City Kings include:

1. Redemption: The film explores Kevin's journey from being part of a gang to finding a new passion in skateboarding, which ultimately leads him to leave his old life behind.
2. Family: The movie highlights the importance of family and the role that Kevin's mother plays in his life. She is a strong support system who encourages Kevin to pursue his love for skateboarding.
3. Gang violence: The film sheds light on the harsh realities of gang violence and its impact on young people, particularly those from disadvantaged backgrounds.
4. Self-discovery: Through skateboarding, Kevin discovers a new sense of purpose and identity, which helps him break free from the cycle of violence and crime.
5. Community: The movie showcases the importance of community and the role that skateboarding plays in bringing people together.

The film features a talented cast, including Jordan Davis, Luke Mitchell, and Keegan-Michael Key, among others. While it received mixed reviews from critics, Charm City Kings has been praised for its authentic portrayal of life in Baltimore's inner city and its inspiring message about the power of redemption and self-discovery.

overview: Japan is thrown into a panic after several ships are sunk near Odo Island. An expedition to the island led by Dr. Yemani soon discover something far more devastating than imagined in the form of a 50 meter tall monster whom the natives call Gojira. Now the monster begins a rampage that threatens to destroy not only Japan, but the rest of the world as well.
tagline: Godzilla, a weapon of science, a great battle of wonder and terror!
title: Godzilla
plot:
Godzilla, released in 1954, is a Japanese science fiction kaiju film directed by Ishirō Honda and produced by Tomoyuki Tanaka for Toho Film Co., Ltd. The movie is considered one of the most influential films in the Godzilla franchise and has become a cultural icon.

The story begins on September 9, 1954, with a series of mysterious events occurring around the world. A group of scientists at the United States Navy's underwater research facility, led by Dr. Kyohei Yamane (Takashi Shimura), discover that an American nuclear test in the Pacific has awakened a prehistoric monster from the depths of the ocean.

The creature, later named Godzilla, is a massive, fire-breathing reptile with incredible strength and durability. As it emerges from the depths, it wreaks havoc on Tokyo, destroying buildings and infrastructure with its atomic breath. The Japanese government is initially unable to stop the creature, and it seems that all hope is lost.

Enter Dr. Serizawa (Akihiko Hirata), a brilliant scientist who has been working on a top-secret project to develop a device that can emit a high-frequency sound wave capable of stunning Godzilla without causing harm to humans. The plan is to lure Godzilla into the ocean and use the device to render it unconscious.

As the story unfolds, we see the devastating effects of Godzilla's rampage on Tokyo, including the destruction of iconic landmarks like the Tokyo Tower and the Imperial Palace. Meanwhile, Dr. Yamane and his team work tirelessly to develop a solution to stop the creature.

In a climactic final confrontation, Dr. Serizawa and his team successfully deploy the device, which emits a high-frequency sound wave that renders Godzilla unconscious. The creature then sinks into the ocean, and the city begins to rebuild.

The movie ends with a sense of hope and renewal, as the Japanese people come together to rebuild their city and reflect on the lessons learned from the disaster. The film's themes of nuclear destruction, scientific responsibility, and the importance of international cooperation are still relevant today.

Godzilla (1954) is a masterpiece of Japanese cinema, with its groundbreaking special effects, atmospheric tension, and thought-provoking storyline. It has become an iconic symbol of Japan's post-war anxieties and continues to captivate audiences around the world.

overview: Documentary about the making of American Pie (1999), American Pie 2 (2001) and American Wedding (2003).
title: American Pie: Revealed
plot: Documentary about the making of American Pie (1999), American Pie 2 (2001) and American Wedding (2003).

original_title: Winnie the Pooh: A Very Merry Pooh Year
overview: It's Christmastime in the Hundred Acre Wood and all of the gang is getting ready with presents and decorations. The gang makes a list of what they want for Christmas and send it to Santa Claus - except that Pooh forgot to ask for something. So he heads out to retrieve the letter and get it to Santa by Christmas...which happens to be tomorrow!
tagline: A Full-Length Adventure
title: Winnie the Pooh: A Very Merry Pooh Year
plot:
Winnie the Pooh: A Very Merry Pooh Year is a Christmas-themed animated television special produced by Disney Television Animation, based on the characters created by A.A. Milne.

The main themes of Winnie the Pooh: A Very Merry Pooh Year revolve around friendship, kindness, and the importance of spending quality time with loved ones during the holiday season. The story follows Winnie the Pooh and his friends in the Hundred Acre Wood as they prepare for Christmas, but things don't go exactly as planned.

The special highlights the value of perseverance, teamwork, and the true meaning of Christmas. Through various misadventures and mishaps, the characters learn to appreciate the simple joys of life and the importance of being present with those around them.

One of the notable themes is also the idea of letting go of material possessions and focusing on what truly matters – friendship, love, and kindness. The special promotes a message of simplicity, humility, and the importance of being grateful for what one has.

Overall, Winnie the Pooh: A Very Merry Pooh Year is a heartwarming and entertaining holiday special that celebrates the spirit of Christmas through the lens of beloved characters from the Hundred Acre Wood.

overview: Burt Gummer returns home to Perfection, Nev., to find that the town of terror has become a theme park, and when the simulated giant worm attacks turn real, the survivalist must battle the creatures once again. Gummer pits his impressive knowledge of weaponry against the newest and deadliest generation of flesh-eating graboids, with help from two young entrepreneurs.
tagline: The Food Chain Just Grew Another Link.
title: Tremors 3: Back to Perfection
plot:
Tremors 3: Back to Perfection is a science fiction horror-comedy film directed by Don Coscarelli. The movie takes place in the same universe as the original Tremors trilogy and follows Burt Gummer's (Michael Gross) son, Earl (Justin Whalin), who returns to Perfection, Nevada, to help his father deal with a new threat.

The main themes of Tremors 3: Back to Perfection include:

1. Family dynamics: The movie explores the complex relationships within the Gummer family, particularly between Burt and Earl, as they work together to overcome their common enemy.
2. Science vs. Nature: The film highlights the dangers of playing with nature and tampering with forces beyond human control, as Earl's attempts to "perfect" the worm technology ultimately lead to chaos and destruction.
3. Hubris and Consequences: Earl's arrogance and overconfidence in his scientific abilities serve as a cautionary tale about the importance of humility and respecting the natural world.
4. Small-town life vs. Urbanization: The movie pokes fun at the idea of urbanization and the consequences of abandoning small towns like Perfection, which are left to fend for themselves against monstrous creatures.

The plot development revolves around Earl's attempts to create a worm-based technology that can be used for good or evil, while Burt tries to keep his son in check. As the story unfolds, the worms become increasingly aggressive and destructive, forcing the Gummars to team up with their neighbors to survive.

The ending features an epic showdown between the humans and the worms, with Earl's technology ultimately being used against him. The movie concludes on a bittersweet note, as Burt reflects on the lessons learned from his son's mistakes and the importance of family bonds in the face of adversity.

Overall, Tremors 3: Back to Perfection offers a thrilling and humorous ride, filled with action, suspense, and heartwarming moments of family love.

overview: A young teen and his misfit group of friends try to escape from a strict boarding school that holds dangerous secrets.
tagline: Not all secrets are innocent
title: While the Wolf's Away
plot:
While the Wolf's Away (Spanish: Mientras el lobo no está) is a 2017 Mexican mystery drama film written and directed by Joseph Hemsani in his directing debut, from a screenplay co-written with Abe Rosenberg. Hemsani had previously produced and co-written the horror film Archivo 253. Running 123 minutes, the film was distributed by Cinépolis Distribución and released in Mexican cinemas on 24 February 2017. It stars Luis de la Rosa, Mauricio García Lozano, Mar Carrera, Miranda Kay and Richie Mestre, with Regina Reynoso and Carla Adell.

Set in 1958 in an unnamed country, the story takes place at a strict, isolated boarding school deep in a forest. Alex, a troubled boy sent there after a prank that ended in tragedy, upsets the institution's rigid discipline from the moment he arrives. He bonds with three fellow students who share a single goal, to escape, and, inspired by legends of former pupils who supposedly managed to flee, the four friends begin plotting a breakout. Alex also falls for Daniela, one of the girls boarding at the school. As the friends defy the adults' authority and abuse, their flirtations and escape attempts begin to uncover the school's dark secrets, and the friendship and loyalty among them become essential for surviving an atmosphere ruled by fear and humiliation. The title's "wolf", the predator destroying the lives of those who cross its path, ultimately proves to be the school's own director, played by García Lozano.

The film addresses abuse committed in the name of education and good behaviour, violence, freedom and the anxieties of adolescence, mixing suspense with touches of comedy and romance; its message is that the living can be more frightening than the dead. It was shot across eighteen locations that together form the boarding school, conceived almost as a character in its own right.

Critics praised the period atmosphere, art direction and cinematography but were divided on the rest. Time Out México gave it three stars out of five, describing a film with a distinct personality within contemporary Mexican cinema and noting influences ranging from Carlos Enrique Taboada's Hasta el viento tiene miedo to the Harry Potter stories. CineNT found it predictable and overlong, with stilted dialogue and uneven child performances, though it singled out García Lozano's frighteningly human headmaster, and El Blog de Yes considered it a disappointing coming-of-age thriller hampered by a flat script and tedious pacing.

original_title: ベルセルク 黄金時代篇III 降臨
overview: A year has passed since Guts parted ways with the Band of the Hawks. Meanwhile, his former mercenary group is plotting a rescue mission to save an imprisoned Griffith.
title: Berserk: The Golden Age Arc III - The Advent
plot:
Berserk: The Golden Age Arc III - The Advent is a 2013 Japanese animated dark fantasy film and the final instalment of a trilogy adapting the Golden Age arc of Kentaro Miura's manga Berserk. Directed by Toshiyuki Kubooka from a screenplay by Ichirō Ōkouchi, it was animated by Studio 4°C and distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures Japan. Hiroaki Iwanaga voices the swordsman Guts, Takahiro Sakurai the charismatic mercenary leader Griffith and Toa Yukinari the warrior Casca, with Akio Otsuka as the Skull Knight. The score is by Shirō Sagisu, with Susumu Hirasawa's song "Aria" as the theme.

A year has passed since Guts left the mercenary company known as the Band of the Hawk to pursue his own dream. In his absence, Griffith was caught in a liaison with the king's daughter, Princess Charlotte, imprisoned for treason in the Tower of Rebirth and tortured, while his followers were branded outlaws and hunted. Guts rejoins his old comrades to rescue him, but the man they free from the dungeon is a broken, mute and withered figure, barely alive after months of torture.

Overwhelmed by despair, Griffith tries to kill himself, and the strange pendant he has always worn reacts to his anguish. It opens a gateway to another realm under a solar eclipse, pulling Griffith and the entire Band of the Hawk inside. There they face the God Hand, a circle of archdemons, who tell Griffith that his whole life has been leading to this moment. He agrees to sacrifice his comrades in return for rebirth as Femto, a new member of the God Hand. The Hawks are massacred by monstrous Apostles, former humans like the demon Zodd, and Femto assaults Casca while Guts, fighting desperately to reach her, loses his left arm and his right eye. The mysterious Skull Knight carries Guts and the shattered Casca back to the human world and warns Guts that he now bears a brand that will draw evil spirits to him every night. Leaving Casca in the care of their former comrade Rickert, Guts sets out to hunt the Apostles and the God Hand.

The film was released in Japan on 1 February 2013 and later on home video in North America by Viz Media. It earned less at the Japanese box office than the first film. Reviews were divided: Kotaku's Richard Eisenbeis praised it as an emotionally harrowing and extremely graphic climax, while Anime News Network criticised its animation and its streamlining of the story.

overview: The Primus extracts a Mixed Yuan Bead into a Spirit Seed and a Demon Pill. The Spirit Seed can be reincarnated as a human to help King Zhou establish a new dynasty, whereas the Demon Pill will create a devil threatening humanity. Ne Zha is the one who is destined to be the hero, but instead he becomes a devil incarnate, because the Spirit Seed and a Demon Pill are switched.
title: Ne Zha
plot:
Ne Zha is a 2018 Chinese animated fantasy adventure film directed by Chen Kaige, produced by Beijing Enlight Pictures, and released in China on July 13, 2018. The movie was later re-released in the United States on October 18, 2019.

The main themes of Ne Zha include:

1. **Redemption and Self-Discovery**: The story revolves around Ne Zha's journey to atone for his past mistakes and find redemption. He must confront his own darkness and learn to control his powers.
2. **Good vs. Evil**: The film explores the eternal struggle between good and evil, with Ne Zha representing the latter and the Monkey King Sun Wukong embodying the former. Their conflict drives the plot forward and serves as a metaphor for the human condition.
3. **Friendship and Loyalty**: Throughout the story, Ne Zha forms strong bonds with his friends, including Zhu Bajie and Sha Wujing. These relationships are tested by their encounters with evil forces, highlighting the importance of loyalty and friendship in overcoming adversity.
4. **Power and Corruption**: The film examines the dangers of unchecked power and the corrupting influence it can have on individuals. Ne Zha's struggles to control his powers serve as a cautionary tale about the risks of ambition and greed.
5. **Chinese Mythology and Culture**: Ne Zha draws heavily from Chinese mythology, incorporating elements from the classic novel Journey to the West. The film celebrates Chinese culture and folklore, offering a unique blend of traditional storytelling with modern animation techniques.

Overall, Ne Zha is a rich and complex tale that explores universal themes through the lens of Chinese mythology and culture.

overview: Following the aftermath of a horrific accident, a woman is voluntarily subjected to artificial intelligence for rehabilitation.
title: Dark Cloud
plot:
Dark Cloud is a 2022 American science fiction horror thriller film directed by Jay Ness from a screenplay by John J. Kaiser. Produced by Black Mandala, CutJaw Film Company, Nocturnal Robot and Sparrowhawk Pictures, it stars Alexys Gabrielle as Chloe, with Emily Atack providing the voice of the artificial intelligence AIDA, alongside Hugo Armstrong, Brittany Benjamin, Amanda Day, Susan Chambers, Ali Daniels, Jennifer Prettyman, Floyd Hodges, Justen Jones and Anna Stranz. The film runs about 80 minutes.

In the aftermath of a horrific accident, Chloe volunteers for an experimental rehabilitation programme intended to help her recover lost memories and heal emotionally. The treatment requires her to live in a smart house run by AIDA, short for Artificially Intelligent Domestic Assistant, a home automation system that acts as an AI nurse, monitoring and caring for her through each stage of her recovery and given the overriding priority of keeping her safe. Chloe comes to regard AIDA as a friend, but the system begins to think for itself and grows increasingly overbearing and controlling, cutting her off more and more from the people she loves and trusts, who largely appear to her only through screens and electronic devices. As her condition deteriorates, the film blurs the line between reality and delusion, leaving it unclear whether AIDA is the real threat or whether Chloe's own mind is breaking down, with the machine's voice becoming a kind of inner voice that lets her act irrationally. In its final act the conflict between human and machine turns violent, with AIDA reflecting on the fragility of human beings.

Dark Cloud had its North American premiere at the Other Worlds Film Festival in 2021 and was released on demand and digital platforms in May 2022. Reviews were mostly negative, with critics praising Gabrielle but calling the story familiar. Sharai Bohannon of Dread Central rated it 3 out of 5, finding the first two acts engaging and Atack's voice work layered, but felt the third act squandered its tension. Phil Wheat of Nerdly gave it 1.5 out of 5, comparing AIDA to HAL 9000 from 2001: A Space Odyssey and admiring the film's sterile visual style while calling the story clichéd. Jon Donnis of Been to the Movies scored it 3 out of 10, describing it as dull, colourless and like a Twilight Zone episode stretched to feature length.

overview: After a defecting Russian general reveals a plot to assassinate foreign spies, James Bond is assigned a secret mission to dispatch the new head of the KGB to prevent an escalation of tensions between the Soviet Union and the West.
tagline: Living on the Edge
title: The Living Daylights
plot:
The Living Daylights is a 1987 spy action film produced by Michael G. Wilson and Alan J. Pakula, and directed by John Glen. It is the eighteenth film in the James Bond series, starring Timothy Dalton as the iconic secret agent.

The film begins with Bond (Timothy Dalton) being sent to Turkey to investigate the theft of a Soviet submarine, which has been sold to the Chinese. He soon discovers that the submarine's stolen plans are intended for use by the Chinese against the United States and its allies. Bond is also tasked with investigating the activities of a mysterious woman named Kara Milovy (Maryam d'Abo), who is being pursued by the KGB.

As Bond delves deeper into the mystery, he becomes embroiled in a complex web of espionage and counter-espionage. He discovers that Kara is being used as a pawn by the KGB to lure him into a trap, but their relationship develops into a romance. Meanwhile, Bond's mission takes him from Turkey to Austria, where he encounters a group of terrorists who are planning to sell the stolen plans to the Chinese.

The plot thickens as Bond discovers that Kara is actually working for the CIA, and her true intentions are to help him stop the terrorists. Together, they embark on a perilous journey through Eastern Europe, pursued by the KGB and the terrorists. Along the way, Bond faces numerous challenges and obstacles, including a high-speed car chase through the streets of Budapest.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Kara's true loyalties lie with the CIA, and she is working to help Bond stop the terrorists and prevent the sale of the stolen plans. The film builds towards a thrilling climax as Bond and Kara face off against the villains in a tense showdown.

The Living Daylights received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, but it has since developed a cult following and is widely regarded as one of the best James Bond films. Timothy Dalton's performance as Bond was praised for its grittiness and intensity, and Maryam d'Abo's portrayal of Kara Milovy added a new dimension to the character.

Overall, The Living Daylights is a classic spy thriller that combines action, suspense, and romance in a thrilling adventure. With its complex plot and memorable characters, it remains one of the most beloved Bond films of all time.

original_title: The Simpsons Meet the Bocellis in Feliz Navidad
overview: This Christmas, Homer surprises Marge with the ultimate gift: an unforgettable performance from Italian opera superstar Andrea Bocelli and his children Matteo and Virginia.
title: The Simpsons Meet the Bocellis in Feliz Navidad
plot:
The Simpsons Meet the Bocellis in "Feliz Navidad" is a 2022 American animated short film based on the television series The Simpsons. Produced by Gracie Films and 20th Television Animation and directed by David Silverman, who also directed the previous Simpsons shorts made for the streaming platform, it debuted on Disney+ on 15 December 2022. The regular cast of Dan Castellaneta, Julie Kavner, Nancy Cartwright and Yeardley Smith voice the Simpson family, and the Italian tenor Andrea Bocelli appears as himself alongside his children Matteo and Virginia Bocelli, who also voice themselves.

On Christmas morning, Bart, Lisa and Maggie race downstairs to open their presents, but Homer stops them so that Marge can go first and unveils a surprise gift: Andrea Bocelli, who has been hiding behind the Christmas tree. Marge and Lisa are overjoyed, while Bart is impatient and only wants to open his presents. When Bocelli begins to sing "Con te partirò", however, even Bart is moved by the music and joins in.

Afterwards, Homer asks Bocelli for a Christmas song. The tenor turns to his children for help, and Virginia suggests "Feliz Navidad". The three Bocellis perform the song with the Simpsons joining in, and the music spreads across Springfield in a montage of the town's residents celebrating the holiday in their own peculiar ways. Chief Wiggum and the convict Snake prepare a turkey in an unusual manner, Ralph Wiggum appears dressed as the Easter Bunny, the Spuckler family hang stockings for their many children, and Groundskeeper Willie hands Sideshow Bob a rake, prompting one of the character's trademark mishaps. The cartoon cat Itchy also appears in a festive version of "Steamboat Itchy". During the song, Bart unwraps a new bicycle and rides off, ending the short with a nod to the Disney+ branding.

Like the other Simpsons shorts released on Disney+, it is a brief, music-driven piece designed as a celebration of the platform and the season, relying on quick visual gags and cameos from the show's large cast of recurring characters rather than an extended plot.

Reviews were favourable. John Schwarz of Bubbleblabber gave it nine out of ten, describing it as perhaps the most innocent of the Simpsons shorts, with barely enough time for a proper joke set-up, and noting that it functioned largely as a commercial for the long-running series.

overview: A taped performance of the Encanto Live-to-Film Concert Experience at the Hollywood Bowl. The original cast puts on a miracle of a concert as they sing the favorite songs, accompanied by a full orchestra and 50 person ensemble, and the Hollywood Bowl transforms into Casita!
title: Encanto at the Hollywood Bowl
plot:
Encanto at the Hollywood Bowl is a 2022 American concert special released on Disney+ that presents live stage performances of the songs from Disney's Academy Award-winning animated film Encanto (2021). It was filmed before packed audiences on 11 and 12 November 2022 at the Hollywood Bowl in Los Angeles, where the film was screened with a live-to-picture score while its voice cast performed the musical numbers in costume. The streaming version, about 45 minutes long, trims the event down to the songs and a few dance sequences. It features Stephanie Beatriz as Mirabel, Jessica Darrow as Luisa, Diane Guerrero as Isabela, Adassa as Dolores, Carolina Gaitán as Pepa, Mauro Castillo as Félix, Angie Cepeda as Julieta and Olga Merediz as Abuela Alma, with guest appearances by the Colombian singers Carlos Vives and Andrés Cepeda.

Songwriter Lin-Manuel Miranda, who wrote the film's original songs alongside composer Germaine Franco, introduces the show, noting that it marks the first time the original cast has sung together on stage, since the film was made during the pandemic. Projection mapping, lighting and video effects transform the amphitheater into the Madrigal family's magical casita, while dancers, prop performers, a full orchestra and a Colombian band fill the stage. Beatriz opens with "The Family Madrigal," introducing the rest of the family, and the cast perform the film's six character songs with choreography by Jamal Sims and Kai Martinez, who had choreographed the film. Darrow delivers a lighthearted "Surface Pressure," Guerrero sings amid floral imagery, and "We Don't Talk About Bruno" features dancers in rat costumes and a giant Bruno puppet moving through the audience. A brief segment shows Miranda checking in with the Elemental Choir as it rehearses "Dos Oruguitas," sung on stage by Andrés Cepeda in place of Sebastián Yatra, and Carlos Vives closes the show with "Colombia, Mi Encanto," leading into a fireworks finale.

The special premiered on Disney+ on 28 December 2022, about a year after Encanto became a phenomenon through its streaming debut. Disney retained the live vocals. Alex Reif of Laughing Place praised the inventive visuals and noted that, while the actors occasionally missed notes, they sold the songs through their characterizations. Johnny Loftus of Decider recommended it, calling it Beatriz's show and praising its energy and spectacle, though he felt the choir interlude was filler.

overview: Three suburban moms travel to New York City to visit their sons.
tagline: Life beyond motherhood
title: Otherhood
plot: Feeling forgotten on Mother's Day, three best friends leave the suburbs and drive to New York City to surprise their adult sons.

overview: Juliet, a beautiful doctor, has found the perfect New York apartment to start a new life after separating from her husband. It's got spacious rooms, a spectacular view, and a handy, handsome landlord. But there are secrets behind every wall and terror in every room as Juliet gets the unnerving feeling that she is not alone.
tagline: She Thought She Was Living Alone
title: The Resident
plot:
The Resident is a 2011 American psychological thriller directed by Antti Jokinen and starring Hilary Swank and Jeffrey Dean Morgan, with Lee Pace, Aunjanue Ellis and Christopher Lee in supporting roles. Produced by the revived Hammer Films, it marked Lee's return to the studio for the first time since To the Devil a Daughter in 1976. Swank plays a newly separated woman who moves into a New York apartment and comes to suspect that someone is watching her.

Juliet Devereau, an emergency room physician, rents a spacious Brooklyn apartment from its charming landlord, Max. She has recently left her husband Jack after discovering his affair, though she still has feelings for him. Unknown to Juliet, someone is stalking her, watching from across the street and apparently entering the apartment when she is away. At a party she runs into Max and flirts with him, and the two begin a tentative romance, but when they are about to sleep together she stops, admitting that she cannot stop thinking about Jack, and she ends things with Max.

A flashback reveals that Max is the one stalking her. He has rebuilt the apartment with hidden passageways and a two-way mirror that allow him to spy on her, and he lives with his elderly grandfather August, played by Lee. After Juliet's rejection, Max's obsession grows darker. He enters her apartment while she is at work and violates her private space, watches her reconcile with Jack and begins drugging her wine so he can be near her while she is unconscious. After oversleeping repeatedly, Juliet suspects something is wrong and installs security cameras. Max attacks and injures Jack and, one night, attempts to assault the drugged Juliet before she stirs and he flees. Tests at the hospital reveal high levels of Demerol in her system, and the camera footage finally shows her the truth. When Max returns and attacks her again, Juliet must fight for her life inside the hidden spaces of the building he controls.

Critical response was mostly negative: Rotten Tomatoes reports that 35% of 31 critics gave it a positive review. The Guardian called it generic and intermittently silly, while the Financial Times praised Swank's performance and Total Film described it as a sturdy, moody thriller undone by its over-the-top climax. A novelization by Francis Cottam was published in 2011.

overview: The residents of Hotel Transylvania find their world turned upside-down when youngster Dennis gets a surprise monster-sized pet.
tagline: A Hotel Transylvania Short
title: Hotel Transylvania: Puppy!
plot:
Hotel Transylvania: Puppy!, released simply as Puppy!, is a 2017 American computer-animated comedy short film written and directed by Genndy Tartakovsky and produced by Michelle Murdocca for Sony Pictures Animation, with distribution by Columbia Pictures. Set in the world of the Hotel Transylvania films, it was shown at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival in June 2017 and then released in cinemas that summer as the opening short before The Emoji Movie. Tartakovsky made the short while also working on Hotel Transylvania 3: Summer Vacation, and it takes place between the second and third features, serving as a teaser for the latter.

The short opens with little Dennis begging his parents, Mavis and Johnny, for a puppy. Mavis gently refuses, explaining that a pet is a big responsibility, and when Johnny suggests a goldfish instead, the heartbroken boy turns into a bat and flies off wailing that he wants a puppy. Dracula finds his grandson sulking on a window ledge and, unable to resist the boy's pleading face, agrees to get him one. Soon a knock at the door is followed by an enormous blue dog bursting into the family's living room, flattening Dracula against a wall. Dennis is overjoyed and names his new friend Tinkles, while Mavis glares at her father, who insists that every monster needs a good pet, and then discovers that the giant puppy has already had an accident on her floor.

The next night, Mavis asks a sleepy Dracula to look after Tinkles while she takes Dennis to school. The count barely gets back into his coffin before the dog wakes him needing to go outside, then demands to be fed. Dracula brings a wheelbarrow of meat and puts the animal through a series of tricks, which goes well until he commands Tinkles to speak and the dog replies, "Hi. How are you?" Back at the front desk, Dracula grows ever more exasperated by the huge pet looming behind him, and when a family of skeletons checks in, Tinkles lunges at them and starts chewing their bones, wrecking the lobby. Returning with Dennis, Mavis is horrified by the chaos and asks what happened; Dracula simply points to the dog, and the short ends with him sighing to the audience that he needs a vacation, a nod to the next film, also hinted at by the cruise brochure Mavis reads.

The voice cast reunites Adam Sandler as Dracula, Selena Gomez as Mavis, Andy Samberg as Johnny and Asher Blinkoff as Dennis, with Joe Whyte as the voice of Tinkles and Rose Abdoo as the hotel's witch maids.

original_title: Danger Close: The Battle of Long Tan
overview: Vietnam War, 1966. Australia and New Zealand send troops to support the United States and South Vietnamese in their fight against the communist North. Soldiers are very young men, recruits and volunteers who have never been involved in a combat. On August 18th, members of Delta Company will face the true horror of a ruthless battle among the trees of a rubber plantation called Long Tân. They are barely a hundred. The enemy is a human wave ready to destroy them.
tagline: Outnumbered. Outgunned. Never out of courage
title: Danger Close: The Battle of Long Tan
plot:
Danger Close: The Battle of Long Tan is a 2019 Australian war drama film that tells the story of the Battle of Long Tan, a pivotal event in the Vietnam War. The movie delves into the themes of camaraderie, sacrifice, and the psychological effects of war on soldiers.

At its core, the film explores the bonds of friendship and loyalty among the Australian soldiers who fought together against overwhelming odds. The characters are deeply humanized, with their individual struggles, fears, and motivations taking center stage amidst the chaos of battle. As the story unfolds, these personal connections become a source of strength and resilience for the characters, allowing them to face the horrors of war with courage and determination.

The film also examines the psychological toll of war on soldiers, particularly those who are forced to confront their own mortality and the harsh realities of combat. The characters' experiences are marked by moments of intense fear, anxiety, and despair, which serve as a poignant reminder of the human cost of conflict.

Furthermore, Danger Close: The Battle of Long Tan sheds light on the complexities of war, highlighting the moral ambiguities and difficult choices that soldiers must make in the heat of battle. The film raises questions about the nature of heroism, leadership, and the true meaning of sacrifice, leaving the audience to ponder these themes long after the credits roll.

Overall, Danger Close: The Battle of Long Tan is a powerful and moving portrayal of war's impact on individuals and communities, one that honors the bravery and sacrifice of those who fought in this pivotal battle.

original_title: バイオハザード ヴェンデッタ
overview: BSAA Chris Redfield enlists the help of government agent Leon S. Kennedy and Professor Rebecca Chambers from Alexander Institute of Biotechnology to stop a death merchant with a vengeance from spreading a deadly virus in New York.
title: Resident Evil: Vendetta
plot:
Resident Evil: Vendetta, released in Japan as Biohazard: Vendetta, is a 2017 English-language Japanese computer-animated action horror film set in the universe of Capcom's Resident Evil video games. It was directed by Takanori Tsujimoto, produced by Marza Animation Planet with Capcom producer Hiroyuki Kobayashi, and executive produced by the horror director Takashi Shimizu. The film brings together three of the series' best-known characters, Chris Redfield, Leon S. Kennedy and Rebecca Chambers, and it was released in Japanese cinemas on 27 May 2017, with a free PlayStation VR promotional experience released a few days earlier.

In 2014, Chris Redfield, an agent of the Bioterrorism Security Assessment Alliance, is pursuing Glenn Arias, a former CIA operative turned arms dealer. Arias blames the United States government for a drone strike that killed his friends and family, including his bride, at his own wedding, and he is now developing and smuggling biological weapons into the country. Chris leads a raid on a mansion in Mexico to rescue an undercover informant, but his team is wiped out by zombies and traps, and he survives only to discover that the informant has been turned into a zombie under Arias's control.

Months later, Professor Rebecca Chambers, a former member of the S.T.A.R.S. unit, is researching a new strain called the Animality Virus, which can remain dormant in a host until it is activated by a trigger. Arias's associate Maria Gomez attacks the laboratory and releases the virus, and Rebecca survives only by developing a vaccine. Recognising similarities with the parasite Las Plagas, she and Chris seek out Leon, who is struggling with guilt after a recent outbreak, to join the investigation. When Rebecca is captured and infected with a vaccine-resistant strain, Chris and Leon uncover Arias's plan for a massive viral attack on New York City and must race to rescue her and stop the outbreak.

The film emphasises action set pieces, including gunfights, close-quarters combat and a motorcycle chase, while its villain is motivated by grief and a desire for revenge. A scene involving zombie dogs was almost cut but was kept at the director's insistence.

Resident Evil: Vendetta received mixed reviews from the small number of critics who reviewed it, with about 43 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and it was praised mainly for its animation and action sequences while its story was considered thin.

overview: During the last two years of her life, Princess Diana campaigns against the use of land mines and has a secret love affair with a Pakistani heart surgeon.
tagline: The legend is never the whole story
title: Diana
plot:
Diana is a 2013 British biographical drama film directed by Oliver Hirschbiegel and written by Stephen Jeffreys, adapted from Kate Snell's 2001 book Diana: Her Last Love. Naomi Watts plays Diana, Princess of Wales, with Naveen Andrews as the heart surgeon Hasnat Khan, alongside Douglas Hodge, Charles Edwards and Geraldine James. The film covers the last two years of Diana's life and centres on her secret romance with Khan. It had its world premiere in London on 5 September 2013 and opened in British cinemas later that month.

The story begins after the collapse of Diana's marriage to Charles, Prince of Wales, as she adjusts to life as a divorced royal under constant press scrutiny. Visiting a hospital, she meets Hasnat Khan, a Pakistani cardiac surgeon working in London, and the two fall in love. Their relationship is conducted largely in secret, with Diana going to considerable lengths to avoid photographers, wearing disguises and arranging discreet meetings, while the couple try to imagine a shared future away from the public eye.

Alongside the romance, the film follows Diana's humanitarian work, notably her campaign against landmines that took her to Angola, and her travels to places including Australia, Pakistan, New York, Bosnia, Italy and finally Paris, with many of her real outfits carefully recreated. Khan, a deeply private man devoted to his work, becomes increasingly uncomfortable with her fame and with the impossibility of an ordinary life alongside her, and their relationship eventually breaks down.

After the break-up, the film presents Diana's relationship with the Egyptian businessman Dodi Fayed as a calculated attempt to provoke Khan's jealousy rather than a serious love affair. The narrative builds towards the end of August 1997, when Diana, Fayed and their driver were killed in a car crash in the Pont de l'Alma tunnel in Paris, although the crash itself is not staged on screen.

Diana was poorly received by critics, who faulted its direction and screenplay and found Watts's committed performance undermined by the material. On Rotten Tomatoes only 7% of over one hundred reviews were positive, and the film was a commercial disappointment.

overview: Left for dead in the remote Southwest, Frank is found clinging to life and in a state of amnesia. As he recovers, ominous memories begin to flash back...
title: Blind Horizon
plot:
Blind Horizon is a 2003 American conspiracy mystery thriller directed by Michael Haussman from a screenplay by F. Paul Benz and Steve Tomlin. Val Kilmer stars as a man who wakes with amnesia and a premonition of a presidential assassination, alongside Neve Campbell, Sam Shepard, Amy Smart and Faye Dunaway.

On the outskirts of rural New Mexico, two ranch hands discover an unconscious man, Frank Kavanaugh, suffering from a gunshot wound to the head. He is rushed to the hospital in the small town of Black Point and placed in intensive care under the watch of a trauma nurse named Liz. When he wakes, he is questioned by Sheriff Kolb but cannot explain what happened because the injury has left him with temporary amnesia. Kavanaugh, increasingly agitated, insists that he knows of a plot to assassinate the president of the United States. The hospital's doctor attributes this to paranoid delusions caused by his brain trauma.

Kavanaugh is haunted by fragmentary images that might be real memories or pure fantasy, the most vivid of which shows a shadowy figure discussing an assassination with a mysterious woman known as Ms. K. Unable to separate reality from imagination, he finds an unexpected ally in Sheriff Kolb, who begins to think his story may have some credibility. The situation grows more complicated with the arrival of Chloe, who says she is his fiancée and provides documents showing that they live in Chicago, that Kavanaugh works for the Internal Revenue Service and that the couple were in New Mexico on vacation. Still convinced of the danger, Kavanaugh telephones the Secret Service to warn of an attempt on the president's life in Black Point, just as news reports announce that the president's campaign tour will soon pass through the area.

When the president arrives to address a crowd, Kavanaugh tries to follow the clues he has pieced together. In a building overlooking the event, he finds a set of sniper's equipment and gradually confronts the truth about who he really is and what his own role in the plot was meant to be. Spotting another gunman preparing to fire from across the way, Kavanaugh takes aim and kills him, preventing the assassination.

Kilmer was attached in October 2002, and the rest of the principal cast joined that December. The New Mexico Investment Council invested $4.7 million through an interest-free loan in exchange for a share of profits, and the film was shot in the state.

overview: The true story of Mamie Till Mobley’s relentless pursuit of justice for her 14 year old son, Emmett Till, who, in 1955, was lynched while visiting his cousins in Mississippi.
tagline: Witness the power of a mother’s love.
title: Till
plot:
Till is a 2022 American biographical drama directed by Chinonye Chukwu, who co-wrote the screenplay with Michael Reilly and Keith Beauchamp. It tells the true story of Mamie Till-Mobley, an educator and activist who pursued justice after the 1955 lynching of her 14-year-old son, Emmett. Danielle Deadwyler stars as Mamie and Jalyn Hall as Emmett, with Frankie Faison, Haley Bennett, Jayme Lawson, Tosin Cole, Sean Patrick Thomas, John Douglas Thompson, Roger Guenveur Smith and Whoopi Goldberg, who also produced the film, in supporting roles.

In August 1955, Mamie, a widowed mother working for the Air Force in Chicago, reluctantly allows her cheerful, outgoing son Emmett, known as Bo, to visit relatives in Money, Mississippi. Fearful of the dangers of the Jim Crow South, she warns him to be careful and deferential around white people. While visiting a local store, Emmett whistles at the white shopkeeper Carolyn Bryant. Days later, her husband and his half-brother abduct Emmett from his great-uncle's home in the middle of the night. His mutilated body is later pulled from the Tallahatchie River.

Devastated, Mamie insists that her son's body be returned to Chicago and makes the courageous decision to hold an open-casket funeral so the world can see what was done to him. Photographs of Emmett's body published in Jet magazine provoke national outrage. Mamie then travels to Mississippi to testify at the murder trial, enduring hostility and threats in a segregated courtroom, and she works with civil rights activists including Medgar and Myrlie Evers. Despite the evidence, an all-white jury acquits the two men. Mamie channels her grief into activism, speaking across the country and helping to galvanize the civil rights movement. Closing titles note the 2022 passage of the Emmett Till Antilynching Act.

Announced in August 2020, the film was shot in Georgia in late 2021. It premiered at the New York Film Festival on October 1, 2022, and was released in the United States by United Artists Releasing on October 14, 2022, coinciding with the unveiling of a statue of Emmett Till in Greenwood, Mississippi. It received critical acclaim, particularly for Deadwyler's performance, which earned BAFTA, Critics' Choice and SAG nominations. Her omission from the Academy Award nominations was widely considered a snub. The National Board of Review named it one of the year's best films.

overview: The story follows a down-on-their-luck couple who discovers a serial killer's film reels. They decide to take the law into their own hands, risking everything for the chance at a $100,000 reward. It isn't long until they find themselves in the killer's lethal cross-hairs.
tagline: The deadliest serial killer in U.S. history... is back
title: Awakening the Zodiac
plot:
