Awakening the Zodiac is a 2017 Canadian mystery crime thriller directed by Jonathan Wright, a veteran assistant director best known for family comedies and romances made for television, from a screenplay he wrote with Jennifer Archer and Michael Horrigan. Produced by Bunk 11 Pictures and TAJJ Media in association with The Movie Network, it stars Shane West and Leslie Bibb as Mick and Zoe Branson, with Matt Craven as Harvey, Kenneth Welsh as Ben, Nicholas Campbell as Ray and Stephen McHattie as the "Zodiac". Mark Korven wrote the score.

After a prologue in Northern California in 1968, in which a couple parked on a lovers' lane is shot dead, the story jumps to present-day rural Virginia. Mick and Zoe are a down-on-their-luck couple living in a trailer park and struggling to make ends meet. To Zoe's exasperation, Mick spends three months' rent on the unseen contents of an abandoned storage locker, hoping to resell whatever valuables it holds. The gamble seems to be another failure until his partner Harvey, who owns a pawnshop, finds a rusty box of 8mm film cans. When the three watch the reels, they see footage of apparently real violence, including the lovers' lane killings, and suspect the films were made by the Zodiac Killer, the never-identified murderer who taunted police with cryptic letters. Zoe wants to hand the reels to the police, but she is persuaded that if they can prove a link to the case, they could claim a 100,000-dollar reward or sell the films for a fortune. As the couple play amateur detectives and follow the clues, they draw the attention of the killer himself.

Although the story is set in Virginia, the film was shot in Ontario, notably in Almonte, outside Ottawa. Sony Pictures Worldwide Acquisitions and Vertical Entertainment gave it a limited theatrical release in the United States on 9 June 2017. Reviews were mixed to negative, with a 45 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes. The Los Angeles Times found that solid performances grounded the thriller, and other critics liked the chemistry of the leads and the premise. In Variety, Dennis Harvey found the couple's banter initially pleasant but judged the film increasingly silly and short on suspense, with scant action until the final half hour and a cliffhanger ending that made no sense, while crediting its atmospheric photography and production design. Barry Hertz of The Globe and Mail gave it one star out of four.

overview: A sea plane is destroyed in a freak accident, five people find themselves drifting on a raft. At the mercy of the tide and with no hope of rescue, the helpless situation takes a horrifying turn when they are terrorized by a ravenous great white.
tagline: Take your final breath.
title: Great White
plot:
Great White is a 2021 Australian survival horror film directed by Martin Wilson, written by Michael Boughen and produced by Neal Kingston and Michael Robertson. Katrina Bowden and Aaron Jakubenko star as Kaz Fellows and Charlie Brody, a couple who run a seaplane charter business, with Tim Kano, Te Kohe Tuhaka and Kimie Tsukakoshi as their passengers. The story centres on five people stranded at sea and circled by two great white sharks. The film was released theatrically in Spain in May 2021 and in the United States in July 2021, in cinemas and on video on demand.

Kaz, an American nurse who is pregnant with Charlie's child, and Charlie, a former marine biologist, fly their seaplane to the remote and picturesque Hell's Reef with three passengers: the Japanese businessman Joji Minase, his wife Michelle, and Benny, the charter company's cook. On arrival they discover a corpse washed up on the beach, apparently the victim of a shark attack. They report it to the coast guard, but the dead man's phone contains a photograph of his girlfriend, and Charlie and Benny persuade the others to search for the couple's yacht in case she is still alive, despite Joji's objections.

They find the yacht capsized, and when Benny dives to investigate, he discovers the young woman's mutilated remains. As he returns to the surface, a great white shark attacks one of the seaplane's floats, and the plane begins to sink. The five are forced into a small life raft and left drifting with limited supplies. Charlie attempts to navigate with a basic compass and oars, while exhaustion, fear and jealousy cause tensions among the passengers, particularly between Joji and Benny. When one of them falls into the water, the sharks begin to circle the raft, and the group must make desperate decisions as they try to reach land before the predators pick them off one by one.

The film follows the familiar conventions of the shark survival thriller, relying on the vulnerability of its characters in open water and on the isolation of its tropical setting.

Great White received mixed reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds an approval rating of about 43 percent; the consensus says that it is far from the most toothless shark thriller but lacks the storytelling instinct needed to stay afloat. Cath Clarke of The Guardian gave it two stars out of five.

original_title: The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou
overview: Renowned oceanographer Steve Zissou has sworn vengeance upon the rare shark that devoured a member of his crew. In addition to his regular team, he is joined on his boat by Ned, a man who believes Zissou to be his father, and Jane, a journalist pregnant by a married man. They travel the sea, all too often running into pirates and, perhaps more traumatically, various figures from Zissou's past, including his estranged wife, Eleanor.
tagline: The deeper you go, the weirder life gets.
title: The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou
plot:
The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou is a 2004 film directed by Wes Anderson, produced by Scott Rudin Productions, and released by Fox Searchlight Pictures. 

The movie follows the story of Steve Zissou (played by Bill Murray), a washed-up oceanographer who leads an expedition to hunt down the shark that killed his partner, Klaus Daimler (played by Willem Dafoe). Alongside his crew, including his loyal assistant, Kenji (played by Seann William Scott), and his new recruit, Ned Plimpton (played by Jason Schwartzman), Zissou sets out on a quest for revenge and redemption.

The main themes of The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou include:

1. **Obsession and Redemption**: Steve Zissou's relentless pursuit of the shark is driven by his desire to redeem himself after Klaus Daimler's death. This theme explores the complexities of obsession, guilt, and personal growth.
2. **Friendship and Loyalty**: The film highlights the strong bonds between Zissou and his crew members, particularly Kenji and Ned. Their relationships are tested as they face various challenges on their journey.
3. **Identity Crisis**: Steve Zissou's character is a metaphor for the midlife crisis that many people experience. He struggles to come to terms with his fading fame and relevance in the scientific community.
4. **The Search for Meaning**: The movie explores the idea of finding meaning and purpose in life, particularly for those who feel lost or disconnected from their passions.

Throughout the film, Wes Anderson's signature visual style and quirky humor add depth and complexity to these themes, making The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou a thought-provoking and entertaining cinematic experience.

overview: A young botanist relocates to a small desert town to study an invasive plant species. While out on research, she comes to the aid of a downed plane only to find herself taken captive by an inexperienced drug mule who forces her to lead a trek across the sweltering desert to his drop. A local sheriff is drawn into the hunt as his rebellious daughter sets out to find the missing botanist, all the while being pursued by a local drug receiver.
tagline: Fight your way out.
title: Borrego
plot:
Borrego is a 2022 American survival crime thriller written and directed by Jesse Harris in his feature directorial debut. Lucy Hale stars as a young botanist, with Nicholas Gonzalez, Leynar Gomez, Olivia Trujillo and Jorge A. Jimenez. The film was released in theaters and on demand by Saban Films on 14 January 2022 and later arrived on Netflix, where it entered the global top ten in its first week. Harris has said that the story was inspired by his father, who is a botanist.

The botanist moves to a small town in the Anza-Borrego Desert in Southern California to study an invasive plant species that is spreading through the area. While working alone in the desert, she witnesses the crash of an ultralight aircraft being used to smuggle drugs across the border from Mexico. The pilot, an inexperienced and reluctant drug mule, survives the crash and, desperate to complete his delivery, takes Elly hostage and forces her to guide him across the harsh terrain on foot, carrying the drugs on their backs.

As the two struggle through the heat with limited water, they are pursued from several directions. The local sheriff realizes something has happened when the botanist goes missing, and his teenage daughter becomes involved in the search. Meanwhile, the dangerous man waiting to receive the shipment, is determined to recover it at any cost. She must rely on her knowledge of the desert's plants and landscape to survive, while the uneasy relationship between captor and captive develops as both realize they may be victims of the same ruthless operation. The paths of all the characters converge as the story heads toward a violent climax.

The film received mixed reviews from critics, with a 27 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Some reviewers were positive: James Verniere of the Boston Herald gave it a B+ and called it a well-made and gripping crime thriller, and Movie Mensch praised Hale's performance in a timely thriller. Jeffrey Anderson of Common Sense Media gave it three stars out of five, while Jon Mendelsohn of Comic Book Resources called it dull and Sheila O'Malley of RogerEbert.com gave it two stars.

overview: Stoic and heartbroken, Einar Gilkyson quietly lives in the rugged Wyoming ranchlands alongside his only trusted friend, Mitch Bradley. One day, the woman he blames for the death of his only son arrives at his door broke, desperate and with a granddaughter he's never known. But even as buried anger and accusations resurface, the way is opened for unexpected connection, adventure and forgiveness.
production_companies: Kalis Productions GmbH & Co. Zweite KG
tagline: Every secret takes on a life of its own.
title: An Unfinished Life
plot:
An Unfinished Life is a 2005 American drama film directed by Lasse Hallström. The movie revolves around the story of a widowed rancher, Bob Decker, who embarks on a journey to find his estranged son after he's involved in a hit-and-run accident.

The main theme of An Unfinished Life explores the complexities of family dynamics and the consequences of past mistakes. It delves into the emotional turmoil that arises when individuals are forced to confront their unresolved relationships and unfinished business with one another. The film highlights the struggle for forgiveness, redemption, and healing as Bob navigates his complicated past and tries to reconnect with his son.

Through the character of Bob Decker, the movie portrays a man grappling with feelings of guilt, regret, and responsibility, which ultimately lead him on a path of self-discovery and reconciliation. The film's narrative is characterized by its poignant portrayal of human vulnerability, emotional depth, and the resilience of the human spirit in the face of adversity.

The movie also touches upon themes of redemption, forgiveness, and the power of human connection, as Bob forms an unlikely bond with his son and begins to rebuild their relationship. Ultimately, An Unfinished Life presents a powerful exploration of the complexities of family relationships, personal growth, and the transformative nature of love and forgiveness.

overview: A thirty-seven-year-old woman wakes up from a twenty-year coma and returns to the high school where she was once a popular cheerleader to finish her senior year and become prom queen. The main plot is the empowerment of LGBTQ rights and progress through the years.
tagline: High school has changed. But she hasn’t.
title: Senior Year
plot:
Senior Year is a 2022 American comedy film directed by Alex Hardcastle, in his feature debut, from a screenplay by Andrew Knauer, Arthur Pielli and Brandon Scott Jones. Rebel Wilson, who also produced, stars as a woman who wakes from a twenty-year coma and returns to high school, with Angourie Rice playing her teenage self. Mary Holland, Sam Richardson, Zoe Chao, Justin Hartley and Chris Parnell co-star. Netflix released the film on May 13, 2022.

In 1999, after a humiliating birthday party, fourteen-year-old Australian newcomer Stephanie Conway resolves to become one of the popular kids. By 2002 she has remade herself as cheer captain, girlfriend of the popular Blaine, and a frontrunner for prom queen, which she hopes will lead to a charmed life like that of a famous alumna, Deanna Russo. She remains friends with Martha and Seth, who secretly loves her. Her rival Tiffany, Blaine's ex, has her cheer stunt sabotaged at a pep rally, and Stephanie falls into a coma.

She wakes in 2022 at the age of 37. Her father Jim and Martha, now the school principal, help her return to Harding High to finish her senior year, where Seth works as the librarian. Tiffany has married Blaine and moved into Deanna's old mansion, their daughter Bri is a social media star, prom king and queen have been abolished, and cheerleading has become bland and inoffensive. Stephanie wins back popularity online with a racy cheer routine that goes viral, but clashes with Martha, who felt abandoned by her years earlier, while growing closer to Seth.

Tiffany uses Bri's influence to restore the prom crown and plans an exclusive afterparty, so Stephanie throws a rival party at Martha's lake house without asking. At the prom, Bri withdraws so Stephanie wins queen, but Seth is hurt after seeing a drunken Blaine try to kiss her, and Tiffany has the party shut down. Her ride home is driven by an adult Deanna, now divorced and struggling, who warns her not to repeat her mistakes. Stephanie makes peace with Tiffany, publicly apologises, and at graduation finally lands her old cheer move with her friends, kisses Seth and reconciles with Martha.

Critics were largely unimpressed, with a 23% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 47.

overview: Although living a comfortable life in Salon-de-Provence, a charming town in the South of France, Julie has been feeling depressed for a while. To please her, Philippe Abrams, a post office administrator, her husband, tries to obtain a transfer to a seaside town, on the French Riviera, at any cost. The trouble is that he is caught red-handed while trying to scam an inspector. Philippe is immediately banished to the distant unheard of town of Bergues, in the Far North of France...
title: Welcome to the Sticks
plot:
Welcome to the Sticks (French: Bienvenue chez les Ch'tis) is a 2008 French comedy film directed and co-written by Dany Boon, who stars alongside Kad Merad, Zoé Félix and Anne Marivin, with Line Renaud and Michel Galabru in supporting roles. A comedy about the clash between the sunny south of France and the stereotypically grim north, it became a phenomenon at home and is the highest-grossing French film ever released in France.

Philippe Abrams runs the post office in Salon-de-Provence and is desperate to obtain a transfer to a seaside town on the Riviera to please his discontented wife, Julie. Believing that disabled applicants are favoured, he fakes a disability during an inspection, is caught, and is punished with a two-year posting to Bergues, a small town near Dunkirk in the Nord-Pas-de-Calais. Southerners regard the region as a frozen, rainy backwater inhabited by uncouth Ch'tis who speak an incomprehensible dialect, and Philippe heads north full of dread, leaving his wife and young son behind.

His first night is spent at the home of Antoine Bailleul, a postman who also plays the town's carillon and who lives with his domineering mother. Despite a rocky start, the two become close friends, and Philippe is gradually won over by the warmth of his colleagues and neighbours. He joins Antoine on his rounds, accepting drinks at every door, learns to enjoy strong Maroilles cheese and local beer, and even attends an RC Lens football match. Julie, however, refuses to believe that he could be happy there, so he tells her what she expects to hear, describing the north as miserable.

When Julie announces she is coming to support him, Philippe confesses his lies to his friends. Annoyed at first, they agree to help by acting like barbarians and lodging her in a bleak former mining village presented as Bergues. Julie is shaken but resolves to stay, until she discovers the deception. Philippe admits how happy he has been, and she accepts it. Meanwhile, Philippe urges the timid Antoine to stand up to his mother and win back his former girlfriend Annabelle, whom he proposes to from the bell tower. When Philippe is finally transferred south years later, he weeps at leaving, just as a local saying predicted.

Released in February 2008, the film earned around 193 million dollars in France and positive reviews.

overview: Forced to give up his dreams of art school, Zach works dead-end jobs to support his sister and her son. Questioning his life, he paints, surfs and hangs out with his best friend, Gabe. When Gabe's older brother returns home for the summer, Zach suddenly finds himself drawn into a relationship he didn't expect.
tagline: The power of being true to yourself.
title: Shelter
plot:
Shelter is a 2007 American romantic drama written and directed by Jonah Markowitz in his feature directorial debut and produced by JD Disalvatore. Trevor Wright, Brad Rowe and Tina Holmes star. The film became a favorite on the LGBT festival circuit and won Outstanding Film – Limited Release at the 2009 GLAAD Media Awards.

Zach is an aspiring artist living in the working-class port town of San Pedro, California. He has postponed his dream of going to art school to support his family: his disabled father, his older sister Jeanne and her five-year-old son Cody, whom Zach looks after much of the time while Jeanne goes out partying. He works as a short-order cook and spends his free time painting, surfing, seeing his on-and-off girlfriend Tori and hanging out with his best friend Gabe.

When Gabe's older brother Shaun, a published writer, returns home from Los Angeles for a few weeks, he and Zach bond over surfing. Shaun encourages Zach to take control of his life and apply to CalArts. One night after drinking, Shaun kisses Zach. Zach is unsure about his feelings and struggles with whether he might be gay, but after breaking up with Tori he goes to Shaun's house and the two spend the night together. When Jeanne leaves town with her boyfriend Alan for a job interview in Portland, Zach brings Cody along to see Shaun, and their relationship blossoms as Shaun forms a close bond with the boy.

When Gabe and Jeanne find out about the relationship, Gabe is supportive, but Jeanne expresses homophobic views and says she does not want Cody around Shaun. Overwhelmed, Zach ends things with Shaun, insisting that he is not like him, and Shaun calls him a coward for refusing to face his feelings. Shaun secretly submits Zach's portfolio to CalArts, and Zach is accepted, just as Jeanne announces that she intends to move to Oregon permanently with Alan without Cody. Torn between his responsibilities and his own future, Zach must finally decide whether to keep sacrificing his dreams for his family and whether he has the courage to choose the life and the love he truly wants.

Shelter won numerous festival honors, including Best New Director and Favorite Narrative Feature at the Seattle Lesbian & Gay Film Festival, the People's Choice Award at the Vancouver Queer Film Festival, Outfest's award for Outstanding First Dramatic Feature and the Best Actor prize for Wright in Tampa.

original_title: Lego DC Comics Super Heroes: The Flash
overview: Reverse-Flash manipulates the Speed Force to put the Flash into a time loop that forces him to relive the same day over and over again—with progressively disastrous results, including losing his powers and being fired by the Justice League. The Flash must find a way to restore time to its original path and finally apprehend his worst enemy before all is lost for the Flash…and the world!
title: Lego DC Comics Super Heroes: The Flash
plot:
Lego DC Comics Super Heroes: The Flash is an animated superhero film that brings to life the iconic character of Barry Allen, aka The Flash. At its core, this movie explores the theme of identity and self-discovery. As Barry navigates his dual life as a crime scene investigator by day and a superhero by night, he must confront the challenges of balancing his personal and professional responsibilities.

The film also delves into the idea of responsibility and power. The Flash's abilities make him an incredibly powerful hero, but with great power comes great responsibility. As Barry struggles to come to terms with his new role as a superhero, he must learn to wield his powers wisely and use them for the greater good.

Furthermore, Lego DC Comics Super Heroes: The Flash touches on the theme of friendship and camaraderie. Barry's relationships with his friends and allies, particularly Cisco Ramon and Caitlin Kane, are crucial in helping him navigate the complexities of being a superhero. The film showcases the importance of having a support system and working together to overcome adversity.

Lastly, the movie explores the idea of embracing one's true nature. As Barry struggles to reconcile his secret identity with his life as a superhero, he must ultimately come to terms with who he is and what he wants to achieve. This theme is particularly relevant in the context of The Flash's character, who has always been driven by a desire to help others and make a positive impact on the world.

Overall, Lego DC Comics Super Heroes: The Flash is a lighthearted and entertaining film that explores some deeper themes and ideas, making it a fun and engaging watch for both kids and adults.

overview: Guillermo del Toro presents Mama, a supernatural thriller that tells the haunting tale of two little girls who disappeared into the woods the day that their parents were killed. When they are rescued years later and begin a new life, they find that someone or something still wants to come tuck them in at night.
tagline: A Mother's Love is Forever
title: Mama
plot:
Mama is a 2013 American supernatural horror film directed by Andrés Muschietti and written by Neil Cross. The film stars Jessica Chastain, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau, Megan Charpentier, and Joel Edgerton.

The story begins with the disappearance of two young girls, Vera (Megan Charpentier) and her sister Alice (Nikolaj Coster-Waldau), who are taken by their mother, Anne (Jessica Chastain), to a remote cabin in the woods. The family is struggling financially, and Anne hopes that the isolation will help them escape their troubles.

However, things take a dark turn when Anne's husband, Matt (Joel Edgerton), returns home with a mysterious woman named Kanaq (Daniel Brühl). It becomes clear that Kanaq has been manipulating Matt, using his grief over Alice's disappearance to control him. As the days pass, Vera and Alice begin to experience strange and terrifying occurrences in the cabin.

One night, they are taken by Kanaq and left in the woods, where they are forced to fend for themselves. The girls soon discover that they have been abandoned by their mother and father, who seem to be under some sort of mind control. As they try to survive, they begin to uncover the truth about Kanaq's intentions.

Kanaq reveals that he has been using his powers to manipulate Matt and Anne, forcing them to abandon their daughters in order to keep them for himself. The girls soon realize that they must escape from Kanaq if they want to survive.

As the story unfolds, Vera and Alice face numerous challenges as they try to outsmart Kanaq and find a way back home. Along the way, they discover that Kanaq's powers are rooted in an ancient ritual that has been passed down through his family for generations.

In the end, Vera and Alice manage to escape from Kanaq and make their way back to civilization. However, the experience leaves them with emotional scars, and they struggle to come to terms with what happened to them while they were in the woods.

The film ends on a hopeful note, with Vera and Alice reunited with their mother and father, who have finally broken free from Kanaq's mind control. The girls are able to heal and move forward, but the experience has left an indelible mark on their lives.

Overall, Mama is a tense and suspenseful horror film that explores themes of trauma, survival, and the power of love. The film features strong performances from its young cast, particularly Megan Charpentier and Nikolaj Coster-Waldau, who bring depth and nuance to their characters.

overview: A teenage girl deals with her parents forgetting her birthday and a crush on her high school's heartthrob.
tagline: When you're just sixteen anything can happen!
title: Sixteen Candles
plot:
Sixteen Candles is a classic American coming-of-age comedy film released in 1984, directed by John Hughes and produced by Universal Pictures.

The story revolves around Samantha "Sam" Baker (played by Molly Ringwald), a high school sophomore who is struggling to navigate her 16th birthday. Sam's life is marked by embarrassment and humiliation as she tries to fit in with her peers. Her parents are divorced, and her mother has remarried, making Sam feel like an outsider.

On the day of her birthday, Sam wakes up to find that her family has forgotten her special day. She feels unloved and unwanted, especially when her mother gives her a pair of white Keds as a gift instead of something more exciting. As she walks through school, Sam is subjected to ridicule and teasing from her classmates, who seem to be enjoying her misfortune.

However, things take a turn for the better when Sam meets Jake Ryan (played by Michael Schoeffling), a popular and charming student who becomes her crush. Despite their initial awkward encounter, Sam and Jake start to develop feelings for each other, but their social differences make it difficult for them to connect.

Meanwhile, Sam's life is further complicated by her ex-boyfriend Ted (played by Anthony Michael Hall), who still has feelings for her. As the day progresses, Sam must navigate a series of embarrassing and humiliating situations, including a disastrous dance with Ted and a awkward encounter with her mother's new husband.

Despite the ups and downs, Sam ultimately finds herself at the school dance, where she gets to experience the magic of Jake Ryan's presence. The film culminates in a romantic moment between Sam and Jake, as they share a kiss under the mistletoe.

Throughout the movie, John Hughes' signature wit and insight into teenage life shine through, capturing the complexities and nuances of adolescence with humor and sensitivity. The film's portrayal of high school cliques, social hierarchies, and first loves resonated with audiences in the 1980s and continues to be relatable today.

Sixteen Candles is widely regarded as one of the greatest teen movies of all time, and its influence can still be seen in many modern coming-of-age films. The movie's success helped establish John Hughes as a major voice in American cinema, and it remains a beloved classic among fans of 80s cinema.

original_title: Ivy + Bean: The Ghost That Had to Go
overview: Cold, white mist. Clanking pipes. And an eerie voice that's coming from the drain. Is the school bathroom... haunted? Ivy and Bean are on the case!
title: Ivy + Bean: The Ghost That Had to Go
plot:
Ivy + Bean: The Ghost That Had to Go is a 2022 American family comedy film directed by Elissa Down and released by Netflix, the second of three hour-long films adapted from the bestselling Ivy + Bean children's book series. Running 61 minutes, it stars Keslee Blalock as the introverted Ivy and Madison Skye Validum as the extroverted Bean, with Jane Lynch as the stern school principal Mrs. Noble, Lidya Jewitt as Bean's older sister Nancy, Sasha Pieterse as their teacher Ms. Aruba-Tate, Jaycie Dotin as Ivy's mother and Marci T. House as Bean's mother.

Having become best friends in the first film, the two imaginative girls now do their best to stay inseparable at school. Slipping in through a back door to the teachers' restroom, Ivy notices old pipes rattling near the ceiling and wisps drifting from the vents and concludes that the school, supposedly built on top of graves, is haunted, picturing ghosts in a skull-filled underworld cemetery beneath it. Since the girls' fantasies are often shown on screen, it remains doubtful that the ghosts are real, but Ivy, who keeps a dead frog in a bag in the fridge, consults a creepy spell book and plans a potion to send the spirits away. Dressing in a cape and dark makeup, she rounds up classmates to help, while the pair keep landing on the timeout rug and try to avoid Mrs. Noble, a shoe-loving, dragon-like figure whom the students suspect of locking children in a closet. One ingredient of the spell is a lock of Nancy's hair, cut after midnight, which leads to a nighttime raid on her bedroom amid Nancy's own campaign to get her ears pierced. The plan requires sneaking into the school at night, and the climax ends with the girls accidentally flooding the school bathroom. They are duly punished, but before being sent to their rooms they swear a sweet oath of friendship.

The film premiered on Netflix on 2 September 2022. Common Sense Media's Jennifer Green rated it suitable for ages six and up, calling it good, innocent fun that captures childhood energy and ingenuity, praising Lynch's gusto and its messages about friendship and the responsible use of imagination, while noting potentially scary ghost imagery and pee and fart jokes. John Serba of Decider recommended it, judging Lynch's mean principal an improvement on the first film's villain and praising the series for celebrating friendship, imagination and mischief, though he found some classmates dull and the toilet-flooding climax overly noisy.

overview: Two divers are left out at sea without a boat. There’s nothing but water for miles, unless they look at what’s underneath them...
tagline: Scream all you want.
title: Open Water
plot:
Open Water is a 2003 psychological thriller film directed by Chris Kentis, not Plunge Pictures LLC (I couldn't find any information on this production company). The movie was released in 2003, not 2004.

The main themes of Open Water include:

1. **Survival and Human Nature**: The film explores the human condition when faced with extreme circumstances, such as being stranded at sea without rescue. It highlights the psychological effects of isolation, fear, and desperation on a couple.
2. **Marriage and Relationships**: The movie delves into the complexities of marriage and relationships under pressure. As the days pass, the couple's dynamics shift from romantic to primal, revealing their true selves.
3. **Isolation and Loneliness**: Open Water masterfully conveys the feeling of being completely alone in a vast, unforgiving environment. This theme is amplified by the fact that the characters are surrounded by water, emphasizing their vulnerability.
4. **Psychological Breakdown**: As the couple's situation becomes increasingly dire, they begin to experience mental breakdowns, revealing deep-seated fears, anxieties, and insecurities.

The film's tense atmosphere and slow-burning tension keep the audience engaged, making it a gripping and unsettling watch.

overview: An architect's desire to speak with his wife from beyond the grave using EVP (Electronic Voice Phenomenon), becomes an obsession with supernatural repercussions.
production_companies: Canadian Film or Video Production Tax Credit (CPTC)
Province of British Columbia Film Incentive BC
tagline: The line separating the living from the dead has been crossed.
title: White Noise
plot:
White Noise is a 2005 supernatural horror film directed by Geoffrey Sax and starring Michael Keaton as Jonathan Rivers and Deborah Kara Unger as Sarah Tate, with Chandra West as Anna Rivers and Ian McNeice as Raymond Price. Its title refers to electronic voice phenomena, or EVP, in which voice-like sounds found on electronic recordings are interpreted by some people as messages from the dead. Released by Universal Pictures in January 2005, the film proved an unexpected box-office success for a horror film released in the first weekend after New Year's Day.

Jonathan Rivers is an architect married to Anna, a best-selling author who is newly pregnant, and the couple are raising Jonathan's young son from his previous marriage. One evening Anna fails to come home, and she remains missing for weeks. During this time, Jonathan is approached by Raymond Price, a man who lost his son and who claims to receive regular messages from the dead through EVP. Raymond tells Jonathan that he has recorded messages from Anna, implying that she is dead. Jonathan angrily dismisses him, but soon afterwards Anna's body is found; she has drowned, and her death is reported as an accident.

Grief-stricken, Jonathan begins to notice what he believes are attempts by Anna to contact him. He returns to Raymond and meets Sarah Tate, a woman whose fiancé has recently died and who also seeks comfort in Raymond's recordings. When Jonathan captures what he believes is Anna's voice, he becomes obsessed with EVP, filling his home with televisions, radios and recording equipment. But he also begins to hear other voices, angry, threatening and malevolent. After Raymond is found dead in mysterious circumstances, Jonathan and Sarah examine his recordings and discover that some of the messages seem to predict deaths that have not yet happened, leading Jonathan to try to intervene and save lives while dark entities take an interest in him.

The film draws on genuine beliefs about EVP and uses static-filled screens and distorted voices as its central sources of dread, while exploring grief and the desperate desire to communicate with lost loved ones.

White Noise was panned by critics, with only about 7 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, a Metacritic score of 30 and a C grade from CinemaScore audiences. Nevertheless, its commercial success influenced studio strategies for January horror releases, and a sequel, White Noise: The Light, followed in 2007.

original_title: The Map of Tiny Perfect Things
overview: The story of two teenagers trapped in an endless time loop who set out to find all the tiny things that make that one day perfect.
tagline: One day. Infinite possibilities.
title: The Map of Tiny Perfect Things
plot:
The Map of Tiny Perfect Things is a romantic drama film that explores the complexities of love, time, and human connection. At its core, the movie delves into the idea of finding meaning and purpose in life, particularly for those who feel stuck or uncertain about their place in the world.

Through the story of two high school students, Mark (played by Kyle Allen) and Margaret (played by Britton Robinson), the film examines the concept of time and how it affects our relationships. The movie's unique premise, where time loops repeat over and over, serves as a metaphor for the fragility and beauty of human connection.

As the story unfolds, the characters are forced to confront their own desires, fears, and insecurities, leading to a deeper understanding of themselves and each other. The film also touches on themes of identity, community, and the importance of human relationships in shaping our experiences and perspectives.

Ultimately, The Map of Tiny Perfect Things is a poignant exploration of what it means to find love, acceptance, and belonging in a world that can often feel overwhelming and unpredictable.

original_title: LEGO DC Comics Super Heroes: Batman Be-Leaguered
overview: When Batman, claiming to be a loner, refuses to join the Justice League, he is drawn into working with them when they are kidnapped one-by-one and held prisoner by one of Batman's nemeses.
title: LEGO DC Comics Super Heroes: Batman Be-Leaguered
plot:
LEGO DC Comics Super Heroes: Batman Be-Leaguered is an animated film that satirizes the Batman franchise, poking fun at its over-the-top elements and tropes. The movie's main theme revolves around the absurdity of superhero culture, particularly in the context of Batman's obsessive personality.

The story follows Batman as he becomes trapped in a never-ending loop of battles against various villains, with no escape or respite. This repetitive cycle serves as a commentary on the monotony and futility of heroism, highlighting the psychological toll it takes on those who dedicate their lives to protecting others.

Throughout the film, the characters' personalities are amplified for comedic effect, with Batman's rigidity and seriousness being particularly exaggerated. The movie also explores the theme of friendship and camaraderie, as Batman is forced to rely on his allies for support in breaking the cycle.

Ultimately, LEGO DC Comics Super Heroes: Batman Be-Leaguered uses humor and satire to critique the conventions of superhero storytelling, while also celebrating the enduring appeal of these characters. The film's lighthearted tone and playful approach make it an entertaining commentary on the genre, rather than a scathing critique.

overview: Three fairy tale princesses find themselves engaged to the same guy, Prince Charming.
title: Charming
plot:
I couldn't find any information on a movie called "Charming" released in 2018 by Cinesite Animation. The title and release date do not match any known film.

However, I did find that there is a 2018 animated fantasy adventure film called "Charming" directed by Ben Stassen and produced by Cinesite Animation, but it was released in 2017 for the UK market and in 2018 for other countries.

overview: A single mother becomes Ariel Castro's first kidnapping victim, and finds herself trapped in his home with two other women for 11 years.
tagline: Based on a true story.
title: Cleveland Abduction
plot:
Cleveland Abduction is a 2015 television film that tells the story of Amanda Berry, Gina DeJesus, and Michelle Knight, three women who were kidnapped and held captive for years in Cleveland, Ohio. The movie explores the themes of trauma, survival, and the complexities of human relationships.

At its core, the film delves into the psychological effects of captivity on the victims, revealing the ways in which their captors manipulated and controlled them to break their spirits. The movie also examines the ways in which the women found strength and resilience within themselves, often through subtle moments of defiance and resistance.

The film also touches on the theme of the complexities of human relationships, particularly the ways in which people can be both perpetrators and victims of abuse. The character of Ariel Castro, the man who kidnapped and held the women captive, is a prime example of this complexity, as his actions are motivated by a twisted desire for control and companionship.

Furthermore, the movie highlights the importance of community and support in overcoming trauma. The film shows how the women's families and friends rallied around them, providing emotional support and advocating for their release. This theme is particularly significant, as it underscores the idea that healing and recovery are not individual processes, but rather ones that require the involvement and care of others.

Overall, Cleveland Abduction is a powerful and thought-provoking film that sheds light on one of the most shocking and disturbing crimes in American history. Through its portrayal of trauma, survival, and human relationships, the movie provides a nuanced and empathetic exploration of the complexities of the human experience.

overview: World famous movie star Olivia faces a PR disaster when a paparazzi snaps a photo of her with her married lover, Vincent. The hard-working valet Antonio accidentally appears in the same photo and is enlisted to pose as Olivia’s new boyfriend as a cover-up. This ruse with Olivia thrusts Antonio into the spotlight and unexpected chaos.
tagline: Never judge a couple by their cover.
title: The Valet
plot:
The Valet is a 2022 American romantic comedy directed by Richard Wong and written by Bob Fisher and Rob Greenberg, a remake of Francis Veber's 2006 French comedy of the same name. Eugenio Derbez and Samara Weaving star, with Max Greenfield, Betsy Brandt, Marisol Nichols and Carmen Salinas in supporting roles. The film is dedicated to Salinas, who died in 2021, and it was released on Hulu on May 20, 2022.

Antonio Flores is a humble parking valet in Los Angeles who lives with his mother Cecilia. He is separated from his wife Isabel, with whom he shares custody of their teenage son, and his neighborhood faces the threat of gentrification. Meanwhile, the movie star Olivia Allan is having a secret affair with Vincent Royce, a married billionaire real estate developer. One night, as Olivia gets into a car with Vincent beside her, Antonio crashes his bicycle into it, and a paparazzo photographs all three, setting off rumors about the affair.

Fearing that a divorce from his wife Kathryn would cost him his company, Vincent concocts a cover story: Olivia and Antonio will pretend to be a couple. Olivia agrees in order to avoid bad press ahead of the premiere of her new film, a biopic of Amelia Earhart, and Antonio accepts in exchange for money to pay off Isabel's debts. Their first public outings are awkward, with Olivia rude and calculating and Antonio out of place. Everyone believes the ruse except Kathryn, who hires private investigators to follow them.

Antonio's newfound fame makes him a celebrity in the Latino community, and as the fake romance continues, Olivia is welcomed by his warm, close-knit family and discovers the pleasure of anonymity in his neighborhood. Antonio and Olivia gradually become genuine friends, teasing the investigators watching them and sharing their personal disappointments. Olivia grows increasingly doubtful that Vincent will ever leave his wife, while Antonio's time with her rekindles his own family ties, and both must decide what they truly want and whether to stand up to the powerful man pulling the strings.

The film received generally positive reviews. Critics praised the chemistry between Derbez and Weaving, its warm and modern humor, and its treatment of class and the experiences of immigrants in Los Angeles, though some felt that subplots were underdeveloped. The film received Imagen Award nominations for Best Primetime Program – Special or Movie and for Derbez's performance.

overview: A hit man named Kai flies into Bangkok, gets a gun, and orders a cab. He offers a professional female driver big money to be his all-night driver. But when she realizes Kai is committing brutal murders at each stop, it's too late to walk away. Meanwhile, an offbeat police detective races to decode the string of slayings before more blood is spilled.
tagline: Six Hours. Five Hits. Who Will Survive?
title: One Night in Bangkok
plot:
One Night in Bangkok is a 2020 American action thriller film written and directed by Wych Kaosayananda, starring Mark Dacascos as a hitman on a night of revenge, with Vanida Golten, Michael S. New, Kane Kosugi and Sahajak Boonthanakit. Released by Grindstone Entertainment Group, it was issued in the United States directly on DVD and digital download on 25 August 2020 because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

Kai Kahale (Dacascos), a middle-aged Hawaiian former soldier, flies into Bangkok and orders a cab through an app. The driver is Fha (Golten), a young Anglo-Thai woman, and he offers her 6,000 dollars to drive him around the city all night without asking questions. His first stop is a law firm, where he shoots a lawyer in her office; the second is the apartment of a police officer, whom he kills with the words "This is for Lisa." As the bodies are discovered, an offbeat detective begins piecing together the string of killings. Over food at a roadside stall, Kai tells Fha that his daughter, her husband and their little girl died in a crash in Thailand and that he wants to meet everyone involved; shaken, Fha confesses that she too was involved in an accident in which a child died. After shooting a young man at a nightclub for destroying a family with his Porsche, Kai admits that he knows the car in the crash was hers and that he chose her as his driver on purpose, but that he will not kill her, preferring to let her live with her guilt. At a hospital he kills the wealthy gallery owner Davies (Boonthanakit), who had bribed the police to falsify reports and protect his son, along with his wife, bodyguard and son, and is wounded escaping in a doctor's disguise. Fha admits that she lied about the accident out of fear of the boy's father and used the money she received to pay for her sick brother's treatment. Kai offers her his bitcoins should he not return from his final target, a Japanese fixer with underworld ties (Kosugi). After defeating the fixer's men, a weakened Kai loses their hand-to-hand fight, but the detective arrives in time to shoot the fixer, and Kai insists that Fha was his hostage, not his accomplice. As she drives him to hospital, he loses consciousness.

Critics compared the film to Collateral and the John Wick series, and it holds a 33% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Francesco Ceccamea of the Italian magazine Nocturno reviewed it favourably, calling Dacascos's lead role the most incisive of his career.

overview: The story follows a married couple, apart for a night while the husband takes a business trip with a colleague to whom he's attracted. While he's resisting temptation, his wife encounters her past love.
tagline: Temptation can lead anywhere.
title: Last Night
plot:
Last Night is a 2010 Canadian drama film directed by Pat Mills. The movie revolves around the lives of two couples, exploring the complexities and nuances of relationships, intimacy, and human connection.

At its core, Last Night delves into the themes of desire, loneliness, and the search for meaning in a seemingly mundane world. The film masterfully weaves together the interconnected stories of four characters, each struggling with their own unique set of emotions and insecurities.

As the night unfolds, the characters' facades begin to crumble, revealing the raw, vulnerable aspects of their personalities. The movie expertly captures the tension between intimacy and isolation, highlighting the ways in which people often use relationships as a means of coping with their own emotional pain.

Through its thoughtful portrayal of human relationships, Last Night raises important questions about the nature of connection, trust, and vulnerability. The film ultimately presents a poignant exploration of what it means to be alive, to love, and to truly understand one another.

overview: 1920, rural Ireland. Anglo-Irish twins Rachel and Edward share a strange existence in their crumbling family estate. Each night, the property becomes the domain of a sinister presence (The Lodgers) which enforces three rules upon the twins: they must be in bed by midnight; they may not permit an outsider past the threshold; and if one attempts to escape, the life of the other is placed in jeopardy. When troubled war veteran Sean returns to the nearby village, he is immediately drawn to the mysterious Rachel, who in turn begins to break the rules set out by The Lodgers. The consequences pull Rachel into a deadly confrontation with her brother - and with the curse that haunts them.
title: The Lodgers
plot:
The Lodger is a psychological horror film that delves into the dark and complex world of the Black family, who are bound together by their repressed desires and twisted relationships.

At its core, the movie explores the theme of isolation and confinement, as the characters are trapped in their own private hell, with no escape from their suffocating emotions. The film's use of atmospheric tension and claustrophobic settings creates a sense of unease, mirroring the characters' feelings of being trapped in their own lives.

The Lodger also examines the destructive nature of repressed desires and the devastating consequences of keeping secrets buried. The Black family's dark past and their inability to confront their emotions lead to a downward spiral of madness and terror, highlighting the dangers of unresolved trauma and the importance of facing one's demons.

Furthermore, the film touches on the theme of female empowerment and the struggle for independence in a patriarchal society. The main character, Alice, is a strong-willed and determined individual who refuses to be bound by the conventions of her family's twisted world. Her journey towards self-discovery and liberation serves as a powerful counterpoint to the oppressive forces that seek to control her.

Ultimately, The Lodger is a haunting and unsettling film that probes the darkest recesses of the human psyche, revealing the horrors that can unfold when secrets are kept and desires are repressed.

overview: After civilization succumbs to a deadly pandemic and his wife is murdered, a special forces soldier abandons his duty and becomes a hermit in the Nordic wilderness. Years later, a wounded woman appears on his doorstep. She's escaped from a lab and her pursuers believe her blood is the key to a worldwide cure. He's hesitant to get involved, but all doubts are cast aside when he discovers her pursuer is none other than Commander Stone, the man that murdered his wife some years ago.
tagline: They will pay.
title: Last Man Down
plot:
Last Man Down is a 2021 Swedish-British post-apocalyptic action film directed by Fansu Njie from a screenplay by Andreas Vasshaug, based on a story by Njie and its star Daniel Stisen, who also produced it with Njie through Daniel Stisen Productions and Fansu Film. Stisen, a Norwegian actor from Mandal previously seen in small background roles in films such as Edge of Tomorrow, Spectre and Justice League, plays the lead role, with Olga Kent, Daniel Nehme, Stanislav Yanevski, Madeleine Vall and Natassia Malthe in supporting roles. The film was released on digital and on-demand platforms in North America by Saban Films on 19 October 2021, and became available to buy and rent in Norway in February 2022.

The story is set in a dystopian Europe where most of the population has been wiped out by a deadly virus. John Wood (Stisen), a special forces soldier who is immune to the disease, deserts his armed unit after its commander, Stone (Nehme), takes him captive and murders his wife; Stone is convinced that controlling a cure will hand him an empire. Years later Wood lives as a brooding hermit in a cabin in the Nordic wilderness, spending his days chopping wood, until a badly wounded woman, Maria (Kent), stumbles out of the forest one night. She has escaped from a laboratory, and her pursuers believe her blood holds the key to a worldwide cure. Wood reluctantly nurses her back to health and slowly grows used to her company, but armed soldiers soon track them to the cabin and launch a series of deadly attacks. When he learns that the man hunting Maria is Stone, Wood casts aside his doubts and prepares for a final confrontation.

Critics noted the film's deliberate homage to 1980s muscle-bound action films. Birger Vestmo of NRK's Filmpolitiet gave it three out of six, describing it as an old-fashioned actioner of the kind once rented on VHS, plainly modelled on Commando, with the same awkward one-liners but plenty of cheerful violent drive, and judged that Stisen proved capable of far more than his earlier extra work. Lee B. Golden III of Film Combat Syndicate saw potential in Stisen but found much of the fight work more miss than hit, the timeline confusing and the villain's backstory a contrived twist. Emilie Black of Cinema Crazed praised a few well-executed fights but felt the familiar story lost the viewer's interest early and much of the acting was wooden.

overview: An unexpected affair quickly escalates into a heart-stopping reality for two women whose passionate connection changes their lives forever.
tagline: Where desire lives.
title: Below Her Mouth
plot:
Below Her Mouth is a 2017 Canadian romantic drama film directed by Susanna Fuchs and written by Fuchs and Michelle Sheppard. The movie follows the story of two women, Margot (Uma Thurman) and Jen (Eva Green), who engage in a passionate and intense relationship.

The film begins with Margot, a successful businesswoman, attending a party where she meets Jen, a free-spirited artist. Despite their initial reservations about each other, they find themselves drawn to one another's passion and energy. As they spend more time together, they begin to explore the depths of their desires and connect on a physical level.

As Margot and Jen's relationship deepens, they face challenges from both within and outside themselves. Margot struggles with her own identity and sense of purpose, while Jen grapples with her past traumas and fears. Through their interactions, they begin to confront these issues and learn more about themselves and each other.

One of the central themes of the film is the power dynamic between the two women. Margot, who appears to be the more confident and assertive partner, is actually struggling with her own insecurities and desires. Jen, on the other hand, is more open and vulnerable, allowing herself to be swept up in the intensity of their relationship.

As the story unfolds, Margot and Jen's relationship becomes increasingly intense and all-consuming. They engage in a series of passionate and often reckless encounters, pushing each other to explore new depths of desire and intimacy. However, as their connection grows stronger, they also begin to confront the risks and consequences of their actions.

Ultimately, Below Her Mouth is a film about the complexities and challenges of human relationships. Through Margot and Jen's story, the movie explores themes of identity, vulnerability, and the power of human connection. While the film does not shy away from exploring darker aspects of desire and intimacy, it ultimately presents a hopeful and empowering message about the potential for growth and transformation through love and relationships.

Overall, Below Her Mouth is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that explores the complexities of human desire and relationships. With strong performances from its leads and a nuanced script, the movie offers a compelling and often uncomfortable look at the challenges and rewards of loving another person.

overview: In the deep south during the 1930s, three escaped convicts search for hidden treasure while a relentless lawman pursues them. On their journey they come across many comical characters and incredible situations. Based upon Homer's 'Odyssey'.
tagline: They have a plan... but not a clue.
title: O Brother, Where Art Thou?
plot:
O Brother, Where Art Thou? is a 2000 American crime comedy film written, produced, and directed by the Coen brothers. The movie is loosely based on Homer's Odyssey, set in the Deep South during the Great Depression.

The story follows three escaped convicts: Ulysses Everett McGill (played by George Clooney), Pete Hogwallop (played by John Turturro), and Delmar O'Donnell (played by Tim Blake Nelson). The trio is on the run from the law, searching for a hidden treasure that they believe will lead them to freedom.

The movie begins with the three convicts escaping from prison in Mississippi. They are pursued by the ruthless Sheriff Bill Skaggs (played by John Goodman), who is determined to capture them and bring them back to justice. Along the way, they encounter various characters, including a blind man named Big Dan Teague (played by Danny Glover) who becomes their ally.

As they journey through the rural South, the three convicts face numerous challenges, including run-ins with the law, wild animals, and treacherous terrain. They also sing and dance to bluegrass music, which becomes a recurring theme throughout the film.

Throughout their journey, Ulysses, Pete, and Delmar encounter various women, including Penny (played by Holly Hunter), who becomes Ulysses' love interest. However, their quest for treasure is constantly thwarted by Sheriff Skaggs and his deputies.

As the story unfolds, the three convicts begin to realize that they are not as different from each other as they initially thought. They develop a sense of camaraderie and loyalty, which ultimately helps them overcome their differences and work together to achieve their goal.

The movie's climax features an epic musical number, "I'll Fly Away," in which the three convicts sing and dance with Big Dan Teague and his family. The song is a celebration of freedom and redemption, and it marks a turning point in the story as Ulysses, Pete, and Delmar finally find what they have been searching for.

In the end, Ulysses and Penny escape from Sheriff Skaggs' clutches, while Pete and Delmar are captured. However, in a surprising twist, Pete is revealed to be the long-lost son of Big Dan Teague, and he is welcomed into his family as a member. The movie ends with Ulysses and Penny riding off into the sunset, free at last.

Overall, O Brother, Where Art Thou? is a quirky and entertaining film that combines elements of comedy, drama, and music to create a unique and memorable cinematic experience.

overview: In 1630, a farmer relocates his family to a remote plot of land on the edge of a forest where strange, unsettling things happen. With suspicion and paranoia mounting, each family member's faith, loyalty and love are tested in shocking ways.
tagline: Evil takes many forms.
title: The Witch
plot:
The Witch is a 2015 American supernatural horror film written and directed by Robert Eggers. The film takes place in 17th-century New England, specifically in the Puritan community of Salem Village.

**Beginning:**
The story begins with the Puritan family, William (Ralph Ineson) and Katherine (Kate Dickie), who have just moved to the outskirts of their village due to a dispute over land ownership. The family consists of five children: Thomasin (Anya Taylor-Joy), Caleb (Harvey Scrimshaw), Mercy (Ellie Grainger), Jonas (Lucas Dawson), and Samuel (Angus Wall). The family is struggling to adapt to their new life, and tensions are high.

**Plot Development:**
As the family tries to establish a new home, they begin to experience strange occurrences. Tools go missing, animals die, and strange noises are heard in the night. The family attributes these events to the devil's influence, as they believe that Satan is responsible for their misfortunes. William, who has been away from his family for some time, returns with a new wife, Katherine, who is pregnant.

As the story progresses, the family becomes increasingly paranoid and isolated. They begin to suspect each other of witchcraft, leading to a series of tense confrontations. Thomasin, the eldest daughter, becomes particularly concerned about her family's well-being and begins to investigate the strange occurrences on her own.

**Ending:**
The film builds towards a tragic conclusion as the family's paranoia reaches a boiling point. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Caleb has been possessed by a malevolent spirit, which he had conjured through his own dark magic. The family, in their desperation to rid themselves of the evil presence, turns on each other.

In the end, Thomasin is forced to confront her own fears and doubts as she tries to save her family from themselves. The film ends with a haunting image of Caleb's corpse, which has been left out in the woods, a symbol of the devastating consequences of their actions.

**Themes:**
The Witch explores themes of fear, paranoia, and the dangers of unchecked superstition. The film is also notable for its historical accuracy, drawing heavily from Puritan folklore and mythology. Eggers' use of natural lighting and atmospheric tension creates a sense of unease and foreboding, which adds to the overall sense of dread.

Overall, The Witch is a slow-burning, atmospheric horror film that builds towards a shocking and devastating conclusion. Its exploration of themes such as fear, paranoia, and superstition makes it a thought-provoking and unsettling viewing experience.

overview: In the aftermath of a personal tragedy, Harper retreats alone to the beautiful English countryside, hoping to find a place to heal. But someone — or something — from the surrounding woods appears to be stalking her, and what begins as simmering dread becomes a fully-formed nightmare, inhabited by her darkest memories and fears.
tagline: What haunts you will find you.
title: Men
plot:
Men is a 2022 psychological thriller film directed by Alex Garland, written by Garland and Seth Owen, and produced by DNA Films.

The movie follows the story of Jack (played by Jessie Buckley), a young woman who embarks on a road trip to visit her estranged father in rural England. As she drives through the countryside, she encounters a series of unsettling and surreal events that challenge her perceptions of reality.

Upon arriving at her father's farm, Jack discovers that he has been murdered, and his body is found in a field. The police investigation that follows reveals that several other men have also gone missing in the area, all with similar circumstances.

As Jack delves deeper into the mystery, she becomes increasingly unhinged, questioning her own sanity and the nature of reality. She begins to experience strange visions and hallucinations, which blur the lines between what is real and what is not.

Throughout the film, Garland explores themes of trauma, grief, and the fragility of the human psyche. The movie's use of long takes, atmospheric sound design, and a haunting score creates a sense of unease and tension that propels the viewer through the narrative.

One of the most striking aspects of Men is its exploration of the concept of "the Other," which refers to the idea that there are forces beyond human understanding that can shape our experiences. The film's use of symbolism, particularly in relation to the rural landscape and the character of Jack's father, adds depth and complexity to the narrative.

Ultimately, Men is a thought-provoking and unsettling film that challenges its audience to confront the darker aspects of human nature. With its slow-burning tension and haunting atmosphere, it is a must-see for fans of psychological thrillers and those who appreciate a good mystery.

original_title: Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker
overview: The surviving Resistance faces the First Order once again as the journey of Rey, Finn and Poe Dameron continues. With the power and knowledge of generations behind them, the final battle begins.
tagline: Every generation has a legend
title: Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker
plot:
Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker is a 2019 science fiction film directed by J.J. Abrams, written by Abrams and Chris Terrio, and produced by Lucasfilm Ltd.

The film takes place nine years after the events of The Last Jedi (2017) and follows the story of Rey (Daisy Ridley), Finn (John Boyega), Poe Dameron (Oscar Isaac), and Kylo Ren (Adam Driver). The Resistance, led by General Leia Organa (Carrie Fisher in a previously recorded performance), is on the run from the First Order, which has taken over the galaxy.

The film begins with Rey discovering that she is strong in the Force, but also struggling to understand her connection to it. She sets out on a journey to find Luke Skywalker (Mark Hamill), who has gone into exile after the events of The Last Jedi. Along the way, she encounters Ben Solo, Kylo Ren's father, who was thought to be dead.

As Rey searches for Luke, she is pursued by Kylo Ren and his allies, including Supreme Leader Snoke's (Andy Serkis) clone, Emperor Palpatine (Ian McDiarmid). The film's plot thickens as it becomes clear that Palpatine has returned from the dead and is seeking to reclaim his power over the galaxy.

Meanwhile, Finn and Poe are on a mission to disable the First Order's ability to track the Resistance. They team up with Rose Tico (Kelly Marie Tran), who has discovered a way to disable the tracking device using a code from an ancient Sith temple.

As the story unfolds, Rey discovers that she is the granddaughter of Emperor Palpatine and that she has the potential to become a powerful Force user. However, she also struggles with her connection to the dark side, which is represented by Kylo Ren.

The film's climax features an epic battle between the Resistance and the First Order on the planet Exegol, where Rey confronts Palpatine and Kylo Ren. In a surprising twist, it is revealed that Emperor Palpatine had been manipulating events from behind the scenes to bring about his own return to power.

In the end, Rey uses her connection to the Force to defeat Palpatine and destroy him once and for all. However, in doing so, she also sacrifices herself, as she becomes one with the Force. The film ends on a hopeful note, with Finn, Poe, and Rose mourning the loss of their friend, but also celebrating their victory over the First Order.

Throughout the film, there are many nods to classic Star Wars characters and storylines, including a memorable appearance by Emperor Palpatine's iconic theme music. The film's climax features an epic lightsaber duel between Rey and Kylo Ren, which is reminiscent of the iconic duels between Luke Skywalker and Darth Vader in the original trilogy.

Overall, Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker is a satisfying conclusion to the sequel trilogy, bringing together many of the storylines and characters from the previous two films. While it has its flaws, the film's epic scope, memorable characters, and nostalgic value make it a must-see for fans of the franchise.

overview: In this belated sequel to 'The Decline of the American Empire', 50-something Montreal college professor, Remy, learns that he is dying of liver cancer. He decides to make amends meet to his friends and family before he dies. He first tries to made peace with his ex-wife Louise, who asks their estranged son Sebastian, a successful businessman living in London, to come home. Sebastian makes the impossible happen, using his contacts and disrupting the entire Canadian system in every way possible to help his father fight his terminal illness to the bitter end, while he also tries to reunite his former friends, Pierre, Alain, Dominique, Diane, and Claude to see their old friend before he passes on.
tagline: A provocative new comedy about sex, friendship, and all other things that invade our lives.
title: The Barbarian Invasions
plot:
The Barbarian Invasions is a poignant and introspective drama that explores the complexities of human relationships, love, loss, and the passage of time. At its core, the film delves into the intricate web of emotions that bind family members together, particularly between parents and children.

As the story unfolds, we witness the tender yet tumultuous relationship between Maurice (played by Stéphane Brutus), a widowed father struggling to cope with his wife's passing, and his adult daughter, Léa (played by Marie-Josée Croze). The film masterfully captures the bittersweet nostalgia that permeates their interactions, as they navigate the delicate balance between preserving cherished memories and confronting the harsh realities of life.

Through Maurice's character, the film also explores the theme of grief and its various forms. His journey is marked by a deep sense of longing, as he grapples with the loss of his partner and the impermanence of human connections. The Barbarian Invasions poignantly conveys that even in the midst of sorrow, there is beauty to be found in the memories we hold dear.

Furthermore, the film touches on the theme of intergenerational relationships, highlighting the ways in which our experiences shape us and inform our understanding of the world around us. As Maurice navigates his complex emotions, he comes to realize that his relationship with Léa is not only a reflection of their shared past but also a source of comfort and strength in the present.

Ultimately, The Barbarian Invasions is a moving exploration of love, loss, and the human condition, one that invites viewers to reflect on the complexities of family relationships and the enduring power of memories to shape our lives.

overview: Abandoned after coming out, Shun befriends Mio just before he has to move. Years later, Mio returns with a confession. How will Shun feel?
title: The Stranger by the Shore
plot:
The Stranger by the Shore (Japanese: Umibe no Étranger) is a 2020 Japanese animated romantic drama directed by Akiyo Ohashi and animated by Studio Hibari, adapted from L'étranger de la Plage, the debut boys' love manga by Kanna Kii, published in English as Seaside Stranger. Fuji TV produced the film as part of its Blue Lynx label for boys' love anime. Kii, a former animator, supervised the production and designed the characters and Mina Kubota composed the music. Taishi Murata voices Shun Hashimoto and Yoshitsugu Matsuoka voices Mio Chibana, reprising their roles from an earlier drama CD, with Yū Shimamura as Sakurako and Kanae Itō and Sayaka Nakaya as the couple Eri and Suzu.

Shun is a gay novelist who has settled on a small island in Okinawa after being cut off by his family in Hokkaido when they learned of his sexuality. There he meets Mio, a high school student who has lost his mother and lives with relatives. When Shun reaches out to him, the boy's prickly reaction stirs painful memories of Shun's estrangement from his parents, yet the two gradually become close. Before anything can develop, Mio reveals that he must move away to the city, promising to keep in touch.

Three years later Mio, now an adult, suddenly returns to the island and declares that he is in love with Shun. Shun is attracted to him but holds back, wracked with guilt at the idea of depriving the younger man of a so-called normal life and doubting that Mio understands what being gay will mean. Complications arrive with Sakurako, Shun's childhood friend and former fiancée, whose arranged wedding ended when Shun came out to his parents during the ceremony and who still loves him. She comes to the island to persuade him to return to Hokkaido because his father is in poor health. Shun is determined to stay with Mio, but Mio urges him to go home and make peace with his family. Realizing that Mio's feelings are sincere and his advice is right, Shun decides to return to Hokkaido and asks Mio to go with him.

The film opened in Japanese cinemas on 11 September 2020, and Funimation began streaming it in North America and other territories in July 2021. Reviews were mixed to positive. Anime News Network gave it a B-minus, feeling that it needed more time to develop its characters, especially Mio, but offered tantalizing glimpses of a satisfying love story, while The Japan Times rated it 2.5 out of 5, arguing that the adaptation lost some of the strength of the excellent manga.

overview: After total humiliation at her thirteenth birthday party, Jenna Rink wants to just hide until she's thirty. With a little magic, her wish is granted, but it turns out that being thirty isn't as always as awesome as she thought it would be!
tagline: For some, 13 feels like it was just yesterday. For Jenna, it was.
title: 13 Going on 30
plot:
"13 Going on 30" is a romantic comedy film released in 2004 by Columbia Pictures. The movie follows the story of Jenna Rink, played by Jennifer Garner, who wakes up one morning to find herself transformed back into her 13-year-old self.

The film begins with Jenna, now a successful businesswoman living in New York City, feeling unfulfilled and disconnected from her childhood. On her 13th birthday, she makes a wish that she could be "30, flirty, and thriving" like the popular girl she used to admire. However, when she wakes up the next morning, she finds herself back in her body as a 13-year-old girl.

As Jenna navigates her way through high school again, she meets a new group of friends and catches the eye of Matt Flamhaff, played by Mark Ruffalo, who is now a successful architect. Despite their instant attraction, Jenna struggles to adjust to her new life and reconcile her past and present selves.

Throughout the film, Jenna's transformation serves as a metaphor for self-discovery and growth. As she navigates high school again, she learns valuable lessons about friendship, love, and identity. Meanwhile, Matt becomes a source of support and encouragement for Jenna, helping her to confront her insecurities and find her true self.

As the story unfolds, Jenna's past and present selves begin to intersect in unexpected ways. She must confront the choices she made as a teenager that led her to where she is today, and learn to appreciate the person she has become. The film culminates with Jenna making a new wish, this time for herself rather than someone else, and waking up to find herself transformed back into her 30-year-old self.

The ending of the film is bittersweet, as Jenna must come to terms with leaving behind her childhood and embracing adulthood. However, she also finds that she has gained a newfound appreciation for life and a deeper understanding of herself. The movie ends on a hopeful note, suggesting that it's never too late to make changes and find happiness.

Overall, "13 Going on 30" is a heartwarming and humorous film that explores themes of identity, self-discovery, and the complexities of growing up. With its witty dialogue, relatable characters, and engaging storyline, it has become a beloved classic among romantic comedy fans.

overview: The story of a super-secret spy organization that recruits an unrefined but promising street kid into the agency's ultra-competitive training program just as a global threat emerges from a twisted tech genius.
tagline: Manners maketh man.
title: Kingsman: The Secret Service
plot:
Kingsman: The Secret Service is a 2014 spy comedy film directed by Matthew Vaughn, produced by 20th Century Fox, and based on the comic book series "The Secret Service" by Mark Millar and Dave Gibbons. The movie follows the story of Eggsy Unwin (Taron Egerton), an orphan who dreams of becoming a spy.

The film begins with Colin Salmon's character, Harry Hart (also known as Galahad), a seasoned Kingsman agent, visiting a prison to recruit a new member for the organization. He meets Gary 'Eggsy' Unwin (Taron Egerton), a street-smart and charismatic young man who has grown up on the streets of London. Eggsy is recruited by Harry, who recognizes his potential as a spy.

Harry takes Eggsy under his wing and begins to train him in the ways of espionage. Eggsy quickly proves himself to be a skilled fighter and strategist, but he also struggles with the moral implications of his new role. Meanwhile, a wealthy tech mogul named Richmond Valentine (Samuel L. Jackson) announces that he will destroy humanity unless 100 million people are killed within 24 hours.

Harry is tasked with stopping Valentine, who has created a deadly virus that can kill anyone in under an hour. Eggsy joins Harry on a mission to infiltrate Valentine's organization and gather intelligence on his plans. Along the way, they encounter a beautiful and alluring woman named Ginger Ale (Hannah Al-pachachi), who becomes Eggsy's love interest.

As the story unfolds, Eggsy and Harry face numerous challenges and obstacles as they try to stop Valentine. They must use their skills and cunning to evade Valentine's henchmen and prevent the destruction of humanity. The film features a range of action-packed sequences, including a memorable fight scene at a high-stakes poker game.

In the end, Eggsy and Harry successfully infiltrate Valentine's organization and gather enough information to stop him. However, not before Valentine reveals that he has already set off the virus, which is spreading rapidly around the world. The film ends with Eggsy and Harry escaping from Valentine's lair, but not before Eggsy is left shaken by the events of the mission.

Throughout the film, Vaughn pays homage to classic spy movies, including James Bond films and the works of Ian Fleming. The movie features a range of witty one-liners and humorous moments, which add to its lighthearted tone. However, it also explores themes of loyalty, duty, and the moral implications of espionage.

Overall, Kingsman: The Secret Service is a fun and action-packed spy comedy that pays tribute to the genre while also offering something new and original. With its talented cast, clever script, and stylish visuals, it has become a modern classic in the world of spy movies.

overview: South Korea, 1993. An agent of the National Intelligence Service is sent to Beijing to infiltrate a group of North Korean officials with the ultimate goal of obtaining information about their nuclear program.
tagline: In the lasting days of the Cold War.
title: The Spy Gone North
plot:
The Spy Gone North (Korean: Gongjak) is a 2018 South Korean spy drama directed by Yoon Jong-bin. Hwang Jung-min stars as a South Korean agent who infiltrates the North Korean elite, with Lee Sung-min, Cho Jin-woong and Ju Ji-hoon in the main supporting roles. The film is loosely based on the true story of Park Chae-seo, a former agent known by the code name "Black Venus". It premiered at Cannes and was released in South Korean theaters on August 8, 2018.

In January 1992, Major Park Seok-young is recruited by the Agency for National Security Planning, South Korea's intelligence service, to uncover the truth about North Korea's nuclear weapons program, the extent of which is known only to the regime's inner circle and its leader Kim Jong-il. On the orders of Director Choi, played by Cho Jin-woong, Park takes on a carefully constructed cover as a disgraced former officer turned debt-ridden, hard-drinking businessman. His assignment is to get close to Ri Myung-woon, played by Lee Sung-min, the head of North Korea's External Economic Committee.

Operating out of Beijing, Park presents himself as an entrepreneur eager to do business with the North, and he gradually earns Ri's attention. The agency engineers a situation that leaves Ri in need of money, opening the door for Park, though Ri remains wary and demands proof of good faith. A suspicious officer of the North's State Security Department, Jung Moo-taek, played by Ju Ji-hoon, keeps a close eye on the newcomer. Park eventually proposes a joint venture to film South Korean television commercials in the North, a plan that brings him all the way to Pyongyang and into a rare audience with Kim Jong-il himself.

As he climbs higher, Park discovers that political figures in Seoul are secretly negotiating with North Korean officials to manipulate tensions ahead of the 1997 South Korean presidential election, betraying the very mission he has risked his life for. Caught between two governments, Park and Ri, who has come to see the cost of the regime's policies on his own people, form an unlikely bond of mutual respect that transcends the border dividing them.

The film was a major box office success in South Korea, drawing nearly five million admissions and grossing more than US$38 million.
