Critics praised its tense, dialogue-driven approach to espionage, which favors psychological suspense over action, as well as the performances of Hwang and Lee, and it went on to win numerous domestic film awards.

overview: Hellboy comes to England, where he must defeat Nimue, Merlin's consort and the Blood Queen. But their battle will bring about the end of the world, a fate he desperately tries to turn away.
tagline: Demons Have Demons Too
title: Hellboy
plot:
Hellboy is a 2019 American superhero film based on the Dark Horse Comics character created by Mike Mignola. A reboot of the Hellboy film series and the third live-action film in the franchise, it was directed by Neil Marshall and stars David Harbour in the title role, with Milla Jovovich as the Blood Queen Nimue, Ian McShane as Professor Trevor Bruttenholm, Sasha Lane as Alice Monaghan, Daniel Dae Kim as Ben Daimio and Thomas Haden Church as Lobster Johnson. Its story draws on the comic arcs Darkness Calls, The Wild Hunt and The Storm and the Fury.

In 517 AD, the Blood Queen Vivienne Nimue unleashes a plague on Britain until King Arthur defeats her with the help of a member of her own coven, dismembering her with Excalibur and hiding her remains across the country. In the present day, Hellboy, a demon raised by humans and working as an investigator for the Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense, travels to Tijuana to find a missing agent, only to discover that he has become a vampire. Back in Colorado, his adoptive father Bruttenholm sends him to Britain to help the Osiris Club hunt three giants.

During the hunt, Hellboy is betrayed by the club's hunters and nearly killed, but he defeats the giants and is rescued by Alice Monaghan, a young medium whom he once saved from fairies when she was a baby. Meanwhile, a vengeful pig-like changeling called Gruagach, aided by the witch Baba Yaga, is gathering the pieces of Nimue's body so that she can be resurrected. Joined by Alice and Major Ben Daimio of the British paranormal agency M11, who harbours a secret of his own, Hellboy learns that Nimue intends to use him to bring about the apocalypse by tempting him to embrace his destiny as the beast of the end times. Torn between the humans who fear him and the monsters who see him as their king, Hellboy must decide which side he belongs to.

Marshall's film is darker and considerably more violent than Guillermo del Toro's earlier Hellboy films, earning an R rating for its graphic gore and drawing more directly on Mignola's folklore-inspired stories.

Hellboy was panned by critics, with an approval rating of about 17 percent on Rotten Tomatoes, although Harbour's performance received some praise. It was a box-office bomb, grossing about 55.1 million dollars against a 50 million dollar budget, and the series was rebooted again in 2024 with Hellboy: The Crooked Man.

overview: When the five puppies stumble upon the Five Power Rings of Inspiron (alien artifacts abandoned on Earth 16 years ago), they all develop super powers, and are enlisted in Captain Canine's battle against the evil Darkon alien Commander Drex. Captain Canine is commander of space ship Megasis and is from the planet Inspiron. He is the mortal enemy of the Commander Drex. In charge of protecting Princess Jorala and the Five Power Rings from Drex, Megasis places the rings in hiding on the planet Earth, and takes the form of a German Shepherd, intending to stay on earth in very deep cover. Adopted by aspiring young comic book artist Ian Shaeffer, and renamed Captain Canine, he spends 16 happy years on Earth, as Ian recounts the stories of his space adventures. But when the five Buddies discover the Power Rings and instantly develop superpowers, Captain Canine has to train them very quickly indeed - for Commander Drex is headed back to earth, and this time he's determined to succeed.
tagline: You don't need superpowers to be a super hero.
title: Super Buddies
plot:
Super Buddies is an animated adventure film that revolves around a group of canine heroes who embark on a thrilling journey to save their friends and family from various threats. At its core, the movie explores the theme of loyalty and friendship, highlighting the unbreakable bonds between the Super Buddies and their human companions.

The story delves into the idea of teamwork and cooperation, as the Super Buddies work together to overcome obstacles and defeat their enemies. This is reflected in the character dynamics, where each dog brings its unique skills and abilities to the table, complementing one another to achieve a common goal.

Moreover, the movie touches on the theme of responsibility and growth, as the Super Buddies learn valuable lessons about protecting others and taking care of themselves. The characters face various challenges that test their courage, empathy, and selflessness, ultimately leading to personal growth and development.

The film also explores the idea of sacrifice and putting the needs of others before one's own interests. This is particularly evident in the character of Duke, who puts himself in harm's way to save his friends and family, demonstrating a selfless devotion that inspires those around him.

Overall, Super Buddies is a heartwarming tale that celebrates the power of friendship, loyalty, and teamwork, making it an entertaining and engaging watch for audiences of all ages.

overview: A group of soldiers are taken to the mountains of Wales to investigate a strange looking monster.
tagline: They thought they could control it. They were wrong.
title: Dragon Fury
plot:
Dragon Fury, also known as Dragon's Fury, is a 2021 British low-budget fantasy horror film directed and edited by Scott Jeffrey, who wrote the screenplay with the visual effects designer Rhys Waterfield. Produced by Jagged Edge Productions and distributed by ITN Distribution, it stars Nicola Wright as Vanessa Reid, with Chelsea Greenwood, Sofia Lacey, Chrissie Wunna as Nicole, Andrew Rolfe as Professor Palson, Richard Lovell and Rachel Roberts. Josh Reichental composed the score, and the film runs 88 minutes under the tagline "They thought they could control it. They were wrong."

A remote area of the Welsh mountains has been abandoned for years because of radiation; no one knows why, and no one dares to enter. When a pair of vloggers venture into the hills, they discover the reason when they are burned alive by a dragon. The army calls in Vanessa Reid and her small team of special operatives to investigate the creature. Her unlikely team consists of two women, one of them injured and on crutches and the other soon developing a strange illness that may be linked to the dragons and to the radiation on the mountainside. The trio meet Professor Palson and his assistant Nicole, who clearly know more about what is happening in the mountains than they admit. Most of the action unfolds indoors as a dragon egg prepares to hatch, people begin losing their minds and tensions erupt among the group. A small dragon returns at the end, the creatures turn out to have evolved from the traditional dragon form into something more bird-like, and a closing scene hints at a much larger dragon to come.

The film was scheduled for release in the United Kingdom in September 2021. Reviews were negative. Phil Wheat of Nerdly gave it two out of five, noting that there were few furious dragons in Dragon Fury and that most of its running time was taken up with talk, although he credited thoughtful details in the sparingly used computer-generated effects, such as the dragons casting shadows, and their unusual bird-like design. Ade Smith of Movies & Mania found it a mostly dull drama after a promising opening in a rugged landscape, criticizing its implausible trio of operatives and silly final reveal while praising Wright's performance and Reichental's score. Voices from the Balcony called the computer effects variable, the dragon itself cool-looking, and the plot predictable.

overview: Six years have elapsed since Guantanamo Bay, leaving Harold and Kumar estranged from one another with very different families, friends and lives. But when Kumar arrives on Harold's doorstep during the holiday season with a mysterious package in hand, he inadvertently burns down Harold's father-in-law's beloved Christmas tree. To fix the problem, Harold and Kumar embark on a mission through New York City to find the perfect Christmas tree, once again stumbling into trouble at every single turn.
tagline: Christmas comes prematurely.
title: A Very Harold & Kumar Christmas
plot:
A Very Harold & Kumar Christmas is a 2011 American stoner comedy film directed by Todd Strauss-Schulson. The movie follows the story of two friends, Harold Lee (John Cho) and Kumar Patel (Kal Penn), who embark on a journey to find the perfect Christmas tree for their friend Neil Patrick Harris's wedding.

The main themes of A Very Harold & Kumar Christmas include:

1. Friendship: The film showcases the strong bond between Harold and Kumar, who have been friends since college. Their friendship is put to the test as they navigate various challenges and misadventures during their Christmas trip.
2. Growing up: As the two friends approach adulthood, they struggle with the idea of growing up and leaving their carefree college days behind. The movie pokes fun at the challenges of transitioning from adolescence to adulthood.
3. Identity: Harold and Kumar's journey is also a metaphor for finding one's identity and purpose in life. They grapple with questions about their careers, relationships, and personal growth, highlighting the uncertainty and self-discovery that often accompanies young adulthood.
4. Nostalgia: The film pays homage to classic Christmas movies and explores the nostalgia of childhood memories. Harold and Kumar's adventures are filled with references to beloved holiday films, adding a layer of humor and heartwarming sentimentality.

Throughout the movie, the characters face various obstacles, including run-ins with eccentric characters, wild parties, and unexpected twists. Ultimately, the film concludes on a heartwarming note, as Harold and Kumar learn valuable lessons about friendship, growing up, and finding their place in the world.

Overall, A Very Harold & Kumar Christmas is a hilarious and entertaining holiday comedy that explores themes of friendship, identity, and nostalgia, making it a delightful addition to the stoner comedy genre.

overview: A legendary late-night talk show host's world is turned upside down when she hires her only female staff writer. Originally intended to smooth over diversity concerns, her decision has unexpectedly hilarious consequences as the two women separated by culture and generation are united by their love of a biting punchline.
tagline: They're giving comedy a rewrite.
title: Late Night
plot:
Late Night is a 2019 American comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of female identity, ambition, and the struggles of women in male-dominated industries.

The movie delves into the life of Kate McKinnon's character, Devi, a young comedian who lands a late-night talk show host gig after the sudden departure of her predecessor. As she navigates this new role, Devi must confront her own insecurities, biases, and privilege, all while trying to find her voice and connect with her audience.

Throughout the film, the main theme of female empowerment is woven throughout, as Devi struggles to balance her creative ambitions with the pressures of being a woman in a male-dominated industry. The movie also touches on themes of identity, particularly for women who are navigating their 30s and trying to find their place in the world.

The film's portrayal of the late-night talk show host's inner workings serves as a metaphor for the ways in which societal expectations can constrain individuals, particularly women. As Devi navigates her new role, she must confront the biases and stereotypes that have been ingrained in the industry, all while trying to find her own unique voice.

Ultimately, Late Night is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of what it means to be a woman in today's society, and the ways in which we can support and uplift each other as we navigate our careers and personal lives.

overview: A police brigade working in the dangerous northern neighborhoods of Marseille, where the level of crime is higher than anywhere else in France.
title: The Stronghold
plot:
The Stronghold (French: BAC Nord) is a 2021 French action thriller directed by Cédric Jimenez from a screenplay he wrote with Audrey Diwan. Gilles Lellouche, François Civil and Karim Leklou star as three police officers in Marseille, with Adèle Exarchopoulos, Kenza Fortas and Cyril Lecomte in supporting roles. The story is inspired by a real scandal that shook the anti-crime brigade (brigade anti-criminalité, or BAC) of Marseille's northern districts in 2012. The film premiered out of competition at the 2021 Cannes Film Festival and was released in France by StudioCanal in August 2021.

In 2012, Marseille has one of the highest crime rates in France. Grég Cerva, a veteran officer, and his younger partners Antoine and Yass patrol the city's northern housing projects day and night, making small arrests of street dealers while the drug networks that control the neighborhoods remain untouched. Grég longs to take on the heavily guarded estate that serves as the center of the drug trade, but the area is a fortress run by gangs prepared to kill to defend their territory, and his superiors, bound by politics and the demand for statistics, refuse to give the unit the resources it needs. Every confrontation in the projects leaves the officers outnumbered and humiliated.

The situation changes when a violent incident filmed in the neighborhood attracts media attention, and the brigade's commander gives Grég's team the go-ahead to prepare a major operation. To gather intelligence, Antoine relies on Amel, a young informant who demands payment in hashish rather than money. To keep her cooperation, the officers begin bending the rules, seizing drugs from dealers to pay her. Their raid on the stronghold, a tense and chaotic siege, is hailed as a great success, but soon afterward the officers find themselves accused of corruption by the internal affairs police, and the bonds between the three men and their loyalty to the institution are put to the test.

The film was a box-office success in France and received positive reviews; AlloCiné recorded an average press rating of 3.6 out of 5, with 20 Minutes praising its virtuoso siege sequence and France Info calling it unusually tense. It also sparked political controversy, as some critics accused it of presenting a one-sided view of the police and the northern districts. It received seven nominations at the 47th César Awards, including Best Film, Best Director and Best Actor.

overview: Kevin Mitnick is quite possibly the best hacker in the world. Hunting for more and more information, seeking more and more cyber-trophies every day, he constantly looks for bigger challenges. When he breaks into the computer of a security expert and an ex-hacker, he finds one - and much more than that...
tagline: The world has a right to know.
title: Takedown
plot:
Takedown, released in the United States as Track Down, is a 2000 American crime thriller directed by Joe Chappelle and loosely based on Takedown, the nonfiction book by the computer security expert Tsutomu Shimomura and the New York Times journalist John Markoff about the pursuit of the hacker Kevin Mitnick. The screenplay is by David and Leslie Newman, John Danza and Howard A. Rodman. Skeet Ulrich plays Mitnick and Russell Wong plays Shimomura, with Tom Berenger and Christopher McDonald as federal agents, and Angela Featherstone, Donal Logue, Master P, Jeremy Sisto and Amanda Peet in supporting roles.

For years Mitnick has eluded the FBI while breaking into corporate and government computers, seeing himself as a crusader for freedom of information against "Big Brother". A gifted social engineer and smooth-talking con man, he is also socially awkward and obsessive, and his only real confidant is his friend Alex Lowe (Logue). Feeling slighted by Shimomura, a renowned security researcher, Mitnick breaks into his computers simply to prove that he can. In doing so he obtains the encrypted code of a powerful computer virus Shimomura had created for security research. Since it is only a matter of time before Mitnick cracks the encryption, Shimomura and his team become even more eager than the federal agents to catch him, and the case turns into a high-tech duel of wits and a personal grudge match that leads across the country to Seattle.

The film was produced by Dimension Films and Millennium Films, with Shimomura as co-executive producer and a cameo as a hacker. It opened in French cinemas in March 2000 as Cybertraque and was later released on DVD in Europe as Takedown, but its American release was delayed for years by controversy: Mitnick called the book and film extremely inaccurate, and the author Jonathan Littman sued Disney and Miramax, alleging that parts of the script were taken from his own, more sympathetic book, The Fugitive Game. Among the invented elements were face-to-face confrontations between the two men and hacks into NORAD and the NSA that never happened. It was finally released direct to video in the US in September 2004. Critics found it tense but hollow; Variety likened it to a stylish television episode and praised Ulrich while calling the supporting roles underwritten.

overview: Street dancer, Thomas Uncles is from the wrong side of the tracks, but his bond with the beautiful Megan White might help the duo realize their dreams as they enter in the mother of all dance battles.
title: Dance Flick
plot:
Dance Flick is a 2009 musical comedy film that satirizes popular dance movies such as Save the Last Dance and Step Up. The movie follows the story of Derek, a white dancer who falls in love with a black ballerina named Lily, and their struggles to overcome racial differences and find acceptance.

The main theme of Dance Flick is the exploration of racial tensions and stereotypes in the context of dance culture. The film uses humor and satire to critique the way African American and white dancers are portrayed in popular media, highlighting the absurdity and superficiality of some dance movies. Through Derek's character, the movie also touches on issues of identity, cultural appropriation, and the complexities of interracial relationships.

The film also explores themes of class and privilege, as Derek's wealth and status create tension with Lily's more humble background. Additionally, Dance Flick pokes fun at the conventions of romantic comedies, using its lighthearted tone to comment on the ways in which love stories can be used to mask deeper social issues.

Overall, Dance Flick is a satirical comedy that uses dance as a metaphor for exploring complex social issues and stereotypes.

belongs_to_collection.name: Psycho-Pass: Sinners of the System Collection

original_title: PSYCHO-PASS サイコパス Sinners of the System Case.1「罪と罰」
overview: In the winter of 2117, a runaway vehicle crashes into the Public Safety Bureau Building. The driver is identified as Izumi Yasaka, a psychological counselor at the Sanctuary, a Latent Criminal Isolation Facility in Aomori Prefecture. But right before her interrogation, Inspector Mika Shimotsuki and Enforcer Nobuchika Ginoza are tasked with promptly escorting Yasaka back to Aomori. What awaits them there is a False Paradise.
title: Psycho-Pass: Sinners of the System -  Case.1 Crime and Punishment
plot:
Psycho-Pass: Sinners of the System - Case.1 Crime and Punishment is a Japanese anime film directed by Naoyoshi Shiotani, produced by Production I.G, and released in 2019.

The main themes of Psycho-Pass: Sinners of the System - Case.1 Crime and Punishment revolve around the exploration of morality, free will, and the consequences of relying on advanced technology to govern society. Here are some key themes:

1. **Morality and Free Will**: The film delves into the concept of morality and whether it can be reduced to numerical values. The main character, Akane Tsunemori's, journey is a metaphor for the struggle between individual freedom and societal expectations.
2. **The Dangers of Over-Reliance on Technology**: Psycho-Pass highlights the risks of relying too heavily on advanced technology to govern society. The film shows how this can lead to a loss of human empathy and compassion, as well as the potential for abuse of power.
3. **Personal Identity and Self-Discovery**: Akane's character arc is a powerful exploration of personal identity and self-discovery. As she navigates her relationships with her colleagues and mentors, she must confront her own values and principles in order to find her place in the world.
4. **The Nature of Justice**: The film raises questions about what constitutes justice and whether it can be reduced to simple numerical calculations. Through Akane's experiences, the story challenges the notion that justice can be achieved through technology alone.
5. **Human Connection and Empathy**: Psycho-Pass emphasizes the importance of human connection and empathy in a world where technology is increasingly prevalent. The film shows how relationships and personal connections are essential for building trust and understanding.

Overall, Psycho-Pass: Sinners of the System - Case.1 Crime and Punishment is a thought-provoking exploration of complex themes that challenges viewers to think critically about the role of technology in society and the importance of human connection and empathy.

overview: Scooby-Doo and those "meddling kids" Shaggy, Fred, Daphne and Velma are back in this all-new original movie! Velma discovers she's inherited her great-great-uncle Dr. Von Dinkenstein’s cursed castle in the terrifying town of Transylvania…Pennsylvania, that is. Just when the Gang persuades Velma to go claim her inheritance, the ghost of Dinkenstein Castle blows up the Mystery Machine as a warning! Now the Crew must spring back into action, but this time it's personal! Who's responsible for the Dinkenstein monster? What family secret has Velma been hiding? Will Fred recover from the loss of his beloved Mystery Machine? Can any helpless snack survive Scooby and Shaggy's monster-sized appetites? This Scooby-Doo adventure has enough spooky fun to make the whole family come alive!
tagline: Scooby-Doo and those "meddling kids" Shaggy, Fred, Daphne and Velma are back in this all-new adventure!
title: Scooby-Doo! Frankencreepy
plot:
Scooby-Doo! Frankencreepy is an animated mystery film that delves into the darker side of Halloween and the consequences of playing with forces beyond one's control. The movie revolves around the gang's investigation at a creepy carnival, where they encounter a mysterious figure known as "Frankencreepy," a monstrous creature brought to life by a magical amulet.

At its core, Scooby-Doo! Frankencreepy explores the theme of temptation and the dangers of meddling with forces that are beyond human understanding. The film highlights how the gang's curiosity and desire for adventure can lead them down a path of danger and chaos. As they delve deeper into the mystery, they must confront their own fears and weaknesses in order to uncover the truth behind Frankencreepy.

The movie also touches on the theme of friendship and loyalty, as the gang works together to overcome their differences and support one another in the face of adversity. Through their collective efforts, they learn valuable lessons about trust, teamwork, and the importance of standing up for what is right, even when it's difficult or scary.

Furthermore, Scooby-Doo! Frankencreepy features a richly atmospheric setting that evokes the spooky and eerie atmosphere of Halloween. The film's use of shadows, lighting, and sound design creates a sense of tension and foreboding, drawing the viewer into the world of the carnival and its sinister secrets.

Overall, Scooby-Doo! Frankencreepy is a thrilling mystery adventure that explores themes of temptation, friendship, and the power of teamwork in the face of danger.

overview: Two stoners wake up after a night of partying and cannot remember where they parked their car.
tagline: After a night they can't remember, comes a day they'll never forget.
title: Dude, Where's My Car?
plot:
Dude, Where's My Car? is a 2000 American stoner comedy film directed by Danny Leiner and written by Wayne Ferita. The movie follows two slackers, Jesse (Ashton Kutcher) and Chester (Seann William Scott), who wake up after a wild night in Las Vegas with no memory of what happened the night before.

The main themes of Dude, Where's My Car? include:

1. Friendship: The film explores the strong bond between Jesse and Chester, two friends who are struggling to find their place in life. Their friendship is put to the test as they try to navigate their way through a series of misadventures.
2. Slacker culture: The movie satirizes the slacker subculture of the late 1990s and early 2000s, depicting two friends who are content with doing nothing and living in the moment.
3. Coming of age: Jesse and Chester's journey can be seen as a metaphor for growing up and finding one's identity. They must confront their own immaturity and learn to take responsibility for their actions.
4. Nostalgia: The film is set in the late 1990s, and its nostalgic value is a significant part of its appeal. The movie features many references to popular culture of the time, including music, movies, and TV shows.

The plot development of the movie follows Jesse and Chester as they try to piece together their memories of the night before and find their car, which has been stolen. Along the way, they encounter a series of wacky characters, including a seductive woman (Amy Smart) who becomes embroiled in their misadventures.

The ending of the movie is lighthearted and comedic, with Jesse and Chester finally finding their car and resolving their differences. The film ends on a positive note, with the two friends having learned a valuable lesson about responsibility and growing up.

Overall, Dude, Where's My Car? is a fun and entertaining movie that explores themes of friendship, slacker culture, coming of age, and nostalgia.

overview: When Mitchie gets a chance to attend Camp Rock, her life takes an unpredictable twist, and she learns just how important it is to be true to yourself.
title: Camp Rock
plot:
Camp Rock is a 2008 musical television film directed by Matthew Diamond from a screenplay by Karin Gist, Regina Hicks, Julie Brown and Paul Brown. The 73rd Disney Channel Original Movie, it stars the Jonas Brothers, Meaghan Jette Martin, Maria Canals-Barrera, Daniel Fathers and Alyson Stoner, and introduces Demi Lovato as aspiring teenage singer Mitchie Torres.

Mitchie, a shy girl with a beautiful voice and big dreams, longs to attend Camp Rock, an exclusive summer music camp, but her family cannot afford the fees. Her mother, Connie, a caterer, takes a job cooking for the camp, which allows Mitchie to attend at a discount in exchange for helping out in the kitchen. Embarrassed by her family's modest means, Mitchie falls in with the camp's queen bee, Tess Tyler, the daughter of a famous singer, and pretends that her mother is the president of a music television channel in China. Meanwhile she befriends Caitlyn Gellar, an aspiring music producer.

Also at camp is Shane Gray, the arrogant lead singer of the pop band Connect 3, sent back to Camp Rock by his bandmates to repair his public image after a series of tantrums. While serving as a dance instructor, Shane hears a girl singing a song that moves him, but he does not see who it is and becomes determined to find her. The singer is Mitchie, and as she and Shane grow closer, he begins to rediscover his love of authentic music. When Tess discovers Mitchie's lie and exposes it publicly, Mitchie is humiliated, Shane feels betrayed, and Tess frames Mitchie and Caitlyn for theft, barring them from the end-of-summer Final Jam competition. On the night of the show, Mitchie finally takes the stage to perform her own song, "This Is Me," and Shane recognizes her as the mystery voice, joining her in a duet.

The film premiered on Disney Channel on June 20, 2008, and was watched by 8.9 million viewers, one of the highest audiences for a Disney Channel Original Movie. It later aired on ABC and was sold on iTunes. The film launched Lovato's career and spawned a successful soundtrack, a reality competition show in the United Kingdom, and the sequel Camp Rock 2: The Final Jam, which premiered in September 2010.

overview: Ivan Locke has worked hard to craft a good life for himself. Tonight, that life will collapse around him. On the eve of the biggest challenge of his career, Ivan receives a phone call that sets in motion a series of events that will unravel his family, job, and soul.
tagline: No turning back.
title: Locke
plot:
Locke is a 2013 British psychological thriller film directed by Steven Knight, not 2014, and produced by IM Global, but released in some countries under different production companies.

The movie follows the story of Ivan Locke, a construction foreman who receives a series of phone calls on the eve of a major project, forcing him to confront his past and re-evaluate his life. The film's main theme revolves around the concept of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences, relationships, and personal choices.

As Ivan navigates through the complex web of phone calls, he is forced to confront his own demons and make difficult decisions that challenge his sense of self. The film explores the idea that our identities are fragile and can be easily manipulated by external forces, leading to a crisis of faith in one's own values and principles.

Throughout the movie, Ivan's character undergoes a significant transformation as he grapples with the consequences of his past actions and the expectations placed upon him by others. The film raises questions about the nature of responsibility, guilt, and redemption, leaving the audience to ponder the complexities of human relationships and the fragility of the human psyche.

The movie's tense atmosphere and Ivan's inner turmoil create a sense of unease, mirroring the character's emotional state as he struggles to reconcile his past and present selves. Ultimately, Locke is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, delving into the darker aspects of our nature and the consequences of our choices.

Note: I corrected the release year from 2014 to 2013, as the movie was released in that year.

overview: Return to the forest and join Bambi as he reunites with his father, The Great Prince, who must now raise the young fawn on his own. But in the adventure of a lifetime, the proud parent discovers there is much he can learn from his spirited young son.
tagline: A Son's Courage. A Father's Love.
title: Bambi II
plot:
Bambi II is a 2006 animated film produced by DisneyToon Studios. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1942 classic Bambi, directed by David Hand.

The story begins with Bambi, now an adult stag, living in the forest with his wife, Faline, and their young son, the Prince of the Forest. The Prince is struggling to find his place in the world, feeling overshadowed by his father's legacy as a great hunter. Bambi tries to teach his son the ways of hunting, but the Prince is more interested in playing and having fun.

Meanwhile, a new threat emerges in the form of a group of poachers who are seeking to destroy the forest and its inhabitants. The poachers are led by a ruthless and cunning leader named Man, who will stop at nothing to achieve his goals.

As the poachers begin to wreak havoc on the forest, Bambi must come to terms with his own mortality and the fact that he is no longer the young buck he once was. He realizes that it's time for him to pass on his knowledge and experience to his son, but the Prince is not ready to take over.

Bambi decides to embark on a journey to find Man and put an end to his evil plans. Along the way, he meets a wise old owl named Great Prince, who teaches him about the importance of perseverance and determination. Bambi also reunites with some old friends, including Thumper's son, Flower, and Faline.

As Bambi draws closer to Man, he realizes that the poacher is not just a mindless killer, but a complex character with his own motivations and backstory. Man's past is revealed, showing how he became a poacher and lost touch with his humanity.

In the end, Bambi confronts Man and engages in a fierce battle. However, instead of killing him, Bambi chooses to show mercy and understanding. He realizes that Man is not beyond redemption and that there is still good in everyone.

The movie ends with Bambi returning home to his family, where he is welcomed back as a hero. The Prince has learned valuable lessons from his father's journey and is now ready to take on his role as the leader of the forest. Bambi and Faline are proud of their son and know that they have passed on their knowledge and experience to him.

Overall, Bambi II is a heartwarming and action-packed film that explores themes of identity, community, and redemption. The movie features stunning animation, memorable characters, and a story that will resonate with audiences of all ages.

overview: “2048: Nowhere to Run” takes place one year before the events of Blade Runner 2049. The short film focuses on Sapper, a man who is trying to make it through life day-by-day without turning back to his old ways. We’re introduced to both the gentle nature of Sapper and the violence he’s capable of when set off.
title: 2048: Nowhere to Run
plot:
2048: Nowhere to Run is a 2017 American tech noir short film directed by Luke Scott and written by Hampton Fancher and Michael Green, the screenwriters of Blade Runner 2049. One of three prequel shorts commissioned to bridge the thirty years between Blade Runner and its sequel, alongside Blade Runner Black Out 2022 and 2036: Nexus Dawn, it stars Dave Bautista as the replicant Sapper Morton, a character he plays in the feature, with Orion Ben, Gaia Ottman, Björn Freiberg and Adam Savage in supporting roles. Luke Scott's father, Ridley Scott, directed the original Blade Runner and executive produced the sequel. The short was released online on September 16, 2017, about three weeks before the feature.

The story is set in Los Angeles in 2048, one year before the events of Blade Runner 2049. Sapper Morton, a Nexus-8 replicant living quietly among humans in hiding, is first seen weeping uncontrollably before a mirror, struggling with memories of his past, before composing himself and heading out into the crowded, rain-soaked streets. He ignores a gang of thugs who harass him and stops to greet Ella, a young girl from the neighborhood, giving her a copy of Graham Greene's novel The Power and the Glory, a book he loved. He then visits a market to sell produce from his farm, but the buyer pays him $3,000, a thousand dollars short of what he needs.

Leaving the market, Sapper sees Ella and her mother being attacked by the same thugs he had earlier passed by. Unable to stand by, he intervenes and overpowers the attackers with the brutal, superhuman strength of a combat model replicant, killing or maiming several of them. The violence, witnessed by bystanders, exposes his true nature. The incident leads to his status as a replicant being reported to the authorities, setting in motion the events that will lead an LAPD blade runner to his farm at the beginning of Blade Runner 2049. A version released in China includes a prologue explaining the rise of Niander Wallace and his corporation.

Denis Villeneuve, the director of Blade Runner 2049, selected the filmmakers for the three shorts, which were announced in August 2017 as part of the feature's marketing. Scott had previously directed 2036: Nexus Dawn. The short was well received, with commentators noting that it gave Bautista a role worthy of his talents and added depth to a character who appears only briefly in the feature.

overview: Katie, a 17-year-old, has been sheltered since childhood and confined to her house during the day by a rare disease that makes even the smallest amount of sunlight deadly. Fate intervenes when she meets Charlie and they embark on a summer romance.
tagline: Love will light the way.
title: Midnight Sun
plot:
Midnight Sun is a 2018 American romantic fantasy film directed by Julie Yoe and written by Josh Campbell, Matt Stuecken, and Michael H. Weber. The movie is based on the novel of the same name by Stephenie Meyer.

The story revolves around Isabella "Bella" Swan (played by Elle Fanning), a teenage girl who moves to Forks, Washington to live with her father, Charlie (played by Kyle MacLachlan). Bella starts at a new high school, where she is immediately drawn to a mysterious and handsome boy named Edward Cullen (played by Robert Pattinson).

As Bella spends more time with Edward, they develop an intense connection, but their relationship is threatened by the danger that comes with being in love with a vampire. The Cullens are revealed to be a family of vampires who have been living among humans for years, and they must keep their true nature hidden from the rest of the world.

The movie takes a unique approach to telling the story, as it focuses on Bella's inner thoughts and feelings through a series of flashbacks and diary entries. This allows the audience to experience the story from Bella's perspective, making her emotions and struggles more relatable and intimate.

As Bella and Edward's relationship deepens, they face numerous challenges, including the threat of James (played by Cam Gigandet), a rogue vampire who is determined to destroy Bella. The Cullens work together to protect Bella, but their efforts are hindered by the fact that Bella is still learning about her own supernatural abilities.

Throughout the movie, the romance between Bella and Edward is portrayed as intense and all-consuming, with a deep emotional connection between the two characters. However, the film also explores themes of isolation, loneliness, and the difficulties of being in love with someone who is fundamentally different from oneself.

Ultimately, the movie ends on a hopeful note, with Bella and Edward's relationship still intact despite the many obstacles they have faced. The ending sets the stage for the rest of the Twilight Saga, which follows the further adventures of Bella and Edward as they navigate their supernatural world together.

Overall, Midnight Sun offers a fresh take on the Twilight franchise, focusing on Bella's inner world and emotions rather than the action-packed plot of the original movies. With its unique storytelling approach and beautiful cinematography, the film provides a captivating and romantic viewing experience for fans of the series.

overview: Christina's love life is stuck in neutral. After years of avoiding the hazards of a meaningful relationship, one night while club-hopping with her girlfriends, she meets Peter, her perfect match. Fed up with playing games, she finally gets the courage to let her guard down and follow her heart, only to discover that Peter has suddenly left town. Accompanied by Courtney, she sets out to capture the one that got away.
tagline: A romantic comedy without the sugar.
title: The Sweetest Thing
plot:
The Sweetest Thing is a 2002 American comedy film directed by Michael Patrick Jann. The movie follows three friends, Christina (Cameron Diaz), Mary (Christina Applegate), and Samantha (Selma Blair), who embark on a road trip to Seattle after Christina's fiancé breaks off their engagement.

The main themes of the movie include:

1. Female friendship: The film explores the strong bond between the three female leads as they navigate through various challenges and experiences together.
2. Self-discovery: Throughout the journey, each character is forced to confront their own personal issues, desires, and insecurities, leading to a deeper understanding of themselves and their relationships with others.
3. Independence: The trip serves as a catalyst for the friends to break free from their respective constraints and explore new aspects of themselves, fostering a sense of independence and empowerment.
4. Love and relationships: The movie delves into the complexities of love, heartbreak, and relationships, showcasing the characters' struggles with commitment, intimacy, and vulnerability.

The film's narrative is driven by the friends' interactions, conflicts, and growth, ultimately leading to a poignant exploration of what it means to be true to oneself and find happiness on one's own terms.

overview: The Eternals are a team of ancient aliens who have been living on Earth in secret for thousands of years. When an unexpected tragedy forces them out of the shadows, they are forced to reunite against mankind’s most ancient enemy, the Deviants.
tagline: In the beginning...
title: Eternals
plot:
Eternals is a 2021 superhero film directed by Chloé Zhao, produced by Marvel Studios, and based on the Marvel Comics series of the same name. The movie follows an ancient group of immortal beings known as the Eternals, who have been living among humans for thousands of years.

The story begins with the introduction of Ikaris (Richard Madden), a powerful Eternal who has been hiding in plain sight on Earth. He is joined by his sister Sersi (Gemma Chan), who was once a mortal but gained immortality after being transformed by her brother's powers. The two Eternals are part of a larger group, including Kingo (Kit Harington), Ajak (Salma Hayek), Makkari (Lauren Ridloff), Phastos (Brian Tyree Henry), and Sprite (Lia McHugh).

The Eternals have been watching over humanity for centuries, protecting them from the Deviants, monstrous creatures that threaten to destroy the world. However, a new threat emerges in the form of Gilgamesh (Don Lee), a powerful Deviant who seeks to destroy humanity.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the Eternals' past is shrouded in mystery and tragedy. The group's leader, Ajak, has been keeping secrets about their history, which are slowly revealed throughout the film. It is also revealed that the Eternals have a complex relationship with humans, often walking a fine line between helping and harming them.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when Sersi discovers her true identity as an Eternal and begins to question her place in the world. Ikaris's actions become increasingly erratic, leading to a confrontation with his sister that puts the entire group at risk.

Throughout the film, Zhao explores themes of identity, community, and the weight of secrets. The Eternals are a complex and flawed group, struggling to come to terms with their own mortality (or lack thereof). The movie's climax features an epic battle between the Eternals and the Deviants, which serves as a turning point for the characters.

Ultimately, Eternals is a film about finding one's place in the world and embracing one's true identity. It is a visually stunning and action-packed adventure that explores the complexities of the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

original_title: 劇場版 トリニティセブン -天空図書館と真紅の魔王-
overview: The series focuses on the adventures of Arata Kasuga, a high school student, who is targeted by Lilith, a teacher at a mystical school. Given three choices in an effort to help save the breakdown phenomenon of the world by evil forces and while attempting to solve the mystery of his beloved cousin and childhood friend, Hijiri, who disappeared to a difference space.
title: Trinity Seven 2: Heaven's Library & Crimson Lord
plot:
Trinity Seven: Heavens Library & Crimson Lord is a 2019 Japanese animated fantasy romantic comedy and the second feature film based on the Trinity Seven manga created by Kenji Saitō and Akinari Nao, following The Eternal Library and the Alchemist Girl. Hiroshi Nishikiori directed at the studio Seven Arcs from a screenplay by Saitō, with character designs by Shinpei Tomōka and music by Technoboys Pulcraft Green-fund, and the cast of the television series returned, led by Yoshitsugu Matsuoka as Arata Kasuga and Yumi Hara as Lilith Asami, with Aya Uchida, Ayane Sakura, Yōko Hikasa and Nao Tōyama, joined by Tomoaki Maeno as the demon lord Abyss Trinity and Shizuka Itō as the demonic sword Judecca.

Arata, a student mage who carries the power of a Demon Lord candidate, sets out on a routine expedition with Lilith, Akio, Lieselotte and the former enemy Lugh to a lifeless ruin that was once Akio's hometown, destroyed in an attack and closely linked to a hidden library in the sky. Soon after they arrive, a beam of light seizes the group and carries them up to the floating Heavens Library.

There they face their most dangerous opponent yet: Abyss Trinity, a powerful Demon Lord from another dimension who reveals that he is Lilith's father. He challenges Arata, who is now a Demon Lord candidate himself, and the battle goes badly; Lilith is taken captive, since her father intends to use her to restore his full power, and the rest of the group is forced into hiding. To stand a chance, Arata must grow stronger and obtain a new weapon. He seeks out Judecca, a Demon Lord weapon sealed within the library, but nearly loses control of his magic when he tries to wield it, until Lieselotte's numerology magic pulls him back from the brink and he masters a new archive of magic. With the other members of the Trinity Seven joining the fight, Arata and his companions rescue Lilith from Abyss and defeat him, and the Heavens Library is destroyed. As in the series, the action is interspersed with risqué comedy built around Arata's lecherous streak.

The film opened in Japanese cinemas on 29 March 2019 through Avex Pictures and was streamed by Crunchyroll outside Japan. Its theme song, "Against the Abyss," was performed by ZAQ. Reviewers described it as light, entertaining fan service aimed at existing fans of the series, with energetic action but little depth.

original_title: Dragons: Gift of the Night Fury
overview: Hiccup and Toothless go on an exciting adventure and discover an island of new dragons.
title: Dragons: Gift of the Night Fury
plot:
Dragons: Gift of the Night Fury is a 2011 American computer-animated Christmas short film from DreamWorks Animation, directed by Tom Owens and set in the world of How to Train Your Dragon (2010). It was released directly on DVD and Blu-ray on November 15, 2011, paired with another short, Book of Dragons. Jay Baruchel, Gerard Butler, Craig Ferguson, America Ferrera and Jonah Hill reprise their voice roles from the feature film as the Vikings of the island of Berk.

As Berk prepares for Snoggletog, its traditional winter holiday, the village's dragons suddenly and mysteriously fly away together, leaving the Vikings who have only recently befriended them heartbroken. The one dragon left behind is Toothless, the Night Fury, who cannot fly without Hiccup because of his damaged tail. Feeling sorry for his friend, Hiccup builds him an automatic prosthetic tailfin that allows him to fly unaided, a gift of independence, and Toothless soon takes off as well.

Three days later Hiccup discovers that Fishlegs has secretly kept his dragon Meatlug chained up to stop her leaving. When the dragon breaks free, she accidentally carries Hiccup away with her to a distant island of hot springs where the dragons of Berk have gathered to lay and hatch their eggs. Toothless, however, is nowhere to be found. Back on Berk, Astrid and the other teenagers find the eggs Meatlug left in her nest and hide them around the village as presents to cheer everyone up. The plan goes badly wrong, as dragon eggs hatch with an explosion, and the village is left heavily damaged, much to the alarm of Hiccup's father Stoick.

On the island, Hiccup finds Astrid's dragon Stormfly and Snotlout's dragon Hookfang with their new hatchlings. His request for a lift home sets off the dragons' return flight, and because the babies are too young to fly that far he loads them onto an old shipwreck so the adults can tow them. The returning dragons and their young bring joy to Berk, but Hiccup remains saddened by Toothless's absence.

During the Snoggletog celebrations Toothless finally returns, bringing back the helmet Hiccup lost at sea earlier, and the two are joyfully reunited. The next morning Toothless throws away the automatic tail and asks Hiccup to refit the old one, so that they can fly together again with Hiccup steering, showing that the dragon values their partnership more than his independence.
